title: Strong cooperativity and loose geometry between CUB domains are the basis for procollagen C-proteinase enhancer activity

review_notes: Authoritative review of CUB domain biology. Establishes CUB domains as protein-protein interaction modules with beta-sandwich fold, not structural ECM components. Cited by OpenScientist report.

review_notes: This is the bullfrog genome paper cited by UniProt for the nucleotide sequence. It provides the genomic context but no functional characterization of this specific gene.

title: Deep research report for A0A2G9RZF1

title: OpenScientist deep research: GO:0005201 as core function of A0A2G9RZF1
review_notes: OpenScientist autonomous investigation refuted GO:0005201 assignment on three independent grounds: (1) semantic mismatch -- GO:0005201 describes structural ECM proteins, not CUB-domain interaction modules; (2) PCPE-1 FunFam evidence chain failure -- PCPE-1 real function is peptidase activator activity (GO:0016504), and single CUB domains cannot perform PCPE-1 function (requires cooperative CUB1+CUB2 per PMID:19801683); (3) A0A2G9RZF1 is a gene prediction fragment from a poorly assembled genome -- a 2024 chromosome-level assembly (GCF_042186555.1) encodes complete BMP-1 (1,020 aa) and TLL1 (1,005 aa).

Supports the kinase-activity, protein phosphorylation, and stomatal movement annotations.

title: The role of Arabidopsis Rubisco activase in jasmonate-induced leaf senescence.

title: Discovering the RNA-Binding Proteome of Plant Leaves with an Improved RNA Interactome Capture Method.
review_notes: Full text verified; proteome-wide RNA interactome capture identifying many photosynthetic enzymes (including RCA) as unconventional RNA binders. Supports the mRNA-binding annotation only as a moonlighting/unconventional observation, not a core function.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS transfer of "Ndc80 complex" from human SPC24 (UniProtKB:Q8NBT2). The orthology and complex membership are independently confirmed experimentally in Arabidopsis (SUBUNIT statement plus IPI interactions with all three other NDC80 subunits in PMID:29356153).

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt

title: AtSubP analysis

title: MUN (MERISTEM UNSTRUCTURED), encoding a SPC24 homolog of NDC80 kinetochore complex, affects development through cell division in Arabidopsis thaliana.

The defining functional study of AtSPC24/MUN, supplying FUNCTION, SUBUNIT, SUBCELLULAR LOCATION, TISSUE SPECIFICITY and DISRUPTION PHENOTYPE, and the source of all experimental (IDA/IMP/IPI) annotations. Cached as abstract-only (full text not in cache); the TAIR experimental annotations were made from the full text.

title: AtNUF2 modulates spindle microtubule organization and chromosome segregation during mitosis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Characterizes AtNUF2, a direct partner subunit of AtSPC24 in the NDC80 complex (NUF2 binds SPC25), corroborating the complex's role in spindle organization and chromosome segregation in plant mitosis.

title: Arabidopsis transcription factors: genome-wide comparative analysis among eukaryotes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified genome-wide TF survey; supports the general statement that SPCH is a transcription factor but does not establish SPCH-specific function.

title: The basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor family in plants: a genome-wide study of protein structure and functional diversity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified plant bHLH family analysis; basis for the family-level bHLH/AtbHLH98 assignment, not SPCH-specific functional evidence.

title: Transcription factor control of asymmetric cell divisions that establish the stomatal lineage.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; original identification of SPCH as the bHLH TF necessary and sufficient for the asymmetric divisions initiating the stomatal lineage (abstract-only in cache).

title: SCREAM/ICE1 and SCREAM2 specify three cell-state transitional steps leading to arabidopsis stomatal differentiation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available; establishes that SCRM/ICE1 and SCRM2 directly interact with SPCH (and MUTE/FAMA) as nuclear DNA-binding heterodimers.

title: Arabidopsis stomatal initiation is controlled by MAPK-mediated regulation of the bHLH SPEECHLESS.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; defines SPCH as a MAPK (MPK3/6) phosphorylation target and provides IDA nuclear localization and IMP stomatal-development evidence (abstract-only in cache).

title: Low relative humidity triggers RNA-directed de novo DNA methylation and suppression of genes controlling stomatal development.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available; shows the SPCH locus is de novo methylated and transcriptionally repressed under low humidity (SPCH as environmental target).

title: Arabidopsis reduces growth under osmotic stress by decreasing SPEECHLESS protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available; shows osmotic stress decreases SPCH protein via a MAPK cascade, integrating stress into stomatal development.

title: Phosphorylation of Serine 186 of bHLH Transcription Factor SPEECHLESS Promotes Stomatal Development in Arabidopsis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; demonstrates CDKA;1 phosphorylation of SPCH Ser186 positively regulates stomatal development (basis for the CDKA;1 IPI and IMP annotations).

title: A Mutation in the bHLH Domain of the SPCH Transcription Factor Uncovers a BR-Dependent Mechanism for Stomatal Development.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available; bHLH-domain (spch-5) mutant shows the domain is required for SPCH target-gene activation; basis for the IDA activator MF annotation.

title: Extensive signal integration by the phytohormone protein network.
review_notes: PubMed-verified large-scale phytohormone interactome; source of the SPCH-RACK1B (Q9C4Z6) binary interaction, functional relevance to SPCH unestablished.

title: Falcon/Edison deep research report: SPCH

title: Cloning of the Arabidopsis clock gene TOC1, an autoregulatory response regulator homolog.

title: Two-component signal transduction pathways in Arabidopsis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified review of Arabidopsis two-component signaling; not a TOC1-specific functional study. Supports general transcriptional-regulation context only.

title: Circadian rhythm of circumnutation in inflorescence stems of Arabidopsis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; toc1 shortens the period of circumnutation, a circadian output (non-core).

title: PRR3 Is a vascular regulator of TOC1 stability in the Arabidopsis circadian clock.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; PRR3 binds TOC1 and stabilizes it by hindering ZTL degradation; explicitly notes the pseudo-receiver domain lacks the catalytic Asp.

title: Post-translational regulation of the Arabidopsis circadian clock through selective proteolysis and phosphorylation of pseudo-response regulator proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; demonstrates nuclear localization and circadian phosphorylation of TOC1/PRR proteins and SCF(ZTL)-dependent turnover.

title: A functional genomics approach reveals CHE as a component of the Arabidopsis circadian clock.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; identifies CHE and the TOC1-CHE interaction recruiting TOC1 to the CCA1 promoter. Reports no direct TOC1 binding to the CCA1 promoter region tested (basis of the negated GO:0000976); later superseded for other elements by PMID:22315425.

title: PRR5 regulates phosphorylation, nuclear import and subnuclear localization of TOC1 in the Arabidopsis circadian clock.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; PRR5-TOC1 N-terminal oligomerization promotes TOC1 nuclear import, phosphorylation and subnuclear foci.

title: Arabidopsis circadian clock protein, TOC1, is a DNA-binding transcription factor.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; key paper showing purified TOC1 binds DNA via the CCT domain and acts as a general transcriptional repressor of CCA1/LHY, with DNA binding required for repression.

title: Accurate timekeeping is controlled by a cycling activator in Arabidopsis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; RVE8 activator study; describes TOC1 as an evening PRR that represses CCA1/LHY and is itself activated by RVE8.

title: Pseudo Response Regulators Regulate Photoperiodic Hypocotyl Growth by Repressing PIF4/5 Transcription.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; PRRs (including TOC1) directly bind PIF4/PIF5 promoters to repress transcription; TOC1 DNA-binding-domain mutants disrupt photoperiodic hypocotyl growth.

title: Falcon/Edison deep research report: TOC1

title: A UV-B-specific signaling component orchestrates plant UV protection.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text. Establishes UVR8 as UV-B-specific regulator of HY5, shows chromatin/histone association at the HY5 promoter, and critically that UVR8 has little GEF activity, does not bind Ran, and does not complement yeast RCC1 - refuting the GEF-activity annotation.

title: UV-B promotes rapid nuclear translocation of the Arabidopsis UV-B specific signaling component UVR8 and activates its function in the nucleus.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text. Demonstrates UV-B-specific, rapid (within 5 min) nuclear accumulation of UVR8 and that nuclear localization is necessary but not sufficient for function.

title: Interaction of COP1 and UVR8 regulates UV-B-induced photomorphogenesis and stress acclimation in Arabidopsis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text. Shows UV-B-dependent direct UVR8-COP1 interaction in planta and that uvr8-null plants lack UV-B photomorphogenesis.

title: Interaction of the Arabidopsis UV-B-specific signaling component UVR8 with chromatin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (abstract-only in cache). Shows native UVR8 binds chromatin in vivo, preferentially via histone H2B, at the HY5 locus.

title: Negative feedback regulation of UV-B-induced photomorphogenesis and stress acclimation in Arabidopsis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text. Identifies RUP1/RUP2 as direct UVR8-interacting repressors providing negative feedback on UV-B signaling.

title: Functional interaction of the circadian clock and UV RESISTANCE LOCUS 8-controlled UV-B signaling pathways in Arabidopsis thaliana.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (abstract-only in cache). Shows UVR8 (and COP1) required for UV-B entrainment of the circadian clock, supporting the non-core circadian annotation.

title: Structural basis of ultraviolet-B perception by UVR8.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (abstract-only in cache). Crystal structure showing the seven-bladed beta-propeller homodimer with no external chromophore; identifies Trp-285 and Trp-233 as the UV-B chromophore.

title: C-terminal region of the UV-B photoreceptor UVR8 initiates signaling through interaction with the COP1 protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text. Maps the C27 C-terminal region as necessary and sufficient for interaction with the COP1 WD40 domain (and with RUP1/RUP2).

title: Reversion of the Arabidopsis UV-B photoreceptor UVR8 to the homodimeric ground state.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (abstract-only in cache). Shows UVR8 monomerization is reversible and RUP1/RUP2 mediate redimerization to regenerate the homodimeric ground state.

title: A proteomic strategy for global analysis of plant protein complexes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text. A methods paper presenting a global cytosolic protein-complex SEC/MS survey; the UVR8 cytosol annotation is a high-throughput data point.

title: Arabidopsis transcription factors: genome-wide comparative analysis among eukaryotes.

review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mas et al., Nature 2003). Establishes ZTL-dependent, proteasome-dependent degradation of TOC1 and its role in setting circadian period.

title: ZEITLUPE is a circadian photoreceptor stabilized by GIGANTEA in blue light

title: The F-box protein ZEITLUPE controls stability and nucleocytoplasmic partitioning of GIGANTEA

title: UniProt entry P25816 (Profilin-1 / Bet v 2), Betula pendula
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; source for the profilin actin-binding core function.

review_notes: Curated UniProt record; supports secreted pheromone-carrier lipocalin classification.

title: Collagen processing and cuticle formation is catalysed by the astacin metalloprotease DPY-31 in free-living and parasitic nematodes.

title: Identification and activity of inhibitors of the essential nematode-specific metalloprotease DPY-31.
review_notes: Cited in the UniProt record (reference [3]) for catalytic activity and activity regulation; reports hydroxamate/marimastat inhibition of DPY-31, supporting its identity as a druggable zinc metalloprotease and nematode-specific target. PubMed-verified title; no cached full text, so not used for verbatim supporting_text.

title: The FAR proteins of filarial nematodes: secretion, glycosylation and lipid binding characteristics.
review_notes: Primary reference establishing the retinol- and fatty-acid-binding activity and secretion of Bm-FAR-1. Abstract directly supports the IDA fatty acid binding and retinol binding annotations and the ISS secreted location.

title: Transmission-blocking antibodies recognize microfilarial chitinase in brugian lymphatic filariasis.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS transfer from the experimentally characterized C. elegans ortholog cep-1 (UniProtKB Q20646). Appropriate for transcription factor activity, DNA binding, nuclear localization, and DNA-damage apoptosis given strong orthology and conserved p53-family DNA-binding domain.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Automated Compara-based transfer from the C. elegans ortholog. Most transferred terms are appropriate, but some electronically propagated component terms (nucleolus, transcription repressor complex) over-reach relative to the established activator biology of CEP-1.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined IEA (InterPro2GO and related) annotations. Consistent with the p53-like DNA-binding domain (IPR008967, IPR012346); the generic DNA binding term is subsumed by the more specific sequence-specific DNA binding annotation.

title: Rapid coevolution of the nematode sex-determining genes fem-3 and tra-2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Haag, Wang, Kimble, Curr Biol 2002). Cached entry is abstract-only; abstract directly supports the conserved male-promoting function of C. briggsae fem-3 (IMP) and the species-specific FEM-3-TRA-2 interaction (IPI). Provides the experimental basis for the male sex-determination and TRA-2-binding annotations.

title: DNA binding and in vivo function of C.elegans PEB-1 require a conserved FLYWCH motif.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary research on PEB-1; the C. briggsae sequence is characterized here and the FLYWCH motif is shown to be required for DNA binding and in vivo function. Establishes the YDTGCCRW consensus and nuclear localization requirements. Cached entry is abstract-only (full_text_available: false); quotes used are verbatim from the abstract.

title: Independent recruitment of F box genes to regulate hermaphrodite development during nematode evolution.
review_notes: Sole primary characterization of she-1 (Guo, Lang & Ellis, Curr. Biol. 2009). PMID is the reference cited by the UniProt entry (A8XDR5) for FUNCTION, DEVELOPMENTAL STAGE, DISRUPTION PHENOTYPE, and mutagenesis of Arg-49/Gly-111. Full text is not available in the local publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text is quoted and citation soundness is not independently verified here; claims are drawn from the UniProt summary and the published abstract.

title: The TRA-1 transcription factor binds TRA-2 to regulate sexual fates in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Establishes tra-1 as terminal regulator promoting female fates and reports the conserved MX-dependent TRA-1/TRA-2 physical interaction in both C. elegans and C. briggsae; directly supports the sex-determination and protein-interaction annotations for Cbr-tra-1.

title: RNA-Regulated TRA-1 nuclear export controls sexual fate.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Shows TRA-1 is a GLI-family TF required for female development with sex-specific nuclear distribution and CRM1-dependent nuclear export coupled to tra-2 3'UTR binding; supports the nucleus/cytoplasm localization annotations and the regulated-export mechanism.

title: Evolutionary change within a bipotential switch shaped the sperm/oocyte decision in hermaphroditic nematodes.
review_notes: Cited in the GO:0045944 annotation review as the source for TRA-1's context-dependent activating role on fog-3 (with the TRR-1/Tip60 HAT complex) in the sperm/oocyte decision. Added to references for traceability; full-text verification pending.

title: Proteolysis in Caenorhabditis elegans sex determination: cleavage of TRA-2A by TRA-3.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Establishes that the membrane protein TRA-2A is a substrate of the TRA-3 calpain-like protease and that cleavage generates a feminizing fragment; supports the IDA membrane localization. Work is in C. elegans but directly informs the conserved Cbr-TRA-2 biology.

title: The TRA-1 transcription factor binds TRA-2 to regulate sexual fates in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache, but explicitly reports an MX-dependent Cb-TRA-1/Cb-TRA-2 interaction in C. briggsae (no cross-species interaction), directly supporting the Cbr-specific TRA-1 binding and germline sex-determination (spermatogenesis) roles.

title: Rapid coevolution of the nematode sex-determining genes fem-3 and tra-2.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Directly addresses C. briggsae: FEM-3 interacts with TRA-2 in a strictly species-specific manner and the FEM-3-binding domain of TRA-2 is hypervariable and rapidly coevolving. Supports the FEM-3 sequestration/adaptor function and the comparative-evolution framing.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS transfer of nuclear localization from the C. elegans ortholog G5EEV2; consistent with the UniProt-documented nuclear/condensed-chromosome localization of Cbr-TRR-1.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PANTHER/GO_Central phylogenetic (IBA) inferences for the TRRAP/Tra1 family. The complex memberships (NuA4, SAGA), nuclear localization, and chromatin/transcription processes are all consistent with the well-characterized conserved scaffolding role of this family.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Keyword-to-GO mapping of the Nucleus subcellular location; redundant with but consistent with the IBA/ISS nucleus annotations.

title: Evolutionary change within a bipotential switch shaped the sperm/oocyte decision in hermaphroditic nematodes.

Shows trr-1 acts through TRA-1 and the Tip60 HAT complex to activate fog-3 and control the germline sperm/oocyte fate decision; reduced trr-1 gives a feminized (Fog) germ line, and the gene is required for spermatogenesis and embryonic development. Full text is available in the local publications cache (content_type: full_text_pdf); the verbatim finding above is quoted directly from it.

title: Genome sequence of the nematode C. elegans: a platform for investigating biology
review_notes: This is the C. elegans genome sequencing paper; it is the source of the genomic DNA sequence for the mcm-4 locus (Y39G10AR.14) but does not provide functional characterization.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis investigation - LPL1 monoacylglycerol lipase activity

title: Structural and ligand binding analysis of the pet allergens Can f 1 and Fel d 7.

title: UniProt entry O18873 (Major allergen Can f 1), Canis lupus familiaris

title: Dog saliva - an important source of dog allergens.

title: AmiC2 (Cylst_4888 / K9X2S2) gene review notes

title: Fra proteins influencing filament integrity, diazotrophy and localization of septal protein SepJ in the heterocyst-forming cyanobacterium Anabaena sp.
review_notes: Primary functional paper for the Anabaena/Nostoc sp. PCC 7120 FraC ortholog (P46078). Establishes fraC = alr2392 as the first gene of the constitutively expressed fraC-fraD-fraE operon, septal (GFP) localization of FraC, and fraC-mutant defects in SepJ localization, intercellular calcein transfer, filament integrity and diazotrophy. Cited here as the ISS source for the C. stagnale ortholog K9WTD1; PMID matches title; abstract-only in cache but annotations rest on the full-text assays.

title: A short-filament mutant of Anabaena sp. strain PCC 7120 that fragments in nitrogen-deficient medium.
review_notes: Discovery/cloning of fraC in the PCC 7120 short-filament fragmentation strain 129; 179-aa phenylalanine-rich protein; insertional inactivation reproduces the phenotype; establishes the filament/cell-junction integrity role distinct from differentiation and N2 fixation. Cited here as ISS source for the C. stagnale ortholog; PMID matches title; abstract + short full text in cache.

title: Fra proteins influencing filament integrity, diazotrophy and localization of septal protein SepJ in the heterocyst-forming cyanobacterium Anabaena sp.
review_notes: Establishes fraD = alr2393 in the fraC-fraD-fraE operon, septal localization of FraD (GFP fusions) and fra-mutant defects in calcein transfer, filament integrity and diazotrophy in PCC 7120. Basis for ISS transfer of membrane localization and cell-cell communication to the C. stagnale ortholog. Abstract-only in cache.

title: SepN is a septal junction component required for gated cell-cell communication in the filamentous cyanobacterium Nostoc.
review_notes: Identifies SepN as the FraD-interacting SJ plug component and shows SepN co-occurs phylogenetically with FraD; supports the family-level SJ role transferred by orthology. Full text available in cache.

title: The SepN-FraD structural module serves as an anchor and assembly platform for septal junctions in cyanobacteria.
review_notes: Characterization of the PCC 7120 FraD ortholog (Kieninger et al., Cell Rep 2026): defines FraD as the transmembrane/periplasmic anchor of the septal junction via cryoET, AlphaFold 3 and MD. Used here as the basis for ISS transfer to the C. stagnale ortholog K9WUY7; no experiment was done on K9WUY7 itself.

title: Fra proteins influencing filament integrity, diazotrophy and localization of septal protein SepJ in the heterocyst-forming cyanobacterium Anabaena sp.
review_notes: Primary source characterizing the orthologous PCC 7120 fraC-fraD-fraE operon (fraE = alr2394), its constitutive expression, and the shared mutant phenotype (filament fragmentation under nitrogen deprivation, loss of diazotrophic growth despite heterocyst formation), plus septal localization of FraC and FraD. The functional inference for K9WTV4 is transferred by orthology (reciprocal best hit, forward E = 7.2e-109, 70.3% identity, and conserved operon synteny). Abstract-only in cache; the abstract does not report a FraE-specific localization or biochemical assay, and does not study C. stagnale directly.

title: Septum-localized protein required for filament integrity and diazotrophy in the heterocyst-forming cyanobacterium Anabaena sp. strain PCC 7120.
review_notes: Flores et al. 2007 (J Bacteriol). Original description of the PCC 7120 ortholog sepJ (= alr2338): SepJ-GFP localizes to the intercellular septa and forms a Z-ring-like ring during division; the mutant fragments, arrests heterocyst maturation and cannot fix N2; multidomain protein with a permease-like C-terminal domain. Full text cached; PMID matches title. Used here as the ISS basis for K9WRN1 (septal location, multidomain architecture).

title: Fra proteins influencing filament integrity, diazotrophy and localization of septal protein SepJ in the heterocyst-forming cyanobacterium Anabaena sp.
review_notes: Merino-Puerto et al. 2010 (Mol Microbiol). FraC/FraD are required for correct SepJ septal localization and for intercellular calcein transfer; places SepJ among the septal proteins governing intercellular communication. Abstract cached; PMID matches title.

title: Functional dissection of the three-domain SepJ protein joining the cells in cyanobacterial trichomes.
review_notes: Mariscal et al. 2011 (Mol Microbiol). Domain-swap/deletion dissection of PCC 7120 SepJ: coiled-coil domain drives polar localization, filament integrity, tracer transfer and diazotrophy; the permease domain provides intercellular molecular exchange. Abstract cached; PMID matches title. ISS basis for the cell-cell signaling / anchoring role.

title: Septal protein SepJ from the heterocyst-forming cyanobacterium Anabaena forms multimers and interacts with peptidoglycan.
review_notes: Ramos-León et al. 2017 (FEBS Open Bio). Primary evidence that PCC 7120 SepJ forms multimeric complexes and binds peptidoglycan (via its coiled-coil domain), and that SepJ/FraC/FraD are cytoplasmic-membrane proteins at the intercellular septa. Full text cached; PMID matches title. PRIMARY ISS basis for the structural role and plasma membrane location.

title: SepJ (FraG, Cylst_0707 / K9WRN1) research notes
review_notes: Local notes documenting the orthology evidence (reciprocal best hit with the PCC 7120 SepJ exemplar A0ACD7RSI0 / alr2338 at forward E = 1.7e-206, 52.3% amino-acid identity), the broad EamA/DMT domain caveat, the multidomain architecture from the UniProt record, and the annotation plan mirroring the PCC 7120 SepJ review.

title: SepN is a septal junction component required for gated cell-cell communication in the filamentous cyanobacterium Nostoc.
review_notes: Discovery/characterization paper for the PCC 7120 SepN ortholog (Kieninger et al., Nat Commun 2022). Identifies SepN as the FraD-interacting septal-junction plug component required for gated cell-cell communication. Functional statements are transferred to C. stagnale K9WXR0 by orthology (ISS); no direct assay on K9WXR0. Full text available in cache; PMID matches title.

title: The SepN-FraD structural module serves as an anchor and assembly platform for septal junctions in cyanobacteria.
review_notes: Structural paper for the PCC 7120 SepN ortholog (Kieninger et al., Cell Rep 2026). Models SepN as a pentameric plug anchored by FraD. Basis for the transferred structural-plug function; PubMed-verified (abstract in cache).

title: SepN (K9WXR0 / Cylst_2059) research notes
review_notes: Orthology-evidence notes for K9WXR0: reciprocal-best-hit homology to PCC 7120 SepN (forward E = 9.3e-111, 69.4% identity), absence of any family model (exemplar- homology detection only), and Nostocales-signature / FraD co-occurrence context.

title: Disruption of zebrafish cyclin G-associated kinase (GAK) function impairs the expression of Notch-dependent genes during neurogenesis and causes defects in neuronal development.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; this is the primary zebrafish study on auxilin/GAK function (Bai et al. 2010, BMC Dev Biol). The paper focuses mainly on GAK knockdown but includes functional characterization and localization data for zAux. Full text available via PMC2821301.

title: UniProt entry P08176 (Peptidase 1 / Der p 1), Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus

title: UniProt entry P49278 (Mite group 2 allergen Der p 2), Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus

title: Conversion of Der p 23, a new major house dust mite allergen, into a hypoallergenic vaccine.

title: TSG-6 potentiates the antitissue kallikrein activity of inter-alpha-inhibitor through bikunin release.
review_notes: Cached full text available. Human airway biology; cited for the covalent TSG-6-heavy-chain complex and the antiplasmin potentiation, not for any bat-specific claim.

title: The TSG-6/HC2-mediated transfer is a dynamic process shuffling heavy chains between glycosaminoglycans.
review_notes: Cached full text available. Human/bovine biochemistry, cited here as the orthologue evidence underpinning the ISS transfer to the bat protein; the bat protein itself has not been assayed.

title: The "Vampirome": Transcriptome and proteome analysis of the principal and accessory submaxillary glands of the vampire bat Desmodus rotundus, a vector of human rabies.

title: Metal Ion-dependent Heavy Chain Transfer Activity of TSG-6 Mediates Assembly of the Cumulus-Oocyte Matrix.
review_notes: Cached full text available. Human TSG-6 structure and mouse genetics; used as orthologue evidence for the catalytic and hyaluronan-metabolic calls on the bat protein.

Several of its cited sources are flagged in the report itself as low-quality journals, so it is used here to corroborate rather than to establish claims, each of which is also anchored to the UniProt record or to PMID:23411029.

title: The "Vampirome": Transcriptome and proteome analysis of the principal and accessory submaxillary glands of the vampire bat Desmodus rotundus, a vector of human rabies.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available via PMC. This is the source publication for the EMBL entry (JAA44981.1) behind K9IWC0 and it names the bat salivary natriuretic peptide as CNP, in agreement with the sequence analysis in the local bioinformatics report and against the ARBA-derived "Natriuretic peptides B" name in UniProt.

title: Sequence classification of K9IWC0 among the natriuretic peptide paralogues
review_notes: Reproducible analysis added with this review. All four sequences are fetched from the UniProt REST API at run time and the alignment is computed by Biopython; nothing is hardcoded. Raw output in results.json, script in classify_natriuretic_peptide.py.

title: Deep research report on K9IWC0
review_notes: LLM-generated survey that propagated the UniProt paralogue misassignment. It did not consult the PANTHER subfamily assignment in the same UniProt record, did not find the Vampirome study that names the bat salivary peptide as CNP, and devoted most of its length to human heart-failure biomarker literature irrelevant to this protein. Cited here only as the record of that error and for its correct statement of family receptor usage.

title: The "Vampirome": Transcriptome and proteome analysis of the principal and accessory submaxillary glands of the vampire bat Desmodus rotundus, a vector of human rabies.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. This is the source publication for the EMBL entry (JAA45881.1) from which K9IWX5 was derived; the salivary gland tissue attribution in the UniProt record traces to this transcriptome/proteome study. It supports secretion and salivary-gland origin, and explicitly states that the function of the salivary antigen-5/CRISP family is unknown.

title: Deep research report on K9IWX5
review_notes: LLM-generated literature survey. Useful for the CAP/CRISP family background and for its explicit statement that no protein-specific studies exist, but several of its cited sources are flagged in the report itself as low-quality journals, and none concerns Desmodus rotundus. Not used here to support any positive functional claim.

title: The "Vampirome": Transcriptome and proteome analysis of the principal and accessory submaxillary glands of the vampire bat Desmodus rotundus, a vector of human rabies.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available via PMC. Establishes salivary gland expression and proteomic detection of lysozyme in D. rotundus, which is what supports the proposed extracellular region annotation.

title: Adaptive Evolution of C-Type Lysozyme in Vampire Bats.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. This is the study behind the third EMBL record in the UniProt entry (MK561737 / QEQ43371.1, liver), and it is the only publication that analyses this specific gene. Only the abstract is cached (full_text_available: false), so all statements used here are drawn from the abstract; the sequence-level substitution analysis is not available for inspection.

title: Deep research report on K9IWH5
review_notes: LLM-generated survey. Accurate and useful at the GH22 family level, and appropriately explicit that no D. rotundus-specific experimental data were recovered. It did not surface PMID:31506780, the one study that does analyse this gene. Cited here only for family-level mechanism.

title: Blinded OpenScientist function-assignment report (TreeGrafter audit)
review_notes: Blinded run (given only 'aprA has succinate dehydrogenase activity') independently refuted the term: aprA is adenylyl-sulfate (APS) reductase alpha (EC 1.8.99.2), grafted onto the SDH flavoprotein subfamily; the covalent FAD-binding histidine required for all SDH/FRD catalysis is absent. Blinded OpenScientist function-assignment run: given only the propagated term (the prior curation action withheld), it independently reached the same conclusion as this review. Corroborating evidence, not a primary source.

title: Structurally distinct and stage-specific adenylyl cyclase genes play different roles in Dictyostelium development.

title: Intracellular role of adenylyl cyclase in regulation of lateral pseudopod formation during Dictyostelium chemotaxis.
review_notes: Establishes the intracellular (cAMP/PKA circuit) role of ACA in lateral pseudopod suppression and chemotaxis.

title: Collective cell migration requires vesicular trafficking for chemoattractant delivery at the trailing edge.
review_notes: Key paper establishing ACA vesicular trafficking and rear-of-cell accumulation underlying the cAMP relay.

title: Adenylyl cyclase localization to the uropod of aggregating Dictyostelium cells requires RacC.
review_notes: Demonstrates RacC-dependent trafficking of ACA vesicles to the uropod required for streaming.

title: Adenylate cyclase A acting on PKA mediates induction of stalk formation by cyclic diguanylate at the Dictyostelium organizer.
review_notes: Establishes a later-development role for ACA at the organizer, transducing c-di-GMP to PKA for stalk cell differentiation.

title: Adenylyl cyclase A mRNA localized at the back of cells is actively translated in live chemotaxing Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Shows localized translation of ACA at the cell rear as part of the relay mechanism.

title: The neonicotinoid insecticide imidacloprid has unexpected effects on the growth and development of soil amoebae.
review_notes: Broad toxicant transcriptome study; acaA response is a general stress/developmental readout, not a specific ACA function.

title: Exploring the mechanisms of cadmium tolerance and bioaccumulation in a soil amoeba.
review_notes: High-throughput expression screen; acaA is a differentially expressed gene rather than a dedicated cadmium-response effector.

title: Identification of detergent-resistant plasma membrane microdomains in dictyostelium: enrichment of signal transduction proteins.
review_notes: Biochemical evidence for ACA plasma membrane localization in signaling microdomains.

title: Peptide signaling during terminal differentiation of Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Primary paper establishing AcbA as the SDF-2 precursor, its acyl-CoA binding, the acbA-null sporulation defect, and the DhkA kinase- inhibition mechanism. Full text available and quotes verified against it.

title: Global transcriptional responses to cisplatin in Dictyostelium discoideum identify potential drug targets.
review_notes: Cisplatin-sensitivity screen; the acbA phenotype is attributed to sphingolipid metabolism, supporting a metabolic role but not a bona fide DNA damage response annotation.

title: Unconventional secretion of AcbA in Dictyostelium discoideum through a vesicular intermediate.
review_notes: Establishes the vesicular, NSF/GRASP-dependent unconventional secretion route and cortical vesicle localization of AcbA; quotes verified.

title: Leaps and lulls in the developmental transcriptome of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Developmental RNA-seq time course; provides expression-pattern (IEP) support consistent with AcbA's dual metabolic/signaling roles.

title: Adenylyl cyclase G is activated by an intramolecular osmosensor.
review_notes: PMC full text confirms ACG is an intramolecular osmosensor whose osmoactivation is retained in yeast; directly supports the osmosensor activity, osmosensory signaling, and germination-control annotations.

title: Pharmacological profiling of the Dictyostelium adenylate cyclases ACA, ACB and ACG.
review_notes: Supports the response-to-caffeine annotation and confirms ACG is an osmosensor controlling spore germination that is not activated by G proteins.

title: cAMP production by adenylyl cyclase G induces prespore differentiation in Dictyostelium slugs.
review_notes: Establishes the prespore-differentiation role of ACG-derived cAMP and the plasma-membrane localization of ACG in spores.

title: From drought sensing to developmental control: evolution of cyclic AMP signaling in social amoebas.
review_notes: Provides the evolutionary/conservation context for ACG's osmosensing and germination-control functions across dictyostelid species.

title: The polyketide MPBD initiates the SDF-1 signaling cascade that coordinates terminal differentiation in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Supports a signal transduction role for ACG in the SDF-1 relay; the ACG-SDF-1 link is described as apparent, not a demonstrated direct peptide-receptor interaction.

title: Regulation of Dictyostelium adenylylcyclases by morphogen-induced modulation of cytosolic pH or Ca2+ levels.
review_notes: Supports the pH-dependence (response to acidic pH) annotation and documents ACG's Ca2+ insensitivity.

title: Adenylyl cyclase G, an osmosensor controlling germination of Dictyostelium spores.
review_notes: Original characterization of ACG as an osmosensor that controls spore germination via PKA; abstract-only cache but the key findings are explicit.

title: An adenylyl cyclase that functions during late development of Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Primary discovery/characterization of acrA; abstract-only in cache but establishes catalytic activity, developmental expression, and the sporulation/stalk phenotype. Verified via PubMed title match.

title: Pharmacological profiling of the Dictyostelium adenylate cyclases ACA, ACB and ACG.
review_notes: Full text available; supports the caffeine-response annotation and confirms acrA=ACB identity and its spore-maturation role.

title: High-throughput analysis of spatio-temporal dynamics in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Full text available; high-throughput phenotyping supporting the late/culmination-stage sorocarp development annotation.

title: Cytokinins induce sporulation in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache but the abstract explicitly names AcrA as required for cytokinin signal transduction leading to sporulation.

title: Functional dissection of adenylate cyclase R, an inducer of spore encapsulation.
review_notes: Full text available; the definitive domain-dissection and localization study, and the basis for removing the phosphorelay and transferase (histidine-kinase) domain-based IEA annotations.

title: Transcriptomic and metabolomic insights into light-mediated unicellular-to-multicellular transition in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Full text available; supports only the expression-level (HEP) light-response annotation, not a direct protein function.

title: Autophagy gene disruption reveals a non-vacuolar cell death pathway in Dictyostelium.

title: Function of the Dictyostelium discoideum Atg1 kinase during autophagy and development.

title: The autophagic machinery ensures nonlytic transmission of mycobacteria.

title: Dictyostelium discoideum as a Novel Host System to Study the Interaction between Phagocytes and Yeasts.

review_notes: Solid genetic evidence linking dhkA to RegA/cAMP and sporulation. The authors' proposed directionality (that DhkA activates RegA phosphodiesterase) explicitly contradicts Wang et al. (PMID:10373524 / PMID:15897458), who show ligand binding to DhkA inhibits phosphorelay to RegA; the direction of DhkA-RegA regulation is therefore contested. Hand-curated expert assessment - the Wang/Anjard-Loomis inhibition model is the better-supported working model. DhkA autophosphorylation on His1395 and phosphorelay through RdeA to the RegA receiver aspartate are biochemically demonstrated, and SDF-2 binding lowers this relay so RegA is dephosphorylated and inactivated, raising intracellular cAMP and activating PKA to trigger encapsulation. The fbxA genetic-interaction study reported here infers the opposite direction only indirectly, so it is recorded as a contested minority interpretation pending direct measurement of the RegA phosphorylation state in dhkA-null versus SDF-2-treated cells.

title: The green tea catechin epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) blocks cell motility, chemotaxis and development in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: gbfA appears only as one of several developmentally-delayed transcripts under EGCG; the response-to-catechin annotation is indirect.

title: Leaps and lulls in the developmental transcriptome of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Developmental transcriptome study confirming gbfA as a transition-stage transcription factor.

title: Transcriptomic and metabolomic insights into light-mediated unicellular-to-multicellular transition in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Light-transition transcriptomic study; gbfA appears as a differentially expressed post-aggregation regulator, supporting only the expression-based light-response annotation.

title: A GBF-binding site and a novel AT element define the minimal sequences sufficient to direct prespore-specific expression in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Directly demonstrates GBF sequence-specific DNA binding to defined regulatory elements; core evidence for the DNA-binding function.

title: Cloning and characterization of the G-box binding factor, an essential component of the developmental switch between early and late development in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Foundational cloning/characterization paper establishing GBF's transcription-factor activity, nuclear localization, and essential developmental-switch role.

title: lagC-null and gbf-null cells define key steps in the morphogenesis of Dictyostelium mounds.
review_notes: Defines the mound-morphogenesis defects of gbf-null cells, linking GBF loss to failed signaling-center establishment.

title: Identification of four candidate cGMP targets in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Original identification of GbpC and its domain architecture; abstract confirms it is the dominant high-affinity cGMP-binding protein.

title: RasGEF-containing proteins GbpC and GbpD have differential effects on cell polarity and chemotaxis in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Establishes GbpC's role in chemotactic polarity via myosin; the adhesion phenotype in this paper belongs to the paralog GbpD, not GbpC.

title: Myosin light chain kinase A is activated by cGMP-dependent and cGMP-independent pathways.
review_notes: Places GbpC upstream of MLCK-A activation in the chemotaxis myosin pathway; supports an indirect kinase-regulatory role.

title: The Legionella pneumophila phosphatidylinositol-4 phosphate-binding type IV substrate SidC recruits endoplasmic reticulum vesicles to a replication-permissive vacuole.
review_notes: This PMID is a Legionella pneumophila SidC effector study with no relation to GbpC or cGMP binding. It is cited in GOA as the reference for GbpC cGMP binding (IDA) and regulation of chemotaxis (IMP); those functions are genuine but the identifier is mis-attributed. The correct GbpC references are PMID:12011437, PMID:18703517 and PMID:15827084.

title: Intramolecular activation mechanism of the Dictyostelium LRRK2 homolog Roco protein GbpC.
review_notes: Full-text PMC article; directly demonstrates the intramolecular cGMP to GEF to Roc to kinase signaling cascade underpinning several core molecular functions.

title: Switching direction in electric-signal-induced cell migration by cyclic guanosine monophosphate and phosphatidylinositol signaling.
review_notes: Supports a GbpC role in electrotaxis directionality; the cached text does not clearly document GbpC-specific leading-edge localization.

title: Multiple regulatory mechanisms for the Dictyostelium Roco protein GbpC.
review_notes: Full-text PMC article; establishes the GRAM-dependent membrane/cortex localization and phospholipid-binding activity of GbpC.

title: Microtubule-Mediated Inositol Lipid Signaling Plays Critical Roles in Regulation of Blebbing.
review_notes: Genetic blebbing screen; note the paper parenthetically mislabels gbpC/gbpD as guanylate cyclases, but the mutant blebbing phenotype is the basis for the IGI annotation.

title: RasGEF-containing proteins GbpC and GbpD have differential effects on cell polarity and chemotaxis in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; abstract directly establishes GbpD's loss-/gain-of-function effects on adhesion, lateral pseudopodia, polarity and chemotaxis. Assigned by dictyBase for multiple IMP annotations.

title: Characterization of the GbpD-activated Rap1 pathway regulating adhesion and cell polarity in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; establishes the direct GEF-substrate relationship (GbpD to Rap1 to Phg2) that underpins the IDA GEF-activity annotation and the specificity supporting the MODIFY to Rap-GEF activity.

title: Microtubule-Mediated Inositol Lipid Signaling Plays Critical Roles in Regulation of Blebbing.
review_notes: Full text available. gbpD contribution comes from a gbpC/gbpD double-deficient background and the paper informally labels these as guanylate cyclases; supports a modulatory (non-core) bleb-regulation role.

title: Excitable Ras dynamics-based screens reveal RasGEFX is required for macropinocytosis and random cell migration.
review_notes: Full text available. Explicitly equates RasGEFU with GbpD, confirms plasma-membrane localization and adhesion/pseudopod/motility phenotypes underpinning the dictyBase IMP/IDA/IGI annotations.

title: Guanylate cyclase in Dictyostelium discoideum with the topology of mammalian adenylate cyclase.
review_notes: Original cloning and characterization of DdGCA; PubMed-verified, establishes topology, catalytic activity, and redundancy with a second guanylyl cyclase.

title: GTPgammaS regulation of a 12-transmembrane guanylyl cyclase is retained after mutation to an adenylyl cyclase.
review_notes: Direct assay of GCA activity and regulation; supports the guanylate cyclase MF (IDA) annotation.

title: Characterization of two unusual guanylyl cyclases from dictyostelium.
review_notes: Defines GCA versus sGC redundancy, membrane localization, expression pattern, and calcium inhibition.

title: Chemotaxis: signalling modules join hands at front and tail.
review_notes: Review framing the cGMP/rear module of chemotaxis; supports downstream myosin and pseudopod annotations.

title: Chemoattractant signaling in dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Broad review of chemoattractant signaling modules; the TAS receptor-guanylyl-cyclase pathway annotation derived from it over-specifies GCA's mechanism.

title: Guanylyl cyclase protein and cGMP product independently control front and back of chemotaxing Dictyostelium cells.
review_notes: Focuses on sGC but establishes the cGMP-myosin rear module to which GCA-derived cGMP contributes.

title: The role of cGMP and the rear of the cell in Dictyostelium chemotaxis and cell streaming.
review_notes: Supports the chemotaxis and lateral pseudopodium retraction annotations via the cGMP rear module.

title: Switching direction in electric-signal-induced cell migration by cyclic guanosine monophosphate and phosphatidylinositol signaling.
review_notes: Supports the electrotaxis and leading-edge annotations for the GCase pathway.

title: Dictyostelium chemotaxis: essential Ras activation and accessory signalling pathways for amplification.
review_notes: Places the guanylyl cyclase pathway as accessory/amplifying for chemotaxis; supports the regulation of chemotaxis non-core call.

title: Intracellular Calcium Responses to External Calcium Stimuli in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Genetic-interaction basis for the NOT calcium-mediated signaling annotation.

title: Receptor-mediated activation of heterotrimeric G-proteins in living cells.
review_notes: FRET between Gα2 and Gβγ in living Dictyostelium cells directly demonstrates receptor-triggered heterotrimer dissociation; supports G-protein activity, heterotrimeric complex membership and receptor coupling.

title: Loss-of-function mutations identified in the Helical domain of the G protein alpha-subunit, G alpha2, of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Loss-of-function screen establishing that Gα2 is essential for the developmental life cycle; supports the aggregation and chemotaxis core processes.

title: Heterotrimeric G-protein shuttling via Gip1 extends the dynamic range of eukaryotic chemotaxis.
review_notes: Establishes the cytosolic reserve pool of the heterotrimeric G protein and Gip1-dependent shuttling to the plasma membrane; supports plasma membrane and cytosol localization annotations.

title: A Gα-Stimulated RapGEF Is a Receptor-Proximal Regulator of Dictyostelium Chemotaxis.
review_notes: Identifies GflB as a Gα2 binding partner and Gα-stimulated Rap1 GEF that couples the cAMP GPCR to Rap1; primary support for the GEF-adaptor core function.

title: MAPK docking motif in the Dictyostelium Gα2 subunit is required for aggregation and transcription factor translocation.
review_notes: Full text available; the Gα2 amino-terminal D-motif is required for cAMP-stimulated GtaC transcription-factor nucleocytoplasmic shuttling and for aggregation; supports the transcription/nuclear-export non-core roles.

title: Soil Amoebae Affect Iron and Chromium Reduction through Preferential Predation between Two Metal-Reducing Bacteria.
review_notes: Environmental-microbiology predation study; cached abstract does not mention Gα2/gpaB, so its support for a Gα2 response-to-bacterium annotation could not be verified.

title: Heterotrimeric G Protein-RasGAP Coupling Drives Adaptation During Chemotaxis.
review_notes: Shows the RasGAP C2GAP1 directly associates with Gα2 (preferentially the activated state) as a G-protein effector; supports the C2GAP1 interaction.

title: Phospholipase C in Dictyostelium discoideum. Identification of stimulatory and inhibitory surface receptors and G-proteins.
review_notes: Gα2-null (fgd A) abolishes cAMP/GTP-analog-stimulated phospholipase C, identifying Gα2 as the stimulatory G protein; supports G protein activity and GTP binding.

title: G protein beta subunit-null mutants are impaired in phagocytosis and chemotaxis due to inappropriate regulation of the actin cytoskeleton.
review_notes: This is a Gβ-null study; it explicitly reports that Gα2-null mutants are NOT impaired in phagocytosis, so it does not support a Gα2 phagocytosis annotation (the phagocytosis phenotype is Gβ-specific).

title: A metabotropic glutamate receptor family gene in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: PubMed-verified abstract (Taniura et al., J Biol Chem 2006). Establishes GrlE identity as an mGluR-family GPCR, plasma membrane localization, and the early-development/chemotaxis phenotype used for the localization and early-development annotations.

title: GABA induces terminal differentiation of Dictyostelium through a GABAB receptor.
review_notes: PubMed-verified abstract (Anjard & Loomis, Development 2006). Directly identifies GrlE as the GABA receptor driving terminal differentiation and provides the core GABA receptor and GABA signaling annotations; glutamate is described as a competitive inhibitor.

title: Cell type specificity of a diffusible inducer is determined by a GATA family transcription factor.
review_notes: Full text cached and verified; establishes GtaC as a DIF-regulated GATA factor controlling a subset of cell-type-specific (stalk-related) differentiation events.

title: Nucleocytoplasmic shuttling of a GATA transcription factor functions as a development timer.
review_notes: Full text cached and verified; the definitive mechanistic study of GtaC as a cAMP-decoding developmental timer.

title: Leaps and lulls in the developmental transcriptome of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Full text cached; provides fine-scale developmental expression profiling supporting gtaC's aggregation-phase expression and master-regulator status (basis of the IEP annotation).

title: The GATA transcription factor GtaC regulates early developmental gene expression dynamics in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Full text cached and verified; direct genome-wide ChIP-seq/RNA-seq evidence for GtaC's core DNA-binding and transcriptional-regulatory functions.

title: An atypical MAPK regulates translocation of a GATA transcription factor in response to chemoattractant stimulation.
review_notes: Full text cached and verified; establishes Erk2-dependent regulation of GtaC translocation and a negative role of GtaC in folate chemotaxis (basis of the folate chemotaxis annotation).

title: Collective oscillatory signaling in Dictyostelium discoideum acts as a developmental timer initiated by weak coupling of a noisy pulsatile signal.
review_notes: Full text not available in cache (abstract is focused on Hbx5). The GtaC IMP/IDA annotations attributed to this paper (DNA-binding TF activity, nucleus, cytosol) are experimental curator annotations and are corroborated by other cached studies; specific supporting text from this paper could not be verified.

title: Ca(2+) signalling is not required for chemotaxis in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Original characterization of the iplA-null mutant; establishes the channel family placement, the Ca2+-entry defect, and the caveat that InsP3 gating is unproven.

title: Influx of extracellular Ca2+ is necessary for electrotaxis in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; shows iplA is required for chemoattractant-induced Ca2+ but dispensable for electrotaxis-associated Ca2+ influx.

title: The inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor is required to signal autophagic cell death.
review_notes: Establishes the ER Ca2+-efflux channel mechanism and the ACD/cellulose phenotypes of iplA-null cells.

title: Arachidonic acid is a chemoattractant for Dictyostelium discoideum cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; supports an iplA role in arachidonate (AA) chemotaxis via extracellular Ca2+.

title: Mechano-chemical signaling maintains the rapid movement of Dictyostelium cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; UniProt attributes the intracellular-store Ca2+ burst component to IplA (with PMID:35859163).

title: The IplA Ca2+ channel of Dictyostelium discoideum is necessary for chemotaxis mediated through Ca2+, but not through cAMP, and has a fundamental role in natural aggregation.
review_notes: Defines the selective role of IplA in Ca2+-gradient chemotaxis and natural aggregation; also the source of the plasma-membrane and vesicle-membrane IDA localizations.

title: Microtubule-Mediated Inositol Lipid Signaling Plays Critical Roles in Regulation of Blebbing.
review_notes: Supports an iplA role in bleb regulation among several Ca2+/lipid-signaling components.

title: An endogenous chemorepellent directs cell movement by inhibiting pseudopods at one side of cells.
review_notes: Supports the G protein-coupled chemorepellent (AprA) signaling annotation.

title: An Autocrine Negative Feedback Loop Inhibits Dictyostelium discoideum Proliferation through Pathways Including IP3/Ca(2).
review_notes: Supports the negative-regulation-of-proliferation (asexual reproduction) annotation via the IP3/Ca2+ feedback loop.

title: Calcium responses to external mechanical stimuli in the multicellular stage of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Supports the cellular-response-to-mechanical-stimulus and ER Ca2+-release roles of IplA in the multicellular (slug) stage.

title: Intracellular Calcium Responses to External Calcium Stimuli in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Recent GCaMP3 imaging study; supports the calcium-mediated signaling role of IplA and the ER Ca2+-release channel identity.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment analysis of the IplA IP3-gated channel hypothesis
review_notes: Independent OpenScientist function-assignment run (3 iterations). Verdict PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. The IP3R/RyR-superfamily intracellular Ca2+-release channel identity is well supported (RIH domain, IP3-receptor-binding-core armadillo fold, six-TM pore; single-copy in the genome, so no paralog confusion). The specific IP3-GATED molecular function is NOT directly supported - the metazoan MIR domain is absent, 0 of 9 canonical IP3-coordinating residues map, no primary study demonstrates IP3 binding or IP3-gated conductance, and the literature hedges ("putative"), with a competing Ca2+-sensing interpretation. Directly corroborates this review's MODIFY of GO:0005220 (IP3-gated channel) to the generic GO:0005262 (calcium channel activity). Best-supported MF is a generalized calcium channel term pending direct IP3-binding data.

title: LvsA, a protein related to the mouse beige protein, is required for cytokinesis in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Supports myosin II furrow localization during cytokinesis (studied via the LvsA cytokinesis mutant).

title: Dictyostelium myosin bipolar thick filament formation: importance of charge and specific domains of the myosin rod.
review_notes: Directly supports myosin II self-assembly into bipolar thick filaments and its regulation.

title: Subsecond reorganization of the actin network in cell motility and chemotaxis.
review_notes: Abstract concerns actin-network dynamics and does not establish a myosin II role; basis of the two IMP annotations to mhcA could not be verified.

title: Actin-based propulsive forces and myosin-II-based contractile forces in migrating Dictyostelium cells.
review_notes: Direct force-microscopy evidence for myosin II motor activity driving rear/pseudopod retraction during migration.

title: A mechanosensory system governs myosin II accumulation in dividing cells.
review_notes: Establishes myosin II as a component of the cortical mechanosensor.

title: Expression and characterization of a functional myosin head fragment in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Direct evidence of the actin-based motor activity of the myosin II head.

title: Proteomic profiling of the extracellular matrix (slime sheath) of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Slime-sheath proteomic detection of a cytoplasmic motor likely reflects contamination rather than genuine ECM localization.

title: Gene replacement in Dictyostelium: generation of myosin null mutants.
review_notes: Genetic proof that mhcA is required for cytokinesis and later development.

title: Disruption of the Dictyostelium myosin heavy chain gene by homologous recombination.
review_notes: Classic genetic proof of the myosin II cytokinesis requirement.

title: Talin force coupling underlies eukaryotic cell-substrate adhesion.
review_notes: Focuses on talin-A/SibA force coupling; a direct myosin II interaction could not be verified from the available text.

title: Targeted disruption of the Dictyostelium RMLC gene produces cells defective in cytokinesis and development.
review_notes: Concerns the regulatory myosin light chain (mlcR); the cited calcium-dependent ATPase activity for the heavy chain could not be verified from the abstract.

title: Myosin dynamics in live Dictyostelium cells.
review_notes: Live-cell evidence for the dynamic localization of myosin II to furrow, rear cortex and pseudopod tips.

title: Dictyostelium cell shape generation requires myosin II.
review_notes: Establishes the cortical-tension/cell-shape role of myosin II.

title: Seven Dictyostelium discoideum phosphodiesterases degrade three pools of cAMP and cGMP.
review_notes: PMC full text available and read; directly characterizes PdsA (DdPDE1) function, localization, dual specificity, and the pdsA-null aggregation phenotype.

title: The group migration of Dictyostelium cells is regulated by extracellular chemoattractant degradation.
review_notes: Garcia et al. 2009 (Mol Biol Cell). Full text IS cached (content_type full_text_html) and directly localizes the intracellular pool of PdsA to the ER; the ER annotation is now ACCEPTed with a verbatim quote. The negated plasma-membrane call is kept UNDECIDED because a positive plasma-membrane annotation (PMID:9168471) for the cell-surface form coexists, i.e. distinct pools.

title: Binding of inhibitor alters kinetic and physical properties of extracellular cyclic AMP phosphodiesterase from Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Establishes the PdsA-inhibitor (PdiA) interaction and DTT-mediated relief of inhibition; supports the protein-binding and response-to-DTT annotations.

title: Role of cAMP-dependent protein kinase during growth and early development of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; pkaC-null cells show reduced discoidin expression, supporting a positive gene-regulatory role for PKA.

title: DdPK3, which plays essential roles during Dictyostelium development, encodes the catalytic subunit of cAMP-dependent protein kinase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; definitive genetic/biochemical assignment of pkaC as the PKA catalytic subunit and its requirement for culmination.

title: Chemoattractant signaling in dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Review of Dictyostelium chemoattractant signaling; cited for cytosolic localization (TAS). Abstract does not itself detail pkaC localization.

title: Molecular and functional analysis of the dictyostelium centrosome.
review_notes: Centrosome review cited (TAS) for centrosome localization; the cached abstract does not mention PKA/pkaC, so the localization claim is unverified here.

title: STAT signaling in Dictyostelium development.
review_notes: A review focused on Dd-STAT proteins; the cached abstract does not establish a pkaC-specific culmination role. Culmination dependence on PKA is instead well supported by PMID:1332055 and PMID:8565818.

title: Curcumin inhibits development and cell adhesion in Dictyostelium discoideum: Implications for YakA signaling and GST enzyme function.
review_notes: Cached abstract concerns curcumin effects on YakA/GST and does not mention PKA/pkaC; the pkaC 'response to curcumin' IDA annotation cannot be verified from this text.

title: An unusual adenosine cyclic 3',5'-phosphate-dependent protein kinase from Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: PubMed-verified biochemical characterization (de Gunzburg et al. 1984) of the R-C holoenzyme; supports the complex and catalytic/regulatory-binding annotations.

title: Adenylate cyclase A acting on PKA mediates induction of stalk formation by cyclic diguanylate at the Dictyostelium organizer.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; places PKA as the terminal effector of the c-di-GMP/ACA stalk-induction pathway at the organizer.

title: Protein kinase A regulates the Ras, Rap1 and TORC2 pathways in response to the chemoattractant cAMP in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Establishes PKA's role in spatiotemporal control of chemotactic signaling via Ras/Rap1/TORC2.

title: The transcription factor Spores Absent A is a PKA dependent inducer of Dictyostelium sporulation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Places PKA upstream of the SpaA transcription factor in the sporulation gene-expression pathway.

title: cAMP-dependent protein kinase differentially regulates prestalk and prespore differentiation during Dictyostelium development.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; demonstrates differential PKA control of prestalk versus prespore differentiation.

title: An unusual catalytic subunit for the cAMP-dependent protein kinase of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; identifies the unusually large PkaC as the catalytic subunit and documents R-C association.

title: Induction of terminal differentiation of Dictyostelium by cAMP-dependent protein kinase and opposing effects of intracellulr and extracellular cAMP on stalk cell differentiation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; PKA is sufficient to drive terminal (spore/stalk) differentiation.

title: A molecular network that produces spontaneous oscillations in excitable cells of Dictyostelium.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; models PKA as an essential negative-feedback node of the cAMP-relay oscillator.

title: CulB, a putative ubiquitin ligase subunit, regulates prestalk cell differentiation and morphogenesis in Dictyostelium spp.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; genetic-interaction evidence that pkaR disruption (PKA activation) promotes stalk differentiation.

title: Mutation of protein kinase A causes heterochronic development of Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Key genetic evidence that the R subunit inhibits the catalytic subunit; source of the rdeC mutant.

title: Surrogate hosts: protozoa and invertebrates as models for studying pathogen-host interactions.
review_notes: This review of protozoan/invertebrate surrogate hosts does not document a pkaR sporulation phenotype and does not appear to support the GO:0030435 sporulation annotation it is cited for; likely a mis-attributed reference.

title: Chemoattractant signaling in dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Signaling review; source of the TAS cytosol localization, contextual rather than gene-specific.

title: Molecular and functional analysis of the dictyostelium centrosome.
review_notes: Centrosome proteome review supporting the TAS centrosome localization; secondary localization.

title: Culmination in Dictyostelium is regulated by the cAMP-dependent protein kinase.
review_notes: Establishes the PKA requirement for culmination and stalk cell differentiation.

title: A cAMP-dependent protein kinase is present in differentiating Dictyostelium discoideum cells.
review_notes: Biochemical demonstration of high-affinity cAMP binding and cAMP-reversible inhibition of the catalytic subunit.

title: Multiple roles for cAMP-dependent protein kinase during Dictyostelium development.
review_notes: Structure-function mutagenesis of the R subunit and multiple developmental roles of PKA.

title: Expression and properties of the regulatory subunit of Dictyostelium cAMP-dependent protein kinase encoded by lambda gt11 cDNA clones.
review_notes: Recombinant expression confirms cAMP binding and catalytic-subunit inhibition are intrinsic R-subunit properties.

title: An unusual adenosine cyclic 3',5'-phosphate-dependent protein kinase from Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Original biochemical characterization of the unusual R-C dimeric holoenzyme and single cAMP-binding site.

title: Adenylate cyclase A acting on PKA mediates induction of stalk formation by cyclic diguanylate at the Dictyostelium organizer.
review_notes: Places PKA as a downstream effector in the c-di-GMP stalk induction pathway.

title: Curcumin affects gene expression and reactive oxygen species via a PKA dependent mechanism in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Narrow condition-specific PKA-dependent response to curcumin.

title: Protein kinase A is a positive regulator of spore coat gene transcription in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Direct evidence that PKA positively regulates spore coat gene transcription.

title: An unusual catalytic subunit for the cAMP-dependent protein kinase of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Characterizes the catalytic subunit pkaC and confirms R-C physical association and cAMP-reversible inhibition.

title: Induction of terminal differentiation of Dictyostelium by cAMP-dependent protein kinase and opposing effects of intracellulr and extracellular cAMP on stalk cell differentiation.
review_notes: PKA activity drives terminal differentiation and cell-type gene expression.

title: A cAMP-phosphodiesterase controls PKA-dependent differentiation.
review_notes: Establishes the RegA-PKA-R interaction and the PKA terminal- differentiation checkpoint.

title: Tumor suppressor PTEN mediates sensing of chemoattractant gradients.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary study establishing PTEN rear-membrane localization and its role in gradient sensing; abstract supports the cited claims.

title: Spatial and temporal regulation of 3-phosphoinositides by PI 3-kinase and PTEN mediates chemotaxis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes reciprocal PI3K/PTEN localization during chemotaxis.

title: Novel mechanism of PTEN regulation by its phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate binding motif is critical for chemotaxis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the PI(4,5)P2-binding motif both localizes PTEN and regulates its activity. The GO:0034485 5-phosphatase annotation linked to this PMID conflicts with PTEN's 3-phosphatase mechanism and could not be verified from the abstract.

title: PTEN plays a role in the suppression of lateral pseudopod formation during Dictyostelium motility and chemotaxis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; defines PTEN's core role in suppressing lateral pseudopods.

title: PTEN is a mechanosensing signal transducer for myosin II localization in Dictyostelium cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; links PTEN to posterior/furrow localization, myosin II recruitment, and cytokinesis.

title: Disruption of PKB signaling restores polarity to cells lacking tumor suppressor PTEN.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; demonstrates that PTEN's effects on polarity, cytokinesis and chemotaxis are mediated through PKB (PkbA) substrate phosphorylation.

title: Single-molecule imaging of PI(4,5)P(2) and PTEN in vitro reveals a positive feedback mechanism for PTEN membrane binding.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; in vitro and in vivo single-molecule evidence for PI(4,5)P2-dependent stabilization of PTEN at the rear membrane.

title: Gradients of PI(4,5)P(2) and PI(3,5)P(2) Jointly Participate in Shaping the Back State of Dictyostelium Cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; in vitro liposome binding supports PTEN PI(3,5)P2 and PI(4,5)P2 binding, though the paper's main focus is the novel back protein Teep1.

title: PTEN and the PTEN-like phosphatase CnrN have both distinct and overlapping roles in a Dictyostelium chemorepulsion pathway.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; PTEN and the PTEN-like phosphatase CnrN have distinct and overlapping roles in AprA chemorepulsion.

title: Starvation promotes Dictyostelium development by relieving PufA inhibition of PKA translation through the YakA kinase pathway.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary paper (Souza, da Silva and Kuspa, Development 1999) that defines PufA as a PUF-family translational repressor of PKA-C mRNA and establishes the YakA-PufA-PKA axis. Abstract-only cache; all supporting text quotes are verbatim from the abstract.

title: RasC is required for optimal activation of adenylyl cyclase and Akt/PKB during aggregation.
review_notes: Foundational rasC-null study establishing RasC's role in cAMP relay (ACA activation) and PKB activation during aggregation; PMID/title verified against the cached full text.

title: Chemoattractant-induced Ras activation during Dictyostelium aggregation.
review_notes: Directly demonstrates cAMP-induced RasC activation via an RBD-binding assay; supports GTP-binding and G-protein activity.

title: Loss of the Dictyostelium RasC protein alters vegetative cell size, motility and endocytosis.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; documents vegetative-cell phenotypes and shows cytokinesis/division rate are unaffected in rasC-null cells.

title: Delineation of the roles played by RasG and RasC in cAMP-dependent signal transduction during the early development of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Defines the division of labor between RasC (ACA/relay) and RasG (chemotaxis) using isogenic single and double null strains.

title: Cyclic AMP signalling in Dictyostelium: G-proteins activate separate Ras pathways using specific RasGEFs.
review_notes: Establishes RasGEFA-RasC specificity in vitro and in vivo and the RasC-to-ACA / RasG-to-chemotaxis division.

title: Nanovesicles released by Dictyostelium cells: a potential carrier for drug delivery.
review_notes: High-throughput vesicle proteome; RasC recovery here does not indicate a functional vesicle role.

title: A Ras signaling complex controls the RasC-TORC2 pathway and directed cell migration.
review_notes: Establishes leading-edge, spatiotemporally controlled RasC-TORC2 signaling via the Sca1 scaffold complex.

title: Ras-mediated activation of the TORC2-PKB pathway is critical for chemotaxis.
review_notes: Genetic plus in vitro reconstitution evidence that activated RasC is an upstream regulator of TORC2; TORC2 binds the activated form of RasC.

title: Dictyostelium lipid droplets host novel proteins.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment analysis of the SpiA SCAMP trafficking hypothesis
review_notes: Independent OpenScientist function-assignment run (3 iterations). Verdict PARTIALLY SUPPORTED / over-annotated on the trafficking claim. SCAMP family membership is strongly supported by concordant orthogonal signatures (Pfam PF04144, InterPro IPR007273, PANTHER PTHR10687:SF2, a canonical four-transmembrane core, ~28 percent identity to the five human SCAMPs), and SpiA is the single SCAMP gene in the D. discoideum genome, so the family call is not paralog-confused. However the vesicular-trafficking function is homology-only (all trafficking GO terms are IBA/IEA), SpiA lacks the N-terminal NPF motifs that drive canonical SCAMP trafficking, and the only experimentally demonstrated role is the structural spore-coat / spore-viability function. Concordant with this review keeping the trafficking terms non-core and the spore-coat role core.
