title: A glycoprotein involved in aggregation of D. discoideum is distributed on the cell surface in a nonrandom fashion favoring cell junctions.
review_notes: Immuno-EM shows gp150 is closely associated with the plasma membrane and enriched at cell-cell contact/junction sites.

title: LagC is required for cell-cell interactions that are essential for cell-type differentiation in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Identifies lagC and shows null cells arrest at the loose aggregate stage with defective cell-type differentiation and sporulation.

title: High-throughput analysis of spatio-temporal dynamics in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Full-text screen; independently corroborates a tipA developmental defect at slug/culmination stages, supporting the HMP sorocarp development annotation. It does not address molecular function.

title: Sorting of the initial cell types in Dictyostelium is dependent on the tipA gene.
review_notes: Primary characterization of tipA. Cached copy is abstract-only (full_text_available false); the abstract establishes the developmental and cell-sorting role but does not describe subcellular localization, hence the cytoplasm IDA cannot be verified from available text.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment analysis of the TipA PP2C phosphatase hypothesis
review_notes: Independent OpenScientist function-assignment run (3 iterations). Verdict PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. The PP2C/PPM domain membership is well supported (InterPro IPR001932 / IPR053287, PANTHER PTHR21586, confident AlphaFold PP2C fold), but the canonical catalytic-His motif (DGHxG) is absent across the entire TIPA-specific phosphatase family (0/100 members) while the metal-coordinating aspartate scaffold is conserved (~69-86 percent). Best supported computed molecular function is metal ion binding; protein Ser/Thr phosphatase activity should NOT be asserted with experimental confidence. Concordant with this review leaving molecular_function unasserted. Lead - TipA is likely a metal-binding but catalytically divergent (pseudo)PP2C; requires an enzyme assay to resolve.

title: Starvation promotes Dictyostelium development by relieving PufA inhibition of PKA translation through the YakA kinase pathway.
review_notes: Primary Kuspa-lab study establishing the YakA-PufA-PKA-C axis; abstract verified against PubMed.

title: The protein kinase YakA regulates g-protein-linked signaling responses during growth and development of Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Provides the direct cytosolic localization and dual-specificity DYRK homology; abstract verified against PubMed.

title: Role for YakA, cAMP, and protein kinase A in regulation of stress responses of Dictyostelium discoideum cells.
review_notes: Full-text open-access primary study; establishes YakA/cAMP/PKA in oxidative, nitrosative and heat stress responses.

title: Chemoattractant signaling in dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Review of Dictyostelium chemoattractant signaling used as a traceable source for signal-transduction, chemotaxis, aggregation and cytosol annotations; abstract-only in cache, so specific YakA claims are supported by primary papers.

title: High-throughput analysis of spatio-temporal dynamics in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: High-throughput mutant phenotyping placing yakA among developmentally null genes; supports sorocarp development annotation.

title: KeaA, a Dictyostelium Kelch-domain protein that regulates the response to stress and development.
review_notes: Study of the YakA-pathway suppressor keaA; corroborates YakA's roles in stress survival and cAMP-signaling gene induction.

title: Bio-electrospraying and aerodynamically assisted bio-jetting the model eukaryotic Dictyostelium discoideum: assessing stress and developmental competency post treatment.
review_notes: Uses yakA as a stress-response marker gene; supports the expression-based hyperosmotic-response annotation but not a core function.

title: Glutathione initiates the development of Dictyostelium discoideum through the regulation of YakA.
review_notes: Places YakA downstream of glutathione and upstream of PKA-C/ACA/cAR1 induction; supports positive regulation of developmental gene expression.

title: Response of Dictyostelium discoideum to UV-C and involvement of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase.
review_notes: yakA analysed as a UV-C-responsive developmental gene; supports the non-core response-to-UV-C annotation.

title: Curcumin inhibits development and cell adhesion in Dictyostelium discoideum: Implications for YakA signaling and GST enzyme function.
review_notes: Pharmacological study; supports the non-core response-to-curcumin annotation via effects on yakA signaling.

title: YakA, a protein kinase required for the transition from growth to development in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Founding paper defining YakA as the growth-to-development kinase; provides the direct in vitro kinase-activity evidence.

title: Blinded OpenScientist function-assignment report (TreeGrafter audit)
review_notes: Blinded run independently refuted the term: squid ADAR2 is a dsRNA/mRNA adenosine deaminase (three dsRBDs upstream of the deaminase domain), not a tRNA-specific ADAT; the ancestral node carried both ADAR and ADAT terms. Blinded OpenScientist function-assignment run: given only the propagated term (the prior curation action withheld), it independently reached the same conclusion as this review. Corroborating evidence, not a primary source.

title: Drosophila HNF4 regulates lipid mobilization and beta-oxidation.
review_notes: Full text cached and verified; yip2 appears in the beta-oxidation gene list and among the most highly dHNF4-down-regulated genes. Supports the fatty acid beta-oxidation (GO:0006635) annotation for the fly gene. Transcriptional/genetic evidence, not a direct enzyme assay.

title: An inventory of peroxisomal proteins and pathways in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache (full_text_available: false). A prediction/inventory study; supports mitochondrial (not peroxisomal) targeting of Acaa as a bioinformatic inference, with no gene-specific experimental validation.

title: UniProtKB A1ZBJ2 (Acadvl / CG7461, Drosophila melanogaster) TrEMBL record
review_notes: Local UniProt record for A1ZBJ2; the entry is unreviewed (TrEMBL) and its functional block is ARBA/rule-derived, but the family assignment, EC numbers, cofactor and localization are internally consistent and concordant with the well-characterized human ortholog P49748 and with the fly VLCAD subfamily/CDD assignments.

title: Mapping organelle proteins and protein complexes in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false); the LOPIT method and mitochondrial assignment underpin the HDA mitochondrion annotation. Method is verifiable from the abstract.

title: An inventory of peroxisomal proteins and pathways in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Citation is correct, but the peroxisomal prediction it supports is contradicted by the mitochondrial identity of the ACAT1/T2 subfamily and the direct LOPIT mitochondrial assignment; the peroxisome annotation is marked over-annotated.

title: Glia fuel neurons with locally synthesized ketone bodies to sustain memory under starvation.
review_notes: Full text available and read; directly establishes the fly Acat1 ortholog identity and its neuronal ketone-body catabolic (oxidation) role. Supports the ketone-body-catabolism core; the GOA NAS annotations to ketone-body BIOSYNTHESIS from this paper are the weaker reading for Acat1 and are kept as non-core.

title: Characterizing fatty acid oxidation genes in Drosophila.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified primary research (G3 Bethesda 2025, PMC12341901); full text available. Directly establishes Arc42 as the functional ACADS ortholog in Drosophila via CRISPR knockout and acylcarnitine profiling (elevated C4). Basis for the FlyBase IMP annotation on GO:0033539. Note the legacy fly name "Activator-recruited cofactor subunit 42" is a misnomer; the closest human symbol is ACADS.

title: Mapping organelle proteins and protein complexes in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: High-throughput organelle proteomics; source of the HDA mitochondrion localization for CG4598.

title: An inventory of peroxisomal proteins and pathways in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: PubMed-verified Drosophila peroxisomal proteome inventory (Faust et al. 2012). Cited by FlyBase as the reference for the ISS annotations (WITH UniProtKB:Q709F0) to the general ACAD activity and fatty acid beta-oxidation terms. Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available: false) and does not itself name CG4860; the ISS transfers only the family-level (not short-chain-specific) function, which is consistent with the evidence.

title: Characterizing fatty acid oxidation genes in Drosophila.
review_notes: Primary research paper (Geronazzo et al. 2025, G3), full text available and cached. This is the only in vivo, fly-specific functional study of CG4860. It directly tests CG4860 by CRISPR knockout and acylcarnitine profiling and shows that CG4860 loss does not phenocopy human SCAD (ACADS) deficiency, whereas the paralog Arc42 does. This is the key evidence for treating the short-chain/butyryl-CoA substrate-specificity annotations on CG4860 as over-specific and unverified for this paralog.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment hypothesis: CG4860 (Q9VGC2) short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity (GO:0016937)
review_notes: In-repo OpenScientist report for the chain-length-specificity hypothesis. Verdict over-specific (retain general acyl-CoA dehydrogenase GO:0003995, flag GO:0016937) - independently corroborates our MODIFY. The binding-pocket residue analysis (Leu-to-Thr at RIGIA+8) is a computational lead from this report; the in vivo disambiguation it also relies on (PMID:40519079) is independently cited and verbatim-checked in this review.

title: Genetic analysis of Drosophila melanogaster susceptibility to intestinal Vibrio cholerae infection.
review_notes: Vibrio cholerae susceptibility screen; basis for the (non-core) defense-response IMP annotation. The connection to Dci's enzymatic function is indirect.

title: An inventory of peroxisomal proteins and pathways in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Computational peroxisomal-proteome inventory; source of the ISM peroxisome prediction. Abstract-only in cache. Consistent with the UniProt peroxisomal assignment for Dci.

title: An inventory of peroxisomal proteins and pathways in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Computational peroxisomal-proteome inventory; source of the ISM peroxisome prediction and the NAS beta-oxidation call. Contributes to the unresolved mito-vs-peroxisome localization of fly Ech1 (human ECH1 is peroxisomal). Abstract-only in cache.

title: Clinical, biochemical and metabolic characterisation of a mild form of human short-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase deficiency: significance of increased N-acetyl-S-(2-carboxypropyl)cysteine excretion.
review_notes: Key biochemical characterization of the human ortholog ECHS1 (purified enzyme, substrate specificity across five enoyl-CoA thioesters). Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false); grounds the enoyl-CoA hydratase activity annotation and the core function for the fly gene by orthology.

title: Ectopic protein lysine methacrylation contributes to defects caused by loss of HIBCH or ECHS1.
review_notes: Organism-matched (Drosophila) evidence: fly tissues lacking the ECHS1 ortholog show elevated lysine methacrylation and eye degeneration, mechanistically linking Echs1 loss to valine-pathway intermediate accumulation. Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false). Supports the valine catabolism / beta-oxidation core functions.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment hypothesis: Echs1 (Q7JR58) enoyl-CoA hydratase activity / substrate breadth (GO:0004300)
review_notes: In-repo OpenScientist report for the substrate-breadth hypothesis. Verdict strongly supported - confirms the fly crotonase pocket is not narrowed relative to human ECHS1, underpinning the dual hydratase / valine-catabolism core functions. The residue-level conservation is a computational lead from this report; the in vivo methacrylyl-CoA evidence (PMID:40056416) and the substrate-specificity framing (PMID:26251176) are independently cited and verbatim-checked in this review.

title: Enigma, a mitochondrial protein affecting lifespan and oxidative stress response in Drosophila.
review_notes: PubMed-verified foundational Drosophila paper. Directly supports mitochondrial localization and the essential/lipid/oxidative-stress/lifespan phenotypes. Its beta-oxidation interpretation is explicitly indirect and predates the ACAD9 CI-assembly-factor paradigm; the metabolic phenotypes are equally consistent with complex I / OXPHOS deficiency.

title: Proteomics reveals novel Drosophila seminal fluid proteins transferred at mating.
review_notes: PubMed-verified seminal-fluid proteomics screen. Egm's presence in seminal fluid is an expression/ proteomic detection (HEP); it does not establish a functional role in insemination, so the GO:0007320 annotation is treated as an over-annotation.

title: Using natural variation in Drosophila to discover previously unknown endoplasmic reticulum stress genes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified DGRP natural-variation study. Egm is a genetic-association candidate with a putative lipid-metabolism link to ER-stress survival; the connection is plausibly indirect (via mitochondrial/ lipid metabolism) rather than a dedicated ER-stress function.

title: Proteomic mapping in live Drosophila tissues using an engineered ascorbate peroxidase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified APEX matrix proteomics. Supports the mitochondrial matrix localization annotation, consistent with a peripheral, matrix-facing inner-membrane MCIA factor.

title: Dissecting the concordant and disparate roles of NDUFAF3 and NDUFAF4 in mitochondrial complex I biogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The primary Drosophila source establishing Egm/dACAD9 as an MCIA-complex CI assembly factor (PP-b/ND2 sub-module), directly supporting the core CI-assembly annotations.

title: Analysis of dominant enhancers and suppressors of activated Notch in Drosophila.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only (full text unavailable); the specific Egm/CG9006 allele data underlying the IGI annotation cannot be verified here. This is an experimental FlyBase genetic-interaction annotation whose full text was read by the curator; the eye requirement is independently consistent with Egm-null eye-clone phenotypes (PMID:16434470).

title: Characterization of the Drosophila melanogaster mitochondrial proteome.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only; the abstract does not name Mcad, so no protein-level verbatim quote is extractable. Supports the HDA mitochondrion localization; not core.

title: Mapping organelle proteins and protein complexes in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only; the abstract does not name Mcad, so no protein-level verbatim quote is extractable. Supports the HDA mitochondrion localization; not core.

title: Phosphorylation of MCAD selectively rescues PINK1 deficiencies in behavior and metabolism.
review_notes: Full text available (PMC5935071); the sole primary experimental study on fly Mcad and the source of the EXP/IDA/IMP annotations. Directly supports the core medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase MF, beta-oxidation BP, and mitochondrial matrix / cytosol localization.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment hypothesis: Mcad (Q9VSA3) medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity (GO:0070991)
review_notes: In-repo OpenScientist report for the medium-chain-specificity hypothesis. Verdict supported - corroborates our ACCEPT of GO:0070991 via substrate-cavity residue and AlphaFold geometry analysis. The residue/geometry claims are computational leads from this report; the in vivo fly evidence (PMID:29563254) is independently cited and verbatim-checked in this review.

title: UniProtKB - Q9VSA3 (ACADM_DROME) Medium-chain specific acyl-CoA dehydrogenase, mitochondrial
review_notes: Local UniProt record used to ground molecular function (EC 1.3.8.7, FAD cofactor), localization, and family assignment. Reaction details propagated by similarity from human MCAD (P11310); fly-specific experimental support is from PMID:29563254.

title: Characterization of the Drosophila melanogaster mitochondrial proteome.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Large-scale mitochondrial proteome study; supports the general mitochondrion localization only.

title: Mapping organelle proteins and protein complexes in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Organelle-mapping proteomics; supports the general mitochondrion localization only.

title: Genetic screen in Drosophila melanogaster uncovers a novel set of genes required for embryonic epithelial repair.
review_notes: Abstract/full-abstract cache. Supports only a high-throughput screen-hit (HMP) wound-healing phenotype, treated here as pleiotropic/non-core rather than a direct molecular role.

title: Impaired fatty acid oxidation in a Drosophila model of mitochondrial trifunctional protein (MTP) deficiency.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache but the abstract directly and unambiguously establishes the fly MTP alpha subunit's role in long-chain fatty acid beta-oxidation via loss-of-function phenotypes. Key functional reference for this gene.

title: An inventory of peroxisomal proteins and pathways in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Supports a secondary peroxisomal localization; the abstract does not name Mtpalpha explicitly (the curator had the full inventory). Canonical location remains mitochondrial.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment hypothesis: Mtpalpha (Q8IPE8) peroxisome (GO:0005777)
review_notes: In-repo OpenScientist report generated for the mitochondrion-vs-peroxisome hypothesis. Verdict SUPPORTED (retain peroxisome). Its underlying primary source PMID:22758915 is abstract-only in our cache, so the isoform/PTS1 mechanism is recorded as an independent computational lead attributed to this report, not asserted as verbatim from the paper. Kept as a non-core (secondary) localization pending isoform-resolved experimental confirmation.

title: UniProt entry Q8IPE8 (Mtpalpha, Trifunctional enzyme subunit alpha, mitochondrial)
review_notes: Local UniProt record used to anchor the domain/architecture, localization and complex claims. Enzymatic and MLCL-acyltransferase details are ARBA-inferred, not fly experimental.

title: Mapping organelle proteins and protein complexes in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Supports mitochondrial localization of Mtpbeta as a high-throughput organelle-proteomics assignment; the specific protein call is in the full dataset, not the abstract.

title: Impaired fatty acid oxidation in a Drosophila model of mitochondrial trifunctional protein (MTP) deficiency.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full text not available). Directly establishes the in vivo beta-oxidation function of the Drosophila Mtpbeta gene through loss-of-function genetics and acylcarnitine biomarker accumulation.

title: An inventory of peroxisomal proteins and pathways in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Prediction-based (ISM) mitochondrion localization; consistent with the experimental HDA annotation but lower confidence and tangential to the paper's peroxisome focus.

title: Axon guidance of Drosophila SNb motoneurons depends on the cooperative action of muscular Krüppel and neuronal capricious activities.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; establishes Caps as a cell-surface recognition molecule regulating the RP5 motoneuron-muscle 12 connection. Directly supports the axon-guidance annotations.

title: Size isn't everything.
review_notes: Abstract-only Bioessays review on tissue size/shape control; the abstract does not mention caps or cell migration. It is the TAS basis for GO:0016477 but is only background/contextual for caps - the real support for a migration role comes from the tracheal study (PMID:16764850).

title: Pattern formation in the Drosophila wing: The development of the veins.
review_notes: Abstract-only Bioessays review on wing-vein patterning; the abstract does not mention caps. Cited as NAS support for GO:0007155 (cell adhesion); the general adhesion function is correct for caps but is not directly supported by this review - a weak/likely-inappropriate NAS citation, adjudicated identically in the trn review, which carries the same GOA row.

title: Regulation of layer-specific targeting by reciprocal expression of a cell adhesion molecule, capricious.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache but content-verified: demonstrates Caps homophilic adhesion in S2 cells and reciprocal R8/R7 layer-specific targeting. Supports the homophilic-adhesion MF and photoreceptor-targeting annotations.

title: Distinct functions of the leucine-rich repeat transmembrane proteins capricious and tartan in the Drosophila tracheal morphogenesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; shows Caps on bridge-cells instructing dorsal-trunk branch fusion and requiring both extra- and intracellular domains. Supports GO:0035147.

title: A screen of cell-surface molecules identifies leucine-rich repeat proteins as key mediators of synaptic target selection.
review_notes: Full text available and reviewed; quantifies trn caps redundancy in ISNb/SNa motor-axon targeting and Caps expression on muscle 12. Supports GO:0008045.

title: A targeted gain-of-function screen identifies genes affecting salivary gland morphogenesis/tubulogenesis in Drosophila.
review_notes: Full text available and reviewed; implicates caps/trn in salivary gland morphogenesis and summarizes the homophilic/heterophilic adhesion-receptor hypothesis. Supports GO:0007436.

title: Target recognition at the tips of postsynaptic filopodia: accumulation and function of Capricious.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache but content-verified: Caps-GFP accumulates at myopodia tips and caps/ caps trn mutants show fewer myopodia-growth-cone contacts and reduced nascent synaptic sites. Supports the muscle cell projection localization and the NMJ synapse-formation contribution.

title: Cytoneme-mediated contact-dependent transport of the Drosophila decapentaplegic signaling protein.
review_notes: Full text available and reviewed; Caps:GFP localizes to ASP cytonemes (enriched at tips) and caps is required for cytoneme-mediated Dpp reception. Supports GO:0035230.

title: Assessing the role of cell-surface molecules in central synaptogenesis in the Drosophila visual system.
review_notes: Full text available and reviewed; reassesses Caps in R8 targeting/synaptogenesis, finding a marginal, non-homophilic guidance role and no major direct role in R8 synapse formation. Important nuance for the synapse-assembly and photoreceptor annotations.

title: Huckebein repressor activity in Drosophila terminal patterning is mediated by Groucho.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified against PubMed. Concerns Huckebein but establishes the shared WRPW/FRPW Groucho-recruitment paradigm for Hairy-related repressors; supports Hairy's transcription corepressor (Groucho) binding at the family level.

title: The origin and evolution of segmentation.
review_notes: General review on the evolution of segmentation used as a TAS source for the pair-rule/periodic-partitioning role; does not itself describe Hairy specifics.

title: Epithelial tube morphology is determined by the polarized growth and delivery of apical membrane.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; a new hairy allele causes salivary tube branching/bulging via prolonged huckebein expression. Supports non-core salivary/tube morphogenesis roles (indirect, via loss of Hairy repression).

title: Tube morphogenesis: no pipe dream in Drosophila.
review_notes: Current Biology dispatch on tube lumen size and vesicle transport; does not describe a Hairy molecular function. Basis of the over-annotated membrane organization TAS for Hairy.

title: The role of class I HLH genes in neural development--have they been overlooked?
review_notes: Generic review of HLH classes in neural development; a weak TAS source for the broad nervous system development annotation. Hairy's neural role is better supported by PMID:7958929.

title: Drosophila Topors is a RING finger-containing protein that functions as a ubiquitin-protein isopeptide ligase for the hairy basic helix-loop-helix repressor protein.
review_notes: Directly on Hairy: dTopors binds the basic region of Hairy and mediates its polyubiquitination, antagonizing repression. Supports MODIFY of a bare protein-binding IPI to ubiquitin protein ligase binding.

title: The evolution of arthropod segmentation mechanisms.
review_notes: Review grouping Hairy among the primary pair-rule genes of Drosophila; TAS source for periodic partitioning, trunk, and posterior-head segmentation.

title: A molecular link between FGF and Dpp signaling in branch-specific migration of the Drosophila trachea.
review_notes: Cached full text (available) contains zero occurrences of the hairy gene name; foregrounds btl, pointed, kni/knrl. Cannot verify the Hairy tracheal IMP from the cache; annotation left UNDECIDED.

title: Physical and genetic interactions link hox function with diverse transcription factors and cell signaling proteins.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; the abstract names Hairy directly as a UBX partner and states the assays (yeast two-hybrid, phage display confirmation, immunoprecipitation for a subset). The GOA row's WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:P83949 = Ubx (hairy-uniprot.txt:131) identifies the partner as a Hox homeodomain DNA-binding transcription factor, so the annotation is a MODIFY to GO:0140297. Peripheral to Hairy's core repressor function, which is recorded in the annotation reason.

title: A Myc-Groucho complex integrates EGF and Notch signaling to regulate neural development.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache concerns the dMyc-Groucho complex and does not name Hairy, hence UNVERIFIED as a statement about the cached text. The partner behind this protein-binding IPI is nonetheless curated input data, since the GOA row carries WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:P16371-2, resolved by the fetched UniProt record as Groucho isoform 2 (hairy-uniprot.txt:129), so the annotation is a MODIFY to GO:0001222 rather than UNDECIDED.

title: Mechanisms underlying hypoxia tolerance in Drosophila melanogaster: hairy as a metabolic switch.
review_notes: Full text available and verified; hairy up-regulated in hypoxia-tolerant flies and acts as a metabolic switch, with hairy mutations reducing tolerance. Supports non-core response-to-hypoxia role.

title: Groucho corepressor functions as a cofactor for the Knirps short-range transcriptional repressor.
review_notes: Full text available; experimental interaction data concern Knirps-Groucho, and Hairy appears only as a long-range-repressor comparison, so the text does not itself document the Hairy interaction. The GOA row supplies the partner as WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:P16371, resolved by the fetched UniProt record as Groucho (hairy-uniprot.txt:128), so the annotation is a MODIFY to GO:0001222 rather than UNDECIDED.

title: Degringolade, a SUMO-targeted ubiquitin ligase, inhibits Hairy/Groucho-mediated repression.
review_notes: Directly on Hairy: the E3 ligase Degringolade binds and ubiquitinates Hairy to inhibit Groucho recruitment. Supports MODIFY of a bare protein-binding IPI to ubiquitin protein ligase binding for the dgrn partner, and to transcription corepressor binding for the CtBP and Groucho partners that the same reference contributes as separate GOA rows (WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:O46036 and UniProtKB:P16371).

title: Origins of context-dependent gene repression by capicua.
review_notes: Full text available and verified; uses a Hairy WRPW/Gro-dependent Sxl-repression assay. Supports Hairy's negative regulation of Pol II transcription.

title: Pair-rule expression of the Drosophila fushi tarazu gene: a nuclear receptor response element mediates the opposing regulatory effects of runt and hairy.
review_notes: Directly on Hairy: Hairy represses ftz through the fDE1 element during blastoderm segmentation. Supports negative regulation of DNA-templated transcription and the segmentation role.

title: Negative regulation of proneural gene activity: hairy is a direct transcriptional repressor of achaete.
review_notes: Key primary paper: establishes Hairy as a sequence-specific DNA-binding transcriptional repressor and identifies achaete as a direct in vivo target controlling PNS/bristle patterning.

title: The WRPW motif of the hairy-related basic helix-loop-helix repressor proteins acts as a 4-amino-acid transcription repression and protein-protein interaction domain.
review_notes: Key primary paper: the WRPW motif is a sufficient active repression domain that recruits Groucho/TLE corepressors. Supports the core repression mechanism and corepressor binding.

title: A network of interacting transcriptional regulators involved in Drosophila neural fate specification revealed by the yeast two-hybrid system.
review_notes: Verified; Hairy interacts directly with Groucho but not with the tested proneural/E(spl)/Da bHLH proteins. Supports transcription corepressor binding and informs the dimerization caveat.

title: Drosophila CtBP: a Hairy-interacting protein required for embryonic segmentation and hairy-mediated transcriptional repression.
review_notes: Directly on Hairy: dCtBP binds a C-terminal region of Hairy and is required for Hairy-mediated repression and segmentation. Supports transcription corepressor binding and the pair-rule role.

title: Groucho and dCtBP mediate separate pathways of transcriptional repression in the Drosophila embryo.
review_notes: Verified; Hairy-mediated repression in vivo depends on the WRPW/Groucho interaction rather than the weak dCtBP motif. Supports Groucho as the dominant corepressor and the core repressor function.

title: UniProtKB P14003 (HAIR_DROME): Protein hairy
review_notes: UniProt record for P14003. Its SUBUNIT block records the gro (Groucho) and Topors interactions and its INTERACTION block resolves the WITH/FROM accessions carried by the GOA protein-binding rows, which is what anchors the corepressor-binding MODIFY calls on the IPI annotations whose cached papers do not themselves name the partner.

title: Rotation and asymmetry of the mitotic spindle direct asymmetric cell division in the developing central nervous system.
review_notes: Live-imaging study of neuroblast spindle rotation and anaphase spindle asymmetry directing ACD; supports the spindle-orientation role. PubMed-verified title/abstract match.

title: Multiple signalling pathways establish cell fate and cell number in Drosophila malpighian tubules.
review_notes: Malpighian tubule tip-cell study (wingless/Notch/Numb). Cached abstract does not name insc; the IMP presumably rests on full-text data not available here. Relevance to insc plausible (asymmetric tip-cell division; insc expressed in Malpighian tubules) but unverified.

title: Mechanism of glia-neuron cell-fate switch in the Drosophila thoracic neuroblast 6-4 lineage.
review_notes: Shows insc (and miranda) mutations disrupt Prospero behavior and the glia-neuron fate switch in NB6-4T; supports cortical/ACD role. Abstract explicitly names inscuteable.

title: Genetics of heart development.
review_notes: Cited (TAS) for insc sensory organ development, but this is a review of cardiac/heart development in zebrafish and Drosophila; the abstract does not mention inscuteable or sensory organs. Appears to be a wrong/mis-applied citation for this annotation; the sensory-organ-development role itself is real but should be sourced to a primary pI/SOP study (e.g. PMID:12526793).

title: Inscuteable-dependent apical localization of the microtubule-binding protein Cornetto suggests a role in asymmetric cell division.
review_notes: Directly on insc; documents apical-cortex localization (interphase-metaphase), the Insc-Cornetto interaction (2-hybrid), and inscuteable-dependent apical protein localization. PubMed-verified.

title: Apical complex genes control mitotic spindle geometry and relative size of daughter cells in Drosophila neuroblast and pI asymmetric divisions.
review_notes: Apical-complex (incl. insc pathway) control of spindle geometry and daughter-cell size in NB and pI (sensory organ precursor) divisions; supports ACD and sensory-organ roles. PubMed-verified.

title: Microtubule-induced Pins/Galphai cortical polarity in Drosophila neuroblasts.
review_notes: Defines the Inscuteable/Par pathway acting from prophase in parallel to a microtubule/Khc-73/Dlg pathway; supports apical Insc/Par localization and function. PubMed-verified.

title: Galphai generates multiple Pins activation states to link cortical polarity and spindle orientation in Drosophila neuroblasts.
review_notes: Full text states Galphai-bound Pins (GoLoco1) recruits Insc to the apical cortex; supports apical localization and the Insc-Pins(raps) relationship. PubMed/PMC-verified.

title: Genetic analysis of Drosophila melanogaster susceptibility to intestinal Vibrio cholerae infection.
review_notes: Genome-wide V. cholerae susceptibility screen; insc mutant increased susceptibility, but the authors explicitly state the immune role was not characterized. Correctly cited for a weak, peripheral IMP. Full text (PMC) confirms the insc hit.

title: Ancestry-independent fate specification and plasticity in the developmental timing of a typical Drosophila neuronal lineage.
review_notes: GOA reference for insc regulation of asymmetric cell division and regulation of nervous system development, but the cached abstract and full text concern the T-box gene mid in the RP2/sib lineage and do not describe insc experiments. Its specific support for these insc annotations could not be verified; the annotated functions are independently well established.

title: On the roles of Notch, Delta, kuzbanian, and inscuteable during the development of Drosophila embryonic neuroblast lineages.
review_notes: Directly on insc; shows lineage/stage-dependent requirement of insc for sibling cell fate specification via ACD feeding differential Notch. PubMed-verified.

title: Inscuteable and NuMA proteins bind competitively to Leu-Gly-Asn repeat-enriched protein (LGN) during asymmetric cell divisions.
review_notes: Crystal structure of Drosophila Pins(LGN) TPR bound to Insc peptide; defines the adaptor bridge (Par3 to Pins/Galphai) and raps-insc complex. Core molecular-function and complex-membership evidence. PMC full text verified.

title: The mutant not enough muscles (nem) reveals reduction of the Drosophila embryonic muscle pattern.
review_notes: nem is an allele of insc (UniProt/FlyBase synonym). Documents somatic-muscle and PNS (chordotonal) defects - peripheral, pleiotropic insc phenotypes. PubMed-verified.

title: inscuteable, a neural precursor gene of Drosophila, encodes a candidate for a cytoskeleton adaptor protein.
review_notes: Founding characterization of insc; apical submembranous localization, candidate cytoskeleton adaptor, expression in neuroblasts/trachea/Malpighian tubules. PubMed-verified.

title: Role of inscuteable in orienting asymmetric cell divisions in Drosophila.
review_notes: Foundational functional study; insc required for spindle orientation and Numb/Prospero localization; apical-cortex localization; ectopic insc reorients spindles. PubMed-verified.

title: Inscuteable and Staufen mediate asymmetric localization and segregation of prospero RNA during Drosophila neuroblast cell divisions.
review_notes: Insc nucleates the apical complex; required for protein localization, spindle orientation, and (with Staufen) prospero RNA localization; apical colocalization. PubMed-verified.

title: Identification of Miranda protein domains regulating asymmetric cortical localization, cargo binding, and cortical release.
review_notes: Miranda-focused study that documents Inscuteable among the apically localized proteins in interphase neuroblasts (apical cortex localization); notes Insc uniquely stays apical while other factors move basally. PubMed-verified.

title: The transmembrane molecule kekkon 1 acts in a feedback loop to negatively regulate the activity of the Drosophila EGF receptor during oogenesis.
review_notes: Founding study identifying Kek1 as an EGFR inhibitor acting in a negative feedback loop during oogenesis, with physical association of the extracellular/TM domains with EGFR. Directly supports the core MF and BP annotations. PubMed-verified.

title: Guidance of cell migration by EGF receptor signaling during Drosophila oogenesis.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only and concerns EGFR/Gurken guidance of border-cell migration; the abstract does not mention kek1, so the kek1-specific GO:0042059 IMP annotation cannot be verified from the available text (marked UNDECIDED).

title: Mechanism of activation of the Drosophila EGF Receptor by the TGFalpha ligand Gurken during oogenesis.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only and concerns Gurken/Star/Brho-mediated EGFR activation; the abstract does not mention kek1, so the GO:0030547 IDA annotation cannot be verified from the available text (marked UNDECIDED).

title: Mechanism of inhibition of the Drosophila and mammalian EGF receptors by the transmembrane protein Kekkon 1.
review_notes: Key mechanistic study; LRRs mediate direct DER association, the cytoplasmic tail directs apical localization, Kek1 forms a heterodimer with DER, and in mammalian assays it inhibits ligand binding, autophosphorylation and ERK activation across ErbB receptors. Supports MF (binding, inhibitor), BP and localization annotations.

title: Knockouts of Kekkon1 define sequence elements essential for Drosophila epidermal growth factor receptor inhibition.
review_notes: Loss-of-function alleles map EGFR binding to LRR1/LRR2 (class I, affinity) and localization to class II alleles, and demonstrate that Kek1 inhibits EGFR in eye development. Supports the negative-regulation and binding annotations.

title: Conservation of an inhibitor of the epidermal growth factor receptor, Kekkon1, in dipterans.
review_notes: Establishes kek1 as a transcriptional EGFR target attenuating the receptor, expressed in dorsal follicle cells during D/V patterning, conserved among dipterans but absent from vertebrates and Caenorhabditis. Supports localization and BP context.

title: Bipartite inhibition of Drosophila epidermal growth factor receptor by the extracellular and transmembrane domains of Kekkon1.
review_notes: Demonstrates the bipartite mechanism (LRRs sufficient for binding, juxta/transmembrane region required for inhibition) acting via DER domain V; inhibition is unique to Kek1 among family members. Supports MF binding/inhibitor and BP annotations.

title: The Drosophila kekkon genes: novel members of both the leucine-rich repeat and immunoglobulin superfamilies expressed in the CNS.
review_notes: Original identification of kek1/kek2 as transmembrane LRR+Ig cell-surface proteins expressed in differentiating CNS neurons and in follicle cells (D/V gradient); kek1 deletion has no overt phenotype (family redundancy). Supports architecture and predicted plasma-membrane localization.

title: Ethanol sensitivity and tolerance in long-term memory mutants of Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Full text available and read. The klg allele (ruslan) is among the LTM mutants scored; ruslan shows increased ethanol sensitivity and reduced (rapid+chronic) tolerance. Supports the IMP behavioral response to ethanol annotation (a non-core, pleiotropic phenotype). Paper uses original mutant names; ruslan=klg per PMID:19104051.

title: The Drosophila cell adhesion molecule klingon is required for long-term memory formation and is regulated by Notch.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Establishes that rus is a klg allele encoding a homophilic CAM; Klg is acutely required for LTM but not ARM, its levels rise on LTM induction, and it acts downstream of Notch. Directly supports the homophilic adhesion, LTM (positive) and ARM (negated) annotations.

title: The long-term memory trace formed in the Drosophila α/β mushroom body neurons is abolished in long-term memory mutants.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Confirms the klg mutant (D0417) as an LTM mutant that abolishes the α/β mushroom-body LTM calcium trace; corroborates the acute LTM requirement of klg. Klg is one of 26 diverse LTM mutants, so this is supporting rather than mechanistic for klg specifically.

title: An extracellular interactome of immunoglobulin and LRR proteins reveals receptor-ligand networks.
review_notes: Source of the IPI protein-binding annotation (Drosophila IgSF/LRR extracellular interactome; UniProt IntAct records Klg/Q9VCT4 binding cDIP/Q9VDD5). The cached full text does not name klg/cDIP (pairwise hits are in supplementary tables), so no klg-specific verbatim quote is available here; the annotation is sharpened from bare protein binding to cell adhesion molecule binding.

title: klingon, a novel member of the Drosophila immunoglobulin superfamily, is required for the development of the R7 photoreceptor neuron.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available:false) but the abstract itself establishes the core findings: three C2-type Ig domains + one FN3 repeat, GPI membrane attachment, homophilic adhesion in S2 cells, and an essential role in R7 photoreceptor development. Primary reference for the core adhesion and R7 annotations.

title: Cell-cell interaction during Drosophila embryogenesis: novel mechanisms and molecules.
review_notes: Review; cited as the TAS source for the tracheal epithelial cell migration annotation, but no abstract text is available in the cache so the specific claim could not be verified against it. The underlying biology is supported by PMID:9811580.

title: dCtBP-dependent and -independent repression activities of the Drosophila Knirps protein.
review_notes: Primary structure-function study of Knirps repression; abstract available in cache. Directly supports the repressor MF (GO:0001227) and the dCtBP corepressor binding.

title: Control of endoreduplication domains in the Drosophila gut by the knirps and knirps-related genes.
review_notes: Primary paper on the gut endoreduplication role; abstract available. Shows the process is endoreduplication (endocycle), supporting the MODIFY of GO:0007088 to GO:0032875.

title: A protein interaction map of Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Genome-wide two-hybrid proteome map; abstract available. The cached record does not name the specific Knirps partner, but the GOA row supplies it as WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:O46036, resolved by the fetched UniProt record as dCtBP (kni-uniprot.txt:97), so the bare protein-binding annotation is a MODIFY to GO:0001222 rather than an uninformative non-core keep.

title: The evolution of arthropod segmentation mechanisms.
review_notes: Review of arthropod segmentation used as the TAS source for the trunk segmentation and A-P axis annotations. Supports gap-gene control of segmentation at a general level; kni's explicit gap-gene identity is documented in PMID:18271625.

title: Structurally related Arabidopsis ANGUSTIFOLIA is functionally distinct from the transcriptional corepressor CtBP.
review_notes: Arabidopsis ANGUSTIFOLIA vs dCtBP; abstract-only cache, hence UNVERIFIED as a statement about the cached text, since a direct Knirps interaction is not recoverable from the abstract. Partner identity does not depend on it, because the GOA row carries WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:O46036, resolved by the fetched UniProt record as dCtBP (kni-uniprot.txt:97), so the annotation is a MODIFY to GO:0001222 rather than UNDECIDED.

title: Transcription factors bind thousands of active and inactive regions in the Drosophila blastoderm.
review_notes: Full text available; explicitly names kni as a gap gene and reports in vivo Knirps ChIP. Supports the IDA DNA-binding TF activity and the trunk/A-P segmentation role.

title: Groucho corepressor functions as a cofactor for the Knirps short-range transcriptional repressor.
review_notes: Full text available; directly supports Groucho (corepressor) binding, the short-range repression mechanism, and regulation of even-skipped.

title: A Comprehensive Drosophila melanogaster Transcription Factor Interactome.
review_notes: TF-TF interactome; full text available. Cited for a Knirps protein-binding IPI whose partner is supplied by the GOA row as WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:O46036, resolved by the fetched UniProt record as dCtBP (kni-uniprot.txt:97) - a corepressor, hence the MODIFY to GO:0001222. The screen's nominal restriction to sequence-specific TFs is not a safe basis for inferring the partner class, since dCtBP is itself recorded as a partner detected here; the curated WITH/FROM accession is what carries the call.

title: The transcription factors KNIRPS and KNIRPS RELATED control cell migration and branch morphogenesis during Drosophila tracheal development.
review_notes: Primary tracheal-development paper; abstract available. Supports the tracheal cell migration/branching role and direct repression of spalt.

title: UniProtKB P10734 (KNIR_DROME): Zygotic gap protein knirps
review_notes: UniProt record for P10734; confirms repressor function, nuclear localization, the NR-type C4 zinc-finger DBD, NR0 (LBD-less orphan) subfamily membership, and dCtBP/gro interactions. Used to justify the nucleus, zinc-binding, DNA-binding, and NR-activity MODIFY calls.

title: Regulation of Notch signalling by non-visual beta-arrestin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache. Directly supports the Notch-Deltex-Kurtz complex and ubiquitination-dependent Notch degradation (basis of GO:0045746 IGI and the two Reactome Notch reactions).

title: Exploratory activity in Drosophila requires the kurtz nonvisual arrestin.
review_notes: Full text available; directly supports the neuronal requirement of krz for exploratory locomotor behavior (GO:0035641 IMP).

title: Regulation of smoothened by Drosophila G-protein-coupled receptor kinases.
review_notes: Full text available; primarily about Gprk2, but explicitly shows Krz over-expression reduces Smo (first evidence arrestins regulate Smo in flies), supporting GO:0048260. Notes krz LOF has no Smo phenotype.

title: β-arrestin Kurtz inhibits MAPK and Toll signalling in Drosophila development.
review_notes: Full text available; primary source for Krz-ERK binding/sequestration (MAPK, GO:0043409, GO:0120177, GO:0051019), Krz-Cactus binding and Toll inhibition (GO:0045751), and cytoplasmic localization.

title: Role of the Drosophila non-visual ß-arrestin kurtz in hedgehog signalling.
review_notes: Full text available; primary source for Krz-Smo binding, clathrin/proteasome-dependent Smo internalization and degradation (GO:0002031, GO:0031648, GO:0045879) and cytoplasmic localization. Antagonism of Hh only on over-expression.

title: Regulation of Toll signaling and inflammation by β-arrestin and the SUMO protease Ulp1.
review_notes: Full text available; supports Krz limiting Toll signalling/inflammation in larvae via the SUMO protease Ulp1 (GO:0045751 IMP).

title: SUMO regulates the activity of Smoothened and Costal-2 in Drosophila Hedgehog signaling.
review_notes: Full text available; supports excess Krz inhibiting Smo sumoylation/accumulation (GO:0045879) and Krz facilitating the Smo-Ulp1 interaction that promotes desumoylation (GO:0060189).

title: Expanded substrate screenings of human and Drosophila type 10 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases (HSDs) reveal multiple specificities in bile acid and steroid hormone metabolism: characterization of multifunctional 3alpha/7alpha/7beta/17beta/20beta/21-HSD.
review_notes: Enzymatic characterization of the purified Drosophila HSD17B10 (scully) establishing both the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and the broad 17-beta-hydroxysteroid/bile-acid dehydrogenase activities. Note the abstract reports a cytosolic overexpression pattern for the fly protein, whereas the RNase P and proteomics evidence support a mitochondrial-matrix functional pool.

title: Mapping organelle proteins and protein complexes in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: High-throughput organelle proteomics; source of the HDA mitochondrion localization.

title: Loss of the mitochondrial protein-only ribonuclease P complex causes aberrant tRNA processing and lethality in Drosophila.
review_notes: Establishes scully's essential mt:RNase P role (MRPP2) and complex membership; full text available.

title: Loss of Individual Mitochondrial Ribonuclease P Complex Proteins Differentially Affects Mitochondrial tRNA Processing In Vivo.
review_notes: In-vivo dissection of the mt:RNase P subunits; supports the tRNA 5'-end processing and matrix-localization annotations. Full text available.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment hypothesis: scully (O18404) as the fly step-3 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase
review_notes: In-repo OpenScientist report resolving the module's step-3 fly-ortholog gap. Verdict SUPPORTED. The fold/residue analysis is a computational lead; the enzymatic activity is independently supported by PMID:12917011 (EXP), cited above.

title: Size isn't everything.
review_notes: Short BioEssays commentary on tissue size/shape and cell affinity; the abstract does not mention trn or cell migration. It is the TAS basis for GO:0016477 but is only background/contextual for trn - the real support for a migration role comes from the tracheal study (PMID:16764850).

title: Pattern formation in the Drosophila wing: The development of the veins.
review_notes: Wing-vein-patterning review whose abstract does not discuss trn or cell adhesion; a weak/likely-inappropriate NAS citation for GO:0007155 cell adhesion, although the adhesion annotation itself is biologically correct and supported elsewhere.

title: Distinct functions of the leucine-rich repeat transmembrane proteins capricious and tartan in the Drosophila tracheal morphogenesis.
review_notes: Directly contrasts Caps and Trn in tracheal branch interconnection; establishes that Tartan is expressed broadly in the mesoderm and acts via its extracellular domain as a permissive substrate for migrating tracheal cells. Verified against cached abstract.

title: A screen of cell-surface molecules identifies leucine-rich repeat proteins as key mediators of synaptic target selection.
review_notes: Full text available; directly assays trn loss- and gain-of-function in motor-axon targeting, shows trn/caps redundancy and neuronal Trn rescue, and documents the 65% identity and interchangeability of the Trn/Caps LRR domains.

title: A targeted gain-of-function screen identifies genes affecting salivary gland morphogenesis/tubulogenesis in Drosophila.
review_notes: Full text; recovers trn/caps as LRR adhesion hits in salivary gland tubulogenesis and states their molecular function is still unclear but likely homophilic/heterophilic adhesion. Supports GO:0007436 and the adhesion framing.

title: UniProt entry M9PFH7 (tartan, Drosophila melanogaster)
review_notes: UniProt/TrEMBL record documenting trn domain architecture (signal peptide, LRR ectodomain, single transmembrane helix, LRRCT) and the electronic cell-periphery localization.

title: Identification of functional amino acids in the macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase II
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Taniguchi et al., Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1999). Site-directed mutagenesis defines the catalytic/ATP-binding aspartates of MPH(2')II, confirming the phosphotransfer mechanism.

title: Purification and characterization of macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase type II from a strain of Escherichia coli highly resistant to macrolide antibiotics
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Kono et al., FEMS Microbiol Lett 1992). Original biochemical purification and characterization of MPH(2')II; directly establishes the macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase activity, product identity, broad substrate range, and nucleotide/metal requirements.

title: The role of histidine residues conserved in the putative ATP-binding region of macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase II
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Taniguchi et al., FEMS Microbiol Lett 2004). Identifies the conserved His205 as essential for MPH(2')II catalysis, complementing the earlier aspartate mutagenesis (PMID:10428938).

title: Resistance phenotypes conferred by macrolide phosphotransferases
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Chesneau et al., FEMS Microbiol Lett 2007). Phenotypic comparison of mph genes in an efflux-deficient host; documents mph(B) spiramycin/telithromycin resistance and the historical view that azithromycin resistance was mph(A)-specific (subsequently overturned for MphB by PMID:29317655).

title: Genome sequence of adherent-invasive Escherichia coli and comparative genomic analysis with other E. coli pathotypes
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nash et al., BMC Genomics 2010). Genome/provenance reference for this UniProt entry; provides the strain and plasmid context but no functional characterization of mphB.

title: Structural Basis for Kinase-Mediated Macrolide Antibiotic Resistance
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Fong et al., Structure 2017). First crystal structures of the MphB class (MPH(2')-II); directly establishes the kinase-like fold, GTP-analog/macrolide binding, and structural basis for broad macrolide specificity. Structures determined with GTP analogs, consistent with purine-NTP donor use.

title: The evolution of substrate discrimination in macrolide antibiotic resistance enzymes
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Pawlowski et al., Nat Commun 2018; PMC5760710, full text). Mass-spec confirmation of the 2'-OH phosphorylation site and broad substrate range of MphB (including azithromycin and the ketolide telithromycin), revising the older narrow-spectrum view.

title: Look and Outlook on Enzyme-Mediated Macrolide Resistance
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Golkar et al., Front Microbiol 2018). Authoritative review providing a clean secondary-source statement of the MPH(2')-II (MphB) broad substrate range vs the narrower MPH(2')-I.

title: Cloning and nucleotide sequence of the mphB gene for macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase II in Escherichia coli
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Noguchi et al., FEMS Microbiol Lett 1996). Foundational cloning/sequencing of mphB; the reported 302-aa / 34483-Da product matches this exact UniProt sequence, anchoring gene identity, and the APH-domain note matches the Pfam PF01636 annotation.

title: Expression of the mphB gene for macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase II from Escherichia coli in Staphylococcus aureus
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Noguchi et al., FEMS Microbiol Lett 1998). Demonstrates that mphB is a transferable resistance determinant that functions across species and is active against 16-membered macrolides.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for fepE protein tyrosine kinase activity
review_notes: The report's verdict matches the GOA source trace to PANTHER:PTN000794252 and the established Wzz/PCP-1 domain architecture of FepE.

title: Emergence of plasmid-mediated colistin resistance mechanism MCR-1 in animals and human beings in China: a microbiological and molecular biological study.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Liu et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2016). The original discovery of MCR-1 as a transferable colistin-resistance gene; establishes gene identity and the resistance phenotype.

title: Structure of the catalytic domain of the colistin resistance enzyme MCR-1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Stojanoski et al., BMC Biol 2016; PMC5025626, full text). 1.32 A structure of the MCR-1 catalytic domain; directly supports the pEtN-transferase MF, zinc/metal dependence, Thr285 nucleophile (phosphorylation), and the lipid A target-modification mechanism.

title: Substrate analog interaction with MCR-1 offers insight into the rising threat of the plasmid-mediated transferable colistin resistance.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Wei et al., FASEB J 2018). Substrate-analog/structural study supporting the pEtN-transferase activity and reaction; corroborates EC 2.7.8.43.

title: Blinded OpenScientist function-assignment report (TreeGrafter audit)
review_notes: Blinded run independently refuted the term: MCR-1 is phosphoethanolamine transferase (EC 2.7.8.43), so the correct parent MF is GO:0016780 (EC 2.7.8.*), not the sibling GO:0016776 (EC 2.7.4.*); error traced to a TAS annotation on EptA at the PTHR30443:SF0 node. Consistent with the curated replacement GO:0043838. Blinded OpenScientist function-assignment run: given only the propagated term (the prior curation action withheld), it independently reached the same conclusion as this review. Corroborating evidence, not a primary source.

title: Regulation of transcription of the mph(A) gene for macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase I in Escherichia coli: characterization of the regulatory gene mphR(A)
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Noguchi et al., J Bacteriol 2000). Characterizes the mphR(A) repressor controlling inducible mphA expression; supports the regulatory distinction from constitutive mphB.

title: Resistance phenotypes conferred by macrolide phosphotransferases
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Chesneau et al., FEMS Microbiol Lett 2007). Comparative phenotyping of mph genes; documents mph(A)'s azithromycin activity, consistent with its 14-/15-membered specificity.

title: Purification and characterization of macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase from a strain of Escherichia coli that is highly resistant to erythromycin
review_notes: PubMed-verified (O'Hara et al., Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1989). Original purification and characterization of MPH(2')I; the primary source for MphA's 14-membered (not 16-membered) substrate specificity, inducibility, and purine-NTP donor usage — the direct contrast to MphB (PMID:1330822).

title: Structural Basis for Kinase-Mediated Macrolide Antibiotic Resistance
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Fong et al., Structure 2017). Provides the MphA (MPH(2')-I) crystal structures (PDB 5IGH/5IGI), confirming the APH/protein-kinase-like fold and GTP-analog/macrolide binding.

title: The evolution of substrate discrimination in macrolide antibiotic resistance enzymes
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Pawlowski et al., Nat Commun 2018). Phylogenetic/functional survey of Mph enzymes placing MphA among the clinically mobilized, widespread Gram-negative resistance kinases.

title: Look and Outlook on Enzyme-Mediated Macrolide Resistance
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Golkar et al., Front Microbiol 2018). Authoritative review of enzyme-mediated macrolide resistance; provides a clean secondary-source statement of the MPH(2')-I vs -II substrate-specificity distinction and the GTP phosphate-donor mechanism.

title: Whole-Genome Sequencing of an Escherichia coli ST69 Strain Harboring bla(CTX-M-27) on a Hybrid Plasmid
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Wang et al., Infect Drug Resist 2024). Documents the contemporary mobile genetic context of mphA (IS26 composite transposon, IncF plasmids), supporting its horizontal dissemination.

title: Multidrug-resistant conjugative plasmid carrying mphA confers increased antimicrobial resistance in Shigella
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Asad et al., Sci Rep 2024). Experimental conjugation/MIC evidence that plasmid-borne mphA confers high-level azithromycin resistance transferable into recipient Enterobacterales.

title: Nucleotide sequence and characterization of erythromycin resistance determinant that encodes macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase I in Escherichia coli
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Noguchi et al., Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1995). Cloning/sequencing of the mphA determinant; establishes mphA identity and the mphA+mrx requirement for high-level resistance.

title: abaA controls phialide differentiation in Aspergillus nidulans.

title: The Aspergillus nidulans yA gene is regulated by abaA.

title: brlA is necessary and sufficient to direct conidiophore development in Aspergillus nidulans.

title: Identification of Aspergillus brlA response elements (BREs) by genetic selection in yeast.
