title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Inter-ontology inference from GO:0004784 (SOD activity) → GO:0019430 (removal of superoxide radicals). The inference chain is mechanically correct but its input premise (SOD activity for SPBC3H7.04) is wrong, so the derived BP annotation is also wrong and inherits the same fate as the parent IEA.

title: Bot1p is required for mitochondrial translation, respiratory function, and normal cell morphology in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary characterization paper for the S. pombe mS42 mitoribosomal protein (named Bot1p in the paper). Establishes the mitochondrial-ribosome localization and the mitochondrial translation role, and is the ComplexPortal-cited NAS reference for the mt-SSU annotations under review.

title: UniProtKB entry O74379 (RT26_SCHPO) — Small ribosomal subunit protein mS42
review_notes: Authoritative UniProt curation of the protein as a mitoribosomal mS42 family member, not a SOD; primary evidence anchor for this review's core-function assignment.

title: SPBC3H7.04 (mS42 / bot1) — S. pombe mitoribosomal small subunit protein
review_notes: Local reviewer notes file which reproduces the upstream go-annotation curator issue (geneontology/go-annotation#6474) and integrates it with the UniProt-level and PANTHER subfamily evidence and with the pseudoenzyme detection pattern used elsewhere in this repo (Cu/Zn-SOD fold-match without PROSITE PS00087 active-site match; see projects/PSEUDOENZYMES.md).

title: ORFeome cloning and global analysis of protein localization in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: Genome-wide GFP localization screen that underlies the mitochondrial localization call for acn1 (via the UniProt SubCell inference and PomBase HDA annotation). Cached entry is abstract-only and does not name acn1 in the abstract, so it is supporting/contextual rather than a direct functional characterization.

title: Broad functional profiling of fission yeast proteins using phenomics and machine learning.
review_notes: Large-scale dark-gene phenomics study; the source of most acn1 FYPO phenotype annotations (broad drug/stress resistance and sensitivity). Frames the conserved-unknown ("unknome") problem that acn1 exemplifies. Provides pleiotropic screen phenotypes, not mechanism.

title: Formation of giant ER sheets by pentadecanoic acid causes lipotoxicity in fission yeast.
review_notes: Lipotoxicity screen contributing the FYPO annotation that acn1 deletion shows normal growth on pentadecanoic acid (a negative result). acn1 is not discussed in the paper's body text; relevant only as screen context linking acn1 to lipid metabolism datasets.

title: UniProtKB entry O74380 (YNV5_SCHPO), Uncharacterized membrane protein C3H7.05c
review_notes: Primary record for the reviewed protein. Establishes the Wax_synthase_dom / MBOAT_2 domain (IPR032805 / PF13813), the nine predicted transmembrane helices, the mitochondrial-membrane subcellular-location inference, and the "Predicted" (PE 4) status. All supporting_text quotes are verbatim from the cached UniProt record.

title: Deep research report (falcon/Edison): acn1 / SPBC3H7.05c functional annotation
review_notes: Automated deep-research synthesis. Its acn1-specific conclusion (no primary functional characterization exists; function inferable only from the MBOAT/wax-synthase domain) is consistent with independent inspection of UniProt, PomBase, and the primary literature. Its DOI citations are MBOAT-family reviews, not acn1-specific studies, and are treated as family background only. Note it double-lists IPR032805 and PF13813 as two domains; they are the same domain.

title: Genome-wide identification of fungal GPI proteins.
review_notes: PubMed/DOI-verified (Yeast 2003; De Groot, Hellingwerf, Klis). Abstract-only in cache; the per-gene assignment of SPAC19G12.16c to the 33 S. pombe GPI candidates underlies the PomBase TAS cell-surface annotation. Establishes a predicted GPI-anchored cell-surface role, not an experimentally demonstrated molecular function.

title: The cell cycle-regulated genes of Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PLoS Biol 2005; Oliva et al.; PMID 15966770). Full text cached. The cell-separation role of adg2 is a cluster-level co-regulation inference (shared Ace2 sites + expression timing + a cell-surface-glycoprotein descriptor); adg2 itself was not functionally assayed here, so this supports a plausible process association, not a demonstrated adg2 function.

title: ORFeome cloning and global analysis of protein localization in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed/DOI-verified (Nat Biotechnol 2006; Matsuyama et al.). Genome-scale YFP localization screen; the specific adg2 ER call is in the dataset rather than the abstract. ER is a transit/secretory compartment consistent with a secretory glycoprotein, not confirmation of a mature GPI-anchored cell-wall product.

title: Deciphering the transcriptional-regulatory network of flocculation in Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PLoS Genet 2012; Kwon et al.; PMID 23236291). Full text cached. Provides transcriptional-network context (adg2 as an Ace2 target linked to the Adn2/Adn3 flocculation program) but does not establish an Adg2 molecular activity; cited for regulatory placement, not for a function claim, so no verbatim supporting_text is attached.

title: Use of the ND evidence code for Gene Ontology (GO) terms
review_notes: Standard GO reference documenting the ND (No biological Data) evidence code; supports the root cellular_component placeholder annotation.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: The GO reference describing curator-judged ISO transfer to orthologs; it is the basis for the MAP-kinase scaffold activity (GO:0005078) annotation transferred from S. cerevisiae AHK1 (SGD:S000002231). Correctly applied as a mechanism, but the transferred function remains unverified in S. pombe.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Standard UniProt SubCell-to-GO mapping reference; supports the low-resolution, prediction based membrane (GO:0016020) annotation.

title: Scaffold Protein Ahk1, Which Associates with Hkr1, Sho1, Ste11, and Pbs2, Inhibits Cross Talk Signaling from the Hkr1 Osmosensor to the Kss1 Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the defining paper for the scaffold function, but it characterizes the Saccharomyces cerevisiae protein (Ahk1/YDL073W = SGD:S000002231), not the S. pombe protein. Cache is abstract-only (full_text_available: false). It is the experimental source for the ISO annotations transferred to S. pombe ahk1, so it is highly relevant as the orthology anchor, while the fission-yeast function itself remains inferred.

title: Mechanistic insights into the stimulation of the histone H3K9 methyltransferase Clr4 by proximal H3K14 ubiquitination.
review_notes: PubMed-verified crystal structure of the Clr4 KMT catalytic domain bound to H3 peptide and SAM, supporting H3K9 methyltransferase activity, the pre-SET zinc-binding catalytic module, and H3K14ub-stimulated H3K9 methylation.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Standard GO_Central IBA phylogenetic-inference reference; supports the IBA localization annotation to the mitochondrial intermembrane space via PANTHER family PTHR15590 (PTN000400520), consistent with the twin CX9C / MIA40-import identity of the CMC4 family.

title: The genome sequence of Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: Genome-sequence reference for the locus; background/contextual, does not speak to cmc4 function.

title: Augmented annotation of the Schizosaccharomyces pombe genome reveals additional genes required for growth and viability.
review_notes: PMC full text available and PubMed-verified. Primary S. pombe reference: establishes cmc4/tam2 as a bona fide meiotically regulated protein-coding gene detected by mass spectrometry and shows tam2Δ is viable. Does not assign a molecular or biological function.

title: Regulation of COX Assembly and Function by Twin CX(9)C Proteins-Implications for Human Disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMC7909247; DOI 10.3390/cells10020197). This review is the most CMC4-specific source available and explicitly frames the family member as largely uncharacterized: IMS localization and MIA40-dependent import are firm, but the only functional lead is a non-essential association with SCO1 in COX II sub-assembly. Directly grounds the knowledge-gap framing for this dark gene.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The IPR005024 (SNF7 family) → GO:0007034 vacuolar transport InterPro2GO mapping is the source of an inappropriate IEA on cmp7. The mapping is correctly applied at the InterPro family level but is not biologically appropriate for cmp7, which acts at the nuclear envelope, not in vacuolar transport. Upstream tracker geneontology/go-annotation#6458.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/PANTHER IBA propagation appropriately captures NE-associated core functions for cmp7.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Generates a broad cytoplasm IEA; correct at the keyword level but obscures the specific functional NE / SPB-attachment-site location.

title: Manual transfer of GO annotation data to genes by curator judgment of sequence model
review_notes: Pfam Snf7-based ESCRT-III complex transfer; consistent with EXP and IBA evidence on this gene.

title: ORFeome cloning and global analysis of protein localization in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: Genome-wide overexpression GFP screen; gives a coarse cytoplasmic signal for cmp7 that does not reflect its specific functional NE / SPB-attachment site compartment characterized by later work.

title: LEM2 recruits CHMP7 for ESCRT-mediated nuclear envelope closure in fission yeast and human cells.
review_notes: Foundational paper for cmp7/CHMP7 NE-recruitment-by-Lem2/LEM2 model in fission yeast and human cells.

title: Closed mitosis requires local disassembly of the nuclear envelope.
review_notes: Establishes the local-NE-disassembly/reassembly framework that cmp7 acts in during closed mitosis.

title: An ESCRT grommet cooperates with a diffusion barrier to maintain nuclear integrity.
review_notes: Defines the grommet activity GO:0180024 and the SPB-attachment site GO:0180028 for cmp7.

title: Cms1 coordinates stepwise local 90S pre-ribosome assembly with timely snR83 release.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified primary study of the S. cerevisiae ortholog CMS1 (the ISO source, SGD:S000003993). It establishes the 90S small-subunit-biogenesis role transferred to S. pombe cms1 and (in its full text, cached) explicitly frames CMS1 as poorly characterized with only a hypothetical molecular activity, supporting both the accepted process/complex annotations and the MF knowledge gap. The paper concerns S. cerevisiae, not S. pombe, so it grounds the ortholog, not the pombe protein directly.

title: ORFeome cloning and global analysis of protein localization in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: Genome-wide YFP-tagging localization survey (Matsuyama et al. 2006). The individual localization call for SPBC17D11.08 (cytoplasm, Golgi) is in the supplementary dataset; the cached record is abstract-only and does not name the gene in prose. This is the ECO:0000269 experimental source underlying the cytoplasm and Golgi GO annotations via UniProt Subcellular Location mapping.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of fission yeast.
review_notes: Large-scale S. pombe phosphoproteome (Wilson-Grady et al. 2008); supports the Ser266/Ser388 phosphorylation sites recorded in UniProt. Provides no functional information on dca7 beyond the fact that it is a phosphoprotein.

title: Uncharacterized WD repeat-containing protein C17D11.08 (dca7, SPBC17D11.08), Schizosaccharomyces pombe
review_notes: Swiss-Prot record (reviewed). Source of the DCAF7-like/WD40 domain architecture, the cytoplasm + Golgi subcellular localization (both ECO:0000269|PubMed:16823372), and Ser266/Ser388 phosphorylation (ECO:0000269|PubMed:18257517). Verified by direct inspection of dca7-uniprot.txt.

title: Deep research report: dca7 (SPBC17D11.08) as a DCAF7-like WD40 protein
review_notes: Literature synthesis (falcon/Edison) grounded in peer-reviewed DOI sources on the DCAF7/WDR68 family. Used ONLY for orthology-based context (family is a catalytically inactive WD40 scaffold/adaptor for DYRK kinases, with a debated CRL4 substrate-receptor role) and for the explicit, verifiable statement that no primary literature directly characterizes the S. pombe protein. Not used to assert any established S. pombe function.

title: Identification of a nuclear gene (FMC1) required for the assembly/stability of yeast mitochondrial F(1)-ATPase in heat stress conditions.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:11096112, J Biol Chem 2001; DOI 10.1074/jbc.M009557200). Establishes the FMC1 family function in S. cerevisiae, from which the S. pombe fmc1 annotations are propagated (the IBA source is SGD:S000001360). Abstract only in cache; used strictly for family-level (orthology) support, not as direct evidence about the pombe protein.

title: ORFeome cloning and global analysis of protein localization in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: Genome-wide YFP localization study (Matsuyama et al. 2006, Nat Biotechnol). It is the experimental source of the cytoplasm/nuclear-membrane localization of the paralog ftm2 (P0CU07/SPAC977.02), from which ftm3's localization is transferred by ISS (GOA with:UniProtKB:P0CU07). Cached entry is abstract-only and does not name ftm3 individually, so it is cited as provenance for the ISS transfer rather than as direct ftm3 evidence. PubMed-verified title/authors.

title: Transcriptome sequencing and screening of genes related to glucose availability in Schizosaccharomyces pombe by RNA-seq analysis
review_notes: RNA-seq study of glucose availability (Tarhan & Çakır 2021). PomBase attaches a high-throughput expression annotation (GO:0042149 cellular response to glucose starvation, ECO:0000058, "RNA level decreased") to ftm3 based on this dataset; that annotation is NOT in the QuickGO GOA set reviewed here and the full text does not name ftm3. Recorded only as transcript-level context, not functional evidence.

title: UPF0742 protein SPAC750.04c (ftm3) - Schizosaccharomyces pombe
review_notes: Primary source record for ftm3. Establishes the UPF0742 family membership, the Pombe_5TM (PF09437 / IPR018291) domain content, the predicted transmembrane helix, and the by-similarity subcellular localization (transferred from paralog P0CU07/ftm2). Verified directly against the fetched UniProt record.

title: Chaperone Function of Hgh1 in the Biogenesis of Eukaryotic Elongation Factor 2.
review_notes: PMID verified via NCBI esearch/esummary (Mönkemeyer et al., Mol Cell 74:88-100, 2019; DOI 10.1016/j.molcel.2019.01.034). This is the primary experimental characterization of the S. cerevisiae Hgh1 ortholog and is the biological basis for the ISO transfers to S. pombe hgh1. The work is on budding-yeast Hgh1, not fission-yeast hgh1 directly; abstract-only cache.

title: Iwr1 directs RNA polymerase II nuclear import.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Czeko et al. 2011, Mol Cell 42:261-266). Abstract-only in cache. This is the defining functional study for the Iwr1 family; it establishes the Pol II-specific nuclear-import-adaptor role that is transferred to S. pombe iwr1 by orthology (the ISO annotation cites the S. cerevisiae ortholog SGD:S000002273). The paper concerns S. cerevisiae, not S. pombe.

title: Iwr1 protein is important for preinitiation complex formation by all three nuclear RNA polymerases in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Esberg et al. 2011, PLoS ONE 6:e20829); full text in cache. S. cerevisiae study. Corroborates the conserved Pol II physical interaction and the family's broad relevance to transcription-machinery assembly. The reported Pol I/III preinitiation-complex effects are generally interpreted as downstream consequences of impaired Pol II import rather than a direct pombe function, so relevance to the specific molecular role transferred to S. pombe iwr1 is supporting rather than defining.

title: Genome-wide identification of fungal GPI proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Genome-wide bioinformatic identification of fungal GPI proteins; the S. pombe subset (33 candidates) includes SPBC1E8.05. This is the source cited by PomBase for the cell surface (GO:0009986) annotation. It is a prediction paper (consensus-sequence screen), not an experimental localization of knh4, hence MEDIUM relevance for the cell-surface claim.

title: Analysis of a genome-wide set of gene deletions in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The Bioneer genome-wide deletion resource; source of the "viable" (non-essential) status for knh4-delta. Large-scale resource, not a knh4-specific functional study, hence LOW relevance beyond viability.

title: Comparative functional genomics of the fission yeasts.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Comparative genomics of the Schizosaccharomyces clade; source of the knh4 ortholog assignment (S. japonicus SJAG_03521). No knh4-specific functional data.

title: Overexpression of cell-wall GPI-anchored proteins restores cell growth of N-glycosylation-defective och1 mutants in Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the abstract explicitly names SPBC1E8.05 (knh4). This is the single most direct functional study of knh4: it establishes that knh4-delta is viable but beta-glucanase-sensitive and that the encoded protein non-enzymatically supports cell-surface beta-glucan. Cached record is abstract-only, but the abstract itself states the key knh4-specific claims.

title: Uncharacterized serine-rich protein C1E8.05 (YB95_SCHPO)
review_notes: UniProt record for the reviewed gene. Domain (Kre9/Knh1), signal-peptide, low-complexity/disordered, and glycoprotein features are the primary structural evidence for the cell-surface, non-catalytic scaffold interpretation used in this review.

title: Mmf1p, a novel yeast mitochondrial protein conserved throughout evolution and involved in maintenance of the mitochondrial genome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Cell Biol 2000; abstract-only in cache). Original description of the S. cerevisiae ortholog Mmf1p and its mitochondrial-matrix localization / mtDNA maintenance role; establishes the naming basis for mmf2.

title: Genomic and experimental evidence for multiple metabolic functions in the RidA/YjgF/YER057c/UK114 (Rid) protein family.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified full text (mBio 2015). Defines Rid subfamily structure and the catalytic residues; supports the family/catalytic-residue reasoning for mmf2.

title: Mmf1p Couples Amino Acid Metabolism to Mitochondrial DNA Maintenance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified full text (mBio 2018). Directly establishes the biochemical activity and physiological role of the S. cerevisiae ortholog Mmf1p; used here as orthology-based support for mmf2, not as direct evidence for the fission-yeast protein.

title: Genome-wide identification of fungal GPI proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified genome-wide fungal GPI-protein prediction study (De Groot et al. 2003, Yeast). Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false). It establishes mtl3 as a predicted GPI-anchored cell-surface protein (basis of the TAS GO:0009897 annotation), but says nothing about its molecular function or signaling role.

title: ORFeome cloning and global analysis of protein localization in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed-verified large-scale GFP-localization dataset (Matsuyama et al. 2006, Nat Biotechnol); cited by UniProt (ECO:0000269|PubMed:16823372) as the source of the ER localization. A systematic dataset, not an mtl3-focused study.

title: The fission yeast cell wall stress sensor-like proteins Mtl2 and Wsc1 act by turning on the GTPase Rho1p but act independently of the cell wall integrity pathway.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cruz et al. 2013, MicrobiologyOpen; PMC3831639). Family/pathway context for the S. pombe cell-wall sensor class; explicitly about paralogous sensors (Mtl2, Wsc1), NOT about mtl3. Included to frame the inferred sensor role and to keep the mtl3 (Mid-Two-Like) vs mtl1 (Mtr4-Like helicase) distinction clear.

title: Systematic analysis of the role of RNA-binding proteins in the regulation of RNA stability.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified (Hasan et al. 2014, PLoS Genet; PMC4222612). Systematic dataset; mtl3 is a target in the supplementary data, not discussed by name. Relevant to mtl3 regulation, not to its molecular function.

title: Broad functional profiling of fission yeast proteins using phenomics and machine learning.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified (Rodriguez-Lopez et al. 2023, eLife; PMC10547477). Full text available but mtl3-specific data live in the genome-wide phenotype dataset, so no mtl3-specific prose quote is available; supports the deletion phenotypes at the dataset level, consistent with a cell-surface stress-sensor role.

title: The genome sequence of Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: Genome-sequence reference establishing the SPAC3H1.03 locus; background/contextual, does not address mug151 function.

title: A large-scale screen in S. pombe identifies seven novel genes required for critical meiotic events.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false). The paper deleted 175 meiotically-upregulated genes and reported seven (rec24, rec25, rec27, tht2, bqt1, bqt2, moa1) as critical for meiosis; mug151 is not among them. It is the basis for the UniProt "role in meiosis" statement, which reflects meiotic up-regulation plus inclusion in the deletion set, not a characterized meiotic mechanism.

title: SAP30BP interacts with RBM17/SPF45 to promote splicing in a subset of human short introns.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Characterizes the human ortholog SAP30BP as a splicing cofactor for RBM17/SPF45 on short introns, and notes it was previously implicated in transcriptional control. Informs the plausible molecular hypotheses for the family but does not assay the S. pombe protein mug151.

title: The genome sequence of Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: Background genome reference: the source of the SPAC12G12.17 gene model on chromosome I. Establishes the gene's existence but says nothing about its function.

title: Dynamic repertoire of a eukaryotic transcriptome surveyed at single-nucleotide resolution.
review_notes: Background transcriptome reference underlying the UniProt "Evidence at transcript level" (PE 2) status; confirms the transcript is expressed but provides no functional evidence.

title: A new pathway for protein export in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cleves et al., J Cell Biol 1996; PMC2120850); correctly the primary source behind the NCE101 family and the IBA/InterPro protein secretion annotations. Relevance is MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the S. pombe protein itself is not studied here: the abstract (the only cached text; full_text_available is false) does not name NCE1 individually, and in the full text NCE1 is one of four small proteins recovered in an overexpression screen whose function (export machinery versus export substrate) is explicitly left ambiguous.

title: ORFeome cloning and global analysis of protein localization in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (abstract-only). Genome-scale YFP-tagging screen; the cyto/nuclear call for rrg8 conflicts with orthology-based mitochondrial localization and is not curated as a component by PomBase. Treated as the basis of over-annotated electronic CC terms.

title: Genome-wide deletion mutant analysis reveals genes required for respiratory growth, mitochondrial genome maintenance and mitochondrial protein synthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified. Source of the RRG8 gene name ("Required for Respiratory Growth 8") and of mitochondrial localization/respiratory-deficiency of the ortholog. Table 5 lists RRG8/YPR116w as "Unknown function, GFP-tagged protein in mitochondria".

title: Analysis of a genome-wide set of gene deletions in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PMC-verified genome-wide deletion resource. Per-gene call for SPAC31G5.06 is in supplementary data; PomBase records the inviable deletion phenotype. Cited here for essentiality context and the fission-yeast-specific lethality of mtDNA loss.

title: A genome-wide resource of cell cycle and cell shape genes of fission yeast.
review_notes: PMC-verified. Bioneer/Sysgro microscopy resource; PomBase attributes the FYPO inviable phenotype (microscopy evidence) of rrg8 deletion to this study.

title: 5' processing of Saccharomyces cerevisiae mitochondrial tRNAs requires expression of multiple genes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary paper (abstract-only in cache). This is the functional source for the mt-tRNA 5'-end processing role transferred by ISO to rrg8. Establishes MTA1 (= YPR116W = the RRG8 ortholog) as an inner-membrane, RNase-P-associated accessory factor, not a demonstrated catalytic nuclease.

title: Quantitative proteomics and phosphoproteomics profiling of meiotic divisions in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PMC-verified. Expression/abundance evidence only (protein detected, increased in meiosis); does not inform molecular function.

title: Protein AMPylation by an Evolutionarily Conserved Pseudokinase.
review_notes: PubMed title matches. Foundational paper defining SELO-family AMPylase activity, mitochondrial localization, redox-protein substrates and the oxidative-stress-response role. Assays E. coli YdiU, S. cerevisiae and human SELO; does not assay S. pombe, so it supports the S. pombe annotations only by homology (ISS/IBA/ISO). Cached record is abstract-only but the abstract itself states the key claims.

title: A repurposed AMP binding domain reveals mitochondrial protein AMPylation as a regulator of cellular metabolism.
review_notes: PubMed title matches; full text cached. Mammalian study confirming mitochondrial SELO AMPylation of metabolic enzymes and re-stating family conservation (E. coli, S. cerevisiae). Relevant to S. pombe sel0 only at the family/ortholog level (used as an ISO WITH/FROM source).

title: Education and research: where are we going?
review_notes: This PMID resolves to a 1998 Australian Veterinary Journal editorial ("Education and research: where are we going?", Niethe G) that has no connection to SelO, AMPylation, mitochondria or S. pombe. It appears in GOA as the reference for one ISO AMPylase-activity annotation (WITH/FROM UniProtKB:P31040, human SDHA). It is a spurious/erroneous identifier in the GOA source and cannot support any annotation. Per project policy the GOA id is not rewritten here; the AMPylase-activity annotation itself remains supportable from the other evidence lines (IBA/ISS/Rhea and PMID:30270044).

title: Protein adenylyltransferase SelO, mitochondrial (SELO_SCHPO)
review_notes: UniProt record for the reviewed gene; domain, transit-peptide, ATP/Mg binding-site and family assignments are the primary structural evidence used in this review.

title: Interactions between Kar2p and its nucleotide exchange factors Sil1p and Lhs1p are mechanistically distinct.
review_notes: PMC-verified full text (Hale, Lovell, de Keyzer & Stirling, J Biol Chem 2010). Primary S. cerevisiae biochemistry establishing Sil1p as a BiP/Kar2p NEF acting on the ATPase domain; it is the orthology basis for the pombe sil1 IBA/ISO annotations and directly supports the Sil1/Lhs1 redundancy knowledge gap. Work is in budding yeast, not fission yeast; used here for conserved-function reasoning.

title: A systematic screen for morphological abnormalities during fission yeast sexual reproduction identifies a mechanism of actin aster formation for cell fusion.
review_notes: PMC-verified (Dudin et al., PLoS Genet 2017). A genome-wide morphology screen, not a sil1-focused study; the associated phenotype is HTP-level and does not establish sil1 molecular function.

title: Broad functional profiling of fission yeast proteins using phenomics and machine learning.
review_notes: PMC-verified (Rodriguez-Lopez et al., eLife 2023). Source of several high-throughput drug/stress phenotypes recorded for sil1 in PomBase; illustrates that pombe evidence for this gene is screen-level, not gene-specific characterization.

title: Conservation of polyamine regulation by translational frameshifting from yeast to mammals.
review_notes: Primary experimental characterization of the S. pombe gene itself (called "SPA" in the paper; = spa1 / SPBC577.14c). Full text (PMC302018) verified; directly demonstrates ODC inhibition, the deletion/overexpression polyamine phenotypes, and polyamine-responsive +1 frameshifting for this gene.

title: A homolog of mammalian antizyme is present in fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe but not detected in budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; establishes the family assignment (ODC antizyme) for the S. pombe gene by remote-homology HMM search and notes the low sequence identity (18-22% in the most conserved C-terminal regions).

title: Augmented annotation of the Schizosaccharomyces pombe genome reveals additional genes required for growth and viability
review_notes: Full text cached and verified. This is the discovery paper for tam14 and the only publication with S. pombe-specific data on the gene. It establishes tam14 as a bona fide, meiotically-regulated protein-coding gene but provides only transcript-level (expression) evidence; tam14 was explicitly excluded from the deletion-phenotyping set, so no meiotic or other function was demonstrated.

title: Falcon deep research report for tam14 (G2TRT3, SPCC330.20)
review_notes: Genuine falcon/Edison deep-research output (17 citations, cached:false). Conclusions were cross-checked against the UniProt record and the PomBase curated ortholog set and agree: real conserved RAMP4/SERP1 family, no S. pombe-specific experimental characterization. Its mechanistic sources (Lewis et al. 2024 eLife; Pool 2009 JCB) concern mammalian RAMP4/SERP1, not tam14, and are used here only as family context, not as tam14-specific evidence.

title: ORFeome cloning and global analysis of protein localization in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: Large-scale localisation resource; supports the cytoplasm and cytosol annotations but says nothing about function. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of fission yeast.
review_notes: Large-scale phosphoproteomics; the vms1 site is recorded in UniProt (MOD_RES 38) but no GO annotation depends on it. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: A stress-responsive system for mitochondrial protein degradation.
review_notes: Full text cached. Sound support for the mitochondrial and complex annotations; describes a stress-conditional role, which is why those annotations are kept as non-core rather than core.

title: A Cdc48p-associated factor modulates endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation, cell stress, and ubiquitinated protein homeostasis.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. Correctly cited for the ERAD claim, and the claim is real, but the paper itself frames the effect as modulatory and predates the discovery of the family's tRNA-cleavage activity. This is the evidential weak point in the ERAD IBD.

title: Cytosolic Protein Vms1 Links Ribosome Quality Control to Mitochondrial and Cellular Homeostasis.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Both PAINT rows were traced to their nodes and every WITH/FROM identifier resolved. Neither is a miscitation, and neither term is wrong for the node it was asserted at; the issue is node placement. GO:0016787 came from the very deep PTN009058710, whose 16 donor proteins span plants, fungi, bacteria and animals, and donor-by-donor testing shows that term is the exact lowest common ancestor of the set rather than a cautious approximation to it - GO:0052689 is refuted by two kynurenine formamidases and GO:0017171 by soybean HIDH's threonine nucleophile. Meanwhile GO:0017171 was placed only at the ortholog-specific PTN002745055 and PTN002745068, though it is true of every donor PAINT cites at the family node PTN009058713, and GO:0016020 membrane was placed at that family node where it transfers least reliably.

title: Genetic Study on Small Insertions and Deletions in Psoriasis Reveals a Role in Complex Human Diseases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the cached record is abstract-only, and the abstract itself names AADACL2 explicitly, so the claim used here does not depend on the full text. Supports no GO annotation - a susceptibility association is not a molecular function or a biological process - but it is the only human phenotypic signal that exists for this gene and it motivates the suggested experiments.

title: KIAA1363-A Multifunctional Enzyme in Xenobiotic Detoxification and Lipid Ester Hydrolysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified review by the Lass group, full text available in PMC. The most useful reference for this gene precisely because it states that AADACL2 has no known function, which independently corroborates the empty affinage record rather than leaving it as an argument from silence. Also the source for AADAC and KIAA1363 topology and substrate range, both of which bear directly on the propagated annotations reviewed here.

title: Novel functional insights into ischemic stroke biology provided by the first genome-wide association study of stroke in indigenous Africans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Cited for completeness of the human genetic picture only. The paper itself locates the signal near AADACL2 and MIR5186 rather than within AADACL2, and a stroke locus in a gene whose expression is skin-restricted has no obvious mechanistic reading, so no annotation follows.

title: PANTHER node PTN009058710: which GO term is true of every donor? (shared node-level audit for AADACL2, AADACL3 and AADACL4)
review_notes: Node-level audit written for the three-gene harmonisation, reproducible with audit_node_PTN009058710.py in the same folder; the WITH/FROM sets are read from the committed GOA TSVs and, independently, fetched per accession from QuickGO for all three paralogs, with the two sources cross-checked and a gene covered by neither treated as a hard error, and every donor's chemistry, nucleophile and GO ancestry is fetched at run time. It corrects two premises this review had relied on: soybean HIDH is a bifunctional dehydratase/carboxylesterase rather than a non-hydrolase, and yeast BNA7 resolves to Q04066 with a serine nucleophile.

title: AADACL2: is the esterase call founded, and which of its two localisations is?
review_notes: Bioinformatics analysis carried out for this review; reproducible with the script in the same folder, all values fetched from the UniProt, InterPro, QuickGO, EBI Proteins and Human Protein Atlas REST APIs at run time and written to results.json. It reports a negative result honestly - the hydropathy and cleavage-site measurements undercut the initial hypothesis that the membrane annotation was a simple paralog artefact.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AADACL2 (human)
review_notes: The record is empty - zero discoveries, zero citations, and no self_evaluation_pairwise score, so the tool's trust gates had nothing to catch. An empty provider record is not by itself evidence that literature is absent, so the claim was verified separately: PubMed returns six AADACL2 hits, none of them a functional characterisation, and the three UniProt RN references are all large-scale sequencing papers. The independent confirmation is PMID:35736449, which states in prose that the AADACL2/AADACL3/AADACL4 subgroup has no assigned function.

title: UniProtKB entry Q6P093 (ADCL2_HUMAN), Arylacetamide deacetylase-like 2
review_notes: The primary source for the residue-level evidence used throughout this review. Its active-site and motif features carry ECO:0000250 (by similarity to mouse Nceh1 Q8BLF1 and to Q5NUF3) and PROSITE-ProRule evidence rather than experiment, which is why they were re-tested independently by alignment to the characterised WITH/FROM sources rather than accepted at face value. One correction to report upstream: the SIGNAL 1..18 cleavage position places histidine at -1, which is not a signal peptidase I site.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The InterPro2GO mapping reference behind three of the five annotations. Its two uses here are not equivalent and are reviewed separately: IPR013094 is a fold domain and its mapping to hydrolase activity is a fold-to-activity inference, whereas IPR017157 is a subfamily signature matching residues 19-403 and its mapping to carboxylic ester hydrolase activity is well-grounded.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT reference behind both IBA rows. All WITH/FROM entries on both rows were resolved individually. The two rows used different PANTHER nodes and behaved differently: the membrane row drew on a tight set of three type II membrane proteins, while the hydrolase-activity row drew on a clade mixing esterases, amidohydrolases and a bifunctional esterase/dehydratase, which is why its term is generic. Neither IBA is self-referential.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Behind the located_in membrane row, from ARBA:ARBA00028763 and InterPro:IPR017157. Notable in this review because the conclusion it reaches is not backed by AADACL3's own UniProt feature table, which carries no transmembrane feature at all; comparison with the identically predicted tandem paralog AADACL4 shows the gap is in UniProt's coverage, not in the annotation.

title: Complete sequencing and characterization of 21,243 full-length human cDNAs.
review_notes: Cached title matches. The FLJ full-length cDNA project, cited by UniProt as the source of the AADACL3 transcript from placenta. It is the basis of the transcript-level protein-existence call and contributes nothing about function; it produced no GO annotation, which is correct.

title: Role of endoplasmic reticulum neutral lipid hydrolases.
review_notes: Cached title matches; abstract only, and the abstract covers AADAC and KIAA1363 without mentioning AADACL3. Retained as background on why this family is expected at the endoplasmic reticulum membrane, and deliberately not used to support any AADACL3-specific claim.

title: KIAA1363-A Multifunctional Enzyme in Xenobiotic Detoxification and Lipid Ester Hydrolysis.
review_notes: Cached title matches the citation and the full text was retrieved from PMC9229287, so the quotes above come from the article body rather than an abstract. The most useful reference for this gene: it states in so many words that AADACL3 has no established function, which independently corroborates the PubMed search rather than relying on an absence of hits, and it supplies the family topology and substrate range that the propagated annotations rest on. It is a review, so it is used for family-level framing and for its explicit statement about AADACL3, not as primary evidence for any AADACL3 activity.

title: PANTHER node PTN009058710: which GO term is true of every donor? (shared node-level audit for AADACL2, AADACL3 and AADACL4)
review_notes: Shared node-level audit for the three paralogs, reproducible with audit_node_PTN009058710.py in the AADACL2 bioinformatics folder. It reaches the same lowest-common-ancestor conclusion this review reached, by a different route, and supplies two donor resolutions this gene's own analysis reported as unresolved or weak.

title: Is AADACL3's esterase annotation a fold name, or is the catalytic machinery really there?
review_notes: Analysis written for this review (analyze.py), re-runnable, with sequences, active-site features, InterPro signature matches, InterProScan topology predictions and the PROSITE pattern all fetched live at run time; a missing or empty record raises rather than being counted as absence, and a second run reproduces both RESULTS.md and results.json byte for byte. It was designed to be able to falsify the annotations under review in either direction: had Ser193, Asp347 or His377 read as something other than serine, aspartate and histidine, or had the triad failed to align onto curated active sites, the ester-hydrolase terms would have been argued down; had SignalP called a cleaved signal peptide as it does for AADACL2, the membrane terms would have been. It also records the observations that cut against a tidy story - the PROSITE PS01174 miss, the split Pfam match with the shortest first segment in the panel, and the two-helix rather than single-pass topology call - and resolves the PROSITE miss to individual pattern positions instead of letting it stand as a bare negative. Extended after PR review to add the subfamily-versus-fold signature table (section 6), and again to add the nucleophile audit of the IBA source set (section 7) and the mouse ortholog of the query to the panel. The audit reads its WITH/FROM tokens from the gene's own AADACL3-goa.tsv so they cannot drift from the record under review, resolves model-organism identifiers through the Alliance API and Arabidopsis loci through UniProt, and reports the three tokens it cannot resolve to a single reviewed entry as unresolved rather than dropping them - so the 13-of-14 serine count is a count of what was actually readable. That count is superseded by the shared node audit in genes/human/AADACL2/AADACL2-bioinformatics/, which resolves BNA7 directly through xref:sgd-S000002836 to Q04066 rather than through the Alliance record and so reports 15 of 16 donors with a serine nucleophile; the sole non-serine donor is HIDH either way. Its stated limits are that the topology calls are predictions that cannot name a compartment, and that nothing in it demonstrates catalytic activity.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AADACL3 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched Affinage record. Gates passed, but the record is empty - zero discoveries, zero citations, and the narrative reads "No mechanistic discoveries found in literature." For a gene this dark that restraint is the right output, and nothing was imported from it. Because an empty provider record is not itself evidence that literature is absent, PubMed was searched independently, which returned seven records, all GWAS, selection-scan, resequencing or bulk expression studies and none an assay of the protein; the family review PMID:35736449 then confirms the position in prose.

title: UniProtKB record Q5VUY0 (ADCL3_HUMAN)
review_notes: The primary record for the gene, and mostly notable for what it lacks: no FUNCTION, no CATALYTIC ACTIVITY, no SUBUNIT and no SUBCELLULAR LOCATION comment, protein existence at transcript level only, Pharos Tdark, and only two references, both sequencing papers. The substantive statements used from it are the RecName EC number 3.1.1.-, the ECO:0000305 GDXG lipolytic enzyme family assignment, and the three propagated ACT_SITE features, which are inferences from mouse Nceh1 and so cannot themselves validate the family-derived GO terms. Its missing transmembrane feature is treated as a coverage gap rather than as evidence, on the basis of the identical predictions on AADACL4.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Source of three of the five rows. Both InterPro signatures behind them were checked: IPR013094 is the generic Abhydrolase_3 fold domain and can only support the general hydrolase parent, whereas IPR017157 is the arylacetamide-deacetylase subfamily signature and supports the specific ester term.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Source of both IBA rows. All 21 WITH/FROM tokens across the two rows were resolved - 19 to UniProt accessions, the remaining two being the ancestral PANTHER nodes themselves, which have no sequence; neither row is self-referential, and the rows use different PANTHER nodes (PTN009058710 for hydrolase activity, PTN009058713 for membrane), which is why they differ in how informative they can be.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Source of the located_in membrane row. Its WITH/FROM tokens (SL-0162, ARBA00028763, IPR017157) all encode the same UniProt subcellular-location statement, which is an ECO:0000305 inference over an ECO:0000255 topology prediction, so this row is not independent support for the IBA membrane row.

title: The DNA sequence and biological annotation of human chromosome 1.
review_notes: Included to document what the UniProt record is actually built on. Genome-sequence papers of this kind report no functional data for individual loci, so no supporting quote is drawn from it.

title: Superfamily-wide portrait of serine hydrolase inhibition achieved by library-versus-library screening.
review_notes: Cited only for the methodological claim that grounds the suggested activity-based profiling experiment. Abstract-only in the cache, and any AADACL4 mention is in supplementary material that was not consulted, so no gene-specific claim is drawn from it.

title: The metabolic serine hydrolases and their functions in mammalian physiology and disease.
review_notes: A review, not a primary study of AADACL4, and it mentions the gene only within a section on poorly characterised hydrolases - hence MEDIUM rather than HIGH. It is nonetheless the only publication located that discusses AADACL4 as a gene rather than as a row in a genomics table, and it is the authoritative statement that no functional characterisation existed. Verified from the cached PMC full text; the AADACL1 in the quoted sentence is NCEH1/KIAA1363.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics defines keratinocyte differentiation in avian scutate scales.
review_notes: Chicken mRNA co-expression, and the B suffix indicates a bird-specific duplicate whose orthology to human AADACL4 is not established here. Recorded as a lead in suggested_questions only; no annotation rests on it.

title: PANTHER node PTN009058710: which GO term is true of every donor? (shared node-level audit for AADACL2, AADACL3 and AADACL4)
review_notes: Node-level audit shared by the three paralogs that carry this identical row, kept in the AADACL2 bioinformatics folder and reproducible with audit_node_PTN009058710.py there. The WITH/FROM sets are read from the committed GOA TSVs and, independently, fetched per accession from QuickGO for all three paralogs, with the two sources cross-checked and a gene covered by neither treated as a hard error; every donor's chemistry, nucleophile and GO ancestry is fetched at run time, and the mechanism verdict comes with a sensitivity analysis over the positional nucleophile rule. It corrects one premise this review had relied on: soybean HIDH is a bifunctional dehydratase/carboxylesterase, not a non-hydrolase, so it refutes only the serine mechanism term and not the hydrolase parent.

title: Is human AADACL4 a catalytically competent GDXG hydrolase?
review_notes: Analysis written for this review. Every sequence, feature and comment is fetched from the UniProt REST API at run time and the report is regenerated by the script, so a fresh run reproduces the committed file; no value is hard-coded. The script also verifies each non-PANTHER WITH/FROM resolution against the resolved entry's own UniProt cross-references and aborts on a mismatch, so the donor identities in this review are checked rather than asserted, and it derives the alignment-reliability cut from the computed percent identity rather than from a hand-labelled set, aborting if any panel member lands within 0.75 points of the threshold.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AADACL4 (human)
review_notes: Gates passed but the record is empty (n_discoveries 0, citation_count 0). Treated as absence of a provider result rather than evidence that no literature exists: the UniProt reference list and an independent Europe PMC search were checked separately, and did surface one review that discusses the gene.

title: UniProtKB entry Q5VUY2 (ADCL4_HUMAN), Arylacetamide deacetylase-like 4
review_notes: The primary source for the family assignment, the feature table and the evidence codes behind the membrane annotations. Every quote above was checked against a single physical line of the cached file.

title: Characterization of the human gene encoding alpha-aminoadipate aminotransferase (AADAT).
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary cloning/characterization of human AADAT establishing the 2-aminoadipate aminotransferase activity and lysine-degradation role. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Crystal structure of human kynurenine aminotransferase II.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes KAT II identity, kynurenine to KYNA activity and PLP-dependence. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Substrate specificity and structure of human aminoadipate aminotransferase/kynurenine aminotransferase II.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Definitive biochemical/structural characterization; source of the aminoadipate, kynurenine, methionine and glyoxylate-linked activity annotations.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; high-throughput mitochondrial proteome supporting the mitochondrion location annotation.

title: Nonsense mutations in AAGAB cause punctate palmoplantar keratoderma type Buschke-Fischer-Brauer.
review_notes: Cached record (abstract-only) title matches the citation. Cited inside the UniProt FUNCTION quote used elsewhere in this review, so listed here explicitly. It establishes the disease link and nothing about molecular function beyond a hedge, which is why no annotation derives from it.

title: Haploinsufficiency for AAGAB causes clinically heterogeneous forms of punctate palmoplantar keratoderma.
review_notes: Cached full text matches the cited title. The original disease-gene paper and the source of UniProt's hedged "May be involved in endocytic recycling of growth factor receptors" FUNCTION line. Superseded as a functional account by the later assembly-chaperone work; cited here for the disease link.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Large-scale Y2H interactome; the source of three protein-binding annotations. Individually weak, but it recovered AP2S1 and AP1S3, consistent with six other independent screens and with the focused mechanistic literature.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Large-scale interactome; recovered AP1G1 and AP2S1.

title: An interactome perturbation framework prioritizes damaging missense mutations for developmental disorders.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Interactome perturbation study; recovered AP2S1.

title: AAGAB Controls AP2 Adaptor Assembly in Clathrin-Mediated Endocytosis.
review_notes: Cached full text matches the cited title. The paper that established AAGAB as an AP-2 assembly chaperone.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. HuRI binary interactome; recovered AP1G1, AP2A2, AP2S1 and AP1S3 - the full expected client set in a single screen.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. BioPlex AP-MS, methodologically orthogonal to the two-hybrid screens; recovered AP2A2, AP2S1 and AP1S3.

title: AAGAB is an assembly chaperone regulating AP1 and AP2 clathrin adaptors.
review_notes: Cached record title matches; abstract-only cache, but every claim used is in the abstract. The clearest single statement of AAGAB's function, and the primary support for the proposed GO:0051131 annotation.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Endogenous split-tag immunoprecipitation, so the AP2S1 interaction is detected at native expression levels; the strongest of the high-throughput recoveries.

title: The adaptor protein chaperone AAGAB stabilizes AP-4 complex subunits.
review_notes: Cached full text matches the cited title. Extends the chaperone role to a third adaptor complex, from an independent laboratory.

title: Oligomer-to-monomer transition underlies the chaperone function of AAGAB in AP1/AP2 assembly.
review_notes: Cached full text matches the cited title. Structural basis of the chaperone cycle and the link to PPKP1A truncating mutations.

title: An AAGAB-to-CCDC32 handover mechanism controls the assembly of the AP2 adaptor complex.
review_notes: Cached full text matches the cited title. This is the sole source for the "released before the tetramer is complete" claim, which is what makes AAGAB satisfy the defining clause of GO:0051131 ("chaperone molecules that do not form part of the finished complex"). It is also the reason the complex-binding replacement terms are marked as interim stand-ins rather than accepted at face value.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Multimodal cell-map study; the seventh independent recovery of the AAGAB-AP2S1 interaction.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AAGAB (human)
review_notes: External precomputed LLM research, treated as a preliminary source; every claim used was re-verified against the cited PMIDs. Unusually good for this provider - it correctly identified the assembly-chaperone role, the two-module architecture, the CCDC32 handoff and the AP-3 exemption. Its GO grounding was nonetheless wrong in an instructive way: it proposed GO:0044183 protein folding chaperone, a term whose definition explicitly concerns binding unfolded proteins to fold them, which is not what AAGAB does. That grounding was not imported, and the gap it exposed is filed under proposed_new_terms.

title: Phosphorylation of the AP2 mu subunit by AAK1 mediates high affinity binding to membrane protein sorting signals.
review_notes: Direct site-mapping and biochemical evidence for the core AAK1-AP2M1 mechanism. AP2 was purified from pig brain and tested with recombinant AAK1, so this is conserved mammalian biochemistry rather than a purely human-cell assay.

title: Identification of an adaptor-associated kinase, AAK1, as a regulator of clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
review_notes: Foundational direct interaction, kinase, localization, and endocytosis evidence. The study uses human full-length AAK1 together with rat/bovine preparations and human HeLa/A431 cell assays, so individual findings retain their model context.

title: Differential requirements for AP-2 in clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
review_notes: Direct human-cell AP2/endocytosis study, but its positive phenotype is driven by full-length AAK1 overexpression and is kinase-independent; partial RNAi produced no phenotype, an important redundancy/residual-activity caveat.

title: AAK1-mediated micro2 phosphorylation is stimulated by assembled clathrin.
review_notes: The cached abstract directly supports clathrin-dependent activation of AAK1, a core regulatory mechanism. Full experimental and species details are unavailable locally, so no assay context beyond the abstract is inferred.

title: A novel AAK1 splice variant functions at multiple steps of the endocytic pathway.
review_notes: Direct isoform, clathrin-binding, AP2-kinase, and loss-of-function recycling evidence. The cache contains only the abstract plus a failed PDF placeholder, so detailed cell/species context cannot be independently audited.

title: AAK1 regulates Numb function at an early step in clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
review_notes: The cached abstract supports the reported Numb localization and cargo-selective phenotypes, but the central Numb-T102 substrate claim is contradicted by PMID:42082516: purified AAK1/BMP2K did not phosphorylate the site, RPE phosphoproteomics did not detect it, and its sequence lacks the refined recognition motif. Preserve the localization phenotype; do not treat T102 phosphorylation as established.

title: The adaptor-associated kinase 1, AAK1, is a positive regulator of the Notch pathway.
review_notes: Direct mammalian-cell evidence supports activated-Notch binding, stabilization, endosomal sorting, and positive pathway regulation. Its secondary Numb model is not propagated because that arm depends on the now-disputed PMID:18657069 claim.

title: Identification of novel ATP13A2 interactors and their role in α-synuclein misfolding and toxicity.
review_notes: The cached abstract verifies the ATP13A2 interactor screen but contains no AAK1 or AAK1L mention. Because the full text and supplement are unavailable in cache, the pair cannot be evaluated mechanistically; the generic protein-binding term remains uninformative.

title: Αvβ3-integrin-mediated adhesion is regulated through an AAK1L- and EHD3-dependent rapid-recycling pathway.
review_notes: Direct human HeLa-cell depletion and structure-function evidence for the long AAK1 isoform. EHD3 is a cooperating factor, so the recycling phenotype is not attributable solely to AAK1L.

title: Family-wide Structural Analysis of Human Numb-Associated Protein Kinases.
review_notes: Direct structural and biochemical characterization of human AAK1. Constitutive activity is a kinase-domain structural inference; regulation of full-length AAK1 in cells remains context dependent.

title: WNT Activates the AAK1 Kinase to Promote Clathrin-Mediated Endocytosis of LRP6 and Establish a Negative Feedback Loop.
review_notes: Direct gain-of-function, knockdown, inhibitor, trafficking, and AP2M1-phosphorylation evidence in human HEK293T, HT1080, RKO, and related cell models.

title: Dysregulation of the AP2M1 phosphorylation cycle by LRRK2 impairs endocytosis and leads to dopaminergic neurodegeneration.
review_notes: Direct AP2M1 kinase evidence includes recombinant assays and human SH-SY5Y cells. Tissue-distribution conclusions are specifically from mouse and are not presented as direct human tissue evidence.

title: AAK1 activation-mediated iron trafficking drives ferroptotic cell death.
review_notes: Direct mechanistic evidence in multiple human cancer cell lines identifies the PKCβII-AAK1-AP2M1-TFR1 iron-uptake axis. The tumor-growth result is a human-cell xenograft in mice, and ferroptosis is an induced contextual role rather than necessarily AAK1's basal core function.

title: AAK1-mediated phosphorylation of PDLIM5 and Talin1 promotes focal adhesion disassembly to accelerate cell migration.
review_notes: Direct human RPE-cell genetics, biochemistry, phosphoproteomics, imaging, and focal-adhesion assays. The PDLIM5/Talin1 discovery initially combines AAK1 and BMP2K perturbation, but AAK1-specific genetics establish the migration role. Its negative NUMB Thr102 evidence materially disputes PMID:18657069 and is recorded as counterevidence rather than silently accepting the older claim.

title: LOC66273 isoform 2, a novel protein highly expressed in white adipose tissue, induces adipogenesis in 3T3-L1 cells.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Not cited by GOA for the human gene, but it is the source of the mouse Aamdc IDA and IMP annotations to GO:0045600 from which the human IBA derives, so it was read directly to check whether that IBA is well founded. It is: the evidence is bidirectional (overexpression sufficient, knockdown deleterious). Abstract-only cache, but both claims used are explicit in the abstract.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Proteome-scale two-hybrid map; the source of two single-publication protein-binding annotations (ACY3, GORASP2) with no functional follow-up.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. HuRI binary interactome; source of the VPS9D1 protein-binding annotation.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Cached record title matches and the study itself is sound - correctness is VERIFIED, not LOW_QUALITY; the issue is the weight of its data for THIS gene, which is a relevance question. It contributed five of AAMDC's eight protein-binding annotations (APP, HTT, ATXN3, DNM2, GDAP1) from one systematic yeast two-hybrid pass over ~500 neurodegeneration-related baits. A single small uncharacterised protein scoring against all five within that one pass is more consistent with a promiscuous hit than with five distinct biological interactions, and none has been independently replicated or pursued. Note that the title phrase "Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains" describes aggregation found in postmortem patient brain tissue, not contamination of the interaction dataset; an earlier draft of this review misread it as the latter.

title: The oncogene AAMDC links PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling with metabolic reprograming in estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer.
review_notes: Cached full text matches the cited title. The only substantial human functional study of AAMDC and the source of both proposed new annotations. Note the authors' own hedging on the RABGAP1L interaction ("can interact", "we provide evidence"), which is why the endolysosome annotation is proposed as non-core with the colocalisation caveat stated.

title: Solanine Represses Gastric Cancer Growth by Mediating Autophagy Through AAMDC/MYC/ATF4/Sesn2 Signaling Pathway.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Recorded deliberately without deriving an annotation from it. It is the second human functional study of AAMDC and does corroborate the MYC/ATF4 axis outside breast cancer, placing AAMDC upstream of MYC, ATF4 and Sesn2 in gastric cancer cells. It is set aside because the experimental frame is the pharmacology of solanine rather than AAMDC itself - AAMDC enters as a rescue arm, where its overexpression reverses solanine's effect on autophagy - and the affinage report that surfaced it grades the finding Low confidence. An autophagy-related process annotation would need a study designed around AAMDC.

title: Is a molecular function assignable to AAMDC from its family?
review_notes: Reproducible analysis written for this review (analyze_mth938.py), re-runnable, with every figure fetched at run time from the InterPro, UniProt and QuickGO REST APIs. Added in response to PR review feedback asking that the central negative finding - that no molecular function is justifiable - be tested rather than merely asserted. The result substantiates it and goes further, indicating where to look instead. A first version of the script claimed to query InterPro but only interpolated a hardcoded accession; that was corrected after review, and the report now records InterPro's own entry name and protein count. Failed API calls are distinguished from genuinely empty results in both the script and the report, since a silent fetch failure would otherwise manufacture the negative finding this analysis exists to test.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AAMDC (human)
review_notes: External precomputed LLM research, treated as a preliminary source; every claim used was re-verified against PMID:33772001. Two things are worth recording. First, its mechanism_profile reports molecular_activity as none, which is the correct answer for this protein and a useful negative signal - the provider did not invent a function. Second, it covers only the human cancer literature and does not mention the mouse adipogenesis work that underpins the gene's name and its single best-supported GO annotation, so the IBA assessment had to be done outside the report.

title: Angio-associated migratory cell protein is expressed as an extracellular protein by blood-vessel-associated mesenchymal cells.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Source of the cell-surface IDA and the angiogenesis NAS. The cache holds only the citation and no abstract body, so no quote could be taken from it; the claims it supports are corroborated here from PMID:7743515 and PMID:26350504 instead.

title: Blockade of angio-associated migratory cell protein inhibits smooth muscle cell migration and neointima formation in accelerated atherosclerosis.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation; abstract-only, but the structured abstract states the results used here explicitly. Note the discrepancy flagged in this review: GOA codes the annotation from this paper as IEP, yet the paper reports overexpression, siRNA, antibody-blockade and in vivo perturbation experiments, which is IMP-grade evidence.

title: A function for AAMP in Nod2-mediated NF-kappaB activation.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Basis for the Reactome "AAMP binds NOD2" reaction and for the innate-immune arm described in the gene description. No annotation is derived from it here: the NF-kappaB modulation is reported but its mechanism and its independence from the cytoskeletal role are unresolved, so it is raised in suggested_questions instead.

title: AAMP Regulates Endothelial Cell Migration and Angiogenesis Through RhoA/Rho Kinase Signaling.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Establishes the RhoA/Rho-kinase mechanism in endothelial cells and is a primary support for the proposed GO:0051057 annotation. Abstract-only, but the quoted results are stated there.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Large-scale interactome; one of four screens reporting the functionally uncharacterised AAMP-AEN interaction.

title: An interactome perturbation framework prioritizes damaging missense mutations for developmental disorders.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Interactome perturbation study; another recovery of AAMP-AEN.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. HuRI binary interactome; another recovery of AAMP-AEN.

title: Angio-associated migratory cell protein (AAMP) interacts with cell division cycle 42 (CDC42) and enhances migration and invasion in human non-small cell lung cancer cells.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Independent evidence, from a different laboratory and a second Rho-family GTPase, that AAMP binds and positively regulates small GTPases - which is what makes GO:0031267 rather than a RhoA-specific claim the right generalisation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. BioPlex AP-MS - methodologically orthogonal to the two-hybrid screens, which is the strongest argument that the AAMP-AEN pair is real, even though it remains functionally uncharacterised.

title: AAMP promotes colorectal cancermetastasis by suppressing SMURF2-mediatedubiquitination and degradation of RhoA.
review_notes: Cached full text matches the cited title. The title as indexed contains missing spaces ("cancermetastasis", "SMURF2-mediatedubiquitination"); that is how it appears in the source record and is reproduced verbatim here rather than silently corrected. Primary support for the proposed GO:0031267 and GO:0050821 annotations, and the clearest mechanistic account of how AAMP raises active RhoA.

title: AAMP and MTSS1 Are Novel Negative Regulators of Endothelial Barrier Function Identified in a Proteomics Screen.
review_notes: Cached full text matches the cited title. Added after PR review feedback pointed out that it was cached by this PR but cited nowhere, while two claims depended on it. It is the third independent laboratory to report AAMP-dependent Rho GTPase regulation, extends it to RhoB, and is the sole source for the proposed endothelial-barrier annotation.

title: Identification of a new immunoglobulin superfamily protein expressed in blood vessels with a heparin-binding consensus sequence.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. The founding paper for AAMP and the source of the quantitative heparin-binding IDA, which is one of only two molecular functions the gene has. Abstract-only, but both quoted claims are in the abstract.

title: AAMP, a conserved protein with immunoglobulin and WD40 domains, regulates endothelial tube formation in vitro.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Early functional evidence that anti-AAMP antibody inhibits endothelial tube formation, corroborating the angiogenesis annotation that GOA currently supports only by NAS.

title: AAMP binds to TBXA2R
review_notes: Reactome reaction; source of one cytosol TAS annotation.

title: AAMP binds EGFR
review_notes: Reactome reaction; source of one cytosol TAS annotation.

title: AAMP gene expression is positively regulated by VEGF
review_notes: Reactome reaction; source of one cytosol TAS annotation, and consistent with the VEGF-dependent upregulation reported in PMID:26350504.

title: AAMP binds NOD2
review_notes: Reactome reaction; source of one cytosol TAS annotation, modelling the NOD2 interaction from PMID:19535145.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AAMP (human)
review_notes: External precomputed LLM research, treated as a preliminary source; every claim used was re-verified against the cited PMIDs. Its main value here was assembling the scattered RhoA/RhoB/CDC42 literature into one mechanistic picture, which is what made the three proposed annotations possible - GOA and UniProt between them mention Rho only once, in a hedged "may act through the RhoA pathway". Its GO grounding (GO:0098772, GO:0008092, GO:0060090, GO:0008289) was not imported; GO:0008289 lipid binding in particular has no support in the cited literature and looks like a spurious inference from the heparin and glycosaminoglycan work.

title: cAmp regulation of arylalkylamine N-acetyltransferase (AANAT, EC 2.3.1.87): a new cell line (1E7) provides evidence of intracellular AANAT activation.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false). Directly establishes human AANAT catalytic activity, cytoplasmic localization, and cAMP activation; the UniProt EC and cytoplasm experimental evidence derive from this paper.

title: Significant association of the arylalkylamine N-acetyltransferase (AA-NAT) gene with delayed sleep phase syndrome.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Supports the circadian-rhythm (IMP) annotation and the A129T variant recorded in UniProt (VAR_055086).

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Large-scale binary interactome map; source of a bare "protein binding" IPI for AANAT. AANAT-specific partners are in supplementary data, not the abstract text. Uninformative for molecular function.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Large-scale interaction-perturbation study; source of a bare "protein binding" IPI. Uninformative for AANAT molecular function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome; source of a bare "protein binding" IPI. Uninformative for AANAT molecular function.

title: N-acetylation of serotonin
review_notes: Reactome reaction directly describing the core AANAT-catalyzed step.

title: Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis
review_notes: Reactome pathway context (serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) containing the AANAT-catalyzed step.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Early proteome-scale two-hybrid map; source of the first AAR2-EAPP protein-binding annotation, which has no functional follow-up.

title: Crystallization and biochemical characterization of the human spliceosomal Aar2-Prp8(RNaseH) complex.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. This is the paper that justifies transferring the yeast Aar2p mechanism to the human protein, and therefore underpins the IBA and ISS annotations. It is also the UniProt SUBUNIT evidence (ECO:0000269|PubMed:26527271). Abstract-only, but the orthology claim quoted is explicit there.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Large-scale interactome; second recovery of AAR2-EAPP.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. BioPlex AP-MS; third and methodologically orthogonal recovery of AAR2-EAPP, which makes the physical interaction credible without making it informative.

title: TSSC4 is a component of U5 snRNP that promotes tri-snRNP formation.
review_notes: Cached full text matches the cited title. This is the reference that distinguishes the TSSC4 protein-binding annotation from the three EAPP ones: it is a dedicated functional study rather than a screen, and it establishes TSSC4 as a U5 snRNP assembly chaperone, making the AAR2-TSSC4 interaction mechanistically expected.

title: Structural and functional investigation of the human snRNP assembly factor AAR2 in complex with the RNase H-like domain of PRPF8.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation; abstract-only, but the quoted results are stated there. Flagged in this review because GOA codes all three of its annotations (GO:0000387, GO:0005682, GO:0048025) as NAS, whereas the paper reports a crystal structure, designed interface variants that fail to bind PRPF8, and SEC interaction mapping - direct experimental results on the human protein.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AAR2 (human)
review_notes: Trust gate TRIPPED, but on inspection this is a false positive worth recording. The gate fires when the narrative's opening names a non-human organism in a human record - the ADA symbol-collision failure mode - and here it names yeast. It is not a collision: the narrative correctly covers yeast Aar2p, in which the mechanism was established structurally, and human AAR2, its genuine ortholog. UniProt itself annotates the human FUNCTION as ECO:0000250|UniProtKB:P32357, by similarity to the yeast protein, so a yeast-centred account is the correct description of this gene's literature. Every claim used here was re-verified against the cited PMIDs. The gate did its job by prompting the check; it simply needs curator adjudication for genes whose mechanism was worked out in yeast.

title: Aard is specifically up-regulated in Sertoli cells during mouse testis differentiation.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Establishes the expression pattern that is essentially all that is known about this gene, and describes it plainly as "a gene of unknown function". Expression data only - deliberately not converted into a GO process annotation.

title: Alanine and arginine rich domain containing protein, Aard, is directly regulated by androgen receptor in mouse Sertoli cells.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Important for what it does not license: being a direct transcriptional target of androgen receptor signalling is a downstream relationship, not participation in that pathway, so it does not support an androgen-receptor-signalling process annotation for AARD. This is the same conflation identified for the mouse A1bg growth-hormone annotation earlier in this campaign, and it is avoided here rather than repeated. The paper's own "important in spermatogenesis" is a statement about the AR programme, not a demonstrated AARD requirement - no AARD loss-of-function experiment has been reported.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. The HuRI binary interactome, and the sole source of every GO annotation AARD has. The study itself is sound and large-scale; the caution here concerns what its data support for this particular prey, whose 15 partners show the coiled-coil bias and compartment scatter characteristic of a promiscuous two-hybrid prey.

title: Are AARD's reported interactors a coherent partner set?
review_notes: Reproducible analysis written for this review (analyze_partners.py), re-runnable, with partner accessions read from the gene's own AARD-goa.tsv so they cannot drift from the record under review, and all protein data fetched from the UniProt REST API at run time. Failed fetches are reported rather than silently counted as absence. It tests one specific falsifiable hypothesis - coiled-coil bias - against a fetched background rate, rather than asserting either the bias or the enrichment. Extended after PR review to add that null model, to collapse UniProt's hierarchical location strings to top-level compartments (which reduced an inflated "20 locations" to 14), and to enumerate AARD's PANTHER family.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AARD (human)
review_notes: External precomputed LLM research, treated as a preliminary source; both claims used were re-verified against the cited PMIDs. Notable as a negative signal done well: its mechanism_profile reports no molecular activity, no localisation and no partners, and the narrative says so in prose rather than manufacturing a plausible function. For a gene this dark that restraint is the useful contribution. It also did not attempt to convert the androgen-receptor target relationship into a pathway role.

title: The C-Ala domain brings together editing and aminoacylation functions on one tRNA.
review_notes: Full-text mechanistic study. It supports conserved Gly/Ser-tRNA(Ala) editing specificity and functional conservation of human C-Ala, but the human evidence is a cross-species domain graft rather than a direct full-length human Gly-tRNA(Ala) deacylation assay; it therefore supports only a cautious ISS claim.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. This high-throughput fractionation study is relevant only to the broad HDA membrane tuple; its own caveat makes it unsuitable evidence that soluble AARS1 has a functional membrane location.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. This source supports context-specific high-throughput detection in a B-cell exosome preparation, not a constitutive exosomal role for AARS1.
