review_notes: Supports mitochondrial localization; corroborative high-throughput evidence only.

title: Cloning and sequence analysis of a full length cDNA encoding human mitochondrial 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase.
review_notes: Abstract verified. Supports gene identity and mitochondrial thiolase assignment; does NOT support the NAS cholesterol-biosynthesis annotation, which is recommended for removal.

title: BRCA1 affects lipid synthesis through its interaction with acetyl-CoA carboxylase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; verbatim quotes used. Establishes the BRCA1-ACC1 regulatory interaction (basis for the GO:0005515 IPI annotations).

title: TRB3 links the E3 ubiquitin ligase COP1 to lipid metabolism.
review_notes: Abstract-only; the with/from for the IPI is mouse Trib3 (Q8K4K2). ACC is the substrate targeted for degradation; supports a regulatory protein interaction.

title: Aldo-keto reductase family 1 B10 affects fatty acid synthesis by regulating the stability of acetyl-CoA carboxylase-alpha in breast cancer cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only; directly reports AKR1B10-ACCA co-immunoprecipitation and cytoplasmic co-localization (basis for the O60218 IPI).

title: Identification and characterization of proteins interacting with SIRT1 and SIRT3: implications in the anti-aging and metabolic effects of sirtuins.
review_notes: Abstract-only and does not name ACACA in the abstract; the SIRT1 (Q96EB6) interaction is IntAct-curated from the full interactome. Supports only a generic protein binding annotation.

title: Induced polymerization of mammalian acetyl-CoA carboxylase by MIG12 provides a tertiary level of regulation of fatty acid synthesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports both the acetyl-CoA carboxylase activity IDA and the MID1IP1 interaction, and the citrate/polymerization activation mechanism.

title: Crystal structure of Spot 14, a modulator of fatty acid synthesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only; primarily a S14 structure paper but reports the MIG12-ACC polymerization mechanism (basis for the ISS carboxylase activity and MID1IP1 IPI annotations).

title: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase inhibition by ND-630 reduces hepatic steatosis, improves insulin sensitivity, and modulates dyslipidemia in rats.
review_notes: Abstract-only; directly assays ACC enzymatic activity (basis for the IDA acetyl-CoA carboxylase activity annotation) and establishes ACC as a metabolic-disease drug target.

title: Structural basis for regulation of human acetyl-CoA carboxylase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache but the abstract itself is rich; verbatim quotes support the catalytic activity, cytosolic ACC1 vs mitochondrial ACC2 distinction, and the citrate/BRCA1 filament regulation.

title: Pin1 Exacerbates Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease by Enhancing Its Activity through Binding to ACC1.
review_notes: Full text available; Co-IP, GST pull-down and IF establish the direct Pin1-ACC1 interaction (basis for the Q13526 IPI) and its activating effect on ACC1.

title: Cloning of human acetyl-CoA carboxylase cDNA.
review_notes: Abstract-only; original human ACC cloning paper, basis for the TAS acetyl-CoA carboxylase activity annotation.

title: The subcellular localization of acetyl-CoA carboxylase 2.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Establishes ACC2 mitochondrial (outer membrane) localization and the CPT1-inhibition rationale. Note the GOA nuclear IDA derived from this paper is not supported by the abstract.

title: TRB3 links the E3 ubiquitin ligase COP1 to lipid metabolism.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Concerns ACC regulation broadly; the ACACB IPI is with mouse Trib3 (Q8K4K2, BHF-UCL). Supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: Expression, purification, and characterization of human and rat acetyl coenzyme A carboxylase (ACC) isozymes.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Direct biochemical characterization of human ACC2 activity; basis for the EXP catalytic-activity annotation.

title: Characterization of recombinant human acetyl-CoA carboxylase-2 steady-state kinetics.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Direct malonyl-CoA-formation assay on human ACC2; strong support for the core catalytic function.

title: Molecular mechanism for the regulation of human ACC2 through phosphorylation by AMPK.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Structural/mechanistic study of human ACC2 activity and its AMPK regulation; supports the EXP catalytic-activity annotation.

title: The N-terminal domain of human holocarboxylase synthetase facilitates biotinylation via direct interaction with the substrate protein.
review_notes: Abstract-only and general (does not name ACACB). Cited for the ACACB-HLCS (P50747) IPI (biotinylation enzyme-substrate); supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: Induced polymerization of mammalian acetyl-CoA carboxylase by MIG12 provides a tertiary level of regulation of fatty acid synthesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Establishes the ACC-MIG12 interaction and citrate-dependent polymerization/activation; basis for IPI, identical-protein-binding, and IDA activity annotations.

title: Crystal structure of Spot 14, a modulator of fatty acid synthesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Supports the ACC2 IDA activity, acetyl-CoA metabolic process, protein homotetramerization, and IPI (MIG12) annotations attributed to this PMID.

title: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase inhibition by ND-630 reduces hepatic steatosis, improves insulin sensitivity, and modulates dyslipidemia in rats.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Direct demonstration of ACC2 catalytic inhibition and its therapeutic relevance; supports the IDA activity annotation.

title: Isolation and characterisation of a cDNA encoding the precursor for a novel member of the acyl-CoA dehydrogenase gene family.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes ACAD8 as an ACAD-family member by sequence only; basis for the general (now superseded) acyl-CoA dehydrogenase and lipid metabolic TAS annotations.

title: Isolated 2-methylbutyrylglycinuria caused by short/branched-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency: identification of a new enzyme defect, resolution of its molecular basis, and evidence for distinct acyl-CoA dehydrogenases in isoleucine and valine metabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Although titled around the isoleucine-pathway SBCAD defect, the full study assigns ACAD8 as the mitochondrial isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase of valine catabolism.

title: Identification of isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase and its deficiency in humans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Definitive enzymatic identification of ACAD8 and its deficiency; anchors the core molecular function.

title: Variations in IBD (ACAD8) in children with elevated C4-carnitine detected by tandem mass spectrometry newborn screening.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports the valine-catabolism function and the IBDD disease association via newborn-screening genetics.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. High-throughput interactome screen; the ACAD8-VSTM2A hit is uninformative of ACAD8's molecular function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. High-throughput proteomic support for mitochondrial localization; consistent with matrix ACAD.

title: isobutyryl-CoA + FAD => methacrylyl-CoA + FADH2
review_notes: Reactome curated reaction; matches UniProt catalytic activity and matrix localization.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment hypothesis: ACAD9 (Q9H845) very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity (GO:0017099)
review_notes: In-repo OpenScientist report for the chain-length-specificity hypothesis. Verdict over-annotated (long-chain, not very-long-chain) - independently corroborates our MODIFY of GO:0017099 to GO:0004466 via an enzymatic + substrate-cavity structural analysis. The structural residue claim (Thr-139/Ala-143) is a computational lead from this report; the enzymatic evidence (PMID:16020546, PMID:33320993) is independently cited and verbatim-checked in this review.

title: Human acyl-CoA dehydrogenase-9 plays a novel role in the mitochondrial beta-oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. This is the ACAD9 characterization paper, not an MCAD study; it is the cited support for MCAD's matrix/membrane GO localizations but only informs MCAD indirectly. Used here only for localization context.

title: Prolonged moderate-intensity exercise without and with L-carnitine supplementation in patients with MCAD deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified clinical study. Supports MCAD's in vivo FAO role; the carnitine-process annotations it underpins are indirect compensatory physiology, not direct MCAD functions.

title: Molecular characterization of medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD) deficiency: identification of a lys329 to glu mutation in the MCAD gene, and expression of inactive mutant enzyme protein in E. coli.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Direct genetic and biochemical evidence for MCAD function and the tetramer-assembly requirement; underpins multiple core annotations.

title: Protein misfolding is the molecular mechanism underlying MCADD identified in newborn screening.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Strong support for MCAD molecular function, homotetrameric quaternary structure, and the misfolding loss-of-function disease mechanism.

title: Characterization of wild-type and an active site mutant of human medium chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase after expression in Escherichia coli.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes MCAD catalytic activity, FAD content, and the catalytic-base mechanism; primary support for the core MF and FAD-binding functions.

title: Identification and characterization of new long chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Primary subject is ACAD10/ACAD11/ACAD9, but MCAD is directly assayed and mapped; supports the EXP MF annotation and the (non-core) axon localization.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports the HDA nucleus annotation, which is over-annotated for a mitochondrial matrix enzyme; included for completeness.

title: Identification of a common mutation in patients with medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Foundational genetics of MCAD deficiency; supports the core FAO/activity annotations via loss-of-function.

title: Human METTL20 is a mitochondrial lysine methyltransferase that targets the β subunit of electron transfer flavoprotein (ETFβ) and modulates its activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Primary subject is METTL20/ETFβ; MCAD is used as a model ETF-coupled dehydrogenase, supporting its ETF-dependent FAO process annotation.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. High-throughput confirmation of mitochondrial localization.

title: Purification and properties of short chain acyl-CoA, medium chain acyl-CoA, and isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenases from human liver.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Classic biochemical characterization of native human liver MCAD; establishes homotetramer, FAD content, ETF coupling, and reaction product.

title: Medium-long-chain chimeric human Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase: medium-chain enzyme with the active center base arrangement of long-chain Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Defines MCAD active-site base and the structural basis of medium-chain specificity; primary support for core MF.

title: Role of common gene variations in the molecular pathogenesis of short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Underlies the IMP MF (GO:0003995), IC BP (GO:0006635), and UniProt FUNCTION and disease annotations for ACADS. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Novel localization of OCTN1, an organic cation/carnitine transporter, to mammalian mitochondria.
review_notes: Abstract is about OCTN1/SLC22A4 mitochondrial localization, not ACADS. MGI used this work to assign an IDA mitochondrion annotation to ACADS (likely as a mitochondrial marker in the study); full text unavailable here. The localization itself is independently correct, so the annotation was accepted rather than challenged.

title: Identification and characterization of new long chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenases.
review_notes: UniProt cites this with experimental evidence (ECO:0000269) for ACADS FUNCTION, catalytic activity, and EC 1.3.8.1. Abstract foregrounds ACAD9/10/11 paralogs, but the full text and UniProt curation support ACADS short-chain activity; the EXP annotation was retained.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Large sperm-nucleus proteomics dataset that is the basis for a spurious nucleus annotation on ACADS (a mitochondrial matrix enzyme). Most consistent with contamination/carryover; annotation marked over-annotated.

title: Molecular cloning and nucleotide sequence of complementary DNAs encoding human short chain acyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase and the study of the molecular basis of human short chain acyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase deficiency.
review_notes: Foundational cloning paper establishing the identity of ACADS; basis for TAS MF annotation.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 high-throughput AP-MS interactome; basis for an uninformative 'protein binding' annotation (WITH DPEP1). Marked over-annotated.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 high-throughput AP-MS interactome; basis for an uninformative 'protein binding' annotation (WITH DPEP1). Marked over-annotated.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Rigorous mitochondrial proteomics supporting ACADS mitochondrial localization (HTP).

title: Purification and properties of short chain acyl-CoA, medium chain acyl-CoA, and isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenases from human liver.
review_notes: Definitive biochemical characterization of human SCAD; basis for IDA MF/BP annotations and core enzymology (homotetramer, FAD, ETF, butyryl-CoA -> crotonyl-CoA).

title: Cloning and characterization of the mouse short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase cDNA.
review_notes: Mouse ortholog cloning paper; clearly states the SCAD role in the first step of beta-oxidation and short-chain substrate specificity. Basis for TAS BP annotation.

title: 2-Methylbutyryl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase deficiency: a new inborn error of L-isoleucine metabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. First documented case of isolated 2-methylbutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency in humans; in vitro oxidation studies showed an isolated block in 2-methylbutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase and a variant abolishing enzyme activity in recombinant protein. Directly supports the core molecular function and the isoleucine catabolic role. Abstract-only in cache but the assayed enzyme is human SBCAD/ACADSB.

title: Isolated 2-methylbutyrylglycinuria caused by short/branched-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency: identification of a new enzyme defect, resolution of its molecular basis, and evidence for distinct acyl-CoA dehydrogenases in isoleucine and valine metabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Reports the first SBCAD gene mutation (exon-10 skipping) causing an isolated defect in isoleucine catabolism, confirms substrate-specific enzyme assay with 2-methylbutyryl-CoA, mitochondrial import, and homotetramer formation, and distinguishes SBCAD (isoleucine) from ACAD8/IBD (valine). Supports MF, BP, location and self-association annotations. Cache is abstract + partial PDF.

title: Role of isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase and short branched-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase in the metabolism of valproic acid: implications for the branched-chain amino acid oxidation pathway.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Characterizes purified human SBCAD as a branched-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase of the isoleucine pathway and shows it is the most likely enzyme for the first dehydrogenation step of valproyl-CoA and is competitively inhibited by valproyl-CoA. Supports the core dehydrogenase activity; the valproate angle is xenobiotic metabolism rather than a distinct core function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteome dataset supporting mitochondrial localization of ACADSB. Corroborates the (more specific) matrix localization but is not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Isolation and expression of a cDNA encoding the precursor for a novel member (ACADSB) of the acyl-CoA dehydrogenase gene family.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Original isolation and heterologous expression of human ACADSB; recombinant enzyme is active toward short branched-chain acyl-CoAs (including (S)-2-methylbutyryl-CoA) and short straight-chain acyl-CoAs (butyryl-CoA, hexanoyl-CoA). Establishes both the core branched-chain and secondary straight-chain dehydrogenase activities. Abstract-only in cache.

title: alpha-methylbutyryl-CoA + FAD => tiglyl-CoA + FADH2
review_notes: Curated Reactome reaction placing ACADSB in the mitochondrial matrix catalyzing the 2-methylbutyryl-CoA to tiglyl-CoA dehydrogenation of isoleucine catabolism. Directly supports the core function and matrix location.

title: LONP1 degrades mitochondrial matrix proteins
review_notes: Reactome event about LONP1-mediated turnover of matrix proteins; annotates ACADSB only as a mitochondrial matrix protein/LONP1 substrate. The matrix location is correct but the context is protein degradation, not SBCAD catalytic function.

title: LONP1 binds mitochondrial matrix proteins
review_notes: Reactome event about LONP1 binding matrix proteins; annotates ACADSB only as a matrix protein bound by LONP1. Correct matrix location, but the context is protein turnover rather than the enzyme's function.

title: Human acyl-CoA dehydrogenase-9 plays a novel role in the mitochondrial beta-oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids.
review_notes: This is the ACAD9 (Ensenauer 2005) paper; its membrane-fractionation data concern ACAD-9, not VLCAD. The mitochondrial-membrane term it is cited for is nonetheless correct for VLCAD on independent grounds, so the annotation was kept as non-core rather than removed.

title: The layered structure of human mitochondrial DNA nucleoids.
review_notes: Supports co-purification with nucleoid preparations but the paper itself states these metabolic proteins do not cross-link mtDNA; cited for a nucleoid-localization annotation that is best treated as an over-annotation.

title: Structural basis for substrate fatty acyl chain specificity: crystal structure of human very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified crystal-structure paper for human VLCAD; directly supports the FAD-binding and very-long-chain substrate-specificity annotations.

title: Identification and characterization of new long chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Primarily about ACAD9/10/11 but provides the substrate-based EC 1.3.8.9 assignment context for VLCAD and the tissue-distribution contrast.

title: Analysis of proteomic changes induced upon cellular differentiation of the human intestinal cell line Caco-2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified screen, but it supports only a correlative expression change; cited for an epithelial-cell-differentiation IEP that over-states VLCAD's role.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified high-throughput interactome. The cited interaction (with the Pol I factor TAF1B) is most plausibly a screening artifact for a mitochondrial inner-membrane enzyme; the "protein binding" annotation is uninformative.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified proteomics resource confirming VLCAD mitochondrial localization.

title: Molecular basis of human mitochondrial very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency causing cardiomyopathy and sudden death in childhood.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes the energy-derivation/cardiac role and disease mechanism of VLCAD.

title: Cloning of human very-long-chain acyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase and molecular characterization of its deficiency in two patients.
review_notes: PubMed-verified foundational VLCAD paper supporting its long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity and FAO role.

title: A novel disease with deficiency of mitochondrial very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports VLCAD long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity via patient deficiency.

title: Catalytic and FAD-binding residues of mitochondrial very long chain acyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Direct mechanistic evidence for VLCAD catalytic activity and FAD binding.

title: Very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase subunit assembles to the dimer form on mitochondrial inner membrane.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes VLCAD homodimerization and inner-membrane localization.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The InterPro2GO mapping behind two annotations on this gene. The hyaluronic acid binding mapping from IPR000538 is correct; the cell adhesion mapping from the same domain entry is not, and is reviewed in detail on that annotation.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/PANTHER phylogenetic transfers. Every WITH/FROM donor was resolved via the Alliance API and each of the four IBA rows includes a true ACAN ortholog (mouse Acan MGI:MGI:99602 or rat Acan RGD:68358), so no row is a pure paralog transfer. The residual problems are term granularity and compartment scoping.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA model annotations covering the Golgi lumen, lysosomal lumen and interstitial matrix gel phase. All three duplicate Reactome or TAS statements already present, and none is a functional location.

title: The structure of aggrecan fragments in human synovial fluid. Evidence for the involvement in osteoarthritis of a novel proteinase which cleaves the Glu 373-Ala 374 bond of the interglobular domain.
review_notes: The paper itself is sound and important - it is the study that defined the aggrecanase cleavage site. It is miscited twice in GOA. It carries an NAS annotation to skeletal system development, which it says nothing about, and an NAS annotation to proteolysis in which aggrecan, the substrate, is recorded as a participant. The extracellular matrix structural constituent TAS from the same paper is defensible but too generic.

title: Interaction of cartilage oligomeric matrix protein/thrombospondin 5 with aggrecan.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. A genuine direct binding study, cited by UniProt for the same interaction with an ECO:0000269 tag. Supports replacing the GO:0005515 annotation with GO:0050840.

title: A missense mutation in the aggrecan C-type lectin domain disrupts extracellular matrix interactions and causes dominant familial osteochondritis dissecans.
review_notes: Cached record title matches; abstract-only cache, but the binding result used here is stated explicitly in the abstract. Cited by UniProt as the ECO:0000269 source for the SSOAOD disease entry. Direct human evidence for extracellular matrix binding by the G3 C-type lectin.

title: Proteomics characterization of extracellular space components in the human aorta.
review_notes: Full text cached. Supports the extracellular matrix localisation, and shows aggrecan is present in vascular as well as cartilaginous matrix. The compression-resistance statement the RCA annotation rests on is made for proteoglycans as a class rather than for aggrecan specifically, so this is weaker support for GO:0030021 than the varicose vein paper.

title: Proteoglycan form and function: A comprehensive nomenclature of proteoglycans.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. An authoritative review and the single most useful synthesis for this gene. It is the TAS source for the gel phase of interstitial matrix annotation; the hydrated-gel claim is fully supported, but the review is describing cartilage, so the interstitial scoping of that GO term is the reviewer's caveat rather than a problem with the paper.

title: Extracellular matrix remodelling in response to venous hypertension: proteomics of human varicose veins.
review_notes: Full text cached. The better of the two RCA sources for GO:0030021, because it states the compression-resistance mechanism for aggrecan specifically rather than for proteoglycans as a class, and it supports the extracellular matrix localisation with both discovery and targeted proteomics.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Cached record title matches, and the study is technically sound as a screen; the issue is what a single hit from it can support. The aggrecan-APP pair is one candidate interaction among tens of thousands, in an assay that cannot reproduce the glycosylation or compartment of a secreted proteoglycan, with no orthogonal validation and no follow-up anywhere in the aggrecan literature. Basis for marking the GO:0005515 annotation over-annotated.

title: Novel missense ACAN gene variants linked to familial osteochondritis dissecans cluster in the C-terminal globular domain of aggrecan.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. Human genetic and functional evidence localising a matrix-binding activity to the G3 C-type lectin repeat, and the strongest support for the proposed extracellular matrix binding function.

title: Aggrecan immobilizes to perineuronal nets through hyaluronan-dependent and hyaluronan-independent binding activities.
review_notes: Full text cached and read; residue numbering is explicitly against human ACAN P16112, so the structural and biophysical results are human data rather than transferred. This is the published version of a bioRxiv preprint that the affinage record cited without a PubMed identifier, so it is used here in its peer-reviewed form. The basis for recommending that GO:0005540 be upgraded from InterPro IEA to a direct experimental code.

title: Aggrecan binds Hyaluronan and HAPLN1
review_notes: The one Reactome reaction that captures aggrecan's actual molecular function. Only a generic extracellular region compartment is exported from it to GOA, which is the clearest example of informative pathway content being flattened into an uninformative annotation.

title: Defective B4GALT1 does not transfer Gal to the keratan chain
review_notes: A Reactome disease reaction modelling a congenital disorder of glycosylation. Aggrecan appears only as the acceptor whose glycanation fails, so exporting a normal-physiology Golgi lumen location for aggrecan from it is an artifact of reaction-level export. Five of the fourteen Golgi lumen rows on this gene arise this way.

title: HTRA1 hydrolyzes ACAN (Aggrecan)
review_notes: Records aggrecan as a substrate of HTRA1, which is the correct direction for that relationship and a useful contrast with the incorrect involved_in proteolysis annotation on this gene.

title: ACAPs are arf6 GTPase-activating proteins that function in the cell periphery.
review_notes: Cached title matches the citation and full text was retrieved from PMC2185579, so every quote above is checked against the article body rather than an abstract. The founding paper for the gene and the pivot of this review: it establishes ACAP1's ARF6 GAP activity, its lipid dependence, the R448Q catalytic mutant, and the ARF6-dependent endosomal and surface pools. It is also the paper whose evidence GO captured on the paralog ACAP2 (three IDAs) and not on ACAP1 (zero annotations, confirmed by QuickGO query), which is the finding this review reports.

title: Phosphorylation of ACAP1 by Akt regulates the stimulation-dependent recycling of integrin beta1 to control cell migration.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Abstract only, so quotes are drawn from the abstract; the mutagenesis detail used in this review (S554A abolishes ITGB1 binding and migration, S554D enhances binding) is taken from the UniProt feature table, which cites this paper with ECO:0000269, rather than from the abstract. This is the source of UniProt's experimentally supported recycling endosome membrane location, which reaches GO only as an IEA.

title: Cooperation of phosphoinositides and BAR domain proteins in endosomal tubulation.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Abstract only. The cellular counterpart to the in vitro curvature work, and the source of the K274N phosphoinositide-binding mutant recorded in UniProt with ECO:0000269 for this PMID. Weighted MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the tubulation phenotype depends on co-overexpression of PIP5K1C, so it demonstrates a capacity rather than a physiological event.

title: Regulation of Arf6 and ACAP1 signaling by the PTB-domain-containing adaptor protein GULP.
review_notes: Cached title matches. PMC1930157 is restricted so only the abstract is cached, but the abstract is unusually explicit, enumerating the four levels of regulation, and the GULP1 interaction it reports is corroborated independently in UniProt SUBUNIT with ECO:0000269 for this PMID. Notable as one of the seven ACAP1 primary papers that produced no GO annotation on ACAP1.

title: Systematic identification of SH3 domain-mediated human protein-protein interactions by peptide array target screening.
review_notes: Cached title matches, and the paper genuinely reports the assay from which the GRB2 annotation derives, so the citation is correct. Relevance is LOW because the assay tests a synthetic peptide rather than ACAP1, the ACAP1-GRB2 pair was not among those the authors validated by co-immunoprecipitation, and no functional consequence has been reported since. Cited here to justify marking the resulting protein binding row over-annotated.

title: An ACAP1-containing clathrin coat complex for endocytic recycling.
review_notes: Cached title matches and full text was retrieved from PMC2064835. The basis for treating ACAP1 as a coat component and cargo adaptor rather than only as a GAP, and the source of the direct CLTC interaction recorded in UniProt SUBUNIT. Its title names endocytic recycling, yet ACAP1 has no endocytic recycling annotation in GO at all.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Cited against the annotation it produced rather than for it: the authors state that they stripped peripheral membrane proteins and that much of what remained was only transiently membrane-associated, which is exactly the class ACAP1 belongs to. Useful as confirmation that ACAP1 protein is detected in an NK-like line, consistent with its bone-marrow and lymphoid expression, but not as evidence for any particular membrane.

title: Mechanistic insights into regulated cargo binding by ACAP1 protein.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Abstract only, but it carries the two claims used here - the ITGB1 recycling sorting signal and the phosphorylation-relieved autoinhibition - explicitly. The crystallography that underpins them (3JUE, 3T9K, 4F1P, residues 378-740 with ITGB1 peptide) is corroborated by the UniProt PDB cross-references and the S554 mutagenesis entries.

title: The Arf6 GTPase-activating proteins ARAP2 and ACAP1 define distinct endosomal compartments that regulate integrin α5β1 traffic.
review_notes: Cached title matches and full text was retrieved from PMC4215208. Valuable because it is independent of the Hsu laboratory and because it supplies the one loss-of-function phenotype for ACAP1 (accelerated integrin internalisation on knockdown), which is what distinguishes the genuine traffic role from the overexpression-driven actin readouts.

title: A PH domain in ACAP1 possesses key features of the BAR domain in promoting membrane curvature.
review_notes: Cached title matches, and full text is available from PMC4198613, so every quote above is checked against the article body. Corrected from an earlier reading of this reference as abstract-only: the cache carries full_text_available true with an XML extraction, and the Results section supplies the direct in vitro assay (liposome binding and negative-stain EM tubulation of purified BAR-PH), the negative BAR-domain result in both the liposome assay and the cryoEM reconstruction, the F280 mutagenesis series, and the dimerisation measurements - none of which the abstract contains. This is the basis for GO:0180020 membrane bending activity as a core molecular function and for GO:0042803 protein homodimerization activity as a non-core one, and it is the reference that fixes the domain attribution: PH domain bends, BAR domain self-associates.

title: Phospho-tyrosine dependent protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Cached title matches and full text is available. The citation is correct, but the annotation it supports is problematic on its own terms: a pY-dependent GRB2 interaction presupposes a phosphotyrosine on ACAP1, and UniProt records no tyrosine phosphorylation of ACAP1 - only 3'-nitrotyrosine at 485 and a Y712F mutant with no phenotype. Relevance LOW.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Cached title matches and full text is available; the two quotes are the authors' own statements about how their data should be read. A high-quality resource cited for a low-value annotation: of its three ACAP1 partners, UQCRB is a mitochondrial complex III subunit and NEBL a cardiac Z-disc protein, neither reachable by this protein, while FCHSD2 is mechanistically sensible but seen in one screen.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Cached title matches. The citation is correct and the study is a legitimate one, but ACAP1 is incidental prey in a neurodegeneration-focused screen, and four of its six partners here are mitochondrial (UQCRC2) or nuclear (SETDB1, KAT5, LMO3). The word "candidate" in the authors' own description of the 30000 interactions is the appropriate weighting.

title: A Rab10-ACAP1-Arf6 GTPases cascade modulates M4 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor trafficking and signaling.
review_notes: Cached title matches the citation. Reports that Rab10-GTP recruits ACAP1 to inactivate ARF6 and thereby hold the M4 muscarinic receptor in early endosomes. Consistent with the established mechanism - a third cargo handled by the same ARF6-GAP step - and it would extend ACAP1's cargo range beyond ITGB1 and GLUT4. No annotation is drawn from it here because it is abstract-only in the cache and because the compartment reported, Rab5-positive early endosomes, differs from ACAP1's established recycling-endosome location, so it needs full-text reading before it can support a location or process term.

title: PTPN9 dephosphorylates FGFR2 pY656/657 through interaction with ACAP1 and ameliorates pemigatinib effect in cholangiocarcinoma.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Reports ACAP1 bridging the sec14p domain of PTPN9 to FGFR2 to permit dephosphorylation at pY656/657, with the PH and Arf-GAP domains required. A scaffolding role distinct from anything else on record for this gene, from a single cholangiocarcinoma study, so no annotation is proposed. Recorded because if it replicates it would be a genuine second molecular function for ACAP1, and because it is a plausible route by which a protein-binding-style annotation could enter the record with real mechanism behind it, unlike the screen hits.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACAP1 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched Affinage record; its self_evaluation_pairwise is win and all ten citations are genuine numeric PMIDs, with no bioRxiv DOIs in PMID-shaped fields. Its narrative is broadly accurate and it correctly surfaced the two papers this review had not otherwise reached, PMID:36917255 (Rab10-ACAP1-ARF6 cascade on the M4 muscarinic receptor) and PMID:37505213 (ACAP1 bridging PTPN9 and FGFR2). Marked UNVERIFIED rather than VERIFIED because no sentence from it is used as supporting text anywhere in this review: every mechanistic claim here is quoted from a primary PMID or from the UniProt record instead. Its own GO grounding should not be imported - it offers GO:0005198 structural molecule activity and GO:0060090 molecular adaptor activity where the specific GO:0140312 cargo adaptor activity and GO:0180020 membrane bending activity are available, and omits the GAP activity that is the protein's defining function.

title: ACAPs are arf6 GTPase-activating proteins that function in the cell periphery.
review_notes: Cached title matches the citation and the cache carries full text, not just the abstract. This is the founding characterisation of ACAP2 and the source of three of its GOA annotations (GO:0005096 IDA, GO:0001726 IDA, GO:0030029 IDA). Every quantitative claim used here was read from the Results, including the HeLa (human) provenance of the ARF6 protrusion experiments, which matters for whether the process evidence is human.

title: Vaccinia virus K1L protein supports viral replication in human and rabbit cells through a cell-type-specific set of its ankyrin repeat residues that are distinct from its binding site for ACAP2.
review_notes: Cached title matches; cited by the affinage record, so adjudicated here rather than left unassessed. It is a real ACAP2 interaction but the paper's conclusion is that the host-range function of K1L is separable from ACAP2 binding, so it supports no inference about ACAP2's own function and is not used for any annotation. Not in GOA either.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Correctly cited, but a bulk membrane-fraction proteome of one NK-like cell line is weak support for a localisation claim, and the study's own caveats undercut it for a peripheral membrane protein. Basis for the GO:0016020 HDA row, which is marked over-annotated on those grounds rather than on any doubt that the peptides were detected.

title: Rab35 regulates phagosome formation through recruitment of ACAP2 in macrophages during FcγR-mediated phagocytosis.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Independent demonstration of the RAB35-to-ACAP2-to-ARF6 relay, cited in support of the proposed GO:0032013 annotation. Deliberately NOT used to propose a phagocytosis annotation, because the abstract says only that the work is in macrophages and the cache is abstract-only, so the species is not stated and an ISS transfer cannot be justified from it. The gap is recorded in suggested_questions instead.

title: Rab35 regulates Arf6 activity through centaurin-β2 (ACAP2) during neurite outgrowth.
review_notes: Cached title matches. The experiments are in rat PC12 cells, which is the donor evidence behind the rat Acap2 annotations that GOA transfers to human by ISS - so it is the paper that makes the GO:1990090 ISS row traceable, and the reason that row is judged real but cell-type-specific.

title: The PI(3)P interactome from a colon cancer cell.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Weak, non-specific corroboration for phosphoinositide binding - 681 hits from a single affinity matrix - so it is cited alongside the proposed GO:0035091 annotation but is explicitly not the basis for it. Not in GOA.

title: Rab35, acting through ACAP2 switching off Arf6, negatively regulates oligodendrocyte differentiation and myelination.
review_notes: Cached title matches and the cache has full text. Cited for the ARF6-inactivation relationship supporting the proposed GO:0032013 annotation, not for the differentiation phenotype, which is in rodent oligodendrocyte-lineage cells and so would need an ortholog-based transfer rather than a human annotation.

title: Structure-function analyses of the small GTPase Rab35 and its effector protein centaurin-β2/ACAP2 during neurite outgrowth of PC12 cells.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Establishes the specificity that GO:0031267 cannot express, since GO:0017137 Rab GTPase binding is now a secondary id of GO:0031267 and that term has no children. A caution is recorded in the notes file - the Asn-610/Asn-691 residues named in this paper are not on the same numbering as the human mutagenesis in PMID:30905672 (Asp-721, Arg-727, Met-731, Asp-756), so they must not be quoted as human positions. The affinage record does quote them as ACAP2 positions, which is why no residue-level claim in this review is sourced from it.

title: Human ACAP2 is a homolog of C. elegans CNT-1 that promotes apoptosis in cancer cells.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Used for one claim only, that ACAP2 binds phosphoinositides, which is stated in the abstract. Abstract-only, so neither the lipid species nor the assay format can be checked, which is why the proposed annotation uses the parent term GO:0035091 rather than a specific phosphoinositide child. The apoptosis result is deliberately NOT proposed as an annotation, being a single unreplicated study whose own authors note that ACAP2 is not caspase-cleaved, so the tCNT-1 mechanism does not carry over. Recorded as a knowledge gap and an experiment instead.

title: Rab35/ACAP2 and Rab35/RUSC2 Complex Structures Reveal Molecular Basis for Effector Recognition by Rab35 GTPase.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Abstract-only in the cache, but the structural claims used here are stated in the abstract and are independently visible in the UniProt record, which cites this PubMed id for the SUBUNIT, DOMAIN, SUBCELLULAR LOCATION and MUTAGEN blocks and lists PDB 6IF3 (1.50 A, residues 601-770). Supports the GO:0005515/RAB35 IPI, the GO:0005886 IDA, and the statement that ACAP2 is not a GAP for RAB35.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Correctly cited proteome-scale AP-MS resource. Its ACAP2 result (partner UniProtKB:Q96P50, ACAP3) is one of two orthogonal recoveries of that pair, so the interaction is probably real; the row is marked over-annotated because the term is uninformative, not because the screen is suspect.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Methodologically orthogonal to BioPlex (endogenous tagging rather than overexpression), which is why the ACAP2-ACAP3 pair is judged likely real. Also relevant as endogenous evidence for the compartment ACAP2 occupies. Same over-annotation assessment as the BioPlex row, on the term rather than the data.

title: RNF126 Promotes Ovarian Cancer Progression by Reprogramming Lipid Metabolism Through Degradation of ACAP2.
review_notes: Cached title matches the citation, and it is adjudicated here because the affinage record cites it. Not used for any annotation, because ACAP2 is the substrate rather than the agent, so the finding concerns ACAP2's regulation and not its function, and it is a single 2026 report that has not been independently replicated. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than VERIFIED because only the abstract is available and the mechanistic claims were not checked.

title: ACAP2 WITH/FROM resolution and domain-architecture check
review_notes: Reproducible analysis written for this review, in response to PR feedback that the blow domain-architecture and MGI:MGI:2153589 claims were load-bearing but had no in-repo artifact. The script resolves every WITH/FROM token from primary APIs (UniProt, Alliance of Genome Resources, WormBase, FlyBase, PANTHER, QuickGO), reports domain architectures, and asks of each source what evidence it holds for the term it donates. Nothing is hardcoded; unresolvable tokens are reported as UNRESOLVED rather than guessed, and there are none in the current output. All five quotes above were grep-verified against the generated file.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACAP2 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched Affinage record; self_evaluation_pairwise win, faith 100%. Its value here was the reference list rather than the prose. It surfaced PMID:22045739, PMID:22344257, PMID:24600047, PMID:25694427, PMID:25853217, PMID:16806385 and PMID:40251363, four of which materially shaped this review, and none of which is cited by any GOA row. The prose is unreliable at residue resolution, which is the reason for the LOW_QUALITY mark: it presents Asn-610 and Asn-691 as residues "within the minimal Rab35-binding domain of ACAP2" without noting that PMID:25694427's numbering does not correspond to the human sequence, whose ANK repeats span 640-735 and whose RAB35-contact mutagenesis is at Asp-721, Arg-727, Met-731 and Asp-756. Its own GO grounding (catalytic activity acting on a protein, molecular function regulator activity) is also too coarse to import. review_notes: Fetched and read in full (PMC7615549) in response to review, having previously been asserted only through the affinage narrative. It is the primary source for the MWT374-376/unique-region targeting motif, the giantin/golgin-45 redundancy, the SCFD1-SEC22B upstream step, the GOLD-SEC22B longin interaction and the two-step sequential model. It reconciles with UniProt's DOMAIN line rather than contradicting it: the paper itself calls the motif's location "the UR of the GOLD domain" and notes that UniProt's giantin attribution rests on a yeast two-hybrid result (PMID:11590181) whose recruitment model giantin knockdown did not support.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACBD3 (human)
review_notes: Gates passed with pairwise = win, and its breadth is genuinely useful - it synthesises 30+ primary papers, though what this review took to be its most valuable contribution - the absence of acyl-CoA - turned out to be its most damaging. But it states that PI4KB is recruited 'through its GOLD domain', and that is wrong: UniProt is explicit that the Q domain (241-308) binds PI4KB and TBC1D22A/B while the GOLD domain (384-526) binds picornaviral 3A proteins. An earlier draft of this review propagated that error into seven places by quoting the provider verbatim as supporting_text instead of checking it against UniProt. Marked MISCITED for that specific claim; the quote has been removed from every supported_by block. The lesson is the campaign's own rule applied to itself - a provider sentence is a lead, not evidence, even when the record is otherwise strong. Follow-up: the other domain claim in the same paragraph - the MWT374-376 motif binding giantin and golgin-45, and the two-step SCFD1/SEC22B-then-golgins mechanism - was checked against its cited primary paper (PMID:38134218) in a later round and is substantively correct. So the record's error rate on domain assignments is real but not uniform; the defect on the MWT claim was this review citing the provider narrative rather than the primary paper, not the claim itself. MISCITED is retained for the GOLD/PI4KB sentence specifically. Second follow-up, and the more damaging one: this review repeatedly cited the record's silence on acyl-CoA - "synthesises 30+ primary papers and never mentions acyl-CoA once" - as support for calling GO:0000062 an over-annotation. That was a misuse of the source and it reached the wrong answer. ACBD3 acyl-CoA binding is reported (PMID:26290611) and the ACB domain has a gene-specific SREBP1 function (PMID:23166793); the record simply does not cover them. The campaign's own rule says an empty or silent record is not evidence that literature is absent, and I applied the rule to other people's records while breaking it with this one. Its coverage claim should be treated as a lead, never as a negative result.

review_notes: Paper characterizes the Radil PDZ domain and its KIF14 ligand; the cached full text does not establish an ACOX1 PDZ-binding function. The GO:0030165 IDA annotation to ACOX1 is not verifiable from this reference (marked UNDECIDED rather than removed as it is an experimental annotation).

title: Loss- or Gain-of-Function Mutations in ACOX1 Cause Axonal Loss via Different Mechanisms.
review_notes: Full text available; establishes ACOX1 as first/rate-limiting VLCFA beta-oxidation enzyme and H2O2 producer, homodimer (crystal structure + co-IP), peroxisomal localization, and the N237S gain-of-function toxic-homodimer mechanism (Mitchell syndrome).

title: Overexpression and characterization of the human peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase in insect cells.
review_notes: Purified recombinant human ACOX; establishes straight-chain/prostaglandin substrate specificity, direct electron transfer to O2 with H2O2 production, C12-18 optimum, and A/B/C chain processing.

title: Molecular cloning and functional expression of a human peroxisomal acyl-coenzyme A oxidase.
review_notes: Cloning and functional expression of human AOX; catalytically active, carries the C-terminal SKL PTS1 signal, peroxisome-dependent accumulation.

title: Molecular characterization of the human peroxisomal branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase: cDNA cloning, chromosomal assignment, tissue distribution, and evidence for the absence of the protein in Zellweger syndrome.
review_notes: Primarily characterizes the branched-chain oxidase (ACOX2) but documents the two-oxidase division in human liver peroxisomes and confirms ACOX1 (palmitoyl-CoA oxidase) oxidizes very-long straight-chain fatty acids and eicosanoids.

title: Separate peroxisomal oxidases for fatty acyl-CoAs and trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA in human liver.
review_notes: Establishes a distinct peroxisomal trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA oxidase in human liver (i.e. ACOX2), separate from palmitoyl-CoA oxidase; supports peroxisomal localization and the bile-acid-intermediate role. Cited quotes verified verbatim against the cached abstract.

title: ACOX2 deficiency: An inborn error of bile acid synthesis identified in an adolescent with persistent hypertransaminasemia.
review_notes: Primary experimental (IDA/IMP) source: patient R225W mutation causes accumulation of C27 intermediates and loss of C24 bile acids; WT (not mutant) ACOX2 enhances THCA to cholic acid conversion; peroxisomal localization confirmed by immunofluorescence. Directly supports the bile-acid biosynthesis and THCA-CoA oxidase core functions.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput (BioPlex) interactome study yielding a bare "protein binding" (ACOX2-STRN3) annotation. Correctly cited but functionally uninformative for ACOX2; marked as over-annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary (Y2H) interactome map yielding a bare "protein binding" (ACOX2-DYNLT1) annotation. Correctly cited but functionally uninformative for ACOX2; marked as over-annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale (BioPlex 3.0) interactome study yielding a bare "protein binding" (ACOX2-STRN3) annotation. Correctly cited but functionally uninformative for ACOX2; marked as over-annotation.

title: Molecular characterization of the human peroxisomal branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase: cDNA cloning, chromosomal assignment, tissue distribution, and evidence for the absence of the protein in Zellweger syndrome.
review_notes: Original molecular characterization of human ACOX2 (hBRCACox): 681-aa protein, C-terminal SKL PTS1, peroxisomal (absent in Zellweger livers), human homolog of rat THCC oxidase. Supports peroxisomal localization and identity. Quotes verified verbatim.

title: UniProtKB entry Q99424 (ACOX2_HUMAN), Peroxisomal acyl-coenzyme A oxidase 2
review_notes: Curated UniProt record. Source of FUNCTION, catalytic activities (EC 1.3.3.6; Rhea reactions for THCA-CoA, pristanoyl-CoA, decanoyl/hexadecanoyl-CoA), FAD cofactor, homodimer subunit, peroxisome subcellular location, and CBAS6 disease association.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified proteomics survey; ACOX3 is a bulk hit. Does not inform ACOX3 molecular function and the "membrane" localization is non-specific for a matrix-soluble enzyme.

title: A novel case of ACOX2 deficiency leads to recognition of a third human peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the primary FUNCTION/CATALYTIC ACTIVITY/TISSUE reference in the UniProt record (EC 1.3.3.6 evidence). Establishes ACOX3's branched-chain role and normal-tissue expression. Abstract-only in cache; detailed catalytic claims anchored to the UniProt record.

title: Mammalian peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidases. III. Molecular characterization of human branched chain fatty acyl-CoA oxidase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified conference proceedings (abstract/title only in cache); supports peroxisomal localization of the enzyme. Full text not available.

title: Evidence for the existence of a pristanoyl-CoA oxidase gene in man.
review_notes: PubMed-verified original characterization of the human ACOX3 (pristanoyl-CoA oxidase) gene; establishes identity, PTS1 signal, and low baseline expression. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Beta-oxidation of pristanoyl-CoA
review_notes: Reactome pathway providing the branched-chain beta-oxidation context for ACOX3's substrate (pristanoyl-CoA).

title: (2S)-pristanoyl-CoA + O2 => trans-2,3-dehydropristanoyl-CoA + H2O2 (ACOX3)
review_notes: Reactome pathway entry directly modeling ACOX3's pristanoyl-CoA oxidase reaction; consistent with UniProt catalytic activity.

title: Cargo of PEX5S,L translocates from the cytosol to the peroxisomal matrix
review_notes: Generic peroxisomal import reaction; explains the transient cytosol/matrix annotations rather than ACOX3-specific biology.

title: PEX5S,L:Cargo binds PEX13:PEX14:PEX2:PEX10:PEX12 (Docking and Translocation Module)
review_notes: Generic peroxisomal import docking reaction; not ACOX3-specific.

title: Identification and molecular modeling of a novel, plant-like, human purple acid phosphatase.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Added after PR review pointed out that an earlier draft asserted three times that no primary literature exists for this gene - a claim contradicted by the UniProt file the review was itself citing, which lists this paper as the ECO:0000303 source for the 'Purple acid phosphatase long form' AltName. The error was over-reading an empty affinage record: an empty provider result is evidence about the provider's coverage, not proof that no literature exists. The paper also improves the review's argument, since it shows the kidney bean template is a deliberate published choice for a protein argued to be plant-like, rather than an arbitrary cross-kingdom transfer.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACP7 (human)
review_notes: Gates passed, but the record is empty - 'No mechanistic discoveries found in literature' with no citations. An earlier draft of this review treated that as positive evidence that no literature exists; PMID:16793224 shows it is not. The correct reading is narrower: affinage found no MECHANISTIC discoveries, which is consistent with a gene whose only paper is a bioinformatic identification and structural model rather than a functional study. Useful as a signal about the kind of literature present, not as proof of its absence.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Correctly applied. All with/from donors for this GO_REF on ACRBP (pig Q29016, mouse Q3V140) are true 1:1 orthologs of human ACRBP within PANTHER PTHR21362, which has a single reviewed member per mammalian genome. The one row transferred under it that does not survive review (GO:0002080 acrosomal membrane) fails on term scoping, not on the orthology judgement.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAN-GO annotation for this gene. With/from cites mouse and pig, not human ACRBP, so it is not self-referential; the target term (acrosomal vesicle, is_active_in) is the compartment in which every known ACRBP function occurs.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Mechanically correct mapping of SL-0243 "Secreted" to GO:0005576. The resulting annotation is true but uninformative for this gene, and is kept as non-core rather than challenged.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Compara's ortholog call agrees with PANTHER's: mouse Acrbp is the 1:1 ortholog of human ACRBP. All three terms transferred under this GO_REF derive from IMP annotations on the mouse whole-gene knockout (PMID:27303034), and all three duplicate manual UniProt ISS rows.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Third independent route to the correct acrosomal-vesicle compartment. Redundant with the IBA and the UniProt ISS, but not wrong.

title: Identification of proacrosin binding protein sp32 precursor as a human cancer/testis antigen.
review_notes: The only primary human paper on this gene, and the source of the sequence-identity figures that license every ISS annotation on it. Full text available and read. It also records that Southern blotting suggested two OY-TES-1-related genes in the human genome, which is unresolved and noted in the gene notes as a caution rather than used here.

title: The proacrosin binding protein, sp32, is tyrosine phosphorylated during capacitation of pig sperm.
review_notes: Correctly cited. This is the source of pig ACRBP's GO:0002080 acrosomal membrane IDA, which the human ISS row transfers; the paper's method is indirect immunofluorescence, which cannot resolve acrosomal matrix from acrosomal membrane, and that resolution limit is the basis for the MODIFY on that row. Also the source of pig's GO:0048240 sperm capacitation TAS, which was not propagated to human here because it is author-statement evidence and no human data exist.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Correctly cited, and the mass-spectrometric identification is not disputed, but the paper is a catalogue rather than a localisation study and cannot support a nucleoplasmic assignment for a signal-peptide-bearing secretory protein whose organelle is physically apposed to the sperm nucleus. Basis for MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED on GO:0005634, not for REMOVE.

title: Alteration in the processing of the ACRBP/sp32 protein and sperm head/acrosome malformations in proprotein convertase 4 (PCSK4) null mice.
review_notes: Correctly cited, and used only for what it shows: that the mature form of ACRBP is required for proacrosin autoactivation in vivo. ACRBP is the substrate in this paper, not the agent, so no annotation for ACRBP follows from the PCSK4 relationship itself. The authors' own hedge that ACRBP lacks a convertase consensus site is recorded in the gene notes.

title: Two functional forms of ACRBP/sp32 are produced by pre-mRNA alternative splicing in the mouse.
review_notes: Correctly cited and methodologically sound throughout, including the claim that the two-form arrangement is confined to mouse among the ACRBPs examined: that is an RT-PCR result rather than mere silence, and the same laboratory restates it for human explicitly in PMID:30606959. An earlier draft of this review marked the reference DISPUTED on the strength of the human ENST00000536350 annotation; that was wrong, because a genome annotation does not outrank an expression experiment on the question of what is transcribed. The finding in file:human/ACRBP/ACRBP-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md is best read as an unreconciled discrepancy between GENCODE and this paper, recorded here as a knowledge gap rather than as a fault in the reference.

title: Biogenesis of sperm acrosome is regulated by pre-mRNA alternative splicing of Acrbp in the mouse.
review_notes: The source of the mouse IMP annotations for acrosome assembly, spermatid development and fertilization that all six ortholog-transfer rows on this gene depend on. The knockout removes the whole gene, so those source annotations are gene-level; the isoform partition is a separate result within the same paper. Abstract-only in the cache; PMC restricts the full text, and all quotes used are from the abstract.

title: Behavior of ACRBP-deficient mouse sperm in the female reproductive tract.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Resolves the mechanism behind the knockout's fertility defect and is the primary basis for the proposed GO:0060046 regulation of acrosome reaction annotation. The authors are explicit that the oviductal sperm-number deficit alone would have supported the opposite, migration-based interpretation, and they argue against it. Its introduction also carries the load-bearing statement of the human isoform negative, which an earlier draft of this review overlooked while citing the paper for other claims; that sentence is why the acrosome-assembly discussion here is framed as a discrepancy rather than as a refutation of PMID:23426433.

title: ACRBP (Sp32) is involved in priming sperm for the acrosome reaction and the binding of sperm to the zona pellucida in a porcine model.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Independent, acute-blockade support for a role in regulating the acrosome reaction, in a second species and by a different experimental logic from the mouse knockout. Its plasma-membrane implication was deliberately not carried into an annotation: how a lumenal, signal-peptide-bearing protein becomes surface-accessible is unexplained, and antibody accessibility is not a localisation assay.

title: An acrosomal protein, sp32, in mammalian sperm is a binding protein specific for two proacrosins and an acrosin intermediate.
review_notes: The founding biochemical characterisation of the family and the source of the binding specificity that GO:0035375 records. Abstract-only in the cache; the quoted claims are all in the abstract. Independently corroborated as the basis of MGI's mouse GO:0016504 ISA annotation, which cites this PMID with/from pig Q29016.

title: Does human ACRBP have a counterpart of the 'rodent-specific' ACRBP-V5 isoform?
review_notes: Analysis performed for this review; all figures fetched live from the UniProt and Ensembl REST APIs with raw responses cached, and the report regenerates byte-identically from both the cache and a fresh refetch. It was written to support the hypothesis that GO:0001675 acrosome assembly is a rodent-isoform-specific over-annotation in human, and it falsified the sequence-level premise of that hypothesis: the human locus does carry a structurally equivalent intron-5 read-through transcript. It does not touch the expression-level premise, which PMID:30606959 reports experimentally and against the human transcript, and the report records that in the three limits at the end of Part 2b. Read on its own it would overstate the case, which is why it is cited alongside that PMID everywhere it is used.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACRBP (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated preliminary source with self_evaluation_pairwise win and all twelve citations resolving to numeric PubMed identifiers; its dated findings were checked against the primary abstracts and none was found to misstate them, and its own confidence grading correctly separates the reproductive literature from the low-confidence cancer-cell knockdown work. Cited here only as corroboration alongside primary quotations, never as the sole support for a mechanistic claim. Its own GO grounding was deliberately not imported: GO:0005886 plasma membrane rests only on the boar antibody-accessibility experiment, and GO:0140313 molecular sequestering activity frames the activity as sequestration when the primary papers describe modulation of zymogen autoactivation in both directions.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/PAINT phylogenetic-transfer reference behind the cytoplasm and vesicle rows. The transfer mechanism is sound here - the WITH/FROM donor is the genuine mouse orthologue - but the terms selected are less precise than the donor's own IDA evidence, which is why both rows are modified rather than accepted.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Mechanical mapping of UniProt SL-0007 acrosome to GO:0001669. Verified against the UniProt record's SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line; the mapping is faithful and the source statement is itself well grounded in human immunocytochemistry.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: Human Protein Atlas immunofluorescence curation, the source of the strongest annotation on this gene. Independently corroborated by human sperm light- and electron-microscopic immunocytochemistry and by two IDA annotations on the mouse orthologue.

title: A monoclonal antibody to human SP-10 inhibits in vitro the binding of human sperm to hamster oolemma but not to human Zona pellucida.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the only paper providing a functional handle on human SP-10 and the basis for the proposed GO:0007342 annotation. Caveats stated in the annotation rather than hidden - heterologous hamster oolemma, antibody inhibition rather than direct binding, and a fertile mouse knockout. Assay is on native protein on human sperm, which is why IDA rather than IMP is proposed.

title: Molecular and developmental studies of a sperm acrosome antigen recognized by HS-63 monoclonal antibody.
review_notes: One of the two references behind the mouse orthologue's IDA annotations to GO:0001669 acrosomal vesicle, established by QuickGO query on UniProtKB:P50289. Cited here only to document what the IBA WITH/FROM donor's own evidence is; not read in full.

title: Interactions of human sperm acrosomal protein SP-10 with the acrosomal membranes.
review_notes: Direct biochemical partitioning of native human sperm SP-10; PubMed-verified. Basis for the proposed GO:0043159 acrosomal matrix annotation and for the topology argument against the cytosolic two-hybrid partners.

title: RNF17, a component of the mammalian germ cell nuage, is essential for spermiogenesis.
review_notes: The second reference behind the mouse orthologue's IDA annotation to GO:0001669, per QuickGO on UniProtKB:P50289. The paper's subject is RNF17; SP-10 appears as an acrosomal marker, which is a normal basis for a localisation annotation. Cited only to document the donor's evidence.

title: Purification and microsequencing of the intra-acrosomal protein SP-10. Evidence that SP-10 heterogeneity results from endoproteolytic processes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Also the source of the direct protein sequencing recorded in UniProt (residues 78-100, 106-122, 127-151), which is why this gene's PE 1 status reflects real protein-level detection.

title: Cloning and sequencing of cDNAs coding for the human intra-acrosomal antigen SP-10.
review_notes: PubMed-verified and correctly cited for the sequence architecture. Its unique-protein, no-significant-homology conclusion was correct for 1990 databases but is now superseded - the C-terminal third is a Ly-6/uPAR three-finger domain (InterPro IPR016054, Pfam PF00021, CDD cd23628). Recorded because that stale conclusion is still repeated in secondary sources, including the affinage record for this gene.

title: TDP-43 is a transcriptional repressor: the testis-specific mouse acrv1 gene is a TDP-43 target in vivo.
review_notes: The identifier and title are correct and the paper is a solid study, but it is the wrong support for ACRV1 involved_in spermatogenesis. It establishes that the mouse acrv1 gene is a TDP-43 target whose transcription is restricted to round spermatids; it assays no property of the ACRV1 protein. Cached copy is abstract-only, but the abstract is unambiguous about the paper's subject. Flagged MISCITED for the specific annotation it supports, not as a criticism of the work.

title: Biochemical and morphological characterization of the intra-acrosomal antigen SP-10 from human sperm.
review_notes: Foundational human localisation study; PubMed-verified. Its acrosome-reaction-dependent exposure result is what makes the primary-versus-secondary binding reconciliation between PMID:10775167 and PMID:8882296 coherent. Cached copy is abstract-only but the abstract carries the localisation conclusions directly.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Correctly cited and a legitimate large-scale resource, but methodologically weak as support for individual gene annotations. IntAct shows all five ACRV1 partners come from this one publication, each recorded three times as three yeast two-hybrid variants (two hybrid array, two hybrid pooling, validated two hybrid) with both partners over-expressed and MI-score 0.56, so the apparent NbExp=3 is one experiment in three flavours. No orthogonal assay supports any of the five pairs, and all five partners are cytosol-facing while ACRV1 is lumenal.

title: Individual disruption of 12 testis-enriched genes via the CRISPR/Cas9 system does not affect the fertility of male mice.
review_notes: Full text available and read. This is the decisive evidence against ACRV1 involved_in spermatogenesis and the reason the proposed fertilisation annotation is framed as participation rather than requirement. Note the limitation the authors state themselves - dispensable at least individually - so redundancy is not excluded.

title: ZNF280A and ACRV1 enhance aerobic glycolysis and drive ovarian cancer progression via the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.
review_notes: Full text available and read; the only loss- and gain-of-function work on human ACRV1 that exists. Deliberately not annotated: ACRV1 is testis-restricted, and these are ovarian cancer lines aberrantly expressing it, so the phenotype describes a consequence of ectopic expression rather than a normal function. Raised as a question for the Consortium instead.

title: Characterization of alternatively spliced human SP-10 mRNAs.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of the isoform abundances used as input to the isoform-versus-domain mapping in the bioinformatics analysis. Explains, together with proteolysis, the heterogeneous SP-10 banding pattern, and shows the abundant isoforms differ only in the disordered spacer.

title: Human SP-10: acrosomal distribution, processing, and fate after the acrosome reaction.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Note that this paper's own closing hypothesis favours sperm-zona binding or penetration, which the later human hemizona result (PMID:10775167) does not support for primary binding; the localisation data it reports are unaffected by that and are what is cited here.

title: Inhibition of bovine fertilization in vitro by antibodies to SP-10.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Reads as contradicting PMID:10775167 on sperm-zona binding but does not: the hemizona assay scores primary binding by acrosome-intact sperm whereas this paper reports secondary (post-acrosome-reaction) binding, and SP-10 is inaccessible before the acrosome reaction. Recorded here so the apparent conflict is not mistaken for a citation error. Bovine rather than human, hence MEDIUM.

title: ACRV1 (SP-10): what the LU domain, the splice isoforms and the family do and do not license
review_notes: Own analysis. Computed from a committed snapshot of UniProt, InterPro and QuickGO in data/, so analyze.py touches no network and a fresh run reproduces RESULTS.md byte-for-byte (verified with diff). Its purpose is to make the no-justifiable-molecular-function claim testable rather than asserted; it deliberately reports the complication that PATE1 and PATE4, ACRV1's nearest structural neighbours by CDD naming, do carry acetylcholine receptor regulator activity.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACRV1 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched affinage record; no self_evaluation_pairwise score, faith_pct 100, and all thirteen citations are genuine numeric PMIDs, which is why it was usable as a lead-generator. Every claim taken from it was re-verified against the cited paper, and two needed correction: it presents the human hemizona and bovine secondary-binding results as a flat contradiction, and it repeats the 1990 no-homology conclusion without noting the Ly-6/uPAR domain. Its own GO grounding (cell adhesion mediator activity, plasma membrane) was not imported.

title: UniProtKB P26436 (ASPX_HUMAN) flat-file record
review_notes: Primary sequence, feature and cross-reference record. Source of the signal peptide, the repeat and disorder features, the eleven ALTERNATIVE PRODUCTS entries, the SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line mapped by GO_REF:0000044, and the INTERACTION block whose NbExp=3 entries the IntAct query showed to be three yeast two-hybrid variants of one experiment.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: The ISS pipeline reference. Used here for two very different outcomes, which is the point: the GO:0016887 row transfers from pig ACTA1, a true ortholog holding its own EXP evidence, while the five AgBase rows transfer from chicken ACTA2, a paralog. The GO_REF itself is sound; the discrimination has to be made per row from the WITH/FROM field.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/PAN-GO. On this gene the pipeline is working: GO:0005200 is IBD-asserted at the conventional-actin node PTN000940351 and IRD-negated at eight divergent descendant nodes, and ACTA1 is on the accepting side. Verified against interpro/panther/PTHR11937/PTHR11937-paint.tsv.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Keyword and subcellular-location mapping; yields the general GO:0005856 cytoskeleton row.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Compara transfer from mouse Acta1 (P68134), a true ortholog. Its GO:0048741 donor annotation is a genuine mouse IDA (PMID:2731651), so unlike the ACTR8 case there is no complex-level projection behind this row.

title: Mutations in the skeletal muscle alpha-actin gene in patients with actin myopathy and nemaline myopathy.
review_notes: The founding ACTA1 disease paper and the source of five TAS rows. Queried by PMID in QuickGO: it carries exactly 5 annotations, all on ACTA1, so it is gene-specific curation and not a projection. The TAS rows rest on the paper's introductory account of the contractile mechanism, which is accurate but generic; its skeletal-specific framing is what licenses the MODIFY of GO:0006936 to GO:0003009.

title: Antisense oligodeoxynucleotide complementary to smooth muscle alpha-actin inhibits endothelial-mesenchymal transformation during chick cardiogenesis.
review_notes: Not cited in ACTA1's GOA rows but it is the sole experimental basis for five of them: the AgBase ISS block transfers this paper's chicken smooth-muscle alpha-actin findings onto human ACTA1 via UniProtKB:P08023. Correctly cited as a paper; entirely irrelevant to ACTA1, whose correct ortholog in the same species (P68139, chicken ACTA1) was not used. Recorded here so the provenance of those five rows is visible.

title: Myotilin is mutated in limb girdle muscular dystrophy 1A.
review_notes: Not cited by any GOA row, and that is the point. UniProt records an ACTA1-TTID (myotilin) interaction from this paper with an experimental ECO:0000269 tag, but no GO:0005515 row on ACTA1 corresponds to it. Queried by PMID, the paper carries 7 annotations in all of GO and every one is on MYOT or mouse Myot - including MYOT's own GO:0051393 alpha-actinin binding IDA - so the curation was done from the myotilin side and never reciprocated onto actin.

title: Nemaline myopathy caused by mutations in the muscle alpha-skeletal-actin gene.
review_notes: Source of the GO:0030240 IMP. Queried by PMID in QuickGO: 1 annotation in all of GO, on ACTA1. Abstract-only in the cache, but the thin-filament phenotype it reports is stated explicitly in the abstract.

title: Production of human skeletal alpha-actin proteins by the baculovirus expression system.
review_notes: Recombinant human skeletal alpha-actin shown to polymerise and depolymerise like native actin and to bind DNase I. Queried by PMID: 3 annotations, 2 on ACTA1 plus the reciprocal DNASE1 row. Gene-specific.

title: Differentiation of human skeletal muscle cells in culture: maturation as indicated by titin and desmin striation.
review_notes: Titled for titin and desmin, but the abstract explicitly names skeletal muscle alpha-actin among the sarcomeric constituents followed by immunofluorescence and reports actin cross-striations in mature myotubes, so the GO:0030017 sarcomere IDA is soundly based despite the title. Queried by PMID: 1 annotation in all of GO.

title: Evidence for a dominant-negative effect in ACTA1 nemaline myopathy caused by abnormal folding, aggregation and altered polymerization of mutant actin isoforms.
review_notes: Supports three rows, but not equally. Its patient-muscle work is strong and grounds the GO:0015629 and GO:0005865 rows; the GO:0001725 stress fiber row rests on transfection of C2C12 myoblasts with actin-EGFP constructs, an ectopic-expression readout in an undifferentiated non-sarcomeric host. The abstract does not mention stress fibers at all. Full text not in the cache, so the row is demoted rather than removed.

title: Defining alpha-skeletal and alpha-cardiac actin expression in human heart and skeletal muscle explains the absence of cardiac involvement in ACTA1 nemaline myopathy.
review_notes: Establishes by direct protein quantification that alpha-skeletal actin is the exclusive sarcomeric isoform of skeletal muscle from infancy, while alpha-cardiac actin predominates in heart and fetal skeletal muscle. This is the load-bearing fact behind both the MODIFY to GO:0003009 and the argument that smooth-muscle and mesenchymal annotations cannot belong to this isoform. Title copied from the cached record after an earlier draft of this review got it wrong from memory.

title: The ubiquitin-specific protease USP25 interacts with three sarcomeric proteins.
review_notes: Also uncited by GOA, and the starker of the two omissions: queried by PMID, this paper carries ZERO annotations in the whole of GO, despite being a dedicated study of sarcomeric-protein interactions whose ACTA1 result UniProt records with an experimental ECO:0000269 tag and with a mapped region (the actin C-terminus) and an isoform preference (USP25m in differentiating muscle).

title: Fatal hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and nemaline myopathy associated with ACTA1 K336E mutation.
review_notes: Grounds the proposed GO:0051371 muscle alpha-actinin binding annotation.
