Actin was isolated from the patient's own muscle biopsy and assayed by in vitro motility, and the K336E mutation reduced affinity for alpha-actinin ten-fold - a measurement that presupposes wild-type ACTA1 binds alpha-actinin. Verified verbatim against the cached abstract rather than taken from the affinage narrative.

title: Interaction of the mycobacterial heparin-binding hemagglutinin with actin, as evidenced by single-molecule force spectroscopy.
review_notes: A real, direct biophysical measurement of an actin-HBHA interaction, but the abstract never states which actin isoform was used, so the assignment to ACTA1 specifically is unverified. Host-pathogen rather than core physiology. Queried by PMID: 2 annotations, ACTA1 and the reciprocal on hbhA.

title: Proteomic analysis of human parotid gland exosomes by multidimensional protein identification technology (MudPIT).
review_notes: High-throughput MS in parotid exosomes, 396 annotations across GO. Correctly cited for what it is; the question it raises is isoform attribution, not citation accuracy.

title: Protein profile of exosomes from trabecular meshwork cells.
review_notes: High-throughput MS in an ocular cell type, 49 annotations across GO.

title: Proteomic analysis of microvesicles from plasma of healthy donors reveals high individual variability.
review_notes: High-throughput MS in plasma microvesicles, 141 annotations across GO.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput MS in prostatic-secretion exosomes, 1046 annotations across GO.

title: Shotgun proteomics reveals specific modulated protein patterns in tears of patients with primary open angle glaucoma naïve to therapy.
review_notes: High-throughput MS in tears, 95 annotations across GO.

title: ALKBH4-dependent demethylation of actin regulates actomyosin dynamics.
review_notes: Source of the Lys-86 methylation on ACTA1 and its removal by ALKBH4. Again a modification received, not an ACTA1 activity.

title: Structural differences explain diverse functions of Plasmodium actins.
review_notes: Carries the EXP annotation to GO:0016887 on pig ACTA1 (P68137) that is the donor for ACTA1's ISS ATP-hydrolysis row. Confirmed by QuickGO query of the donor rather than assumed.

title: A developmental study of the abnormal expression of alpha-cardiac and alpha-skeletal actins in the striated muscle of a mutant mouse.
review_notes: Carries the mouse Acta1 IDA to GO:0048741 that both of ACTA1's skeletal-muscle-fiber- development rows descend from, via Ensembl Compara and via UniProt ISS respectively. Confirmed by QuickGO query of the donor.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 affinity-purification MS, 3731 annotations across GO. IntAct records the ACTA1 row as anti tag coip in HEK293T; the same partner recurs in BioPlex 3.0 by the same method, so the two rows are one pipeline rather than independent replication.

title: SETD3 is an actin histidine methyltransferase that prevents primary dystocia.
review_notes: Source of the His-75 tele-methylhistidine modification on ACTA1, cited in the description as a modification the protein receives. It is a function of SETD3, not of ACTA1, so no ACTA1 annotation follows from it.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: A single yeast two-hybrid screen against a neurodegeneration bait panel, 20010 annotations across GO. IntAct logs every one of its seven ACTA1 partners under three sub-method labels of the same experiment - two hybrid pooling, validated two hybrid and two hybrid array - all at MI-score 0.56 with no orthogonal assay, so UniProt's NbExp=3 is one experiment counted three times. Same pattern the ACRV1 review found in this screen.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0, 9514 annotations across GO; anti tag coip in HCT116, not a muscle line.

title: CDH1-associated CTNNA1 binds F-actin
review_notes: The reaction that exposes how ACTA1 enters an epithelial pathway. Its participant is a generic polymer, F-actin (all) in the cytosol, whose reference entities are all six human actins including ACTA1, so membership is by set rather than by evidence. Checked via ContentService/data/participants/R-HSA-9934486/referenceEntities.

title: ACTA1 bioinformatics: WITH/FROM provenance and actin-isoform peptide specificity
review_notes: This review's own reproducible analyses. Supplies the isoform identity figures, the tryptic-peptide specificity measurement behind the HDA verdicts, and the WITH/FROM resolution table whose counts are asserted against the GOA file.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACTA1 (human)
review_notes: The provider record (gates_passed true, 11 citations, all numeric PMIDs - no bioRxiv ids in PMID-shaped fields). Cited once, for a summary clause every element of which was independently checked against a primary source before use: the sarcomeric thin-filament identity against PMID:1423520 and PMID:15198992, polymerisation against PMID:12849983, the myosin interaction against PMID:10508519 and PMID:16945537, and the alpha-actinin interaction against PMID:16945537 and UniProt's two REGION features. It is used as corroboration of a function this review proposes on other grounds, never as the evidence for one, and none of its mechanistic sentences is quoted. Its own GO grounding was deliberately not imported - it offers GO:0005198 structural molecule activity where the conventional-actin node supports the specific child GO:0005200, and GO:0005634 nucleus, which is a mutant-aggregation phenotype rather than a location of the wild-type protein. Its 11 citations were checked for retraction and erratum along with the rest; none is flagged.

title: UniProtKB entry P68133 (ACTS_HUMAN)
review_notes: Used for the alpha-actinin interaction regions, the by-similarity EC assignment, the subcellular location statement, the HPA tissue-restriction line and the Reactome pathway cross-references. All quoted fragments are single physical lines.

title: Antisense oligodeoxynucleotide complementary to smooth muscle alpha-actin inhibits endothelial-mesenchymal transformation during chick cardiogenesis.
review_notes: The single source behind all five chicken ACTA2 (P08023) annotations that AgBase transferred to human by ISS (GO:0010628, GO:0030027, GO:0030175, GO:0044297, GO:0090131). Verified by querying each of those five rows on P08023 in QuickGO; every one returns this PMID. So the five human ISS rows are five terms from one antisense-knockdown experiment, not five independent findings.

title: Endothelial cell senescence in human atherosclerosis: role of telomere in endothelial dysfunction.
review_notes: A study of endothelial senescence in atherosclerotic coronary arteries. ACTA2 appears as a smooth-muscle immunostaining marker, which supports the cytoplasm localisation it was used for and nothing more.

title: Transcriptional regulation of a contractile gene by mechanical forces applied through integrins in osteoblasts.
review_notes: The rat Acta2 IDA that Ensembl Compara turns into ACTA2's only muscle contraction row. The paper is about transcriptional regulation of the alpha-SMA promoter in osteoblasts, so it is a weak basis for involved_in muscle contraction. The conclusion is right for ACTA2 on independent human evidence; this donor is not what makes it right.

title: Cellular localization of cyclooxygenase-1 and cyclooxygenase-2 in the normal mouse, rat, and human retina.
review_notes: A COX-1/COX-2 immunolocalisation study. ACTA2 is a counterstain marker; QuickGO shows the reference carries GO:0005737 for 12 annotations over 6 entities.

title: Proteomics of human umbilical vein endothelial cells applied to etoposide-induced apoptosis.
review_notes: Cited only to record that ACTG1 holds GO:0005200 by IC from GO:0005856 rather than by IBA. Not evidence about ACTA2.

title: Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of rhabdomyosarcoma cells reveal differential cellular gene expression in response to enterovirus 71 infection.
review_notes: Correctly cited and correctly evidenced as IEP, but the reference-projection check shows it carries GO:0009615 for 20 entities, all IEP, from one microarray/2-DE screen. It records differential expression, not participation in an antiviral process.

title: Functional consequences of a mutation in an expressed human alpha-cardiac actin at a site implicated in familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
review_notes: The source of human ACTC1's GO:0005524 ATP binding IDA, and therefore the donor for the ATP binding row proposed here. Checked because the obvious donor was not usable - Sus scrofa ACTA1 (P68137) supplies the ATP hydrolysis ISS but holds no nucleotide-binding annotation of any granularity, so an ISS from it would have transferred an annotation the donor does not have.

title: Prohibitin suppresses renal interstitial fibroblasts proliferation and phenotypic change induced by transforming growth factor-beta1.
review_notes: The rat Acta2 IEP behind ACTA2's cellular response to TGF-beta row. TGF-beta1 induction of alpha-SMA in fibroblasts is a robust and widely reproduced observation, so the transferred term is well founded even though IEP is expression-level evidence.

title: Development of glomerular endothelial cells, podocytes and mesangial cells in the human fetus and infant.
review_notes: The paper states in its own methods sentence that alpha-SMA was used as a marker for mesangial cells. That supports the cytoplasm IDA and undercuts the glomerular mesangial cell development IEP built on the same paper.

title: Mutations in smooth muscle alpha-actin (ACTA2) lead to thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections.
review_notes: The founding ACTA2-TAAD paper, and the source of the framing sentence used here for smooth muscle contraction. Marked DISPUTED only because it carries an unresolved 2008 corrigendum. The cached record shows "Erratum in Nat Genet. 2008 Feb;40(2):255.", PubMed's CommentsCorrections entry has a NULL pmid because the corrigendum was never indexed as its own record, and Crossref resolves it as 10.1038/ng0208-255c with update-to 10.1038/ng.2007.6, type erratum. Its content could not be retrieved from any open source queried. The scientific claims used here are independent of it - seven of the nine variants reported by this paper are also reported by PMID:19409525, and no GO term in this review rests on this reference alone.

title: Blood pressure is regulated by an alpha1D-adrenergic receptor/dystrophin signalosome.
review_notes: Correctly cited. The reference-projection check gives 53 annotations over 39 entities, with GO:0032991 alone on 36 entities while the functional term GO:0003073 stays on 3 - so this is per-protein complex-membership curation rather than a phenotype projection, but the term remains the unnamed root of the complex branch.

title: Mutations in smooth muscle alpha-actin (ACTA2) cause coronary artery disease, stroke, and Moyamoya disease, along with thoracic aortic disease.
review_notes: Independently reports seven of the nine variants in PMID:17994018 and extends the phenotype to coronary artery disease, stroke and Moyamoya disease. Used here as the isoform-scope statement and as the corroboration that makes the PMID:17994018 corrigendum non-load-bearing.

title: De novo ACTA2 mutation causes a novel syndrome of multisystemic smooth muscle dysfunction.
review_notes: Defines SMDYS and the R179H allele. The clearest statement in the literature that ACTA2 expression marks the smooth muscle lineage across arteries, iris, gut and bladder, which is the anatomical scope of the proposed smooth muscle contraction term.

title: Analysis of ACTA2 in European Moyamoya disease patients.
review_notes: Source of the MYMY5 R179H variant in UniProt. Abstract-only in the cache; used only as a variant position in the structural analysis.

title: LRRK2 controls synaptic vesicle storage and mobilization within the recycling pool.
review_notes: The single mouse Acta2 IPI (partner Q5S007, LRRK2) that underlies BOTH of ACTA2's protein kinase binding rows - the Compara IEA and the ParkinsonsUK-UCL ISS are the same inference from the same source. A synaptic-vesicle study is an unexpected context for the smooth-muscle actin isoform, but the curator read the full text and the row is left standing.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Bulk exosome proteomics identifying close to 900 proteins. The reference carries 1046 GOA annotations, which exceeds one QuickGO page, so the distinct-entity count is reported as unavailable rather than estimated from a page total.

title: Shotgun proteomics reveals specific modulated protein patterns in tears of patients with primary open angle glaucoma naïve to therapy.
review_notes: Tear-fluid shotgun proteomics. The reference carries GO:0005576 for 95 entities, all HDA - a detection list, not a localisation finding for any one protein.

title: Smooth muscle α actin (Acta2) and myofibroblast function during hepatic wound healing.
review_notes: A real and well-controlled rat siRNA study, but it is the sole source of FIVE rat Acta2 annotations that Compara transfers to human (GO:0061870, GO:0061874, GO:2000491, GO:0070374 as IMP, GO:0001725 as IDA). One experiment, five human rows. Its own framing places Acta2 downstream of stellate cell activation, and the ERK result is stated as an association.

title: Vascular disease-causing mutation R258C in ACTA2 disrupts actin dynamics and interaction with myosin.
review_notes: The most direct biochemistry on human smooth muscle alpha-actin - baculovirus-expressed protein assayed for filament stability, cofilin severing, tropomyosin protection, profilin affinity and smooth muscle myosin motility. Its explicit conclusion that the defects are allosteric is what keeps this review from reading the disease variants as a map of binding sites, and its motility assay is the basis of the proposed myosin binding row.

title: The defining pathology of the new clinical and histopathologic entity ACTA2-related cerebrovascular disease.
review_notes: The R179 inter-strand model. Its structural claim was tested rather than repeated. It states the equivalence "R179 (R177 in alpha1-actin)", which is used as a numbering control, and it names L112, K193 and T196 as the contacts - K193 and T196 both fall inside an independently computed inter-protomer contact set. R179 itself is at 4.42 A, just outside a 4.0 A cutoff, so the modelling claim is corroborated rather than contradicted.

title: Visceral myopathy: Clinical and molecular survey of a cohort of seven new patients and state of the art of overlapping phenotypes.
review_notes: Source of the SMDYS R179C variant, and the clearest statement of the overlap between the ACTA2, ACTG2 and MYH11 visceral phenotypes - the point at which this review and the parallel ACTG2 review touch.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0. 3731 GOA annotations, entity count unavailable for the same pagination reason as PMID:33961781. Together with PMID:33961781 it supplies all ten of ACTA2's GO:0005515 rows - two releases of one AP-MS programme, which IntAct logs as anti tag coip, not two methods.

title: All-trans Retinoic Acid Disrupts Development in Ex Vivo Cultured Fetal Rat Testes. II: Modulation of Mono-(2-ethylhexyl) Phthalate Toxicity.
review_notes: The rat Acta2 IDA behind ACTA2's basement membrane row. A fetal rat testis toxicology study in which alpha-SMA stains the peritubular myoid cell layer lying against the seminiferous tubule basement membrane. Adjacency in a micrograph, not localisation of the protein to an extracellular matrix structure; marked MISCITED with respect to the GO:0005604 claim specifically, not as a criticism of the paper.

title: SETD3 is an actin histidine methyltransferase that prevents primary dystocia.
review_notes: Establishes the His73 methylation that UniProt annotates on ACTA2 at precursor position 75 with ECO:0000269. Used here as a numbering control rather than as the basis of a GO term - the modification is made TO ACTA2, so it is not an ACTA2 molecular function.

title: Renogenic characterization and in vitro differentiation of rat amniotic fluid stem cells into renal proximal tubular- and juxtaglomerular-like cells.
review_notes: The rat Acta2 IEP behind ACTA2's juxtaglomerular apparatus development row. The experiment is an in vitro differentiation of amniotic fluid stem cells into juxtaglomerular-LIKE cells, in which alpha-SMA is a readout of the differentiated phenotype. It does not evidence involvement in development of the juxtaglomerular apparatus.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0. Carries 9514 GOA annotations, far beyond one QuickGO page, so the distinct-entity count is reported as unavailable and the projection test is declared unreliable for this reference rather than being run on a sample.

title: Resistance of Acta2(R149C/+) mice to aortic disease is associated with defective release of mutant smooth muscle α-actin from the chaperonin-containing TCP1 folding complex.
review_notes: Establishes the CCT chaperonin as the folding step for smooth muscle alpha-actin and explains the reduced penetrance of R149C by retention at that step. Directly relevant to the biology but not to any current GO row.

title: Loss of Acta2 in cardiac fibroblasts does not prevent the myofibroblast differentiation or affect the cardiac repair after myocardial infarction.
review_notes: A useful negative - conditional Acta2 deletion in cardiac fibroblasts is compensated by transcriptional upregulation of other actin isoforms. It bounds how much of ACTA2's myofibroblast biology is isoform-specific rather than actin-generic.

title: A yeast based assay establishes the pathogenicity of novel missense ACTA2 variants associated with aortic aneurysms.
review_notes: Heterologous yeast assay showing dominant-negative disruption of the actin cytoskeleton by TAAD-associated ACTA2 variants. Supports the dominant-negative mechanism; the assay is in yeast actin, so it is cited as mechanism rather than as human evidence.

title: Genomic Editing of a Pathogenic Sequence Variant in ACTA2 Rescues Multisystemic Smooth Muscle Dysfunction Syndrome in Mice.
review_notes: Base-editing correction of R179H reverses the contractile-to-synthetic switch in human iPSC-derived SMCs and rescues aortic, bladder and gut phenotypes in humanized mice. The strongest available demonstration that the disease phenotype is a direct consequence of the variant protein rather than of a secondary process.

title: Immature Acta2(R179C/+) smooth muscle cells cause moyamoya-like cerebrovascular lesions in mice prevented by boosting OXPHOS.
review_notes: States the contractile-unit role of the protein directly - monomers of smooth muscle alpha- actin polymerize to form the thin filaments of SMC contractile units - and links R179 variants to a failure of SMC maturation. No supporting_text is quoted from it because the repository's two cached copies of this PMID differ: one is PMC XML and one is PDF-extracted with ligature substitutions and hard line wraps, so no body sentence is a verbatim substring of both. The same claim is quoted from PMID:17994018 instead.

title: A variant form of beta-actin in a mutant of KB cells resistant to cytochalasin B.
review_notes: Cited here only to record the evidence route by which ACTB holds GO:0005200 (TAS), which is what distinguishes ACTB from the four muscle actins in the PAINT census. Not evidence about ACTA2.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: The pipeline behind eight ACTG2 rows. Sound in principle; six of the eight instances here transfer from a paralog (chicken ACTA2) when the source organism has a genuine ACTG2 orthologue, which is a defect of the individual transfers rather than of the GO_REF.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT reference behind rows 1-3. Two of the three are well founded; the third (GO:0005576) is the subject of a recommendation to PAINT.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Maps UniProt SL-0090 Cytoskeleton onto GO:0005856; consistent with the curated SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Orthology is correct - rat Actg2 is the true one-to-one orthologue - but what it carries across is three IEP marker-panel observations from liver studies, which is the weakness.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Derives GO:0007010 mechanically from GO:0005200; carries no independent evidence.

title: Antisense oligodeoxynucleotide complementary to smooth muscle alpha-actin inhibits endothelial-mesenchymal transformation during chick cardiogenesis.
review_notes: Sole source of six ACTG2 ISS rows, via chicken ACTA2 (P08023). The paper is about alpha-smooth-muscle actin in chick atrioventricular cushion endothelial-to-mesenchymal transformation. It is correctly cited for chicken ACTA2 and correctly used for human ACTA2; it is miscited as evidence about human ACTG2, whose chicken orthologue (P63270) was available and unused. Its GO:0010628 IDA is separately questioned. Abstract only, so no claim here rests on unread full text.

title: Leptin and acetaldehyde synergistically promotes αSMA expression in hepatic stellate cells by an interleukin 6-dependent mechanism.
review_notes: Source of rat Actg2's IEP annotations for GO:0071354 and GO:1905641, propagated to human ACTG2. The measured protein is alpha-SMA in hepatic stellate cells, and the reference annotates six entities as a marker panel with GO:1905641 on all six. Miscited as evidence about enteric gamma-actin. Abstract only, so the possible rat-side symbol conflation is raised as a question rather than asserted.

title: Proteomic analysis of microvesicles from plasma of healthy donors reveals high individual variability.
review_notes: 141 annotations over 141 distinct gene products, one term each. Detection record only.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Correctly cited as a detection record: 1046 annotations over 1046 distinct gene products, one term each, enumerated over all six pages. Supports detection, not localisation.

title: Shotgun proteomics reveals specific modulated protein patterns in tears of patients with primary open angle glaucoma naïve to therapy.
review_notes: 95 annotations over 95 distinct gene products, one term each. Detection record only.

title: De novo ACTG2 mutations cause congenital distended bladder, microcolon, and intestinal hypoperistalsis.
review_notes: First report of de novo ACTG2 variants in MMIHS and of the thin-filament polymerisation mechanism. Abstract only; used only for statements the abstract makes.

title: Structural differences explain diverse functions of Plasmodium actins.
review_notes: Carries pig ACTA1's EXP annotation for GO:0016887, the donor of ACTG2's ATP hydrolysis ISS row, and independently carries GO:0005524 and GO:0016887 IDA on three Plasmodium actins. Full text available.

title: ACTG2 variants impair actin polymerization in sporadic Megacystis Microcolon Intestinal Hypoperistalsis Syndrome.
review_notes: Source of UniProt's TISSUE SPECIFICITY statement and of the polymerisation and contractility defects in patient variants. Abstract only in the cache; the claims used here are stated in the abstract.

title: Antifibrotic effect of diethylcarbamazine combined with hesperidin against ethanol induced liver fibrosis in rats.
review_notes: Source of rat Actg2's IEP annotation for GO:0045471. A pharmacology study whose actin readout is a-SMA in liver. Same conflation concern as PMID:21294755. Abstract only.

title: All-trans Retinoic Acid Disrupts Development in Ex Vivo Cultured Fetal Rat Testes. II: Modulation of Mono-(2-ethylhexyl) Phthalate Toxicity.
review_notes: Correctly cited for rat Acta2's GO:0005604 basement membrane IDA, and the reference-projection check on it is negative - 13 annotations over 7 entities, with only Acta2 receiving the localisation - so the rat annotation is genuine per-protein curation. Its subject, rat Acta2, is the sole IBD seed of PANTHER node PTN004322804, and this IDA is that gene's only non-IBA annotation anywhere under GO:0005576, so it is the only candidate experimental basis for the node's assertion - which is why a fetal-rat-testis toxicology paper appears in an actin review at all. The PAINT table records the seed gene, not which of its annotations was used, so that identification is an inference rather than a fact taken from the record. Note also that this IDA reaches human ACTA2 by a separate Ensembl Compara route (GO:0005604 IEA, GO_REF:0000107) which human ACTG2 does not carry; the two chains are independent.

title: SETD3 is an actin histidine methyltransferase that prevents primary dystocia.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt with ECO:0000269 for ACTG2's His-74 methylation. Independently corroborated here by 4-methyl-histidine being modelled in every protomer of the ACTG2 cryo-EM structures. Full text available.

title: Recurrent arginine substitutions in the ACTG2 gene are the primary driver of disease burden and severity in visceral myopathy.
review_notes: 53-family visceral myopathy cohort establishing the arginine-hotspot genotype-phenotype relationship. Full text available and read; supports the proposed GO:0006939 row.

title: Heterozygous Actg2(R257C) mice mimic the phenotype of megacystis microcolon intestinal hypoperistalsis syndrome.
review_notes: CRISPR knock-in mouse reproducing the human phenotype with an increased G-actin/F-actin ratio and reduced collagen gel contraction. Abstract only; used as cross-species corroboration for GO:0006939, not as the primary human evidence.

title: Molecular mechanisms linking missense ACTG2 mutations to visceral myopathy.
review_notes: The single most important reference for this gene and the source of every experimental annotation proposed here: purified human ACTG2, polymerisation and depolymerisation kinetics, critical concentration, leiomodin-1 nucleation, Tpm1.4 decoration, smooth muscle myosin gliding assays, and three cryo-EM filament structures (PDB 8V2O, 8V2Z, 8V30). PubMed-verified, full text read, no retraction, erratum or correction on the record. QuickGO returns zero GO annotations for it, so none of it has reached GOA. It is also absent from the affinage record for this gene.

title: Actg2(D245G) Mutation Causes Megacystis-Microcolon-Intestinal Hypoperistalsis Syndrome by Impairing Smooth Muscle Contractility.
review_notes: Second independent knock-in mouse line with a milder allele and the same biophysical route. Abstract only.

title: Actin isoform compartments in chicken gizzard smooth muscle cells.
review_notes: Genuinely relevant biology - chicken gizzard is enteric smooth muscle and the antibody used was pan-muscle-actin, so gamma-enteric actin is among what was labelled - but the GO term derived from it is wrong. The paper says labelling was found around the myosin filaments, which cannot support located_in GO:0032982 myosin filament. Basis for the MODIFY to GO:0030485. Abstract only.

title: ATP Hydrolysis By Myosin
review_notes: One of eight per-reaction exports of the same GO:0005829 cytosol claim.

title: Myosin Binds ATP
Calcium Binds Caldesmon
Release Of ADP From Myosin
DGC complex binds AGRN and HSPG2
CDH1-associated CTNNA1 binds VCL
CDH1 forms homotypic trans-dimers
CDH1-associated CTNNA1 binds F-actin
review_notes: The one reaction in the export where ACTG2 stands in for filamentous rather than monomeric actin, which makes cytosol the least apt compartment of the eight.

title: ACTG2: a conventional actin with an entirely inferred GO record
review_notes: Computed at run time from UniProt, RCSB, QuickGO and the cached PANTHER PAINT table. The filament-interface panel refuses to report a new column unless it first reproduces all 14 columns published in the merged ACTL8 review, which it does exactly; the length audit refuses to clear ACTG2 unless it first flags ACTL10, the known short entry; and the WITH/FROM source lists are built from the GOA field with an assertion, so they cannot drift from GOA.

title: UniProtKB entry P63267 (ACTH_HUMAN), Actin, gamma-enteric smooth muscle
Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The GO_REF backing both IBA rows. Verified by working through the underlying PAINT record for PTHR11937 cached in this repository and by resolving all 36 WITH/FROM tokens across the two rows against UniProt and QuickGO; every protein donor carries its own experimental evidence, so the inference is well-founded at source even where this review judges the transfer wrong.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Backs the GO:0007010 row. Verified that the row's WITH/FROM is the GO term GO:0005200 rather than a gene product, which is what makes the annotation wholly derivative of the molecular-function row on the same gene.

title: Prognostic role of ACTL10 in Cytogenetic Normal Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached, and checked for retraction; the PubMed publication type is plain Journal Article. Relevance is LOW despite ACTL10 being in the title, because the paper is a survival correlation on TCGA data with no functional experiment, so it informs the review only by confirming that the gene is uncharacterised. Recorded because the affinage record for this gene returned zero discoveries and zero citations, and an empty provider record is not evidence that literature is absent; this paper is what an independent Europe PMC search found.

title: The Wnt1-Cre2 transgene is active in the male germline.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached, no retraction. Actl10 appears only because it flanks the Wnt1-Cre2 insertion site, so the paper is not about this gene; the whole surrounding paragraph was read before quoting, and it is careful to give Actl10 expression without function, which is exactly how it is used here. Relevance MEDIUM rather than HIGH because it establishes expression and the absence of a linked phenotype, not function.

title: ACTL10: is the Swiss-Prot sequence the protein, and what do its two IBA rows rest on?
review_notes: Generated by the committed analyze_actl10.py; a fresh run was verified to reproduce both RESULTS.md and results.json byte-for-byte, so the report cannot silently diverge from the code. The script asserts that it reproduces the committed ACTL8 analysis's filament-interface tallies on three shared rows before drawing any conclusion, and that guard was tested by deliberately breaking it in two ways. Every quoted span was grep-checked as a verbatim substring.

title: UniProtKB entry Q5JWF8 (ACL10_HUMAN), Actin-like protein 10
review_notes: Machine-fetched by just fetch-gene. Every quoted span was checked to be a verbatim substring lying on a single physical line of the file, because the repository validator does not check quotes taken from file references.

title: Cloning, mapping, and expression of two novel actin genes, actin-like-7A (ACTL7A) and actin-like-7B (ACTL7B), from the familial dysautonomia candidate region on 9q31.
review_notes: The paper itself is sound and correctly identified: it is the original cloning, mapping and expression description of ACTL7A and ACTL7B. It is miscited as the basis of the TAS annotations GO:0005200 structural constituent of cytoskeleton and GO:0005856 cytoskeleton. It reports cDNA selection, direct genomic sequencing, linkage mapping in mouse and Northern expression analysis, with no biochemical, structural, localisation or phenotypic experiment; the only structural statement is the homology-based label actin-like. Those two GO terms therefore rest on a gene name rather than on data, and GO_REF:0000108 then derives GO:0007010 from one of them.

title: Novel actin-like proteins T-ACTIN 1 and T-ACTIN 2 are differentially expressed in the cytoplasm and nucleus of mouse haploid germ cells.
review_notes: The origin of the mouse nucleus annotation that the human IBA and ISS rows transfer, and the source of the mouse GO:0001673 male germ cell nucleus IDA, confirmed via QuickGO on Q9QY84. Also the earliest quantitative statement of the family's divergence from conventional actin. Abstract-only in the cache. Read this paper with the naming key in hand: T-ACTIN-1 is mACTL7B and T-ACTIN-2 is mACTL7A, so its localisation sentence assigns the nucleus to ACTL7A and the cytoplasm to the paralogue ACTL7B. Quoting that sentence in support of an ACTL7A cytoplasm annotation reads as evidence against the term, and it is cited here only on the nucleus rows and, with the paralogue caveat stated, on the cytoplasm propagation review.

title: Molecular recognition of the Tes LIM2-3 domains by the actin-related protein Arp7A.
review_notes: The key mechanistic paper, with full text available. Supplies the TES interaction mapping and crystal structure PDB 2XQN, the Golgi co-localisation, the ACTL7A-TES-ENAH complex, and, crucially for this review, the explicit correction of ACTL7A's location from nucleus and acrosome to the subacrosomal layer, together with a direct negative on filament assembly in cells and an explicit statement that polymerisation remains untested.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Correctly cited for the human sperm-nucleus HDA annotation. Methodologically careful, reporting acrosome-free nuclear preparations, but a nuclear proteome cannot by itself exclude carry-over of the nuclear-adherent perinuclear theca, which is where ACTL7A is most abundant. Treated as supporting a real but secondary compartment.

title: Disruption in ACTL7A causes acrosomal ultrastructural defects in human and mouse sperm as a novel male factor inducing early embryonic arrest.
review_notes: The founding human-genetics paper for ACTL7A-related infertility and the source of the human acrosomal-vesicle IDA. Abstract-only in the cache, so the immunofluorescence figures could not be inspected; the localisation term is proposed for refinement to perinuclear theca on definitional grounds rather than on any doubt about the data.

title: Homozygous pathogenic variants in ACTL9 cause fertilization failure and male infertility in humans and mice.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt and GOA for the ACTL7A-ACTL9 interaction. The title foregrounds ACTL9, which is the interacting partner rather than the reviewed gene; that is normal and not a citation error. Independently valuable because ACTL9 loss reproduces the ACTL7A phenotype, with disorganised perinuclear theca, mislocalised phospholipase C zeta and failed calcium oscillations, which corroborates the interaction functionally.

title: Novel bi-allelic variants in ACTL7A are associated with male infertility and total fertilization failure.
review_notes: The clearest statement of the oocyte-activation mechanism and of its pharmacological rescue, and therefore the anchor for the proposed GO:0007343 egg activation annotation. Note that GOA records this reference with an IMP code for a cellular-component term, GO:0001669; the underlying data are immunofluorescence on patient sperm, which is IDA-shaped. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: Pathogenic variant in ACTL7A causes severe teratozoospermia characterized by bubble-shaped acrosomes and male infertility.
review_notes: Source of the G402S variant used in the structure-guided variant mapping, and of the observation that mutant ACTL7A fails to attach to the acroplaxome and is shed in cytoplasmic droplets together with phospholipase C zeta. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: Actl7a deficiency in mice leads to male infertility and fertilization failure.
review_notes: One of the two mouse studies underlying the mouse fertilization IMP that the human IEA and ISS fertilization rows transfer, confirmed via QuickGO on Q9QY84. Adds the ZPBP mislocalisation and reduced sperm-zona binding phenotypes. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: A novel homozygous mutation in ACTL7A leads to male infertility.
review_notes: Source of the D75A variant, which the structure-guided audit maps to actin Asp11 in the divalent-cation site. Reports ACTL7A protein degradation in patient sperm with irregular perinuclear theca and mislocalised phospholipase C zeta. The 3D-modelling claim about a lost hydrogen bond is in-silico and is not used to support any annotation. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: Testis-specific actin-like 7A (ACTL7A) is an indispensable protein for subacrosomal-associated F-actin formation, acrosomal anchoring, and male fertility.
review_notes: The decisive functional paper and the main basis for the proposed move from GO:0007010 to GO:0030036, with full text available. Establishes that Actl7a knock-out spermatids lose subacrosomal F-actin completely while retaining F-actin elsewhere, documents the intranuclear pool by 3D confocal imaging, reports the co-immunoprecipitation set including a negative for ACTRT2, and states plainly that whether ACTL7A is itself the filament remains unresolved.

title: Loss of ACTL7A causes small head sperm by defective acrosome-acroplaxome-manchette complex.
review_notes: The source of the mouse spermatid development IMP that the human IEA and ISS rows transfer, confirmed via QuickGO on Q9QY84, with full text available. The PI3K/AKT/mTOR and PDLIM1 autophagy mechanism is a downstream proteomic correlate and is not used to support any annotation.

title: Disruption in CYLC1 leads to acrosome detachment, sperm head deformity, and male in/subfertility in humans and mice.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt and GOA for the ACTL7A-cylicin-1 interaction. As with the ACTL9 paper, the title foregrounds the partner rather than the reviewed gene, which is expected. Also the clearest published description of the acrosome-to-nuclear-envelope anchoring module, and the main external justification for the proposed acrosome attachment to nuclear envelope term.

title: Perinuclear theca protein FNDC8 interacts with CCIN and ACTL7A to ensure proper sperm head shaping during spermiogenesis.
review_notes: Source of the mouse perinuclear theca IDA that the human GO_REF:0000107 row transfers, confirmed via QuickGO on Q9QY84, with full text available. Its primary subject is FNDC8; the ACTL7A content is the interaction and a summary of ACTL7A's established role, which is how it is used here.

title: PANTHER PTHR11937 PAINT annotation table - per-node GO propagations and rejections
review_notes: The in-repo cache of GO's phylogenetic annotation decisions for this family, and decisive for the structural molecular-function question. Read together, its two rows for the node that carries ACTL7A show a single curatorial act rather than an omission: PTN008986528 gets GO:0005198 by IBA and GO:0005200 as an IRD with negated set to true, both dated 2025-08-05, while GO:0005200 is IBD-supported one level up at PTN000940351 from conventional actins and Arp2/Arp3. GO:0005198 occurs nowhere else in the table. Q9Y615 is confirmed in PTHR11937-entries.csv, so the negation covers ACTL7A directly. Dates in this file vary per row, so 2025-08-05 is a per-annotation date and not a bulk stamp.

title: Cloning, mapping, and expression of two novel actin genes, actin-like-7A (ACTL7A) and actin-like-7B (ACTL7B), from the familial dysautonomia candidate region on 9q31.
review_notes: Correctly cited as the discovery and expression paper, and it is the paper the two TAS annotations name. Verified against the cached abstract that it contains no protein-level or localisation experiment; the TAS annotations derived from it are restatements of the genes' actin-like name, which is why both are recommended for removal.

title: Novel actin-like proteins T-ACTIN 1 and T-ACTIN 2 are differentially expressed in the cytoplasm and nucleus of mouse haploid germ cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. This is the experimental basis of the mouse Actl7b cytoplasm IDA cited in the WITH/FROM of the human cytoplasm IBA. Its nucleus assignment applies to T-ACTIN 2 (Actl7a), not to ACTL7B; the ACTL7B nuclear pool is a later finding (PMID:37800308, PMID:38464253), so this paper should not be cited for ACTL7B nuclear localisation.

title: Genetic Polymorphisms within The Intronless ACTL7A and ACTL7B Genes Encoding Spermatogenesis-Specific Actin-Like Proteins in Japanese Males.
review_notes: Correctly cited, and deliberately used only for a negative statement: the paper's own conclusion is that causality could not be determined. Cited to document that the human gene has no established disease association, not as support for any function.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: The citation is correct and the study is a legitimate large-scale resource, but for ACTL7B specifically it yields four unreplicated Y2H candidate interactions from a screen whose biological context (neurodegeneration, brain tissue) does not overlap the gene's expression domain. Flagged LOW_QUALITY as support for ACTL7B molecular function, not as a criticism of the paper's own claims.

title: Actin-related protein ACTL7B ablation leads to OAT with multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagellum and male infertility in mice†.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the abstract states the localisation and knockout phenotype quoted. Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available false), so only abstract-level claims are used here. Mouse work, hence proposed as ISS for the human gene rather than IMP or IDA.

title: Actl7b deficiency leads to mislocalization of LC8 type dynein light chains and disruption of murine spermatogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified and full text available in the cache; the co-immunoprecipitation passages were read directly rather than taken from a summary. This is the single most informative reference for ACTL7B molecular function and it is absent from both the human and the mouse GO records. It was also missing from the affinage report, and was found by an independent PubMed search of the gene symbol.

title: Novel Nuclear Roles for Testis-Specific ACTL7A and ACTL7B Supported by In Vivo Characterizations and AI Facilitated In Silico Mechanistic Modeling with Implications for Epigenetic Regulation in Spermiogenesis.
review_notes: Correctly cited and the PMID resolves to the intended record, but PubMed types it as a Preprint (bioRxiv, PMCID PMC10925299) with no peer-reviewed version found by PubMed search as of this review. Its in vivo localisation and HDAC observations are used only as corroboration of the nucleus annotation; its INO80 and SWI/SNF interaction claim is in silico docking and is not used to support any GO term.

title: ACTL7B bioinformatics audit - propagation audit and actin residue audit
review_notes: Generated in this review by ACTL7B-bioinformatics/analyze.py; a fresh run reproduces the committed report byte for byte. Contact residue sets are computed from deposited structures (1ATN, 8A2S) rather than taken from literature, and the WITH/FROM table is built from ACTL7B-goa.tsv with an assertion that token counts match GOA.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACTL7B (human)
review_notes: The record carries no self_evaluation_pairwise score; its narrative correctly surfaced PMID:36617158 and PMID:38464253, but the record missed PMID:37800308 entirely - the Development 2023 Actl7b-null paper that supplies the only informative molecular partner - which was found instead by a direct PubMed search of the gene symbol. Its own GO grounding (GO:0008092 cytoskeletal protein binding) is unsupported. Used as a lead only; every claim taken from it was re-verified against the cited PMIDs, and no affinage sentence is quoted as support for a mechanistic claim.

title: UniProt entry Q9Y614 (ACL7B_HUMAN)
review_notes: Machine-fetched UniProt record; quotes taken verbatim from single physical lines of the flat file.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The GO_REF itself is correctly cited; the issue found here is with where ACTL8 sits in the PANTHER tree, not with the method. Clade membership was verified by querying QuickGO for each node's human targets and aligning each target to beta-actin.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Correctly cited for what it is - an automatic vocabulary mapping. Verified by reading the UniProt CC line the mapping consumes.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Correctly cited; the WITH/FROM field is a GO id, confirming the inference is inter-ontology and not evidence-based.

title: Identification of cancer/testis-antigen genes by massively parallel signature sequencing.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The cached record is abstract-only and does not name ACTL8; the attribution rests on UniProt's ECO:0000269 tag on the TISSUE SPECIFICITY line, which is a checkable anchor, and on HPA independently classifying the gene as testis-enriched.

title: Analysis of proteomic changes induced upon cellular differentiation of the human intestinal cell line Caco-2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the cached record is abstract-only and does not name ACTL8, which the UniProt curator would have seen in the full text or supplement. Cited correctly for what it is, an expression-pattern study, and it does not support an involved_in claim.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Correctly cited for a screen-derived interaction. Not independent of PMID:32296183, which is the same laboratory's expanded screen; treating the two rows as replication would be wrong.

title: Actin-like protein 8 promotes cell proliferation, colony-formation, proangiogenesis, migration and invasion in lung adenocarcinoma cells.
review_notes: Full text available from PMC; both quotes verified verbatim. Provides the only in vivo data for ACTL8.

title: Actin‑like protein 8 executes a promoting function in the malignant progression of endometrial cancer: identification of a promising biomarker.
review_notes: Retraction confirmed from the cached PubMed metadata, which records the publication type and the retraction notice citation. The affinage deep-research record cites this paper as a dated finding without flagging the retraction, and it is the sole source of that record's p21, E-cadherin and EMT-marker claims. Flagged is_invalid so it is not re-imported; the proliferation and migration conclusions it shares with the other studies stand on those studies, not on this one.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Correctly cited. The paper's own description of HI-II-14 as its predecessor is what establishes that the two ACTL8 protein binding rows are not independent evidence.

title: Actin-Like Protein 8 Promotes the Progression of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer via Activating PI3K/AKT/mTOR Pathway.
review_notes: Full text read from PMC; all three quotes verified verbatim. The pathway conclusion is pharmacological and correlative rather than mechanistic - Wortmannin and 740Y-P modulate the phenotype but no ACTL8-pathway interaction is demonstrated. The methods section also describes the siRNA as targeting a "back-splice junction site", a circular-RNA term that does not apply to a linear mRNA knockdown, which is a reporting error worth noting.

title: Actin-like protein 8, a member of cancer/testis antigens, supports the aggressive development of oral squamous cell carcinoma cells via activating cell cycle signaling.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; the quoted result is stated directly in the abstract. A third independent tumour type showing the same direction of effect.

title: Knockdown of actin-like 8 inhibits cell proliferation by regulating FOXM1, STMN1, PLK1, and BIRC5 in lung adenocarcinoma A549 cells.
review_notes: Full text available from PMC; quote verified verbatim. The named downstream effectors are transcriptional consequences of knockdown, not ACTL8 partners, so they support a regulatory BP term and not any molecular function.

title: ACTL8 Promotes the Progression of Gastric Cancer Through PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signaling Pathway.
review_notes: Full text available from PMC; quotes verified verbatim. An independent replication of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR association in a different tumour type, still without a demonstrated molecular interaction.

title: Multiomic Selection of Cancer-Testis Antigens as Precision Immuno-oncologic Targets in Head and Neck Cancer.
review_notes: Full text available from PMC; quotes verified verbatim. Relevant for localisation and expression rather than function - it is an immuno-oncology target-selection study, and the immunohistochemistry is on two FFPE tumour samples with a single commercial antibody, so it establishes cytoplasmic presence in tumour cells and nothing finer.

title: Momordin Ic suppresses breast cancer growth by targeting ACTL8‑dependent glutamine metabolism and PI3K/AKT/mTOR-MYC.
review_notes: Listed for completeness because affinage's mechanistic narrative leans on it, including the only claim of a direct ACTL8 ligand. Cannot be verified from the cached abstract-only record, so it is marked UNVERIFIED and nothing in this review depends on it. If the surface plasmon resonance and thermal shift results hold, they would be the first direct biophysical handle on ACTL8 and would justify revisiting the molecular-function gap.

title: ACTL8: does the actin fold come with actin's residues, and do its IBA sources transfer?
review_notes: Analysis written for this review. All inputs are fetched live from UniProt, RCSB and QuickGO at run time; RESULTS.md and results.json were verified byte-identical on a repeat run.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACTL8 (human)
review_notes: Treated as a preliminary lead source rather than evidence, per its own header. It passed its internal gates, but it cites the retracted PMID:32125225 as a dated finding without flagging the retraction, and that paper is the sole source of its p21, E-cadherin and EMT-marker claims - so its narrative is partly built on withdrawn work. Its remaining claims were independently verified against the cited PMIDs and hold up. Marked LOW_QUALITY for the unflagged retracted citation, not because the summary is wrong.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Pipeline reference for the cytoplasm row. The mapping is faithful: UniProt's own SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line is "Cytoplasm" with ECO:0000305|PubMed:36173861, and SL-0086 is the Cytoplasm subcellular-location keyword.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Pipeline reference for the two Ensembl ortholog projections. The donor resolves to the genuine 1:1 mouse ortholog, so the projection is mechanically correct; its evidential value is nil because the donor's own IDA comes from the same publication as the human IDA it duplicates, and three of the donor's four annotations to GO:0004239 are themselves projections back from human Q5BKX5.

title: Actin maturation requires the ACTMAP/C19orf54 protease.
review_notes: The defining paper for this gene and the source of every experimental annotation in GOA. PubMed-verified; no retraction or correction notice (E-utilities CommentsCorrections is empty). Only the abstract is cached, so all claims taken from it here are abstract-level; the mechanistic details (Cys132 active site, C132A mutagenesis, PFN1/PFN2 interaction, catalytic-activity reactions) are taken from the UniProt entry's own ECO:0000269|PubMed:36173861 annotations rather than from paraphrase.

title: Actin finally matures: uncovering machinery and impact.
review_notes: Independent expert commentary on PMID:36173861 by the group that characterised NAA80. Useful as confirmation that the field reads ACTMAP as the dedicated actin aminopeptidase and as context for the multistep nature of actin N-terminal maturation. Abstract-only in the cache; not used for any mechanistic claim.

title: A Global Ligandability Map of Tryptoline Butynamide Stereoprobes Identifies Covalent Inhibitors of the Actin Maturation Protease ACTMAP.
review_notes: This is the bioRxiv preprint of PMID:42159598, not an independent study: PubMed records UpdateIn 42159598 here and UpdateOf 41757055 there. The affinage record cites both ids side by side for the same finding, which reads as two-source corroboration; it is one study. Retained for provenance only, with the peer-reviewed version used for all quotations.

title: A Global Ligandability Map of Tryptoline Butynamide Stereoprobes Identifies Covalent Inhibitors of the Actin Maturation Protease.
review_notes: Peer-reviewed JACS version of the covalent-probe study; full text available from PMC13367750. Independent laboratory (Cravatt) and independent methodology, so it is genuine corroboration of the cysteine-nucleophile mechanism and of the cellular consequence of blocking it. Note that the paper's "45 kDa" description of ACTMAP is an apparent mass; UniProt computes 37,779 Da for the 351-residue canonical form, so that figure is not used here.

title: ACTMAP GO-record audit - WITH/FROM resolution, peptidase-branch definitions, a census of GO:0004239 usage, and orthologue curation state
review_notes: Computed for this review by ACTMAP-bioinformatics/analyze_actmap_go.py (standard library only). Every number is fetched at run time from QuickGO and UniProt; the script asserts that its source list matches the GOA WITH/FROM field token for token and fails loudly on a missing input file.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACTMAP (human)
review_notes: gates_passed True and faith 100%, and the narrative is substantially correct including the 2026 covalent-probe result, which is a genuine lead. Marked LOW_QUALITY for one citation defect: its single 2026 finding is attributed to "PMID:42159598, PMID:41757055", which are the JACS paper and its own bioRxiv preprint presented as two sources. Its GO grounding (GO:0140096, GO:0016787, GO:0005829) was not imported, per the standing rule that provider groundings collapse to general parents.

title: UniProtKB entry Q5BKX5 (ACTMP_HUMAN) - actin maturation protease
review_notes: Carries the curated, ECO-tagged detail that the abstract-only Science paper cannot supply: four Rhea catalytic-activity reactions, the C39-like peptidase region, the ACT_SITE 132 and its C132A mutagenesis result, the PFN1/PFN2 SUBUNIT statements, and the deliberately unspecific EC 3.4.11.- assignment.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT phylogenetic propagation. Every WITH/FROM token on all four IBA rows was resolved against UniProt and queried in QuickGO for its own evidence for the propagated term (see file:human/ACTR10/ACTR10-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md section A). Three of the four rows propagate from genuine ACTR10/ARP11 orthologs; the nucleus row propagates from nuclear actin-related proteins of a different subfamily.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Maps the UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line "Cytoplasm, cytoskeleton" (itself ECO:0000250 by similarity to pig I3LHK5) to GO:0005856. Correct but a strict ancestor of the dynactin-complex term ACTR10 already carries.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Two rows derive from this inter-ontology inference, each taking its input from another propagated annotation on the same gene (GO:0005200 IBA and GO:0098958 IBA). Neither adds independent evidence.

title: Analysis of dynactin subcomplexes reveals a novel actin-related protein associated with the arp1 minifilament pointed end.
review_notes: The paper that discovered ARP11 as the fourth subunit of dynactin's pointed-end complex, in bovine brain dynactin, and cloned the vertebrate sequences. Its sequence-based predictions - actin fold with nucleotide and metal binding elements retained, barbed-end face conserved, actin residues 38-57 deleted, therefore capping rather than polymerisation - were all subsequently confirmed by cryo-EM and are reproduced independently in this review's alignment.

title: Interactions between the evolutionarily conserved, actin-related protein, Arp11, actin, and Arp1.
review_notes: Full text available. Establishes by coprecipitation that recombinant Arp11 and Arp1 interact, and that cytosolic Arp11 is found exclusively in dynactin with no free pool. Its abstract also refutes a one-sided reading of itself, in the sentence immediately before the one commonly quoted: the authors tested Arp11 against conventional actin and found it could coassemble, so the paper does not show that Arp11 is incapable of engaging actin filaments - the "free cytosolic actin do not interact significantly" statement is about the absence of a free Arp11 pool in cells, not about binding capacity. The full text states it outright in the Discussion ("Arp11 can interact with both Arp1 and conventional actin"), but the abstract alone was sufficient to see it. It also floats an Arp2/3-like nucleation role for Arp11 as a hypothesis while arguing that Arp1 does not require nucleation.

title: Arp10p is a pointed-end-associated component of yeast dynactin.
review_notes: Establishes by genetics and biochemistry that S. cerevisiae Arp10p is the functional ARP11 homolog and associates with the Arp1p filament pointed end. It is the reason SGD:S000002513 on the GO:0005200 row counts as an ortholog rather than a generic actin, and it also states the family's pairing pattern (Arp1/Arp11 versus the nuclear Arp7/Arp9), which is the distinction the nucleus IBA crosses.

title: Dynactin's pointed-end complex is a cargo-targeting module.
review_notes: Cross-linking and siRNA analysis of the pointed-end complex. Shows Arp11 contacts p62 and p25 directly and that Arp11 (with p62) is required for dynactin to remain assembled at all. Work is in Cos7 (African green monkey) cells, so it is ortholog-level rather than human evidence.

title: Proteome profiling of human neutrophil granule subsets, secretory vesicles, and cell membrane: correlation with transcriptome profiling of neutrophil precursors.
review_notes: Bulk proteomics of neutrophil granule fractions, cited by Reactome's Neutrophil degranulation pathway as the source of its granule protein sets. It is the ultimate origin of the ACTR10 azurophil-granule-lumen, ficolin-1-rich-granule-lumen and extracellular-region annotations. Cached as abstract only; the argument against those annotations here is made on protein topology and on the fact that the other dynactin subunits do not carry them, not on this paper's internal details.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: HI-II-14 yeast two-hybrid interactome. Supplies the single ACTR10-NAGK interaction, which has no independent replication and no connection to dynactin biology.

title: The structure of the dynactin complex and its interaction with dynein.
review_notes: Pig dynactin cryo-EM. Gives the mechanism of capping: Arp11 blocks subunit addition on one protofilament because its subdomain-2 loop is too short and sterically on the other, and is the only subunit that caps the pointed end.

title: Regulation of mitochondria-dynactin interaction and mitochondrial retrograde transport in axons.
review_notes: Zebrafish forward-genetic actr10 mutant; the experimental basis of the ZFIN annotation from which GO:0098958 was propagated to human. Shows a cargo-selective retrograde failure for mitochondria and traces it to loss of mitochondria-dynactin attachment, with a separation-of-function construct lacking the dynactin-binding domain that still binds mitochondria.

title: Dynein/dynactin is necessary for anterograde transport of Mbp mRNA in oligodendrocytes and for myelination in vivo.
review_notes: Independent zebrafish actr10 allele (stl83). Important as a control on the cargo-selectivity claim: this allele shows the generic dynein-dynactin loss-of-function phenotypes, so ACTR10 should not be read as a mitochondria-only subunit.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI yeast two-hybrid interactome. Supplies two ACTR10 partners of very different value: DCTN4/p62, a true neighbour of ACTR10 in the dynactin pointed-end complex confirmed by cryo-EM and chemical cross-linking, and KRT31, a hair-cuticle keratin with no shared expression domain.

title: Retrograde Mitochondrial Transport Is Essential for Organelle Distribution and Health in Zebrafish Neurons.
review_notes: Follow-up on the same zebrafish actr10 allele showing the organelle-homeostasis consequence: mitochondria accumulate in axon terminals and are depleted from the soma. Corroborates rather than extends the transport role.

title: Cryo-EM reveals the complex architecture of dynactin's shoulder region and pointed end.
review_notes: Pig dynactin pointed-end structures at 3.8-4.5 A. Assigns p25 and p27 for the first time and shows the p62 saddle wrapping around Arp11, which is the structural content of the ACTR10-DCTN4 interaction row.

title: Structure of dynein-dynactin on microtubules shows tandem adaptor binding.
review_notes: Source of the highest-resolution pointed-end model containing a nucleotide (PDB 7Z8M, 3.37 A). Its methods state explicitly that ATP-Mg was built into Arp11 on the basis of density while ADP-Mg was built into beta-actin and the Arp1 subunits - the strongest single statement that ACTR10's nucleotide site is occupied rather than vestigial. The claim is about pig Arp11, so it supports an ISS-level, not IDA-level, human annotation.

title: ACTR10 Overexpression Facilitates the Progression and Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor Resistance in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
review_notes: Entirely in-silico reanalysis of public expression, DepMap and co-expression data; no wet-lab experiment on ACTR10 protein function. Cited here only because it documents the downstream cost of the Reactome granule annotations: it restates them as ACTR10 biology ("suggested to be present in the cytosol, extracellular region and secretory granules").

title: The Chlamydia effector Dre1 binds dynactin to reposition host organelles during infection.
review_notes: First cryo-EM structure of HUMAN dynactin, purified from human cell culture using a Chlamydia effector as affinity handle; human ACTR10 (Q9NZ32) is chain J of PDB 9B7J and 9B85, and AP-MS from HEK293T recovered all 11 dynactin subunits. This makes human ACTR10's dynactin-complex membership directly demonstrable, whereas GOA still records it only as IBA.

title: Actin-related and actin-like proteins: functional diversification of the actin-fold.
review_notes: 2026 review of the human actin-fold family, cached as abstract only. Cited for the family-level framing that underpins two decisions here: that the dynactin Arps (Arp1, Arp11) form a cytoplasmic dynein-activating and cargo-adaptor branch distinct from the nuclear chromatin-remodelling Arps and from the testis-restricted actin-like proteins - which is exactly the boundary the nucleus IBA crosses - and that nucleotide binding is a defining property of the actin fold rather than an actin-specific one.

title: Exocytosis of azurophil granule lumen proteins
review_notes: The reaction itself is sound; ACTR10's inclusion in its azurophil granule lumen protein set is not. ACTR10 has no signal peptide or transmembrane segment and no route to a granule lumen; it is also the only one of the 11 canonical dynactin subunits annotated to azurophil granule lumen at all, and the only one carrying any annotation from Reactome's Neutrophil degranulation route.

title: Exocytosis of ficolin-rich granule lumen proteins
review_notes: Same issue as R-HSA-6798751: a proteomics-derived granule protein set that places a cytosolic dynactin subunit in a secretory granule lumen and in the extracellular region.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACTR10 (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated deep research, self_evaluation_pairwise win, three numeric PMID citations all of which were fetched and read in full text here. Its narrative summary of the zebrafish work is accurate and is cited only at that summary level, alongside the primary quotations. Its own GO grounding (GO:0060090 molecular adaptor activity, GO:0005739 mitochondrion) was deliberately not imported: no mitochondrial localisation of ACTR10 has been shown, and the adaptor term is coarser than the evidence warrants.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/GO_Central inference reference for the three IBA rows. Every WITH/FROM token was resolved and each source's own evidence queried; the dynactin-complex transfer is well founded, the cortical-anchor and nuclear-migration transfers are not equally so.

title: Self-regulated polymerization of the actin-related protein Arp1.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, but the abstract is unusually detailed and carries both claims used. The species of the purified native Arp1 is not stated in the abstract, so it is cited alongside, not instead of, the human structure.

title: Isolation of a new set of Aspergillus nidulans mutants defective in nuclear migration.
review_notes: Donor evidence for the GO:0030473 IBA. Genuine, but fungal germ-tube nuclear migration; the corresponding UniProt entry Q5BBX7 is unreviewed with the submitted name 'Uncharacterized protein', so only its curated GO evidence is usable.

title: Analysis of dynactin subcomplexes reveals a novel actin-related protein associated with the arp1 minifilament pointed end.
A vertebrate actin-related protein is a component of a multisubunit complex involved in microtubule-based vesicle motility.
review_notes: Founding paper for the gene; abstract-only in the cache but the abstract states the claim used for the GO:0016192 MODIFY.

title: Chromosome- and spindle-pole-derived signals generate an intrinsic code for spindle position and orientation.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Supports the cell-cortex IDA and, independently, the argument against GO:0106006 for human ACTR1A.

title: Dynactin's pointed-end complex is a cargo-targeting module.
review_notes: Cited for the division of labour within dynactin: cargo targeting is a pointed-end-module property, not an Arp1-filament property.

title: Dynactin and Num1 cooperate to establish the cortical anchoring of cytoplasmic dynein in S. pombe.
review_notes: Sole interpretable donor for the GO:0106006 IBA. The source annotation is sound for S. pombe; what fails is the transfer to human ACTR1A.

title: The structure of the dynactin complex and its interaction with dynein.
review_notes: Full text read. Native pig-brain dynactin, hence ISS rather than IDA for the human dynein-heavy-chain-binding proposal.

title: Regulation of spindle integrity and mitotic fidelity by BCCIP.
review_notes: Full text read. The interaction is real and isoform-resolved, matching GOA's with-value Q9P287-2, but the pull-down captured intact dynactin, so it does not localise a binding site to ACTR1A.

title: Cross-linking Proteomics Indicates Effects of Simvastatin on the TLR2 Interactome and Reveals ACTR1A as a Novel Regulator of the TLR2 Signal Cascade.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Single unreplicated study; a dynactin-dependent trafficking effect could produce the phenotype indirectly, so it is raised as a question rather than annotated.

title: Cryo-EM reveals the complex architecture of dynactin's shoulder region and pointed end.
review_notes: Source of pig ACTR1A's own IPI for GO:0005869, i.e. independent experimental support behind one of the dynactin-complex IBA donors.

title: Structure of dynein-dynactin on microtubules shows tandem adaptor binding.
review_notes: Cited correctly and affirmatively in this review, for dynactin filament/adaptor architecture - hence VERIFIED: the correctness enum records this review's use of the reference, not a third party's. Separately, ComplexPortal uses this cryo-EM structure paper as the IDA source for GO:0030989 dynein-driven meiotic oscillatory nuclear movement on pig ACTR1A and six other pig dynactin subunits, which the paper cannot support, and those rows have been propagated to rat by ISO; that defect is recorded where it belongs, as source_status SOURCE_BAD with failure_mode SOURCE_MISCITATION in the GO:0030473 propagation_review, and is escalated in suggested_questions.

title: The Chlamydia effector Dre1 binds dynactin to reposition host organelles during infection.
review_notes: Full text read. The bound ADP is in the deposited coordinates of 9B85 and 9B7J but is not discussed in the paper text; the structural facts used here were computed from the deposited model (see the bioinformatics RESULTS.md).

title: Alpha-centractin is a novel substrate of SETD3 methyltransferase in vitro.
review_notes: In vitro only, and the authors hedge ('may be one of them'). A candidate PTM, not a function of ACTR1A; not annotated.

title: Ultrastructural analysis of the dynactin complex: an actin-related protein is a component of a filament that resembles F-actin.
Beta-centractin: characterization and distribution of a new member of the centractin family of actin-related proteins.
review_notes: Title foregrounds the paralog ACTR1B, but the paper explicitly discriminates and characterises alpha-centractin with isoform-specific antibodies, so the two TAS rows on ACTR1A are not mis-attributed.

title: The yeast dynactin complex is involved in partitioning the mitotic spindle between mother and daughter cells during anaphase B.
review_notes: Establishes the precedent that the orthologous Arp1 carries GO:0005200 structural constituent of cytoskeleton by IDA, which human ACTR1A currently lacks.

title: Bioinformatics: ACTR1A nucleotide site and polymerisation interface
review_notes: Computed for this review; the script derives every position from coordinates rather than from a remembered residue list, and is re-runnable.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACTR1A (human)
review_notes: self_evaluation_pairwise: win, two citations, both real numeric PMIDs (31221720, 41142317), no bioRxiv DOIs in the PMID field. Recorded here for provenance but deliberately not used to support any annotation: its narrative covers only a candidate TLR2 signalling role and an in-vitro SETD3 methylation event, both of which this review declines to annotate, and its own mechanism profile lists no molecular activity, no localization and no pathway. Its silence on dynactin architecture is not treated as evidence that such literature is absent - the structural literature was retrieved separately from the UniProt reference list and PubMed.

title: Curator notes for human ACTR1A
UniProtKB record for human ACTR1A
review_notes: Fetched the same day as the GOA table, which is what makes the UniProt/GOA molecular-function discrepancy checkable rather than anecdotal. The DR GO block diverges in both directions - it lists GO:0005200 and GO:0005524, which GOA lacks, and omits GO:0030473, GO:0106006 and GO:0005515, which GOA has - so it is treated as corroboration of a divergence, not as proof of deletion; the load-bearing evidence is the QuickGO queries (zero human hits for GO_REF:0000043; zero hits for GO:0000166 with goUsage=descendants on ACTB, ACTR1A, ACTR1B and ACTR10).

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/PANTHER phylogenetic inference. Delivers three of ACTR1B's annotations from two different tree nodes: GO:0005869 and GO:0030473 from PTN000233666, and GO:0106006 from PTN007551901. The node distinction matters -- see the GO:0106006 review.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt subcellular-location keyword mapping. Faithful to the curated P42025 SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line; the resulting centrosome term is corroborated by an IDA and the cytoskeleton term is a redundant ancestor of the dynactin complex term.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of intracellular localizations of expressed fusion proteins in living cells
review_notes: LIFEdb localisation of expressed fluorescent fusions. Yields only the generic cytoplasm term, an ancestor of the cytosol annotation.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learning rule. Yields GO:0005815, a strict ancestor of the centrosome IDA, so it adds no information.

title: Self-regulated polymerization of the actin-related protein Arp1.
review_notes: Bingham & Schroer 1999, the paper that purified native Arp1 and characterised its polymerisation. Load-bearing twice. It is the reason the proposed nucleotide term is GO:0043531 ADP binding and not GO:0005524 ATP binding: it states that Arp1 'is predicted to bind ATP and possibly polymerize' on the basis of conserved sequence features, so ATP binding has never been demonstrated for Arp1, whereas ADP is resolved in all eight Arp1 protomers of PDB 9B85. It also bounds the polymerisation claim: Arp1 filaments annealed over time but never reached conventional actin-filament length, which is why no filament-dynamics term is proposed. Abstract-only in the cache; both claims used here are in the abstract.

title: Isolation of a new set of Aspergillus nidulans mutants defective in nuclear migration.
review_notes: The strongest donor evidence on the GO:0030473 IBA. Verified: it cloned nudK, showed it encodes Arp1, and provided the first evidence that dynactin acts in nuclear migration in A. nidulans. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: beta III spectrin binds to the Arp1 subunit of dynactin.
review_notes: Establishes the one documented Arp1-to-membrane-skeleton bridge, to Golgi-associated betaIII spectrin, recruiting dynactin to intracellular membranes. Load-bearing for the GO:0106006 argument: it shows the bridge exists but is not at a cortical membrane. Caveat recorded: the work is alpha-centractin-directed, so it is cited here as evidence about Arp1 generally and explicitly NOT used to annotate ACTR1B with spectrin binding.

title: Interactions between the evolutionarily conserved, actin-related protein, Arp11, actin, and Arp1.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Source of both PMID:12857853 GO:0005515 rows, which IntAct records as two different experiments (density sedimentation with DCTN1; pull down with mouse Arp11). Also the source for Arp1's very low critical concentration for polymerisation and for the point that isolated Arp1 filaments are variable in length whereas dynactin's are not, because other subunits supply a ruler activity. Limitation: the cached HTML lacks the Materials and Methods, so which Arp1 paralog was used in the coprecipitation cannot be checked from the cache.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: NK-cell membrane-proteome survey; source of the GO:0016020 HDA. Correctly cited, and the paper itself states that most of its 1843 proteins are not integral membrane proteins but species that may merely be transiently membrane-associated -- which is the basis for marking that row over-annotated.

title: Novel asymmetrically localizing components of human centrosomes identified by complementary proteomics methods.
review_notes: Source of the centrosome IDA. A multi-method centrosome proteomics study (PCP-SILAC, BAC transgeneOmics, antibody screen); ACTR1A received the same annotation from it. Abstract-only in the cache, so the specific figure showing ACTR1B could not be inspected; the annotation is consistent with UniProt's curated location and is accepted on the curator's reading.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Urine extracellular-vesicle shotgun proteome of about 900 proteins; source of the extracellular exosome HDA on both centractins. Correctly cited, but a bulk EV preparation with no orthogonal validation for ACTR1B.

title: Dynactin and Num1 cooperate to establish the cortical anchoring of cytoplasmic dynein in S. pombe.
review_notes: The sole experimental donor behind the GO:0106006 IBA. Verified against the cached abstract: pombe Arp1, Mug5 and Jnm1 are required for cortical dynein anchoring, but Num1/Mcp5 binds dynein independently of dynactin and the dynactin subunits' measured role was microtubule shrinkage and bundling. Correctly cited by PomBase; the objection here is to the term chosen, not to the paper.

title: A Dynamic Protein Interaction Landscape of the Human Centrosome-Cilium Interface.
review_notes: BioID map of the centrosome-cilium interface; source of one ACTR1B-DCTN1 proximity record. Corroborative for dynactin co-membership and centrosomal localisation, but a proximity screen and not a functional result.

title: Mutation analysis of genes within the dynactin complex in a cohort of hereditary peripheral neuropathies.
review_notes: Directly relevant negative result: ACTR1B was screened alongside ACTR1A and DCTN1-6 in 136 inherited peripheral neuropathy patients and no variants of disease significance were found. Useful because it bounds what can be claimed about ACTR1B and disease; contributes no GO annotation.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0. Not a GOA reference for ACTR1B, cited for the dynactin-subunit co-immunoprecipitation roster, including the ACTR1B-ACTR1A pair.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Correctly cited, but methodologically weak for this purpose. All three IntAct records for the ACTR1B-HTT pair -- two hybrid array, two hybrid pooling, validated two hybrid -- originate from this single publication, so UniProt's NbExp=3 does not represent three independent studies. Basis for marking that row over-annotated.

title: Cryo-EM reveals the complex architecture of dynactin's shoulder region and pointed end.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of the dynactin shoulder and pointed end. Used for the architectural point that p150/DCTN1 is housed in the shoulder and reaches the filament via four p50 subunits, which is why the ACTR1B-DCTN1 protein-binding rows should be read as co-membership rather than direct contact.
