Also the source of pig ACTR1A's own GO:0005869 IPI, one of the WITH/FROM donors.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0. Together with BioPlex 2.0 (PMID:28514442) this is the modern basis for ACTR1B sitting in assembled dynactin: IntAct returns ACTR1B with DCTN1-6, CAPZA1/2, CAPZB, ACTR10 and ACTR1A. The co-purification with ACTR1A is the key datum, since it places the two paralogs in one filament.

title: The Chlamydia effector Dre1 binds dynactin to reposition host organelles during infection.
review_notes: The first cryo-EM structure of human dynactin (PDB 9B85, 9B7J), obtained by affinity purification with the Chlamydia effector Dre1. Three uses here, and the third was initially missed. (i) It states that dynactin binds betaIII spectrin on Golgi membranes through its Arp1 subunit, which is load-bearing for the GO:0106006 argument. (ii) The deposited coordinates supply the nucleotide-site and protomer-interface residues used in the bioinformatics analysis; all eight Arp1 protomers are modelled as ACTR1A with bound ADP, and at 3-5 A local filament resolution two 90-per-cent-identical paralogs could not be distinguished, so ACTR1B's absence from the model is not evidence against its incorporation. (iii) The paper is NOT ACTR1A-only at the bench: it probes Dre1 binding with an anti-Arp1b antibody, testing Dre1 variants in co-transfection assays against p150glued, p50-dynamitin and Arp1b, and immunoblotting Strep affinity-purification eluates for Arp1b. Those are Methods statements; the result is carried by the accompanying report that fold-disrupting Dre1 substitutions 'decreased binding of endogenous dynactin subunits' while a conservative F195Y replacement did not, both presupposing a baseline, in the same Figure 2D panel. So the paper does establish a 2025, human, paralog-resolved recovery of endogenous beta-centractin on Dre1, independent of AP-MS -- but the per-subunit bands are in Figure 2D, which the cached text does not render, so the claim is made at that strength and no further. This third use was added after review; it is a genuine strengthening of the GO:0005869 case that the first pass overlooked because the paper writes 'Arp1b' in lower case.

title: Beta-centractin: characterization and distribution of a new member of the centractin family of actin-related proteins.
review_notes: The primary beta-centractin paper and the only work that resolves the two centractin isoforms experimentally. Verified against the cached abstract: it reports new beta-specific antibodies raised because anti-alpha reagents worked poorly on beta, both isoforms confined to the cytosolic 20S dynactin complex with no free pool, a fixed 15:1 alpha:beta ratio, and equal tissue distribution of the two mRNAs (it is gamma-centractin, not beta, that is tissue restricted). Cached entry is abstract-only; all claims used here come from the abstract itself.

title: Centractin (ARP1) associates with spectrin revealing a potential mechanism to link dynactin to intracellular organelles.
review_notes: The earlier Holleran paper reporting that centractin (ARP1) associates with spectrin. Background for the GO:0106006 discussion; superseded for this purpose by PMID:11461920, which demonstrates direct binding and identifies the isoform.

title: The yeast dynactin complex is involved in partitioning the mitotic spindle between mother and daughter cells during anaphase B.
review_notes: Established the yeast dynactin complex and Act5p/ARP1 within it. Cited because SGD derives from it both the GO:0005869 IDA and the GO:0005200 structural-constituent IDA on P38696, the latter being the precedent for the alternative replacement term offered on the GO:0106006 row. Verified in QuickGO that both annotations carry this reference.

title: Transport of antigen loaded MHC II molecules to surface
review_notes: Transport of antigen-loaded MHC II to the surface, a dynein-dependent step; supports the cytosol annotation, which is independently confirmed by human subcellular fractionation of beta-centractin itself.

title: Exocytosis of secretory granule lumen proteins
review_notes: Exocytosis of secretory granule lumen proteins. The reaction is real; ACTR1B's participation in it is not. Membership traces to neutrophil granule-fraction proteomics and places a cytosolic, signal-peptide-less, dynactin-bound protein in a granule lumen and then in the extracellular region. ACTR1A, in the same complex at fifteen times the abundance, is absent from the pathway, which is the decisive argument that this is fractionation carryover.

title: Exocytosis of ficolin-rich granule lumen proteins
review_notes: Exocytosis of ficolin-rich granule lumen proteins; same problem and same reasoning as R-HSA-6798748.

title: ACTR1B bioinformatics: retention of the Arp1 nucleotide site and protomer interface in beta-centractin
review_notes: Bioinformatics analysis written for this review. Derives the Arp1 nucleotide-site and Arp1-Arp1 interface residues from PDB 9B85 rather than from conventional actin by analogy, verifies the PDB-to-UniProt numbering offset at runtime, and tests retention in ACTR1B and in every WITH/FROM donor. Reruns reproduce the committed report byte-for-byte.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACTR1B (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched affinage record, self_evaluation_pairwise: win. Treated as a lead, not as evidence. Its central claim -- beta-centractin as a stoichiometric minor subunit of the cytosolic 20S dynactin complex with no free pool, at roughly 1:15 against alpha-centractin -- was re-verified verbatim against PMID:7696711 before use, which states the ratio the other way round (15:1 alpha:beta) for the same biology. Its own GO grounding, GO:0005198 structural molecule activity, points to the same conclusion reached independently here (GO:0140378, a child of GO:0005198) one level more general. Its two remaining findings are differential-abundance proteomics correlations in platelets and dendritic cells that assay no ACTR1B function, and are not used for any annotation. No mechanistic claim is sourced from this file.

title: UniProt entry P42025 (ACTY_HUMAN, beta-centractin)
review_notes: The machine-fetched UniProt P42025 record. Used for the FUNCTION and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statements, for the absence of signal-peptide and transmembrane features, and for two cross-reference lines that are informative in themselves: GO:0005200 IBA:GO_Central and GO:0005524 IEA:UniProtKB-KW are both still listed here yet both absent from the current GOA download.

title: A mammalian chromatin remodeling complex with similarities to the yeast INO80 complex.
review_notes: Identification of human INO80 by mass spectrometry; the source of ACTR5's first complex-membership and ACTR8 protein-binding rows. Abstract-only in the cache; the abstract confirms the complex composition and its nucleosome-activated ATPase, which is what the row rests on.

title: A Polycomb group protein complex with sequence-specific DNA-binding and selective methyl-lysine-binding activities.
review_notes: Cited in this review only as the source of the experimental evidence that fly Arp5 itself carries for GO:0006338 and GO:0006355, which is what makes the corresponding IBA transfers to ACTR5 non-vacuous. The title is for the Polycomb PhoRC complex, and the Arp5-relevant content is the Pho-dINO80 complex that the same purification identified - so it is a paper indexed under another complex that nonetheless holds a donor gene's evidence. Abstract-only in the cache; the abstract confirms the Pho-dINO80 complex. Nothing about ACTR5 rests on it directly.

title: A YY1-INO80 complex regulates genomic stability through homologous recombination-based repair.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt with ECO:0000269 for ACTR5's nuclear localisation and INO80 association. The cached abstract foregrounds YY1 and INO80 rather than ARP5, so the curator's full-text reading is relied on for the ARP5-specific data; the claims are corroborated independently.

title: The actin-related protein hArp8 accumulates on the mitotic chromosomes and functions in chromosome alignment.
review_notes: Titled for the paralog ARP8 but load-bearing for ARP5: it establishes the ARP5-ARP8 interaction and its loss in metaphase, and provides two ARP5 negatives (ARP5 does not accumulate on mitotic chromosomes; ARP5 depletion does not misalign them). A good example of a paper indexed under a paralog holding this gene's answer.

title: Distinct modes of regulation of the Uch37 deubiquitinating enzyme in the proteasome and in the Ino80 chromatin-remodeling complex.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt with ECO:0000269 for ACTR5's presence in the INO80 complex, and it is the experimental basis for the Reactome reaction behind the nucleoplasm TAS row. Abstract-only in the cache. Not itself a GOA reference for ACTR5.

title: The human actin-related protein hArp5: nucleo-cytoplasmic shuttling and involvement in DNA repair.
review_notes: The gene's own characterisation paper and the source of four GOA rows. Abstract-only in the cache, but every claim used here is in the abstract. Cross-species complementation of yeast arp5-delta is the warrant for the phylogenetic annotations.

title: Arabidopsis actin-related protein ARP5 in multicellular development and DNA repair.
review_notes: The source of the cytoplasm IDA on Arabidopsis ARP5 (Q940Z2), the WITH/FROM donor for ACTR5's GO:0005737 IBA. Retrieved to establish that the donor's evidence is genuine, which it is - so the objection to that row is the is_active_in qualifier, not the source. Also independently reports the ARP5 DNA-repair phenotype in a third kingdom.

title: Fission yeast Iec1-ino80-mediated nucleosome eviction regulates nucleotide and phosphate metabolism.
review_notes: The source of the chromatin-remodeling IDA and the Ino80-complex IPI on fission-yeast arp5 (Q9Y7X8), another WITH/FROM donor. Retrieved for the same reason: to check that the donor carries its own experimental evidence rather than a further inference. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: INO80 chromatin remodeling complex promotes the removal of UV lesions by the nucleotide excision repair pathway.
review_notes: One of only two process annotations whose experiment was performed on ARP5 itself: ARP5 is named among the deleted core components, and ARP5 enrichment at UV-damaged DNA is incision-independent. Also the source of the DDB1 interaction.

title: Subunit organization of the human INO80 chromatin remodeling complex: an evolutionarily conserved core complex catalyzes ATP-dependent nucleosome remodeling.
review_notes: Places ARP5 in the catalytic module with the Snf2 ATPase domain, IES2, IES6 and Tip49a/b, and shows that remodelling requires the complete conserved subunit set. The basis for contributes_to GO:0140658.

title: The mammalian INO80 chromatin remodeling complex is required for replication stress recovery.
review_notes: Full text cached and checked: it contains zero occurrences of "Arp5" or "ACTR5"; the knockdowns were of INO80 and ARP8. ComplexPortal cites it as IMP for two ACTR5 rows via complex-level projection. Marked MISCITED for this gene in the strict sense that the paper does not support an ARP5-specific inference, not because the complex-level claim is wrong.

title: Assembly of the Arp5 (Actin-related Protein) Subunit Involved in Distinct INO80 Chromatin Remodeling Activities.
review_notes: Not in the GOA rows for ACTR5, but it is the primary evidence behind the yeast IDA that donates GO:0030234 to ACTR5 by IBA, and it fixes the direction and the mechanism: the module stimulates ATP hydrolysis, and its insertion domains are what couple hydrolysis to sliding. Retrieved specifically to check that direction before proposing a refinement.

title: Negative Regulation of p21Waf1/Cip1 by Human INO80 Chromatin Remodeling Complex Is Implicated in Cell Cycle Phase G2/M Arrest and Abnormal Chromosome Stability.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; the experiments described are INO80-complex knockdowns, and whether ARP5 was among the subunits depleted cannot be checked from here. Cited by ComplexPortal for two projected rows.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: High-throughput BAC-GFP affinity-purification mass spectrometry. Its three ACTR5 rows are whole-complex co-purifications of INO80, ACTR8 and INO80C, so they add nothing over complex membership.

title: INO80 is required for oncogenic transcription and tumor growth in non-small cell lung cancer.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; concerns Ino80 and Ino80B in NSCLC and does not name ACTR5. Cited by ComplexPortal for the projected positive-regulation-of-transcription row, whose sign should not be read as general for ACTR5.

title: Structure and regulation of the human INO80-nucleosome complex.
review_notes: The first human INO80-nucleosome structure. Establishes that the ARP5-IES6 module contacts the nucleosome opposite the motor domains, that ARP5 alone binds H2A/H2B dimers, and, in the adjacent panel, that ARP5 alone does not bind nucleosomes at in-vivo-relevant concentrations - the reason the nucleosome-binding annotation uses contributes_to.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: The HuRI two-hybrid map. Its single ACTR5 row pairs a nuclear chromatin-remodelling subunit with periplakin, and IntAct logs that one screen under three method names, which is where UniProt's NbExp=3 comes from. Judged an unreplicated screen hit.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex affinity-purification mass spectrometry; its two ACTR5 rows are whole-complex co-purifications, redundant with complex membership.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Endogenous-tag pull-downs; its two ACTR5 rows are whole-complex co-purifications, redundant with complex membership. Its localisation data are consistent with the nuclear annotations.

title: ACTR5 controls CDKN2A and tumor progression in an INO80-independent manner.
review_notes: The only study to assay ACTR5 itself at a promoter, and the basis for the proposed GO:0000122 row. Two caveats recorded rather than hidden. It carries a 2025 erratum (PMID:41071901) correcting Fig. 2D - the CDKN2A western - because the ACTR5 and U87 panels duplicated those of Fig. 3A; the publisher states the conclusions are unaffected, and the RNA-seq, ChIP-qPCR and H3K9me2 data are independent of that panel. And the title's INO80-independence claim rests on the absence of a HepG2-selective essential domain in other subunits, while the requirement it maps runs through IES6, an INO80 subunit - so that claim is recorded in knowledge_gaps rather than annotated. Marked DISPUTED for the INO80-independence claim specifically; the CDKN2A silencing result is used.

title: Conformational switching of Arp5 subunit regulates INO80 chromatin remodeling.
review_notes: The current mechanistic picture of Arp5 in yeast, and the source of the GO:0031491 nucleosome binding IDA on budding-yeast ARP5 that has never propagated to any other ARP5 ortholog. It also separates the arginine anchor that binds nucleosomes from the hydrophobic/acidic patch that binds free H2A-H2B dimers, which is what dissolves the apparent conflict between the human pull-down and the missing acidic-patch foot.

title: Trio Whole Exome Sequencing in Chinese Childhood-Onset Lupus Reveals Novel Candidate Genes.
review_notes: Cited by the affinage record. Its only ACTR5 datum is that one de novo variant enhanced type I interferon signalling in an IFN-beta luciferase reporter, in a candidate-gene screen of 50 trios. Too preliminary to support any annotation; recorded so that the affinage finding is accounted for rather than silently dropped.

title: Erratum for the Research Article "ACTR5 controls CDKN2A and tumor progression in an INO80-independent manner" by X. Xu et al.
review_notes: The 2025 erratum to PMID:36563143. Retrieved and read: the ACTR5 and U87 western blots in Fig. 2D were inadvertent duplicates of those in Fig. 3A, the figure has been corrected, and the authors' conclusions are stated to be unaffected. Cited here because the affinage record rests on PMID:36563143 and does not flag it.

title: Recognition and remodelling of nucleosomes and hexasomes by the human INO80 complex.
review_notes: The decisive human structural evidence, and it postdates every GOA annotation on this gene. It identifies ARP5's DNA-binding domain as the element contacting nucleosomal DNA in the minor groove at SHL -2/-3, states that human ARP5 lacks the fungal acidic-patch-binding foot, and deposits the structures (9GCG, 9GE5) in whose ARP5 chain ADP is modelled. Note that the ARP5-side sliding requirement it cites is fungal, not human - the mutants made in this study were in IES6 and in the H2A acidic patch.

title: UCHL5 binds INO80 complex
review_notes: The Reactome reaction behind the nucleoplasm TAS row. UCHL5 association with human INO80 is experimentally established (PMID:18922472), and the nucleoplasmic assignment is consistent with every direct localisation result for ACTR5.

title: ACTR5 (ARP5) actin-fold audit: nucleotide site and filament interface
review_notes: This review's own reproducible analysis: nucleotide ligands in the ARP5 chain of all six deposited human INO80 structures, a reciprocal test that the site is the canonical actin cleft, the actin catalytic positions, and the F-actin protomer interface with ARP1 as a positive control. Regenerating it reproduces the committed report byte-for-byte, and four deliberate break-tests confirm the guards fail loudly.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACTR5 (human)
review_notes: The machine-fetched affinage record (self_evaluation_pairwise: win, 2 citations, 3 dated findings). Its narrative is faithful to PMID:36563143 for the HCC/CDKN2A phenotype, which is why that one sentence is cited here, but its corpus coverage is narrow: it found 2 papers where UniProt lists 12 primary references, and it missed the entire structural literature on this gene - both human INO80-nucleosome studies - which is where ARP5's actual molecular function is established. It also cites PMID:36563143 without flagging that paper's 2025 erratum, and its third finding rests on a single de novo variant in a lupus trio-WES screen. Marked LOW_QUALITY for coverage, not for misattribution.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/IBA method reference for the four rows at PANTHER node PTN000234048. The node was audited directly: QuickGO withFrom returns numberOfHits 348 over 87 gene products, all ARP8 orthologues with no conventional actins, each carrying the same 4 terms. The committed PTHR11937 PAINT file confirms 5 assignments at that node, including an IRD (NOT) block on GO:0005200.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SL-0191 and SL-0468 confirmed against the UniProt locations API to map to GO:0005634 and GO:0005694. Both underlying UniProt statements carry ECO:0000269|PubMed:18163988, so these transfers rest on experimental data.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: HPA immunofluorescence; concordant with three other nuclear rows.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: The method reference is correctly cited, but its precondition is not met for the five rows that use it here. It promises transfer of experimentally verified manual annotation; the mouse Actr8 source annotations are ComplexPortal projections of a complex-level phenotype onto all 15 INO80 subunits, from an Ino80 conditional knockout in which Actr8 was not manipulated. Verified by QuickGO reference=PMID:23979016 returning 80 annotations = 16 entities x 5 terms. Flagged MISCITED because the pipeline treats a projected annotation as gene-specific experimental evidence.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: Both ARBA rows are true but subsumed by more specific annotations already present on this gene.

title: A mammalian chromatin remodeling complex with similarities to the yeast INO80 complex.
review_notes: Identification of the mammalian INO80 complex, including ARP8; the source of UniProt's 'IDENTIFICATION IN INO80 COMPLEX' line. Cached abstract-only; IntAct logs 17 ACTR8 records from it.

title: A YY1-INO80 complex regulates genomic stability through homologous recombination-based repair.
review_notes: Supports the nucleus IDA and a second, independent Ino80-complex IDA. The paper's genetic work is on YY1 and INO80, so no ARP8-specific repair claim is drawn from it.

title: The actin-related protein hArp8 accumulates on the mitotic chromosomes and functions in chromosome alignment.
review_notes: The key ARP8-specific human paper for the mitotic function and the source of the INO80-independence controls. Cached abstract-only, but the abstract states the controls explicitly, so nothing is inferred beyond it.

title: Distinct modes of regulation of the Uch37 deubiquitinating enzyme in the proteasome and in the Ino80 chromatin-remodeling complex.
review_notes: Establishes UCHL5/Uch37 as an INO80-complex component, which is why the ACTR8-UCHL5 protein-binding rows were judged real within-complex contacts rather than screen noise. Corroborated by ComplexPortal CPX-846 membership.

title: Proteome-wide search reveals unexpected RNA-binding proteins in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: The sole evidential basis, in any organism, for the GO:0003729 mRNA binding IBA. Full text checked: yeast ARP8 is in the confirmed set (Table 2, 231 targets at FDR <= 0.01 %, the paper's own SAM cut-off), not among the unvalidated candidates, so the source annotation is sound and the objection is to the propagation, not to the paper.

title: The mammalian INO80 complex is recruited to DNA damage sites in an ARP8 dependent manner.
review_notes: The strongest ARP8-specific human evidence for a role in DSB repair, and notable for showing the recruitment mechanism differs from yeast. Cached abstract-only; the ARP8 requirement is stated in the abstract. Not currently cited by any GOA row on this gene.

title: Subunit organization of the human INO80 chromatin remodeling complex: an evolutionarily conserved core complex catalyzes ATP-dependent nucleosome remodeling.
review_notes: Places ARP8 in the remodelling-competent module of the human complex. Supports the chromatin-remodeling IDA and one Ino80-complex IDA; the same term/evidence/reference triple appears twice in the GOA TSV, from ComplexPortal and from UniProt.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: High-throughput detection of ARP8 in highly purified sperm nuclei. Supports the nucleus HDA; no functional inference drawn.

title: Structure of Actin-related protein 8 and its contribution to nucleosome binding.
review_notes: The central structural and biochemical paper on human ARP8: PDB 4FO0 with ATP bound, the loop insertions that explain the inability to polymerise, a measured low basal ATPase on the human protein, and quantitative nucleosome, (H3-H4)2, H2A-H2B and DNA affinities. Full text read, including the paragraph that attributes the S. cerevisiae Arp8-Arp4-actin-HSA sub-complex's DNA binding mainly to the HSA/DBINO domain rather than to Arp8 - a qualification that constrains what can be claimed for human ARP8 DNA binding, and by analogy only, since the module measured was the yeast one. Note that Table 2 is a mixed-species table carrying both Hs and Sc rows, which is the trap this review fell into once and corrected. Not cited by any GOA row on this gene.

title: The mINO80 chromatin remodeling complex is required for efficient telomere replication and maintenance of genome stability.
review_notes: A sound paper, cited for the wrong subject. Its experiment is an Ino80 conditional knockout, and Actr8 is not named in the abstract; yet via a ComplexPortal projection to all 15 subunits and then Ensembl Compara it is the sole basis for five human ACTR8 rows, including regulation of embryonic development and positive regulation of telomere maintenance in response to DNA damage. MISCITED describes the use of the reference, not its quality. Cached abstract-only, which is sufficient because the abstract states the knockout target.

title: The mammalian INO80 chromatin remodeling complex is required for replication stress recovery.
review_notes: One of the few ComplexPortal-assigned rows whose paper genuinely assayed ARP8: the fibre-labelling experiments used cells deficient for Ino80 and Arp8. Full text available; checked specifically to confirm ARP8 was manipulated rather than assumed.

title: DNA binding properties of the actin-related protein Arp8 and its role in DNA repair.
review_notes: The other essential ARP8-specific human paper: ssDNA preference by competition gel shift, the requirement for the basic N-terminal extension, ATP-dependent inhibition of DNA binding mapped to the annotated pocket residues, and a conditional human ARP8 knockout that is repair-defective. Full text read. Not cited by any GOA row on this gene.

title: Negative Regulation of p21Waf1/Cip1 by Human INO80 Chromatin Remodeling Complex Is Implicated in Cell Cycle Phase G2/M Arrest and Abnormal Chromosome Stability.
review_notes: Correctly cited for two complex-level rows, and independently valuable as the repressive counterpart to PMID:27641337 - the pair is why the direction-neutral GO:0006355 is the correct parent and no signed upgrade was proposed. The manipulation is INO80 RNAi; ARP8 is not knocked down.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: Large-scale quantitative AP-MS; corroborates the ACTR8-ACTR5 contact.

title: Synergy and antagonism in regulation of recombinant human INO80 chromatin remodeling complex.
review_notes: A reconstituted human minimal core containing ARP8 that slides nucleosomes, supporting the chromatin-remodeling process annotation. Note the deletions tested were of Ies2 and Arp5/Ies6, not Arp8, so this paper does not establish an ARP8-specific requirement for remodelling.

title: INO80 is required for oncogenic transcription and tumor growth in non-small cell lung cancer.
review_notes: Supports the positive-regulation-of-transcription row at the complex level; the silenced gene is INO80 and the subunits discussed are Ino80 and Ino80B. Cached abstract-only, so the annotation is not second-guessed - it is kept and marked non-core on the grounds that the complex acts in both directions.

title: Distinct roles of ATM and ATR in the regulation of ARP8 phosphorylation to prevent chromosome translocations.
review_notes: ARP8-specific human evidence that ARP8 is a regulated node in DSB repair rather than a passive subunit, and the source of the negative regulatory arm that argues against treating positive regulation of DNA repair as ARP8's core statement. Full text available. Not cited by any GOA row on this gene.

title: The Arp8 and Arp4 module acts as a DNA sensor controlling INO80 chromatin remodeling.
review_notes: Yeast, and used only as yeast: it corroborates that the Arp8 N-terminus is the DNA-contacting element, which matches the human deletion data, but the linker-length-sensor mechanism is not asserted for human ARP8 and is recorded as a knowledge gap instead.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex-style network; the largest contributor to ACTR8's IntAct record (30 of 82) and mostly low-confidence singletons, but the UCHL5 pair it supports is independently established.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Proteome-scale map; corroborates the ACTR8-UCHL5 contact. Carries a Publisher Correction, PMID:41039152 (Nature 646:E16, Oct 2025, 'Publisher Correction: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics'), found via the article's own CommentsCorrections RefType=ErratumIn. It is a publisher-side correction rather than a data or figure-integrity notice, the article is not retracted, and the single claim resting on it here - an ACTR8-UCHL5 association also established by PMID:18922472 and by ComplexPortal CPX-846 membership - is unaffected. Recorded rather than acted on: is_invalid is deliberately NOT set, since that flag is for retracted or replaced references.

title: UCHL5 binds INO80 complex
review_notes: Reaction-level compartment assignment behind the nucleoplasm TAS. Independently corroborates that UCHL5 belongs with the INO80 complex.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACTR8 (human)
review_notes: Recorded so the provider gap is machine-readable, and cited by nothing in this review. The record is empty - n_discoveries 0, citation_count 0, no findings table, no citations, and no self_evaluation_pairwise score - so the trust gates were clear only because there was nothing to gate. That is a provider gap, not a literature gap: the UniProt RN list alone carries 13 references, including a 2.6 A crystal structure whose RP line reads FUNCTION, SUBUNIT, AND ATP-BINDING SITES, and this review rests on 20 primary papers. The file is deliberately not used as a supporting_text anywhere, because a provider's silence is weaker evidence than a provider's assertion, and the campaign has already been burned once by treating an empty provider record as a negative result. The consequence is that the best-practices warning 'No annotations reference available deep research files' stands unresolved on this gene; silencing it would require citing an empty file as if it said something. On the enum value: LOW_QUALITY is defined as 'correctly cited but methodologically weak', and its 'correctly cited' half is vacuous here because nothing cites the file. It is used as the nearest available fit for a machine-generated record that returned nothing on a gene with 13 UniProt references; the alternatives are worse, since UNVERIFIED would imply the record was never examined and VERIFIED would imply there was something to verify.

title: UniProtKB entry Q9H981 (ARP8_HUMAN)
review_notes: Swiss-Prot reviewed, PE 1, entry version 182. Source of the ATP-binding feature positions (55, 56, 283-286, with no ECO:0000250 similarity tag, i.e. from PDB 4FO0), the SUBUNIT and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statements, and the ACTR5/UCHL5 interaction lines. Note the DR block still lists GO:0005524 ATP binding as IEA:UniProtKB-KW while GOA carries no ATP-binding annotation at all, which is the gap this review proposes to fill.

title: PANTHER PTHR11937 PAINT annotation table (cached in this repository)
review_notes: The per-node PAINT assignments, without which the IBA rows can only be read as a flat WITH/FROM list. Shows all 5 assignments at PTN000234048 - four IBD positives and, importantly, an IRD (NOT) block on GO:0005200 structural constituent of cytoskeleton against the conventional-actin node PTN000940351. PTHR11937 carries 9 GO:0005200 rows in total: 8 IRD negatives at divergent nodes and 1 IBD positive at the actin node.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: The UniProt ortholog-transfer pipeline behind the GO:0033011 ISS row. Its single donor, mouse Actrt2 Q9D9L5, was resolved and confirmed to hold GO:0033011 by IDA, so the transfer lands at the donor's own experimentally supported term.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT/PANTHER pipeline behind both IBA rows. All 36 WITH/FROM tokens across the two rows were resolved programmatically; 34 resolve to protein entries and every one of those carries its own experimental evidence for the term it donated. Donor quality is therefore not in question on either row.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Keyword mapping from UniProt subcellular location SL-0090. The location line it renders is itself an ECO:0000250 by-similarity statement with no source entry cited, so the row adds no observation; it survives only because GO:0005856 is a true ancestor of GO:0033011.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara transfer of the GO:0033011 IDA from mouse Actrt2. Same single donor as the GO_REF:0000024 row, so the two are one ortholog inference by two pipelines rather than two independent lines of support.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Inter-ontology inference whose WITH/FROM field is literally the GO term GO:0005200, so the GO:0007010 row contains no observation of its own and stands or falls with that molecular function.

title: Identification of two cDNAs for human actin-related proteins (Arps) that have remarkable similarity to conventional actin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction. The gene identity was checked against the UniProt entry rather than assumed - ACTRT2's AltName is Actin-related protein M2 with synonym ARPM2, so hArpM2 is this gene. Cited for its testable sequence claim, which this review confirms, and flagged for its untestable one, which should not be read as evidence for GO:0007010.

title: Novel actin-related proteins Arp-T1 and Arp-T2 as components of the cytoskeletal calyx of the mammalian sperm head.
review_notes: The founding paper for this gene and the source of its strongest experimental claim. PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum. Abstract only in the cache, so all quotes are from the abstract; the species used for immunofluorescence is genuinely not stated there, which is why the GO:0033150 row uses ISS rather than IDA. Also listed in the UniProt entry as reference 2, where it is recorded only as a nucleotide sequence submission - a reminder that UniProt's silence on function is not evidence that the literature is silent.

title: Proteomic pattern changes associated with obesity-induced asthenozoospermia.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction. Abstract only. This is the only human protein-level localisation for ACTRT2, which is why it is cited despite being a differential-proteomics study in which the abundance change is correlative. The middle-piece signal is reported here as stated rather than filtered out, because it is not a perinuclear-theca compartment and no annotation accounts for it.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction, full text available. The citation is correct and the interaction is real, but the imported pair is one arm of a spoke-expanded co-purification of the CCT chaperonin and its co-chaperone; all ten ACTRT2 records in IntAct come from this one experiment. The merged ACTR1B review characterised the same publication the same way.

title: Loss of perinuclear theca ACTRT1 causes acrosome detachment and severe male subfertility in mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction. Abstract only in the cache. The knockout in this paper is of Actrt1, not Actrt2, so nothing here is used as an ACTRT2 loss-of-function result; what it supports is complex membership, which the abstract states for ACTRT2 by name. This paper has yielded biological-process annotations for ACTL7A and ACTL9 but none for Actrt1 or Actrt2, which is the traceable origin of ACTRT2's process-annotation gap.

title: The perinuclear theca protein Calicin helps shape the sperm head and maintain the nuclear structure in mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction. Found by querying the mouse ortholog's own GOA record, not from the affinage narrative, which does not cite it - a notable omission given that it is the source of the mouse IDA that both of ACTRT2's perinuclear-theca rows are transferred from.

title: Structures and mechanisms of actin ATP hydrolysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction. Abstract only. Corroborates the previous reference on the point that matters here, that hydrolysis is a property of the filamentous state, and is cited for that alone.

title: Mutagenic analysis of actin reveals the mechanism of His161 flipping that triggers ATP hydrolysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction, full text available in the cache. Not about ACTRT2 at all; cited to establish what actin's His161 and Pro-rich loop do, so that the residue census in the bioinformatics analysis rests on a stated mechanism rather than on a residue name. The important consequence, read from the surrounding text rather than the single sentence, is that hydrolysis is coupled to filament incorporation - which is why the lost trigger and the degenerate protomer interface are one observation, not two.

title: ACTRT2 deficiency increases spermatogonia vulnerability to ferroptosis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction, and the only knockout study of this gene, so its relevance is high. Marked LOW_QUALITY on methodological grounds rather than citation grounds: the in vivo busulfan comparison uses heterozygotes rather than nulls, the mechanism rests on expression changes in four regulators rather than a demonstrated activity, and the cell type is several stages earlier than the spermatid stage at which the perinuclear theca forms. The shrunken-tubule phenotype of the null is the part this review relies on.

title: Actin-related protein T3 is required for acrosome biogenesis and sperm function in mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (2026, Development), no retraction. Abstract only. This is the paper being reviewed in parallel for ACTRT3; it is cited here solely for the co-immunoprecipitation that names ACTRT2. Note the F-actin remodelling result in this paper concerns heterologous expression of Actrt3, not Actrt2, and is deliberately not transferred to this gene.

title: ACTRT2 bioinformatics: nucleotide site, filament interface, IBA source audit, PAINT node audit, interaction and annotation censuses
review_notes: Reproducible analysis written for this review; a fresh run of analyze_actrt2.py reproduces both RESULTS.md and results.json byte-identically. Guards were tested by breaking them - a deliberately wrong named-site residue raises, a missing input names its fix command, and the dead-accession guard failed its first break test (a MERGED accession returns a row whose primaryAccession matches the request) and was strengthened to check entryType and sequence length.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACTRT2 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched precomputed research, gates_passed true with 6 citations, used as a lead rather than as evidence. Two concrete defects. One of its six citations, PMID:bio_10.1101_2025.03.27.645694, is a bioRxiv DOI in a PMID-shaped field rather than a PubMed identifier, and nothing in this review rests on it. More importantly it omits PMID:35793634, the calicin paper that is the actual source of mouse Actrt2's GO:0033011 IDA and of its only curated protein interaction - the paper that both of this gene's perinuclear-theca annotations are ultimately transferred from. That was found by querying the ortholog's own GOA record, not from the narrative. Its GO grounding is also engaged with above rather than imported.

title: UniProt entry Q8TDY3 (ACTT2_HUMAN), Actin-related protein T2
review_notes: The primary record. It carries no FUNCTION comment at all, and its only location statement is by similarity, which is why this review's compartment reasoning rests on the literature and on the mouse ortholog rather than on UniProt.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: The pipeline behind the perinuclear-theca ISS row. Its single source, mouse Actrt3 (UniProtKB:Q8BXF8), is a 1:1 orthologue at 79.4 per cent global identity carrying the term by IDA, so this is ortholog transfer of a directly observed location.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PANTHER/PAINT, the source of both IBA rows. All 24 protein donors on the GO:0015629 row and all 10 on the GO:0005200 row resolve and every one carries its own experimental evidence for the term it donated, so no source-weakness argument is available against either row; the questions are about transfer and granularity instead.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Correctly implements the mapping, but the UniProt statement it maps is by similarity in every clause and names no source entry, so the three rows it produces are one inference re-coded three times rather than three independent lines of support.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Compara transfer from mouse Actrt3, which holds both transferred terms by IDA. The rows land on exactly the terms the donor holds rather than above them, so the ACRV1 pattern of a propagation that is less precise than its own donor does not apply here.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: The inter-ontology step from GO:0005200 to GO:0007010. It carries no evidence of its own, so its standing depends entirely on the molecular-function row it is derived from.

title: Identification of two cDNAs for human actin-related proteins (Arps) that have remarkable similarity to conventional actin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, not retracted, abstract only. Sound for what it reports (two cDNAs, broad low-level transcript, conserved ATP motif). It is weaker than it is often used for: it is transcript-level, pre-dates quantitative RNA-seq, and says nothing about protein.

title: Nuclear localization of profilin III-ArpM1 complex in mouse spermiogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, not retracted, abstract only in the cache. Directly supports the GO:0001673 IDA on the mouse orthologue and the proposed GO:0005522 row. The abstract states the co-immunoprecipitation result plainly, so no full-text inference is required for that claim.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, not retracted, full text cached. A high-quality dataset that here yields one partner and no complex. The contrast with the merged ACTR1B review, which kept its row from this same publication, is instructive: there the partner set was coherent with assembled dynactin (DCTN1-DCTN6, CAPZ, ACTR10, ACTR1A). The difference is the partner set, not the publication.

title: Loss of Profilin3 Impairs Spermiogenesis by Affecting Acrosome Biogenesis, Autophagy, Manchette Development and Mitochondrial Organization.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, not retracted, full text cached and read. The only reference here with full text, and reading past the ARPM1 sentences was decisive: the section "F-Actin Organization Is Not Altered in Pfn3-Deficient Sperm" bears directly on the cytoskeletal rows and would have been missed by a symbol-keyed search.

title: The perinuclear theca protein Calicin helps shape the sperm head and maintain the nuclear structure in mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, not retracted, abstract only. The cached abstract does not name Actrt3, so nothing about ACTRT3 is quoted from it and the curator's experimental call is not second-guessed. Listed because it establishes that the perinuclear-theca localisation dates from 2022, four years before the dedicated knockout paper, and because it is absent from the deep-research record - a paper titled for another gene holding this gene's evidence.

title: Actin-related protein T3 is required for acrosome biogenesis and sperm function in mice.
review_notes: Verified by efetch because esummary returned no record for this very recent PMID (Development 153(3):dev205283, 1 Feb 2026; PublicationTypeList is Journal Article only, no CommentsCorrections, not retracted). Abstract only in the cache. Note that the deep-research record lists this study twice, once as PMID:41668650 and once as a bioRxiv DOI in a PMID-shaped field; the two are the same study, not independent corroboration.

title: ACTRT3 bioinformatics: nucleotide site, profilin surface, filament interface, and PAINT's own handling of GO:0005200
review_notes: Reproducible analysis in this gene's folder; both results.json and RESULTS.md were confirmed byte-identical on a fresh run. Contact detection, alignment, substitution classing and the two-scheme sensitivity check are deliberately identical to the merged ACTL8 script so the tallies are comparable; the profilin contact set and the PAINT-negation survey are new here. All ACTRT3 tallies are unchanged under BLOSUM45/-14/-2 as well as BLOSUM62/-11/-1.

title: ACTRT3 reference-scope audit: how many entities each cited reference annotates
review_notes: Written after the merged ACTR8 review showed that querying QuickGO by reference, rather than by gene, exposes complex-to-subunit projections a per-gene view cannot see. Run over every PMID this review cites. Two defects were fixed in it during review, both of the kind it exists to catch. First it counted bare GO:0005515 as a functional claim, which made every interaction paper look like a projection and mis-flagged PMID:35793634. Second, and worse, it reported per-term, per-code and per-database breakdowns from one 200-row page while taking the total from the API's hit count, silently mixing a true total with a 2 per cent sample on the one reference large enough for it to matter; every total is now its own filtered count query, the sampled fields are named *_seen, `truncated` and `unaccounted_annotations` are emitted, and ComplexPortal is probed unconditionally because a projected tail can sit entirely outside a sample. Its per-code totals are deliberately not used for any claim: QuickGO's evidenceCode filter is not exact-only, so they overlap and do not partition the total.

title: ACTRT3 WITH/FROM resolution: every token resolved, with each source's own evidence for the term it donated
review_notes: Companion table to RESULTS.md. All 24 protein donors on the GO:0015629 row and all 10 on the GO:0005200 row resolve, with zero unresolved tokens, and every one carries its own experimental evidence for the donated term.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ACTRT3 (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated, gates_passed true, and its narrative is broadly right. Two defects were found. Its four citations include one bioRxiv DOI in a PMID-shaped field, and comparing that entry with PMID:41668650 shows the two are the same study - the same theca localisation, the same cap-phase acrosome defect, the same GM130 and TGN46 result and the same co-immunoprecipitation set - so the record presents one study as two dated findings. It also omits PMID:35793634 entirely, which is the reference behind the perinuclear-theca IDA on the mouse orthologue and hence behind two of this gene's GOA rows; that paper is titled for a different gene, which is presumably why a symbol-keyed retrieval missed it. Marked LOW_QUALITY on those two counts rather than on any incorrect assertion.

title: UniProt entry Q9BYD9 (ACTT3_HUMAN)
review_notes: Machine-fetched record, used for provenance rather than for conclusions. Its three subcellular-location clauses are all ECO:0000250 with no source entry cited, which is the basis for the redundancy judgement on the three GO_REF:0000044 rows.

title: PANTHER PTHR11937 PAINT annotation table (cached in this repository)
review_notes: The per-node PAINT assignments, without which an IBA row can only be read as a flat WITH/FROM list. The count derived here - one IBD assertion of GO:0005200 at PTN000940351 and eight IRD negations of it at divergent nodes, nine rows in total - was reached independently by the merged ACTR8 review from the same file, which is a useful cross-check because the two reviews approached the family from opposite ends.

title: Endothelial catabolism of extracellular adenosine during hypoxia: the role of surface adenosine deaminase and CD26.
review_notes: Full text available; directly demonstrates hypoxia-induced ecto-ADA/CD26 catabolizing extracellular adenosine to inosine. Supports the ecto-ADA localization, adenosine catabolic process, and hypoxia-response annotations.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Proteome-scale AP-MS interactome (BioPlex). Source of a bare 'protein binding' IPI to POTEF; correctly cited but not functionally informative for ADA.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome dataset; source of a bare 'protein binding' IPI to POTEF. Correctly cited but not functionally informative for ADA.

title: Direct association of adenosine deaminase with a T cell activation antigen, CD26.
review_notes: Foundational paper establishing the specific ADA-CD26/DPP4 interaction via the CD26 extracellular domain. Underpins the ecto-ADA/CD26 (moonlighting) annotations; the bare 'protein binding' MF is uninformative and marked over-annotated.

title: Demonstration of adenosine deaminase activity in human fibroblast lysosomes.
review_notes: Direct biochemical assay of human ADA activity (adenosine->inosine, Km 37 uM) and demonstration of a minor lysosomal pool (~10% of total activity). Supports the core MF and the lysosome localization.

title: Full genetic rescue of adenosine deaminase-deficient mice through introduction of the human gene.
review_notes: In vivo demonstration that the human ADA gene fully complements the lethal ADA-deficient mouse phenotype, confirming ADA's essential catabolic function.

title: An adenosine deaminase (ADA) allele contains two newly identified deleterious mutations (Y97C and L106V) that interact to abolish enzyme activity.
review_notes: Characterizes ADASCID loss-of-function mutations and the link between loss of activity and toxic deoxyATP/deoxyadenosine accumulation. Supports the core adenosine/deoxyadenosine deaminase functions and the disease mechanism.

title: ADAM10-mediated cleavage of L1 adhesion molecule at the cell surface and in released membrane vesicles.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports ADAM10 substrate cleavage at the cell surface and Golgi/vesicle contexts.

title: Endocytosis of synaptic ADAM10 in neuronal plasticity and Alzheimer's disease.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports synaptic ADAM10 clathrin-dependent endocytosis and plasma-membrane removal.

title: TspanC8 tetraspanins differentially regulate the cleavage of ADAM10 substrates, Notch activation and ADAM10 membrane compartmentalization.
review_notes: Cached full text verified; supports broad ADAM10 ectodomain shedding, APP alpha-secretase cleavage, Notch S2 cleavage, and tetraspanin-dependent compartmentalization.

title: A Dock-and-Lock Mechanism Clusters ADAM10 at Cell-Cell Junctions to Promote α-Toxin Cytotoxicity.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports Staphylococcus aureus alpha-toxin pore formation as pathogen exploitation of junctional ADAM10, retained as non-core context.

title: GDE2-RECK controls ADAM10 α-secretase-mediated cleavage of amyloid precursor protein.
review_notes: Cached full text verified; supports ADAM10 alpha-secretase cleavage of APP to generate sAPPalpha and suppress amyloid-beta generation.

title: Use of the ND evidence code for Gene Ontology (GO) terms
review_notes: The GO reference behind all three annotations on this gene. Its use here is correct: ND records that a curator found no data, which is the accurate state of a locus whose protein product has been sought and not found.

title: Transcripts encoding the sperm surface protein tMDC II are non-functional in the human.
review_notes: The gene's primary reference, and the ECO:0000269 source for UniProt's FUNCTION line. PubMed record checked for retraction, erratum and expression of concern via CommentsCorrections/RefType: none. The paper has no DOI in PubMed; a Crossref bibliographic lookup resolves it to 10.1042/bj3410771 with empty update-to and updated-by fields, so there is no correction with a null PubMed id either. Cached abstract only; the quoted claims are both in the abstract.

title: The MDC family of proteins and their processing during epididymal transit.
review_notes: Establishes the orthologous protein's sperm localisation in the very species used as the alignment reference, which is what makes the human loss of signal peptide and transmembrane anchor interpretable. Explicitly not used to annotate the human gene. PMID verified against PubMed; no corrections; no DOI in PubMed and none required, as nothing load-bearing rests on it.

title: The status, quality, and expansion of the NIH full-length cDNA project: the Mammalian Gene Collection (MGC).
review_notes: A resource paper, cited by UniProt as the source of two full-length human ADAM5 cDNA clones from testis. Relevant only as evidence that the locus is transcribed; it makes no claim about ADAM5 itself and no finding is extracted from it.

title: Testicular and epididymal ADAMs: expression and function during fertilization.
review_notes: Background review, used for the complex composition that the 2026 knockout paper corroborates independently. PMID verified against PubMed; no corrections; Crossref relation fields empty. Cached abstract only, and the quoted sentence is in the abstract.

title: Lactadherin is a candidate oviduct Lewis X trisaccharide receptor on porcine spermatozoa.
review_notes: Included to document that orthologue-level evidence for ADAM5 as an adhesion protein exists in a third species, and to record that it was considered and deliberately not propagated to the human pseudogene. PMID verified against PubMed; no corrections. Note the quoted sentence is garbled in the published abstract ("ADAM5, which spermatozoa, was confidently identified"); it is quoted verbatim as printed.

title: Association of Inherited Copy Number Variation in ADAM3A and ADAM5 Pseudogenes with Oropharynx Cancer Risk and Outcome.
review_notes: Cited only for the RNA-level hypothesis recorded under knowledge_gaps, and deliberately not used to support any annotation: the mechanism rests on a sequence-based prediction plus a copy-number association in 152 cases and 155 controls, and the amplicon contains ADAM3A as well as ADAM5, so the effect is not attributed to ADAM5 by the design. PMID verified against PubMed; no corrections, and Crossref update-to/updated-by are empty. Worth recording that verifying this citation caught a bug in my own checking script: an unanchored .//ArticleId XPath returned a DOI from the article's reference list (10.1002/pros.23950, The Prostate) instead of the article's own 10.3390/genes13122408.

title: ADAM5 is required for sperm-zona pellucida binding and sperm oviduct migration†.
review_notes: The decisive current paper for this gene and absent from the affinage record, which returned no content at all for ADAM5; found by searching the orthologue and the family rather than the human symbol. PMID verified against PubMed (Biol Reprod 2026, 10.1093/biolre/ioaf254); no CommentsCorrections of any type, and Crossref shows empty update-to, updated-by and relation. Its value here is twofold: it establishes what the intact orthologue does, and it supplies a 2026 primary-literature statement of the human pseudogene status from authors with every incentive to claim human relevance. Cached abstract only; all three quoted findings are in the abstract.

title: ADAM5 (human, Q6NVV9) — catalytic-motif, ortholog-length and GO-census analysis
review_notes: Local reproducible analysis committed alongside this review. Re-fetches every value from UniProt and QuickGO on each run, asserts numberOfHits == len(results) on every paginated query, asserts the motif scan discriminates in both directions, and asserts the lost/retained feature ordering with no threshold. The --self-test mode break-tests each guard and was itself verified to fail with the expected messages when a guard is disabled. A fresh run reproduces the committed RESULTS.md and results.json byte-identically.

title: UniProt entry Q6NVV9 (ADAM5_HUMAN)
review_notes: The downloaded UniProt record. Both quoted spans are on single physical lines, so neither crosses a CC continuation prefix.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Checked against the current interpro2go release: IPR013273 maps only to GO:0030198, and none of ADAMTSL1's other thirteen InterPro entries carries any GO mapping.

title: Punctin, a novel ADAMTS-like molecule, ADAMTSL-1, in extracellular matrix.
review_notes: Founding description of the protein, cited by UniProt with ECO:0000269 for subunit, subcellular location, tissue specificity, glycosylation, mass spectrometry and disulfide bonds. Cached record is abstract-only. The localisation caveat that must travel with it is that the assay used epitope-tagged recombinant protein in a heterologous cell line.

title: O-fucosylation of thrombospondin type 1 repeats in ADAMTS-like-1/punctin-1 regulates secretion: implications for the ADAMTS superfamily.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt with ECO:0000269 for four glycosylation sites and for subcellular location. Cached record is abstract-only; the claims used here are all stated in the abstract. Experiments were performed on the short punctin-1 form.

title: Post-translational modification of thrombospondin type-1 repeats in ADAMTS-like 1/punctin-1 by C-mannosylation of tryptophan.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt with ECO:0000269 for three carbohydrate sites, five mutagenesis entries and subcellular location. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: MADD-4 is a secreted cue required for midline-oriented guidance in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Used only for the family-level context and for the authors' own statement that the mammalian role is unknown. Nothing from the nematode phenotype is carried into a human annotation.

title: Microenvironmental regulation by fibrillin-1.
review_notes: The most informative molecular-function experiment ever performed on human ADAMTSL1, and it is a negative. Found only because a sibling review of ADAMTSL3 surfaced it: the paper is titled for fibrillin-1, so no ADAMTSL1-keyed search reaches it, and it is absent from ADAMTSL1's GOA and from the affinage record. One caveat travels with it, and it is the isoform question that runs through this whole review. The methods describe the reagent as "Recombinant full length ADAMTSL-1" but give no length, and in 2017 the Apte laboratory stated that no construct for the 1762-residue form existed. Both RefSeq entries were available in 2012 (NP_443098 for the 525-residue isoform 1, NP_001035362 for the 1762-residue isoform 3), so the paper alone does not settle which was tested; the balance of evidence favours the short punctin-1 form. The negative is therefore firm for whatever was assayed and probably does not test the nine additional thrombospondin repeats, four Ig-like domains and PLAC domain of the long isoform. Recorded as a bounded negative rather than a blanket one.

title: Time-resolved analysis of the matrix metalloproteinase 10 substrate degradome.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, but the ADAMTSL1 result is stated in the abstract and named as one of the paper's three headline findings. Independent of the 2002 tagged-construct localisation, which is why it is used as corroboration for the proposed GO:0031012 row.

title: Hedgehog pathway inhibition in chondrosarcoma using the smoothened inhibitor IPI-926 directly inhibits sarcoma cell growth.
review_notes: Adjudicated and deliberately not annotated, recorded here rather than only in the gene notes because it bears on this review's claim that ADAMTSL1 has no gene-specific functional data. Three reasons for declining. The cached record is abstract-only and the abstract does not state the direction of the effect, so neither GO:0008284 nor GO:0008285 can be chosen and picking either would be a guess. The assay is a chondrosarcoma cell line in a Hedgehog-inhibitor study, a disease context with no normal-physiology counterpart for this gene. And a proliferation phenotype bears on neither of this review's recorded gaps, since it identifies no molecular function and says nothing about matrix organisation, so it narrows neither. It does mean the review's claim should be read precisely as no molecular function and no matrix-organisation evidence, rather than no functional observation of any kind.

title: Identification and functional analysis of an ADAMTSL1 variant associated with a complex phenotype including congenital glaucoma, craniofacial, and other systemic features in a three-generation human pedigree.
review_notes: Full text available in the cache and read in full. Co-authored by the Apte laboratory, which discovered the protein, so its explicit statement that the tissue function is unknown is an authoritative negative and not an omission.

title: ADAMTSL1 and mandibular prognathism.
review_notes: The genetic association is reported without functional validation, and the proposed mechanism attributes proteolysis to a protein that has no metalloprotease domain, no catalytic activity comment and no EC number. Cited here as an example of the family-name-to-activity conflation, not as evidence for any annotation.

title: Disentangling glial diversity in peripheral nerves at single-nuclei resolution.
review_notes: Full text available and searched. Every mention of Adamtsl1 is as a cluster marker; there is no perturbation of the gene. Recorded so that a later reviewer does not mistake marker expression for a function, and so the companion cell-ablation study (PMID:39880678) is read as a property of the cell type rather than of the gene.

title: Pmp2+ Schwann Cells Maintain the Survival of Large-Caliber Motor Axons.
review_notes: Not annotated, and recorded so that the decision is visible in the review file rather than only in the gene notes. Adamtsl1 is used only as one of three markers of the ablated population and the gene itself is never perturbed, so attributing the axonal phenotype to ADAMTSL1 would be a cell-level to gene-level projection error. Companion to PMID:35115729, which defined the subtype.

title: B3GALTL transfers glucose to O-fucosyl-proteins
review_notes: Reaction record fetched from the Reactome content service; compartments are endoplasmic reticulum membrane and endoplasmic reticulum lumen, and the catalyst is B3GLCT. The underlying claim for ADAMTSL1 is experimentally supported by PMID:17395588, which detected the fucose-glucose disaccharide on TSR2, TSR3 and TSR4 of punctin-1.

title: POFUT2 transfers fucose to TSR domain-containing proteins
review_notes: Reaction record fetched from the Reactome content service. Directly corroborated for ADAMTSL1 by PMID:17395588.

title: Defective B3GALTL does not transfer glucose to O-fucosyl-proteins
review_notes: Confirmed as schemaClass FailedReaction via the Reactome content service. The location it asserts for ADAMTSL1 is not wrong, but it is the third identical copy of one statement and carries no information the two working reactions do not already supply.

title: PTHR13723 annotation census for ADAMTSL1
review_notes: Generated by check_family_propagation.py in the same directory from live QuickGO and UniProt plus the repo's cached PANTHER files. Two consecutive runs reproduce the file byte for byte, and the script's guards were exercised by deliberately corrupting each cached input and confirming it aborts rather than emitting a stale sentence.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADAMTSL1 (human)
review_notes: Used as a lead only. Every claim taken forward was re-verified against the cited PMID or against UniProt. Two divergences were found and are recorded in the gene notes: the record describes the protein as having four thrombospondin repeats, which is true of the short punctin-1 splice form but not of the 1762-residue canonical sequence, and it restates PMID:30714143's aggrecan mechanism in a softened form that the source paper does not use.

title: UniProtKB Q8N6G6 (ATL1_HUMAN) ADAMTS-like protein 1 record
review_notes: Quotes taken from single physical lines of the flat file so that they survive the validator's whitespace normalisation across CC continuation lines.

title: PANTHER PTHR13723 PAINT node annotations
review_notes: Repo-cached PAINT export for the family. Used for the node-level term placement, which is not visible from the per-gene GOA rows.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The InterPro2GO mapping used is IPR013273 (ADAMTS/ADAMTS-like) to GO:0030198. The signature is family-level and covers catalytic and non-catalytic members alike, so the mapping is a family inference; it is nonetheless independently supported for this gene.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT node PTN000347317 in PTHR13723. All 16 protein donors on the single IBA row were resolved and each carries its own experimental annotation to the propagated term or a descendant.

title: ADAMTSL-3/punctin-2, a novel glycoprotein in extracellular matrix related to the ADAMTS family of metalloproteases.
review_notes: The defining cloning and characterisation paper. Note the TSR count differs between methods: 13 here, 10 PROSITE domains and 12 SMART repeats in the current UniProt entry.

title: ADAMTSL3/punctin-2, a gene frequently mutated in colorectal tumors, is widely expressed in normal and malignant epithelial cells, vascular endothelial cells and other cell types, and its mRNA is reduced in colon cancer.
review_notes: Expression survey by validated IHC and in situ hybridisation. Used only for tissue distribution; the colon-cancer mRNA reduction is not used to support any term.

title: Genome-wide association analysis identifies 20 loci that influence adult height.
review_notes: A locus association, not a statement about the protein's activity. Recorded because it is why the gene is studied; deliberately not used to support any annotation.

title: Antiangiogenic characteristics of astrocytes from optic nerve heads with primary open-angle glaucoma.
review_notes: Cited by the affinage deep-research record as showing an antiangiogenic role for ADAMTSL-3. It shows no such thing: ADAMTSL-3 is one of two transcripts raised in glaucoma astrocytes, and the coculture tube-formation assay compares whole astrocyte populations with no ADAMTSL3 gain or loss of function. Correlation presented as function.

title: ADAMTSL3 as a candidate gene for schizophrenia: gene sequencing and ultra-high density association analysis by imputation.
review_notes: Genetic association only, correctly described by its own abstract as a candidate rather than an established gene. Cited for context behind the two mouse neuronal papers; supports no GO term.

title: MADD-4 is a secreted cue required for midline-oriented guidance in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Worm genetics. Cited for the conserved MADD-4/UNC-40-DCC axis and for the explicit statement that MADD-4 has two mammalian orthologues.

title: Microenvironmental regulation by fibrillin-1.
review_notes: The single most informative paper for ADAMTSL3's molecular function, and entirely absent from its GOA. Verified against the PMC full text. One internal inconsistency, recorded above and raised as a question rather than silently resolved: Results say the ADAMTSL-3 polypeptide was human, Methods say the construct came from a RIKEN clone and mouse lung cDNA.

title: Elastic fibres in health and disease.
review_notes: A review, cached abstract-only, and the abstract does not mention ADAMTSL3, so the statement supporting the annotation is in text I cannot read. Reference-scope check: GO_Central used it for 66 TAS annotations over 62 entities, but selectively within this family - ADAMTSL3, ADAMTSL4, ADAMTSL5 and THSD4 in, ADAMTSL1, ADAMTSL2 and PAPLN out - so it is a real traceable statement rather than a blanket projection. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than VERIFIED because the supporting sentence itself has not been read.

title: C. elegans Punctin specifies cholinergic versus GABAergic identity of postsynaptic domains.
review_notes: About the worm protein, not human ADAMTSL3, and MADD-4 is the co-orthologue of ADAMTSL1 and ADAMTSL3 - so it supports conservation of the role, not a claim about the human gene. The affinage record cites this paper together with PMID:14667842 to assert a synaptic-organiser function for human ADAMTSL3; neither paper makes that claim.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Correctly cited by IntAct as the source of five Y2H pairs. Low relevance to ADAMTSL3's function: all five partners are keratin-family or nuclear/cytosolic proteins that a secreted matrix protein does not encounter, and none has been followed up.

title: Genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens identify ADAMTSL3 and PTEN genes as suppressors of HCC proliferation and metastasis, respectively.
review_notes: The ADAMTSL3 result rests on sgRNAs appearing twice in one genome-wide screen in one cell line, with no mechanistic follow-up and no independent replication. Cited so the claim is on record and explicitly not annotated.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Correctly cited by IntAct. Same limitation as PMID:25416956: the partners recovered for ADAMTSL3 are dominated by high-degree keratin-associated preys.

title: ADAMTSL3 knock-out mice develop cardiac dysfunction and dilatation with increased TGFβ signalling after pressure overload.
review_notes: Verified against the PMC full text. Loss-of-function is mouse; the gain-of-function is human protein in human cells, which is what carries the human annotation. Not in ADAMTSL3's GOA.

title: Adamtsl3 mediates DCC signaling to selectively promote GABAergic synapse function.
review_notes: Cached abstract-only. Mouse conditional knockouts, so it supports an ISS rather than an IMP annotation for the human gene.

title: Schizophrenia-associated glycoprotein Adamtsl3 regulates perineuronal net formation, maintenance, and adult cortical plasticity.
review_notes: 2026 paper, cached abstract-only, mouse. Cited as independent corroboration of extracellular matrix organisation rather than as the basis for an MMP-inhibitor annotation: the abstract reports elevated MMP9 levels as well as activity, so whether ADAMTSL3 inhibits the enzyme or limits its abundance is not resolved from the abstract.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADAMTSL3 (human)
review_notes: gates_passed: False. The tripped gate is a suspected symbol collision raised because the narrative opens on C. elegans; on inspection that is a false positive, since the narrative correctly identifies human ADAMTSL3/punctin-2 and is discussing the worm orthologue Ce-Punctin/madd-4. Every claim taken from the record was nonetheless re-verified against the cited PMIDs, and four defects were found. (1) A mis-joined citation: the record attributes a synaptic-organiser function for human ADAMTSL3 to PMID:14667842 plus PMID:24896188, but the first is a 2003 ECM cloning paper with no synaptic content and the second is about the worm protein - each constituent statement is defensible and the join is not. (2) A finding sourced to bioRxiv with an em dash in the PMID column; it has since appeared as PMID:42497245 but supports no GO term. (3) PMID:18474779 is over-read as showing an antiangiogenic role for ADAMTSL-3 when it shows only that the transcript is raised in glaucoma astrocytes. (4) It misses the two most informative papers for this gene, PMID:22242013 and PMID:36539599, so its statement that no mechanism has been characterised is a statement about its own corpus. Used here only for that corpus-level negative, and only after confirming it independently.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The GO_REF itself is correctly applied - ADAMTSL5 genuinely matches IPR013273. The issue is the breadth of the signature, not a citation error. Verified the signature name, protein count and single GO mapping against the InterPro API.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Verified by resolving all 17 WITH/FROM tokens and confirming the seed set matches the cached PTHR13723 PAINT file exactly, plus the node id.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt

A disintegrin-like and metalloprotease domain containing thrombospondin type 1 motif-like 5 (ADAMTSL5) is a novel fibrillin-1-, fibrillin-2-, and heparin-binding member of the ADAMTS superfamily containing a netrin-like module.
review_notes: The single defining paper for this gene and the source of all five IDA rows. Full text available and read in full; all quotes verified verbatim against the cached PMC text. Projection test negative - QuickGO shows it annotates only 2 entities (ADAMTSL5 and its mouse ortholog), so it is gene-specific curation rather than a complex- or family-wide projection. No retraction, erratum or expression of concern.

title: Elastic fibres in health and disease.
review_notes: Not miscited - the review is a legitimate source for elastic fibre composition, and TAS is the honest evidence code for it. But it is weak support for a gene-specific localisation: full text is unavailable, the abstract never names ADAMTSL5, and the same reference underpins 41 other elastic-fiber assignments. Flagged LOW_QUALITY on those grounds rather than MISCITED. Per campaign policy I did not REMOVE on an unverifiable full text; the row is MODIFIED to the specific term the gene's own IDA evidence supports.

title: Melanocyte antigen triggers autoimmunity in human psoriasis.
review_notes: Verified against the cached full text; peptide position confirmed independently against the UniProt sequence. Included for the description because it is the gene's best-known biology, but it generates no GO annotation - being presented as an MHC-bound peptide is a property of a degradation product in an antigen-presentation pathway, not a molecular function of the secreted glycoprotein. The record carries two Comment in entries, which are commentaries rather than corrections; no retraction or erratum.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Correctly cited and a high-quality resource; the problem is not the paper but what a single unreplicated Y2H hit supports. All three ADAMTSL5 partners are extreme interaction hubs (517, 213 and 108 distinct IntAct partners against ADAMTSL5's 12) and all three are intracellular, so none is topologically accessible to a secreted ECM protein. All three accessions resolve to reviewed canonical Swiss-Prot entries at canonical lengths - no ORFeome or TrEMBL substitution.

title: ADAMTSL5 is an epigenetically activated gene underlying tumorigenesis and drug resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Used for the description but deliberately not used to propose a signalling GO term: the receptor tyrosine kinase changes are downstream readouts in a cancer model, and no mechanism connecting a secreted ECM glycoprotein to receptor levels has been established. Notably co-authored by Apte, who also authored the defining matrix paper. No retraction or erratum.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADAMTSL5 (human)
review_notes: gates_passed is False. The tripped gate is specifically the self-evaluation pairwise tie, not a faithfulness failure (faith_pct is 100.0), and no citation is a bioRxiv PMID:bio_* identifier. Marked LOW_QUALITY per campaign policy for a failed gate. Every claim used from it was re-verified against the cited PMID directly and is quoted from the PMID rather than from the provider prose; its GO grounding was rejected outright.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Node content read from the fetched interpro/panther/PTHR43173/PTHR43173-paint.tsv; reach and per-term membership verified independently through QuickGO with withFrom=PANTHER:PTN005148758 (97 hits returned of 97 reported, so no truncation).

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
Mcp1 and Mcp2, two novel proteins involved in mitochondrial lipid homeostasis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum. Abstract only in the cache (no PMC record); the quoted statements are from the abstract and the corresponding GO annotations were read directly from QuickGO rather than inferred from the text.

title: Mitochondrial ADCK3 employs an atypical protein kinase-like fold to enable coenzyme Q biosynthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum. About a paralog, not about ADCK1, and used only to establish what the family's structural features do - never as evidence for ADCK1 itself. The correspondence between ADCK1 A164 and ADCK3 A339 is asserted by this review's own alignment, which aborts if it cannot reproduce the A339 position.

title: Cerebellar Ataxia and Coenzyme Q Deficiency through Loss of Unorthodox Kinase Activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum. About COQ8A/COQ8B, not ADCK1. Used to characterise what the family's characterised members were shown to do, and specifically not extended into a claim that ADCK1 is catalytically inactive - the alignment shows ADCK1's active site is intact and no purified ADCK1 has been assayed.

title: Drosophila ADCK1 is critical for maintaining mitochondrial structures and functions in the muscle.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text read from the cached PMC record, not only the abstract. No retraction, erratum or expression of concern on the PubMed record (CommentsCorrections empty). The one thing to guard against when citing it is scope: the kinase-independence experiments are all over-expression readouts, and the paper's own section heading says so.

title: ADCK1 activates the β-catenin/TCF signaling pathway to promote the growth and migration of colon cancer cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum, and the co-immunoprecipitation itself is reported at endogenous levels. Marked DISPUTED rather than MISCITED because the citation is accurate and the experiment real, but the conclusion is in tension with every localisation measurement made on this protein and has not been reproduced. Raised as a question rather than acted on.

title: A subcellular map of the human kinome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum. ADCK1 itself appears only in the paper's supplementary data, not in the body text of the cached record, which is normal for a kinome-scale survey.
