The reference carries only 6 annotations over 4 entities in QuickGO, so there is no projection concern.

title: UbiB proteins regulate cellular CoQ distribution in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum. Read in full from the cached PMC text. Directly relevant despite being a yeast paper, because its subject Cqd2 is the WITH/FROM donor for every IBA row on ADCK1. The same paper identifies ADCK2, not ADCK1, as the human ortholog of Cqd1, which prevents ADCK2's coenzyme-Q10-deficiency literature from being misapplied here.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum. The QuickGO result for this reference is paginated (100 of 1235 returned), so the distinct entity count is unavailable and is not inferred from the annotation total.

title: ADCK1 is a potential therapeutic target of osteosarcoma.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum. Corroborative for the bioenergetic consequences of losing ADCK1; the cancer-progression claims are cell-line phenotypes and are not used to support any GO term.

title: In vitro construction of the COQ metabolon unveils the molecular determinants of coenzyme Q biosynthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum. About COQ8B, not ADCK1. Added in a correction round: an earlier draft of this review asserted twice that no UbiB protein had been shown to phosphorylate a protein substrate in trans, which this paper refutes. The UniProt keyword recommendation was re-argued on narrower grounds rather than withdrawn, because the residue class is undetermined and the protein is a reconstruction of a different paralog.

title: FOXQ1 Regulates Brain Endothelial Mitochondrial Function by Orchestrating Calcium Signaling and Cristae Morphology.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum. Not cited by any existing GOA row; brought in from the affinage record and read in full from the cached PMC text. Its ADCK1 experiments are mouse, so they support ISS-strength inference for the human gene rather than direct annotation, and they are used here as corroboration rather than as the primary basis of any call.

title: ADCK1: which protein-kinase catalytic motifs does it actually retain?
review_notes: Generated by ubib_motif_scan.py in the same folder; a fresh run reproduces the file byte-for-byte. Motif columns are anchored on PKA's own feature-table entries, the run aborts unless it reproduces curated and published anchor positions, and the catalytic-loop finding is re-read alignment-free because an alignment gap can be an artefact.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADCK1 (human)
review_notes: Deliberately not quoted as supporting_text anywhere in this review. Provider narrative sentences are leads, not evidence, so every claim it suggested was re-verified against the primary PMIDs and those PMIDs are cited instead. Its five citations were each checked for retraction, erratum and expression of concern; all are clean. Its own coarse GO grounding (GO:0140096 catalytic activity, acting on a protein) was not imported, and would have been wrong: no catalytic activity of any kind has been demonstrated for ADCK1.

title: UniProt entry Q86TW2 (ADCK1_HUMAN)
Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT phylogenetic propagation, supporting the single IBA row. All four WITH/FROM tokens were resolved against UniProt and each non-self source was queried in QuickGO for its own evidence for the propagated term. The node PTN000059786 was also queried directly: it propagates 49 annotations over 49 distinct gene products (counts verified equal, result unpaginated) to exactly one term, GO:0005739, and its reach is the ADCK2/Cqd1 orthologue group - yeast YPL109C is under it, yeast Mcp2/Cqd2, the ADCK1 donor, is not. No propagation defect found in either direction.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Maps two UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION tokens to GO. The mitochondrion mapping (SL-0173) rests on the entry line "SUBCELLULAR LOCATION: Mitochondrion {ECO:0000269|PubMed:33988507}", so it is experimentally grounded and redundant with three independent experimental rows. The membrane mapping (SL-0162) rests on "Membrane {ECO:0000255}; Single-pass membrane protein {ECO:0000255}", a sequence prediction only, which makes it the weakest row in this review even though the predicted helix is well placed.

title: Kinome-wide functional genomics screen reveals a novel mechanism of TNFalpha-induced nuclear accumulation of the HIF-1alpha transcription factor in cancer cells.
review_notes: ADCK2 appears only as one of four hits in an siRNA kinome screen, with no follow-up on this gene. Supplied by the affinage record; too indirect to support any annotation.

title: Mitochondrial ADCK3 employs an atypical protein kinase-like fold to enable coenzyme Q biosynthesis.
review_notes: Not an ADCK2 paper, but the structural basis for judging what the aarF/UbiB domain does and does not imply. Supplies the reference feature positions used by this review's own alignment in ADCK2-bioinformatics/.

title: Cerebellar Ataxia and Coenzyme Q Deficiency through Loss of Unorthodox Kinase Activity.
review_notes: The primary source for the family-level negative on canonical protein kinase activity. Note it is PMID:27499294, one digit from PMID:27499296 (the unrelated AP-MS paper that supplies this gene's GO:0005515 row); both were fetched and read separately.

title: Mitochondrial Protein Interaction Mapping Identifies Regulators of Respiratory Chain Function.
review_notes: Correctly cited and a genuine experiment, but a weak basis for a GO annotation on this gene. Expanding the IntAct records shows UniProt's NbExp=4 is one anti-tag co-IP counted four times (three of the four spoke-expanded, MI-score 0.35), and the partner SLC25A5 carries 385 IntAct interaction evidences of its own.

title: ADCK2 Haploinsufficiency Reduces Mitochondrial Lipid Oxidation and Causes Myopathy Associated with CoQ Deficiency.
review_notes: The only paper that characterises ADCK2 itself, and the source of both experimental rows attributed to it. Combines a human nonsense allele with patient fibroblasts, a heterozygous mouse, and yeast complementation. Checked as a possible complex-level projection (the ACTR8 pattern) and it is not one: the reference annotates only two entities, human ADCK2 and mouse Adck2, two terms each. No retraction, erratum or expression of concern.

title: A subcellular map of the human kinome.
review_notes: Systematic imaging survey. Its conclusion for ADCK2 agrees with subcellular fractionation of endogenous protein in PMID:31480808 and with the MitoCoP proteome, so the overexpression caveat does not change the verdict. Note this paper is also the sole ECO:0000269 support for UniProt's SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line.

title: UbiB proteins regulate cellular CoQ distribution in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: The strongest functional characterisation available for ADCK2's own orthologous branch, and the source of the ontology gap proposed below. Its orthology statement was checked independently against PANTHER family membership (ADCK2 and YPL109C share PTHR45890:SF1; ADCK1 and Mcp2/YLR253W share PTHR43173:SF19) rather than taken on the authors' word.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Proteome-scale survey; the QuickGO result for this reference is paginated (1235 annotations), so an entity count is unavailable and the projection test is unreliable for it. That is not a defect here: HTP already signals the scale of the experiment.

title: ADCK2 Knockdown Affects the Migration of Melanoma Cells via MYL6.
review_notes: siRNA and overexpression phenotypes in melanoma lines with a correlative MYL6 link and no mechanism connecting it to ADCK2 biochemistry. Supplied by the affinage record; supports no GO term and none is proposed from it.

title: Calorie Restriction Rescues Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Adck2-Deficient Skeletal Muscle.
review_notes: Mouse dietary intervention on the Adck2 heterozygote. Supports the physiological picture but adds no molecular function and no GO term; cited as context only.

title: Identification of the mitochondrial protein ADCK2 as a therapeutic oncotarget of NSCLC.
review_notes: Knockout and overexpression in NSCLC lines and xenografts. The mitochondrial dysfunction it reports is the expected consequence of losing a mitochondrial protein and does not localise a molecular activity. Supplied by the affinage record; no GO term proposed from it.

title: The UbiB family member Cqd1 forms a novel membrane contact site in mitochondria.
review_notes: Yeast only. Cited to explain why the yeast donor on the IBA row carries a more specific location term than the target does, and as the basis for a suggested experiment - not used to assert an inner-membrane location for human ADCK2.

title: In vitro construction of the COQ metabolon unveils the molecular determinants of coenzyme Q biosynthesis.
review_notes: Correctly cited and methodologically substantial, but its central claim about protein kinase activity stands in direct contradiction to PMID:27499294 and UniProt records it only as "may act as a protein kinase". Included here specifically so that this review does not assert an unqualified family-level negative that the literature no longer supports.

title: Prenatal and progressive coenzyme Q(10) administration to mitigate muscle dysfunction in mitochondrial disease.
review_notes: Mouse developmental and supplementation study. Shows the muscle phenotype has an embryonic origin and responds to CoQ10, reinforcing that the fatty-acid defect is downstream of the CoQ deficit, but it establishes no molecular activity.

title: ADCK2 bioinformatics: retention of UbiB / uPKL motifs relative to the characterised family members
review_notes: This review's own reproducible analysis: Clustal Omega MSA with COQ8A as projection reference and PKA as negative control, reporting residue identity and landing on the target's own annotated sites as separate conditions. A fresh run reproduces both RESULTS.md and results.json byte-for-byte, and the script aborts if the reference feature positions have drifted from UniProt.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADCK2 (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated provider record, gates_passed True. Used only to widen the literature search: it surfaced the three cancer papers and the 2024 mouse study, all of which were then read and judged on their own. No provider sentence is quoted as evidence for any mechanistic claim in this review, per the campaign rule, and no annotation verdict rests on it. Marked LOW_QUALITY rather than MISCITED because its citations are sound and it is the interpretation layer that over-reaches.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Correctly applied - SL-0162 does map to GO:0016020, confirmed against the UniProt locations endpoint. The weakness is in the pipeline's input, not its operation: ADCK5's SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line is itself an ECO:0000305 inference from a predicted TM helix. ADCK1 and ADCK2 feed the same pipeline SL-0173 and gain GO:0005739 - but that is not a like-for-like comparison and must not be read as one: their SL-0173 rests on an experimental localisation (ECO:0000269|PubMed:33988507) from a kinome-wide imaging screen whose library did not contain ADCK5. The asymmetry is therefore untested versus tested, not identical evidence handled differently.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: The citation is correct and the screen is a legitimate large-scale resource; the caution is about weight, not identity. Counting its three IntAct sub-method rows as independent replication would triple-count one experiment - the same artefact previously documented on ACRV1 and ADAMTSL5.

title: Mitochondrial ADCK3 employs an atypical protein kinase-like fold to enable coenzyme Q biosynthesis.
review_notes: The structural basis for this review's central call. Every residue number taken from it (COQ8A K276, A339, D488, D507) was asserted against the downloaded Q8NI60 sequence before use, and all four matched.

title: Cerebellar Ataxia and Coenzyme Q Deficiency through Loss of Unorthodox Kinase Activity.
review_notes: Central to the family argument but deliberately not treated as evidence about ADCK5 itself - the paper says in terms that ADCK5 was not studied. It constrains what the fold does generically; it does not establish what ADCK5 does.

title: Mitochondrial Protein Interaction Mapping Identifies Regulators of Respiratory Chain Function.
review_notes: Not the source of any GOA row for ADCK5; used only as corroborating interactome context. The 17-of-25 figure was measured against each partner's UniProt subcellular location rather than asserted - an earlier draft claimed all 25 were mitochondrial and the measurement refused it.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
aarF domain containing kinase 5 gene promotes invasion and migration of lung cancer cells through ADCK5-SOX9-PTTG1 pathway.
review_notes: Not miscited and not disputed in the literature, but methodologically thin for the weight placed on it elsewhere: the abstract hedges every step ("might regulate", "might be required"), reports no in vitro kinase assay, and full text is unavailable. The affinage record restates it as an established fact that ADCK5 phosphorylates SOX9 at serine 181, which the abstract does not support. No GOA row depends on it, so nothing in the GO record needed changing on this account.

title: A subcellular map of the human kinome.
review_notes: Not the source of any ADCK5 GOA row - QuickGO returns 0 annotations for Q3MIX3 from this reference, consistent with the paper's own statement that ADCK5 was not in the library. Cited to establish why the paralogs' UniProt mitochondrial annotation does not extend to ADCK5, after an earlier draft of this review wrongly asserted the three genes rested on identical evidence.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Checked for the complex-to-subunit projection pattern and cleared: this is a proteome-wide localisation census with no functional or phenotype term attached, so no phenotype can spread across a complex from it.

title: In vitro construction of the COQ metabolon unveils the molecular determinants of coenzyme Q biosynthesis.
review_notes: Cited specifically to avoid the mirror error of inferring absence of an activity from the family's reputation. Weighted with a caveat that is easy to miss: the COQ8 proteins used were ancestral-sequence reconstructions of the tetrapod enzymes rather than the extant human proteins, so this is strong evidence that the fold can phosphorylate a protein and weaker evidence about human COQ8B specifically.

title: ADCK5 (Q3MIX3) - is the "protein serine/threonine kinase" assignment supported?
review_notes: Analyses committed alongside this review and reproducible from the gene folder. Guards were break-tested in both directions via --self-test, and the anchor guard caught a real error during development: PKA Calpha residue numbers taken from the classical Knighton convention are offset by one from UniProt P17612's numbering.

title: Androglobin: a chimeric globin in metazoans that is preferentially expressed in Mammalian testes.
review_notes: The founding androglobin paper and the source UniProt cites for the domain architecture, the heme binding and, via ECO:0000305, the CAUTION about the missing calpain active-site residues. PubMed-verified; no retraction, erratum or Crossref-only corrigendum. Only the abstract is cached, so nothing here rests on unread full text.

title: Androglobin gene expression patterns and FOXJ1-dependent regulation indicate its functional association with ciliogenesis.
review_notes: The primary FOXJ1/ciliogenesis paper. Absent from the affinage record, which cited the later secondary FOXJ1 paper PMID:37158461 instead; found by independent PubMed search. Full text cached. PubMed-verified; no retraction or erratum.

title: Composition and function of the C1b/C1f region in the ciliary central apparatus.
review_notes: Tetrahymena, not human, so it is used as convergent support for the motile-cilium component and deliberately not as evidence for any human-specific claim. Its negative result - minor motility change on Adgb deletion - is recorded as well as its positive one, because it constrains how strongly the ciliary role should be stated. Full text cached. PubMed-verified; no retraction or erratum.

title: Androglobin, a chimeric mammalian globin, is required for male fertility.
review_notes: The principal in vivo study and the donor of most of this gene's transferred annotations. Full text cached and read rather than relied on at abstract level, which mattered: the abstract's "Adgb contributes to Sept10 proteolysis" reads far more strongly than the Results, where the assay is co-overexpression in HEK293 cells with whole-domain deletions and no catalytic-residue mutant. Checked for the complex-projection pattern - the reference annotates only two distinct entities and its phenotype terms stay on Adgb alone - so it is parallel per-protein curation, not a projection. PubMed-verified; no retraction or erratum.

title: ADGB variants cause asthenozoospermia and male infertility.
review_notes: Abstract only in the cache, but this is the reference UniProt cites with ECO:0000269 for the human FUNCTION, the asthenozoospermia disease link, the truncating variant and the calmodulin interaction, so the human-specific claims used here are independently anchored in the curated entry rather than resting on my reading of the abstract alone. PubMed-verified; no retraction or erratum.

title: Congenital heart defects caused by FOXJ1.
review_notes: Cited by the affinage record for FOXJ1 activating the ADGB promoter, but the paper is about FOXJ1-associated congenital heart defects and uses the ADGB promoter as a reporter readout for FOXJ1 function rather than studying ADGB. Retained for completeness and marked LOW relevance; the ADGB-side claim is taken from the primary source PMID:33453283 instead. No claim in this review rests on it. PubMed-verified; no retraction or erratum.

title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies ADGB as a novel causative gene for male infertility in humans: from motility to fertilization.
review_notes: Second independent human genetics cohort. Used only for the human phenotype, deliberately not for any molecular-function claim, since a knockout or loss-of-function phenotype does not by itself establish a molecular activity. PubMed-verified; no retraction or erratum.

title: The circularly permuted globin domain of androglobin exhibits atypical heme stabilization and nitric oxide interaction.
review_notes: The only full biophysical characterisation of the androglobin globin domain, and the single most important reference for this review's molecular-function calls. Notably it was NOT in the affinage record and was found by an independent PubMed sweep; without it the oxygen-binding row had no experimental anchor in either direction and the distal-glutamine finding was invisible. Full text cached and read, including the paragraphs surrounding each quotation. PubMed-verified; no retraction, erratum or Crossref-only corrigendum.

title: Calmodulin interacts with androglobin and regulates the nitrite reductase activity.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. One internal inconsistency worth flagging for anyone quoting it: the Results body text says "Asn30 in helix E is located in the heme distal position", while the Fig. 1B legend and the concluding sentence of that same paragraph both say Gln30. The Swiss-Prot sequence settles it - UniProt position 792, which the register arithmetic maps to their residue 30, is a glutamine. Quoting the body sentence alone would have propagated a typographical error, so only the legend-consistent statements are used here. PubMed-verified; no retraction or erratum.

title: Expression analysis of androglobin and its influence on the transcriptome in cancer.
review_notes: Cited by the affinage record for RFX3 regulation of the ADGB promoter and for transcriptomic effects of ADGB overexpression in A549 lung cancer cells. Both are transcriptional-regulation and overexpression-phenotype observations rather than evidence of androglobin's own function, so no annotation here rests on it. PubMed-verified; no retraction or erratum.

title: [Whole Exome Sequencing Identified Novel Pathogenic Mutations of ADGB in Patients With Oligoasthenozoospermia].
review_notes: Third independent human genetics cohort, 781 men, published in Chinese with an English abstract; the cached record is bilingual and the English text is abstract-level. Treated accordingly - used for the human localisation and interactor claims that the abstract states explicitly, and not leaned on for anything requiring the figures. PubMed-verified against the correct DOI (10.12182/20260160108); the Crossref update lookup returned 404 for that DOI, which is reported rather than counted as a clean pass.

title: Spectroscopic studies on human androglobin regulated by its heme distal Gln12 and IQ motif via interaction with calmodulin.
review_notes: Abstract only. Also absent from the affinage record and found by independent PubMed search. Its value here is that it converts the distal-glutamine claim from an alignment and spectroscopy inference into a mutational one, and it independently supports the IQ motif being required for calmodulin-dependent activation. Its construct numbering (Gln12, C114S/C190S) differs from both UniProt's and Nie et al.'s, so no positional claim is transferred from it without the register being checked. PubMed-verified; the Crossref lookup for its DOI returned 404, which is recorded rather than treated as a clean result.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO, behind four IEA rows via IPR000832, IPR017981 and IPR017983. Fold-derived and therefore weak on its own, but the family-2 7-TM assignment is correct for this protein and the activity it implies is now independently demonstrated.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/PANTHER phylogenetic inference, behind all four IBA rows. The node structure it produced for this family is sound - see the GO:0005886 and GO:0014069 rows and the node-reach table in ADGRA1-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Behind the single GO:0016020 IEA row, sourced from UniProtKB-SubCell:SL-0162. Refined to GO:0005886 in this review.

title: There exist at least 30 human G-protein-coupled receptors with long Ser/Thr-rich N-termini.
review_notes: Correctly identified, and the source of the durable structural fact that GPR123 alone in the family lacks a GPS domain. MISCITED for the GO:0004930 NAS row that cites it: the paper is a search of human genome databases followed by phylogenetic clustering, with no functional experiment on any of the six receptors it reports.

title: The human and mouse repertoire of the adhesion family of G-protein-coupled receptors.
review_notes: A repertoire catalogue with EST expression charts and no perturbation of any receptor. Querying QuickGO by reference shows it carries 78 annotations across 27 distinct entities - GO:0016020 on 27, GO:0007186 on 26, GO:0004930 on 25, all TAS, all assigned by GDB - i.e. it annotates essentially the entire human adhesion-GPCR family with the same three terms. The terms happen to be defensible for ADGRA1 on other evidence, but this reference does not support them for any individual gene.

title: The evolutionary history and tissue mapping of GPR123: specific CNS expression pattern predominantly in thalamic nuclei and regions containing large pyramidal cells.
review_notes: Genuine, correctly identified paper, and its expression mapping and its prediction of a C-terminal PDZ-binding motif are used here as sound. MISCITED refers specifically to the two GOA rows that rest on it: GO:0004930 and GO:0007165 by NAS. The paper is an in-situ hybridisation and real-time PCR survey containing no functional or biochemical assay, and its only functional statement is hedged as what GPR123 'may' do.

title: Large-scale interaction profiling of PDZ domains through proteomic peptide-phage display using human and viral phage peptidomes.
review_notes: Source of the DLG1 GO:0005515 row. ProP-PD against libraries of all human C-terminal peptides screened with nine PDZ domains including DLG1's; the ADGRA1 entity is its C-terminal peptide rather than the full-length protein, which is noted in the row. No corrections found by PubMed CommentsCorrections or by Crossref relation.

title: International Union of Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. XCIV. Adhesion G protein-coupled receptors.
review_notes: IUPHAR nomenclature review; the source of the ADGRA1 name in UniProt (ECO:0000303|PubMed:25713288). Background only.

title: Correlation profiling of brain sub-cellular proteomes reveals co-assembly of synaptic proteins and subcellular distribution.
review_notes: The experimental basis for both IBA cellular-component rows: mouse Adgra1 (Q8C4G9) holds GO:0014069 and GO:0098978 by IDA/EXP from this paper, curated by SynGO, and is the sole protein donor at PANTHER node PTN002914505. Confirmed via QuickGO that the donor's own annotation is to the same terms that propagated, not to more specific ones.

title: ADGRA1 negatively regulates energy expenditure and thermogenesis through both sympathetic nervous system and hypothalamus-pituitary-thyroid axis in male mice.
review_notes: Constitutive mouse knockout; supports a non-core organismal role not currently represented in GOA. Sex-limited (male mice) and attributed to hypothalamic signalling rather than to a cell-autonomous receptor activity, so it is recorded as background rather than proposed as a term for the human gene.

title: Increased Anxiety-like Behaviors in Adgra1(-/-) Male But Not Female Mice are Attributable to Elevated Neuron Dendrite Density, Upregulated PSD95 Expression, and Abnormal Activation of the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β and MEK/ERK Pathways.
review_notes: Behavioural phenotype of the same constitutive knockout, again male-specific. Organism-level and several steps removed from a molecular function; not used to support any term.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: Source of 21 of the 22 GO:0005515 rows. Quantitative holdup assay over 266 human PDZ domains against 448 PDZ-binding motifs, so the partner set is PDZ-specific by construction. ADGRA1 itself is not named in the main text - its data are in Supplementary Data 1 - so no ADGRA1-specific sentence is quoted from it here; the per-partner numbers come from IntAct. Carries an Author Correction (PMID:36477203) which was read and is figure formatting only (missing PCC values, missing axis labels, panel order), affecting no data.

title: Essential Role of Adhesion GPCR, GPR123, for Human Pluripotent Stem Cells and Reprogramming towards Pluripotency.
review_notes: The only functional study performed on the HUMAN protein, by RNAi in human pluripotent stem cells. Reported as a knowledge gap rather than as a proposed term: the readouts are pleiotropic (colony morphology, cell cycle, NANOG, E-cadherin) and no molecular function of the receptor is isolated.

title: The atypical adhesion GPCR ADGRA1 controls hippocampal inhibitory circuit function.
review_notes: bioRxiv preprint of PMID:41961591 (PubMed records UpdateIn: 41961591). Listed for transparency because the affinage report counts it as a separate dated finding, which double-counts one study. Nothing in this review rests on it uniquely; where the two versions differ - the preprint headline claims PV and SST, the published abstract is narrowed to PV - the published version is used.

title: The atypical adhesion GPCR ADGRA1 controls hippocampal inhibitory circuit function.
review_notes: The only functional characterisation of the receptor itself. PubMed-verified; full text cached. Establishes agonist-independent activation of Galpha13/11/15 by the mouse ortholog (Q8C4G9, stated in the Plasmids section) using the 14-sensor TRUPATH BRET2 panel with a dose-response control, and a PV-interneuron conditional knockout phenotype. No retraction, erratum or expression of concern; Crossref shows no update-to, only has-preprint.

title: ADGRA1 (Q86SQ6) — computed evidence for the GO review
review_notes: Reproducible analysis (analyze_adgra1.py) re-reading UniProt, IntAct and QuickGO at run time; no value is hardcoded. Carries a self-test that was break-tested in the direction each check exists to catch.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADGRA1 (human)
review_notes: Provider record, gates_passed: True, no bioRxiv-DOI pseudo-PMIDs in its citation list, and it surfaced the two most load-bearing references here (PMID:28935861, PMID:41961591). Two defects mean nothing in this review rests on it. First, it lists PMID:40766348 (2025 bioRxiv) and PMID:41961591 (2026 Cell Reports) as two separate dated findings; PubMed records UpdateIn: 41961591 on the former, so they are one study double-counted. Second, its headline claims track the preprint abstract (PV and SST interneurons, learning and memory deficits) where the published abstract is narrowed to PV. It also never mentions the PDZ interactome, which is the best-evidenced molecular fact about this protein.

title: UniProtKB entry Q86SQ6 (AGRA1_HUMAN)
review_notes: Primary source for topology (TOPO_DOM 1..19 extracellular, TRANSMEM 20..40, TOPO_DOM 306..560 cytoplasmic), for the sequence whose C-terminus is ETTV, and for the CC INTERACTION block. Corrections to report upstream are listed in suggested_questions.

title: Direct binding of the human homologue of the Drosophila disc large tumor suppressor gene to seven-pass transmembrane proteins, tumor endothelial marker 5 (TEM5), and a novel TEM5-like protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; no retraction, erratum or Crossref correction. Maps the DLG1 interaction to the hDlg PDZ domains and the TEM5 C-terminal PDZ-binding motif, which is the non-screen anchor for the GO:0030165 replacement.

title: The human and mouse repertoire of the adhesion family of G-protein-coupled receptors.
review_notes: PubMed-verified and a sound paper, but miscited as TAS support for ADGRA2's molecular function. Its abstract describes a genome-mining, phylogenetics and EST-expression survey and reports no functional assay on any receptor; the record is abstract-only, so this review makes no claim about its full text. GDB used it to place one generic triple (GO:0016020, GO:0007186, GO:0004930) on 27 human adhesion-GPCR entities, including the pseudogenes ADGRE4P and ADGRF2P - a bulk classification import rather than a traceable author statement about this gene.

title: Proteolytically processed soluble tumor endothelial marker (TEM) 5 mediates endothelial cell survival during angiogenesis by linking integrin alpha(v)beta3 to glycosaminoglycans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; no correction signal. Human endothelial cells, direct biochemistry. Sole source for the integrin and glycosaminoglycan binding proposed as NEW rows; UniProt records both with ECO:0000269. Single-laboratory work (Vallon and Essler), which is noted rather than discounted.

title: Tumor endothelial marker 5 expression in endothelial cells during capillary morphogenesis is induced by the small GTPase Rac and mediates contact inhibition of cell proliferation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; no correction signal. Supports a contact-inhibition role, but the evidence is blocking reagents (soluble ectodomain, inhibitory antibody) rather than a direct assay, so no GO row is proposed from it.

title: GPR124, an orphan G protein-coupled receptor, is required for CNS-specific vascularization and establishment of the blood-brain barrier.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; no correction signal; full text cached. Mouse global and endothelial-specific knockout establishing the CNS angiogenesis and blood-brain barrier roles. The title's own word 'orphan' is part of the evidence that no ligand is known.

title: Thrombin-induced shedding of tumour endothelial marker 5 and exposure of its RGD motif are regulated by cell-surface protein disulfide-isomerase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; no correction signal. Characterises the thrombin and PDI dependent shedding that exposes the RGD motif, supporting both the plasma-membrane location and the integrin-binding proposal.

title: Large-scale interaction profiling of PDZ domains through proteomic peptide-phage display using human and viral phage peptidomes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; no correction signal; full text cached. One of the two large-scale PDZ-motif assays behind ADGRA2's GO:0005515 rows. Independent method (phage display) from the other (holdup), which is why the PDZ-binding call does not rest on a single technology.

title: Wnt proteins synergize to activate beta-catenin signaling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; no correction signal. Independent confirmation, in a different system from PMID:30026314, that ADGRA2 and RECK are the WNT7B co-receptors required for synergistic beta-catenin signalling.

title: Cell adhesion controlled by adhesion G protein-coupled receptor GPR124/ADGRA2 is mediated by a protein complex comprising intersectins and Elmo-Dock.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; no correction signal. The only paper reporting a heterotrimeric G-protein contact for ADGRA2, and it reports Gbeta-gamma binding the receptor C-tail to promote Elmo complex formation - the opposite direction to GO:0004930's requirement of receptor-driven G-alpha nucleotide exchange. Its assays are ectopic-expression based, so IMP-grade. Its own framing, 'the signaling properties of GPR124 remain poorly defined', is quoted in the GO:0004930 review.

title: A molecular mechanism for Wnt ligand-specific signaling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; no correction signal. The mechanistic basis of the core function and of the GO:1990909 and GO:0060070 IDA rows. Caveat recorded in suggested_questions: the Dishevelled-recruitment step is established largely in zebrafish, and PMID:35649360 subsequently reports that mammalian GPR124 engages Frizzled by an ICD-independent route.

title: An integrated model for Gpr124 function in Wnt7a/b signaling among vertebrates.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; no correction signal; full text cached. Not cited by any GOA row, but decisive for how the intracellular-domain mechanism should be read across species, and therefore for whether the PDZ-motif interactions should be treated as core. Same laboratory as PMID:30026314.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Carries an Author Correction, PMID:36477203 (Nat Commun 2022;13:7555), found by reading CommentsCorrections/RefType on the article's own record; it is a correction, not a retraction or expression of concern, and nothing in this review depends on a figure. Source of 18 of the 21 GO:0005515 rows; the quantitative holdup measurement of the ADGRA2 PDZ-binding motif against the human PDZ domain repertoire.

title: Complex G-protein signaling of the adhesion GPCR, ADGRA3.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached; no correction signal. Not cited by any ADGRA2 GOA row, but it is the single most load-bearing reference for this review's central molecular-function call, in both directions. It refutes the clade-level negative this review originally asserted - ADGRA3 does couple, to Gi and Gs, stachel-dependently - and in the same paper states the ADGRA2-specific negative directly, which is far stronger support than the absence of hits from my own query. Reached this review only because the sibling ADGRA3 branch merged and brought the cached publication with it.

title: The atypical adhesion GPCR ADGRA1 controls hippocampal inhibitory circuit function.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Cited only to establish that the ADGRA clade can couple to heterotrimeric G proteins, which is what makes MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED rather than REMOVE the right action on ADGRA2's InterPro rows. Note ADGRA1 is architecturally the outlier of the family - it lacks both the N-terminal adhesion domains and the GAIN domain - so it corroborates that the shared 7TM can couple, not that ADGRA2's specific architecture does.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADGRA2 (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated deep research (gates_passed: True, faith_pct 85.7, 10 citations, all numeric PMIDs - no bioRxiv DOIs in PMID-shaped fields). Used as a lead list only: it surfaced PMID:28289266, PMID:28600358 and PMID:19853600, which were then read and cited directly, plus PMID:24730523, PMID:27979830 and PMID:27979884, which were read and cached but are NOT cited in this review because no annotation rests on them. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than VERIFIED because no claim in this review rests on an affinage sentence; every mechanistic statement is anchored to a PMID quote or to the UniProt record. Its one substantive omission is that it does not flag the Author Correction on PMID:36115835, and it does not mention PMID:35649360, which qualifies the species scope of the mechanism it describes.

title: Direct binding of the human homologue of the Drosophila disc large tumor suppressor gene to seven-pass transmembrane proteins, tumor endothelial marker 5 (TEM5), and a novel TEM5-like protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract only in cache. The 'TEM5-like protein' the abstract names as a second hDlg partner is ADGRA3/GPR125 (TEM5 is the paralogue ADGRA2/GPR124); UniProt cites this paper with ECO:0000269 for the ADGRA3 SUBUNIT line, and PMID:36089063 cites it as the prior demonstration that the bacterially expressed GPR125 C-terminal tail binds Dlg1 directly. Care is needed with this reference: its endothelial-colocalisation and tumour-angiogenesis claims are about TEM5/ADGRA2, not about ADGRA3, and are not used here.

title: The human and mouse repertoire of the adhesion family of G-protein-coupled receptors.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract only in cache. A bioinformatic survey of the human and mouse adhesion GPCR repertoire, cited by three TAS rows in GOA. Correctly identified and correctly cited, but it contains no experiment on GPR125, so it is background rather than evidence - which is why the TAS provenance is flagged for upgrade even though the terms themselves are accepted.

title: Generation of functional multipotent adult stem cells from GPR125+ germline progenitors.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract only in cache. The source of the mouse Adgra3 GO:0009897 IDA that seeds the ADGRA3-orthologue PAINT node. I ran the reference-projection test on it: QuickGO returns 5 annotations over 5 entities (Adgra3, Cd34, Pou5f1, Vim, Acta2) and each gets a different compartment with no phenotype term spreading across the set, so it is a marker-panel paper and the Adgra3 IDA is its own, not a projection.

title: Gpr125 modulates Dishevelled distribution and planar cell polarity signaling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract only in cache. The zebrafish Wnt/PCP work. Highly relevant to the family and the origin of UniProt's by-similarity FUNCTION line for human ADGRA3, but it is zebrafish gastrulation and is treated here as an open question for the human orthologue rather than as human evidence.

title: Large-scale interaction profiling of PDZ domains through proteomic peptide-phage display using human and viral phage peptidomes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract only in cache. Proteomic peptide-phage display against nine PDZ domains including DLG1's; source of the DLG1 GO:0005515 row. Supports PDZ-motif binding, not a cellular interaction. No retraction or erratum.

title: Elevated G-Protein Receptor 125 (GPR125) Expression Predicts Good Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer and Inhibits Wnt/β-Catenin Signaling Pathway.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Reports that GPR125 overexpression inhibits beta-catenin transcriptional activity in HCT116 cells. Relevant only as a second, independent negative on canonical Wnt engagement; a single-cell-line overexpression study, so not load-bearing, but it is cited as provenance on the Wnt/PCP knowledge gap because it is an independent line pointing the same way as the TOPFlash negative.

title: Arrestin-independent constitutive endocytosis of GPR125/ADGRA3.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Surface expression of N-terminally tagged human GPR125 on non-permeabilised HEK293 cells and constitutive beta-arrestin-independent, clathrin-dependent internalisation. No retraction or erratum.

title: GPR125 positively regulates osteoclastogenesis potentially through AKT-NF-κB and MAPK signaling pathways.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Osteoclastogenesis role by lentiviral knockdown and overexpression. Correctly cited but downstream and pathway-level (MAPK, AKT-NF-kB); no GO action taken from it, and it is cited as provenance on the phenotype-mechanism knowledge gap as a further cellular role with no link to any measured ADGRA3 activity.

title: GPR125 (ADGRA3) is an autocleavable adhesion GPCR that traffics with Dlg1 to the basolateral membrane and regulates epithelial apicobasal polarity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. The single most informative primary paper on human ADGRA3: cis-autoproteolysis at the atypical GPS Ser736-Leu737-Ser738, ETTV-dependent DLG1 binding, basolateral targeting, and spindle-orientation/multilumen phenotypes. Checked for retraction, erratum and expression of concern via CommentsCorrections - none. Note the loss-of-function work is on endogenous canine Gpr125 in MDCK cells, which is why the polarity annotation proposed from it is ISS rather than IMP.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Source of 18 of the 19 GO:0005515 rows. Carries an unflagged Author Correction, PMID:36477203 / doi 10.1038/s41467-022-35177-6, which affinage does not mention; I read it - it restores missing PCC values and axis labels in Figures 2, 4 and 5 and does not touch the affinity data or the ADGRA3 measurements, so nothing in this review rests on corrected material. Crossref update-to/updated-by fields confirm the correction is the only relation besides the bioRxiv preprint. Relevance is MEDIUM rather than HIGH: the assay is a quantitative peptide/domain affinity screen, so it measures a property of the ETTV motif rather than establishing cellular interactions.

title: Loss of Adgra3 causes obstructive azoospermia with high penetrance in male mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Adgra3-null male mice, obstructive azoospermia. Mouse phenotype used only in knowledge_gaps, since no mechanism connects it to a measured ADGRA3 activity.

title: High incidence of imperforate vagina in ADGRA3-deficient mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Adgra3-null female mice, imperforate vagina. Note its opening statement that ADGRA3 'is involved in WNT signaling and planar cell polarity' is background citing the zebrafish work, not a finding of this paper - used here as a statement of the prevailing assumption, not as evidence.

title: Constitutively active receptor ADGRA3 signaling induces adipose thermogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Constitutive Gs-PKA-CREB signalling driving beige adipocyte biogenesis; corroborates the Gs arm. Mouse in vivo plus human adipocyte work. The hesperetin agonist claim is a single pharmacological report and is treated as a candidate, not an established ligand.

title: Complex G-protein signaling of the adhesion GPCR, ADGRA3.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Establishes stachel-dependent Gs and Gi coupling for human ADGRA3, with DVL1-3-null and FZD1-10-null controls showing the signalling is neither Dishevelled-dependent nor beta-catenin-coupled. No retraction or erratum.

title: Organization of the gene for gelatin-binding protein (GBP28).
review_notes: A gene-structure paper (FISH mapping to 3q27, three exons, no TATA box) cited as TAS for GO:0006091 generation of precursor metabolites and energy. It performs no metabolic experiment. This is its only annotation in all of GOA.

title: Adipocyte-derived plasma protein adiponectin acts as a platelet-derived growth factor-BB-binding protein and regulates growth factor-induced common postreceptor signal in vascular smooth muscle cell.
review_notes: The strongest molecular-function evidence in this gene's record: direct, selective radioligand binding of human adiponectin to PDGF-BB in human cells, with the receptor-proximal consequence measured. Verified against the cached abstract.

title: The role of the novel adipocyte-derived hormone adiponectin in human disease.
review_notes: A review article, correctly cited as NAS. Carries exactly two annotations in GOA, both on this gene.

title: Cloning of adiponectin receptors that mediate antidiabetic metabolic effects.
review_notes: The expression cloning of AdipoR1 and AdipoR2 and the primary basis for adiponectin's receptor-ligand function. Also carries an unflagged erratum with a NULL PubMed id (Nature 2004;431:1123, doi:10.1038/nature03091), discoverable only through CommentsCorrections plus Crossref.

title: T-cadherin is a receptor for hexameric and high-molecular-weight forms of Acrp30/adiponectin.
review_notes: Identifies T-cadherin as the receptor for hexameric and HMW adiponectin. Absent from GOA entirely: neither ADIPOQ nor CDH13 carries any annotation naming the other.

title: APPL1 binds to adiponectin receptors and mediates adiponectin signalling and function.
review_notes: Correctly identified; the reciprocal GO:0005515 row exists on ADIPOR1. Two caveats. The paper's subject is APPL1, and what it shows about adiponectin is that ligand stimulates the APPL1-AdipoR1 association rather than measuring adiponectin-AdipoR1 binding directly. Separately, PubMed records an unflagged erratum (Nat Cell Biol 2006;8(6):642, doi:10.1038/ncb1422) with a NULL PubMed id, found only by reading CommentsCorrections/RefType and resolving the DOI at Crossref; its content could not be retrieved here, so nothing beyond the quoted abstract sentence rests on this reference.

title: Effects of adiponectin on the renal sympathetic nerve activity and blood pressure in rats.
review_notes: Supports GO:0045776 negative regulation of blood pressure directly. It is flagged because it also carries GO:0010906 regulation of glucose metabolic process, which the abstract mentions only as background, and GO:0050805 negative regulation of synaptic transmission, whereas the measurement is renal sympathetic nerve activity. Full text was not available, so the curator's reading of the glucose row is not overruled.

title: The peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonist rosiglitazone ameliorates murine lupus by induction of adiponectin.
review_notes: The source of mouse Adipoq's GO:0071466 IDA, which reaches human ADIPOQ by ISS and IEA. The paper shows that rosiglitazone INDUCES adiponectin; adiponectin is the output of the xenobiotic response, not a participant in it.

title: Inhibitory effects of adiponectin on platelet-derived growth factor-induced mesangial cell migration.
review_notes: Source of the mouse rows behind human GO:0030336, GO:2000584 and GO:2000590. Correctly cited; note the assay is cultured mesangial cells while GO:2000590 names metanephric mesenchymal cells, because GO has no mesangial cell migration term.

title: Sialic acid modification of adiponectin is not required for multimerization or secretion but determines half-life in circulation.
review_notes: The identifier resolves to the intended paper and the paper is sound. It is recorded as MISCITED because the annotation it supports, GO:0033691 sialic acid binding, inverts the paper's finding: the study characterises adiponectin as the CARRIER of sialylated O-linked glycans, not as a sialic-acid-binding protein. UniProt encodes the same reference correctly, as CARBOHYD features at Thr-21/Thr-22 and a PTM comment.

title: Adiponectin reduces thermogenesis by inhibiting brown adipose tissue activation in mice.
review_notes: Correctly cited for GO:0120163 (adiponectin suppresses thermogenesis) and incorrectly cited for the opposite term GO:0120162. The scientific claim is also genuinely disputed: PMID:26166748 reports the opposite direction in the same knockout model. Both papers are attached to both terms in GOA and in MGI.

title: Adiponectin Enhances Cold-Induced Browning of Subcutaneous Adipose Tissue via Promoting M2 Macrophage Proliferation.
review_notes: Mirror image of PMID:24531262: correctly cited for GO:0120162 (adiponectin promotes cold-induced browning) and incorrectly cited for GO:0120163. Also the second independent report of the adiponectin-T-cadherin interaction, which GO records nowhere.

title: Characterization of the Extracellular Matrix of Normal and Diseased Tissues Using Proteomics.
review_notes: A legitimate ECM proteomics survey, correctly supporting the GO:0031012 HDA detection row. Flagged because the same reference also drives a bulk RCA block assigning GO:0005201 extracellular matrix structural constituent to 41 entities, a structural claim the proteomics cannot support for a circulating hormone.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI, the human binary reference interactome. Correctly cited as the source of 56 of this gene's GO:0005515 rows; it carries 85343 annotations across GOA. Its relevance to adiponectin's biology is low because the assay is nuclear two-hybrid and the protein is secreted.

title: MatrisomeDB 2.0: 2023 updates to the ECM-protein knowledge database.
review_notes: MatrisomeDB 2.0 is a database-update paper, not a study of adiponectin. In GOA it supplies GO:0140149 to 272 distinct entities, i.e. it is a bulk import rather than an author statement about this gene.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Title verified against the cached record. Correctly cited for a high-throughput detection, but it is a bulk import annotating 1016 gene products with a single term and it says nothing specific about ADIRF; cached abstract-only. No retraction, erratum or correction found on the PubMed record.

title: APM2 is a novel mediator of cisplatin resistance in a variety of cancer cell types regardless of p53 or MMR status.
review_notes: Title verified. One of the two references the affinage record returned, and it checks out. Cited here to record why no GO annotation follows from it: the cisplatin phenotype is downstream physiology in tumour cell lines, not a function of the protein, and it is explicitly not proposed as a new term. Cached abstract-only. No retraction or erratum.

title: A Novel pro-adipogenesis factor abundant in adipose tissues and over-expressed in obesity acts upstream of PPARγ and C/EBPα.
review_notes: Title verified against the cached record; note the source itself contains the typo 'C10orf16' in the abstract, reproduced verbatim above. Cached abstract-only, so claims here are bounded to what the abstract states; UniProt's 'stimulates transcription initiation' wording comes from the full text and is deferred to rather than re-derived. No retraction or erratum. This paper is absent from the affinage record despite being the reference behind three GOA rows.

title: Overexpression of C10orf116 promotes proliferation, inhibits apoptosis and enhances glucose transport in 3T3-L1 adipocytes.
review_notes: Title verified. The second of the two affinage citations; it checks out. InterPro cites this paper in its IPR034450 description, which is part of why the InterPro2GO rows for this gene are circular. Cached abstract-only; cited for scope rather than as support for any annotation. No retraction or erratum.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Title verified; full text available and read. Correctly cited for the HDA detection. ADIRF is not mentioned anywhere in the paper's text, so the annotation rests on a supplementary list; the caveats quoted are the authors' own. No retraction or erratum.

title: Characterization of microRNA expression profiles in 3T3-L1 adipocytes overexpressing C10orf116.
review_notes: Title verified. Cached abstract-only. Cited only to support the scope claim that all ADIRF functional work is 3T3-L1 over-expression. No retraction or erratum.

title: Lipoaspirate fluid proteome: A preliminary investigation by LC-MS top-down/bottom-up integrated platform of a high potential biofluid in regenerative medicine.
review_notes: Title verified against the cached record; cached abstract-only, and the quoted sentence is from the abstract. Corroborating only: a preliminary two-sample study, cited for the fact of detection in an extracellular adipose fluid and for nothing more. No retraction or erratum.

title: Tripartite factors leading to molecular divergence between human and murine smooth muscle.
review_notes: Title verified; full text available and read. This is the single most consequential reference for interpreting ADIRF's annotations and it is absent from GOA, from UniProt's reference list and from the affinage record. One claim in it is NOT relied on, and is adjudicated on sequence rather than on a symbol count: it also states ADIRF is absent from zebrafish and lamprey. An earlier version of this review declined that on the strength of an NCBI symbol/alias count, which is orthology asserted by an annotation pipeline rather than measured, and is exactly the name-based inference the rest of this analysis refuses. Aligning the actual RefSeq proteins instead: NP_001373520.1 (Danio rerio) and XP_085644419.1 (Trachurus japonicus) are both 81 aa and align over 71 of the 76 human residues at 38.2% identity, passing the same coverage criterion used throughout - with a chicken positive control, the 938-aa Cyprinus carpio family member as a negative control that fails as expected, and only 1 of 30 composition-matched shuffles passing. So an ADIRF-like protein is annotated in zebrafish and the paper's zebrafish claim is inconsistent with current RefSeq annotation - though this review examined sequence, not synteny, so it does not adjudicate the genomic-deletion argument the paper actually makes. The mouse/rat/hamster claim, which is what this review does rely on, is independently confirmed. No retraction or erratum.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Title verified; full text available. Correctly cited as the source of the GO:0005515 IPI row. Neither ADIRF nor IL18 appears in the paper's text, so the pair comes from the supplementary interaction list. The reference-projection test is uninformative for this reference - 85,343 annotations over 854 pages - and that is stated rather than a first-page count being substituted. No retraction or erratum.

title: Adipose most abundant 2 protein is a predictive marker for cisplatin sensitivity in cancers.
review_notes: Title verified; full text available and read. Cited only for the measured serum concentration, which is used to corroborate extracellular presence and hence to keep rather than downgrade the GO:0070062 rows. The paper's ERCC6L-upregulation claim rests on bioinformatic plus histological analysis and is deliberately NOT used to support any annotation. No retraction or erratum. Absent from the affinage record.

title: Circadian lncRNA ADIRF-AS1 binds PBAF and regulates renal clear cell tumorigenesis.
review_notes: Title verified; full text available. Deliberately included as a NEGATIVE control on the review's scope rather than as evidence: it documents that the locus/transcript confusion hazard was checked and that the GO record is free of it. Nothing in this review's verdicts depends on it. Separately noted: another ADIRF-AS1 paper, PMID:35937391, is a Retracted Publication, and nothing here rests on it either.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADIRF (human)
review_notes: Recorded so the provider's performance on this gene is measurable, and deliberately NOT cited as supporting_text for any annotation. Precision is fine: gates_passed is True, both citations (PMID:19444912, PMID:23467766) are real numeric PubMed ids rather than bioRxiv DOIs in a PMID-shaped field, both resolve to papers genuinely about this gene under its former names, and neither is retracted. Recall for annotation purposes is close to zero: it returned none of the four PMIDs GOA cites - including PMID:23239344, the reference behind three of the eleven rows and the only nuclear characterisation of the protein - and it missed PMID:31945134 (the 43-kb Muroid deletion and the arterial expression data), which is the single most consequential fact about this gene, and PMID:33737617 (serum at microgram-per-millilitre). Marked LOW_QUALITY for one substantive inaccuracy rather than for its citations: the narrative asserts that no binding partner has been characterised, while a curated IL18 interaction sits in the GO record it did not consult. Its empty molecular_activity, localization, partners and complexes fields are, by contrast, correct for this gene.

title: Use of the ND evidence code for Gene Ontology (GO) terms
review_notes: Read directly for this review. It states that a root-term ND annotation records that curators found no data supporting a more specific term as of the annotation date, which is the basis for retiring the GO:0005575 row now that extracellular region annotations exist.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: The route for five of the thirteen GOA rows. Its premise holds unusually well here: human and mouse ADISSP are both 174 aa and 90.2% identical with no indels.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Requires at least 40% peptide identity between orthologs; the human/mouse pair is at 90.2%, so the threshold is met by a wide margin.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Verified against the GO reference metadata rather than assumed. This is the roll-up reference that integrates identical annotations from several electronic pipelines, including UniRule, ARBA, InterPro2GO, TreeGrafter2GO, KeyWord2GO, SubCellular2GO and Ensembl Compara. Worth stating explicitly because it is easy to read it as the ARBA reference, which is GO_REF:0000117. On this gene the two constituent pipelines named in the WITH/FROM both trace back to the same mouse entry, so the row's apparent multi-method agreement is not independent corroboration.

title: Exploring proteomes and analyzing protein processing by mass spectrometric identification of sorted N-terminal peptides.
review_notes: The direct protein sequencing of ADISSP residues 2-11 from platelets that underlies UniProt's PE 1: Evidence at protein level. Relevant only to the fact that the human protein is detected - which is why this review says there is no human functional data rather than no human data at all - and abstract-only in the cache, so nothing is quoted from it. Listed rather than left as an unreferenced cached file.

title: N-terminal acetylome analyses and functional insights of the N-terminal acetyltransferase NatB.
review_notes: The large-scale proteomics source behind UniProt's ECO:0007744 evidence for initiator-methionine removal and N-acetylalanine at residue 2 of ADISSP - the observation that shows the mature protein begins at residue 2 and therefore has no cleaved signal peptide. Cited here through the UniProt feature lines rather than by quoting the paper, since ADISSP appears in its supplementary peptide tables rather than its text. Listed explicitly because the cached file would otherwise sit in publications/ with nothing in the review pointing at it.

title: C20orf27 Promotes Cell Growth and Proliferation of Colorectal Cancer via the TGFβR-TAK1-NFĸB Pathway.
review_notes: Cached full text read; retraction and erratum checks clean by both routes. The identifier and title are correct and the paper genuinely supports two of its three annotations. The third, GO:1901224 positive regulation of non-canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction, is a term-selection error rather than a citation error: the paper measures only canonical markers. Also worth flagging for GOA - all three of this gene's experimental rows are assigned by FlyBase from a purely human colorectal cancer study with no Drosophila content. A reference-projection query confirms the reference annotates this one entity only, so it is a targeted curation rather than a bulk import, but the assigning database is unexpected.

title: A brown fat-enriched adipokine Adissp controls adipose thermogenesis and glucose homeostasis.
review_notes: Cached full text read in full, not just the abstract. Confirmed clean of retraction, erratum and expression of concern by two independent routes - the PubMed record's own PublicationType and CommentsCorrections fields, and Crossref relation/update-to on DOI 10.1038/s41467-022-35335-w - with a known-retracted PMID as a positive control to show the detector fires. This is the sole experimental source behind every IEA and ISS row on this gene. One reading caution recorded because it is easy to get wrong: the paper infuses GFP, mouse Adissp and human ADISSP adenoviruses, but only the circulating-protein detection is credited to the human construct; the browning and glucose-tolerance panels in the same figure are labelled for the mouse protein, so the human protein should not be said to have produced the metabolic phenotype.

title: C20orf27 promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression via NT5E.
review_notes: Surfaced by the deep-research provider and fetched, but not used to support any annotation and not read beyond the abstract, so it is recorded as unverified rather than assessed. Listed because it is part of the gene's cancer literature and a future reviewer should know it was seen and set aside.

title: C20orf27 regulates colorectal cancer growth and metastasis based on different lipid levels.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache (full_text_available is false). Not used to support any annotation, and nothing in this review rests on it. Listed for completeness of the gene's cancer literature.

title: Adissp activates insulin-independent glucose disposal and energy expenditure in white fat to treat diabetes and cardiometabolic disease.
review_notes: Cached full text read; retraction and erratum checks clean by both routes. Not cited by any GOA row - a QuickGO query by reference returns zero annotations for this PMID - so the whole insulin-independent Akt/GLUT4 arm is currently uncurated in GO. Relevant here mainly because it supplies the human-specific secretion statement and because it answers the question of what molecule was assayed: full-length recombinant protein with an untagged control, not a peptide or a fragment.

title: ADISSP bioinformatics results (human/mouse identity; IntAct PP1 record and its hub null)
review_notes: Committed analysis in this gene's folder, added after review feedback that the identity figure and the IntAct evidence were asserted in prose with no auditable artifact behind them. Every number is computed at run time from UniProt and IntAct; nothing is hardcoded. A fresh run was confirmed to reproduce the committed RESULTS.md and results.json byte-for-byte. Guards break-tested in three directions, each failing with the right message and a non-zero exit status: a merged accession (O15507, which returns HTTP 200 for GFRA1/P56159) is rejected by a primaryAccession assertion; removing the comparator's length guard trips the negative control; and reducing the IntAct page size to 5 is detected as truncation rather than reported as 5 records.

title: UniProtKB entry Q9GZN8 (ADSSP_HUMAN), cached in the gene folder
review_notes: Used for the feature table and the subcellular-location provenance: no SIGNAL feature, mature CHAIN 2..174, N-acetylalanine at residue 2 from mass spectrometry, and a SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line that is ECO:0000250 by similarity to the mouse entry rather than experimental. Each quoted line was checked to lie on a single physical line of the file, because the repository's reference validator skips file: quotes entirely and a quote spanning a CC continuation would pass silently.

title: Complete sequence of a novel protein containing a femtomolar-activity-dependent neuroprotective peptide.
review_notes: The 1999 ADNP cloning paper. Cited here as the source of mouse Adnp's own GO:0043524 IDA; its neuroprotection data are subfemtomolar NAPVSIPQ peptide in mixed cultures, which is why that mouse annotation does not rescue the human row.

title: Vasoactive intestinal peptide and related molecules induce nitrite accumulation in the extracellular milieu of rat cerebral cortical cultures.
review_notes: Correctly identified and a sound paper, but it is titled and framed for vasoactive intestinal peptide and doses cultures with exogenous VIP/SNV/NAP. Using it to annotate the ADNP gene product with cGMP metabolic process and regulation of nitric oxide metabolic process attributes a peptide's pharmacology to the parent protein.

title: NAP accelerates the performance of normal rats in the water maze.
review_notes: A behavioural study of inhaled NAP peptide in normal rats. It supports nothing about the ADNP protein's participation in memory.

title: The neuroprotective peptide NAP inhibits the aggregation of the beta-amyloid peptide.
review_notes: Measures the NAP peptide against beta-amyloid aggregation. Its abstract reports biotin-NAP binding Abeta and mentions no copper, yet it is the sole support for rat Adnp copper ion binding and peptide binding, both of which reach human by Compara.

title: NAP mechanisms of neuroprotection.
review_notes: A NAP-centred article whose new datum is p53 as an intracellular target of the peptide. It is the sole support for a negative-regulation-of-gene-expression annotation on the ADNP protein.

title: Activity-dependent neurotrophic factor-9 and NAP promote neurite outgrowth in rat hippocampal and cortical cultures.
review_notes: Femtomolar ADNF-9 and NAP peptides in rat cultures. ADNF-9 is not an ADNP fragment at all - it is the active site of activity-dependent neurotrophic factor.

title: Synergistic effects of the peptide fragment D-NAPVSIPQ on ethanol inhibition of synaptic plasticity and NMDA receptors in rat hippocampus.
review_notes: Uses D-NAPVSIPQ, the all-D-amino-acid enantiomer, which no gene can encode, and reports that it had no effect on LTP on its own. It is the sole support for rat Adnp negative regulation of synaptic transmission.

title: Neuropeptide receptor transcripts are expressed in the rat clitoris and oscillate during the estrus cycle in the rat vagina.
review_notes: An RT-PCR survey of neuropeptide receptor transcripts in rat vagina and clitoris. ADNP mRNA oscillating with the rat estrus cycle is the sole support for an estrous cycle annotation that reaches human, a species without an estrous cycle.

title: Subcellular localization and secretion of activity-dependent neuroprotective protein in astrocytes.
review_notes: A genuine measurement of the rat ADNP protein by fractionation and immunodetection. The extracellular claim is a ~1.4-fold change detected with an antibody raised against the NAP epitope, which is why it supports a non-core, over-annotated verdict rather than removal.

title: Peptide neuroprotection through specific interaction with brain tubulin.
review_notes: A well-executed identification of betaIII-tubulin as the NAP peptide's binding partner. It is cited for beta-tubulin binding by the full-length ADNP protein, which it does not measure; RGD's reciprocal annotations from the same paper put peptide binding on the tubulins with Adnp as the WITH/FROM partner.

title: Neuroprotective effect of the peptides ADNF-9 and NAP on hypoxic-ischemic brain injury in neonatal rats.
review_notes: Intraperitoneal ADNF-9 and NAP in neonatal rats after hypoxia-ischaemia. Sole support for two human IEA rows about nitric oxide homeostasis and neuronal apoptosis.

title: Activity-dependent neuroprotective protein (ADNP) differentially interacts with chromatin to regulate genes essential for embryogenesis.
review_notes: The mouse ADNP ChIP and knockout expression-profiling study underlying the ISS transfers for GO:0000977, GO:0000981 and GO:0006357. Note MGI read the same paper as GO:0003682 chromatin binding while ARUK-UCL read it as sequence-specific DNA binding and DbTF activity; the later ChAHP work vindicates the stronger reading.

title: Expression of activity-dependent neuroprotective protein in the brain of adult rats.
review_notes: Immunohistological mapping of ADNP protein in adult rat brain; supports the axon localisation row as a real protein measurement.

title: Ethanol inhibits neuronal differentiation by disrupting activity-dependent neuroprotective protein signaling.
review_notes: Cited for positive regulation of axon extension. The agent is the NAP peptide; the only gene silenced is Fyn kinase, not ADNP.

title: Nitric oxide regulates activity-dependent neuroprotective protein (ADNP) in the dentate gyrus of the rodent model of kainic acid-induced seizure.
review_notes: ADNP immunodetection in rat dentate gyrus under NOS inhibition and kainate seizure. Supports dendrite and neuronal cell body. I could not identify in the abstract what supports the accompanying response-to-carbohydrate IEP; full text is not cached.

title: Human POGZ modulates dissociation of HP1alpha from mitotic chromosome arms through Aurora B activation.
review_notes: An HP1alpha proteomics study focused on POGZ; ADNP is a co-purifying partner. Also the source of the general statement that proteins engage HP1 through a PxVxL motif.

title: Analysis of the human HP1 interactome reveals novel binding partners.
review_notes: Tandem affinity purification of all three HP1 isotypes; one of seven independent studies recovering ADNP with HP1.

title: A SWI/SNF-related autism syndrome caused by de novo mutations in ADNP.
review_notes: Establishes de novo ADNP mutations as the cause of Helsmoortel-Van der Aa syndrome. Disease relevance, not a molecular function.

title: Human-chromatin-related protein interactions identify a demethylase complex required for chromosome segregation.
review_notes: Large-scale human chromatin protein interaction map.

title: The NAP motif of activity-dependent neuroprotective protein (ADNP) regulates dendritic spines through microtubule end binding proteins.
review_notes: Identifies the SxIP motif in ADNP's NAP region that binds the microtubule end-binding proteins EB1 and EB3 - the documented route by which the full-length protein reaches microtubules, as distinct from the peptide's direct tubulin binding.

title: A High-Density Map for Navigating the Human Polycomb Complexome.
review_notes: AP-MS map of the human Polycomb complexome.

title: ADNP Is a Therapeutically Inducible Repressor of WNT Signaling in Colorectal Cancer.
review_notes: Reports ADNP as a repressor of WNT signalling in colorectal cancer. Correctly cited, but its direction is opposite to PMID:32533114; recorded as an unresolved disagreement rather than adjudicated.

title: Activity-dependent neuroprotective protein recruits HP1 and CHD4 to control lineage-specifying genes.
review_notes: The defining ChAHP paper and the source of ADNP's only human IDA. Absent from the affinage deep-research record's 28 citations despite that record passing its citation gate - a recall miss, not a precision failure.

title: The ChAHP Complex Counteracts Chromatin Looping at CTCF Sites that Emerged from SINE Expansions in Mouse.
review_notes: Shows ChAHP competing with CTCF for a shared motif set at SINE B2 elements - independent confirmation that ADNP's DNA binding is sequence-specific.

title: ADNP promotes neural differentiation by modulating Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
review_notes: The source of mouse Adnp's beta-catenin IPI and the Wnt/neural-differentiation IMPs that reach human by Compara. Well executed and cached in full text, but a single laboratory, and its direction is contested by PMID:27903678.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0. High-throughput, but corroborated by six other studies and by the purified ChAHP complex.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous tagging - the HP1 interaction is recovered at native expression levels, which removes the overexpression caveat.

title: The cytoplasmic localization of ADNP through 14-3-3 promotes sex-dependent neuronal morphogenesis, cortical connectivity, and calcium signaling.
review_notes: Reports that Adnp knockdown in cortical pyramidal neurons increases basal dendrite number and axon length - the opposite sign to the NAP-peptide neurite annotations.

title: Protein interaction studies in human induced neurons indicate convergent biology underlying autism spectrum disorders.
review_notes: IP-MS in human induced neurons, i.e. human cells of the relevant type.

title: ChAHP2 and ChAHP control diverse retrotransposons by complementary activities.
review_notes: Defines the paralogous ChAHP2 complex and states that ADNP's C-terminal PxVxL HP1 interaction motif is conserved between ADNP and ADNP2. Cached in full text.

title: ADNP Exhibits Methyltransferase Activity in Overexpression Systems and Modulates DNA and Histone Methylation.
review_notes: Reports methyltransferase activity for ADNP, but explicitly in overexpression systems and on immunoprecipitated fractions rather than purified protein, so a co-purifying methyltransferase is not excluded. Recorded as a knowledge gap; no GO annotation is proposed from it.

title: Remodeling activity of ChAHP restricts transcription factor access to chromatin.
review_notes: Dissects ChAHP subunit contributions: CHD4's remodelling activity is required for transposon silencing and CTCF antagonism while HP1 is dispensable, and ADNP recruits that activity sequence-specifically.

title: ChAHP silences SINE retrotransposons by inhibiting TFIIIB recruitment.
review_notes: Establishes the mechanism of ChAHP SINE B2 silencing - blocking TFIIIB recruitment to Pol III - and shows heterochromatin formation plays only a minor role, which is why the general transposable-element-silencing term is proposed rather than the heterochromatin child.

title: Formation of ChAHP complex
review_notes: Reactome's 'Formation of ChAHP complex' event. Its GO:0005654 annotations cover exactly four entities - ADNP, CBX1, CBX3, CHD4 - with no functional term spreading alongside, so it is a benign complex-localisation projection.

title: Ensembl Compara donor provenance for human ADNP (Q9H2P0)
review_notes: Generated by the committed analyze_compara_donors.py, which queries QuickGO and PubMed live, asserts full pagination, and break-tests its classifier. Regenerate with --check to confirm the committed file reproduces.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADNP (human)
review_notes: Read in full and used as a lead-generator, not as evidence; no supporting_text in this review is taken from it. Two defects worth recording. Its own grounding block states the complex as 'ChAHP complex (ADNP-CHD4-BRG1)' - ChAHP is ADNP-CHD4-HP1, and BRG1/SMARCA4 belongs to a separate reported SWI/SNF association. And although gates_passed is True with 28 citations and faith_pct 100.0, PMID:29795351 (the ChAHP-defining Nature paper, and the source of ADNP's only human experimental GO annotation), PMID:31491387 and both 2026 Mol Cell papers are absent from its citation list - a recall miss, which a passing gate does not measure.

title: NAP mechanisms of neuroprotection.
review_notes: Cited here only to characterise a donor annotation, not to support anything about ADNP2. This is the reference behind rat Adnp's GO:0010629 IDA, which is one of the two IBD seed contributions to ADNP2's GO:0010468 IBA row. Its subject is the synthetic octapeptide NAPVSIPQ, not the Adnp gene product - the defect class the merged ADNP review classified SOURCE_BAD plus ROLE_CONFLATION. Abstract-only in the cache, which is sufficient for this purpose since the title and abstract establish the molecule assayed.

title: Activity-dependent neuroprotective protein (ADNP) differentially interacts with chromatin to regulate genes essential for embryogenesis.
review_notes: Cited only as donor evidence: mouse Adnp's GO:0000981 and GO:0006357 IDA rows, both in the GO:0010468 subtree. About ADNP, not ADNP2.

title: Silencing of the ADNP-family member, ADNP2, results in changes in cellular viability under oxidative stress.
review_notes: The sole evidence behind both GO:0007399 rows on this gene, via a mouse Adnp2 IEP. Abstract-only in the cache, so nothing here is asserted beyond what the abstract states. Worth noting that the abstract's functional result is an siRNA experiment about hydrogen peroxide toxicity, not about nervous system development; the nervous-system annotation rests on the expression data in the same abstract.

title: Analysis of the human HP1 interactome reveals novel binding partners.
review_notes: The most informative of the six interaction references: a focused tandem-affinity-purification study of the three human HP1 isotypes, annotating only nine distinct entities across all of GOA, that recovers ADNP2 with both CBX1 and CBX3. Abstract-only in the cache, so the ADNP2-specific detail is taken from the GOA rows rather than from the text.

title: Novel evolutionary-conserved role for the activity-dependent neuroprotective protein (ADNP) family that is important for erythropoiesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. The source of UniProt's by-similarity "May interact with SMARCA4/BRG1" SUBUNIT line, and of the erythroid phenotype. The BRG1 interaction is reported for ADNP2 explicitly in the abstract, so this is not an ADNP result misattributed to the paralogue - but note that the later ChAHP2 proteomics recovered CHD4 rather than SMARCA4, and the two findings have not been reconciled.

title: Human-chromatin-related protein interactions identify a demethylase complex required for chromosome segregation.
review_notes: Chromatin-focused affinity-purification survey; 314 distinct entities in GOA. Corroborates the ADNP2-HP1beta pair. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: A High-Density Map for Navigating the Human Polycomb Complexome.
review_notes: Polycomb complexome interaction map; 135 distinct entities in GOA. Recovers ADNP2 with both CBX1 and CBX3. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: Activity-dependent neuroprotective protein recruits HP1 and CHD4 to control lineage-specifying genes.
