review_notes: The ChAHP paper. Cited as the donor evidence behind human ADNP's GO:0090575 IDA, which seeds ADNP2's nucleus IBA, and as the comparator establishing that ADNP's complex is ADNP-CHD4-HP1. About ADNP, not ADNP2.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI systematic yeast two-hybrid. 85343 annotations in GOA, so a reference-projection test is uninformative for it by construction and no independence claim is made from it. Its value is that a binary method agrees with the affinity-purification references on CBX3.

title: ADNP promotes neural differentiation by modulating Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
review_notes: Cited only as donor evidence. Supplies mouse Adnp's GO:0010468 IMP and zebrafish adnpa's GO:0005634 IDA, that is, the gene-product experiments that carry ADNP2's two IBA rows. About ADNP, not ADNP2.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex; 9514 annotations in GOA. Corroborative only, for both CBX1 and CBX3.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Endogenous tagging, so free of the over-expression objection that applies to HuRI and to transfection-based pulldowns. This is the strongest single line of human cellular evidence for the ADNP2-HP1beta interaction.

title: ChAHP2 and ChAHP control diverse retrotransposons by complementary activities.
review_notes: The single most important reference for this gene and the source of every mechanistic claim in this review. PubMed-verified, PMC11293393, full text cached. No retraction, erratum or expression of concern on the PubMed record. Note that the in vitro reconstitution used full-length HUMAN ADNP2, HP1beta and CHD4, so the complex-assembly evidence applies directly to the human protein, while all cellular and functional experiments are in mouse ES cells.

title: Sex-Specific ADNP/NAP (Davunetide) Regulation of Cocaine-Induced Plasticity.
review_notes: Returned by the affinage record and deliberately not used. Its own title names NAP/davunetide: it is a study of the synthetic ADNP-derived peptide, and its only ADNP2 content is a transient change in Adnp2 mRNA after cocaine injection in mice. Using it would import exactly the peptide-pharmacology confusion that the merged ADNP review identified, into a gene that does not even contain the peptide. Recorded here so that the exclusion is deliberate and visible rather than silent.

title: Genetic and Environmental Factors Co-Contributing to Behavioral Abnormalities in adnp/adnp2 Mutant Zebrafish.
review_notes: Returned by the affinage record. Zebrafish adnp/adnp2 mutants; supports a nervous-system role for the orthologue group but nothing at the molecular level and nothing human. No GO annotation on ADNP2 rests on it.

title: Adnp2 promotes neural induction by antagonizing the ved and vent homeobox genes.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; nothing is asserted here beyond the abstract. Zebrafish adnp2a/adnp2b, so it supports the orthologue group's nervous-system role rather than a human function. Note the abstract's own framing is an indirect role in neuroectoderm formation, so it should not be read as ADNP2 acting within the neural programme itself.

title: ADNP2 bioinformatics: NAP-peptide propagation audit, PxVxL motif with its compositional null, and IBD-seed evidence resolution
review_notes: Generated by the committed analyze_adnp2_propagation.py, which re-derives every number at run time and asserts its own preconditions: the NAP scan fails loudly unless the ADNP orthologue positive controls carry the octapeptide, and the PxVxL scan refuses to report ADNP2's column unless it first reproduces the merged ADNP review's published figures exactly. Note that the repo's reference validator does not check file: quotes, so the three quotations of this document were verified by hand with a literal substring match and a single-physical-line requirement.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline reference; maps IPR012864 (PCO/ADO) to the generic parent dioxygenase MF GO:0016702. Correct but non-specific relative to the experimental GO:0047800 annotations.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS transfer of iron ion binding from the mouse ortholog (UniProtKB:Q6PDY2); concordant with the human IDA structural evidence (PMID:34508780).

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PANTHER/PAN-GO phylogenetic (IBA) inference of mitochondrial localization. This contradicts the curated cytosolic localization in UniProt/Reactome and the known cytosolic substrates of ADO; treated as an over-annotation.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl-Compara IEA transfer from the mouse ortholog (Q6PDY2). The cytosol and taurine-biosynthesis transfers are correct; the mitochondrion transfer conflicts with the curated cytosolic localization.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: ARBA/rule-based electronic inference (via mouse Q6PDY2, RHEA:14409, EC 1.13.11.19); redundant with but concordant with the experimental cysteamine dioxygenase and iron ion binding annotations.

title: Discovery and characterization of a second mammalian thiol dioxygenase, cysteamine dioxygenase.
review_notes: Founding paper establishing ADO as the cysteamine dioxygenase. Abstract only in the cache (full_text_available: false); the curator's IMP annotation is based on the full text.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput affinity-purification interactome (BioPlex). Source of a bare protein-binding IPI (partner FAM76B, Q5HYJ3); no specific molecular function for ADO. ADO is present only in the supplementary interaction data, not the prose.

title: Cofactor Biogenesis in Cysteamine Dioxygenase: C-F Bond Cleavage with Genetically Incorporated Unnatural Tyrosine.
review_notes: Structure-function study of the ADO catalytic machinery; supports the IMP cysteamine dioxygenase annotation via Tyr222 mutants.

title: Conserved N-terminal cysteine dioxygenases transduce responses to hypoxia in animals and plants.
review_notes: Landmark paper reassigning ADO as the N-degron N-terminal cysteine dioxygenase / oxygen sensor. Full text available; directly supports the cellular-response-to-hypoxia IDA and the cysteamine dioxygenase IDA.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Yeast two-hybrid binary interactome (HuRI). Source of bare protein-binding IPIs (partners CAP2/P40123 and DISC1/Q9NRI5-2); no specific molecular function.

title: Characterization of the nonheme iron center of cysteamine dioxygenase and its interaction with substrates.
review_notes: EPR/Mossbauer study confirming a single ferrous iron center that catalyzes both the cysteamine and the N-terminal cysteine peptide reactions.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome (BioPlex 3.0). Source of a bare protein-binding IPI (partner FAM76B, Q5HYJ3); no specific molecular function for ADO.

title: Crystal structure of human cysteamine dioxygenase provides a structural rationale for its function as an oxygen sensor.
review_notes: Structural paper; basis for the iron ion binding IDA annotation and for the 3-His ferrous center.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteome dataset providing the HTP mitochondrion annotation. ADO is not discussed in the cached full text (listed only in supplementary data); the mitochondrial signal conflicts with the curated cytosolic localization and is most likely co-purification.

title: ADO oxidises 2AET to HTAU
review_notes: Curated Reactome reaction; supports the cytosol (TAS) localization and the cysteamine dioxygenase / taurine-biosynthesis functions.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The InterPro entry supplying these rows is IPR012108 "ADP-ribosylarginine hydrolase", a family-specific PIRSF-backed signature rather than a bare fold. Its interpro2go mapping was fetched directly and contains exactly three terms - GO:0000287, GO:0003875 and GO:0051725 - all correct for ADPRH. The three fold-level signatures ADPRH also matches (IPR005502, IPR036705, IPR050792) map to nothing, so InterPro2GO's restraint is the internal control showing the specific mapping is deliberate.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PANTHER node PTN009030515 was checked against the cached PAINT table and against QuickGO by withFrom. Its seeds are UniProtKB:P54922, MGI:MGI:1098234 (mouse Adprh) and RGD:2052 (rat Adprh); its reach is 20 gene products, all ADPRH orthologues, and it includes neither ADPRHL1 nor ADPRS. The sibling node PTN008564042 carries the ARH3 activities separately.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: The Compara transfer itself is mechanically correct - the donor named in WITH/FROM is rat Adprh Q02589, a genuine ortholog. The problem is what is being transferred: a single rat cerebrospinal-fluid western blot (PMID:9037477) as a location for the human protein.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: The WITH/FROM field cites ARBA:ARBA00088955 together with RHEA:14885 and EC:3.2.2.19, both of which match UniProt's experimentally evidenced CATALYTIC ACTIVITY line for P54922, and the mouse and rat orthologs. Correct for ADPRH. Noted separately in suggested_questions that this same route gives GO:0003875 to the catalytically inactive paralog ADPRHL1.

title: Restoration of LDL receptor function in cells from patients with autosomal recessive hypercholesterolemia by retroviral expression of ARH1.
review_notes: A gene-symbol collision, not a finding about this gene. The "ARH1" of this paper is the autosomal recessive hypercholesterolaemia adaptor protein LDLRAP1, which the paper maps to chromosome 1p36; ADPRH is at 3q22.1 and has no role in LDL receptor internalisation. The affinage record lists it as an ADPRH finding, "establishing ARH1 as a functional adaptor required for LDL receptor-dependent LDL internalization". Recorded so that the wrong attribution is not inherited; nothing in this review rests on it.

title: Molecular and immunological characterization of ADP-ribosylarginine hydrolases.
review_notes: Not cited by a human row. Retrieved while querying what the IBA donors carry for GO:0003875 - rat Adprh (Q02589, RGD:2052) holds IDA and IMP from this paper, so the phylogenetic node is seeded by real experimental evidence in two species rather than by the human annotation alone.

title: Identification and characterization of a mammalian 39-kDa poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase.
review_notes: Verified as used here - the paper is sound and is cited only as the reciprocal specificity control, which is what its abstract establishes. The miscitation is the affinage provider's, not this review's, and is recorded here rather than in `correctness` so that a downstream reader does not conclude this review miscites it. Affinage attributes "Critical vicinal acidic amino acids required for catalytic activity were identified by mutagenesis" to ARH1, whereas the abstract attributes the Asp-77/Asp-78 mutagenesis to ARH3, saying that those residues "are located in a region similar to that required for activity in ARH1". A paralog attribution error in the provider narrative, not in GOA.

title: Enhanced sensitivity to cholera toxin in ADP-ribosylarginine hydrolase-deficient mice.
review_notes: Cached abstract-only. Mouse knockout, so it is used here for biological context and for suggested experiments, not to propose a human GO annotation. Crossref could not resolve the DOI (HTTP 404), so the correction check for this reference rests on the PubMed CommentsCorrections/RefType sweep alone, which was clean.

title: Cloning, expression, purification and crystallization as well as X-ray fluorescence and preliminary X-ray diffraction analyses of human ADP-ribosylhydrolase 1.
review_notes: Cached abstract-only, but the structural claim is independently checkable: RCSB reports PDB 3HFW nonpolymer_bound_components as K and MG, and UniProt cites this paper as ECO:0000269|PubMed:19407395 for six Mg2+ BINDING features. The reference-projection test returns 2 annotations on 1 entity.

title: Side chain specificity of ADP-ribosylation by a sirtuin.
review_notes: Found by querying IntAct rather than by any ADPRH-keyed literature search; IntAct records the pair as an "enzymatic study" of type "cleavage" (EBI-7579979). Titled for trypanosome sirtuin ADP-ribosylation. Corroborative only - the arginine specificity it supports is already established by PMID:30472116.

title: Hydrolysis of O-acetyl-ADP-ribose isomers by ADP-ribosylhydrolase 3.
review_notes: Cached abstract-only and titled for the paralog. The ARH1 statement is a one-sentence restatement of earlier work, not this paper's measurement, and it sits alongside PMID:30472116's head-to-head comparison assigning PAR and 1''-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose activity to ARH3. Recorded as a knowledge gap; deliberately NOT used to propose GO:0004649 or GO:0061463 for ADPRH.

title: ADP-ribosylarginine hydrolase regulates cell proliferation and tumorigenesis.
review_notes: Full text cached. A mouse phenotype, so no human GO annotation is proposed from it; it is used to motivate the biological significance of the erasing activity and one suggested experiment.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Correctly cited high-throughput screen; the citation is sound and the interaction is real as a screen output. IntAct expansion shows the pair is logged under three sub-methods (two hybrid array, two hybrid prey pooling approach, validated two hybrid) of the one screen, which is what UniProt's NbExp=3 counts.

title: Role of a TRIM72 ADP-ribosylation cycle in myocardial injury and membrane repair.
review_notes: Full text cached. Mouse work; used for substrate identity and for suggested experiments rather than for a human annotation. Crossref could not resolve the DOI (HTTP 404), so as for PMID:17526733 the correction check rests on the PubMed sweep alone.

title: (ADP-ribosyl)hydrolases: Structural Basis for Differential Substrate Recognition and Inhibition.
review_notes: Full text cached. This is the reference behind ADPRH's EC number, its CATALYTIC ACTIVITY line, its COFACTOR line and all five "Complete loss of activity" MUTAGEN features. The reference-projection test returns 7 annotations over 2 entities - P54922 receives the arginine terms and H3BCW1 (coelacanth ADPRS) receives GO:0004649, GO:0140290 and GO:0140292 - the same paper discriminating the two specificities correctly in one pass.

title: The ARH and Macrodomain Families of α-ADP-ribose-acceptor Hydrolases Catalyze α-NAD(+) Hydrolysis.
review_notes: Full text cached. UniProt encodes this as a second CATALYTIC ACTIVITY on P54922 (Rhea:RHEA:68792, ChEBI:CHEBI:77017 alpha-NAD+, ECO:0000269|PubMed:31599159), and it is also the source of the Asp-55/Asp-56 mutagenesis. No GO annotation exists for it because no suitable GO term exists; see proposed_new_terms.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: As for PMID:25416956 - correctly cited, but a single screen logged as three IntAct sub-methods, MI-score 0.56, and SPSB1 has 78 distinct IntAct partners against ADPRH's 17.

title: ARH Family of ADP-Ribose-Acceptor Hydrolases.
review_notes: Review article from the group that characterised the enzyme; used for orientation, not as primary evidence for any action.

title: Cloning and site-directed mutagenesis of human ADP-ribosylarginine hydrolase.
review_notes: Cached abstract-only. The reference-projection test returns 4 annotations over 2 entities (human P54922 and mouse P54923) and 2 terms, i.e. a normal two-species curation of one paper, not a bulk projection.

title: Immunohistochemical localization of ADP-ribosylarginine hydrolase in rodent CNS.
review_notes: Not cited by any human ADPRH GOA row directly; it is the upstream source of the rat IDA that Ensembl Compara projects onto human as GO:0005576. Identified by querying the donor's own evidence. Cached abstract-only, so the rat IDA itself is not second-guessed here - only its transfer to human.

title: ADPRH catalytic-residue census across PANTHER PTHR16222
review_notes: Generated by the committed script catalytic_residue_census.py in the same folder; a fresh run reproduces both RESULTS.md and results.json byte-identically, and --self-test reports zero problems. The self-test was break-tested by reverting the anchored Swiss-Prot check to the buggy substring form, which makes it fail with the expected message.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADPRH (human)
review_notes: The record's trust gate failed - the frontmatter reads gates_passed: False, with the explanation that Affinage's own head-to-head self-evaluation scored the record pairwise = tie rather than a win. Re-checking every claim against the cited PMIDs found two genuine defects, both name/paralog collisions - PMID:12464675 is about the LDL receptor adaptor LDLRAP1 rather than ADP-ribosylhydrolase 1, and the "critical vicinal acidic amino acids" mutagenesis attributed to ARH1 is ARH3's Asp-77/Asp-78 in PMID:16278211. One further citation, PMID:36945646, is a bioRxiv preprint. Recall was also poor - the record returned none of PMID:9037477, PMID:1375222, PMID:25416956, PMID:32296183 or PMID:19895577, which between them decide four rows of this review. Nothing mechanistic in this review rests on a provider sentence.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The pipeline is correctly applied - the interpro2go file does map IPR012108 to these three terms, confirmed by downloading it and looking up all four signatures ADPRHL1 matches. The defect is in the input signature, not the mapping machinery, and the other three signatures mapping to nothing is the control that shows so.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Q6AZR2 resolved via the UniProt REST API - reviewed Swiss-Prot, Xenopus laevis adprhl1, 354 aa, holding GO:0003242, GO:0055003 and GO:0030017 by IMP from PMID:27217161. Not a paralog and not a partial clone.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Correctly applied. Worth noting only that it is not independent of the ISS row, which is why the two rows are given the same action.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Correctly applied by the pipeline; the rule itself is the problem. Verified by fetching the rule and checking that its FunFam condition matches ADPRHL1's own DR FunFam line, and by confirming that the predicted mammalian and non-mammalian reference split is exactly what GOA shows across the seven reviewed ARH2 orthologues.

title: The family of toxin-related ecto-ADP-ribosyltransferases in humans and the mouse.
review_notes: Correctly cited by UniProt for a sequence submission only. Noted here solely in support of the nomenclature correction request; no functional claim about ARH2 is drawn from it, and its full text is not available.

title: Identification and characterization of a mammalian 39-kDa poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase.
review_notes: Listed because it is the citation the primary literature uses for ARH2's inactivity, but marked unverified rather than verified: only the abstract is cached, the abstract is about ARH3, and this review declines to assert what a paper's unavailable full text contains. Nothing here depends on it.

title: The 39-kDa poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase ARH3 hydrolyzes O-acetyl-ADP-ribose, a product of the Sir2 family of acetyl-histone deacetylases.
review_notes: Cached abstract-only, so nothing is asserted here beyond what the abstract states, and both quoted claims are in the abstract. Found by searching the family rather than the gene symbol - no ADPRHL1-keyed query returns a paper titled for ARH3 - and it is absent from the affinage record. UniProt cites this PMID as the experimental evidence for the mouse ARH2 entry's inactivity. No retraction, erratum or Crossref update-to.

title: The cardiac-restricted protein ADP-ribosylhydrolase-like 1 is essential for heart chamber outgrowth and acts on muscle actin filament assembly.
review_notes: Verified against the cached full text. Fully paginated reference-projection test returns 3 annotations over 1 entity (Q6AZR2), so this is one curator reading one paper about one gene rather than a bulk import. No retraction, erratum or Crossref update-to.

title: Defective heart chamber growth and myofibrillogenesis after knockout of adprhl1 gene function by targeted disruption of the ancestral catalytic active site.
review_notes: Verified against the cached full text. Its reference-projection test is what exposed the split-donor problem: 10 annotations over 2 entities, and both entities are TrEMBL accessions for Xenopus adprhl1.L curated by Xenbase, not the Swiss-Prot entry the ISS rows transfer from. Crossref reports a has-preprint relation and no update-to; no retraction or erratum.

title: Histone deacetylase 4 deletion broadly affects cardiac epigenetic repression and regulates transcriptional susceptibility via H3K9 methylation.
review_notes: Cached abstract-only, so nothing is asserted about its full text and no quote is taken from it. Included for completeness because affinage cites it; a gene whose promoter is a repression target is not thereby annotated with a function.

title: A Recurrent ADPRHL1 Germline Mutation Activates PARP1 and Confers Prostate Cancer Risk in African American Families.
review_notes: Correctly cited and internally sound, but deliberately not used for any annotation: it is ectopic expression in cancer cell lines, one variant in one ancestry group, and it demonstrates no biochemical activity of ADPRHL1. Asp78 is not among the ligand positions in the residue census, so it does not bear on the catalytic question either. Crossref shows is-supplemented-by and has-preprint relations and no update-to.

title: ARH Family of ADP-Ribose-Acceptor Hydrolases.
review_notes: A review, used for the family-level statement of enzymatic status and for its explicit caveat, not as a primary source for any measurement; the underlying measurement is cited separately as PMID:17075046. From the laboratory that characterised all three ARH proteins. Absent from the affinage record. No retraction, erratum or Crossref update-to.

title: The pseudoenzyme ADPRHL1 affects cardiac function by regulating the ROCK pathway.
review_notes: Verified against the cached full text. A fully paginated reference-projection test returns zero annotations over zero entities - this paper is entirely absent from GOA, which is the largest coverage gap on this gene. No retraction, erratum or Crossref update-to.

title: Inhibition of ARH2 by pH/ROS-responsive nanosystem for improved lung adenocarcinoma immunochemotherapy.
review_notes: Correctly cited and genuinely about ARH2, but not used for any annotation. It is a drug-delivery study whose gene-function claims rest on siRNA in tumour models, and its direction contradicts the tumour-suppressor reading of PMID:35816343 in a different tissue. Recorded so the next reviewer knows it was read and set aside.

title: ADPRHL1 (ARH2, Q8NDY3): catalytic-site census against its active paralogues
review_notes: Generated by the committed script catalytic_site_census.py, which fetches every sequence and feature live from UniProt, caches them, self-tests, break-tests its own reproduction gate, and regenerates this file byte-identically. Its two external checks reproduce published identity figures (46.6% versus 46%, 74.6% versus 75%). All quotes taken from it were hand-verified with grep -F because the repo validator skips file references.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADPRHL1 (human)
review_notes: gates_passed True, six citations, all numeric PMIDs with no bioRxiv identifiers in a PMID-shaped field, and each verified against PubMed to be about ADPRHL1/ARH2. No retraction or erratum among them. Used only as a lead: no sentence from it is quoted as supporting_text anywhere in this review, per the campaign rule that provider prose must not carry a mechanistic claim. The repo validator's warning that no annotation references this file is therefore expected and is left standing rather than silenced by inventing a citation.

title: UniProtKB entry Q8NDY3 (ARHL1_HUMAN), Inactive ADP-ribosyltransferase ARH2
review_notes: All four quotes hand-verified with grep -F against the file in this worktree, each on a single physical line so that no UniProt CC continuation is crossed. The repo's reference validator does not check file: quotes, so this was done by hand.

title: The structure of human ADP-ribosylhydrolase 3 (ARH3) provides insights into the reversibility of protein ADP-ribosylation.
review_notes: The 1.6 A ARH3 structure, and the source of the micromolar ADP-ribose binding measurement. Its statement that ARH3 'efficiently de-ADP-ribosylates poly- but not monoADP-ribosylated proteins' was superseded in 2017: ARH3 is the serine mono-ADP-ribosylhydrolase. The 2006 assay used arginine-linked mono-ADP-ribose, on which ARH3 is genuinely inactive, so the two results are compatible once the substrate is specified. Marked DISPUTED so the older negative is not re-imported.

title: ADP-ribosyl-acceptor hydrolase 3 regulates poly (ADP-ribose) degradation and cell death during oxidative stress.
review_notes: The mouse Arh3 oxidative-stress paper. Correctly cited by MGI, but it is the origin of two term-choice defects that propagate into human ADPRS: the stressor is hydrogen peroxide throughout, yet the annotation made from it is GO:0071451 cellular response to SUPEROXIDE; and the death process it characterises is parthanatos (PARP1 - free PAR - AIF release), which is annotated as regulation of necroptosis. Flagged MISCITED for those uses; the experiments themselves are not in question.

title: Structure-function analyses reveal the mechanism of the ARH3-dependent hydrolysis of ADP-ribosylation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Carries an erratum, PMID:30659162 (J Biol Chem 2019;294(3):874), which was retrieved and read: it corrects the affiliation of one author and touches no data. Checked because this paper is the sole support for six GOA rows.

title: Biallelic Mutations in ADPRHL2, Encoding ADP-Ribosylhydrolase 3, Lead to a Degenerative Pediatric Stress-Induced Epileptic Ataxia Syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Two errata (PMID:30388405, PMID:34861176) were retrieved and read; both are author-list corrections with no effect on the data. Not cited by any GOA row on this gene, but it is the CONDSIAS discovery paper and is cited in the description.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: The HuRI reference map. Correctly cited, but it is a single high-throughput yeast two-hybrid screen; IntAct logs it under three sub-methods, which is what UniProt's NbExp=3 counts, so the count is not three independent experiments. Both GO:0005515 rows on this gene rest on it alone.

title: Molecular Tools for the Study of ADP-Ribosylation: A Unified and Versatile Method to Synthesise Native Mono-ADP-Ribosylated Peptides.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text read. The paper is correctly cited as evidence that ARH3 hydrolyses mono-ADP-ribosyl-serine and -threonine linkages, but GOA uses it to support GO:0004649 poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase activity and the study contains no poly(ADP-ribose) experiment of any kind - only synthetic MARylated Ser/Thr/Cys peptides. Flagged MISCITED for that specific row; the paper itself is sound and is the sole evidence for the proposed threonine-hydrolase term.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP. Correctly cited for mitochondrial localisation, but the gene-level call is in the study's supplementary inventory rather than the article text; the reference annotates 1235 GO rows in total, so it is a bulk import and is treated as corroborating rather than establishing.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Source of a block of stimulus-response and off-pathway biosynthesis IEAs (hypoxia, nutrient, starvation, muscle activity, aerobic respiration, GMP, XMP, AMP salvage) transferred from rodent orthologs. Several are biologically unsupportable for human ADSL and are flagged for REMOVE / MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED.

title: Human adenylosuccinate lyase (ADSL), cloning and characterization of full-length cDNA and its isoform, gene structure and molecular basis for ADSL deficiency in six patients.
review_notes: Establishes ADSL as a bifunctional de novo purine synthesis/recycling enzyme, characterizes the enzymatically inactive isoform 2, and defines the molecular basis of ADSL deficiency in six patients (abstract verified against cached record).

title: Determination, activity and biological role of adenylosuccinate lyase in blood cells.
review_notes: Measures ADSL activity in human blood cells and discusses its role in regulating cellular AMP levels; supports the AMP biosynthetic process annotation.

title: Expression, purification, and characterization of stable, recombinant human adenylosuccinate lyase.
review_notes: Defines the recombinant human enzyme's S-AMP lyase kinetics (Vmax/Km) and demonstrates the homotetramer (~220 kDa) by analytical ultracentrifugation; basis for the MF, identical-protein-binding, and protein-complex annotations.

title: Biochemical and biophysical analysis of five disease-associated human adenylosuccinate lyase mutants.
review_notes: Full text available; explicitly states the two beta-elimination reactions (SAMP->AMP+fumarate; SAICAR->AICAR+fumarate) and the homotetramer with three subunits per active site. Primary support for both core MFs.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 induced mutations along de novo purine synthesis in HeLa cells result in accumulation of individual enzyme substrates and affect purinosome formation.
review_notes: CRISPR knockout of de novo purine synthesis enzymes (including ADSL) in HeLa cells causes accumulation of the knocked-out enzyme's substrate and impairs purinosome assembly; supports the in vivo SAICAR-lyase step.

title: SAICAR => AICAR + Fumarate
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the SAICAR-lyase step; states the active enzyme is a cytosolic tetramer and mediates both reactions in vivo.

title: adenylosuccinate => adenosine 5'-monophosphate + fumarate
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the S-AMP lyase step; states the active enzyme is a cytosolic tetramer.

title: UniProtKB P30566 (PUR8_HUMAN) adenylosuccinate lyase record
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; source of the dual catalytic-activity, de novo IMP/AMP pathway, homotetramer subunit, and ADSLD disease annotations.

title: Molecular cloning and characterization of a novel muscle adenylosuccinate synthetase, AdSSL1, from human bone marrow stromal cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary characterization of human ADSS1/AdSSL1 (activity, cytoplasmic localization, muscle-predominant expression). Abstract-only in cache but the abstract directly supports the enzymatic and localization annotations.

title: ADSSL1 mutation relevant to autosomal recessive adolescent onset distal myopathy.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes the disease link (MPD5) and provides mutant-phenotype (IMP) evidence for the catalytic function. Abstract-only in cache; the abstract supports the activity and disease claims.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome study; source of an IntAct IPI protein-binding annotation (partner ADSS2). Does not establish a specific molecular function for ADSS1.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome study; source of an IntAct IPI protein-binding annotation (partner ADSS2). Uninformative bare protein-binding evidence for ADSS1.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map / interactome study; source of an IntAct IPI protein-binding annotation (partner ADSS2). Uninformative bare protein-binding evidence.

title: IMP + L-Aspartate + GTP => Adenylosuccinate + GDP + Pi [ADSS]
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the adenylosuccinate synthase step; source of the cytosol (TAS) localization. Title left exactly as fetched.

title: UniProt entry Q8N142 (PURA1_HUMAN, ADSS1) - adenylosuccinate synthetase isozyme 1
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; primary source for reaction, cofactor, pathway, subcellular location, and the ADSS1-ADSS2 interaction used in this review.

title: Novel protein ADTRP regulates TFPI expression and function in human endothelial cells in normal conditions and in response to androgen.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the paper that named the gene. Cached abstract-only (full_text_available: false), so this review restricts every claim from it to what the abstract states and defers to the UniProt curator on GO:0009986 cell surface. Projection test: 2 entities, ADTRP and TFPI (P10646), with different term sets.

title: AIG1 and ADTRP are atypical integral membrane hydrolases that degrade bioactive FAHFAs.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached with full_text_available: true and read in full. This is the sole source of the gene's molecular function. No retraction, erratum or expression of concern on the PubMed record. Reference-projection test: it annotates 2 entities (ADTRP and AIG1) with 8 annotations - identical term sets, but the paper individually mutated and individually assayed both proteins, so this is parallel per-protein curation and not a projection.

title: Identification of a molecular signaling gene-gene regulatory network between GWAS susceptibility genes ADTRP and MIA3/TANGO1 for coronary artery disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of nine BHF-UCL biological-process rows. Cached abstract-only. Projection test: 4 entities (ADTRP, AKT1, MIA3/TANGO1, PIK3R3) with 22 annotations and a different term set per entity, so the network paper was curated per gene rather than projected. One cell-type problem is flagged on the GO:2000402 row: the abstract describes monocytes only.

title: AIG1 and ADTRP are endogenous hydrolases of fatty acid esters of hydroxy fatty acids (FAHFAs) in mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the in vivo demonstration that ADTRP controls FAHFA levels, using Adtrp-knockout and AIG1/ADTRP double-knockout mice plus a dual inhibitor. Cited here for the core function and knowledge gaps. Not present in GOA for this gene and not returned by the affinage record as a GOA-linked source, so it is added by this review. Mouse data, so it is not used to assert a human-specific claim.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. A systematic yeast two-hybrid interactome map, not an ADTRP study. It carries 85343 annotations across GOA, so the entity count is unavailable and the projection test was not run - recorded rather than approximated from a partial page. Both ADTRP rows trace to this one screen.

title: ADTRP regulates TFPI expression via transcription factor POU1F1 involved in coronary artery disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached abstract-only. Resolves the mechanism behind the GO:0010628 rows: POU1F1, not ADTRP, is the DNA-binding protein. Cited to keep the review from implying any transcriptional molecular function for ADTRP. Not present in GOA for this gene; surfaced by the affinage record and then read directly.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADTRP (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated deep-research record, gates_passed: True, 12 citations. Recall was checked rather than assumed and it performed well on this gene: all 12 PMIDs are numeric (no bioRxiv ids in a PMID-shaped field), all 12 resolve to papers genuinely about ADTRP - there is no gene-symbol collision here - and none carries a retraction, erratum or expression of concern on its PubMed record. It also surfaced two papers absent from GOA that this review uses, PMID:32152231 (in vivo FAHFA control) and PMID:32445923 (POU1F1). Cited only as a lead and for claims independently anchored to a primary PMID; its own GO grounding block is wrong (it lists GO:0140098 catalytic activity, acting on RNA for a lipid hydrolase) and was not used.

title: Gene Ontology annotation of human sequence-specific DNA binding transcription factors (DbTFs) based on the TFClass database
review_notes: Fully paginated, this reference covers 727 human gene products in 1436 annotations, of which 709 (97.5%) receive GO:0000981 DNA-binding transcription factor activity alongside GO:0000785 chromatin. AEBP2 is one of only 18 recipients given GO:0000785 alone. The other 17 are HOPX, ZFPM1, ZFPM2, NCOA1, NCOA2, NCOA3, SMAD6, SMAD7, NR0B1, NR0B2, NFX1, NFXL1, ZC3H6, ZC3H8, TFDP3, DMRTC1 and HMBOX1 - a coherent class of chromatin factors whose DNA-binding-like folds mediate protein contact rather than sequence recognition. So the pipeline withheld the DbTF molecular function from AEBP2 deliberately, and the chromatin location it did assign is independently correct.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: A combinatorial reference is only as independent as its tokens. All three WITH/FROM tokens were resolved: ensembl:ENSMUSP00000084896 IS UniProtKB:Q9Z248 (mouse Aebp2), so the row records one protein twice plus one ARBA rule. That rule, ARBA00089504, asserts exactly one annotation (GO:0035098) from eight alternative FunFam-id-plus-taxon conjunctions containing no residue, interaction or assay condition.

title: Cloning and characterization of a novel zinc finger transcriptional repressor. A direct role of the zinc finger motif in repression.
review_notes: The original characterisation of the protein, and the sole source of the mouse Aebp2 GO:0000122 IMP that Ensembl Compara transfers to human. Two scope limits matter. It is a mouse study, and its repression evidence is sufficiency-type: co-transfection over-expression at the aP2 promoter plus a Gal4-tethering experiment showing that AEBP2 can repress a heterologous promoter when delivered to it. Neither shows the gene is required for repression. Queried by reference, this PMID annotates exactly one entity in all of GOA (mouse Aebp2), so it is per-gene curation and not a projection.

title: SUZ12 is required for both the histone methyltransferase activity and the silencing function of the EED-EZH2 complex.
review_notes: Source of the long-standing view that AEBP2 stimulates PRC2, reported here as a minimal complex of EZH2, EED and SUZ12 with AEBP2 required for optimal activity. PMID:41168462 reports that prior in vitro stimulation was obtained with the short isoform or with N-terminally truncated constructs, and that the broadly expressed long isoform inhibits instead. Marked DISPUTED for the direction of the effect, not for the citation: the disagreement is genuine and in the literature, and the cached record is abstract-only so the construct used cannot be determined from it.

title: AEBP2 as a potential targeting protein for Polycomb Repression Complex PRC2.
review_notes: Defines the protein's bipartite DNA-binding motif and the two developmentally regulated isoforms. All of it is mouse work: mouse GST fusion proteins in the gel shifts, mouse brain chromatin in the ChIP. Notably this reference has zero annotations anywhere in GOA, so the study that established this protein's DNA binding contributes nothing to the GO record.

title: Jarid2/Jumonji coordinates control of PRC2 enzymatic activity and target gene occupancy in pluripotent cells.
review_notes: One of the three independent references behind mouse Aebp2's GO:0035098 IDA rows, which is what makes the GO:0035098 IBA a well-founded transfer rather than a family-level guess. Cited for that donor evidence, not for a claim about the human protein.

title: Jumonji modulates polycomb activity and self-renewal versus differentiation of stem cells.
review_notes: The second of the three references behind mouse Aebp2's GO:0035098 IDA rows. Same role in this review as PMID:20064375.

title: JARID2 regulates binding of the Polycomb repressive complex 2 to target genes in ES cells.
review_notes: The cached record is abstract-only and the abstract is about JARID2, not AEBP2; the GO:0035098 IDA on AEBP2 is a curator call from the full text, which I have not read. The projection test supports it rather than undermining it: this reference gives GO:0035098 IDA to eight PRC2 components, all assigned by UniProt, while its one functional row (GO:0048863 IMP) stays on mouse Jarid2 alone, the gene actually perturbed. That is the signature of per-protein curation, not of a complex-level phenotype spread across subunits.

title: Aebp2 as an epigenetic regulator for neural crest cells.
review_notes: Source for the description's statement that the mouse gene is essential for embryogenesis and is expressed mainly in neural-crest-derived cells, with AEBP2 and PRC2 co-occupying neural-crest migration gene promoters. Mouse throughout, which is why the description attributes it to mouse explicitly and no developmental GO term is proposed for the human gene on its strength.

title: Functional analysis of AEBP2, a PRC2 Polycomb protein, reveals a Trithorax phenotype in embryonic development and in ESCs.
review_notes: The in vivo loss-of-function result, and the first clear signal that the gene restrains rather than promotes PRC2 output: homozygous mutant embryos show a Trithorax phenotype and mutant ESCs show elevated H3K27 methylation at target loci. Mouse.

title: Structures of human PRC2 with its cofactors AEBP2 and JARID2.
review_notes: Correctly cited for the architecture of the holo-complex and for AEBP2's contact with RBBP4. It is however a structure paper, and the three ComplexPortal NAS rows it supports (GO:0000122, GO:0031507, GO:0005634) are given identically to all nine entities the reference annotates - two ComplexPortal complexes plus seven subunits - so for AEBP2 they record complex-level properties rather than anything measured on this protein. Its own cryo-EM construct, per RCSB, covers Q6ZN18 residues 209-503 only.

title: Unique Structural Platforms of Suz12 Dictate Distinct Classes of PRC2 for Chromatin Binding.
review_notes: The most informative reference for this protein's molecular function. It maps the SUZ12 C2 interaction, shows the C-terminus displacing H3K4 from RBBP4 by direct competition, and - importantly for isoform scoping - measures the contribution of the last residues to nucleosome binding using constructs that differ by exactly the 14 residues absent from isoform 2.

title: Distinct Stimulatory Mechanisms Regulate the Catalytic Activity of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2.
review_notes: Reports that AEBP2 stimulates both PRC2-EZH1 and PRC2-EZH2 by a mechanism independent of and additive to allosteric activation. Like PMID:15225548 this is disputed in direction by PMID:41168462, which attributes prior stimulation results to use of the short isoform or of N-terminally truncated protein. Cited here for the mechanism it describes, not as support for a stimulatory annotation.

title: EZHIP/CXorf67 mimics K27M mutated oncohistones and functions as an intrinsic inhibitor of PRC2 function in aggressive posterior fossa ependymoma.
review_notes: Cited only to establish the curation precedent for the proposed GO:0180000 annotation. This is the single experimental anchor for that term anywhere in GOA (human EZHIP Q86X51, IDA); the term's other 14 annotations are all EZHIP orthologs by IEA or ISO.

title: EZHIP constrains Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 activity in germ cells.
review_notes: The third reference behind mouse Aebp2's GO:0035098 IDA rows, and independently relevant because it characterises EZHIP, the only protein that currently holds the GO:0180000 term proposed here for AEBP2.

title: A Dimeric Structural Scaffold for PRC2-PCL Targeting to CpG Island Chromatin.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt's FUNCTION line and by the suggested question about isoform dependence. It shows AEBP2 binding the SUZ12 C2 domain and disrupting the intrinsic PRC2 dimer that MTF2/PHF19 stabilise, so it is part of the evidence that AEBP2's effect on PRC2 is regulatory rather than simply stimulatory.

title: JARID2 and AEBP2 regulate PRC2 in the presence of H2AK119ub1 and other histone modifications.
review_notes: Source for AEBP2 contacting a ubiquitin moiety and the H2A-H2B surface of H2AK119ub1-containing nucleosomes. Its structure, 6WKR, again covers Q6ZN18 residues 209-503 only, so it characterises the region shared by all three isoforms.

title: Structures of monomeric and dimeric PRC2:EZH1 reveal flexible modules involved in chromatin compaction.
review_notes: A structural study of PRC2-EZH1 monomers and dimers. It is correctly cited for complex composition, and its GO:0035098 IPI on AEBP2 is sound. Its three ComplexPortal NAS rows are the same projection as PMID:29348366's: nine entities, identical term set. Note the discriminating detail - the functional rows this reference carries (GO:0031491, GO:0046976, GO:0140693, all IMP) sit on EZH1 alone, so ComplexPortal projected the process and location terms but not the catalytic ones.

title: Auto-inhibition of PRC2 by the broadly expressed long isoform of AEBP2.
review_notes: The reference that reframes this gene's annotation set, and it names UniProt isoform identifiers explicitly, so no inference is needed to map its AEBP2L/AEBP2S nomenclature onto Q6ZN18-1/-2/-3. Its claim that all previous structures used the short isoform or a partial sequence was checked against RCSB rather than repeated: of 17 PDB entries resolving an AEBP2 chain, 15 declare an N-terminally truncated construct, and the two declaring 1-517 are 8EQV (this paper's own structure) and 8FYH (2023). So the pattern is real and near-universal but the word "all" is not exact. Single study for the inhibition mechanism, hence the knowledge gap recorded below.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AEBP2 (human)
review_notes: gates_passed is True and faith_pct 100, and recall was unusually good on this gene: the record surfaced PMID:41168462, which is the reference that reframes the annotation set. Marked LOW_QUALITY for two specific defects rather than as a blanket judgement. First, two of its 24 citations are bioRxiv DOIs in a PMID-shaped field (PMID:bio_10.1101_2025.11.09.687442, PMID:bio_10.1101_2025.10.14.682307); both concern the isoform story and no claim in this review rests on either. Second, its GO grounding block lists GO:0042393 histone binding, which the structural papers it cites do not support (they show AEBP2 mimicking a histone tail, not binding one) and GO:0003677 DNA binding, which GOA carries for no member of this family. It is cited here only as the source of those declined proposals, never for a mechanistic claim; the record's own caveat that the grounding block is coarse is accurate. Its framings also needed re-deriving: describing the short isoform as promoting PRC2 activity conflates a DNA-binding result with an HMTase result whose baseline differs.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: A GO reference, not a publication; cited because GOA rows point at it. Its WITH/FROM tokens were resolved individually and are recorded per row.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: A GO reference, not a publication; cited because GOA rows point at it. Its WITH/FROM tokens were resolved individually and are recorded per row.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: A GO reference, not a publication; cited because GOA rows point at it. Its WITH/FROM tokens were resolved individually and are recorded per row.

title: A mutation in Af4 is predicted to cause cerebellar ataxia and cataracts in the robotic mouse.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Mouse; and a gain-of-function model - the robotic allele stabilises Af4 rather than removing it - which is why the nervous-system row is kept as non-core rather than promoted.

title: The synthetic peptide PFWT disrupts AF4-AF9 protein complexes and induces apoptosis in t(4;11) leukemia cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cited only to record that the PFWT peptide is a synthetic inhibitor modelled on AFF1's AF9-binding domain, so its cellular effects are properties of the peptide and no GOA row rests on it - the peptide-pharmacology hazard checked and found absent from this gene's annotation set.

title: The mixed-lineage leukemia fusion partner AF4 stimulates RNA polymerase II transcriptional elongation and mediates coordinated chromatin remodeling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, and cited here ONLY for what it actually shows: a mouse Af4 result. It carries an unflagged 2023 Erratum (PMID:37777189), and its DOT1L-recruitment claim rests on an ENL co-immunoprecipitate that PMID:20159561 reports was misinterpreted. Nothing in this review asserts DOT1L recruitment by AFF1.

title: AF4 is a critical regulator of the IGF-1 signaling pathway during Purkinje cell development.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Mouse Purkinje cells; cited only as the tissue-specific downstream consequence supporting the non-core nervous-system call.

title: AFF4, a component of the ELL/P-TEFb elongation complex and a shared subunit of MLL chimeras, can link transcription elongation to leukemia.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; titled for AFF4. Checked which molecule underlies the AFF1 row: the GO:0032783 IDA rests on Flag-AFF4/Flag-ELL purifications recovering endogenous AFF1, not on the paper's MLL-AFF1 fusion constructs. Also the strongest available refutation of the claim that AFF1 recruits DOT1L.

title: Human mediator subunit MED26 functions as a docking site for transcription elongation factors.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Source of one AFF1-AF9 protein-binding row via SEC co-purification with Mediator; the projection test returns 26 annotations over 17 entities, all GO:0005515, i.e. an interaction network.

title: Global landscape of HIV-human protein complexes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. A systematic AP-MS survey of all 18 HIV-1 proteins; the projection test returns 183 annotations over 104 entities, all GO:0005515, so it is a screen rather than a targeted assay. The AFF1-Tat records are 3 IntAct entries from this one publication across two cell lines.

title: The little elongation complex regulates small nuclear RNA transcription.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached abstract-only. UniProt's own reference table records its contribution as identification in the SEC complex, which is the basis for refining the GO:0008023 row. Its projection profile is what revealed that the same reference gave the specific complex term to 10 Drosophila recipients and only the generic parent to all 11 human ones.

title: The super elongation complex family of RNA polymerase II elongation factors: gene target specificity and transcriptional output.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached abstract-only. Supplies AFF1's only EXP-coded row and, importantly for two MODIFY calls, states that the SEC family members are RNA polymerase II CTD kinases and that AFF2/AFF3 occupy the SEC-L2 and SEC-L3 variants.

title: Leukemia fusion target AF9 is an intrinsically disordered transcriptional regulator that recruits multiple partners via coupled folding and binding.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; titled for AF9 but it holds the only quantitative binding measurement on human AFF1. What was assayed is a 14-residue AFF1 peptide (residues 761-774) against MBP-AF9 AHD, which the review states explicitly rather than presenting it as full-length protein.

title: AFF1 is a ubiquitous P-TEFb partner to enable Tat extraction of P-TEFb from 7SK snRNP and formation of SECs for HIV transactivation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cached abstract-only, so nothing is asserted about its figures. Cited for the constitutive CDK9-CycT-AFF1 association and for the Tat/CycT1 mechanism, and used to note that raising Tat's affinity for cyclin T1 does not establish a direct AFF1-Tat contact.

title: AFF1 and AFF4 differentially regulate the osteogenic differentiation of human MSCs.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Carries an unflagged 2020 Correction (PMID:32257529) whose content is not stated in its abstract or its PMC record, and one sentence in the overexpression section says "AFF1-depleted" where the figure describes overexpressing cells; both are recorded in the notes and the claims used avoid that sentence. LOW_QUALITY is not the right flag - the experiments are sound and bidirectional - but the correction is unresolved.

title: AFF1 acetylation by p300 temporally inhibits transcription during genotoxic stress response.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. The acetyl-mimic rescue experiment here is the cleanest evidence that the bridging function is AFF1's own rather than an emergent property of SEC, and it is why GO:0030674 is placed in molecular_function while the elongation-factor and coregulator terms are placed in contributes_to_molecular_function.

title: Stabilization of AFF1 by PARylation ensures transcriptional restart after DNA damage.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supplies 7 of the 20 GOA rows. The cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available: false), so this review characterises only what the abstract states and defers to the curator on the direct assays. The reference-projection test (fully paginated) returns 8 annotations over 2 distinct entities, with the functional terms confined to AFF1, so it is not a complex-level projection. No retraction, erratum or expression of concern in its PubMed CommentsCorrections, and Crossref reports no update-to/updated-by relation.

title: LAF-4 encodes a lymphoid nuclear protein with transactivation potential that is homologous to AF-4, the gene fused to MLL in t(4;11) leukemias.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, and titled for the paralog LAF-4/AFF3 - which is why no AFF1-keyed search surfaces it. It reports that AF-4 as well as LAF-4 has a domain that transactivates when fused to the GAL4 DNA-binding domain. Not used to support a term: the molecule assayed is a GAL4 chimera, so it shows a region can activate when artificially tethered, not that AFF1 does so natively. GOA uses this reference for AFF3's nucleus IDA and not at all for AFF1.

title: AFF1 (P51825) annotation-provenance analysis
review_notes: Machine-fetched project artifact; every quotation from it was verified with an exact-substring check that also requires the span to lie inside one physical line, because the repo's reference validator skips file: quotes entirely.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AFF1 (human)
review_notes: Adjudicated and deliberately not used as evidence anywhere in this review; recorded here so the judgement lives in the repository. Its gates_passed: True and faith_pct: 100.0 concern PRECISION - the 23 citations are all well-formed numeric PMIDs with no preprint ids in PMID-shaped fields. Recall was measured, not estimated: of the 7 PMIDs that AFF1's GOA rows actually cite, affinage returned 0, including the 2026 paper behind 7 of the 20 rows (computed in RESULTS.md section G). Four substantive defects: two cited papers carry unflagged corrections (PMID:28955517 -> PMID:32257529; PMID:17135274 -> PMID:37777189); the claim that AFF1 recruits DOT1L is contradicted by PMID:20159561; a stated hypothesis in PMID:12629167 is reported as demonstrated causation; and a result PMID:20007461 attributes to "the AF4 transcriptional regulatory complex" is attributed to Af4 alone. LOW_QUALITY refers to this record as a source, not to the underlying papers.

title: UniProt entry P51825 (AFF1_HUMAN)
review_notes: Machine-fetched project artifact; every quotation from it was verified with an exact-substring check that also requires the span to lie inside one physical line, because the repo's reference validator skips file: quotes entirely.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The interpro2go route. Which signature supplies which term was measured rather than assumed, by fetching each of AFF3's three InterPro entries individually - IPR007797 (AF4/FMR2 family, 5800 proteins) maps to GO:0010468, IPR043640 (C-terminal homology domain, 4950) maps to GO:0005634, and IPR043639 (AF4 interaction motif, 3235) maps to nothing. No molecular-function term is produced by any of them. This reproduces the merged AFF4 review's measurement exactly.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/PAN-GO, the source of five of AFF3's eleven rows. Every WITH/FROM token on all five rows was resolved to a reviewed UniProt entry and then queried for its own evidence on the propagated term. The critical resolution is MGI:MGI:106927, which is mouse Aff3 (P51827), the genuine orthologue, holding GO:0006355 by both IDA and IMP - so the family-level rows are not resting on paralogues alone.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: Human Protein Atlas immunofluorescence, supplying the nucleoplasm IDA. Consistent with the antibody localisation reported in PMID:8555498 and with the nuclear-speckle localisation in PMID:26214578, speckles being a nucleoplasmic sub-compartment.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Correct for the nucleus, but its three WITH/FROM tokens are not three independent witnesses. ARBA00026330 was fetched from rest.uniprot.org/arba - of its 1309 condition sets exactly one reaches AFF3, and that set is IPR007797 AND IPR043640 AND Eukaryota, so the InterPro:IPR043640 token is the same signature the rule already uses. The third token, UniProtKB-SubCell:SL-0191, derives from UniProt's own SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line, which carries no evidence tag. One signature counted twice plus UniProt citing itself.

title: Transcriptional regulation of cytoskeletal functions and segmentation by a novel maternal pair-rule gene, lilliputian.
review_notes: Not about AFF3. Cited because it is the source of the donor evidence on two of AFF3's IBA rows - Drosophila lilli holds both GO:0003712 and GO:0006355 by IMP from this paper. The merged AFF4 review reached the same reference for the same donor, independently.

title: Impaired conditioned fear and enhanced long-term potentiation in Fmr2 knock-out mice.
review_notes: Not about AFF3. Source of mouse Aff2's GO:0007611 IMP, one of the two donors on AFF3's GO:0050877 row, and therefore the evidence whose specificity that row generalises away from. MGI also attaches a GO:0003700 TAS to mouse Aff3 from this paper, which is an author-statement rather than a measurement.

title: LAF4, an AF4-related gene, is fused to MLL in infant acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
review_notes: Background for the description. Deliberately not used for any annotation - a translocation fusion protein's behaviour is not the wild-type protein's function, and no row in this review derives from a fusion.

title: Fusion of an AF4-related gene, LAF4, to MLL in childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia with t(2;11)(q11;q23).
review_notes: Background for the description, as for PMID:12203795. No annotation rests on it.

title: Identification of the novel AML1 fusion partner gene, LAF4, a fusion partner of MLL, in childhood T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia with t(2;21)(q11;q22) by bubble PCR method for cDNA.
review_notes: Background for the description, as for PMID:12203795. No annotation rests on it.

title: Visual pattern memory requires foraging function in the central complex of Drosophila.
review_notes: Not about AFF3, and cited only as the reference FlyBase attaches to lilli's GO:0007611 IMP, the second donor on AFF3's GO:0050877 row. The cached record is abstract-only and its title names a different gene, so what the full text assays for lilli was not checked; per campaign policy this is recorded as unverified rather than treated as a curation error.

title: Triangular tibia with fibular aplasia associated with a microdeletion on 2q11.2 encompassing LAF4.
review_notes: Sole support for the embryonic hindlimb morphogenesis IMP. A single case report, which would normally be weak, but PMID:25162227 independently confirms the deletion encompasses only AFF3, so it is not a contiguous-gene event. The same paper's mouse embryo in-situ was curated separately and correctly as IEP on mouse Aff3.

title: Investigation of rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility genes identifies association of AFF3 and CD226 variants with response to anti-tumour necrosis factor treatment.
review_notes: Correctly identified and internally consistent, but it does not support the annotation it is cited for. It is a pharmacogenetic association study - 18 tag SNPs genotyped in RA patients receiving TNF-blocking drugs, with change in DAS28 as the outcome - and it contains no TNF stimulus and no experiment on the AFF3 gene product. PubMed records an ErratumIn reference to Ann Rheum Dis 2011;70(8):1519 whose PubMed id is null; it could not be resolved through Crossref (empty relation/update-to/updated-by on the DOI) or Europe PMC (no hits for the journal, year and page, nor for a citing Published Erratum), so its scope is unestablished. The REMOVE verdict does not depend on it.

title: The little elongation complex regulates small nuclear RNA transcription.
review_notes: Not about AFF3. Source of Drosophila lilli's GO:0032783 IPI, the sole protein donor on AFF3's super elongation complex row. Recorded rather than leaned on, because AFF3's own human evidence for that row (PMID:22547686, PMID:26214578) is much stronger.

title: The super elongation complex family of RNA polymerase II elongation factors: gene target specificity and transcriptional output.
review_notes: The paper that defines AFF3 biochemically, and the single most under-used reference on this gene. Querying QuickGO by reference shows it has produced exactly one annotation in the whole of GOA - GO:0006354 EXP on UniProtKB:P51825, the paralogue AFF1 - so the paper whose headline result is the isolation of AFF3-containing SEC-L3 gave AFF3 nothing, and AFF3 receives the term back only as an IBA pointing at AFF1. Abstract-only in the cache; every claim used here is in the abstract.

title: FRA2A is a CGG repeat expansion associated with silencing of AFF3.
review_notes: Full text available. Establishes functional haploinsufficiency as a human mechanism and records the mouse embryonic expression domains - brain, somites and limb buds - that corroborate the limb annotation. No annotation rests on it alone.

title: Laf4/Aff3, a gene involved in intellectual disability, is required for cellular migration in the mouse cerebral cortex.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Two distinct uses. First, it is the only functional study of the gene in the nervous system and supports the proposed cerebral cortex cell migration row. Second, it independently establishes that the PMID:18616733 deletion encompasses only AFF3. Its ChIP result, which is the source of mouse Aff3's GO:0003700 IDA and hence of UniProt's Ensembl-projected GO:0003700 on human AFF3, is over-read by that annotation - the assay is ChIP-qPCR of over-expressed HA-tagged Laf4 at a single locus, and the authors themselves frame it as testing a potential direct transcriptional regulator.

title: Combined transcriptome studies identify AFF3 as a mediator of the oncogenic effects of β-catenin in adrenocortical carcinoma.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Despite a cancer-focused title it contains the best human cell-biological data on AFF3 - endogenous AFF3 immunoprecipitated from nuclear extracts brings down CDK9 and cyclin T1, with the reciprocal co-IP done on endogenous protein, and AFF3 colocalises with the speckle marker SC35. The speckle-disruption and CDK9 redistribution results are from strong over-production and are treated here as such, not as native-level observations.

title: A permissive chromatin state regulated by ZFP281-AFF3 in controlling the imprinted Meg3 polycistron.
review_notes: Full text available. Mouse embryonic stem cells, so ISS-grade for human, but it is the clearest statement of the mechanism that distinguishes AFF3 from AFF1 and AFF4 - AFF3 is recruited to specific regulatory elements by sequence-specific zinc-finger proteins rather than binding a motif itself. Used for the coregulator molecular function rather than for a new imprinting annotation.

title: AFF3 upregulation mediates tamoxifen resistance in breast cancers.
review_notes: Returned by the affinage record and read. A gain-of-function phenotype from AFF3 over-expression in a tumour context; it says what excess AFF3 can do, not what the normal protein does, so no term is proposed from it.

title: AFF3-DNA methylation interplay in maintaining the mono-allelic expression pattern of XIST in terminally differentiated cells.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Human throughout - HEK293T and IMR-90 - with shRNA knockdown, AFF3 ChIP-qPCR, ChIP-seq and MeDIP. Supplies the human evidence for direct, methylation-dependent binding of AFF3 to a defined CpG island and for transcriptional repression, and is the basis of the proposed negative-regulation row.

title: De novo AFF3 variant in a patient with mesomelic dysplasia with foot malformation.
review_notes: Abstract-only. The second, independent KINSSHIP family, reported before the syndrome was named, and one of the two references UniProt cites for the disease association. Cited here as corroboration that the limb phenotype recurs across unrelated patients rather than as support for any single row - the mesomelic dysplasia claim in the GO:0035116 review rests on PMID:18616733 and PMID:33961779.

title: Variants in the degron of AFF3 are associated with intellectual disability, mesomelic dysplasia, horseshoe kidney, and epileptic encephalopathy.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, and everything used here is in the abstract - the homozygous Aff3 knockout phenotype including kidney defects, and the knockin animals reproducing lower mesomelic limb deformities. Care is taken not to treat the KINSSHIP variants' consequences as AFF3's normal activity - they are degradation-resistance defects, so they establish that the gene is dosage-critical in limb and kidney development without licensing any claim about a new molecular function.

title: AFF3, a susceptibility factor for autoimmune diseases, is a molecular facilitator of immunoglobulin class switch recombination.
review_notes: Full text available. Mouse knockout plus switch-region binding by the AFF3 C-terminal domain and reduced AID recruitment, so ISS-grade for human. GO:0045190's own usage comment directs mechanism-level participants such as this to the process term rather than to the regulation branch, which is why isotype switching rather than positive regulation of isotype switching is proposed.

title: Loss of AR-regulated AFF3 contributes to prostate cancer progression and reduces ferroptosis sensitivity by downregulating ACSL4 based on single-cell sequencing analysis.
review_notes: Returned by the affinage record, which itself rates the finding low-confidence. Abstract-only, cancer-context, and a downstream transcriptional consequence rather than an AFF3 activity. No term proposed.

title: Variant-specific pathophysiological mechanisms of AFF3 differently influence transcriptome profiles.
review_notes: Full text available. Isogenic human lines carrying loss-of-function and KINSSHIP genotypes; supports the dosage-sensitivity framing and shows that both directions perturb a large fraction of AFF3-bound loci. Cited for interpretation rather than for a term.

title: A phenome-wide association study of methylated GC-rich repeats identifies a GCC repeat expansion in AFF3 associated with intellectual disability.
review_notes: Full text available. Population-scale human evidence that reduced AFF3 expression impairs neurodevelopment, which is what keeps the general nervous-system-process row standing on AFF3's own data rather than on its paralogues'.

title: LAF-4 encodes a lymphoid nuclear protein with transactivation potential that is homologous to AF-4, the gene fused to MLL in t(4;11) leukemias.
review_notes: The gene's founding paper and the only direct assay of the human protein's DNA binding. Abstract-only in the cache, and the abstract carries all three load-bearing statements used here - nuclear localisation by antibody staining, strong binding of in-vitro translated LAF-4 to double-stranded DNA cellulose, and transactivation by a GAL4 fusion. Read as a whole it supports a recruited coregulator rather than a sequence-specific transcription factor, because the transactivation was measured only when the protein was tethered by a heterologous DNA-binding domain.

title: Cloning and developmental expression of the murine homolog of the acute leukemia proto-oncogene AF4.
review_notes: Not about AFF3. Source of mouse Aff1's GO:0045893 IDA, one of the four donors on AFF3's GO:0006355 row. An earlier draft of this review cited it as evidence that the row's donors disagree in sign; that was wrong - GO:0045893 is positive and so are the other two signed donor terms - and the reason for keeping the row unsigned rests on the recipient instead.

title: AFF3 bioinformatics results - WITH/FROM resolution, donor evidence, ancestry checks, reference projection and automated-route provenance
review_notes: Hand-written interpretation of the committed scripts' machine-readable outputs (withfrom_resolution.json, reference_projection.json, corrections.json). Written by hand rather than generated so that a later regeneration cannot silently revert it, and the JSON rather than the prose is what a re-run reproduces.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AFF3 (human)
review_notes: Adjudicated and deliberately not quoted as evidence anywhere in this review; recorded here so the judgement lives in the repository. Its gates_passed True and faith_pct 100.0 concern PRECISION only - all 15 citations are well-formed numeric PMIDs with no preprint ids in PMID-shaped fields, and none of them is retracted or carries an expression of concern. They say nothing about recall, and recall was measured rather than estimated - the record omits PMID:22547686, the paper that isolated AFF3-containing SEC-L3 and that this review's sharpest finding turns on, and it omits both PMID:18616733 and PMID:20444755, the sole support for AFF3's only two experimental biological-process rows. So it returned the gene's notable literature and not the annotation-relevant literature, which is the same characterisation the ADIPOQ review reached. Its own GO grounding was also not imported - it offers GO:0140110 where GO:0003712 is the term AFF3's evidence actually supports.

title: UniProtKB entry P51826 (AFF3_HUMAN)
review_notes: Used for the PANTHER subfamily assignment, the unevidenced SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line that underlies the SL-0191 token, and the two Ensembl-projected GO cross-references that GOA does not carry.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The interpro2go route. Which signature supplies which term was measured rather than assumed: of AFF4's three InterPro signatures, IPR007797 maps to GO:0010468, IPR043640 maps to GO:0005634, and IPR043639 maps to nothing. No molecular-function term is produced by any of them.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Used for the euchromatin ISS row. The donor is mouse Aff4 (Q9ESC8), a genuine orthologue holding the term by its own IDA.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: All five IBA rows. Every protein donor named in their WITH/FROM fields was resolved and its own evidence for the propagated term queried; each row's chain contains at least one donor with its own experimental annotation, so no row rests on family-level inference alone.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SL-0468 Chromosome, which derives from the same UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statement (evidenced by PubMed:12065898) that the EXP row already records.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: The three HPA rows. HPA's own record grades nucleoplasm as the main location and fibrillar centre plus nuclear bodies as additional locations, which is the basis for grading the three rows differently.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Two rows with opposite outcomes. The euchromatin transfer comes from mouse Aff4's own IDA and is sound; the ER-stress transfer comes from a single rat IEP and is not.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: A combinatorial reference is only as independent as its tokens. Its three tokens here reduce to two witnesses: ARBA00026330 fires on the IPR007797+IPR043640 pair (one of its 1309 condition sets), IPR043640 separately carries its own interpro2go mapping to the same term, and SL-0191 derives from the PubMed:12065898 localisation that the EXP row already records.

title: Impaired conditioned fear and enhanced long-term potentiation in Fmr2 knock-out mice.
review_notes: Not an AFF4 paper. It is the donor evidence behind the nervous-system-process IBA, and it is an Aff2/Fmr2 knockout, i.e. a paralogue. Cited to make the paralogue origin of that row explicit.

title: MCEF, the newest member of the AF4 family of transcription factors involved in leukemia, is a positive transcription elongation factor-b-associated protein.
review_notes: The original identification of AFF4/MCEF as a P-TEFb-associated protein and the source of UniProt's nucleus and chromosome localisation statements. Cached copy is abstract-only, so the localisation claim is taken from UniProt's curated SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line rather than from the paper text.

title: Infertility with defective spermiogenesis in mice lacking AF5q31, the target of chromosomal translocation in human infant leukemia.
review_notes: The Aff4-null mouse. Establishes a requirement in Sertoli cells for spermiogenesis; annotated in GOA on mouse Aff4 only, and correctly so, since the experiment is a mouse knockout.

title: MCEF is localized to the nucleus by protein sequences encoded within three distinct exons, where it represses HIV-1 Tat-transactivation of LTR-directed transcription.
review_notes: Cited only for the exclusively nuclear localisation of an MCEF-EGFP fusion, which is a tagged-overexpression result and is used here only as corroboration of the compartment, not of a transcriptional direction. Its repression finding runs opposite to the activation reported elsewhere and is not relied on.

title: A higher-order complex containing AF4 and ENL family proteins with P-TEFb facilitates oncogenic and physiologic MLL-dependent transcription.
review_notes: Source of three of the protein-binding rows (CCNT1, MLLT1, MLLT3). A focused biochemical study, not a screen; the reference-projection test returns 12 annotations over 6 entities.

title: AFF4, a component of the ELL/P-TEFb elongation complex and a shared subunit of MLL chimeras, can link transcription elongation to leukemia.
review_notes: The paper that named AFF4 as an SEC component and showed AFF4 is required for SEC stability. It is cited nowhere in AFF4's GOA; the single annotation it has produced anywhere in GOA is GO:0032783 IDA on AFF1.

title: HIV-1 Tat and host AFF4 recruit two transcription elongation factors into a bifunctional complex for coordinated activation of HIV-1 transcription.
review_notes: Carries the sentence that licenses an adaptor molecular function for AFF4 itself rather than only for the complex - AFF4 mediates the ELL2-P-TEFb interaction in the absence of Tat. Has produced no GO annotation anywhere in GOA.

title: Human mediator subunit MED26 functions as a docking site for transcription elongation factors.
review_notes: Source of three protein-binding rows. A directed study (17 entities in the projection test), and its own subject is MED26 rather than AFF4, so it is treated as corroborating rather than establishing the SEC interactions.

title: Global landscape of HIV-human protein complexes.
review_notes: An AP-MS survey annotating 104 entities in the projection test, so the Tat row it supports is screen-scale on its own. The AFF4-Tat interaction is nonetheless real, established independently by crystallography.

title: The little elongation complex regulates small nuclear RNA transcription.
review_notes: Supports AFF4's transcription-elongation-factor-complex IDA and, via mouse Aff4, the euchromatin transfer. The reference-projection test was run and came back negative for subunit-projection: its GO:0008023 IDA reaches 16 entities, all genuine elongation-complex subunits, while its functional term GO:0042795 stays on the 7 ELL/ICE1 proteins actually perturbed and does not reach AFF4.

title: The ubiquitin ligase Siah1 controls ELL2 stability and formation of super elongation complexes to modulate gene transcription.
review_notes: The decisive reference for the SIAH1 row and the only measurement of a direct AFF4-SIAH1 interaction with purified proteins. Also maps AFF4's ELL2-binding region by deletion. Absent from the affinage record and cited nowhere in GOA, which carries no annotation at all from it.

title: Regulation of AMP-activated protein kinase signaling by AFF4 protein, member of AF4 (ALL1-fused gene from chromosome 4) family of transcription factors, in hypothalamic neurons.
review_notes: Included only in the literature-coverage census. No annotation in this review rests on it; the AMPK-alpha2 result is a single-laboratory overexpression and knockdown study that has not been independently replicated.

title: The super elongation complex family of RNA polymerase II elongation factors: gene target specificity and transcriptional output.
review_notes: Cited because it is the donor evidence behind the DNA-templated-transcription-elongation IBA, where it supplies human AFF1's own EXP annotation to that term.

title: The super elongation complex (SEC) family in transcriptional control.
review_notes: A review, used for framing only. No annotation action rests on it.
