title: HIV-1 Tat recruits transcription elongation factors dispersed along a flexible AFF4 scaffold.
review_notes: Establishes that the recruitment motifs are dispersed along the disordered AFF4 axis. Cached copy is abstract-only, so only what the title and abstract state is used.

title: The AFF4 scaffold binds human P-TEFb adjacent to HIV Tat.
review_notes: The AFF4-P-TEFb crystal structure, and the source of the interface-mutation result that ties cyclin T1 binding to AFF4-dependent transcription. Direct evidence about AFF4 itself, not about the complex.

title: AFF4 binding to Tat-P-TEFb indirectly stimulates TAR recognition of super elongation complexes at the HIV promoter.
review_notes: The quaternary Tat/P-TEFb/AFF4 structure, showing that Tat and AFF4 interact directly on the cyclin T1 surface. Its 30-fold figure describes the affinity of Tat-P-TEFb for TAR and is not used numerically here.

title: A single point mutation in cyclin T1 eliminates binding to Hexim1, Cdk9 and RNA but not to AFF4 and enforces repression of HIV transcription.
review_notes: Independent evidence that the AFF4 site on cyclin T1 is a distinct surface from the CDK9 and Hexim1 sites, which corroborates the crystallographic result by mutation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: The HuRI yeast two-hybrid screen and the sole GOA support for five partners. IntAct logs it as three sub-methods of one experiment per partner, which is what UniProt reports as NbExp=3. Four of the five partners have no other evidence anywhere; the fifth, SIAH1, does.

title: Germline gain-of-function mutations in AFF4 cause a developmental syndrome functionally linking the super elongation complex and cohesin.
review_notes: CHOPS syndrome. Read for the mechanism rather than the phenotype; it establishes that the disease variants resist SIAH1-directed degradation and accumulate, which is a statement about AFF4 dose and not about a new activity. Also the source of the chromatin co-occupancy of AFF4, cohesin and RNAP2.

title: Insights into HIV-1 proviral transcription from integrative structure and dynamics of the Tat:AFF4:P-TEFb:TAR complex.
review_notes: Adds TAR RNA to the complex and shows by hydrogen-deuterium exchange that AFF4 helix 2 is stabilised without contacting the RNA. Its 50-fold figure and the 30-fold figure of PMID:24843025 describe the same phenomenon measured by two groups, not two arms of one comparison; neither is used numerically here.

title: Structural basis for ELL2 and AFF4 activation of HIV-1 proviral transcription.
review_notes: The 2.0 A co-crystal of the ELL2 C-terminal domain with the AFF4 ELLBow. This is a measured binary interaction and it has never been curated - GOA carries no annotation from this reference and AFF4 has no ELL2 protein-binding row.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: A large affinity-purification map. Its projection test is uninformative (3731 annotations, entity count not derivable without sampling), so it is treated as corroborating an interaction established elsewhere rather than as independent support.

title: AFF1 and AFF4 differentially regulate the osteogenic differentiation of human MSCs.
review_notes: Added after review: the description previously asserted an osteogenic role for AFF4 whose only source in this PR was the affinage record, which is the one thing this campaign never relies on. The paper is strong - siRNA depletion of AFF4 in human MSCs inhibits osteogenic potential, overexpression enhances it, and it is tested in vivo by MSC-mediated bone formation - and it is the direct counterpart of PMID:37528066 for differentiation rather than elongation, since AFF1 does the opposite. It carries a 2020 erratum, PMID:32257529, and the erratum is narrow and specific: the second lane of Fig. 7b was mislabelled and should be siAFF4, the alpha-tubulin images in Figs. 6b and 7b were misused and have been replaced, and the authors state it does not affect any of their original conclusions. Both corrected panels are protein blots in the mechanism figures - Fig. 6b is the AFF1-to-DKK1 western and Fig. 7b the AFF4-to-ID1 western - and neither is among the differentiation or bone-formation assays the GO:0045669 row rests on. Marked VERIFIED on that basis. An earlier version of this review marked it DISPUTED solely because the scope appeared unknown; it was not unknown, and the reason that mistake was made is recorded in AFF4-notes.md.

title: Structure of the super-elongation complex subunit AFF4 C-terminal homology domain reveals requirements for AFF homo- and heterodimerization.
review_notes: The C-terminal homology domain structure, the homo- and heterodimerisation result, and the CDK9 substrate loop. Cached copy is abstract-only; its in vitro nucleic-acid binding is reported as suggested by fluorescence anisotropy and is deliberately not turned into an annotation here.

title: Fused in sarcoma silences HIV gene transcription and maintains viral latency through suppressing AFF4 gene activation.
review_notes: Independent corroboration that AFF4 occupies nuclear puncta, which is why the HPA nuclear-bodies row is kept rather than doubted. Its FUS-dependent regulation of AFF4 is not turned into an AFF4 annotation.

title: Genipin attenuates mitochondrial-dependent apoptosis, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and inflammation via the PI3K/AKT pathway in acute lung injury.
review_notes: Not an AFF4 paper. It is the sole evidence, by IEP, behind rat Aff4's ER-stress annotation, which Ensembl Compara then projected onto human AFF4. A drug-intervention study in a rat lung-injury model; the projection test shows it produces exactly one annotation on one entity in the whole of GOA. Marked LOW_QUALITY as support for the propagated term, not as a judgement on the paper's own subject.

title: Structural and functional insight into the effect of AFF4 dimerization on activation of HIV-1 proviral transcription.
review_notes: The second structure of the same C-terminal region, named THD here and CHD by PMID:31147444. Supplies the F1014A and Y1096A point mutants that make the homodimerisation call mutational rather than only crystallographic.

title: Correction to: AFF1 and AFF4 differentially regulate the osteogenic differentiation of human MSCs.
review_notes: The 2020 erratum for PMID:28955517, recorded because a correction that is not flagged is exactly the one that gets quoted back. Found by the committed retraction/erratum check, which reports 2 flagged references out of 32 rather than the 0 of 30 it reported before that reference was added. Its scope is narrow and stated in full in the cached record - the second lane of Fig. 7b was mislabelled and should be siAFF4, the alpha-tubulin images in Figs. 6b and 7b were misused and the correct images have been replaced, and the authors state it does not affect any of their original conclusions. Reading the source paper places both panels in the mechanism figures rather than in the assays this review annotates from, since Fig. 6b is the AFF1-to-DKK1 protein blot and Fig. 7b the AFF4-to-ID1 protein blot, so the alpha-tubulin loading controls are what was replaced. The mislabelled lane is the one AFF4-relevant detail and is named in the GO:0045669 row.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex. Projection test uninformative (9514 annotations); treated as corroboration only.

title: AFF4 regulates cellular adipogenic differentiation via targeting autophagy.
review_notes: The one AFF4 process paper that establishes both requirement and sufficiency (knockdown, overexpression, and an adipose-specific Aff4 knockout). Has produced no GO annotation anywhere in GOA.

title: Distinct roles of two SEC scaffold proteins, AFF1 and AFF4, in regulating RNA polymerase II transcription elongation.
review_notes: Separates AFF4 from AFF1 functionally and positionally, and shows that AFF4 loss slows elongation and causes early termination. The most directly relevant evidence for a Pol II-specific elongation annotation on AFF4 rather than a family-level one.

title: AFF4 globally affects the release of paused RNA polymerase II in HEL cells.
review_notes: The genome-wide knockdown result behind the proposed positive-regulation-of-elongation annotation. Cached copy is abstract-only, and the abstract states the Ser2-phosphorylation and pausing results directly, so nothing beyond it is asserted.

title: The phosphatase PP1 sustains global transcription by promoting RNA polymerase II pause release.
review_notes: UniProt curates AFF4 Ser-549 dephosphorylation by PNUTS-PP1 from this paper, but the cached copy is abstract-only and the abstract does not mention AFF4, so that claim is attributed to the UniProt curation and not quoted from the paper. In GOA the paper yields GO:0032968 IDA on the four PNUTS-PP1 components and nothing on AFF4.

title: Stabilization of AFF1 by PARylation ensures transcriptional restart after DNA damage.
review_notes: An AFF1 paper, cited for a curation-consistency point rather than for AFF4 biology - it is the source of AFF1's GO:0003711 IMP, which shows GO already accepts transcription elongation factor activity for an AFF scaffold.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Luck et al., Nature 2020, HuRI). This is a proteome-scale binary Y2H interactome map, not an AFMID-specific study; it is the source of the three GO:0005515 protein-binding IPI annotations (with MEI4, DDIT4L, MED18). High-throughput interactions with no established functional role for AFMID, hence LOW relevance.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The interpro2go route, and the source of the only molecular-function row in GOA. Which signature supplies the term was checked rather than assumed: of AGFG1's four InterPro signatures, only IPR001164 (the pan-ArfGAP catalytic-domain entry) maps to GO:0005096. The signature correctly identifies the conserved domain but cannot distinguish the AGFG subfamily, whose members examined here lack two of three residues required for efficient GAP catalysis; the AGFG-specific IPR052248 maps to no GO term. The row is therefore retained but marked as over-annotated rather than dismissed as a spurious domain match.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: All five IBA rows. Every protein donor named in their WITH/FROM fields was resolved and its own evidence for the propagated term queried; each row's chain contains at least one donor with its own experimental annotation at the exact term, so no row rests on family-level inference alone. The defect these rows do carry is node reach, not evidence quality - see the GO:0001675 entry.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SL-0191 Nucleus and SL-0088 Cytoplasmic vesicle, both of which derive from the same UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statement (evidenced by PubMed:10613896 and PubMed:7634337) that the EXP rows already record independently.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA00026971. All 2414 of the rule's condition sets were evaluated against AGFG1's own signature and taxon profile: exactly one fires, and it requires both FunFam 1.10.220.150:FF:000005 and FunFam 3.30.450.50:FF:000005, two FunFams named for AGFG1 itself. A second set mentioning IPR001164 does not fire because it also requires IPR051718, which AGFG1 does not have. So this is a gene-specific rule granting one location AGFG1 independently has by experiment.

title: The eps15 homology (EH) domain-based interaction between eps15 and hrb connects the molecular machinery of endocytosis to that of nucleocytosolic transport.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Supplies the nucleus and cytoplasmic-vesicle localisations, the EPS15/EPS15R interaction and its NPF/EH dependence, and - directly against the nuclear-pore row - the statement that AGFG1's status as an NPC constituent is not established.

title: Two closely related human nuclear export factors utilize entirely distinct export pathways.
review_notes: Cited for the AGFG1-NXF3 IPI row. Not retrievable (Europe PMC reports isOpenAccess N, inEPMC N, no PMC id), so the interaction's mechanism cannot be read. The reference-projection test argues it is considered curation rather than pipeline output: it annotates four proteins (AGFG1, NXF3, NXF1, XPO1) with five different terms. IntAct holds no record of the pair, consistent with a curator reading the paper directly.

title: Lack of acrosome formation in Hrb-deficient mice.
review_notes: The decisive orthologue phenotype and the basis of the acrosome-assembly IBA. Also the source of the mouse cytoplasmic-vesicle IDA. Absent from the affinage record.

title: hRIP, a cellular cofactor for Rev function, promotes release of HIV RNAs from the perinuclear region.
review_notes: Establishes that the export defect is specific to Rev-directed RNA and that bulk host poly(A)+ mRNA distribution is unaffected. This is the result that makes GO:0006406 mRNA export from nucleus the wrong branch for this gene.

title: The acroplaxome is the docking site of Golgi-derived myosin Va/Rab27a/b- containing proacrosomal vesicles in wild-type and Hrb mutant mouse spermatids.
review_notes: The donor evidence for both the acrosome-assembly and the intermediate-filament IBAs. It supports the latter specifically: the mutant acroplaxome retains F-actin but is deficient in keratin 5, an intermediate-filament protein.

title: The cellular HIV-1 Rev cofactor hRIP is required for viral replication.
review_notes: Corroborates the Rev-cofactor role with two independent ablation methods and a rescue, and adds that AGFG1 is not required for cell viability. Not cited by any GOA row.

title: Changes in intranuclear chromatin architecture induce bipolar nuclear localization of histone variant H1T2 in male haploid spermatids.
review_notes: This is the sole reference behind mouse Agfg1's GO:0007289 IMP, from which the human IBA descends, and its result for hrb is a NEGATIVE: H1T2 polar localisation is unaltered in hrb-null spermatids, which the authors use to argue that acrosome development is not required for nuclear polarity. The mouse spermatid nuclear phenotype (nucleopodes) is reported in PMID:14724135 instead, so the term is defensible for the orthologue but attached to the wrong reference.

title: Molecular basis for the sorting of the SNARE VAMP7 into endocytic clathrin-coated vesicles by the ArfGAP Hrb.
review_notes: The strongest molecular study on this gene and the basis for most of the proposed new annotations: cargo-binding region mapped to residues 136-176, ITC affinity, a crystal structure, reciprocal mutations that abolish binding on both sides, colocalisation with clathrin and AP-2 in coated pits and vesicles, and a depletion phenotype. In all of GOA it has produced only two annotations, both bare protein binding. Absent from the affinage record.

title: Consensus nomenclature for the human ArfGAP domain-containing proteins.
review_notes: The family reference, used for two opposite purposes. It supplies the published catalytic-spacing anchor (CX2CX16CX2CX4R) and ArfGAP1's residue numbers, which the motif scan reproduces as a positive control; and it supplies the disconfirming control, since it reports that the ADAP subfamily lacks in vitro GAP activity although ADAP1's motif is complete. Both clauses of that sentence are used: the same sentence also asserts, at subfamily level and without a citation, that at least one member of every non-ADAP subfamily - which includes AGFG - has demonstrated in vitro GAP activity. Its AGFG section names no such measurement for either paralogue, so the blanket clause is treated as raising the prior rather than as the evidence.

title: Role of HRB in clathrin-dependent endocytosis.
review_notes: Supports the clathrin-dependent-endocytosis role by knockdown, and is one of only two papers the affinage record returned. Marked DISPUTED because its generality is contested rather than because the paper is unsound: it reports transferrin uptake strongly reduced on HRB knockdown, while PMID:18775314 reports no effect of HRB depletion on EGF internalisation or degradation and reads AGFG1 as a SNARE-specific adaptor. Both results are recorded; this review does not adjudicate between them. The cache's Full Text section holds only page boilerplate, so only the abstract is used.

title: Distinct and separable activities of the endocytic clathrin-coat components Fcho1/2 and AP-2 in developmental patterning.
review_notes: An independent second laboratory classifying AGFG1 as a CLASP and showing concentration-dependent binding of Hrb to the FCHO1 mu-homology domain in HeLa lysates, with controls excluding an indirect, Asn-Pro-Phe-mediated route. The source of UniProt's FCHO1 SUBUNIT line, which has no GOA counterpart.

title: Ancient complexity, opisthokont plasticity, and discovery of the 11th subfamily of Arf GAP proteins.
review_notes: The paper that reverses this review's verdict on GO:0005096, and it was nearly missed: it was fetched, judged to be a family-classification paper with nothing resting on it, deleted before the first commit, and came back only through the concurrent AGFG2 review. Full text available and read. It names three catalytically required ASAP3 positions with the statement that mutating any one severely impairs activity, reports that only 2 of 40 AGFG sequences retain the aspartate and that the AGFG consensus uniquely lacks the tryptophan, and concludes that the AGFG subfamily is predicted to have lost substantial GAP activity while explicitly warning that this must not be confused with loss of Arf binding. Every claim used from it was re-measured here on AGFG1's own sequence with GAP-competent positive controls, rather than transferred from the paper's consensus analysis or from the sibling review.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: The HuRI yeast two-hybrid screen behind the POLE2 and NYAP2 rows. Correctly cited; the objection is evidence strength, not identity. Its projection test is uninformative by construction - it carries 24,599 annotations, too many to enumerate honestly - so no entity count is reported for it.

title: The temporally controlled expression of Drongo, the fruit fly homolog of AGFG1, is achieved in female germline cells via P-bodies and its localization requires functional Rab11.
review_notes: The donor evidence for the cytoplasm IBA: Drosophila drongo holds GO:0005737 by its own IDA from this paper. Cited to show that the cytoplasm row's chain is not empty of experimental evidence.

title: The ArfGAP Drongo Promotes Actomyosin Contractility during Collective Cell Migration by Releasing Myosin Phosphatase from the Trailing Edge.
review_notes: The only functional evidence anywhere that an AGFG-family GTPase-activating function matters in vivo, and it names a specific Arf class. Abstract-only, so what is used is the abstract's statement that the GTPase-activating function is essential; the assay that established it is not asserted here.

title: Arf GTPase-activating proteins SMAP1 and AGFG2 regulate the size of Weibel-Palade bodies and exocytosis of von Willebrand factor.
review_notes: Cited only for the paralogue argument. It gives AGFG2 its own characterised function in endothelial von Willebrand factor secretion and does not mention AGFG1 anywhere, which is what makes the spermatid terms reaching AGFG2 by IBA look like node over-reach rather than genuine shared biology.

title: Mapping the global interactome of the ARF family reveals spatial organization in cellular signaling pathways.
review_notes: The only human dataset placing AGFG1 in the ARF orbit, and it is proximity labelling rather than a GAP assay - evidence for association, not catalysis. Absent from GOA and from the affinage record. It supports retained Arf binding while leaving the catalytic prediction untested.

title: AGFG1 increases cholesterol biosynthesis by disrupting intracellular cholesterol homeostasis to promote PDAC progression.
review_notes: Recorded as an uncurated human result, not used to propose terms. A single cancer-cell study reporting a CAV1 interaction and altered cholesterol biosynthesis is not a basis for new process annotations here.

title: Identification of a novel cellular cofactor for the Rev/Rex class of retroviral regulatory proteins.
review_notes: A sound paper cited for two things it does not establish. Its own abstract has Rev binding the RNA and Rab/AGFG1 binding Rev's protein activation domain, so it cannot support GO:0003723 RNA binding; and the RNA it concerns is RRE-containing viral RNA, not host mRNA, so GO:0006406 mRNA export from nucleus reads more broadly than the evidence. The nucleus localisation it also carries is correct. This reference annotates exactly one entity in all of GOA, with three rows, which is the legacy ProtInc import signature.

title: A human nucleoporin-like protein that specifically interacts with HIV Rev.
review_notes: The abstract's nucleoporin claim is explicitly one of sequence homology, yet it is the sole support for GO:0005643 nuclear pore, a term whose definition asserts membership of the nuclear pore complex. A primary paper states outright that it is not certain whether AGFG1 is an authentic NPC constituent, and UniProt, curating this same paper, records Nucleus rather than nuclear envelope or nuclear pore. This reference annotates exactly one entity in all of GOA, with one row.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AGFG1 (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated provider record, gates_passed True, and its two citations (PMID:10613896 and PMID:18819912) are real and correctly quoted - so its precision is fine. Its recall is not, and that was measured rather than asserted: it returned neither of the two papers that decide this review (PMID:18775314, the VAMP7 structure and depletion phenotype, and PMID:11711676, the mouse null with no acrosome), nor PMID:18809720, the family reference supplying the catalytic-motif anchor, nor PMID:38606629, the only human dataset placing AGFG1 with ARF1/ARF3/ARF6. It also states the general clathrin-mediated-endocytosis requirement as settled when PMID:18775314 contradicts it for EGF. Cited here for exactly one thing: its explicit statement about the extent of its own corpus, used as a statement about that corpus and corroborated independently.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Standard GO_REF for InterPro2GO. Verified by looking up each of AGFG2's four InterPro entries separately and reading its go_terms field; the three that map to nothing are the control showing the pipeline is capable of restraint here.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Standard PAINT GO_REF. Node membership and per-node term donation were read from QuickGO by withFrom, fully paginated with a truncation assertion, and the taxon ids of the recipients were resolved to names rather than left as numbers.

title: The eps15 homology (EH) domain-based interaction between eps15 and hrb connects the molecular machinery of endocytosis to that of nucleocytosolic transport.
review_notes: Full text available and read in full around every sentence quoted. Titled for Hrb, but Hrbl is co-assayed throughout the functional experiments, which is exactly the pattern where a paper titled for a paralogue holds evidence about the gene under review. Care was taken to separate what was measured on Hrbl (Rev reporter, synergy, Rev levels) from what was measured only on Hrb (localisation, fractionation, the NPF-to-NPV mutant).

title: Lack of acrosome formation in Hrb-deficient mice.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, and nothing is asserted beyond the abstract. The annotation it supports on mouse Agfg1 is not disputed here; the review's objection is to propagating it to the paralogue AGFG2, not to the experiment.

title: The acroplaxome is the docking site of Golgi-derived myosin Va/Rab27a/b- containing proacrosomal vesicles in wild-type and Hrb mutant mouse spermatids.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; the quoted sentence and the authors' own interpretation of it are both in the abstract, and no claim is made about the full text.

title: Changes in intranuclear chromatin architecture induce bipolar nuclear localization of histone variant H1T2 in male haploid spermatids.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, and the abstract is about H1T2 localisation. The mouse Agfg1 IMP attributed to it was made by an MGI curator with the full text, so per project policy it is not second-guessed; the review's objection is to the transfer to AGFG2, not to the mouse annotation. Marked UNVERIFIED because the Hrb content cannot be read from what is cached, not because anything is suspected wrong.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: The citation is correct and the measurement is real; the limitation is what a subtractive membrane fraction can establish for a protein with no membrane-anchoring feature. Entity count derived as a distinct set of gene-product ids, not from the annotation total, with a non-zero positive control on the same endpoint.

title: Organization patterns of the AGFG genes: an evolutionary study.
review_notes: Cited by the affinage record as the source of a mammals-only claim. That claim is contradicted by PMID:23433073, which places the AGFG duplication among the subfamilies that duplicated at the base of vertebrates, and by a UniProt symbol census that finds agfg2 in 72 ray-finned fish (Actinopterygii), 23 sauropsids and 4 amphibians, with a non-zero agfg1 control in every clade. Aves is a subset of Sauropsida rather than a separate tally, and within it the asymmetry is striking: 1 avian agfg2 against 363 avian agfg1. A symbol census is a name-matching pipeline's output rather than an orthologue count, so it would not settle this alone; combined with the phylogenetic result it is enough. Consistently, the PANTHER node that reaches AGFG2 also reaches lamprey, hagfish and zebrafish. Marked LOW_QUALITY rather than MISCITED: the paper says what it is cited as saying, but its method cannot support the conclusion.

title: Ancient complexity, opisthokont plasticity, and discovery of the 11th subfamily of Arf GAP proteins.
review_notes: Full text available and read around each quotation. This is the reference that makes the GO:0005096 verdict a measurement rather than an assertion: it names a specific residue and a specific control protein (ASAP3 D484), which is what allowed the claim to be tested independently for human AGFG2. It is a prediction, not an assay, and the review says so; it is also the source of the effector hypothesis recorded under knowledge_gaps.

title: Genome-wide shRNA screening identifies host factors involved in early endocytic events for HIV-1-induced CD4 down-regulation.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Primary human-cell shRNA evidence for AGFG2 that has produced no annotation in GOA. Note that the affinage record's table row for the companion paper PMID:26701340 states AGFG2 knockdown raises CD4 in Vpu-expressing but not Nef-expressing cells; that is contradicted both by this paper's Nef-specific result and by the companion abstract's own dual-role conclusion, so the affinage row was not used.

title: The human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) Rev-binding protein (HRB) is a co-factor for HIV-1 Nef-mediated CD4 downregulation.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, and only the abstract is relied on. Titled for HRB (AGFG1) while carrying the decisive AGFG2 result, which is why a symbol-keyed search would not surface it. The affinage record's rendering of this paper - that AGFG2 knockdown raises CD4 in Vpu- but not Nef-expressing cells - misstates the abstract, which concludes a dual role in both; the affinage narrative section states it correctly, so the provider's own two summaries disagree.

title: The temporally controlled expression of Drongo, the fruit fly homolog of AGFG1, is achieved in female germline cells via P-bodies and its localization requires functional Rab11.
review_notes: Cited only to identify the donor evidence on the cytoplasm row; the drongo annotations were read from QuickGO, not from this paper. Abstract-only in the cache and nothing beyond the annotation attribution is claimed. Note that FB:FBgn0020304 resolves to seven UniProt entries, none reviewed, so the curated GO evidence is real but the entry name has no Swiss-Prot authority.

title: Arf GTPase-activating proteins SMAP1 and AGFG2 regulate the size of Weibel-Palade bodies and exocytosis of von Willebrand factor.
review_notes: Full text available and read in full. This paper decides the review, and the affinage record does not cite it despite gates_passed being true - a clean demonstration that a passing gate bounds precision and says nothing about recall. It was found by a PubMed query on ArfGAP activity terms crossed with the gene synonyms, not by the symbol alone.

title: Binding specificity and in vivo targets of the EH domain, a novel protein-protein interaction module.
review_notes: Cited only as UniProt reference 1 for the AGFG2 sequence and as the source PMID:10613896 attributes the Hrbl-EH interaction to. Full text is not available from PMC even after a forced re-fetch, so the AGFG2-specific content is taken on PMID:10613896's word and flagged as such rather than asserted.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for AGK ceramide kinase activity
review_notes: The report's central conclusion is consistent with direct human AGK enzymology, the independent ceramide-kinase follow-up, and GOA source tracing to PANTHER:PTN008994514.

title: Molecular cloning and nucleotide sequence of cDNA encoding human muscle glycogen debranching enzyme.
review_notes: PubMed-verified cloning of the human muscle debranching enzyme cDNA; establishes AGL as a single multifunctional polypeptide (~172 kDa). Cited by GOA for the "isoamylase complex" component, which is not supported by this paper.

title: A role for AGL ubiquitination in the glycogen storage disorders of Lafora and Cori's disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; directly about human AGL. Establishes cytoplasmic localization (IDA), condition-dependent nuclear relocalization during glycogenolysis, and interaction with malin/NHLRC1 (E3 ligase) regulating AGL stability via ubiquitination.

title: The carbohydrate-binding domain of overexpressed STBD1 is important for its stability and protein-protein interactions.
review_notes: Full-text verified; primarily about STBD1 but documents a direct physical interaction between STBD1 and endogenous GDE/AGL (co-IP and GST pull-down), supporting the AGL protein-binding IPI to O95210.

title: Glycogen debranching enzyme: purification, antibody characterization, and immunoblot analyses of type III glycogen storage disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; purification and immunochemical characterization of the glycogen debranching enzyme and its deficiency in type III GSD, underpinning the experimental MF annotations (EC 2.4.1.25 and EC 3.2.1.33). Abstract-only in cache.

title: Let-7a-regulated translational readthrough of mammalian AGO1 generates a microRNA pathway inhibitor.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (EMBO J 2019). The paper whose readthrough quantification is directly challenged by PMID:40500330. Listed as DISPUTED for that reason, not because the AGO1x proteoform is shown not to exist - the ribosome-profiling, mass-spectrometry and antibody evidence here is orthogonal to the dual-luciferase measurement and was not addressed by the 2025 Letter. No GOA annotation on AGO1 derives from this paper.

title: Prevention of dsRNA-induced interferon signaling by AGO1x is linked to breast cancer cell proliferation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (EMBO J 2020). Independent of the Eswarappa laboratory, so AGO1x is not a single-group claim. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than VERIFIED or DISPUTED because its AGO1x-dependent conclusions inherit whatever uncertainty attaches to the existence of the proteoform, and PMID:40500330 does not address this paper's evidence either way. No GOA annotation on AGO1 derives from it.

title: Transcript-specific induction of stop codon readthrough using a CRISPR-dCas13 system.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (EMBO Rep 2024). Method paper; AGO1 appears as a test substrate. Named alongside PMID:31330067 in PMID:40500330. Not relevant to any AGO1 GO annotation.

title: The dual luciferase assay does not support claims of stop codon readthrough on the AGO1 mRNA.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (EMBO J 2025; Letter/Comment on EMBO J 2019;38:e100727). Full text cached. Scope is narrow and should not be overstated - it challenges the dual-luciferase quantification in PMID:31330067 and PMID:38499809, and does not address the ribosome-profiling, mass-spectrometry or antibody evidence, nor the independent AGO1x work in PMID:32812257. No published reply was indexed in PubMed as of this review.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for AGO4 GO:0004521
review_notes: Focused OpenScientist report directly evaluates the GO:0004521 IBA and supports removal as AGO2/AGO3 paralog over-propagation onto slicer-dead AGO4.

title: Enzymatic activity of naturally occurring 1-acylglycerol-3-phosphate-O-acyltransferase 2 mutants associated with congenital generalized lipodystrophy.
review_notes: Directly on AGPAT2; supports the core MF via CGL-mutant enzymology. Abstract-only cache.

title: The microsomal cardiolipin remodeling enzyme acyl-CoA lysocardiolipin acyltransferase is an acyltransferase of multiple anionic lysophospholipids.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache is about ALCAT1; the AGPAT2 IDA rests on full text the curator read. Function (GO:0003841) is the correct core MF, so annotation accepted deferring to curator.

title: Human 1-acylglycerol-3-phosphate O-acyltransferase isoforms 1 and 2: biochemical characterization and inability to rescue hepatic steatosis in Agpat2(-/-) gene lipodystrophic mice.
review_notes: Primary source for AGPAT2 enzymology and ER membrane localization (EXP). Abstract-only cache.

title: Cloning and expression of two human lysophosphatidic acid acyltransferase cDNAs that enhance cytokine-induced signaling responses in cells.
review_notes: Original cloning/characterization of LPAAT-beta (AGPAT2). The cytokine claim is an overexpression correlation and underpins the over-annotated cytokine terms. Abstract-only cache.

title: Human lysophosphatidic acid acyltransferase. cDNA cloning, expression, and localization to chromosome 9q34.3.
review_notes: Original human AGPAT2 cloning and direct enzymatic demonstration. Abstract-only cache.

title: Characterization of a human lysophosphatidic acid acyltransferase that is encoded by a gene located in the class III region of the human major histocompatibility complex.
review_notes: Paper's primary subject is the AGPAT1 paralog (hLPAATalpha), not AGPAT2; cited as a family-level NAS. Function assignment is correct at family level. Abstract-only cache.

title: Synthesis of PA
review_notes: Reactome PA-synthesis pathway; supports the core BP.

title: Exocytosis of specific granule membrane proteins
review_notes: Bulk neutrophil-degranulation pathway propagation; the resulting plasma-membrane / specific-granule-membrane locations do not fit an ER enzyme.

title: 1-acyl LPA is acylated to PA by AGPAT (LPAAT)
review_notes: Reactome reaction for AGPAT-mediated LPA-to-PA at ER membrane; supports core MF and location.

title: In vitro processing of the human alkyl-dihydroxyacetonephosphate synthase precursor.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Directly supports peroxisomal localization (IDA) and PTS2-dependent import/processing of human AGPS; also supports the alkyl-DHAP synthase activity annotation. Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false).

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified high-throughput NK-cell membrane proteome; AGPS is one of ~1843 proteins identified. Supports only the generic "membrane" HDA annotation, which is an over-annotation relative to the specific peroxisomal membrane localization.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified muscle mitochondrial phosphoproteome. AGPS is peroxisomal; its appearance in an isolated-mitochondria preparation most plausibly reflects peroxisome co-fractionation, so the mitochondrion HDA annotation is treated as an over-annotation.

title: PEX14 is required for microtubule-based peroxisome motility in human cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Study of PEX14/peroxisomal membrane complexes; AGPS was identified as a peroxisomal-membrane-associated protein (HDA), consistent with its peroxisomal membrane localization.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: PubMed-verified systematic binary interactome map. Source of an IPI protein-binding annotation for the AGPS-GORASP1 (Q9BQQ3) interaction, which is also in the curated UniProt INTERACTION record. Uninformative "protein binding"; interaction's role in AGPS function is unclear.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: PubMed-verified variant-interaction screen. Source of an IPI protein-binding annotation for AGPS-GORASP1 (Q9BQQ3). Bare "protein binding"; functional relevance to AGPS not established.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified HuRI reference binary interactome. Source of an IPI protein-binding annotation for AGPS-GORASP1 (Q9BQQ3). Uninformative "protein binding" term.

title: Ether lipid synthesis: purification and identification of alkyl dihydroxyacetone phosphate synthase from guinea-pig liver.
review_notes: PubMed-verified original purification of alkyl-DHAP synthase (guinea-pig liver ortholog); one of the two ECO:0000269 sources UniProt cites for EC 2.5.1.26 and FUNCTION. Establishes the core enzymatic activity. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Alkyl-dihydroxyacetonephosphate synthase. Fate in peroxisome biogenesis disorders and identification of the point mutation underlying a single enzyme deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Key human AGPS paper: peroxisomal/PTS2 localization, ether phospholipid biosynthesis role, and the R419H RCDP3 loss-of-activity mutation. Second ECO:0000269 source UniProt cites for EC 2.5.1.26/FUNCTION. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Flux of the L-serine metabolism in rabbit, human, and dog livers. Substantial contributions of both mitochondrial and peroxisomal serine:pyruvate/alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes AGT/SPT dual role in glyoxylate and serine metabolism and supports the EC 2.6.1.51 serine:pyruvate transaminase activity.

title: Functional synergism between the most common polymorphism in human alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase and four of the most common disease-causing mutations.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; purified recombinant AGT is a folded, dimerized, catalytically active enzyme; documents cofactor and mistargeting biology.

title: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 in the Canary Islands: a conformational disease due to I244T mutation in the P11L-containing alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text; AGXT*LTM colocalises with peroxisomal marker PMP70 and L11P/I244T causes loss of enzymatic activity.

title: Crystal structure of alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase and the relationship between genotype and enzymatic phenotype in primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; crystal structure of the AGT homodimer with PLP at Lys209 and amino-oxyacetic acid inhibitor.

title: Overexpression of human alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase in Escherichia coli: renaturation from guanidine-HCl and affinity for pyridoxal phosphate co-factor.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; determines KM for PLP by apoenzyme reconstitution, supporting the PLP-binding annotation.

title: Peroxisomal import of human alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase requires ancillary targeting information remote from its C terminus.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; shows human AGT interacts with Pex5p and requires ancillary PTS1A targeting information (basis of the Pex5p IPI annotation).

title: Consequences of missense mutations for dimerization and turnover of alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase: study of a spectrum of mutations.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; spectrum of PH1 missense mutations characterized for activity and dimerization (dimerization failure frequent).

title: Identification of mutations associated with peroxisome-to-mitochondrion mistargeting of alanine/glyoxylate aminotransferase in primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; defines the P11L/G170R mistargeting biology and describes AGT as the normally peroxisomal enzyme.

title: Human wild-type alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase and its naturally occurring G82E variant: functional properties and physiological implications.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; kinetic characterization concluding AGT is highly specific for glyoxylate-to-glycine processing; PLP binding (2 mol/dimer).

title: Reactions of human liver peroxisomal alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase with beta-chloro-L-alanine and L-cysteine: spectroscopic and kinetic analysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; documents amino-acid (substrate) binding and in vitro L-cysteine side reactions (basis of the amino acid binding and L-cysteine catabolic annotations).

title: Molecular defects of the glycine 41 variants of alanine glyoxylate aminotransferase associated with primary hyperoxaluria type I.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; G41 variants increase the dimer-monomer dissociation constant and reduce coenzyme binding (supports homodimerization and PLP binding).

title: The N-terminal extension is essential for the formation of the active dimeric structure of liver peroxisomal alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; N-terminal extension required for the active dimer; confirms peroxisomal targeting and PLP dependence.

title: Molecular requirements for peroxisomal targeting of alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase as an essential determinant in primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text; crystal structure of the Pex5p-(AGT)2-Pex5p cargo-receptor complex; basis of the PEX5 protein-binding IPI.

title: Four of the most common mutations in primary hyperoxaluria type 1 unmask the cryptic mitochondrial targeting sequence of alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase encoded by the polymorphic minor allele.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text; establishes that failure to transaminate glyoxylate to glycine in peroxisomes lets glyoxylate be oxidised to oxalate.

title: Human peroxisomal L-alanine: glyoxylate aminotransferase. Evolutionary loss of a mitochondrial targeting signal by point mutation of the initiation codon.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; human AGT lost the ancestral mitochondrial targeting signal via an initiation-codon point mutation, explaining peroxisomal localization.

title: Gly161 mutations associated with Primary Hyperoxaluria Type I induce the cytosolic aggregation and the intracellular degradation of the apo-form of alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; wild-type AGT is peroxisomal, Gly161 mutants aggregate in cytosol; supports peroxisome localization and catalytic activity.

title: Misfolding caused by the pathogenic mutation G47R on the minor allele of alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase and chaperoning activity of pyridoxine.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; G47R-Mi is partly mistargeted to mitochondria and rescued to peroxisomes by pyridoxine; supports peroxisome localization and activity.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; proteome-scale HuRI Y2H map. AGXT protein-binding hits are mostly keratins/keratin-associated proteins with no established relationship to AGT function; over-annotated as bare protein binding.

title: Immunocytochemical localization of human hepatic alanine: glyoxylate aminotransferase in control subjects and patients with primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; AGT confined to peroxisomes, randomly dispersed through the peroxisomal matrix (supports peroxisome/peroxisomal matrix).

title: Peroxisomal alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase deficiency in primary hyperoxaluria type I.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; complete absence of peroxisomal AGT in PH1 liver; foundational for the peroxisomal enzyme deficiency model.

title: Evolution of alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase 1 peroxisomal and mitochondrial targeting. A survey of its subcellular distribution in the livers of various representatives of the classes Mammalia, Aves and Amphibia.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; in human liver essentially all AGT is peroxisomal (type I), with species-dependent compartmentalization.

title: Immunocytochemical localization of peroxisomal proteins in human liver and kidney.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; methods paper localizing peroxisomal proteins including AGT in human liver.

title: Human alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase 2 lowers asymmetric dimethylarginine and protects from inhibition of nitric oxide production.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes human AGXT2 as a mitochondrial enzyme that metabolises ADMA and protects endothelial NO production; foundational for the localization and methylarginine/NO annotations. Abstract-only in cache; localization and NO-protection quotes taken verbatim from the abstract.

title: Alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase 2 (AGXT2) polymorphisms have considerable impact on methylarginine and β-aminoisobutyrate metabolism in healthy volunteers.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Directly assays human AGXT2 activity on BAIB and SDMA and characterizes the activity-reducing p.Val140Ile variant; supports the BAIB/methylarginine transaminase and alanine:glyoxylate transaminase annotations.

title: Kidney and liver are the main organs of expression of a key metabolic enzyme alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase 2 in humans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Immunohistochemistry and double immunofluorescence establish AGXT2 protein expression in human kidney convoluted tubule and liver hepatocytes and its mitochondrial localization.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified high-confidence mitochondrial proteome; supports the HTP mitochondrion localization. AGXT2 is one of thousands of proteins in the dataset, so it is corroborating rather than gene-specific.

title: Mitochondrial AGXT2 tetramer transaminates glyoxylate and alanine to glycine and pyruvate
review_notes: Reactome reaction for AGXT2 in the mitochondrial matrix; notes that most in vivo glyoxylate-to-glycine flux is peroxisomal (AGXT) and the physiological role of the AGXT2 reaction is uncertain, useful context for weighting the glyoxylate BP annotations.

title: Substrate binding stabilizes S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase in a closed conformation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; IDA basis for GO:0004013 and UniProt FUNCTION/CATALYTIC ACTIVITY. Characterizes substrate-induced closed conformation of the homotetramer.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Large-scale exosome proteomics; AHCY detected among ~1132 proteins. Supports HDA exosome localization but not a functional secreted role.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: Large-scale B-cell exosome proteomics (539 proteins). Supports HDA exosome detection only.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Large-scale prostatic-secretion urinary exosome proteomics. Supports HDA exosome detection only.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale binary interactome map; source of bare "protein binding" IPI. No specific functional AHCY interaction defined.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome-perturbation study; source of bare "protein binding" IPI.

title: Sequence of full length cDNA for human S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase.
review_notes: Original human AHCY full-length cDNA report; TAS basis for GO:0004013.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome study; source of bare "protein binding" IPI.

title: Mutations in S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase (AHCY) affect its nucleocytoplasmic distribution and capability to interact with S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase-like 1 protein.
review_notes: AHCY-specific study; EXP basis for nucleus/ER localization and for the AHCYL1 interaction and disease-variant nucleocytoplasmic effects.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Large-scale variant/interaction study; source of bare "protein binding" IPI.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Reference binary interactome (HuRI); source of bare "protein binding" IPI.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale affinity-MS interactome; source of bare "protein binding" IPI.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous-tagging IP-MS/imaging resource; source of bare "protein binding" IPI.

title: AHCY:NAD+ tetramer hydrolyses AdoHcy
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the core AHCY activity; TAS basis for cytosol localization.

title: Defective AHCY does not hydrolyse AdoHcy
review_notes: Reactome reaction capturing loss of AHCY activity in HMAHCHD; TAS basis for cytosol.

title: Characterization of a novel variant (S145C/L311V) of 3alpha-hydroxysteroid/dihydrodiol dehydrogenase in human liver.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports 3alpha-HSD/dihydrodiol dehydrogenase activity of the human liver enzyme and the L311V/S145C polymorphism noted in UniProt.

title: Human 3alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase isoforms (AKR1C1-AKR1C4) of the aldo-keto reductase superfamily: functional plasticity and tissue distribution reveals roles in the inactivation and formation of male and female sex hormones.
review_notes: Abstract-only but foundational characterization of the four AKR1C 3alpha-HSDs including AKR1C4 substrate specificity and tissue distribution.

title: Human types 1 and 3 3 alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases: differential lability and tissue distribution.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports liver-exclusive expression and 3alpha-HSD activity (including bile-acid-precursor role).

title: Human cytosolic 3alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases of the aldo-keto reductase superfamily display significant 3beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activity: implications for steroid hormone metabolism and action.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports the 3beta-HSD activity and the in-vivo reductive directionality of AKR1C4.

title: Human cytosolic hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases of the aldo-ketoreductase superfamily catalyze reduction of conjugated steroids: implications for phase I and phase II steroid hormone metabolism.
review_notes: Full text available; establishes AKR1C4 as the dominant, most efficient hepatic 3-keto reductase for free and conjugated DHT.

title: AKR1C isoforms represent a novel cellular target for jasmonates alongside their mitochondrial-mediated effects.
review_notes: The paper shows jasmonate INHIBITION of AKR1C enzymes (drug-target relationship), so its use to support a "cellular response to jasmonic acid stimulus" process annotation is a misinterpretation.

title: Naturally occurring variants of human aldo-keto reductases with reduced in vitro metabolism of daunorubicin and doxorubicin.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports AKR1C4 anthracycline (doxorubicin/daunorubicin) carbonyl-reductase drug metabolism.

title: Why boys will be boys: two pathways of fetal testicular androgen biosynthesis are needed for male sexual differentiation.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports the SRXY8 disease-modifier role and AKR1C4's 3alpha-HSD activity in the backdoor pathway.

title: Retinaldehyde is a substrate for human aldo-keto reductases of the 1C subfamily.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports retinaldehyde (retinoid) reductase activity as a minor AKR1C4 function.

title: Isolation and characterization of cloned cDNAs encoding human liver chlordecone reductase.
review_notes: Abstract-only; cloning of the human liver chlordecone reductase (= AKR1C4), supports chlordecone reductase activity.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Abstract-only; a bulk proteomic exosome catalog. Correctly cited but not evidence of a functional extracellular localization for this cytosolic liver enzyme.

title: Purification and characterization of chlordecone reductase from human liver.
review_notes: Abstract-only; direct purification/characterization of chlordecone reductase (= AKR1C4).

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome screen; supports generic protein-binding annotations but not a specific molecular function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome screen; supports generic protein-binding annotations but not a specific molecular function.

title: Substrate specificity, gene structure, and tissue-specific distribution of multiple human 3 alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases.
review_notes: Abstract-only; establishes AKR1C4 (type 1 3alpha-HSD) DHT/3alpha-diol interconversion and liver-restricted expression.

title: Molecular cloning of two human liver 3 alpha-hydroxysteroid/dihydrodiol dehydrogenase isoenzymes that are identical with chlordecone reductase and bile-acid binder.
review_notes: Abstract-only; cloning identity of AKR1C4 with chlordecone reductase. Note the "bile-acid binder" is the related DD2 isoenzyme; the transporter/transport GO annotations attached to this reference over-interpret binding.

title: Molecular cloning of multiple cDNAs encoding human enzymes structurally related to 3 alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cloning paper; supports the general steroid-metabolism annotation.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 proteome-scale AP-MS interactome; source of a bare protein binding IPI (interactor AKR1C1). Correctly cited but low relevance to AKR1D1's molecular function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 proteome-scale AP-MS interactome; source of a bare protein binding IPI (interactor AKR1C1). Correctly cited but low relevance to AKR1D1's molecular function.

title: Cloning and expression of cDNA of human delta 4-3-oxosteroid 5 beta-reductase and substrate specificity of the expressed enzyme.
review_notes: Seminal cloning/expression/characterization paper (abstract only in cache). Establishes the 5-beta-reductase activity, cytosolic localization, and the dominant bile acid biosynthetic role. Multiple experimental GOA annotations trace to it.

title: Synthesis and structure based optimization of novel Akt inhibitors.
review_notes: Medicinal-chemistry structure-based optimization of pyrrolopyrimidine Akt inhibitors whose X-ray co-crystal structures with the AKT1 kinase domain (PDB 3CQU/3CQW) resolve the kinase active site and ATP pocket, confirming the kinase domain/ATP-binding site without characterizing physiological substrate phosphorylation.

title: The molecular mechanism of lead inhibition of human porphobilinogen synthase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; on human PBGS. Establishes 8 Zn(II)/homo-octamer, 4 required for activity, catalytic role of the cysteine-rich ZnB site, and the mechanism of lead inhibition (Pb interacts with ZnA and ZnB ligands). Source of the IDA porphobilinogen synthase activity, zinc ion binding, heme B/heme biosynthesis, and EXP lead ion binding annotations. Abstract-only in cache; full text was read by the curators.

title: Control of tetrapyrrole biosynthesis by alternate quaternary forms of porphobilinogen synthase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; human PBGS crystal structures. Establishes the octamer (predominant) vs hexamer (F12L allele) quaternary equilibrium and allosteric Mg2+ site. Supports the EXP porphobilinogen synthase activity annotation.

title: Allosteric inhibition of human porphobilinogen synthase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Confirms human PBGS catalyzes the first common step in tetrapyrrole biosynthesis, the octamer/hexamer/dimer equilibrium, ALAD porphyria and lead poisoning as low-activity disease states. Supports EXP porphobilinogen synthase activity.

title: delta-Aminolevulinate dehydratase deficient porphyria: identification of the molecular lesions in a severely affected homozygote.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; identifies G133R/V275M lesions causing severe ALAD-deficiency porphyria and describes ALAD as the heme biosynthetic enzyme active as a homooctamer. Cited (TAS) for catalytic activity; here used to support heme biosynthesis/disease context.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: High-throughput sperm-nucleus proteomics; supports only an HDA nucleus localization for an abundant cytosolic enzyme. Not indicative of a nuclear function.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; supports only an HDA extracellular-exosome localization. Bystander detection of an abundant cytosolic protein.

title: Human delta-aminolevulinate dehydratase: nucleotide sequence of a full-length cDNA clone.
review_notes: cDNA cloning of human ALA-D (porphobilinogen synthase, EC 4.2.1.24), the second enzyme in the heme biosynthetic pathway; a zinc metalloenzyme with a Cys/His-rich zinc site. Cited (TAS) for porphobilinogen synthase activity.

title: Molecular cloning of a cDNA for human delta-aminolevulinate dehydratase.
review_notes: cDNA cloning of human ALA-D (EC 4.2.1.24), the second enzyme in the heme biosynthetic pathway. Cited (TAS) for heme biosynthetic process.

title: 240-kDa proteasome inhibitor (CF-2) is identical to delta-aminolevulinic acid dehydratase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; identifies the 240-kDa proteasome inhibitor CF-2 as identical to ALAD (the second enzyme of heme synthesis), a gene-sharing/moonlighting activity. Supports the CAFA IDA porphobilinogen synthase, proteasome inhibition, and homooligomer annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: ALAD condenses 2 dALAs to form PBG
review_notes: Reactome reaction: ALAD catalyzes the asymmetric condensation of two ALA molecules to form porphobilinogen; active form is a Zn2+ homo-octamer. Directly describes the core catalytic step.

title: Heme biosynthesis
review_notes: Reactome pathway: eight-enzyme heme biosynthesis; the cytosolic steps (which include the ALAD-catalyzed condensation of 2 ALA to PBG) follow the mitochondrial ALA synthase step. Supports heme biosynthetic process and cytosol.

title: ALAD binds to Pb2+
review_notes: Reactome reaction: lead binds ALAD, displacing half the essential zinc ions and inactivating the enzyme; ALAD is a principal molecular target of lead. Supports lead ion binding.

title: Exocytosis of secretory granule lumen proteins
review_notes: Reactome neutrophil-degranulation reaction; ALAD is a cargo protein detected in granule/secretory proteomes. Supports only bystander extracellular/granule localization, not a secreted function.

title: Exocytosis of ficolin-rich granule lumen proteins
review_notes: Reactome neutrophil-degranulation reaction; ALAD detected in ficolin-1-rich granule proteomes. Supports only bystander extracellular/granule localization.

title: UniProtKB entry P13716 (HEM2_HUMAN), Delta-aminolevulinic acid dehydratase
review_notes: Curated UniProt record documenting catalytic activity (EC 4.2.1.24, RHEA:24064), Zn2+ cofactor, octamer/hexamer subunit equilibrium, cytosolic localization, lead inhibition, and ALAD-deficiency porphyria variants.

title: Interaction between succinyl CoA synthetase and the heme-biosynthetic enzyme ALAS-E is disrupted in sideroblastic anemia.
review_notes: Identifies the ALAS2 (ALAS-E) interaction with SUCLA2 (SCS-betaA) and its mitochondrial localization; supports substrate-supply and localization claims.

title: The major splice variant of human 5-aminolevulinate synthase-2 contributes significantly to erythroid heme biosynthesis.
review_notes: Isoform characterization; establishes functional enzyme, transit-peptide-driven mitochondrial import, and SUCLA2 interaction for human ALAS2.

title: Erythroid-specific 5-aminolevulinate synthase protein is stabilized by low oxygen and proteasomal inhibition.
review_notes: Establishes oxygen-dependent ALAS2 protein stability and vHL interaction; basis for the hypoxia/oxygen-homeostasis annotations (regulatory, not core).

title: Human erythroid 5-aminolevulinate synthase: promoter analysis and identification of an iron-responsive element in the mRNA.
review_notes: Original human erythroid ALAS characterization; IRE, erythroid promoter elements, and the first-step-of-heme-synthesis claim.

title: New mutation in erythroid-specific delta-aminolevulinate synthase as the cause of X-linked sideroblastic anemia responsive to pyridoxine.
review_notes: Functional assay of the K156E XLSA variant showing decreased ALAS2 activity; supports the IMP synthase-activity annotation.

title: Sideroblastic anemia: molecular analysis of the ALAS2 gene in a series of 29 probands and functional studies of 10 missense mutations.
review_notes: Expression and enzyme assays of 10 XLSA missense mutants; supports the IMP synthase-activity annotation.

title: ALAS2 acts as a modifier gene in patients with congenital erythropoietic porphyria.
review_notes: Characterizes the Y586F C-terminal gain-of-function variant with increased ALA release; supports the IMP synthase-activity annotation and C-terminal regulation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Large-scale binary interactome (Y2H) reporting an ALAS2-BANP interaction; basis for a generic protein binding IPI with no established functional significance.

title: Human aminolevulinate synthase structure reveals a eukaryotic-specific autoinhibitory loop regulating substrate binding and product release.
review_notes: Human ALAS2 crystal structure, PLP/active-site details, homodimer, kinetics, and C-terminal autoinhibitory loop; strongest structural/mechanistic reference.

title: The immunometabolite itaconate inhibits heme synthesis and remodels cellular metabolism in erythroid precursors.
review_notes: Enzymatic assay of recombinant ALAS2 with itaconyl-CoA competitive inhibition; supports the EXP synthase-activity annotation and rate-limiting-step framing.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteome (MitoCoP) including ALAS2; corroborates mitochondrial localization.

title: ALAS condenses SUCC-CoA and Gly to form dALA
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the ALAS2-catalyzed condensation in the mitochondrial matrix; supports the TAS matrix-location annotation.

title: UniProtKB P22557 (HEM0_HUMAN) 5-aminolevulinate synthase, erythroid-specific, mitochondrial
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; source for catalytic reaction, cofactor, subcellular location, family, and isoform annotations.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline. Recovers the two catalytic activities and ATP binding, but also transfers generic parents (catalytic/kinase/oxidoreductase activity) and a family-driven cytoplasm localization that is misleading for this mitochondrial-matrix protein.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/IBA pipeline; correctly recovers the mitochondrial localization and the C-terminal dehydrogenase catalytic activity.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt SubCell mapping correctly yields mitochondrion and mitochondrial matrix.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: HPA immunofluorescence supports the core mitochondrial localization.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara transfer from a rat ortholog; yields a weak "response to temperature stimulus" process and an imprecise "mitochondrial membrane" localization for a matrix enzyme.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learning assignment of the generic "amino acid biosynthetic process" parent.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined IEA (ARBA/InterPro/RHEA/EC/UniPathway) correctly assigns both catalytic activities and the L-proline biosynthetic process.

title: Hyperammonemia with reduced ornithine, citrulline, arginine and proline: a new inborn error caused by a mutation in the gene encoding delta(1)-pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache (full_text_available: false), but the abstract directly assays human P5CS catalytic activity (R84Q loss of function) and establishes the proline/ornithine/citrulline/arginine deficiency phenotype; supports the catalytic MF and biosynthetic BP annotations.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: Large-scale mRNA-interactome capture; supports the HDA RNA-binding call as a genuine but non-core moonlighting observation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Systematic binary (Y2H-type) interactome map; source of generic IntAct "protein binding" interactions (AGTRAP, CMTM5) with no ALDH18A1-specific functional interpretation.

title: ALDH18A1 gene mutations cause dominant spastic paraplegia SPG9: loss of function effect and plausibility of a dominant negative mechanism.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only (a Brain Letter/Comment); the associated full study characterizes both catalytic activities of P5CS and SPG9A variant effects, underpinning the IMP catalytic-MF and biosynthetic-BP annotations. Experimental annotations accepted per policy.

title: Recurrent De Novo Mutations Affecting Residue Arg138 of Pyrroline-5-Carboxylate Synthase Cause a Progeroid Form of Autosomal-Dominant Cutis Laxa.
review_notes: Establishes ADCL3 (dominant cutis laxa) from recurrent Arg138 variants and supports mitochondrial localization plus P5CS self-association (identical protein binding).

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome; source of generic IntAct "protein binding" interactions (COQ9, DARS2) with no ALDH18A1-specific functional meaning.

title: Pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthase senses cellular stress and modulates metabolism by regulating mitochondrial respiration.
review_notes: Full-text available; directly supports the mitochondrial-matrix IDA and informs the stress-response and respiration links (non-core).

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteomics corroborating the core mitochondrial localization.

title: Database cloning human delta 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthetase (P5CS) cDNA: a bifunctional enzyme catalyzing the first 2 steps in proline biosynthesis.
review_notes: Original human P5CS cloning paper; supports the bifunctional-enzyme and proline-biosynthesis framing (TAS).

title: glutamate + ATP + NADPH + H+ => L-glutamate gamma-semialdehyde + NADP+ + ADP + orthophosphate [P5CS]
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the two-step P5CS activity; correctly captures the chemistry but places the enzyme at the inner mitochondrial membrane, an imprecise localization relative to the matrix.

title: LONP1 binds mitochondrial inner membrane proteins
review_notes: LONP1-substrate reaction; the inner-membrane localization it confers on ALDH18A1 reflects its role as a protease substrate, not its own compartment.

title: LONP1 degrades mitochondrial inner membrane proteins
review_notes: LONP1-substrate degradation reaction; same localization caveat as R-HSA-9837978.

title: Structural and biochemical studies of human 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase: implications for hydroxyproline metabolism in primary hyperoxaluria.
review_notes: Full text confirms 1P5CDH/ALDH4A1 is the second enzyme of the 4-hydroxyproline pathway (Fig. 1), supporting the GO:0019470 TAS. The paper primarily characterizes HOGA1; it supports ALDH4A1's pathway membership but does not itself assay ALDH4A1.

title: The three-dimensional structural basis of type II hyperprolinemia.
review_notes: PMC full text (PMC3372638) directly establishes the core catalytic activity, homodimer, dual substrate specificity, and disease-variant mechanism for human ALDH4A1.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale Y2H interactome screen; source of the single "protein binding" (RBBP4) IPI. Abstract-only in cache; does not describe ALDH4A1 biology. Correctly cited as the interaction evidence but of low relevance to the gene's function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Mitochondrial proteome dataset; supports mitochondrial localization (HTP). Abstract-only in cache; corroborates the more specific matrix localization.

title: Structure of mitochondrial pyruvate carrier and its inhibition mechanism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nature 2025, PMC12043432). Bears on ALDH4A1 only indirectly: it defines the MPC transport unit as an MPC1-MPC2 heterodimer and restates that the two subunits are sufficient for MPC activity. Because the sample was reconstituted from co-expressed MPC1 and MPC2 alone, the absence of ALDH4A1 from the map is a property of the preparation, not an observation about the native complex.

title: Structures and mechanism of the human mitochondrial pyruvate carrier.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nature 2025;641:258-265). Abstract-only in the cache. Independent structural support that the pyruvate translocation pathway and its conformational cycle are contained within MPC1-MPC2; it makes no statement about ALDH4A1.

title: Biochemical genetic analysis of human and rodent aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH).
review_notes: Cited as the CACAO IDA source for general aldehyde dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity. The available abstract discusses ALDH1/ALDH2/ALDH3 and does not mention ALDH4/P5CDH; full text is unavailable, so the specific support for ALDH4A1 could not be verified.

title: ALDH4A1 functions as an active component of the MPC complex maintaining mitochondrial pyruvate import for TCA cycle entry and tumour suppression.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Cell Biol 2025;27:847-862, PMC12188464). The citation is correct and the experiments are internally consistent, but the central claim - that ALDH4A1 is a constituent subunit of the MPC - is a single-laboratory result that has not been independently replicated and is in tension with three 2025 cryo-EM analyses of human MPC (PMID:40101766, PMID:40044865, PMID:40691140) that define the transporter as an MPC1-MPC2 heterodimer enclosing the whole translocation pathway. Those structures do not refute an accessory association, since each was built from heterologously co-expressed MPC1 and MPC2 only. The paper's own reconstitution shows MPC1 plus MPC2 transporting pyruvate without ALDH4A1, which fits an accessory/stabilising role better than the "third component" framing. Recorded as disputed rather than annotated.

title: Structure of human mitochondrial pyruvate carrier MPC1 and MPC2 complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2025;16, PMC12280002). Third independent structure of the MPC1-MPC2 heterodimer. As with the other two, the complex was assembled from co-expressed, tagged MPC1 and MPC2, so it constrains the architecture of the translocation pathway without testing whether ALDH4A1 associates in vivo.

title: Cloning, characterization, and expression of cDNAs encoding human delta 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Original human ALDH4A1 cloning/characterization paper. Abstract in cache directly supports the core catalytic activity, mitochondrial matrix location, and role in proline catabolism. (Used older EC 1.5.1.12; current EC is 1.2.1.88.)

title: Structure of human succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase gene: identification of promoter region and alternatively processed isoforms.
review_notes: Primary study of the human ALDH5A1 gene; states SSADH is the last enzyme of GABA catabolism and irreversibly oxidizes SSA to succinate. Supports core MF and BP.

title: Mutational spectrum of the succinate semialdehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH5A1) gene and functional analysis of 27 novel disease-causing mutations in patients with SSADH deficiency.
review_notes: Functional expression of human variants; disease-causing missense alleles reduce SSADH activity to <5% of normal, directly linking the activity to the gene.

title: Proton MR spectroscopy in succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency.
review_notes: Case report of SSADH deficiency; documents that the disorder is one of CNS GABA catabolism with GABA and GHB accumulation, supporting the GABA shunt / catabolic role.

title: High-level expression and characterization of the recombinant enzyme, and tissue distribution of human succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Biochemical characterization of recombinant human SSADH (kinetics, homotetramer). Supports both the NAD+ activity and the identical-protein-binding (oligomerization) annotation.

title: Redox-switch modulation of human SSADH by dynamic catalytic loop.
review_notes: Crystal structures and mutagenesis of human SSADH; explicitly states the enzyme converts succinic semialdehyde to succinic acid in the mitochondrial matrix as the final step of GABA degradation. Anchors core MF, BP and location.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
review_notes: Large-scale mitochondrial phosphoproteomics; supports mitochondrial localization only (SSADH detected in isolated mitochondria).

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP high-confidence mitochondrial proteome inventory; supports mitochondrial localization.

title: Molecular cloning of the mature NAD(+)-dependent succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase from rat and human. cDNA isolation, evolutionary homology, and tissue expression.
review_notes: Cloning of mature NAD+-dependent SSADH (EC 1.2.1.24) from rat and human; assigns the enzyme to the aldehyde dehydrogenase superfamily.

title: Two exon-skipping mutations as the molecular basis of succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (4-hydroxybutyric aciduria).
review_notes: Establishes the genetic basis of SSADH deficiency; source for the GABA catabolic process (IDA) and CNS development (IMP) annotations.

title: ALDH5A1 dehydrogenates SUCCSA to SUCCA
review_notes: Reactome reaction; places the SSADH-catalyzed conversion of succinate semialdehyde to succinate in the mitochondrial matrix.

title: UniProtKB P51649 (SSDH_HUMAN), Succinate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase, mitochondrial
review_notes: UniProt record; source for catalytic activity (RHEA:13217, EC 1.2.1.24), mitochondrial subcellular location, homotetramer, 4-aminobutanoate degradation pathway, and SSADH deficiency disease association.

title: CoA-dependent methylmalonate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase, a unique member of the aldehyde dehydrogenase superfamily. cDNA cloning, evolutionary relationships, and tissue distribution.
review_notes: Original cDNA-cloning paper for MMSDH; abstract-only in cache. Establishes the enzyme's identity, CoA dependence, ALDH-superfamily membership, mitochondrial targeting peptide, and kidney/liver-predominant tissue distribution. Correctly cited for the NAS mitochondrion annotation.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: Correctly cited high-throughput interactome-capture screen (abstract-only in cache), source of the HDA RNA binding annotation. The screen enriched for metabolic enzymes; there is no independent evidence that MMSDH has a physiological RNA-binding function, so the resulting GO:0003723 annotation is an over-annotation.

title: Mutations in ALDH6A1 encoding methylmalonate semialdehyde dehydrogenase are associated with dysmyelination and transient methylmalonic aciduria.
review_notes: Full text available and read. This is the key human functional paper and the source of all three BHF-UCL IMP annotations (GO:0004491, GO:0006210, GO:0006574). Directly links ALDH6A1 genotype to reduced MMSDH catalytic activity and describes the valine/thymine catabolic pathway placement.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Source of the HTP mitochondrion localization annotation. Corroborates the mitochondrial localization established by HPA immunofluorescence and MitoCarta; abstract/full text not needed to confirm the localization call.

title: methylmalonate semialdehyde + NAD+ + CoA + H2O => propionyl-CoA + HCO3- + NADH + H+
review_notes: Reactome reaction record; source of the TAS GO:0004491 and GO:0005759 annotations. Accurately describes the enzyme, its cofactors, product, and matrix localization.

title: Branched-chain amino acid catabolism
review_notes: Source of the TAS branched-chain amino acid catabolic process annotation. A valid but broad parent process relative to the more specific L-valine catabolic process.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline; assigns only the root oxidoreductase-activity term, superseded by specific experimental MF annotations.
