title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS from the plant ortholog (P83402); correctly recovers aldehyde dehydrogenase activity and aldehyde metabolism, now backed by human data.

title: Biochemical, structural, and computational analyses of two new clinically identified missense mutations of ALDH7A1.

title: alpha-aminoadipoate semialdehyde + NAD+ => alpha-aminoadipate + NADH + H+

title: Aldolase binding to actin-containing filaments. Formation of paracrystals.

title: UniProtKB entry P04075 (ALDOA_HUMAN), fructose-bisphosphate aldolase A

title: Functional and molecular modelling studies of two hereditary fructose intolerance-causing mutations at arginine 303 in human liver aldolase.
review_notes: Kinetic characterization of WT and Arg303 (Gln/Trp) ALDOB against F1,6BP and F1P; supports both catalytic activities and the glycolytic role.

title: Molecular analysis of the aldolase B gene in patients with hereditary fructose intolerance from Spain.
review_notes: Functional analysis of ALDOB HFI variants; a UniProt EC 4.1.2.13 evidence source for both aldolase activities.

title: Physical interaction between aldolase and vacuolar H+-ATPase is essential for the assembly and activity of the proton pump.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Shows aldolase binding to the V-ATPase B subunit is required for pump assembly independently of catalysis; the abstract refers to "aldolase" generically and the ALDOB attribution is the curator's (BHF-UCL). title: Novel interaction partners of Bardet-Biedl syndrome proteins.

title: Hereditary fructose intolerance: functional study of two novel ALDOB natural variants and characterization of a partial gene deletion.
review_notes: Functional study of ALDOB variants p.R46W and p.Y343H with residual F1P activity measurements; a UniProt EC 4.1.2.13 evidence source.

title: Toward an understanding of the protein interaction network of the human liver.
review_notes: Large-scale human liver interactome; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (ALDOA). Not informative about ALDOB molecular function.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Shotgun proteomics of urinary prostatic-secretion exosomes; ALDOB is a bystander detection. Basis for the non-core extracellular exosome localization.

title: Construction and expression of human aldolase A and B expression plasmids in Escherichia coli host.
review_notes: Recombinant human ALDOB expressed in E. coli was enzymatically active and reproduced the authentic F1,6BP/F1P activity ratio; supports the F1P aldolase activity.

title: Catalytic deficiency of human aldolase B in hereditary fructose intolerance caused by a common missense mutation.
review_notes: Identifies the common A149P/A150P HFI mutation causing catalytic deficiency and inability to metabolize fructose; supports the fructose metabolic process annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex affinity-purification interactome; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (ALDOA). Not informative about ALDOB molecular function.

title: Aldolase B suppresses hepatocellular carcinogenesis by inhibiting G6PD and pentose phosphate pathways.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Establishes the non-catalytic scaffold function (Aldob-G6PD-p53 ternary complex, scaffolding independent of enzymatic activity) and cytosolic localization; basis for molecular adaptor activity, negative regulation of PPP shunt, and G6PD/TP53 protein-binding annotations. Full text (not cached) reports the active-site mutant assays supporting the IDA catalytic-activity annotation.

title: Human skeletal-muscle aldolase: N-terminal sequence analysis of CNBr- and o-iodosobenzoic acid-cleavage fragments.
review_notes: Cached abstract describes N-terminal protein-sequence analysis of human skeletal-muscle aldolase (aldolase A / ALDOA), not an ALDOB activity assay. The Reactome EXP GO:0004332 annotation on ALDOB citing this reference appears to be a reference-term mismatch; flagged for curator verification. The activity itself is correct for aldolase B and abundantly supported by other references.

title: Mode of interactions of human aldolase isozymes with cytoskeletons.
review_notes: Shows all three aldolase isozymes bind actin-containing cytoskeleton with tissue-specific preference (aldolase B prefers liver cytoskeleton); supports the cytoskeletal-protein-binding (non-core) annotation.

title: Deficiency of GDP-Man:GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol mannosyltransferase causes congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ik.

Directly establishes the human ALG1 beta-1,4-mannosyltransferase activity (enzymatic assay in patient fibroblast extracts), its role in LLO assembly and N-glycosylation, and the S258L disease variant. Abstract-only in cache but the abstract itself supplies the enzymatic and localization statements used here.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: NK-cell (YTS) membrane-proteome mass-spectrometry survey; basis of the generic HDA "membrane" annotation. Correctly cited but only supports a non-specific membrane localization, not ALG1-specific function.

title: ALG1-CDG: Clinical and Molecular Characterization of 39 Unreported Patients.
review_notes: Large ALG1-CDG clinical/molecular series; full text cached. States the ALG1 enzymatic role (first of nine mannoses onto the DLO, ER-localized beta-1,4-mannosyltransferase) and demonstrates loss-of-function by yeast complementation, supporting the N-linked glycosylation and disease annotations.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified HuRI interactome paper. Correctly cited for the six IPI protein binding annotations, but as a high-throughput binary screen it does not establish a specific molecular function for ALG10; these annotations are flagged as over-annotated.

title: UniProtKB Q5BKT4 ALG10 (AG10A_HUMAN) record
review_notes: Primary source for ALG10 function, catalytic activity, pathway and localization used throughout this review.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane-proteome MS survey of YTS NK-like cells; ALG11 detected in the membrane fraction. Correctly cited for a generic HDA membrane annotation but contributes no functional insight and is subsumed by the specific ER membrane annotations.

review_notes: BioPlex proteome-scale AP-MS interactome study; source of the ALG11 IPI to GLA (P06280). Correctly cited but the interaction is a high-throughput co-purification supporting only bare "protein binding".

title: Defective ALG11 does not transfer Man to the N-glycan precursor
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing the ALG11 step and its loss-of-function disease (CDG-1p). Title left exactly as fetched.

title: Congenital disorders of glycosylation type Ig is defined by a deficiency in dolichyl-P-mannose:Man7GlcNAc2-PP-dolichyl mannosyltransferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary paper establishing human ALG12 identity, the Dol-P-Man-dependent alpha-1,6-mannosyltransferase activity, LLO biosynthesis role, and CDG-Ig disease. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Deficiency of dolichyl-P-Man:Man7GlcNAc2-PP-dolichyl mannosyltransferase causes congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ig.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; independent confirmation of ALG12 mannosyltransferase activity, LLO role, and CDG-Ig. Abstract-only in cache.

title: ALG12 mannosyltransferase defect in congenital disorder of glycosylation type lg.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; high-throughput proteomics providing only generic membrane localization, not gene-specific function.

title: Gene identification in the congenital disorders of glycosylation type I by whole-exome sequencing.

title: An in vitro assay for enzymatic studies on human ALG13/14 heterodimeric UDP-N-acetylglucosamine transferase.

title: Alg14 recruits Alg13 to the cytoplasmic face of the endoplasmic reticulum to form a novel bipartite UDP-N-acetylglucosamine transferase required for the second step of N-linked glycosylation.

title: An in vitro assay for enzymatic studies on human ALG13/14 heterodimeric UDP-N-acetylglucosamine transferase.

title: ALG13:ALG14 transfers GlcNAc from UDP-GlcNAc to GlcNAcDOLP

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.

title: Human AlkB homologue 1 (ABH1) exhibits DNA lyase activity at abasic sites.

title: ALKBH1 is a histone H2A dioxygenase involved in neural differentiation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference interactome; source of an ASL self-interaction (GO:0042802) and generic protein-binding (GO:0005515) annotations.

title: Intragenic complementation at the human argininosuccinate lyase locus. Identification of the major complementing alleles.

title: Deep research report (falcon) for human ASL

title: Crystal structure and functional mapping of human ASMT, the last enzyme of the melatonin synthesis pathway.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Primary structural/enzymatic paper on human ASMT; source of the EC 2.1.1.4 assignment and the experimental IDA annotations for acetylserotonin O-methyltransferase activity and melatonin biosynthesis, and of the homodimer (IPI) annotations. Abstract-only in cache; the abstract directly supports the catalytic-activity, homodimer, and melatonin-pathway claims.

title: Human hydroxyindole-O-methyltransferase: presence of LINE-1 fragment in a cDNA clone and pineal mRNA.
review_notes: PubMed-verified cloning paper. Correctly identifies HIOMT/ASMT as the last enzyme of melatonin synthesis and describes the LINE-1-containing pineal mRNA (isoform 3). title: Methylation of N-acetyl-5-HT to form melatonin
review_notes: Reactome reaction correctly describes the ASMT-catalyzed final methylation step. Note the Reactome-derived S-methyltransferase (GO:0008172) MF mapping is the wrong branch (ASMT is an O-methyltransferase); the cytosol location is appropriate.

title: Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis
review_notes: Pathway-level Reactome entry; basis for the indolalkylamine biosynthetic process (broad parent) TAS annotation.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.

title: Restructuring of the dinucleotide-binding fold in an NADP(H) sensor protein.

title: Toward an understanding of the protein interaction network of the human liver.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.

title: Sequence for human argininosuccinate synthetase cDNA.

title: Characterization of human wild-type and mutant argininosuccinate synthetase proteins expressed in bacterial cells.

title: Falcon deep research report for ATP6V1G2
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report (Edison/Falcon), not independently verified against primary sources. Its most useful, cross-checkable isoform-specific claims are: (1) mass spectrometry of rat-brain synaptic-vesicle V-ATPase finding G2 as the predominant G subunit (~83% G2 vs ~17% G1; attributed to Abbas et al. 2020 Science brain V-ATPase structure); (2) neuron-restricted G2 expression with astrocytes/glia using only G1, and the G2-null mouse showing post-transcriptional G1 up-regulation with no overt phenotype (attributed to Kawamura et al. 2015 Sci Rep). title: Falcon deep research report for AZI2
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report; treat as a lead, not as primary evidence. AZI2-SPECIFIC claims it surfaces (anchored to retrievable primary papers not in the current GOA) include: NAP1/AZI2 is required for TBK1 activation at centrosomes during mitosis/cytokinesis, with TBK1 phosphorylating NAP1 at Ser318 to trigger its degradation (Paul et al. 2023, J Cell Biol, doi:10.1083/jcb.202303082); AZI2 mediates TBK1 activation at unresolved selective-autophagy cargo-receptor complexes upon RB1CC1/FIP200 loss, driving IRF3 chemokine signaling and CD8 T-cell infiltration in breast cancer (Yeo et al. 2024, Autophagy, doi:10.1080/15548627.2023.2259775; Okamoto et al. 2020, Cancer Res); AZI2/NAP1 with SINTBAD controls mitophagy initiation/progression by tuning TBK1 recruitment to OPTN/NDP52 (Adriaenssens et al. 2024); AZI2 and TANK cooperatively recruit TBK1 to the TNF receptor to restrain RIPK1-driven cell death (Ujevic et al. 2024, Nat Commun, doi:10.1038/s41467-024-54399-4). GENERAL TBK1-PATHWAY / ADAPTOR-FAMILY inference (TBK1 as the central kinase downstream of RLR-MAVS, cGAS-STING, TLR3-TRIF; competition among NAP1/TANK/SINTBAD for TBK1) is shared pathway/family context, not necessarily AZI2-specific. The Glon et al. 2025 condensate model is a non-peer-reviewed bioRxiv preprint and is treated as speculative. None of these primary papers are cited in the current GOA, so no existing-annotation action was changed on the basis of this report alone; it is recorded to flag candidate functions (mitosis/cytokinesis, selective autophagy/mitophagy, TNF-receptor cell-death checkpoint) for future curation.

title: Falcon deep research report for BBIP1
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison Scientific) deep-research report. title: Falcon deep research report for BBS10
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/falcon) deep-research summary; correctness UNVERIFIED as for any LLM synthesis. BBS10-chaperonin-specific claims that are well-anchored and corroborated by primary literature: BBS10 is NOT a subunit of the mature octameric BBSome but a chaperonin-like assembly factor that, with BBS6/MKKS and BBS12 plus CCT/TRiC subunits (CCT1-8), forms the BBS/CCT machinery required for BBSome biogenesis (Seo 2010 / PMID:20080638, Zhang 2012 / PMID:22500027); the complex stabilizes BBS7 and promotes the BBS2-BBS7-BBS9 core; the ATPase activity of BBS10 has NOT been validated and it is unlikely to act as a classical ATP-driven chaperonin; localization is at the basal body/pericentriolar region and chaperonin-like BBS proteins are generally not detected along the primary cilium. CAUTION (BBSome/CCT over-generalization to be read skeptically, not transferred to BBS10 as fact): claims about generic group-II/CCT three-domain ATP-dependent folding mechanism are framed as canonical-chaperonin background, not demonstrated for BBS10; the emerging non-ciliary roles (direct insulin-receptor binding, leptin signaling, adipogenesis) are explicitly flagged in the report as requiring further validation and are not used here to alter any annotation.

title: Falcon deep research report for BBS12
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report (Edison/Falcon) drawing chiefly on two review articles (Tian et al. 2023 eLife, Gupta et al. 2022 Am J Med Genet C) plus Singh 2020, Delvallee 2023 and Masek 2022. BBS12-specific, well-anchored claims that this review uses: (i) BBS12 is a chaperonin-like BBSome assembly chaperone, NOT a structural BBSome subunit, and has never been observed along the ciliary axoneme (localizing instead to the basal body / pericentriolar region / centriolar satellites); (ii) BBS12 lacks the conserved ATP-binding / ATP-hydrolysis motif of canonical CCT chaperonins, so it probably lacks intrinsic ATPase activity and is not a bona fide ATP-dependent folding chaperonin, with the folding activity of the BBS/CCT complex supplied by the incorporated CCT subunits while BBS6/BBS10/BBS12 act as the substrate-binding unit; (iii) BBS12 helps the chaperonin complex stabilize BBS7 and seed the BBS2-BBS7-BBS9 core. NOT used (BBSome/CCT generalization or unverified specifics that the report imputes to BBS12 but that are properties of the BBSome as a whole or of canonical CCT): downstream Shh/WNT/GPCR/leptin/insulin signaling, "59-60 variants", "5-11% of cases", and any quantitative claim. correctness left UNVERIFIED because the report is an LLM synthesis of reviews rather than primary data; the BBS12-specific points above are consistent with the curated primary literature (PMID:20080638, PMID:22500027) already in this review.

title: Recruitment of PCM1 to the centrosome by the cooperative action of DISC1 and BBS4: a candidate for psychiatric illnesses.

title: CEP290 interacts with the centriolar satellite component PCM-1 and is required for Rab8 localization to the primary cilium.

title: BBS mutations modify phenotypic expression of CEP290-related ciliopathies.

title: Bardet-Biedl syndrome proteins 1 and 3 regulate the ciliary trafficking of polycystic kidney disease 1 protein.

title: Recruitment of PCM1 to the centrosome by the cooperative action of DISC1 and BBS4: a candidate for psychiatric illnesses.

title: Intrinsic protein-protein interaction-mediated and chaperonin-assisted sequential assembly of stable bardet-biedl syndrome protein complex, the BBSome.

review_notes: Documents the BBS5-PKD1 interaction (UniProt) and BBSome-mediated ciliary trafficking of PKD1 cargo; the GO:0005515 term is uninformative.

review_notes: Discovery of BBIP10/BBIP1 as a BBSome subunit; source of ComplexPortal BBSome membership and ciliary membrane localization annotations for BBS7.

review_notes: Establishes the BBS-chaperonin complex and its role in BBSome assembly; BBS7 is a chaperonin client. Supports BBSome membership (IDA).

title: A comprehensive resource of interacting protein regions for refining human transcription factor networks.
review_notes: High-throughput interaction resource (JUN); supports generic protein binding only.

title: Novel asymmetrically localizing components of human centrosomes identified by complementary proteomics methods.
review_notes: Proteomic identification of BBS7 as an asymmetric centrosomal component; supports centrosome localization (IDA).

title: A novel protein LZTFL1 regulates ciliary trafficking of the BBSome and Smoothened.
review_notes: Full text available; establishes BBSome (and BBS7-SMO) ciliary trafficking and Hedgehog signaling role, and experimental cytoplasmic localization of BBS7.

review_notes: Reports a non-canonical nuclear role for BBS7 via RNF2/PcG interaction and regulation of RNF2 levels; supports the transcription/proteasome/TF-binding annotations as non-core. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Intrinsic protein-protein interaction-mediated and chaperonin-assisted sequential assembly of stable bardet-biedl syndrome protein complex, the BBSome.
review_notes: Full text available; defines the BBS7-BBS2-BBS9 BBSome core and the ordered, chaperonin-assisted assembly pathway in which BBS7 stability is chaperonin-dependent.

title: A core complex of BBS proteins cooperates with the GTPase Rab8 to promote ciliary membrane biogenesis.
review_notes: Founding BBSome paper; abstract verified. Defines the seven-subunit BBSome (including BBS9), its centriolar-satellite and ciliary-membrane localization, its requirement for ciliogenesis, and the Rab8/Rabin8 connection. Directly supports BBSome part_of and ciliary/centriolar-satellite localizations.

title: A BBSome subunit links ciliogenesis, microtubule stability, and acetylation.
review_notes: Abstract verified. Characterizes BBIP10/BBIP1 as an eighth BBSome subunit and confirms BBSome membrane trafficking to/within the cilium; underpins the ComplexPortal BBSome membership and ciliary-membrane localization annotations.

title: A novel protein LZTFL1 regulates ciliary trafficking of the BBSome and Smoothened.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt for the BBS9 685-765 LZTL1-interaction region and BBSome function. Establishes LZTFL1 as a regulator of BBSome ciliary trafficking and Hedgehog/Smoothened. Supports the BBS9-LZTFL1 interaction annotation.

title: BBS mutations modify phenotypic expression of CEP290-related ciliopathies.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Confirms BBS1/2/4/5/7/8/9 form the BBSome that sorts membrane proteins to cilia, and that loss of BBSome subunits affects ciliary cargo localization; supports the protein-localization-to-cilium IMP and the cilium / transition zone / centriolar satellite IDA annotations.

title: Structural characterization of Bardet-Biedl syndrome 9 protein (BBS9).
review_notes: Cited by UniProt (PDB 4YD8) for the BBS9 N-terminal seven-bladed beta-propeller structure and for the destabilizing G141R disease variant. Supports the structural/scaffold role of BBS9. Abstract not cached; verified via the UniProt cross-reference and FT annotations.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 proteome-scale AP-MS; source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (interactors incl. HSPD1/P10809). PMC full text confirmed. Not informative about BCAT2's catalytic function.

title: An AP-MS- and BioID-compatible MAC-tag enables comprehensive mapping of protein interactions and subcellular localizations.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.

title: Two yeast homologs of ECA39, a target for c-Myc regulation, code for cytosolic and mitochondrial branched-chain amino acid aminotransferases.
review_notes: Cached abstract-only (full_text_available: false); UniProt cites the full text (ECO:0000269) for the EC 2.6.1.42 catalytic activity and BCAA-catabolism FUNCTION. Directly establishes BCAT activity toward Leu/Ile/Val. Underlies the core MF and BP annotations.

title: Cloning of the rat and human mitochondrial branched chain aminotransferases (BCATm).
review_notes: Cached abstract-only; defining cloning paper that proposed BCAT1 (cytosolic)/BCAT2 (mitochondrial) nomenclature, mapped BCAT2 to chromosome 19, and showed a 27-residue mitochondrial presequence and BCAT activity. Supports MF and mitochondrial localization.

title: Branched-chain-amino-acid aminotransferase, mitochondrial (Mus musculus)
review_notes: Mouse ortholog UniProt entry; source of the By-similarity FUNCTION statement (BCAA-catabolism acetyl-CoA used by EP300 to acetylate/inhibit PRDM16, preventing adipose browning) underlying the ISS brown-fat annotations. Verbatim supporting text quoted from the human O15382 UniProt FUNCTION comment, which attributes the statement to O35855.

title: Deep research report on BCAT2 (falcon/Edison)
review_notes: AI-generated deep-research synthesis (falcon/Edison). Used to corroborate the core BCAA catabolic pathway framing; primary catalytic/localization claims are independently grounded in UniProt O15382 and PMID:8702755/PMID:9165094.

title: Crystal structure of human branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase and the molecular basis of multienzyme complex deficiency in maple syrup urine disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; structural basis for E1-alpha function, cofactor binding, and MSUD variant effects. Cached abstract-only but experimental annotations (IDA/IMP) reflect full-text data.

title: Solution structure and dynamics of the lipoic acid-bearing domain of human mitochondrial branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Correctly cited but studies the E2/DBT lipoyl domain, not E1-alpha; used only as curator-transferred (TAS) broad localization/carboxy-lyase support for the complex.

title: Roles of His291-alpha and His146-beta' in the reductive acylation reaction catalyzed by human branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase: refined phosphorylation loop structure in the active site.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports the E1-alpha catalytic mechanism. Cited in GOA only as a bare protein-binding IPI (WITH/FROM BCKDHB).

title: Cross-talk between thiamin diphosphate binding and phosphorylation loop conformation in human branched-chain alpha-keto acid decarboxylase/dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports TPP-binding/regulatory coupling on E1. Cited in GOA as bare protein-binding IPI (WITH/FROM BCKDHB).

title: Molecular mechanism for regulation of the human mitochondrial branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex by phosphorylation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports phospho-regulation of BCKDH. Cited in GOA as bare protein-binding IPI (WITH/FROM BCKDHB).

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; HDA mitochondrial localization support only.

review_notes: PubMed-verified high-throughput screen; only supports a bare protein-binding IPI (WITH/FROM BCKDHB).

review_notes: PubMed-verified high-throughput screen; only supports a bare protein-binding IPI (WITH/FROM BCKDHB).

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.

title: Purification and characterization of human liver branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex.

title: Impaired assembly of E1 decarboxylase of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex in type IA maple syrup urine disease.

title: Crystal structure of human branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase and the molecular basis of multienzyme complex deficiency in maple syrup urine disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Crystal structure of the human E1b alpha2-beta2 heterotetramer; directly establishes BCKDHB as a subunit of the E1 decarboxylase and its role in cofactor/K+ binding. Cached abstract only (full_text_available: false), but the catalytic-activity and structural claims are also anchored in UniProt.

title: Roles of His291-alpha and His146-beta' in the reductive acylation reaction catalyzed by human branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase: refined phosphorylation loop structure in the active site.
review_notes: Mechanistic study of the assembled E1; basis for an IPI 'protein binding' annotation (WITH/FROM BCKDHA). Cached abstract only.

title: Cross-talk between thiamin diphosphate binding and phosphorylation loop conformation in human branched-chain alpha-keto acid decarboxylase/dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Basis for an IPI 'protein binding' annotation (WITH/FROM BCKDHA), reflecting the E1 heterotetramer. Cached abstract only.

title: Molecular mechanism for regulation of the human mitochondrial branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex by phosphorylation.
review_notes: Regulation of the assembled complex by E1-alpha phosphorylation; basis for an IPI 'protein binding' annotation (WITH/FROM BCKDHA). Cached abstract only.

title: Maple syrup urine disease. Complete defect of the E1 beta subunit of the branched chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex due to a deletion of an 11-bp repeat sequence which encodes a mitochondrial targeting leader peptide in a family with the disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Directly on BCKDHB (E1-beta): 11-bp deletion in the mitochondrial targeting peptide; loss of E1-beta destabilizes E1-alpha and reduces BCKDH activity to ~6% of normal. Supports complex membership, BCAA catabolism, and mitochondrial localization annotations. Full text (JCI, PMC295312) available.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale BioPlex interactome; basis for a high-throughput IPI 'protein binding' annotation with BCKDHA (E1 heterotetramer). Recovers the genuine interaction but uninformative at the bare protein-binding level.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Large-scale BioPlex 3.0 interactome; basis for a high-throughput IPI 'protein binding' annotation with BCKDHA. Genuine but uninformative bare protein binding.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome (HTP); supports mitochondrial localization of BCKDHB.

title: Purification and characterization of human liver branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex.

title: Impaired assembly of E1 decarboxylase of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex in type IA maple syrup urine disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes the E1 decarboxylase as an alpha2-beta2 tetramer of E1-alpha and E1-beta; supports BCKDHB complex membership and its contribution to E1 catalytic activity. Cached abstract only.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified proteomics resource; supports the HTP mitochondrion localization for BDH1.

title: Wild type and mutant human heart (R)-3-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase expressed in insect cells.
review_notes: Directly establishes the human enzyme's 3-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase activity and PC requirement; supports the IDA for GO:0003858. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Mutations in amphiphysin 2 (BIN1) disrupt interaction with dynamin 2 and cause autosomal recessive centronuclear myopathy.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports BIN1 membrane tubulation biology and SH3-domain interaction with DNM2/dynamin 2 in muscle membrane remodeling.

title: Structure and dynamics of helix-0 of the N-BAR domain in lipid micelles and bilayers.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports N-BAR/BIN1 membrane binding and curvature generation/sensing as the core biochemical function.

title: Mutations in BIN1 associated with centronuclear myopathy disrupt membrane remodeling by affecting protein density and oligomerization.

title: BIN1 regulates BACE1 intracellular trafficking and amyloid-β production.

title: Molecular basis for phosphospecific recognition of histone H3 tails by Survivin paralogues at inner centromeres.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.

title: An interactome perturbation framework prioritizes damaging missense mutations for developmental disorders.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.

title: Purification and characterization of human biliverdin reductase.

title: BRCA2 function in DNA binding and recombination from a BRCA2-DSS1-ssDNA structure.

title: BRCA2 chaperones RAD51 to single molecules of RPA-coated ssDNA.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The route for the only IEA row on this gene. Confirmed live rather than assumed: it returns 139,714 human annotations, against 0 for GO_REF:0000043, the Swiss-Prot keyword reference that GOA stopped importing. So the SubCell mapping route is current while the keyword route is not, and the distinction matters for reading this gene's record. Its input here, UniProtKB-SubCell:SL-0243 'Secreted', rests on the entry's own ECO:0000305 SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line, which in turn rests on a predicted signal peptide - so the row's evidence path is a prediction chain even though its conclusion is independently measured.

title: Proteomic analysis of human parotid gland exosomes by multidimensional protein identification technology (MudPIT).
review_notes: The source of the GO:0070062 HDA row. The cached copy does not contain the 497-protein catalogue in which C5orf46 appears, so no sentence from it is quoted about this gene specifically and the row is assessed on its provenance rather than on a quotation. A reference-projection test was run and came back clean: fully paginated, the reference carries 396 annotations over 396 distinct entities, every one to GO:0070062 alone, all HDA, all assigned by UniProt. One entity, one annotation, one localisation term, and no functional or phenotype term anywhere in the reference - a proteomic inventory rather than a projection in which a phenotype spreads across a set. Retraction, erratum and correction checks clean by PubMed CommentsCorrections and by Crossref on DOI 10.1021/pr800658c.

title: AP-57/C10orf99 is a new type of multifunctional antimicrobial peptide.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, so nothing beyond the abstract is asserted about it. Cited here for one purpose: it is the curatorial precedent that makes the coverage gap on C5orf46 a consistency defect rather than a wish. GOA carries four IDA rows from this paper on C10orf99/GPR15LG (Q6UWK7), including GO:0050830 and GO:0050832, all assigned by UniProt, and UniProt took the AP-57 name into that entry. Note a correction to my own working assumption, recorded because it nearly propagated: I first looked C10orf99 up as Q6UWT2, which is adropin (ENHO) and an entirely different protein. The right accession is Q6UWK7, confirmed by primaryAccession and by its gene synonyms including C10orf99.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0. Supplies one GO:0005515 row, for TMBIM6, by anti tag coip. Its partner is re-reported in BioPlex 3.0, so the two GOA rows for TMBIM6 are one method in two releases. The reference carries 3,731 annotations in GOA, so a reference-projection entity count is not obtainable at reasonable cost and is reported as unavailable rather than estimated from one page. IntAct also records a second partner from this study, PPCS (Q9HAB8) at MI-score 0.35, which has no GOA row; noted so the 13-versus-14 partner count is not read as a missing review row. Retraction and correction checks clean.

title: Small-protein Enrichment Assay Enables the Rapid, Unbiased Analysis of Over 100 Low Abundance Factors from Human Plasma.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache (full_text_available: false), so nothing beyond the abstract is asserted about its contents; the quoted sentence is from the abstract and names the gene explicitly. It carries no GOA annotation of its own - a QuickGO query by reference returns zero - so the plasma detection is uncurated. Retraction and correction checks clean by both routes.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI, the source of twelve of the fourteen GO:0005515 rows. Correctly cited and a sound study; the issue is what a single hit from it can support. IntAct logs each of the twelve partners three times under three names of the same screen, so UniProt's NbExp=3 counts sub-methods rather than experiments - the third instance of that pattern in this campaign, with a new shape in SLC30A2's NbExp=5, where two sub-methods are logged twice. At 85,343 annotations in GOA the reference-projection test cannot be run affordably and is reported as uninformative rather than approximated. Retraction and correction checks clean.

title: AP-64, Encoded by C5orf46, Exhibits Antimicrobial Activity against Gram-Negative Bacteria.
review_notes: Cached full text read in full. The sole functional characterisation of this gene in any organism, and the basis for both proposed new terms. Retraction, erratum and expression-of-concern checks clean by two independent routes - the PubMed record's PublicationType and CommentsCorrections fields, and Crossref relation/update-to/updated-by on DOI 10.3390/biom11040485. Identity of the assayed molecule verified computationally rather than assumed: the paper's stated 64 residues, MW 7.2 and PI 4.54 are all reproduced from UniProt's annotated mature CHAIN 24..87, so this is the gene's physiological secreted product and not a synthetic sub-fragment. Two reading cautions recorded. First, the paper is careful that the killing mechanism is unresolved, and the deep-research record's framing invites a membrane-permeabilisation reading the paper declines to support; no molecular function is proposed here as a result. Second, the Jurkat/Raji cytotoxicity must not be reported without the immediately following result that normal T cells, HaCaT keratinocytes and mouse embryonic fibroblasts are equally susceptible - it is general cytotoxicity at micromolar concentration, not selective anti-tumour activity. Notably, a QuickGO query by reference returns zero annotations citing this PMID anywhere in GOA (positive control: PMID:19199708 returns 396), so none of it has ever been curated.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0. Supplies the second TMBIM6 row by the same anti tag coip method as BioPlex 2.0, so it is a re-report rather than independent corroboration. 9,514 annotations in GOA, so the projection test is uninformative here too. Retraction and correction checks clean.

title: Preliminary study on the role of the C5orf46 gene in renal cancer.
review_notes: Cached full text read; retraction and correction checks clean. Marked LOW_QUALITY on methodological grounds rather than citation grounds - the identifier and title are correct and the paper is honestly presented, its own title beginning 'Preliminary study'. The in vitro part is siRNA knockdown in two lines with proliferation, migration and apoptosis read-outs, no rescue, no mechanism, and no molecular function assayed; the remainder is TCGA bioinformatics. Sufficient to record a cancer-cell-line dependency as a knowledge gap, not sufficient to support a GO process term, and no term is proposed from it. Its background sentence that the gene has 'antibacterial and anti-inflammatory effects via sequencing and microarray technologies' garbles the antibacterial finding, which came from purified protein assays, not sequencing; that sentence is not relied on.

title: C5orf46 bioinformatics results (mature-peptide identity; partner-set composition; annotation coverage gap)
review_notes: Generated by analyze_c5orf46.py in the same folder, with the fetched records cached under data/ so the numbers reproduce without network access. Every reported zero in it is paired with a non-zero positive control from the same endpoint in the same call pattern - ADGRA2 and ACTB for the IBA count, PMID:19199708 for the reference-coverage count, IPR001879 for the interpro2go lookup - because a rejected query and a genuine negative are indistinguishable downstream. Its guards are break-tested in both directions with the failure message asserted, and one of them caught a real defect in the script's own first version: a single-request IntAct fetch silently dropped 32 of AQP6's 1032 interaction records, and the self-test now re-runs that exact call and requires it to raise. Quotations into this file are deliberately taken from computed table rows rather than from prose, because a file: quote into a generated artifact is a two-way dependency and prose gets reworded.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for C5orf46 (human)
review_notes: A machine-generated secondary source, assessed rather than trusted. Its value here was real: it surfaced all three of the papers that GOA does not cite, including the sole functional characterisation of the gene, so both proposed terms trace to a lead it provided. Marked LOW_QUALITY on two grounds, neither of which is a fabricated citation. First, the cytotoxicity finding is framed without the disconfirming result that follows it in the same paper, which turns general micromolar cytotoxicity into an apparent anti-tumour selectivity - exactly the kind of error a verbatim-quote gate cannot catch, because the sentence itself is true. Second, the narrative's shape invites a membrane-permeabilisation reading of the mechanism, which the source explicitly leaves open between envelope damage and an intracellular target; no molecular function is proposed anywhere in this review as a result. The record's own GO grounding offers no molecular activity and only GO:0005576, which agrees with the conclusion reached here independently. Nothing from it is used as evidence for any mechanistic claim - it is cited once, for a corpus-level negative that three independent sources corroborate.

title: UniProtKB entry Q6UWT4 (CE046_HUMAN), cached in the gene folder
review_notes: The cached Swiss-Prot entry, and the source of the mature-chain boundaries that everything in section A of the bioinformatics results depends on. Verified live that primaryAccession is Q6UWT4, so this is not a merged accession silently resolving to another protein - a failure mode that returns HTTP 200 with a complete, normal-looking reviewed record. Every quotation taken from this file is a single physical line, because a supporting_text that spans a CC continuation cannot be verbatim and the repo validator does not check file: quotes at all; each was additionally hand-verified with grep -F. Two features of the entry are worth flagging for UniProt rather than for GO: there is no FUNCTION comment and the recommended name is still 'Uncharacterized protein C5orf46', although a 2021 paper purified this exact mature chain and measured its bactericidal activity; and the reference list stops at four large-scale sequencing submissions. The entry is otherwise internally consistent - notably it does NOT carry an unsupported activity from its domain name, since its only InterPro signature, IPR027950/DUF4576, maps to nothing.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Correctly cited high-throughput binary interactome screen. Supplies only bare protein binding; partners are unrelated to the established function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.

title: Large-scale phosphomimetic screening identifies phospho-modulated motif-based protein interactions.
review_notes: Correctly cited motif-based screen. The RANBP2/Nup358 hit is contextually interesting given the NXF1 export role, but the screen tested no function and the interaction was not followed up.

title: Novel nuclear RNA export factor 1 adaptor drives tumor growth by increasing proliferation-stimulatory mRNA export.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Signal Transduct Target Ther 2026;11:275). Full text available and read. The sole source of every functional claim for this gene, and not yet reflected in GOA. Single laboratory, no independent replication, and all experiments are in hepatocellular carcinoma models; the conformational mechanism is inferred from mutagenesis, FRET and bimolecular fluorescence complementation rather than from a structure, which the authors acknowledge.

title: Carbonic anhydrase-related protein is a novel binding protein for inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor type 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Biochem J 2003;372(Pt 2):435-41, DOI 10.1042/BJ20030110; abstract-only in cache. The primary description of the CA8/CARP-IP3R1 interaction - yeast two-hybrid discovery, co-precipitation, mapping of the interacting regions, Purkinje-cell co-localisation, and the functional result that CARP lowers the receptor's affinity for IP3. This is the evidentiary basis for the replacement molecular function.

title: CA8 mutations cause a novel syndrome characterized by ataxia and mild mental retardation with predisposition to quadrupedal gait.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: PLoS Genet 2009;5(5):e1000487, DOI 10.1371/journal.pgen.1000487; full text cached. Establishes the human disease link (homozygous S100P) and shows the variant acts by proteasome-mediated destabilisation, i.e. as a null - which is what makes the ataxia phenotype attributable to loss of CA8 function rather than to a neomorphic effect.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Source of a GO:0005515 IPI row. Systematic interactome screen; correctly cited but functionally uninformative for this gene.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Source of a GO:0005515 IPI row. Systematic interactome screen; functionally uninformative for this gene.

title: Pooled-matrix protein interaction screens using Barcode Fusion Genetics.
review_notes: Source of a GO:0005515 IPI row. A methods paper for pooled two-hybrid screening; functionally uninformative for this gene.

title: Aberrant IP(3) receptor activities revealed by comprehensive analysis of pathological mutations causing spinocerebellar ataxia 29.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 2018;115(48):12259-12264, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1811129115; full text cached. The strongest corroboration of the CA8 regulatory function, because it perturbs the interface from the receptor side: the SCA29 variant V1538M in the CA8-binding region of IP3R1 abolishes both the interaction and CA8-mediated inhibition, while CA8 disease variants reduce that inhibition from the other side.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Source of a GO:0005515 IPI row. Population-scale variant interactome survey; functionally uninformative for this gene as cited.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Source of a GO:0005515 IPI row. Reference binary interactome; functionally uninformative for this gene.

title: Structural Characterization of Carbonic Anhydrase VIII and Effects of Missense Single Nucleotide Variations to Protein Structure and Function.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Int J Mol Sci 2020;21(8):2764, DOI 10.3390/ijms21082764; full text cached. Computational/structural analysis. Cited here for its clear statements of the acatalytic status and of the allosteric mechanism (reduced IP3 affinity with no change in the number of binding sites); its molecular-dynamics conclusions about individual variants are modelling, not measurement, and are not relied on.

title: Carbonic anhydrase VIII as a regulator of intracellular calcium signaling: mechanistic insights and implications in human disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Mol Biol Rep 2026;53(1):923, DOI 10.1007/s11033-026-12124-y, PMC13253706; full text cached. A review, so used for framing and for statements that the primary literature independently supports - the missing catalytic histidine, the negative-regulator directionality, and the point that CA8 binds the receptor's modulatory domain rather than IP3 itself.

title: Two point mutations convert a catalytically inactive carbonic anhydrase-related protein (CARP) to an active enzyme.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: FEBS Lett 1996;398(2-3):322-5, DOI 10.1016/s0014-5793(96)01263-x; abstract-only in cache. The identifier is correct and the paper is highly relevant, but it is cited by GOA (PINC, TAS) in support of GO:0004089 carbonate dehydratase activity, which is the opposite of what it reports: unmodified CARP is catalytically inactive and is not isolated as a zinc complex, and activity appears only in an engineered double mutant. Flagged MISCITED for that reason. The work is on murine CARP, the CA8 ortholog, which carries the same active-site substitution as the human protein.

title: Biophysical properties, pharmacology, and modulation of human, neuronal L-type (alpha(1D), Ca(V)1.3) voltage-dependent calcium currents.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Neurophysiol 2001). Human alpha-1D/alpha-2delta-1/beta-3a stable line; supports the contributes_to framing of the channel activity.

title: Structure and functional expression of alpha 1, alpha 2, and beta subunits of a novel human neuronal calcium channel subtype.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neuron 1992). Founding human reconstitution. Notably the paper itself calls the alpha-2 subunit accessory, which argues against the enables qualifier it is used to support.

title: Loss-of-function mutations in the cardiac calcium channel underlie a new clinical entity characterized by ST-segment elevation, short QT intervals, and sudden cardiac death.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Circulation 2007). CACNA2D1 loss-of-function in a Brugada/short-QT phenotype, with CaV1.2 reconstitution patch-clamp.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (large-scale urinary exosome proteomics). Correctly cited, but a detection list rather than evidence of a functional location.

title: Gabapentin receptor alpha2delta-1 is a neuronal thrombospondin receptor responsible for excitatory CNS synaptogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell 2009). The origin of the thrombospondin-receptor/synaptogenesis model. Correctly cited and highly influential, but the claim is contested - a 2025 presynaptic triple conditional knockout found synapse development intact. Note that the original claim was specifically postsynaptic, so the 2025 presynaptic result narrows it rather than overturning it outright. Not used to support any annotation in this file.

title: Identification of a novel loss-of-function calcium channel gene mutation in short QT syndrome (SQTS6).
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Eur Heart J 2011). Single-family CACNA2D1 p.Ser755Thr short-QT variant; the cardiac conduction annotations rest on it.

title: A β-amyloid oligomer directly modulates P/Q-type calcium currents in Xenopus oocytes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Br J Pharmacol 2012). Supports the reconstituted P/Q-type channel annotation. The cellular response to amyloid-beta annotation derived from it is a stretch - the system is Xenopus oocytes and the stimulus is an applied synthetic globulomer.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (exosome proteomics of expressed prostatic secretions). Correctly cited, but a detection list rather than evidence of a functional location.

title: Functional characterization of CaVα2δ mutations associated with sudden cardiac death.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2015). Side-by-side flow cytometry and patch clamp separating surface density from current density; the strongest single support for the calcium channel regulator activity proposed here.

title: Biallelic CACNA2D1 loss-of-function variants cause early-onset developmental epileptic encephalopathy.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Brain 2022, Dolphin lab). Human biallelic loss-of-function causing developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; establishes that the human protein is required in vivo.

title: α2δ-1-Linked NMDA and AMPA Receptors in Neuropathic Pain and Gabapentinoid Action.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as an article (J Neurochem 2025), but it is a review from the same laboratory that generated the alpha-2/delta-1-NMDAR model it summarises. Marked UNVERIFIED for the scientific claim rather than the citation - the model is not independently replicated. Cited here only to state the claim, not to support an annotation.

title: Presynaptic α(2)δs specify synaptic gain, not synaptogenesis, in the mammalian brain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neuron 2025). Presynaptic triple conditional knockout of Cacna2d1/2/3 at the calyx of Held. Reassigns presynaptic alpha-2/delta to Munc13-1-dependent synaptic gain and finds synapse development, active-zone ultrastructure and transsynaptic alignment unaffected. Caveat recorded in the notes - it ablates three paralogues together and only presynaptically, so it does not test the original postsynaptic thrombospondin-receptor claim.

title: Tonic GABA and Glycine Inhibition Control Pain Hypersensitivity via Limiting α2δ-1- and mGluR5-Dependent NMDA Receptor Activity at Primary Afferent→Excitatory Neuron Synapses.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Neurosci 2025). Uses Cacna2d1 knockout mice and the alpha-2/delta-1 C-terminus peptide. Same laboratory as PMID:40191897 and PMID:42225412, so it corroborates rather than replicates.

title: Astrocyte Senescence Impairs Synaptogenesis due to Thrombospondin-1 Loss.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Aging Cell 2026). An independent group still using and supporting the thrombospondin-1/alpha-2/delta-1 synaptogenic signalling model in astrocyte-conditioned-medium experiments, which is why the synaptogenesis question is recorded as narrowed rather than settled.

title: Chaihu-Baishao confers antidepressant effects in CSDS mice by ameliorating hippocampal synaptic plasticity impairment via blocking α2δ-1-NR2B interaction.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Ethnopharmacol 2026). The nearest thing found to an out-of-house test of the alpha-2/delta-1-NMDAR model, using Cacna2d1-knockout cells and gabapentin, but it is a herbal-medicine efficacy study with molecular docking, and one author has a long publication history with the originating laboratory. Not treated as independent replication.

title: HIV-1 gp120 Induces Nociceptive Hypersensitivity via α2δ-1-Bound NMDA Receptors at Primary Afferent→Excitatory Neuron Synapses.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Neurosci 2026). Applies the alpha-2/delta-1-bound NMDAR model to HIV-1 gp120 nociception. Same laboratory as PMID:40191897 and PMID:41006062.

title: CACUL1/CAC1 Regulates the Antioxidant Response by Stabilizing Nrf2.
review_notes: PMID resolved from DOI 10.1038/srep12857 via NCBI and the cached title matches; supporting_text quotes are verbatim from the cached full text. title: CACUL1 reciprocally regulates SIRT1 and LSD1 to repress PPARγ and inhibit adipogenesis.
review_notes: PMID resolved from DOI 10.1038/s41419-017-0070-z via NCBI and the cached title matches; supporting_text quotes are verbatim from the cached full text. Establishes a SIRT1/LSD1-coupled nuclear-receptor (PPARgamma) transcription-corepressor activity, broadening the ERalpha co-regulator report.

title: Comprehensive proteomic analysis of interphase and mitotic 14-3-3-binding proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified proteomic screen; supports a 14-3-3 (YWHAZ) interaction but only a bare protein binding annotation, uninformative about CAD's molecular function.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.

review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary structural/functional study of human CAD - defines the multienzyme, the Zn2+-dependent DHOase mechanism, and homohexamer assembly. Anchor for core catalytic MFs.

title: Biallelic mutations in CAD, impair de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis and decrease glycosylation precursors.

title: Falcon deep research report for CALR3

Marked UNVERIFIED because the primary calsperin paper (Ikawa 2011, PMID:21343304 / doi:10.1074/jbc.M110.140152) is not in the local publications cache and its full text could not be independently checked here; the falcon synthesis is internally consistent with the cached UniProt record and PMID:21590275, and is used only as a verbatim supporting source for claims already corroborated by those records.

title: TBP-interacting protein 120B, which is induced in relation to myogenesis, binds to NOT3.

title: Proteolytic targeting of transcriptional regulator TIP120B by a HECT domain E3 ligase.

title: The identification of novel proteins that interact with the GLP-1 receptor and restrain its activity.

title: Modulation function of sphingomyelin molecular species in TLR4 signaling and cell death.

title: LPS-induced structural reorganization and polymerization drive noncanonical inflammasome activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached from PMC and quotes checked verbatim. Directly informs the CARD folding-on-LPS and polymerisation model and localises LPS recognition to an acyl-chain pocket.

title: Caspase-4 binds to LPS membranes with positive curvature for non-canonical inflammasome activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Immunity 2026, Broz lab); abstract-only in cache, full text not retrieved. Correctly cited, but its central claim - that caspase-4 engages LPS membranes of defined geometry rather than individual LPS molecules - is in tension with the direct LPS/lipid A binding measurements underlying the GO:0001530 IDAs and with the 2026 HDX-MS pocket mapping. Flagged as DISPUTED for that reason, not because of any citation defect.

review_notes: PubMed-verified (PLoS Pathog 2026); full text cached from PMC and quotes checked verbatim. The CASP3/CASP7 substrate claim is direct biochemistry but single-source, and the accompanying claim that most GSDMD cleavage in non-canonical signalling is CASP1-mediated is a cell-context flux argument that cuts against the widely reproduced CASP4-GSDMD axis. Contested rather than miscited.

title: The dynamic and heterogeneous structure of the non-canonical inflammasome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PNAS 2026); abstract-only in cache (publisher blocks PMC full text). Note the NMR work is on the caspase-11 CARD and protease domain, so its conclusions transfer to human CASP4 only by homology.

title: A novel Cas family member, HEPL, regulates FAK and cell spreading.

title: Overexpression of CASS4 promotes invasion in non-small cell lung cancer by activating the AKT signaling pathway and inhibiting E-cadherin expression.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports CASS4-dependent NSCLC invasion and AKT phosphorylation, useful for non-core downstream pathway and migration annotations.

title: A genetic polymorphism in the coding region of the gastric intrinsic factor gene (GIF) is associated with congenital intrinsic factor deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Reports the GIF Q5R (mature Q23R) coding polymorphism associated with congenital IF deficiency and shows recombinant IF is secreted with native-like properties; supports secreted localization and cobalamin binding of the protein.

title: Hereditary juvenile cobalamin deficiency caused by mutations in the intrinsic factor gene.

title: Structural basis for receptor recognition of vitamin-B(12)-intrinsic factor complexes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (abstract-only in cache). Crystal structure of the IF-Cbl complex bound to cubilin CUB(5-8); source of the CUBN IPI and defines cubam receptor recognition.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.

title: Human gastric intrinsic factor expression is not restricted to parietal cells.

title: UniProtKB entry P27352 (IF_HUMAN), Cobalamin binding intrinsic factor
review_notes: UniProt curated record; source of the FUNCTION (secreted cobalamin absorption via CUBN), SUBUNIT (interacts with CUBN via CUB domains), secreted subcellular location, gastric-mucosa tissue specificity, and IFD disease association.

title: Dissection of epistasis in oligogenic Bardet-Biedl syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes CCDC28B (MGC1203) as a BBS modifier that interacts and colocalizes with BBS proteins and localizes pericentriolarly; supports the centrosome localization and BBSome-interaction annotations.

title: Characterization of CCDC28B reveals its role in ciliogenesis and provides insight to understand its modifier effect on Bardet-Biedl syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Provides the loss-of-function (IMP) evidence that CCDC28B is required for ciliogenesis in cells and zebrafish; supports the cilium assembly core-function annotation.

title: The Bardet-Biedl syndrome-related protein CCDC28B modulates mTORC2 function and interacts with SIN1 to control cilia length independently of the mTOR complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes the SIN1/mTORC2 mechanism for cilium-length control; not currently the source of a GOA annotation but directly informs the core functions.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: PubMed-verified high-throughput binary interactome study (CCDC28B-ATRIP). Supports only an uninformative "protein binding" annotation; biological relevance to CCDC28B ciliary function is unestablished.

title: Falcon deep research report for CCDC28B
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report (Edison/Falcon). It corroborates the well-established, CCDC28B-specific picture already in this review - a non-enzymatic coiled-coil regulatory/adaptor protein that positively regulates ciliogenesis and cilium length, localizes to the ciliary basal body/axoneme, and acts as a BBS-associated modifier rather than a core BBSome subunit. Other assertions in the report are weaker, secondary, or generalize from BBSome/BBS-core biology rather than from CCDC28B-specific data and are NOT used to drive annotation changes here, including KIF5B-regulated nuclear accumulation/possible nuclear roles, BBS/CCT chaperonin coupling, regulatory-B-cell expression, brain-aging expression dynamics, rat hypertension/senescence SNPs, and the CCDC28A paralog characterization. Correctness UNVERIFIED because the report cites only internal keys/DOIs (no PMIDs) and is LLM-generated synthesis.

title: Falcon deep research report for CHAF1B
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report (Edison/Falcon); claims are machine-aggregated and not independently verified, so marked UNVERIFIED. The report's own summary table usefully distinguishes CHAF1B/p60 subunit-specific evidence from broader CAF-1 holo-complex inference. The strongest subunit-specific claims trace to the Liu et al. 2023 Science cryo-EM structure (add8673): that the p60 subunit is the principal H3-H4 binding component, contacting histone H4 through its ventral beta-propeller surface and engaging a partially unfolded H3 region, and that CHAF1B is required for CAF-1 histone binding and nucleosome assembly activity. The report also surfaces a CHAF1B-specific genome-stability function (Shrestha et al. 2023, jcs.260944): CHAF1B depletion causes CENP-A mislocalization and chromosomal instability. Many other statements (PCNA recruitment, heterochromatin/H3K9me3-H3K27me3 maintenance, viral latency, transcriptional/cell-fate control, cancer overexpression) are attributed to the CAF-1 holo-complex or to CHAF1B knockdown phenotypes rather than to a direct, isolated p60 molecular activity, and should not be transferred to CHAF1B as subunit-specific molecular functions without primary-source verification. None of the underlying primary papers are in the publications cache; supporting_text quotes below are verbatim from this report, not from the primary articles.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for CRYAA protein refolding (GO:0042026)
review_notes: Mechanistically sound and useful -- the holdase-not-foldase reasoning, the no-NBD architectural argument, and the identification of PMID:8093612 and PMID:1438232 as paralog-derived/mixed-oligomer evidence were all checked and hold up. However, the report's annotation-set enumeration is wrong in two ways that undercut its recommendations, so its verdict was not adopted. (1) It reports the GO:0042026 ISS (GO_REF:0000024) as positive supporting evidence; in CRYAA-goa.tsv that row is NOT|involved_in from bovine UniProtKB:P02470, i.e. it refutes rather than supports the hypothesis. This is the single most decisive datum for the seed hypothesis and the run missed it. (2) Its headline recommendation, ADD the "missing" GO:0051082 (unfolded protein binding), is a no-op -- GOA already carries three GO:0051082 annotations for P02489 (IBA GO_REF:0000033; IPI PMID:8943244 with UniProtKB:P07320; IMP PMID:18407550) -- and is also obsolete advice, since GO:0051082 is now a formally obsolete term whose GO obsoletion note directs replacement to GO:0044183 or GO:0140309 -- neither of which fits an in-situ holdase, so the run's "add GO:0051082" advice is doubly unusable. review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report. The safe, well-supported framing it conveys is that DCAF10 is a WD40 beta-propeller substrate-recognition receptor of CRL4 (DDB1-CUL4) that docks DDB1 via WDxR motifs and contributes to substrate ubiquitination; this is consistent with the founding DCAF biochemistry (PMID:16949367) and is now reinforced by a primary paper defining DCAF10 as an N-recognin for N-terminally acetylated glycine (Ac-Gly) degrons (Kremer et al. 2026, Nat Commun, PMID:41484149, in vitro reconstitution + AlphaFold3). The specific substrate and pathway claims (Src-family kinases via the Ac-Gly/MO N-degron pathway; RUVBL1/2 in adenovirus E1A hijacking, Zemke et al. 2023, PMID:37962355; ALOX15B in KRAS-mutant PDAC, Li et al. 2025, PMID:40569151; high testis expression, Mistry et al. 2020, PMID:32867693) are each supported by single primary studies not yet independently replicated, and the underlying full texts are NOT in the local publications cache, so they have not been verified against source here and are treated as promising-but-provisional rather than established core functions. No specific substrate or pathway is attributed to DCAF10 in this review beyond what a primary paper directly demonstrates.
