review_notes: Human genetic proof that FTO catalytic activity is essential - homozygous R316Q causes a lethal recessive polymalformation syndrome. PubMed-verified (Am J Hum Genet 2009). Not currently used as a GOA source for this gene but decisive for the in vivo importance of the enzyme.

title: Crystal structure of the FTO protein reveals basis for its substrate specificity.
review_notes: Structural basis for single-strand selectivity. Cached record is abstract-only; the abstract does not state ferrous iron binding explicitly, so the GO:0008198 IDA is taken on the curator's reading of the full structure.

title: N6-methyladenosine in nuclear RNA is a major substrate of the obesity-associated FTO.
review_notes: The in vitro m6A demethylation is not in question and the paper is correctly cited. Its central inference - that nuclear mRNA m6A is the major physiological substrate - is what the direct-sequencing reassessment (PMID:41279954) and the m6Am literature contest.

title: Meclofenamic acid selectively inhibits FTO demethylation of m6A over ALKBH5.
review_notes: Sound inhibitor biochemistry and structure. Supports in vitro m6A turnover; the cellular m6A readout is antibody-based and so inherits the substrate dispute.

title: FTO Obesity Variant Circuitry and Adipocyte Browning in Humans.
review_notes: Excellent paper, wrong gene for these annotations. It dissects the FTO locus and concludes the causal mechanism runs through IRX3 and IRX5; FTO protein is never perturbed. Used in GOA as the IMP source for two FTO biological-process annotations, which conflates locus with gene product. The annotations would be better re-homed to IRX3 and IRX5.

title: Fluorescein Derivatives as Bifunctional Molecules for the Simultaneous Inhibiting and Labeling of FTO Protein.
review_notes: Inhibitor and co-crystal study; supports in vitro FTO demethylase activity. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Dynamic m(6)A mRNA methylation directs translational control of heat shock response.
review_notes: Correctly cited and a genuine mutant-phenotype experiment, but the m6A readout is antibody-based, which is the methodology under challenge. It is the IMP leg of the contested GO:1990931 annotation.

title: Reversible methylation of m(6)A(m) in the 5' cap controls mRNA stability.
review_notes: Establishes cap m6Am as a preferred FTO substrate over m6A - one of the pillars of the substrate reassessment. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Differential m(6)A, m(6)A(m), and m(1)A Demethylation Mediated by FTO in the Cell Nucleus and Cytoplasm.
review_notes: The most informative single reference for this gene. Establishes the snRNA, U6 and tRNA m1A substrates alongside mRNA, and is candid that the tRNA m1A effect size dwarfs the mRNA m6A and cap m6Am effects in Fto-knockout cells.

title: Decoding m(6)Am by simultaneous transcription-start mapping and methylation quantification.
review_notes: Describes CROWN-seq, the quantitative m6Am method used as the FTO-activity positive control in PMID:41279954. Background rather than direct FTO evidence.

title: FTO degrader impairs ribosome biogenesis and protein translation in acute myeloid leukemia.
review_notes: Peer-reviewed 2025 support for the m6A-eraser model in AML, and the stronger of the two pro-m6A 2025 papers because degradation does not depend on active-site occupancy, so it is not vulnerable to the inhibitor-specificity objection. Its m6A quantification is still antibody-dependent.

title: Evidence human FTO catalyses hydroxylation of N6-methyladenosine without direct formation of a demethylated product contrasting with ALKBH5/2/3 and bacterial AlkB.
review_notes: Peer-reviewed comparative MS and real-time NMR study (Nucleic Acids Res 2025). Grounds the chemistry layer of the dispute - isolated FTO forms the hemiaminal hm6A rather than releasing formaldehyde itself. Its own caveat "at least in isolated form" is why the GO demethylase terms were not downgraded on this basis.

title: Structure-Based Design of a Highly Potent Dual-Competitive FTO Inhibitor for Targeted m(6)A Demethylase Inhibition in AML.
review_notes: Representative of the active drug-discovery literature that assumes the m6A-eraser model. Cited here to show that side of the dispute is current, not superseded. Its cellular m6A readouts are antibody-based, and the claim that FTO inhibitors act through FTO is exactly what PMID:41279954 challenges. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: FTO depletion does not alter m(6)A stoichiometry in AML mRNA: a reassessment using direct RNA nanopore sequencing.
review_notes: PREPRINT (bioRxiv, Oct 2025) - not peer reviewed, and marked UNVERIFIED for that reason rather than for any identified defect. Weighed as substantial but not decisive: it is methodologically orthogonal to MeRIP rather than a failed replication, it carries an internal positive control (snRNA m6Am rises as expected, confirming FTO activity was abolished), and it converges with peer-reviewed prior work (PMID:28002401, PMID:30197295) and with an independent chemistry result (PMID:40874592). Used here to demote GO:1990931 from core, never to remove an annotation.

title: Transmembrane topology of human glucose 6-phosphate transporter.
review_notes: Primarily about the G6P transporter (SLC37A4/G6PT); establishes that the glucose-6-phosphatase active site is situated in the ER lumen. Supports the luminal-active-site location of the G6PC1 system.

title: Glucose-6-phosphatase mutation G188R confers an atypical glycogen storage disease type 1b phenotype.
review_notes: G188R loss-of-function G6PC1 variant; supports glucose-6-phosphatase catalytic activity and the GSD1a disease association.

title: The catalytic center of glucose-6-phosphatase. HIS176 is the nucleophile forming the phosphohistidine-enzyme intermediate during catalysis.
review_notes: Defines the catalytic mechanism (His-176 nucleophile, His-119 proton donor); primary support for glucose-6-phosphatase activity.

title: Glycogen storage disease type Ia in Argentina: two novel glucose-6-phosphatase mutations affecting protein stability.
review_notes: T16R and Y209C variants abolish enzymatic activity in expression assays; supports glucose-6-phosphatase activity and GSD1a.

title: Brain contains a functional glucose-6-phosphatase complex capable of endogenous glucose production.
review_notes: Abstract foregrounds glucose-6-phosphatase-beta (G6PC3) in astrocytes; cited by MGI for a G6PC1 IDA of glucose-6-phosphatase activity. Function is correct for G6PC1, but the abstract does not directly assay G6PC1.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome screen; source of bare protein-binding IPI annotations (WFS1, RNF11). No functional consequence established for G6PC1.

title: Mutations in the glucose-6-phosphatase gene that cause glycogen storage disease type 1a.
review_notes: Cloning and expression of human G6Pase; inactivating GSD1a mutations. Primary support for glucose-6-phosphatase activity, gluconeogenesis, and glucose homeostasis.

title: Glycogen storage disease type 1a in Israel: biochemical, clinical, and mutational studies.
review_notes: States G6Pase catalyzes the final common step of glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis; V166G variant causes complete inactivation.

title: Transmembrane topology of glucose-6-phosphatase.
review_notes: Establishes nine-TM ER membrane topology with luminal active site and His-176 as catalytic phosphoryl acceptor; primary support for ER membrane location.

title: Histidine 167 is the phosphate acceptor in glucose-6-phosphatase-beta forming a phosphohistidine enzyme intermediate during catalysis.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache but directly establishes the catalytic mechanism and active-site residues of G6PC3 (G6Pase-beta); supports the core MF.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Generic high-throughput membrane proteomics; supports only a non-specific membrane localization, superseded by ER membrane. Not G6PC3-specific.

title: Functional analysis of mutations in a severe congenital neutropenia syndrome caused by glucose-6-phosphatase-β deficiency.
review_notes: Full text available (PMC4794745). Directly supports G6PC3 catalytic activity, ER-membrane localization, SLC37A4/G6PT partnership, and the SCN4 disease mechanism. Basis of the IMP GO:0004346 annotation.

title: Cell growth and cholesterol metabolism in human glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficient lymphomononuclear cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports an indirect NADPH-supply role of G6PD in cholesterol synthesis (G6PD-deficient PBMC show reduced cholesterol synthesis).

title: Structural studies of glucose-6-phosphate and NADP+ binding to human glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified human G6PD structural study; directly supports catalytic activity, NADP binding (catalytic and structural sites), substrate binding, and homo-oligomerization.

title: Production of inflammatory molecules in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from severely glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase-deficient subjects.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports only an indirect lipid/inflammatory phenotype of G6PD deficiency, not a direct lipid-metabolic function.

title: Mutation in G6PD gene leads to loss of cellular control of protein glutathionylation: mechanism and implication.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; strongly supports G6PD's role in glutathione metabolism and the cellular oxidative-stress response via NADPH.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; incidental localization of an abundant cytosolic enzyme.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane proteomics; peripheral/incidental membrane association, not a primary functional site.

title: ATM activates the pentose phosphate pathway promoting anti-oxidant defence and DNA repair.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text; documents HSPB1/Hsp27 binding and direct stimulation of G6PD activity in the ATM oxidative-stress/DNA-damage response.

title: Quantitative proteomic analysis of human substantia nigra in Alzheimer's disease, Huntington's disease and Multiple sclerosis.
review_notes: Disease proteomics survey; detection/altered expression does not support a substantia nigra developmental role for G6PD (HEP annotation over-interpreted).

title: Sex steroid hormone modulation of NADPH pathways in MCF-7 cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; measures G6PD activity and NADPH-generating pathways, supporting the pentose phosphate shunt annotation.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; incidental localization of an abundant cytosolic enzyme.

title: Ribose metabolism and nucleic acid synthesis in normal and glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase-deficient human erythrocytes infected with Plasmodium falciparum.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; deficiency-based evidence for the oxidative-branch PPP role, glutathione maintenance, and ribose-phosphate contribution.

title: Regulation of G6PD acetylation by SIRT2 and KAT9 modulates NADPH homeostasis and cell survival during oxidative stress.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports catalytic activity, K403 acetylation-dependent regulation, homodimerization requirement, and the SIRT2 interaction.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome map; corroborates G6PD self-interaction (identical protein binding).

title: Severe G6PD Deficiency Due to a New Missense Mutation in an Infant of Northern European Descent.
review_notes: PubMed-verified case report; very low enzymatic activity of a novel variant supports the catalytic function and X-linked deficiency phenotype.

title: Aldolase B suppresses hepatocellular carcinogenesis by inhibiting G6PD and pentose phosphate pathways.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; identifies G6PD as the rate-limiting PPP enzyme, directly assays its activity, and documents the ALDOB-G6PD-TP53 ternary complex.

title: Substitution of arginine 219 by glycine compromises stability, dimerization, and catalytic activity in a G6PD mutant.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text; direct biochemical/biophysical evidence for catalytic activity, dimerization, and substrate binding of human G6PD.

title: Biochemical variants of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase giving rise to congenital nonspherocytic hemolytic disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified classic study; variant enzymes causing CNSHA support the catalytic function and erythrocyte oxidative-defense role.

title: Glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase activity in membranes of erythrocytes from normal individuals and subjects with Mediterranean G6PD deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports catalytic activity, cytosolic localization, and a minor peripheral membrane-associated pool in erythrocytes.

title: Mutation profile of the GAA gene in 40 Italian patients with late onset glycogen storage disease type II.
review_notes: Late-onset Pompe mutation-profile study; establishes that GAA deficiency impairs glycogen degradation with lysosomal accumulation. Supports the disease context but the diaphragm-contraction annotation derived from it is a disease consequence, not a molecular function.

title: Integral and associated lysosomal membrane proteins.
review_notes: Placental lysosomal-membrane proteome; basis for UniProt's lysosome and lysosome-membrane location. GAA co-purifies with lysosomal membranes though it is a soluble lumenal enzyme.

title: Molecular and functional characterization of eight novel GAA mutations in Italian infants with Pompe disease.
review_notes: Functional (enzyme-activity) characterization of GAA missense mutants; supports the alpha-1,4-glucosidase activity annotation. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Human lysosomal alpha-glucosidase. Characterization of the catalytic site.
review_notes: Defines the catalytic residues (Trp-516, Asp-518) of GAA via inhibitor labelling and mutagenesis; strong support for the core catalytic activity.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary exosome proteomics; incidental detection of GAA, not a specific functional localization.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: NK-cell (YTS) membrane-proteome dataset; incidental detection of GAA in a generic membrane fraction.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput prostatic-secretion exosome proteomics; incidental detection of GAA, not a specific functional localization.

title: The molecular heterogeneity of purified human liver lysosomal alpha-glucosidase (acid alpha-glucosidase).
review_notes: Purification/characterization of human liver acid alpha-glucosidase; basis for the IDA alpha-1,4- and alpha-1,6-glucosidase activity annotations. Cached record is title-only.

title: Structure of human lysosomal acid α-glucosidase-a guide for the treatment of Pompe disease.
review_notes: High-resolution rhGAA crystal structures with substrate analogues; assigns catalytic residues D518/D616, documents preference for alpha-1,4 over alpha-1,6 linkages, M6P targeting and proteolytic maturation. Full text available; central reference for the molecular function and mechanism.

title: Simultaneous absence of alpha-1,4-glucosidase and alpha-1,6-glucosidase activities (pH 4) in tissues of children with type II glycogen storage disease.
review_notes: Classic demonstration that both acid alpha-1,4- and alpha-1,6-glucosidase activities are absent in GSD II tissues, establishing GAA as the acid alpha-glucosidase. Cached record is title-only.

title: Leaky splicing mutation in the acid maltase gene is associated with delayed onset of glycogenosis type II.
review_notes: Genotype-phenotype study relating residual GAA activity (~12% of normal) to delayed-onset GSD II; supports the catalytic activity annotation.

title: Recombinant human acid alpha-glucosidase corrects acid alpha-glucosidase-deficient human fibroblasts, quail fibroblasts, and quail myoblasts.
review_notes: ERT proof-of-concept: recombinant GAA normalizes glycogen in deficient cells, is taken up by M6P-receptor-mediated endocytosis, and localizes to lysosomes. Supports alpha-1,4-glucosidase activity, glycogen catabolism and lysosomal localization.

title: UniProtKB entry P10253 (LYAG_HUMAN), lysosomal alpha-glucosidase
review_notes: Primary UniProt record for GAA; source of the FUNCTION, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY, SUBCELLULAR LOCATION, PTM (M6P targeting, proteolytic maturation) and GH31 family assignments used throughout this review.

title: Alternative splicing of GAD67 results in the synthesis of a third form of glutamic-acid decarboxylase in human islets and other non-neural tissues.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes GAD67 enzymatic activity and describes the enzymatically inactive GAD25 splice variant (isoform 3) in non-neural tissues. Source of IDA for glutamate decarboxylase activity and TAS for L-glutamate catabolic process. Abstract-only cache.

title: Two human glutamate decarboxylases, 65-kDa GAD and 67-kDa GAD, are each encoded by a single gene.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cloning of human GAD65 and GAD67 cDNAs; shows both encode enzymatically active decarboxylases (EC 4.1.1.15) and maps GAD67 to 2q31.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Proteome-scale Y2H interactome (CCSB-HI1); source of a bare protein-binding IPI. Not informative about GAD1's specific function.

title: GABA production by glutamic acid decarboxylase is regulated by a dynamic catalytic loop.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Crystal structures of GAD67 and GAD65; establishes catalytic activity, PLP cofactor, homodimer, and that GAD67 is constitutively active for basal GABA production. Primary experimental support (IDA) for the core functions. Abstract-only cache.

title: Systematic identification of SH3 domain-mediated human protein-protein interactions by peptide array target screening.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. SH3-domain peptide-array (PATS) systematic screen; source of a bare protein-binding IPI. Not informative about GAD1's specific function.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Stitch-seq NGS-based high-throughput Y2H interactome; source of a bare protein-binding IPI. Not informative about GAD1's specific function.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Systematic binary interactome map (HI-II-14); source of a bare protein-binding IPI. Not informative about GAD1's specific function.

title: Widespread Expansion of Protein Interaction Capabilities by Alternative Splicing.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Isoform-resolved interactome profiling; source of bare protein-binding IPIs. Not informative about GAD1's specific function.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Variant-interactome disruption study (Y2H/PCA); source of a bare protein-binding IPI. Not informative about GAD1's specific function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. HuRI all-by-all human binary interactome reference map; source of bare protein-binding IPIs. Not informative about GAD1's specific function.

title: Mice lacking the 65 kDa isoform of glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD65) maintain normal levels of GAD67 and GABA in their brains but are susceptible to seizures.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. GAD65-knockout mice retain normal GAD67 and brain GABA levels but are seizure-prone, supporting GAD67's role as the constitutive GABA-synthesizing enzyme and its link to synaptic (inhibitory) transmission.

title: Paranodal junction formation and spermatogenesis require sulfoglycolipids.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 2002;99:4227-32), full text available via PMC123630. The mouse Cst/Gal3st1 knockout. This is the experimental grounding behind the myelination IBA (WITH/FROM MGI:MGI:1858277) and behind the claim that a single gene makes both sulfatide and seminolipid.

title: Histone tyrosine sulfation by SULT1B1 regulates H4R3me2a and gene transcription.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Chem Biol 2023;19:855-864). Defines the H3Y99sulf mark that PMID:41686426 later attributes to GAL3ST1, and attributes it to a different enzyme (SULT1B1). Formally contested by PMID:40890505; the authors replied (PMID:40890506) and an Author Correction was issued (PMID:40890508). Not retracted. Cited only to document the dispute; no GAL3ST1 annotation derives from it.

title: Mass spectrometry and enzyme assays refute histone tyrosine sulfation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Chem Biol 2025;21:1667-1670), full text available via PMC12978989. A formal Matters Arising arguing that the H3Y99sulf spectra fit a phosphotyrosine peptide, that sulfotyrosine cannot give the reported 100% sulfate-retaining HCD fragments, and that recombinant enzyme gave no histone H3.2 sulfation. Bears on GAL3ST1 because it questions the existence of the mark and the specificity of the antibody used to detect it. Marked DISPUTED because the original authors contest it, not because of any citation problem.

title: Reply to: Mass spectrometry and enzyme assays refute histone tyrosine sulfation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Chem Biol 2025;21:1671-1674). The original authors' reply. No abstract in PubMed and the cached record is abstract-only, so its arguments could not be assessed. Its existence is why the dispute is treated as unresolved rather than settled.

title: GAL3ST1-Mediated Histone Tyrosine Sulfation Induced by Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Promotes Gastric Cancer Metastasis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cancer Res 2026;86:2429-2446), full text available via PMC13176828. Claims GAL3ST1 is a histone sulfotransferase writing H3Y99sulf in the cytosol. Three concerns: the mark itself is contested by PMID:40890505, which this paper does not cite; the readouts rest on the anti-H3Y99sulf antibody class the refutation says needs further validation; and the proposed cytosolic reaction is hard to reconcile with GAL3ST1's type II Golgi topology, since the in vitro assay used purified soluble His-GAL3ST1. No GO annotation for GAL3ST1 currently derives from this paper.

title: Purification and characterization of 3'-phosphoadenosine-5'-phosphosulfate:GalCer sulfotransferase from human renal cancer cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biochem 1996;119:421-7). Purification to homogeneity of the human enzyme with a systematic acceptor panel; the direct basis for the galactosylceramide sulfotransferase, sphingolipid and glycerolipid annotations.

title: Molecular cloning and expression of cDNA encoding human 3'-phosphoadenylylsulfate:galactosylceramide 3'-sulfotransferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 1997;272:4864-8). Correct and important paper, but note that two legacy TAS annotations traced to it are misreadings: plasma membrane (the paper places the product sulfatide, not the enzyme, at the cell surface) and protein N-linked glycosylation (the paper only notes two potential N-glycosylation sites in GAL3ST1 itself). Both are marked REMOVE.

title: Implications of galactocerebrosidase and galactosylcerebroside metabolism in cancer cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified review describing GALC as the enzyme degrading galactosylcerebroside to ceramide. Correctly supports the catabolic role but is a review (used as IDA in GOA), so it corroborates rather than establishes the core function.

title: Endolysosomes Are the Principal Intracellular Sites of Acid Hydrolase Activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified general study establishing that endolysosomes are the principal sites of acid hydrolase activity. It does not assay GALC; it underpins the curator (IC) inference for GALC's endolysosome-lumen localization only indirectly.

title: The mechanism of glycosphingolipid degradation revealed by a GALC-SapA complex structure.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. GALC-SapA complex structure defining the saposin-A dependent mechanism of galactocerebroside cleavage in the endolysosomal compartment. Directly relevant to GALC's mechanism and localization.

title: Structure and organization of the human galactocerebrosidase (GALC) gene.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Gene-structure paper that also states GALC catalyzes lysosomal hydrolysis of galactolipids including galactosylceramide and galactosylsphingosine (psychosine); supports catalytic function and lysosomal localization.

title: Cloning and expression of cDNA encoding human galactocerebrosidase, the enzyme deficient in globoid cell leukodystrophy.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary paper cloning and expressing human GALC cDNA; establishes GALC as responsible for lysosomal catabolism of galactosylceramide.

title: Galactocerebrosidase from human urine: purification and partial characterization.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary biochemistry; purification and enzymatic characterization of human GALC (EC 3.2.1.46), including acid pH optimum and KM. Direct support for the core molecular function.

title: Crystallographic evidence for Tyr 157 functioning as the active site base in human UDP-galactose 4-epimerase.
review_notes: Crystal structure of human GALE in complex with NAD and UDP-glucose; establishes the bound NAD+ cofactor, the homodimer, and Tyr157 as the active-site proton acceptor.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome screen; source of the Q14376-Q14376 self-interaction (identical protein binding) annotation. Consistent with the known homodimer but does not directly inform GALE's catalytic function.

title: Functional analysis of disease-causing mutations in human UDP-galactose 4-epimerase.
review_notes: Direct enzymatic characterization of recombinant human GALE and disease variants; supports the core epimerase activity, homodimerization, and role in galactose catabolism / type III galactosemia.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome map; source of a GALE self-interaction annotation.

title: A massively parallel pipeline to clone DNA variants and examine molecular phenotypes of human disease mutations.
review_notes: Large-scale variant/interaction phenotyping pipeline; source of a GALE self-interaction annotation.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Systematic study of variant-driven interaction disruption; source of a GALE self-interaction annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome; source of a GALE self-interaction annotation consistent with the homodimer.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline. Correctly transfers galactokinase and ATP-binding terms from GHMP-kinase/galactokinase InterPro signatures, but also assigns generic parent MF terms (kinase activity, phosphotransferase) that are less informative than the specific galactokinase activity term.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/GO_Central phylogenetic (IBA) annotations. The three IBA calls (galactokinase activity, galactose metabolic process, cytosol) match the experimentally established function and localization of the human enzyme.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automated (ARBA/ensembl/RHEA/EC) pipeline. Correctly infers galactokinase activity and Leloir-pathway galactose catabolism.

title: Functional analysis of disease-causing mutations in human galactokinase.
review_notes: Purified recombinant human GALK1 characterized kinetically (ordered ternary mechanism, ATP first; KM ~970 uM galactose, ~34 uM ATP) and multiple disease-causing variants assayed. Basis for galactokinase-activity and ATP-binding IDA annotations and the EC 2.7.1.6 catalytic-activity assertion.

title: Sugar recognition by human galactokinase.
review_notes: Full-text available. Establishes substrate/sugar recognition of the human enzyme: D-galactose and 2-deoxy-D-galactose are substrates; D-glucose, D-fucose, L-arabinose and N-acetyl-D-galactosamine are not phosphorylated. Basis for the galactose-binding IDA annotation.

title: Biochemical characterization of two GALK1 mutations in patients with galactokinase deficiency.
review_notes: Biochemical characterization of the V32M and R239Q GALK1 variants in patients, showing drastic reduction of GALK activity, establishing pathogenicity and the enzyme's role in galactose metabolism (IMP).

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary exosome proteomics; GALK1 detected as one of many co-purifying proteins. Localization is incidental, not a functional site for this soluble metabolic enzyme.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput NK-cell membrane proteome. The resulting "membrane" localization is a proteomic co-purification and is directly contradicted by the curated NOT|located_in membrane IDA (PMID:8908517).

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI high-throughput yeast two-hybrid interactome. Reports a single binary interactor (PNRC2, Q9NPJ4). Supports only a bare, uninformative "protein binding" annotation with no established functional consequence.

title: Comparison of the enzymatic activities of human galactokinase GALK1 and a related human galactokinase protein GK2.
review_notes: Demonstrates that GALK1 (expressed in COS cells) produces high galactokinase activity and is the major galactose-metabolizing enzyme, distinguishing it from the related GK2 protein. Basis for the EXP and IDA galactokinase-activity annotations.

title: Fine structure of the human galactokinase GALK1 gene.
review_notes: In vitro translation shows the GALK1 protein is cytosolic and not associated with the ER membrane. Basis for the cytoplasm IDA and the NOT|membrane IDA (informative negation).

title: Defective GALK1 does not phosphorylate Gal
review_notes: Reactome reaction annotation capturing GALK1 galactokinase activity in the cytosol.

title: GALK1 phosphorylates Gal to Gal1P
review_notes: Reactome reaction: GALK1 phosphorylates galactose to galactose 1-phosphate in the cytosol. Directly captures the core Leloir-pathway step.

title: Galactose catabolism
review_notes: Reactome "Galactose catabolism" pathway; basis for the Leloir-pathway galactose catabolic process TAS annotation.

title: Identification and characterisation of human aldose 1-epimerase.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false), but the abstract directly establishes GALM's core aldose 1-epimerase activity and galactose preference; PMID matches title.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput proteomics survey supporting only the extracellular-exosome detection (non-core); does not inform GALM's catalytic function.

title: Biallelic GALM pathogenic variants cause a novel type of galactosemia.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; establishes the disease relevance (galactosemia type IV) and, via variant characterization, supports GALM's role in the Leloir galactose catabolic pathway.

title: Sulphatase activities are regulated by the interaction of sulphatase-modifying factor 1 with SUMF2.
review_notes: PMC full text available. Establishes the SUMF1/formylglycine dependence shared by GALNS; GALNS is among the sulphatases assayed. Supports the general sulfatase-maturation requirement rather than a GALNS-specific function.

title: Distinct effects of N-acetylgalactosamine-4-sulfatase and galactose-6-sulfatase expression on chondroitin sulfates.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache, but the abstract explicitly links GALNS expression to cellular chondroitin sulfate content in MCF-7 cells; supports the chondroitin sulfate catabolic-process annotation.

title: The structure of human GALNS reveals the molecular basis for mucopolysaccharidosis IV A.
review_notes: PMC full text. Definitive structural and enzymological characterisation of human GALNS; the primary support for the core molecular function, formylglycine mechanism, and homodimeric Ca2+ cofactor biology.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput proteomic detection in prostatic-secretion exosomes; supports extracellular-exosome localisation only, not a core function.

title: Expression, activity and localization of lysosomal sulfatases in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
review_notes: PMC full text. Direct immunolocalisation evidence for lysosomal localisation of GALNS; source of the IDA lysosome annotation.

title: N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfate sulfatase in man. Absence of the enzyme in Morquio disease.
review_notes: UniProt cites this (ECO:0000269|PubMed:820716) for FUNCTION and CATALYTIC ACTIVITY. Not separately annotated in GOA but underpins the core molecular function.

title: Mucopolysaccharidosis IV A: assignment of the human N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfate sulfatase (GALNS) gene to chromosome 16q24.
review_notes: This is a gene-mapping (FISH/chromosome-assignment) abstract for GALNS. It was cited (TAS) to support GO:0003943 N-acetylgalactosamine-4-sulfatase activity, but GALNS is a 6-sulfatase (EC 3.1.6.4); the 4-sulfatase is ARSB. The paper does not support a 4-sulfatase activity.

title: The human galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase gene.
review_notes: Cloning of the human GALT gene; establishes GALT deficiency as the cause of classic galactosemia and reports the common Q188R variant. Abstract verified.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome map; source of a bare protein-binding IPI. Not functionally informative for GALT.

title: Molecular characterization of two galactosemia mutations: correlation of mutations with highly conserved domains in galactose-1-phosphate uridyl transferase.
review_notes: Characterizes galactosemia missense variants (Q188R, R333W) by effect on GALT enzymatic activity; supports the core uridylyltransferase function.

title: The Lyn kinase C-lobe mediates Golgi export of Lyn through conformation-dependent ACSL3 association.
review_notes: Paper is about Lyn kinase/ACSL3 Golgi trafficking, not GALT. Cited as the basis of a GALT Golgi-apparatus IDA that is almost certainly mis-attributed; that localization is therefore flagged as MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED (retained, not removed, pending full-text confirmation).

title: Correlation assessment among clinical phenotypes, expression analysis and molecular modeling of 14 novel variations in the human galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase gene.
review_notes: In vitro kinetic characterization (Vmax/KM) of recombinant human GALT and variants; direct support for the uridylyltransferase activity. Full text verified.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome map; bare protein-binding IPI source, not functionally informative for GALT.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Interactome-perturbation study; bare protein-binding IPI source, not functionally informative for GALT.

title: Widespread Expansion of Protein Interaction Capabilities by Alternative Splicing.
review_notes: Systematic splicing-isoform interactome study; bare protein-binding IPI source, not functionally informative for GALT.

title: Molecular basis of classic galactosemia from the structure of human galactose 1-phosphate uridylyltransferase.
review_notes: 1.9 A crystal structure of human GALT (PDB 5IN3) with covalent uridylyl-His186 intermediate and Glc-1-P; establishes homodimer, catalytic mechanism, and structural zinc site. Full text verified.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome/community study; bare protein-binding IPI source, not functionally informative for GALT.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Reference binary interactome map; multiple bare protein-binding IPIs, not functionally informative for GALT.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Dual proteome-scale interactome study; bare protein-binding IPI source, not functionally informative for GALT.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput BioPlex interactome screen; source of a generic GAMT protein-binding (IPI) annotation with no characterized functional consequence.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome screen; source of a generic GAMT protein-binding (IPI) annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 proteome-scale interactome; source of a generic GAMT protein-binding (IPI) annotation.

title: Cloning and sequence analysis of human guanidinoacetate N-methyltransferase cDNA.
review_notes: Correctly identifies and clones human GAMT cDNA, but is used to support a 'muscle contraction' (GO:0006936) annotation, which is a distal physiological consequence rather than a direct GAMT process.

title: Guanidinoacetate methyltransferase deficiency: the first inborn error of creatine metabolism in man.
review_notes: First report of GAMT deficiency; provides IDA/IMP support for GAMT activity and creatine biosynthesis and establishes the disease.

title: The human guanidinoacetate methyltransferase (GAMT) gene maps to a syntenic region on 19p13.3, homologous to band C of mouse chromosome 10, but GAMT is not mutated in jittery mice.
review_notes: GAMT gene mapping/characterization paper; consistent with the creatine biosynthetic role.

title: Guanidinoacetate N-methyltransferase (GAMT), Homo sapiens - UniProtKB Q14353
review_notes: UniProt record for the gene under review; establishes the catalytic activity, pathway step, cytosolic reaction context and disease association.

title: Crystal structures of human GAR Tfase at low and high pH and with substrate beta-GAR.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Crystal structures of the human GAR transformylase (purN) domain with substrate beta-GAR; provides EXP support for GO:0004644 and establishes GAR Tfase as a folate-dependent antitumor drug target. PubMed-verified.

title: Rational design, synthesis, evaluation, and crystal structure of a potent inhibitor of human GAR Tfase: 10-(trifluoroacetyl)-5,10-dideazaacyclic-5,6,7,8-tetrahydrofolic acid.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Structure-based folate-analogue inhibitor of human GAR Tfase (Ki=15 nM), an improvement over Lometrexol; supports GO:0004644 (EXP) and the antifolate-target framing. PubMed-verified.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only. A B-cell exosome proteome MS survey that identified 539 proteins; the basis of the extracellular-exosome HDA localization. High-throughput bulk proteomics, not a specific GART localization or function claim.

title: Cloning and in vivo expression of the human GART gene using yeast artificial chromosomes.
review_notes: Abstract-only. YAC cloning of the full-length human GART gene; confirms the trifunctional GARS-GART-AIRS protein and maps it to 21q22.1. TAS basis for the GAR transformylase activity.

title: Cloning of three human multifunctional de novo purine biosynthetic genes by functional complementation of yeast mutations.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Functional complementation of yeast ade5/ade7/ade8 mutations by a single human cDNA establishes the trifunctional GARS-AIRS-GART protein; primary basis of the MGI IDA annotations for the three activities, cytosol, and de novo IMP biosynthesis. PubMed-verified.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; supports only an incidental co-purification, not a functional extracellular location for this mitochondrial enzyme.

title: Arginine:glycine amidinotransferase (AGAT) deficiency: Clinical features and long term outcomes in 16 patients diagnosed worldwide.
review_notes: Clinical cohort establishing AGAT deficiency as a treatable creatine-deficiency disorder (intellectual disability, myopathy); used (via CAFA) for the learning/memory and muscle atrophy annotations, which are downstream disease consequences rather than core functions.

title: Arginine-Glycine Amidinotransferase Deficiency and Functional Characterization of Missense Variants in GATM.
review_notes: Functional assays of GATM missense variants directly measuring glycine amidinotransferase activity; supports the core MF annotation and links activity loss to pathogenicity.

title: Genetic Depletion of Adipocyte Creatine Metabolism Inhibits Diet-Induced Thermogenesis and Drives Obesity.
review_notes: Mouse adipocyte-specific Gatm knockout; basis for the cold-induced thermogenesis annotations. Establishes a tissue-specific physiological role of creatine energetics, retained as non-core for the human gene.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome/Y2H map; source of 13 uninformative protein binding IPI annotations. No defined functional GATM complex established.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; corroborates mitochondrial localization.

title: Guanidino acid hydrolysis by the human enzyme annotated as agmatinase.
review_notes: Demonstrates purified human GATM amidinates glycine (preferred) plus GABA, beta-alanine and taurine; supports both the specific and parent amidinotransferase MF annotations.

title: The purification and characterization of human kidney L-arginine:glycine amidinotransferase.
review_notes: Classic purification/characterization of human AGAT as a dimeric transamidinase; supports the core catalytic activity.

title: Crystal structure and mechanism of human L-arginine:glycine amidinotransferase: a mitochondrial enzyme involved in creatine biosynthesis.
review_notes: Crystal structure and mechanism; supports the core MF, the creatine biosynthetic process, and the mitochondrial intermembrane space localization.

title: Substrate binding and catalysis by L-arginine:glycine amidinotransferase--a mutagenesis and crystallographic study.
review_notes: Mutagenesis/crystallography defining catalytic residues; supports the core glycine amidinotransferase activity.

title: Use of fluorescent substrates for characterization of Gaucher disease mutations.
review_notes: Supports the core glucosylceramidase activity via variant analysis with fluorescent GlcCer substrates. Abstract verified.

title: Analyses of variant acid beta-glucosidases: effects of Gaucher disease mutations.
review_notes: Direct enzymatic characterization of wild-type and mutant GCase; establishes the core acid beta-glucosidase / glucosylceramidase activity and saposin-C dependence.

title: Structure of acid beta-glucosidase with pharmacological chaperone provides insight into Gaucher disease.
review_notes: Crystal structure of GCase; supports lysosomal-membrane-associated localization and active-site biology.

title: Integral and associated lysosomal membrane proteins.
review_notes: Lysosomal membrane proteomics; supports GBA lysosomal-membrane localization (HDA).

title: LIMP-2 is a receptor for lysosomal mannose-6-phosphate-independent targeting of beta-glucocerebrosidase.
review_notes: Landmark paper identifying LIMP-2/SCARB2 as the M6P-independent trafficking receptor for GCase; grounds the ER/Golgi/TGN transit and lysosomal localization annotations.

title: Acid beta-glucosidase 1 counteracts p38delta-dependent induction of interleukin-6: possible role for ceramide as an anti-inflammatory lipid.
review_notes: Supports downstream ceramide-mediated signalling (IL-6/p38/MAPK) roles in MCF-7 cells; these are indirect, non-core physiological effects of GBA-generated ceramide.

title: Involvement of acid beta-glucosidase 1 in the salvage pathway of ceramide formation.
review_notes: Establishes that GBA1 hydrolyses GlcCer to lysosomal ceramide and feeds the PKC-activated ceramide salvage pathway; supports the core hydrolase activity and the non-core ceramide/sphingosine terms.

title: Decreased glucocerebrosidase activity in Gaucher disease parallels quantitative enzyme loss due to abnormal interaction with TCP1 and c-Cbl.
review_notes: Underlies the TCP1 'protein binding' IPI; relates to GCase folding/quality control, not core function.

title: Gaucher disease glucocerebrosidase and α-synuclein form a bidirectional pathogenic loop in synucleinopathies.
review_notes: Loss of GCase compromises lysosomal degradation and accumulates alpha-synuclein; supports core activity/process and the Parkinson-disease link.

title: Beta-glucosidase 1 (GBA1) is a second bile acid β-glucosidase in addition to β-glucosidase 2 (GBA2). Study in β-glucosidase deficient mice and humans.
review_notes: Shows GBA1 hydrolyses glucosylceramide (main substrate) and also bile-acid-beta-glucoside; supports core glucosylceramidase and broad beta-glucosidase activities.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; source of the non-core extracellular-exosome HDA localization.

title: Loss of β-glucocerebrosidase activity does not affect alpha-synuclein levels or lysosomal function in neuronal cells.
review_notes: Pharmacological GCase inhibition study (assays beta-glucocerebrosidase activity); supports the core activity as the manipulated variable, though it reports no alpha-synuclein effect.

title: Functional analysis of 11 novel GBA alleles.
review_notes: Variant functional analysis; supports core acid beta-glucosidase activity and glucosylceramide catabolism.

title: Structure of LIMP-2 provides functional insights with implications for SR-BI and CD36.
review_notes: LIMP-2 crystal structure showing where beta-glucocerebrosidase binds; underlies the LIMP-2 'protein binding' IPI (non-core trafficking interaction).

title: Cholesterol glucosylation is catalyzed by transglucosylation reaction of β-glucosidase 1.
review_notes: Demonstrates GBA1 transglucosylation forming cholesteryl-glucoside; supports the non-core transglucosylase/ glycolipid-biosynthetic and steryl-beta-glucosidase activities.

title: The LIMP-2/SCARB2 binding motif on acid β-glucosidase: basic and applied implications for Gaucher disease and associated neurodegenerative diseases.
review_notes: Maps the 11-residue LIMP-2/SCARB2-binding motif on GCase; supports lysosomal localization (LIMP-2-dependent) and the scavenger-receptor-binding annotation.

title: iPSC-derived dopamine neurons reveal differences between monozygotic twins discordant for Parkinson's disease.
review_notes: Source of the two supported NOT annotations (normal mitochondria and normal neurite outgrowth in GBA-N370S neurons) and the (over-annotated) neuronal-action-potential term.

title: Identification of miRNAs that modulate glucocerebrosidase activity in Gaucher disease cells.
review_notes: miRNA modulation of GCase activity in Gaucher cells; supports the core glucosylceramidase activity/process.

title: Mitochondrial dysfunction associated with glucocerebrosidase deficiency.
review_notes: Review establishing GCase as a lysosomal sphingolipid-metabolism enzyme (GlcCer -> glucose + ceramide) and the indirect autophagy/mitochondrial consequences of its deficiency.

title: Glucocerebrosidase gene therapy prevents α-synucleinopathy of midbrain dopamine neurons.
review_notes: GCase gene therapy reduces alpha-synuclein in PD models; underlies the (over-annotated) lysosomal-protein-catabolism link, which is indirect.

title: Glucosylated cholesterol in mammalian cells and tissues: formation and degradation by multiple cellular β-glucosidases.
review_notes: Shows GBA both synthesizes and degrades glucosylated cholesterol via transglucosylation, and restates the core role (GBA degrades GlcCer to ceramide and glucose in lysosomes, assisted by saposin C).

title: Autophagic lysosome reformation dysfunction in glucocerebrosidase deficient cells: relevance to Parkinson disease.
review_notes: Establishes that GCase deficiency impairs autophagic lysosome reformation/macroautophagy/mTOR; these are the basis for the several over-annotated autophagy/TOR/lysosome-organization terms.

title: Progranulin Recruits HSP70 to β-Glucocerebrosidase and Is Therapeutic Against Gaucher Disease.
review_notes: Progranulin (GRN) binds GCase and recruits HSP70; underlies the GRN 'protein binding' IPI (non-core chaperone interaction).

title: Cryo-TEM structure of β-glucocerebrosidase in complex with its transporter LIMP-2.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structure of the GCase-LIMP-2 complex; concisely restates GCase's core hydrolase activity and the ER->Golgi->lysosome trafficking route with LIMP-2.

title: Effect of saposins A and C on the enzymatic hydrolysis of liposomal glucosylceramide.
review_notes: Establishes saposin-A/C-dependent, anionic-phospholipid-dependent hydrolysis of liposomal glucosylceramide by glucosylceramidase; supports the core activity and its activator requirement.

title: GBA1:SAPC hydrolyzes GlcCer
review_notes: Reactome reaction capturing the saposin-C-dependent lysosomal hydrolysis of glucosylceramide by GBA1; matches the core function.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Bulk urinary-exosome proteomics catalog; GBE1 appears among 1132 identified proteins. Supports only the (over-annotated) exosome localization, not GBE1 function.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Bulk exosome proteomics from prostatic-secretion urine; supports only the over-annotated extracellular exosome localization.

title: The carbohydrate-binding domain of overexpressed STBD1 is important for its stability and protein-protein interactions.
review_notes: Study of STBD1; GBE1 co-immunoprecipitates with STBD1 (Fig. 4A), a glycogen-associated protein. Supports a plausible glycogen-hub interaction but only the generic protein binding term.

title: Structural basis of glycogen branching enzyme deficiency and pharmacologic rescue by rational peptide design.
review_notes: Crystal structures of human GBE1 (PDB 4BZY/5CLT/5CLW) with mechanistic and activity analysis; the definitive primary source for GBE1's branching enzyme activity, monomeric state, catalytic triad, and disease mutations.

title: A proteome-scale map of the SARS-CoV-2-human contactome.
review_notes: High-throughput viral-host interaction screen; records a GBE1-SARS-CoV-2 rep binary interaction. Supports only the generic (over-annotated) protein binding term, not native function.

title: Hepatic and neuromuscular forms of glycogen storage disease type IV caused by mutations in the same glycogen-branching enzyme gene.
review_notes: Primary human GBE1 genetics/biochemistry paper; expression assays show GSD IV mutations inactivate GBE activity. Supports core branching enzyme activity and the GSD IV disease association.

title: A role for Gbx2 in repression of Otx2 and positioning the mid/hindbrain organizer.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary mouse genetic study; its abstract directly supports organizer positioning and Otx2-boundary claims.

title: Changing requirements for Gbx2 in development of the cerebellum and maintenance of the mid/hindbrain organizer.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary conditional-knockout study; the cached abstract directly supports the cerebellar and organizer claims used here.

title: Gbx2 and Fgf8 are sequentially required for formation of the midbrain-hindbrain compartment boundary.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary mouse fate-mapping and genetic study; the cached abstract directly supports the hindbrain-fate claim.

title: Elongation factor 1 alpha1 and genes associated with Usher syndromes are downstream targets of GBX2.
review_notes: Full text is locally available and directly supports GBX2 DNA binding, chromatin occupancy, nuclear localization, and promoter activation.

title: Impact of cytosine methylation on DNA binding specificities of human transcription factors.
review_notes: The identifier, assay scope, and official GBX2 IDA GOA row are verified; GBX2-specific measurements reside in supplementary data rather than searchable main text.

title: The Temporal Contribution of the Gbx2 Lineage to Cerebellar Neurons.
review_notes: Full text is locally available; lineage tracing supports cerebellar developmental context but does not alone establish a cell-autonomous molecular mechanism.

title: Characterization and sequence analysis of the human homeobox-containing gene GBX2.
review_notes: The PMID and human GBX2 expression result are verified from the abstract, but full text is unavailable and the abstract does not establish a causal role in nervous-system development.

title: The homeobox gene GBX2, a target of the myb oncogene, mediates autocrine growth and monocyte differentiation.
review_notes: The PMID and abstract are verified, but the full text needed to inspect the older TAS transcription-factor assignment is unavailable locally.

title: Human METTL20 is a mitochondrial lysine methyltransferase that targets the β subunit of electron transfer flavoprotein (ETFβ) and modulates its activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Directly supports GCDH as an ETF electron donor, but does NOT support the attached GO:0033539 fatty-acid beta-oxidation process term (GCDH is amino-acid catabolic); that annotation is over-annotated.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteome dataset; GCDH identity in supplementary data supports mitochondrial localization only.

title: Lysine catabolism reprograms tumour immunity through histone crotonylation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary research. Establishes GCDH's role in L-lysine catabolism and a moonlighting nuclear crotonyl-CoA-supplying function in glioblastoma stem cells.

title: Cloning of glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase cDNA, and expression of wild type and mutant enzymes in Escherichia coli.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache (full_text_available false) but abstract directly supports the catalytic activity, mitochondrial import, and inactive short isoform.

title: glutaryl-CoA + FAD => crotonyl-CoA + FADH2 + CO2
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the core GCDH catalytic step; matrix localization and homotetramer.

title: Structures of human insulin-degrading enzyme reveal a new substrate recognition mechanism.
review_notes: Correctly cited for the GCG-IDE interaction (GO:0005515 IPI). Reflects hormone clearance, not a core function of glucagon.

title: Crystal structure of the incretin-bound extracellular domain of a G protein-coupled receptor.
review_notes: Paper structurally characterizes GIP (a paralogous incretin from a different gene), not a proglucagon peptide directly; underpins only a generic "protein binding" annotation.

title: Neuropeptide Y, B-type natriuretic peptide, substance P and peptide YY are novel substrates of fibroblast activation protein-α.
review_notes: Supports the GCG-FAP interaction (GO:0005515 IPI); relevant to GLP-1 clearance, non-core.

title: Interleukin-6 enhances insulin secretion by increasing glucagon-like peptide-1 secretion from L cells and alpha cells.
review_notes: Full text available; directly supports GLP-1 secretion (extracellular region, EXP) and the incretin/insulin-secretion functions.

title: Mapping out the multistage fibrillation of glucagon.
review_notes: Correctly cited for glucagon self-association (GO:0042802 IPI), but the behavior is an in-vitro biophysical property, not a physiological function.

title: A microbial amino-acid-conjugated bile acid, tryptophan-cholic acid, improves glucose homeostasis via the orphan receptor MRGPRE.
review_notes: Cited (EXP) for secreted GLP-1/extracellular location; full text not in cache, so the precise supporting passage could not be quoted verbatim.

title: Synergistic activation of the type I adenylyl cyclase by Ca2+ and Gs-coupled receptors in vivo.
review_notes: The paper is about adenylyl cyclase regulation; glucagon is a tool agonist. Adequately supports a general GPCR-signaling annotation but is not a primary GCG functional study.

title: A role for glucagon-like peptide-1 in the central regulation of feeding.
review_notes: Classic study underpinning the GLP-1 feeding-behavior annotation (GO:0007631 TAS).

title: Prototypic G protein-coupled receptor for the intestinotrophic factor glucagon-like peptide 2.
review_notes: Defines the GLP-2 chain function and its dedicated receptor; supports the GLP-2 signaling-receptor-binding and GPCR-signaling annotations.

title: UniProtKB entry P01275 (GLUC_HUMAN), Pro-glucagon
review_notes: Canonical curated entry; FUNCTION blocks are split per cleavage product and are the backbone of the chain-resolved review.

title: A hybrid approach reveals the allosteric regulation of GTP cyclohydrolase I.
review_notes: PubMed-verified hybrid cryo-EM/X-ray crystal structures (PDB 6Z80/6Z85 and related) of human GTP cyclohydrolase I resolving the active-site Zn and the phenylalanine/BH4 allosteric regulation of the enzyme.

title: Regulation of gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase regulatory subunit (GLCLR) gene expression: identification of the major transcriptional start site in HT29 cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Establishes GLCLR (GCLM) role in glutathione synthesis and oxidant-inducible transcription (SNP raised GSH ~2-fold, GCS activity ~6-fold, GLCLR transcription ~2.5-fold). Supports the GSH biosynthesis and oxidative-stress-response annotations.

title: Polymorphism in the 5'-flanking region of human glutamate-cysteine ligase modifier subunit gene is associated with myocardial infarction.
review_notes: Abstract-only. GCLM promoter -588C/T polymorphism; T allele has lower oxidant-inducible promoter activity and is a genetic risk factor for myocardial infarction. Supports GCLM's role in GSH synthesis/antioxidant defense indirectly (gene dosage/expression), not a direct loss-of-function enzyme assay.

title: Polymorphism in glutamate-cysteine ligase modifier subunit gene is associated with impairment of nitric oxide-mediated coronary vasomotor function.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Same GCLM -588T allele associated with impaired NO-mediated coronary vasomotor function; supports a GCL-GSH-NO vascular axis. Downstream physiological association.

title: Knockdown of glutamate-cysteine ligase by small hairpin RNA reveals that both catalytic and modulatory subunits are essential for the survival of primary neurons.
review_notes: Abstract-only but rich. shRNA knockdown of GCLM (modulatory subunit) disrupts GCL activity and glutathione, causing neuronal apoptosis rescued by gamma-glutamylcysteine/GSH. Directly supports contributes_to glutamate-cysteine ligase activity and the anti-apoptotic downstream role. Notes GCLM is rate-optimizing (overexpressing catalytic, not modulatory, subunit raises activity).

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 high-throughput AP-MS. Source of an IPI protein-binding annotation for the GCLM-GCLC interaction (WITH UniProtKB:P48506). Supports the interaction only as bare protein binding; the specific role is captured by GO:0035226.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome. Source of an IPI protein-binding annotation with partner OSGIN1 (UniProtKB:Q9UJX0), not GCLC. High-throughput; conveys no specific function for GCLM.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 high-throughput AP-MS. Source of an IPI protein-binding annotation for the GCLM-GCLC interaction (WITH UniProtKB:P48506). Bare protein binding; specific role captured by GO:0035226.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal (AP-MS + immunofluorescence) cell-mapping study. Source of an IPI protein-binding annotation for the GCLM-GCLC interaction (WITH UniProtKB:P48506). Bare protein binding; specific role captured by GO:0035226.

title: Expression and purification of human gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Co-expression and purification of the human gamma-GCS holoenzyme (catalytic GCLC + regulatory GCLM); holoenzyme assembles intracellularly and is fully active, feedback-inhibited by glutathione and inhibited by BSO. Directly supports GCLM as a subunit of the GCL complex (GO:0017109), catalytic-subunit binding (GO:0035226), and participation in GSH biosynthesis.

title: Identification of an important cysteine residue in human glutamate-cysteine ligase catalytic subunit by site-directed mutagenesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only but rich. Characterizes GCLC-GCLR (GCLC-GCLM) heterodimer formation; incubating wild-type GCLC with GCLR increases GCL activity by 110%, and GCLC Cys-553 maps to the heterodimer interface. Supports catalytic-subunit binding, complex membership, and regulator activity.

title: Overexpression of the regulatory subunit of gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase in HeLa cells increases gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase activity and confers drug resistance.
review_notes: Abstract-only but rich. Adding recombinant GCSl (GCLM) to HeLa extracts raised GCS activity 2-3-fold; GCLM overexpression increased GCS activity, glutathione regeneration, and xenobiotic (doxorubicin/cadmium) resistance. Directly supports GCLM regulator activity and its role in GSH synthesis and xenobiotic response.

title: An E3 ligase network engages GCN1 to promote the degradation of translation factors on stalled ribosomes.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_36638793.md title matches YAML; establishes the human core functions — GCN1 as a ribosome-collision sensor and RNF14 adaptor. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0170011 (stalled ribosome sensor activity), GO:0060090 (molecular adaptor activity) and GO:0072344 (rescue of stalled ribosome), all IDA.

title: Evidence that GCN1 and GCN20, translational regulators of GCN4, function on elongating ribosomes in activation of eIF2alpha kinase GCN2.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_9234705.md title matches YAML; foundational (yeast) evidence that GCN1 stimulates the eIF2alpha kinase GCN2 on ribosomes, supporting the core kinase-activator function. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0008135 (NAS) and ribosome localization.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline mapping the GCV_H family (IPR002930/IPR017453) to the glycine cleavage complex and glycine decarboxylation. Consistent with the well-established identity of GCSH; broad but appropriate.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/GO_Central phylogenetic (IBA) annotations for the GcvH family. Captures the three core, well-supported facets of GCSH biology (glycine cleavage complex, glycine decarboxylation, mitochondrion).

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt SubCell mapping (SL-0173 Mitochondrion) to GO:0005739. Consistent with the experimentally verified mitochondrial localization.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Large-scale yeast two-hybrid interactome (CCSB-HI1). Source of a bare protein binding IPI; the interactor is not a GCS/lipoylation partner and does not inform GCSH function.

title: The glycine cleavage system: structure of a cDNA encoding human H-protein, and partial characterization of its gene in patients with hyperglycinemias.
review_notes: Original human H-protein cDNA paper; establishes GCSH identity, lipoylation at Lys107 and the (R)-lipoate cofactor, and links defects to nonketotic hyperglycinemia. Abstract-only in cache but the underlying assignments are corroborated by UniProt.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome map. Source of multiple bare protein binding IPIs (NMI, MAGEA6/11, MED11, MIS18A, RHBDD2); none are GCS or lipoylation-pathway partners, so they do not inform GCSH molecular function.

title: Cloning of cDNA encoding human H-protein, a constituent of the glycine cleavage system.

title: DLD dimer:2xFAD oxidises GCSH:DHLL to GCSH:lipoate

title: LIPT2 transfers octanoyl group to GCSH

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms

title: Cloning and characterization of human guanine deaminase. Purification and partial amino acid sequence of the mouse protein.
review_notes: Primary paper cloning and biochemically characterizing the human enzyme (guanine deaminase activity, KM ~9.5 uM for guanine, ~1 Zn per monomer, dimeric). Cache is abstract-only; the TAS annotations derive from the full text. Underpins the core MF and zinc cofactor.

title: A novel NE-dlg/SAP102-associated protein, p51-nedasin, related to the amidohydrolase superfamily, interferes with the association between NE-dlg/SAP102 and N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor.

title: Pan-pathway based interaction profiling of FDA-approved nucleoside and nucleobase analogs with enzymes of the human nucleotide metabolism.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.

title: Guanine + H2O => Xanthine + NH4+

title: WRB is the receptor for TRC40/Asna1-mediated insertion of tail-anchored proteins into the ER membrane.

title: Tail-anchored Protein Insertion in Mammals: FUNCTION AND RECIPROCAL INTERACTIONS OF THE TWO SUBUNITS OF THE TRC40 RECEPTOR.

title: The WRB Subunit of the Get3 Receptor is Required for the Correct Integration of its Partner CAML into the ER.

title: Capture and delivery of tail-anchored proteins to the endoplasmic reticulum.

title: The Get1/2 insertase forms a channel to mediate the insertion of tail-anchored proteins into the ER.

title: The GET insertase exhibits conformational plasticity and induces membrane thinning.

title: Identification of a targeting factor for posttranslational membrane protein insertion into the ER.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.

title: WRB is the receptor for TRC40/Asna1-mediated insertion of tail-anchored proteins into the ER membrane.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.

title: Loss of GFAT-1 feedback regulation activates the hexosamine pathway that modulates protein homeostasis.

title: GFPT2/GFAT2 and AMDHD2 act in tandem to control the hexosamine pathway.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.

title: The murine glutamine:fructose-6-phosphate amidotransferase-encoding cDNA sequence.

title: cDNA cloning and mapping of a novel subtype of glutamine:fructose-6-phosphate amidotransferase (GFAT2) in human and mouse.

Original GFAT2 cloning paper; establishes GFAT2 as a GFAT-family amidotransferase subtype and its restricted tissue distribution (CNS/spinal cord, heart, placenta). title: Genome-wide YFP fluorescence complementation screen identifies new regulators for telomere signaling in human cells.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex proteome-scale AP-MS interactome; underlies the IPI "protein binding" annotation with GFPT1 (Q06210), matching the UniProt INTERACTION record. High-throughput; no specific function assigned.

title: GFPT2/GFAT2 and AMDHD2 act in tandem to control the hexosamine pathway.

Basis of the IDA GO:0004360/GO:0006048/GO:0006002 annotations and the UniProt EC 2.6.1.16.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map (AP-MS/imaging) study; underlies the IPI "protein binding" annotation with GFPT1 (Q06210). High-throughput; no specific function assigned.

title: A novel 21-kDa cytochrome c-releasing factor is generated upon treatment of human leukemia U937 cells with geranylgeraniol.

title: Crystal structure of Homo sapiens protein LOC79017.
review_notes: PubMed-verified structural-genomics paper; cached record is abstract-only with no body text, so the homodimer claim is anchored to the UniProt SUBUNIT line (ECO:0000305|PubMed:17932939).

title: The identification and structural characterization of C7orf24 as gamma-glutamyl cyclotransferase. An essential enzyme in the gamma-glutamyl cycle.

title: GGCT transforms gGluCys to OPRO
review_notes: Reactome curation of the GGCT reaction step; source of the cytosol TAS annotation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.

Source of the GGPS1-ATOX1 binary hit and a self-interaction; GGPS1 is not individually discussed in the article text (data in interactome tables). title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.

title: Human geranylgeranyl diphosphate synthase: isolation of the cDNA, chromosomal mapping and tissue expression.

title: Synthesis and metabolism of leukotrienes in gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase deficiency.

title: Hemoxygenase-2 is an oxygen sensor for a calcium-sensitive potassium channel.

title: Human colostrum: identification of minor proteins in the aqueous phase by proteomics.

title: Kinetic characterization and identification of the acylation and glycosylation sites of recombinant human gamma-glutamyltranspeptidase.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.

title: Gamma-glutamyl compounds: substrate specificity of gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase enzymes.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.

title: Novel insights into eukaryotic γ-glutamyltranspeptidase 1 from the crystal structure of the glutamate-bound human enzyme.

review_notes: Photoaffinity-labeling and mutagenesis identifying Glu279 at the NAD(+) coenzyme-binding site of human GDH. Supports the NAD+ binding annotation.

title: Study of structure-function relationships in human glutamate dehydrogenases reveals novel molecular mechanisms for the regulation of the nerve tissue-specific (GLUD2) isoenzyme.
review_notes: Structure-function/mutagenesis of human GDH isoenzymes (GLUD1 vs GLUD2) mapping allosteric (ADP/leucine/GTP) determinants. Supports ADP- and L-leucine-binding annotations.

title: Molecular basis of human glutamate dehydrogenase regulation under changing energy demands.
review_notes: Characterizes GLUD1-derived GDH activity/regulation and confirms mitochondrial localization by GFP fusion. Supports the catalytic-activity and mitochondrion annotations.

title: Identification of ADP-ribosylation site in human glutamate dehydrogenase isozymes.
review_notes: Measures human GDH activity and its inhibition by ADP-ribosylation; establishes one-subunit-per-hexamer stoichiometry and the reactive Cys. Supports catalytic activity and the ADP-ribosylation PTM.

title: SIRT4 inhibits glutamate dehydrogenase and opposes the effects of calorie restriction in pancreatic beta cells.
review_notes: Shows SIRT4 ADP-ribosylates and downregulates GDH, linking GDH activity to amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion in beta-cells. Supports catalytic-activity and the SIRT4-interaction/regulation annotations.

title: Mitochondrial targeting adaptation of the hominoid-specific glutamate dehydrogenase driven by positive Darwinian selection.
review_notes: Full-text-available; directly states GLUD1 localizes to both mitochondria and cytoplasm (vs mitochondria-specific GLUD2). Supports the cytoplasm annotation.

title: Human GLUD1 and GLUD2 glutamate dehydrogenase localize to mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum.
review_notes: Experimental subcellular localization: most GDH translocates into mitochondria, with a minor ER pool. Supports the mitochondrion and endoplasmic-reticulum location annotations.

title: Quantitative proteomic analysis of human substantia nigra in Alzheimer's disease, Huntington's disease and Multiple sclerosis.
review_notes: Proteomic abundance survey of substantia nigra in neurodegenerative disease. Detection/differential abundance does not support a role in substantia nigra development; the derived GO annotation is an over-interpretation.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale BioPlex interactome. Correctly cited as source of a high-throughput protein-protein interaction, but yields only an uninformative protein-binding term for GLUD1.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 interactome; source of a high-throughput interaction giving only a generic protein-binding annotation.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; corroborates mitochondrial localization of GLUD1.

title: Cryo-EM structure of the KLHL22 E3 ligase bound to an oligomeric metabolic enzyme.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structure of CUL3(KLHL22)-RBX1 bound to the GDH1 hexamer; KLHL22 polyubiquitinates GDH1 in vitro. Biologically meaningful KLHL22 interaction, but recorded in GOA only as generic protein binding.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map/interactome; source of a generic protein-binding annotation.

title: Abnormal glutamate metabolism in an adult-onset degenerative neurological disorder.
review_notes: Human patients with partial GDH deficiency show elevated plasma glutamate and reduced alpha-ketoglutarate, indicating decreased glutamate catabolism. Supports the L-glutamate catabolic process annotation.

title: Nerve tissue-specific (GLUD2) and housekeeping (GLUD1) human glutamate dehydrogenases are regulated by distinct allosteric mechanisms: implications for biologic function.
review_notes: Primary characterization of recombinant human GLUD2 vs GLUD1: GLUD2 is GTP-insensitive, strongly activated by ADP and L-leucine. Supports the catalytic activity and allosteric-effector binding annotations. Abstract-only in cache; annotations defer to the original curator's reading of the full text.

title: Study of structure-function relationships in human glutamate dehydrogenases reveals novel molecular mechanisms for the regulation of the nerve tissue-specific (GLUD2) isoenzyme.
review_notes: Structure-function/mutagenesis study identifying Arg443Ser and Gly456Ala as the adaptive substitutions underlying GLUD2's GTP resistance and ADP dependence. Supports ADP and L-leucine binding annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Molecular basis of human glutamate dehydrogenase regulation under changing energy demands.
review_notes: Characterizes GLUD1/GLUD2 regulation under changing energy demands; GLUD2 has low basal activity, is GTP-resistant, and is fully activatable by ADP/L-leucine, functioning under acidification and high ADP. Supports the catalytic-activity annotation. Abstract-only.

title: Mitochondrial targeting adaptation of the hominoid-specific glutamate dehydrogenase driven by positive Darwinian selection.
review_notes: Full-text available. Establishes GLUD2 as a hominoid retrogene specifically targeted to mitochondria (unlike cytoplasm+mitochondria GLUD1) via a positively selected E7K MTS substitution. Directly supports the mitochondrion IDA and the NOT-cytosol IDA.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale AP-MS interactome (BioPlex). GLUD2 appears only in supplementary interaction data (WITH GLUD1/P00367); yields a bare, uninformative "protein binding" annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Large-scale AP-MS interactome (BioPlex 3). Same situation as PMID:28514442: bare "protein binding" with WITH GLUD1/P00367.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial-proteome study; identifies GLUD2 as mitochondrial (HTP), corroborating its mitochondrial-matrix localization.

title: Novel human glutamate dehydrogenase expressed in neural and testicular tissues and encoded by an X-linked intronless gene.
review_notes: Founding GLUD2 paper: cloning of the X-linked intronless GLUD2, expression in retina, testis and brain, and recombinant enzyme catalyzing oxidative deamination of glutamate. Supports the catalytic-activity and glutamate-metabolism annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Large-scale Y2H interactome map; source of a GLUL self-interaction (identical protein binding). Cached full text does not mention GLUL by name (hit in supplementary data). Consistent with the known homo-oligomer.

title: Congenital glutamine deficiency with glutamine synthetase mutations.
review_notes: Establishes human GS activity and disease (congenital glutamine deficiency) via R324C/R341C variants; abstract-only cache but directly supports the EXP glutamine synthetase activity annotation.

title: Glutamine synthetase is essential for proliferation of fetal skin fibroblasts.
review_notes: Shows GS activity is required for fetal fibroblast proliferation (downstream of glutamine supply). Supports GO:0008283 IDA.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary-exosome proteomics; source of the extracellular exosome HDA localization. Over-annotation for an abundant cytosolic enzyme.

title: Shifted Transversal Design smart-pooling for high coverage interactome mapping.
review_notes: Smart-pooling interactome screen; source of a GLUL self-interaction. Consistent with homo-oligomerization but uninformative on its own.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
