Its headline negative claim - that GSDMB does not lyse host cells - was contested at the time (PMID:36157507) and is now better read as a property of the isoform used (Q8TAX9-1) rather than of GSDMB in general. Cited here only for the bactericidal and bacterial-lipid claims, which are not in dispute.

title: GSDMB N-terminal assembles in plasma membrane to execute pyroptotic cell death.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Genes Dis 2022, Gong et al., full text cached. A short rebuttal-style report rather than a full study, but it does the decisive fractionation experiment (GSDMB-NT in plasma membrane, not mitochondria, no cytochrome c release) and it identifies the isoform question itself, stating that it used the 416-residue form while Hansen et al. used isoform 1. Format is brief and the evidence is a single figure, so it is weighted as corroborating rather than decisive.

title: Insights into the GSDMB-mediated cellular lysis and its targeting by IpaH7.8.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Nat Commun 2023, Yin et al., full text cached. Crystal structure of the GSDMB-IpaH7.8 complex; cited as corroboration for the Shigella targeting and the membrane-engagement surfaces, not as primary evidence for any annotation here.

title: Distinct GSDMB protein isoforms and protease cleavage processes differentially control pyroptotic cell death and mitochondrial damage in cancer cells.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Cell Death Differ 2023, Molina-Crespo/Sarrio/Moreno-Bueno group, full text cached. Source of the GSDMB1-4 nomenclature that UniProt now maps onto its own isoform IDs, and of the key dissociation that granzyme A cleaves all isoforms while only exon-6-containing ones become pyroptotic. Also reports concomitant mitochondrial damage, which is not reconciled with PMID:36157507.

title: Structural basis for GSDMB pore formation and its targeting by IpaH7.8.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Nature 2023, Wang et al. (Ruan lab), full text cached. Independent cryo-EM pore structure reaching the same isoform conclusion as PMID:36991125 from a different laboratory, which is what makes the exon-6 result solid rather than single-source.

title: Structural mechanisms for regulation of GSDMB pore-forming activity.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Nature 2023, Zhong et al. (Shao/Ding labs). Cached abstract only, but the abstract states the pore stoichiometry, the exon-6 requirement and the explanation for earlier negative results. The strongest single reference for the isoform adjudication.

title: Alternative splicing of GSDMB modulates killer lymphocyte-triggered pyroptosis.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Sci Immunol 2023, Lieberman lab, full text cached. Tests isoform behaviour under real NK cell attack rather than only with recombinant protease, and reports the dominant-negative behaviour of the non-cytotoxic fragments. Uses the GSDMB1-5 naming scheme, which has no UniProt synonym for GSDMB5, so that one mapping was left unasserted.

title: Exosite-mediated targeting of GSDMB by dimeric granzyme A in lymphocyte pyroptotic killing.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Immunity 2026, Wang et al. (Shao/Ding labs), cached abstract only. Gives the recognition mechanism (granzyme A dimerization, exosite engagement of the GSDMB C-terminal domain, cleavage at Lys244) and the species caveat that mouse granzyme A engages the exosite inefficiently. Also serves as independent structural re-derivation of the 2020 Science claim, which matters given the erratum to that paper.

title: Erratum for the Research Article "Granzyme A from cytotoxic lymphocytes cleaves GSDMB to trigger pyroptosis in target cells" by Z. Zhou et al.
review_notes: Existence and target verified: PubMed and Europe PMC both record this as a Published Erratum (Science 2026 Jul 9;393(6807):eaej7549) for PMID:32299851. The substance could NOT be retrieved - no abstract in PubMed, Europe PMC reports isOpenAccess N / inPMC N with subscription required, and science.org returns HTTP 403. What was corrected is therefore unknown to this review, and no annotation here depends on the corrected paper. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than VERIFIED to make that limitation explicit. A curator with journal access should read it and, if the correction touches the cleavage-site or pyroptosis data, revisit PMID:32299851.

title: Structure, expression and chromosome mapping of MLZE, a novel gene which is preferentially expressed in metastatic melanoma cells.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Jpn J Cancer Res 2001, the original MLZE/GSDMC cloning paper. Cached entry is abstract-only, so the cytoplasm IDA it supports could not be checked against the figures. Relevant for gene identity, tissue expression and the melanoma link rather than for molecular function.

title: PD-L1-mediated gasdermin C expression switches apoptosis to pyroptosis in cancer cells and facilitates tumour necrosis.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Nat Cell Biol 2020, Hou et al. Full text cached. Provides the only reconstituted biochemistry for GSDMC pore formation (liposome pelleting, EM pores, Tb3+ leakage) and is the source of the plasma membrane EXP annotation. Note PubMed lists an erratum for this article (Nat Cell Biol 2020;22(11):1396); the erratum content was not retrieved and no claim used here depends on it.

title: The metabolite α-KG induces GSDMC-dependent pyroptosis through death receptor 6-activated caspase-8.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Cell Res 2021, Zhang et al. Independent replication that caspase-8 cleavage of GSDMC produces pyroptosis, here downstream of alpha-ketoglutarate and DR6. Cited as corroboration of pore competence, not of any particular target membrane.

title: Gasdermin C cleavage by Cathepsin S modulates Rab7 vesicles in intestinal epithelial cells to amplify anti-helminth immunity.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Immunity 2025, Pandey et al., full text available via PMC12380176. The principal challenge to the pyroptosis paradigm for GSDMC. Note that much of the mechanistic imaging uses murine Gsdmc2/Gsdmc4 in HeLa cells and C. elegans, though human GSDMC is also cleaved by cathepsin S and the human N-terminal fragment was imaged in HeLa.

title: Cutting the Gordian knot: Untangling gasdermin C from pyroptosis.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Immunity 2025, Lin and Ruan, a commentary on PMID:40701157. Cached abstract only. Used to document that the community treats the GSDMC/pyroptosis relationship as unresolved, not as primary evidence.

title: Disruption of heme homeostasis by nuclear receptor Nur77 induces pyroptosis through granzyme B-dependent GSDMC cleavage.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Signal Transduct Target Ther 2025, Wu et al., full text cached. Correctly cited, but weighed cautiously: pyroptosis is induced by a synthetic Nur77 ligand (DdBIC) acting through a long mito-ROS/OMA1/OPA1/PERK cascade, so it establishes that GSDMC can form a lytic pore rather than that it normally does. It also introduces a third activating protease (granzyme B) alongside caspase-8 and cathepsin S.

title: Gasdermin C reprograms metabolism through the CAMKK2-AMPK axis to promote lung adenocarcinoma progression and radioresistance.
review_notes: Identifier verified against PubMed (Cell Rep 2026, Ren et al.) and the nuclear scaffold claim is in the abstract, but the claim itself is unverified: cached entry is abstract-only, the result is from a single laboratory, and no independent replication of nuclear GSDMC recruiting NAT10 or BAZ1B/SMARCA5 was found. Deliberately not used to support any annotation in this review; raised in suggested_questions and suggested_experiments instead.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: High-use curator-reviewed orthology-transfer provenance for GSK3B annotations; retained as propagated evidence rather than direct experimental support. Action counts in this review: {'KEEP_AS_NON_CORE': 23, 'ACCEPT': 3, 'MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED': 1}.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PANTHER/phylogenetic inference provenance used for conserved GSK3B kinase, localization, and pathway annotations. Action counts in this review: {'KEEP_AS_NON_CORE': 7, 'ACCEPT': 11}.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: High-use Compara orthology-transfer provenance for many non-core and some accepted GSK3B annotations; useful for interpreting propagated annotation strength. Action counts in this review: {'ACCEPT': 6, 'KEEP_AS_NON_CORE': 35}.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA electronic annotation provenance; relevant mainly for non-core or over-annotated propagated calls and interpreted cautiously. Action counts in this review: {'MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED': 1, 'KEEP_AS_NON_CORE': 3, 'ACCEPT': 2}.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automated annotation provenance; relevant mainly as electronic support and interpreted cautiously in the review. Action counts in this review: {'MODIFY': 1, 'ACCEPT': 6}.

title: Control of beta-catenin phosphorylation/degradation by a dual-kinase mechanism.
review_notes: Primary beta-catenin phosphorylation/degradation paper supporting GSK-3 action downstream of CKI priming in Wnt/beta-catenin regulation.

title: Primed phosphorylation of tau at Thr231 by glycogen synthase kinase 3beta (GSK3beta) plays a critical role in regulating tau's ability to bind and stabilize microtubules.
review_notes: Primary tau-phosphorylation study supporting GSK3B tau-protein kinase activity and reduced tau microtubule binding/stabilization.

title: Endoplasmic reticulum stress induces p53 cytoplasmic localization and prevents p53-dependent apoptosis by a pathway involving glycogen synthase kinase-3beta.
review_notes: GOA original evidence for ER-stress/p53/apoptosis-related GSK3B annotations; supports a real but non-core stress-response branch. Action counts in this review: {'MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED': 1, 'KEEP_AS_NON_CORE': 4, 'ACCEPT': 4}.

title: Dual regulation of Snail by GSK-3beta-mediated phosphorylation in control of epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
review_notes: Primary Snail/EMT paper supporting a non-core EMT and protein-localization/degradation branch.

title: GSK-3beta-regulated interaction of BICD with dynein is involved in microtubule anchorage at centrosome.
review_notes: GOA original evidence for BICD/dynein, microtubule anchorage, and centrosome-related GSK3B annotations; supports non-core cytoskeletal context. Action counts in this review: {'MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED': 1, 'KEEP_AS_NON_CORE': 4, 'ACCEPT': 1}.

title: Activation of glycogen synthase kinase-3 inhibits long-term potentiation with synapse-associated impairments.
review_notes: GOA original evidence for synaptic/LTP-related GSK3B annotations; supports non-core neuronal signaling consequences. Action counts in this review: {'KEEP_AS_NON_CORE': 6}.

title: Glycogen synthase kinase 3: more than a namesake.
review_notes: Review supporting broad GSK3 pathway context in metabolism, Wnt, tau, diabetes, and Alzheimer disease.

title: ErbB2 receptor controls microtubule capture by recruiting ACF7 to the plasma membrane of migrating cells.
review_notes: GOA original evidence for localization, phosphorylation, and microtubule-process annotations in an ErbB2/ACF7 migration context; supports a cytoskeletal branch. Action counts in this review: {'ACCEPT': 4}.

title: ER stress inhibits mTORC2 and Akt signaling through GSK-3β-mediated phosphorylation of rictor.

title: Investigation of the oligomeric status of the peroxisomal isoform of human 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA lyase.

title: Crystal structure of human 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA Lyase: insights into catalysis and the molecular basis for hydroxymethylglutaric aciduria.

title: Characterization of a novel HMG-CoA lyase enzyme with a dual location in endoplasmic reticulum and cytosol.

title: 3-Hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA lyase: expression and isolation of the recombinant human enzyme and investigation of a mechanism for regulation of enzyme activity.

title: Evidence supporting a role for histidine-235 in cation binding to human 3-hydroxy-3-methyglutaryl-CoA lyase.

title: PEX5S,L:Cargo binds PEX13:PEX14:PEX2:PEX10:PEX12 (Docking and Translocation Module)

title: Molecular cloning and nucleotide sequence of complementary DNA for human hepatic cytosolic acetoacetyl-coenzyme A thiolase.
review_notes: This paper is about cytosolic acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase (ACAT2), the enzyme immediately UPSTREAM of HMGCS1 in the mevalonate pathway, not about HMGCS1 itself. It is used only as the reference for a curator IC (inferred from GO:0004421) placing HMGCS1 in cholesterol biosynthesis. The conclusion (HMGCS1 acts in cholesterol biosynthesis) is correct, but the reference is not about this gene.

title: Human cytoplasmic 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A synthase: expression, purification, and characterization of recombinant wild-type and Cys129 mutant enzymes.
review_notes: Expression, purification and kinetic characterization of recombinant human cytoplasmic HMG-CoA synthase, and demonstration that the active-site Cys129 is required for catalysis. Directly establishes HMGCS1 catalytic activity.

title: Mitochondrial 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase deficiency: clinical course and description of causal mutations in two patients.
review_notes: Establishes HMGCS2 catalytic activity via bacterial expression of wild-type and the F174L disease variant (no detectable activity); supports the EXP MF annotation and the disease link. PubMed-verified title/abstract match.

title: Crystal structures of human HMG-CoA synthase isoforms provide insights into inherited ketogenesis disorders and inhibitor design.
review_notes: Crystal structures of the human mitochondrial (HMGCS2) and cytosolic (HMGCS1) isoforms; documents the homodimer (supporting identical protein binding) and explicitly separates the mitochondrial ketogenic isoform from the cytosolic mevalonate/cholesterol isoform.

title: New case of mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase deficiency. Functional analysis of eight mutations.
review_notes: Expression/activity assay of eight HMGCS2 disease mutations; supports the IMP MF and ketone body biosynthetic process annotations. Abstract-only cached but title/abstract verified.

title: Human Mitochondrial HMG-CoA Synthase Deficiency: Role of Enzyme Dimerization Surface and Characterization of Three New Patients.
review_notes: Full text available; expresses and assays wild-type and ten HMGCS2 variants, confirming the condensation reaction of ketone body synthesis and the homodimeric nature of mHS.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Large-scale MitoCoP proteomic study; HMGCS2 is included in the high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome (supplementary data), supporting the HTP mitochondrion annotation. The protein is not discussed by name in the extracted body text.

title: Human mitochondrial HMG CoA synthase: liver cDNA and partial genomic cloning, chromosome mapping to 1p12-p13, and possible role in vertebrate evolution.
review_notes: Original cloning of human liver mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase; identifies mHS as the first enzyme of ketogenesis, distinct from the cytoplasmic cholesterol-synthesis isozyme. Supports the mitochondrion (TAS) annotation and the HMGCS1/HMGCS2 distinction.

title: Disruption of an active site hydrogen bond converts human heme oxygenase-1 into a peroxidase.
review_notes: Active-site Asp-140 mutagenesis abolishes heme oxygenase (biliverdin-forming) activity of human HO-1, directly supporting the core catalytic function.

title: Large-scale identification and characterization of human genes that activate NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways.
review_notes: Genome-scale overexpression luciferase screen; supports an NF-kappaB-activating signal from HMOX1 cDNA only in that artificial context, hence the over-annotation flag.

title: Involvement of NADPH in the interaction between heme oxygenase-1 and cytochrome P450 reductase.
review_notes: Characterizes the functional HO-1/NADPH-CPR interaction (electron donor for catalysis); supports the enzyme binding annotation.

title: BMP4 induces HO-1 via a Smad-independent, p38MAPK-dependent pathway in pulmonary artery myocytes.
review_notes: Shows BMP4-induced HO-1 inhibits pulmonary artery SMC proliferation; supports the negative-regulation-of-SMC-proliferation annotation but not the positive-regulation one.

title: Expression and characterization of full-length human heme oxygenase-1: the presence of intact membrane-binding region leads to increased binding affinity for NADPH cytochrome P450 reductase.
review_notes: Direct biochemical characterization of full-length human HO-1 heme degradation and CPR binding; supports the core catalytic function and heme binding.

title: Oligomerization is crucial for the stability and function of heme oxygenase-1 in the endoplasmic reticulum.
review_notes: Establishes ER-membrane anchoring, TM-driven homo-oligomerization, and its requirement for HO-1 stability and enzymatic activity.

title: Genome-wide YFP fluorescence complementation screen identifies new regulators for telomere signaling in human cells.
review_notes: High-throughput YFP-complementation telomere-signaling screen; the HO-1/POT1 hit is a generic protein-binding observation without a defined HO-1 function.

title: Endoplasmic reticulum anchored heme-oxygenase 1 faces the cytosol.
review_notes: Protease-protection assays place endogenous HO-1 in the ER membrane with a cytosol-facing active site; supports the core location and topology.

title: Haem oxygenase-1 overexpression alters intracellular iron distribution.
review_notes: Shows HO-1 overexpression reroutes iron into ferritin and reduces redox-active loose iron; supports the intracellular iron homeostasis annotation.

title: Activation of the p62-Keap1-NRF2 pathway protects against ferroptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma cells.
review_notes: HO-1 knockdown (with NQO1/FTH1) promoted ferroptosis; supports a protective (negative-regulation-of-ferroptosis) role as an NRF2 target.

title: APEX Fingerprinting Reveals the Subcellular Localization of Proteins of Interest.
review_notes: APEX proximity fingerprinting directly resolved HMOX1 membrane topology/ER localization.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome (HuRI); numerous ER/membrane partners largely reflect co-compartmentalization rather than specific HO-1 functions.

title: SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a induces RETREG1/FAM134B-dependent reticulophagy and triggers sequential ER stress and inflammatory responses during SARS-CoV-2 infection.
review_notes: Reports HMOX1-ORF3a interaction promoting ORF3a-induced autophagy during SARS-CoV-2 infection; a host-virus interaction, not a core HO-1 function.

title: Expression and characterization of truncated human heme oxygenase (hHO-1) and a fusion protein of hHO-1 with human cytochrome P450 reductase.
review_notes: Truncated human HO-1 converts heme to biliverdin with cytochrome P450 reductase; primary evidence for the core catalytic function and the soluble form.

title: Oxidative stress causes enhanced endothelial cell injury in human heme oxygenase-1 deficiency.
review_notes: First human HMOX1-deficiency case; establishes the in vivo consequences (hemolysis, erythrocyte fragmentation, iron deposition, oxidative-stress hypersensitivity).

title: Hemoxygenase-2 is an oxygen sensor for a calcium-sensitive potassium channel.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache (full_text_available false). PubMed-verified Science 2004 paper on HO-2 as an O2 sensor for BK channels; directly supports the GO:0001666 response to hypoxia IDA and the HO-2/KCNMA1 (Q12791) interaction. Supports a genuine, distinctive HO-2 physiological role (kept as non-core relative to the heme-catabolic core).

title: Human heme oxygenase-2: characterization and expression of a full-length cDNA and evidence suggesting that the two HO-2 transcripts may differ by choice of polyadenylation signal.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. PubMed-verified 1992 characterization of the human HO-2 cDNA and enzyme; supports the GO:0004392 heme oxygenase activity IDA and metalloporphyrin inhibition (ACTIVITY REGULATION). Directly about HMOX2 (HO-2).

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. High-throughput membrane-proteome MS study; the HO-2 identification supports a generic membrane HDA row only and is not informative about the specific ER-membrane location.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput binary-interactome screen. Interactions are numerous and heterogeneous and yield only uninformative bare protein binding; over-annotated as MF.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome; HO-2 partners are generic and yield only uninformative bare protein binding; over-annotated as MF.

title: Heme oxygenase-2. Properties of the heme complex of the purified tryptic fragment of recombinant human heme oxygenase-2.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. PubMed-verified biochemical/spectroscopic characterization of purified human HO-2; strong direct support for GO:0004392 heme oxygenase activity and GO:0020037 heme binding.

title: HMOX1 dimer, HMOX2 cleave heme
review_notes: Reactome curated reaction; supports the ER-membrane location (GO:0005789 TAS) and the heme-catabolic/CO-producing core of HO-2.

title: Exocytosis of specific granule membrane proteins
review_notes: Reactome neutrophil-degranulation pathway; a specialized cell-type context. Supports the specific-granule-membrane / plasma-membrane TAS rows but is peripheral to HO-2's core ER-membrane heme-catabolic function.

title: UniProtKB record for human HMOX2 (P30519)
review_notes: Authoritative UniProt record for HMOX2; primary source for the description and core-function calls.

title: Mutational analysis of a heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A2 response element for RNA trafficking.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Munro et al., J Biol Chem 274:34389-34395 (1999). The A2RE mapping study underlying the mRNA-trafficking annotations.

title: hnRNP A2, a potential ssDNA/RNA molecular adapter at the telomere.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Moran-Jones et al., Nucleic Acids Res 33:486-496 (2005). Rat brain hnRNP A2; supports the telomeric ssDNA binding activity but is the reason those annotations are treated as non-core for the human protein.

title: Mutations in prion-like domains in hnRNPA2B1 and hnRNPA1 cause multisystem proteinopathy and ALS.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Kim et al., Nature 495:467-473 (2013). Establishes the prion-like-domain mutations causing multisystem proteinopathy and ALS; the disease side of the low-complexity-domain function.

title: Sumoylated hnRNPA2B1 controls the sorting of miRNAs into exosomes through binding to specific motifs.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Villarroya-Beltri et al., Nat Commun 4:2980 (2013). Source of the exosomal miRNA sorting annotations.

title: HNRNPA2B1 Is a Mediator of m(6)A-Dependent Nuclear RNA Processing Events.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Alarcon et al., Cell 162:1299-1308 (2015). This is the IDA source for GO:1990247, GO:0031053 and the splicing IMP. The in vivo binding and pri-miRNA processing results are accepted here; only the inference from CLIP-motif overlap to selective methyl-mark recognition is marked as over-annotation.

title: Mechanistic View of hnRNPA2 Low-Complexity Domain Structure, Interactions, and Phase Separation Altered by Mutation and Arginine Methylation.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Ryan et al., Mol Cell 69:465-479 (2018). NMR and simulation of the hnRNPA2 low-complexity domain; the IDA source for GO:0140693.

title: Molecular basis for the specific and multivariant recognitions of RNA substrates by human hnRNP A2/B1.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Wu et al., Nat Commun 9:420 (2018), doi 10.1038/s41467-017-02770-z. Crystal structures of the tandem RRMs with several RNA substrates. Independent of and four years earlier than PMID:41662154, and reaching the same conclusion via a different method, which is why the m6A-reader demotion does not rest on a single 2026 paper.

title: Nuclear hnRNPA2B1 initiates and amplifies the innate immune response to DNA viruses.
review_notes: Identifier and title verified against PubMed: Wang, Wen & Cao, Science 365(6454):eaav0758 (2019), doi 10.1126/science.aav0758. Not retracted and carries no notice in the PubMed record as of this review. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than VERIFIED for its central claim: the nuclear DNA-sensor function it reports has been built on by later work (PMID:41134667, PMID:40689679) but I found no independent replication of the core claim, and GOA itself cites this paper only for subcellular localisation, not for any molecular function or biological process. Relevance MEDIUM because only the localisation is used in this review.

title: Nuclear U1 snRNA facilitates the dimerization of hnRNPA2B1 to enhance anti-DNA viral innate immunity.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Zhang et al., Cell Rep 44(11):116462 (2025), doi 10.1016/j.celrep.2025.116462. Cached entry is abstract-only. Cited here only as evidence that the DNA-sensor claim remains an active line of work rather than an abandoned one; it assumes that role rather than testing it, so it is not independent confirmation.

title: Mechanistic studies on HNRNPA2B1 suggest binding but not selective recognition of m(6)A.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Park et al., RNA Biol 23(1):1-28 (2026), doi 10.1080/15476286.2026.2627781. Full text read. MD simulation plus microscale thermophoresis on an RRM1-RRM2 fusion construct. Directly addresses the selectivity implied by GO:1990247. Scope limitation recorded in the annotation review: isolated RRM construct, single GGACU context, no full-length protein and no low-complexity domain.

title: Mutations in DHDPSL are responsible for primary hyperoxaluria type III.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Identifies DHDPSL/HOGA1 mutations as the cause of primary hyperoxaluria type 3 and proposes HOGA1 as the gene encoding 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase.

title: Primary hyperoxaluria type III gene HOGA1 (formerly DHDPSL) as a possible risk factor for idiopathic calcium oxalate urolithiasis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports a loss-of-function mechanism for HOGA1 and links HOGA1 variants to oxalate/urolithiasis risk.

title: Structural and biochemical studies of human 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase: implications for hydroxyproline metabolism in primary hyperoxaluria.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text. Definitive structural and enzymatic characterization of human HOGA1 - retro-aldol cleavage of HOG to pyruvate and glyoxylate, homotetramer (dimer of dimers), catalytic residues Lys196/Tyr168, terminal step of hydroxyproline degradation.

title: Mitochondrial Protein Interaction Mapping Identifies Regulators of Respiratory Chain Function.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial protein-interaction mapping; source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (STARD7). Not informative for HOGA1's molecular function.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome (BioPlex); source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (USP47). Not informative for molecular function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Binary interactome map (HuRI); source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (CIMAP1A). Not informative for molecular function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome (BioPlex 3.0); source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (USP47). Not informative for molecular function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; independent proteomic support for mitochondrial localization of HOGA1.

title: HOGA1 tetramer aldol-cleaves 4-OH-2-oxoglutarate (HOG) to glyoxylate and pyruvate
review_notes: Reactome reaction curating the HOGA1-catalyzed HOG cleavage in the mitochondrial matrix.

title: UniProt entry Q86XE5 (HOGA1_HUMAN)
review_notes: UniProt/Swiss-Prot record; source of function, subunit, subcellular location, transit peptide, active-site, and disease annotations.

title: Primary structure deduced from complementary DNA sequence and expression in cultured cells of mammalian 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvic acid dioxygenase. Evidence that the enzyme is a homodimer of identical subunits homologous to rat liver-specific alloantigen F.
review_notes: Foundational cloning/expression paper establishing the human enzyme's catalytic activity and homodimeric structure. Abstract-only in cache but claims are internally consistent and corroborated.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary exosome proteomics; supports only an incidental exosome localization, not core function.

title: HPD degradation regulated by the TTC36-STK33-PELI1 signaling axis induces tyrosinemia and neurological damage.
review_notes: Full-text verified. Establishes HPD as the key tyrosine-metabolizing enzyme whose loss causes tyrosinemia, and its regulation by TTC36/STK33/ PELI1 (basis for the IPI protein-binding annotations).

title: Functional role of residues involved in substrate binding of human 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase.
review_notes: Kinetic and mutagenesis characterization of the human enzyme's substrate binding and catalysis; directly supports the core dioxygenase activity.

title: HPD is an m(6)A Methyltransferase that Protects Colorectal Cancer Cells from Ferroptotic Cell Death by m(6)A Methylating SLC7A11/GPX4.
review_notes: Full-text verified 2025 experimental study reporting a moonlighting nuclear mRNA m6A methyltransferase activity (recombinant protein, mutagenesis, KO mouse). The activity is genuinely reported but unusual for an iron dioxygenase and is flagged with a CAUTION note by UniProt; treated as a non-core secondary function, not HPD's defining activity.

title: Structure of the human 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvic acid dioxygenase gene (HPD).
review_notes: Gene-structure characterization; supports the TAS tyrosine-catabolic-process annotation.

title: HPD dioxygenates HPP
review_notes: Reactome reaction placing HPD dioxygenation of HPP in the cytosol; supports the core molecular function and cytosolic location.

title: The 2.0 A structure of human hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase in complex with a transition-state analog inhibitor.
review_notes: Structure of human HGPRT with transition-state analog and Mg2+-PPi; directly supports magnesium ion binding and catalytic mechanism.

title: The crystal structure of free human hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase reveals extensive conformational plasticity throughout the catalytic cycle.
review_notes: Apoenzyme structure; describes movement of subunits within the tetramer, supporting the homotetramer annotation.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome; supports only a bare protein binding annotation, uninformative for HPRT1 function.

title: An empirical framework for binary interactome mapping.
review_notes: Systematic HT-Y2H framework paper; underlies a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Inhibition of hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase by acyclic nucleoside phosphonates: a new class of antimalarial therapeutics.
review_notes: Abstract foregrounds the P. falciparum enzyme but explicitly assays the corresponding human HGPRT (Ki values) and reports structures of human HGPRT; a UniProt EC 2.4.2.8 evidence source for HPRT1 catalytic activity.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: HT mass-spec detection of HPRT1 in B-cell exosome proteome; a sighting, not functional localization.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: HT interactome map; supports bare protein binding and self-interaction (identical protein binding) annotations.

title: A massively parallel pipeline to clone DNA variants and examine molecular phenotypes of human disease mutations.
review_notes: HT variant/interaction pipeline; supports a self-interaction (identical protein binding) annotation consistent with the homotetramer.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: HT interactome perturbation study; supports a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: HT variant-interaction study; supports bare protein binding and self-interaction annotations.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HT binary interactome reference map (HuRI); supports bare protein binding and self-interaction annotations.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: HT interactome of neurodegenerative disease proteins; supports a bare protein binding annotation (incl. HTT).

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex AP-MS interactome; supports a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Human hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT): purification and properties.
review_notes: Classic purification/biochemical characterization of the human enzyme; supports guanine PRT activity and GMP salvage (abstract-only in cache; curator read full text).

title: Isolation and characterization of a full-length expressible cDNA for human hypoxanthine phosphoribosyl transferase.
review_notes: Cloned human HPRT cDNA expresses functional enzyme activity (HAT selection); supports hypoxanthine PRT activity and cytoplasmic localization.

title: The crystal structure of human hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase with bound GMP.
review_notes: Structure with bound GMP; Lys165 confers specificity for guanine and hypoxanthine over adenine (argues against AMP salvage).

title: Dopamine transporters are markedly reduced in Lesch-Nyhan disease in vivo.
review_notes: Documents reduced striatal DA transporters in LND patients (a downstream disease phenotype); does not establish an HPRT1 molecular function of regulating dopamine metabolism. Underlies an over-annotated GO:0045964 annotation.

title: Catalysis in human hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase: Asp 137 acts as a general acid/base.
review_notes: Mechanistic study of human HGPRTase; states the enzyme catalyzes reversible IMP/GMP formation from hypoxanthine/guanine and PRPP.

title: Purine metabolism in female heterozygotes for hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase deficiency.
review_notes: Carrier study; reduced HPRT activity causes purine overproduction and elevated hypoxanthine/xanthine excretion, evidencing the salvage role.

title: The N-terminal anchor sequences of 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases determine their orientation in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane.
review_notes: Establishes ER-membrane localization and single-pass type II topology with lumen-facing catalytic domain; also reports enzymatic activity. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Appropriate function of 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 in the endoplasmic reticulum lumen is dependent on its N-terminal region sharing similar topological determinants with 50-kDa esterase.
review_notes: Supports pre-receptor glucocorticoid function, ER-lumen orientation dependence of activity, and 7-ketocholesterol metabolism. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Conformational flexibility in crystal structures of human 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type I provide insights into glucocorticoid interconversion and enzyme regulation.
review_notes: Crystal structures establishing cortisone/cortisol interconversion, oligomerization motif, and adipose-tissue disease relevance. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Adamantane sulfone and sulfonamide 11-beta-HSD1 Inhibitors.
review_notes: Inhibitor study confirming 11beta-HSD1 activity in liver, fat and brain. Abstract-only in cache.

title: The discovery of 2-anilinothiazolones as 11beta-HSD1 inhibitors.
review_notes: Inhibitor/X-ray co-crystal study confirming enzymatic activity and structure. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Structural characterization and pharmacodynamic effects of an orally active 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 inhibitor.
review_notes: Structural inhibitor study; supports homodimeric assembly. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Pyridine amides as potent and selective inhibitors of 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1.
review_notes: Structural inhibitor study; supports homodimeric assembly. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Discovery of novel, potent benzamide inhibitors of 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 (11beta-HSD1) exhibiting oral activity in an enzyme inhibition ex vivo model.
review_notes: Structural inhibitor study; supports homodimeric assembly. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Discovery and optimization of piperidyl benzamide derivatives as a novel class of 11beta-HSD1 inhibitors.
review_notes: Structural inhibitor study; supports homodimeric assembly. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane-proteome MS screen; source of the generic 'membrane' HDA annotation, not targeted localization evidence.

title: UniProtKB entry P28845 (DHI1_HUMAN), 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 1
review_notes: Curated UniProtKB record; source of catalytic-activity, subunit, subcellular location and function statements used as file-quote support.

title: Hypertension in the syndrome of apparent mineralocorticoid excess due to mutation of the 11 beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 gene.
review_notes: PubMed-verified case report of an AME kindred with an R374X truncating mutation showing severely attenuated NAD-dependent 11beta-HSD activity; directly supports the enzyme's NAD+-dependent 11beta-HSD activity and its role in cortisol metabolism and mineralocorticoid receptor specificity.

title: Intrinsic alcohol dehydrogenase and hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activities of human mitochondrial short-chain L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Kinetic characterization showing the alcohol/hydroxysteroid activities are orders of magnitude weaker than the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA activity, supporting non-core status of the steroid/ADH side activities.

title: Expanded substrate screenings of human and Drosophila type 10 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases (HSDs) reveal multiple specificities in bile acid and steroid hormone metabolism: characterization of multifunctional 3alpha/7alpha/7beta/17beta/20beta/21-HSD.
review_notes: Definitive substrate screen and mitochondrial localization; source of most steroid and bile-acid MF/BP annotations (in-vitro, non-core).

title: RNase P without RNA: identification and functional reconstitution of the human mitochondrial tRNA processing enzyme.
review_notes: Identified HSD17B10/MRPP2 as an essential subunit of the protein-only mitochondrial RNase P; foundational for the tRNA-processing core function.

title: Study of patients and carriers with 2-methyl-3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase (MHBD) deficiency: difficulties in the diagnosis.
review_notes: Patient/carrier study of MHBD deficiency supporting the isoleucine-catabolism role.

title: Mental retardation linked to mutations in the HSD17B10 gene interfering with neurosteroid and isoleucine metabolism.
review_notes: Links disease mutations to loss of both MHBD (isoleucine) and allopregnanolone (neurosteroid) oxidation; source of the brexanolone metabolic process annotation.

title: A non-enzymatic function of 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 10 is required for mitochondrial integrity and cell survival.
review_notes: Key evidence that disease severity is independent of enzymatic activity and driven by an essential non-enzymatic mitochondrial-integrity function; also the 1.2 A crystal structure.

title: Involvement of human ELAC2 gene product in 3' end processing of mitochondrial tRNAs.
review_notes: ELAC2 mitochondrial 3'-processing study; source of a NAS mitochondrion localization for HSD17B10 in the context of the tRNA-processing machinery.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: Global mRNA-interactome capture screen; source of the non-specific HDA "RNA binding" annotation, marked over-annotated (the relevant ligand is tRNA).

title: A subcomplex of human mitochondrial RNase P is a bifunctional methyltransferase--extensive moonlighting in mitochondrial tRNA biogenesis.
review_notes: Establishes the MRPP1-MRPP2 subcomplex as the m1A9/m1G9 methyltransferase requiring HSD17B10 as a non-catalytic partner.

title: Mutation or knock-down of 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 10 cause loss of MRPP1 and impaired processing of mitochondrial heavy strand transcripts.
review_notes: Shows HSD17B10 maintains MRPP1 levels and that its loss impairs heavy-strand mitochondrial tRNA processing; disease-relevant.

title: Initial steps in RNA processing and ribosome assembly occur at mitochondrial DNA nucleoids.
review_notes: Localizes RNase P/ELAC2 to mtDNA nucleoids; supports the mitochondrial-nucleoid localization annotation.

title: Mitochondrial energy failure in HSD10 disease is due to defective mtDNA transcript processing.
review_notes: Supports that HSD10 disease pathology stems from defective mtDNA transcript (tRNA) processing rather than the metabolic defect. Cited in notes; not an existing GOA annotation source.

title: Molecular insights into HSD10 disease: impact of SDR5C1 mutations on the human mitochondrial RNase P complex.
review_notes: Shows disease mutations impair dehydrogenation, tRNA processing, methylation, homotetramerization and TRMT10C interaction; source of several core annotations.

title: Myxococcus CsgA, Drosophila Sniffer, and human HSD10 are cardiolipin phospholipases.
review_notes: Establishes the cardiolipin phospholipase C-like (cardiolipin dehydrogenase) activity, inhibited by Aβ; a distinct in-vitro moonlighting activity (non-core).

title: A novel HSD17B10 mutation impairing the activities of the mitochondrial RNase P complex causes X-linked intractable epilepsy and neurodevelopmental regression.
review_notes: K212E patient mutation impairing SDR5C1-dependent RNase P activities; source of an EXP dehydrogenase annotation.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome study; source of a bare protein-binding (TRMT10C) IPI, marked over-annotated.

title: Novel patient missense mutations in the HSD17B10 gene affect dehydrogenase and mitochondrial tRNA modification functions of the encoded protein.
review_notes: V12L/V176M patient mutations reduce dehydrogenase, methyltransferase and tRNA processing; clean statement of the dual catalytic/non-catalytic functions.

title: The MRPP1/MRPP2 complex is a tRNA-maturation platform in human mitochondria.
review_notes: Shows MRPP1/2 retains tRNA after 5'-cleavage, enhances ELAC2 3'-processing and presents tRNA to the CCA-adding enzyme; source of tRNA-binding and processing annotations.

title: A Map of Human Mitochondrial Protein Interactions Linked to Neurodegeneration Reveals New Mechanisms of Redox Homeostasis and NF-κB Signaling.
review_notes: Mitochondrial interactome map; source of bare protein-binding IPIs (EEF2, TRAP1) of unclear functional significance, marked over-annotated.

title: Structural insight into the human mitochondrial tRNA purine N1-methyltransferase and ribonuclease P complexes.
review_notes: Structural study of the MRPP1/MRPP2 and RNase P complexes; source of RNase P complex, mitochondrion and 5'-processing annotations.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegeneration interactome; source of a bare protein-binding (APP/Aβ) IPI, marked over-annotated.

title: Study of Biomolecular Interactions of Mitochondrial Proteins Related to Alzheimer's Disease: Toward Multi-Interaction Biomolecular Processes.
review_notes: Alzheimer-related mitochondrial interaction study; source of a bare protein-binding (Aβ peptide) IPI, marked over-annotated.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome; source of a bare protein-binding (TRMT10C) IPI, marked over-annotated.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; supports mitochondrion localization.

title: Structural basis for human mitochondrial tRNA maturation.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of the four mt-tRNA maturation steps; supports the maturation-platform, CCA-addition and catalytic-complex annotations.

title: Structural basis of 3'-tRNA maturation by the human mitochondrial RNase Z complex.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of the mitochondrial RNase Z (ELAC2/SDR5C1/TRMT10C) complex; supports the 3'-processing and endoribonuclease-complex annotations.

title: An intracellular protein that binds amyloid-beta peptide and mediates neurotoxicity in Alzheimer's disease.

review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/Falcon) report; not independently verified, so marked UNVERIFIED. title: IDI2, a second isopentenyl diphosphate isomerase in mammals.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false). Definitive primary characterization of human IDI2: skeletal-muscle-restricted expression, IPP-to-DMAPP isomerase activity (Km 22.8 uM, pH optimum 8.0), yeast idi1 complementation, PTS1-dependent peroxisomal localization, and PPARalpha-linked regulation. Experimental basis for the GO:0004452 (IDA), peroxisome, and isoprenoid-process annotations.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Genome-scale AP-MS interactome (BioPlex). Cached full text does not name IDI2, but the IDI2-LDB1 (Q86U70-2) interaction it supports is recorded in the UniProt INTERACTION block. Supports only a bare "protein binding" annotation with no established functional role for IDI2; marked over-annotated.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Yeast two-hybrid binary interactome (HuRI). Cached full text does not name IDI2, but the IDI2-LDB1 (Q86U70-2) interaction it supports is recorded in the UniProt INTERACTION block. Supports only a bare "protein binding" annotation; marked over-annotated.

title: Evolution of vertebrate indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache. UniProt cites this paper (ECO:0000269) for the catalytic activity and biophysicochemical properties (Km 21.23 uM L-Trp vs 4.6 mM D-Trp). Directly supports the indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase MF for IDO1.

title: Molecular cloning, sequencing and expression of human interferon-gamma-inducible indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase cDNA.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Establishes the tryptophan-catabolizing (kynurenine-pathway) function and IFN-gamma inducibility. Does NOT establish electron transfer activity; the GO:0009055 TAS from this paper is an over-annotation.

title: Human renal tubular epithelial cells suppress alloreactive T cell proliferation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Supports the IMP annotations for indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase activity and positive regulation of T cell apoptotic process, and is consistent with the NOT annotation for regulation of activated T cell proliferation (IDO inhibitor failed to restore proliferation).

title: Prevention of allogeneic fetal rejection by tryptophan catabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Classic maternal-fetal tolerance study (mouse model). Supports the female pregnancy / maternal-fetal immune tolerance role annotated by TAS.

title: IDO1 dioxygenates L-Trp to NFK
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing the IDO1-catalyzed L-Trp -> N-formyl-L-kynurenine step and its cytosolic localization. Title left as fetched.

title: Expression of five iduronate-2-sulfatase site-directed mutations.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; supports IDS iduronate-2-sulfatase activity (residual activity of R88H/R88P mutants), the CXPSR formylglycine motif, and poor lysosomal transport of mutants. PubMed-verified title.

title: The effect of four mutations on the expression of iduronate-2-sulfatase in mucopolysaccharidosis type II.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; transient-expression/activity study of IDS MPS II mutations, supporting the iduronate-2-sulfatase activity annotation. PubMed-verified title.

title: Sulphatase activities are regulated by the interaction of sulphatase-modifying factor 1 with SUMF2.
review_notes: Full text available; source of the IDS-SUMF2 (Q8NBJ7) IntAct IPI. SUMF2 stably associates with IDS and modulates SUMF1/FGE-mediated sulfatase activation in the ER. Supports a real but peripheral interaction; the protein binding term is uninformative.

title: Hunter syndrome: isolation of an iduronate-2-sulfatase cDNA clone and analysis of patient DNA.
review_notes: Original IDS cDNA cloning paper; establishes IDS (EC 3.1.6.13) as required for lysosomal degradation of heparan and dermatan sulfate, and defines the precursor processing. PubMed-verified title.

title: Insights into Hunter syndrome from the structure of iduronate-2-sulfatase.
review_notes: Full text available; crystal structure (PDB 5FQL) of human IDS. Defines the catalytic mechanism (formylglycine at Cys84, active-site Ca2+), specific activity on iduronide-2-sulfate substrate, and role in stepwise GAG (HS/DS) degradation. Primary support for the MF, calcium binding, and GAG catabolism annotations.

title: Mucopolysaccharidosis type I, unique structure of accumulated heparan sulfate and increased N-sulfotransferase activity in mice lacking α-l-iduronidase.
review_notes: Murine Idua-knockout study directly demonstrating loss of terminal iduronate removal from heparan sulfate; supports the HS/heparin catabolic-process annotations.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; supports the extracellular-exosome localization annotation but is peripheral to IDUA's core lysosomal function.

title: Human α-L-iduronidase uses its own N-glycan as a substrate-binding and catalytic module.
review_notes: Structural/kinetic characterization of human IDUA; strong experimental support for the core L-iduronidase activity.

title: Insights into mucopolysaccharidosis I from the structure and action of α-L-iduronidase.
review_notes: Definitive structural and mechanistic study of human IDUA; primary support for the molecular function and HS/DS catabolic processes.

title: Immunopurification and characterization of human alpha-L-iduronidase with the use of monoclonal antibodies.
review_notes: Early biochemical characterization of the human enzyme; supports catalytic activity but its disaccharide-metabolic-process annotation reflects the assay substrate rather than the in vivo polymeric substrate.

title: Regulation of signal transduction by enzymatically inactive antiviral RNA helicase proteins MDA5, RIG-I, and LGP2.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Bamming & Horvath, J Biol Chem 284:9700-9712 (2009). This is the IMP source for both GO:0003724 and GO:0016887; what it measures is ATP hydrolysis and signalling competence, and it concludes that interferon induction is independent of helicase catalytic activity - the basis for the MODIFY on GO:0003724.

title: Ribose 2'-O-methylation provides a molecular signature for the distinction of self and non-self mRNA dependent on the RNA sensor Mda5.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Zuest et al., Nat Immunol 12:137-143 (2011). One of the two IDA sources for GO:0038187; demonstrates MDA5-dependent interferon induction by coronavirus mRNA lacking 2'-O-methylation.

title: Cooperative assembly and dynamic disassembly of MDA5 filaments for viral dsRNA recognition.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Peisley et al., PNAS 108:21010-21015 (2011). Source of the ATP-driven filament assembly/disassembly proofreading model.

title: Structural basis for dsRNA recognition, filament formation, and antiviral signal activation by MDA5.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Wu et al., Cell 152:276-289 (2013). The other IDA source for GO:0038187; crystal structure of MDA5 on dsRNA plus filament and CARD-oligomerisation model. Cached entry is abstract-only (full_text_available: false), so quoting is limited to the abstract.

title: Gain-of-function mutations in IFIH1 cause a spectrum of human disease phenotypes associated with upregulated type I interferon signaling.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Rice et al., Nat Genet 46:503-509 (2014). Establishes IFIH1 gain-of-function variants as a cause of Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome and related interferonopathies, with increased RNA binding - used here as evidence bearing on self-RNA sensing.

title: RNA editing by ADAR1 prevents MDA5 sensing of endogenous dsRNA as nonself.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Liddicoat et al., Science 349:1115-1120 (2015). Mouse genetics, not human IFIH1 biochemistry, hence MEDIUM: it shows that ADAR1 editing of endogenous dsRNA exists to prevent MDA5 activation, which is relevant background for the ligand question rather than direct evidence about the human protein.

title: Loss of cellular RNA homeostasis contributes to MDA5 activation during virus infection.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Sampaio et al., Nat Immunol 27:1815-1828 (2026), doi 10.1038/s41590-026-02614-3. Full text read. The central claim used here - that endogenous MDA5 iCLIP in SARS-CoV-2- and EMCV-infected cells recovers host, not viral, RNA - is quoted verbatim. The authors' own stated limitation (other viruses, cell types and timepoints not excluded) is recorded alongside it.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for IL23R prolactin receptor activity
review_notes: The focused GO:0004925 verdict is consistent with the GOA source trace and primary IL23R literature, but the report's separate suggestion that peptide hormone binding is acceptable is not adopted here.

title: Inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase binds nucleic acids in vitro and in vivo.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Hedstrom lab, Biochem J 2004). Establishes the CBS-subdomain single-stranded nucleic-acid-binding activity for both human IMPDH isoforms and IMPDH nuclear localization. Supports a moonlighting/regulatory (non-core) role rather than the enzyme's principal catalytic function; abstract-only in the cache.

title: Two distinct cDNAs for human IMP dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Natsumeda et al., J Biol Chem 1990). Original cloning of the two human IMPDH cDNAs (type I = IMPDH1, type II = IMPDH2); identifies IMP dehydrogenase (EC 1.1.1.205) as the rate-limiting enzyme of de novo guanine nucleotide biosynthesis. Directly supports the core catalytic function.

title: IMP + H2O + NAD+ => XMP + NADH + H+ [IMPDH1,2]
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the human IMP -> XMP dehydrogenation catalysed by IMPDH1 and IMPDH2; the summary confirms this is the rate-limiting step in GMP synthesis from IMP. Directly supports the core molecular function.

title: Inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase binds nucleic acids in vitro and in vivo.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes the rate-limiting role, the CBS-subdomain single-stranded nucleic-acid-binding moonlighting activity, and nuclear localization.

title: Two distinct cDNAs for human IMP dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; defines the two human isoforms (type I=IMPDH1, type II=IMPDH2) and the rate-limiting role in de novo GTP biosynthesis.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane proteome; supports only a peripheral/contaminant membrane detection of the cytosolic enzyme.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: Exosome proteomics; IMPDH2 detected as an abundant cytosolic protein, not a functional exosomal component.

title: PEX14 is required for microtubule-based peroxisome motility in human cells.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.

title: CLOCK Acetylates ASS1 to Drive Circadian Rhythm of Ureagenesis.

title: ANKRD9 is a metabolically-controlled regulator of IMPDH2 abundance and macro-assembly.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.

title: Mapping adipocyte interactome networks by HaloTag-enrichment-mass spectrometry.
review_notes: HaloTag affinity-MS adipocyte interactome; source of an uninformative protein binding IPI.
