title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were checked. This is the correct source for the eight grouped ITIH6 Y2H pairs, but it is a proteome-scale reference map rather than a gene-specific physiological study.

title: Characterization of ITIH6, a novel inter-α-inhibitor family member with prognostic significance in cholangiocarcinoma.
review_notes: PubMed identity, cached abstract, and open-access full text were checked. This is the first ITIH6-focused structure/expression study. It identifies a conserved candidate cleavage motif but explicitly leaves HA interaction, complex assembly, and mechanistic function for future investigation; the repository cache is abstract-only.

title: Manual literature synthesis for human ITIH6 (Q6UXX5)
review_notes: Manual evidence synthesis used because both configured automated providers failed. Conclusions are anchored to primary sources and clearly distinguish measured ITIH6 properties from family-based hypotheses.

title: Manual literature and annotation review notes for human ITIH6
review_notes: Manual synthesis of local GOA, reviewed UniProt, cached primary literature, and the open-access 2025 full text; it records provider failures and the evidence boundaries used for all four annotation groups.

title: UniProtKB record for human ITIH6 (Q6UXX5)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProtKB record checked directly. It supports identity, sequence architecture, signal peptide, and predicted secretion, but does not annotate ITIH6-specific heavy-chain processing, bikunin linkage, or biochemical function.

title: Molecular characterization of four different classes of mutations in the isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase gene responsible for isovaleric acidemia.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes IVD as a mitochondrial matrix enzyme and that its deficiency causes isovaleric acidemia (leucine metabolism disorder). Used as source for matrix localization (NAS) and the leucine-catabolism role.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified HuRI interactome paper. Correctly cited for the IPI protein-binding annotation (ACTN3, GPSM3), but these are high-throughput binary Y2H hits of unclear physiological relevance to a mitochondrial matrix enzyme; supports only a generic, over-annotated protein binding term.

title: Purification and properties of short chain acyl-CoA, medium chain acyl-CoA, and isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenases from human liver.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Purified human IVD to homogeneity, identified the isovaleryl-CoA reaction product as 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA, showed homotetrameric structure with 1 FAD/subunit and ETF as electron acceptor. Anchors the core MF, FAD binding, homotetramer, and the minor short-chain activity annotations.

title: Identification of the active site catalytic residue in human isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Defines the catalytic active-site glutamate by mutagenesis and confirms isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase activity of the human enzyme; the UniProt evidence for FUNCTION and EC 1.3.8.4/1.3.8.1. Primary source for the core molecular function.

title: KCTD10 interacts with proliferating cell nuclear antigen and its down-regulation could inhibit cell proliferation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source for the PCNA interaction and nuclear localization of KCTD10.

title: KCTD10 is involved in the cardiovascular system and Notch signaling during early embryonic development.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports KCTD10's role in Notch1 degradation during cardiovascular development.

title: Structural complexity in the KCTD family of Cullin3-dependent E3 ubiquitin ligases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; structural basis for KCTD10's pentameric BTB assembly and CUL3 binding.

title: The Cullin-3-Rbx1-KCTD10 complex controls endothelial barrier function via K63 ubiquitination of RhoB.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary experimental source for the RHOB substrate and the K63/endothelial-barrier function.

title: Cullin-3-KCTD10-mediated CEP97 degradation promotes primary cilium formation.
review_notes: Primary source for the CEP97 substrate, the adapter activity, and cytoplasmic localization. NOTE: this paper is mis-cited in GOA as the IDA evidence for GO:0160020 (positive regulation of ferroptosis); its abstract contains no ferroptosis/SLC7A11 content. The correct ferroptosis source is PMID:38959043.

title: The CRL3(KCTD10) ubiquitin ligase-USP18 axis coordinately regulates cystine uptake and ferroptosis by modulating SLC7A11.
review_notes: PMC-verified full text. The correct primary source for KCTD10's positive regulation of ferroptosis via SLC7A11 (the function GOA mis-attributes to PMID:30404837). UniProt cites this paper for the same function.

title: Subcellular localization and membrane topology of serine palmitoyltransferase, 3-dehydrosphinganine reductase, and sphinganine N-acyltransferase in mouse liver.
review_notes: Primary biochemical study localizing 3-dehydrosphinganine reductase (KDSR) activity to the cytosolic face of mouse liver ER; supports the reductase function and ER cytosolic-side topology.

title: FVT-1 is a mammalian 3-ketodihydrosphingosine reductase with an active site that faces the cytosolic side of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane.
review_notes: Key paper identifying human FVT-1/KDSR as the mammalian KDS reductase; purified enzyme has NADPH-dependent activity, localizes to ER, catalytic domain faces cytosol.

title: Lateral diffusion of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor type 1 is regulated by actin filaments and 4.1N in neuronal dendrites.
review_notes: This PMID is a study of IP3R1 lateral diffusion in neurons and does not concern KDSR, yet it is cited as the MGI IDA source for three KDSR annotations (ER localization, 3-keto-sphinganine metabolic process, and reductase activity). Appears to be a wrong-PMID/mis-attributed citation. The affected annotations are nonetheless biologically correct and are independently supported by PMID:15328338 and PMID:19141869.

title: Serinc, an activity-regulated protein family, incorporates serine into membrane lipid synthesis.
review_notes: Study of the Serinc family that forms complexes with serine/sphingolipid biosynthetic enzymes; abstract only, does not directly assay KDSR in ceramide synthesis. Used to support a pathway-level ceramide biosynthesis annotation.

title: Tsc10p and FVT1: topologically distinct short-chain reductases required for long-chain base synthesis in yeast and mammals.
review_notes: Establishes FVT1/KDSR as the principal mammalian 3-ketosphinganine reductase required for long-chain base (sphingoid) synthesis; provides silencing, mutagenesis, localization and topology data.

title: Identification of small subunits of mammalian serine palmitoyltransferase that confer distinct acyl-CoA substrate specificities.
review_notes: Abstract focuses on SPT small subunits; cited as the IDA source for KDSR being active on the cytoplasmic side of the ER membrane. Only the abstract is available; the cytosolic-face topology of KDSR is independently well established.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane proteomics; supports only the general "membrane" localization of KDSR.

title: Mutations in KDSR Cause Recessive Progressive Symmetric Erythrokeratoderma.
review_notes: Disease-gene identification; biallelic KDSR mutations cause progressive symmetric erythrokeratoderma, with yeast complementation showing loss of KDSR function.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale yeast two-hybrid interactome; source of four uninformative protein-binding interactions for KDSR (KIF1B, HSPB1, TTR, WFS1). No established functional relevance to KDSR's enzymatic role.

title: Glucosylceramide and galactosylceramide, small glycosphingolipids with significant impact on health and disease.
review_notes: Review of glucosyl-/galactosylceramide biology; does not mention or assay KDSR. Cited for a glycosphingolipid biosynthesis annotation that is several enzymatic steps downstream of KDSR - a pathway-level over-annotation.

title: De novo sphingolipid biosynthesis necessitates detoxification in cancer cells.
review_notes: Full text available; shows KDSR reduces 3KDS to sphinganine and that KDSR loss causes toxic 3KDS accumulation, ER dysfunction and proteotoxic stress, highlighting KDSR as a cancer therapy target.

title: FVT-1, a novel human transcription unit affected by variant translocation t(2;18)(p11;q21) of follicular lymphoma.
review_notes: Original FVT-1 cloning paper describing the follicular-lymphoma translocation and predicting a "putatively secreted protein"; the secretion prediction (basis of the extracellular-region annotation) was later superseded by ER membrane topology.

title: UniProtKB entry Q06136 (KDSR_HUMAN)
review_notes: UniProt record for human KDSR; source of catalytic activity (EC 1.1.1.102, RHEA:22640), ER membrane multi-pass topology, NADPH-binding sites, and disease associations.

title: Properties of normal and mutant recombinant human ketohexokinases and implications for the pathogenesis of essential fructosuria.
review_notes: Primary enzymology of recombinant human KHK; establishes ketohexokinase activity (EC 2.7.1.3), that both KHK-A and KHK-C isoforms are active, kinetic parameters, and the disease mechanism of essential fructosuria (G40R null, A43T thermolabile). Directly supports the core catalytic function and fructose metabolic process annotations. Cached entry is abstract-only (full_text_available false).

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary exosome proteomics; source of the extracellular exosome HDA localization. Detection of a highly expressed cytosolic enzyme in exosomes, not a functional localization. Abstract-only cache does not name KHK individually (part of the 1132-protein dataset).

title: Structures of alternatively spliced isoforms of human ketohexokinase.
review_notes: Full-text-available crystal structures of KHK-A and KHK-C and the KHK-A ternary complex with fructose and AMP-PNP. Directly supports ATP binding, fructose binding, homodimerization/identical protein binding, and the committed fructolysis role. Verified against cached full text.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale Y2H interactome; source of the bare "protein binding" IPI (KHK-LHX9, Q9NQ69). The cached full text does not mention KHK or LHX9 specifically (the interaction lives in the supplementary dataset). Low information value for KHK's molecular function; retained as over-annotated.

title: Molecular basis of essential fructosuria: molecular cloning and mutational analysis of human ketohexokinase (fructokinase).
review_notes: Original cloning and mutational analysis defining KHK as hepatic fructokinase (EC 2.7.1.3) and the molecular basis of essential fructosuria (compound heterozygous G40R / A43T). Supports ketohexokinase activity and disease role. Abstract-only cache.

title: Liver-specific activities of FGF19 require Klotho beta.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The paper directly supports the curated FGFR-binding record and mammalian FGF19-KLB-FGFR4 signaling; its physiological CYP7A1 experiment is in mouse, so the human process proposal uses ISS.

title: C-terminal tail of FGF19 determines its specificity toward Klotho co-receptors.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. Chimera experiments directly support endocrine-FGF recognition by KLB; only the abstract is cached.

title: FGF21 N- and C-termini play different roles in receptor interaction and activation.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The paper supports replacing generic protein binding with fibroblast growth factor binding; only the abstract is cached.

title: Different roles of N- and C- termini in the functional activity of FGF21.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. Binding and deletion experiments independently support FGF21 recognition by KLB; only the abstract is cached.

title: Structures of β-klotho reveal a 'zip code'-like mechanism for endocrine FGF signalling.
review_notes: PubMed identity, PMC full text, human crystal structures, quantitative binding assays, mutagenesis, and cell-signaling experiments were verified. This is the decisive source for pseudoenzyme status and KLB coreceptor mechanism.

title: Structures of ligand-occupied β-Klotho complexes reveal a molecular mechanism underlying endocrine FGF specificity and activity.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The paper supplies direct human structural support for FGF19 binding to KLB; locally accessible content is abstract-only.

title: Manual deep-research synthesis for human KLB
review_notes: Reviewer-authored synthesis of the fetched UniProt record, complete GOA set, and cached primary literature, including explicit evidence boundaries and provider failures.

title: Manual KLB curation notes
review_notes: Reviewer-authored annotation decision log with inline provenance and explicit handling of the inactive GH-like domains.

title: UniProtKB record for human KLB (Q86Z14)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProt record fetched by the project; used for accession, sequence, membrane topology, family, and domain metadata.

title: Functional characterization and mechanism of action of recombinant human kynurenine 3-hydroxylase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Characterizes recombinant human KMO: NADPH-dependent flavin monooxygenase, one non-covalently bound FAD per enzyme, pH optimum 7.5, kinetics; documents peroxide-forming uncoupling. Directly supports the core catalytic, FAD-binding and OMM annotations.

title: Structural basis of kynurenine 3-monooxygenase inhibition.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Reports the first KMO crystal structures (yeast KMO +/- inhibitor) validated against human KMO, confirms FAD-dependence and outer mitochondrial membrane localization, and documents inhibitor-accelerated H2O2 formation (basis of the non-core NAD(P)H oxidase activity).

title: Kynurenine-3-monooxygenase inhibition prevents multiple organ failure in rodent models of acute pancreatitis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Kmo-knockout metabolic profiling establishes KMO as the gatekeeper of kynurenine metabolism (loss diverts flux to kynurenic acid); characterizes human KMO activity and a potent inhibitor. Supports the tryptophan-catabolism/gatekeeper role and refutes a kynurenic-acid-biosynthesis role.

title: Biochemistry and structural studies of kynurenine 3-monooxygenase reveal allosteric inhibition by Ro 61-8048.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Biochemical/structural study of human KMO with active-site mutagenesis (R85, Y99, N363, E366, M367, Y398 abolish/strongly reduce activity) and evidence that the C-terminal region is essential; supports the core catalytic MF annotation.

title: Structural Basis for Inhibitor-Induced Hydrogen Peroxide Production by Kynurenine 3-Monooxygenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Human KMO structure (PDB 5X68) in complex with FAD; defines FAD-binding residues and inhibitor-induced H2O2 production. Supports the core FAD-binding annotation and the non-core NAD(P)H oxidase side activity.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified large-scale quantitative mitochondrial proteome dataset. Provides HTP-level support for mitochondrial localization of KMO but is not KMO-specific; less informative than the experimental outer-mitochondrial-membrane evidence.

title: Cloning and functional expression of human kynurenine 3-monooxygenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Original cloning and functional expression of human KMO; establishes it as an NADPH-dependent flavin monooxygenase hydroxylating L-kynurenine, tissue expression (liver/placenta/kidney), and OMM localization. Foundational support for the core catalytic and localization annotations.

title: Purification and biochemical characterization of some of the properties of recombinant human kynureninase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; biochemical characterization establishing kynureninase activity and the strong 3-hydroxykynurenine preference. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Crystal structure of Homo sapiens kynureninase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; structural and kinetic characterization establishing PLP dependence, fold-type I superfamily membership and substrate preference. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Xanthurenic aciduria due to a mutation in KYNU encoding kynureninase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; links KYNU deficiency to hydroxykynureninuria (HYXKY). Abstract-only in cache.

title: High-performance liquid chromatographic assay of human lymphocyte kynureninase activity levels.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports the vitamin-B6 (PLP) dependence of kynureninase activity (basis for the response-to-vitamin-B6 annotation). Abstract-only.

title: NAD Deficiency, Congenital Malformations, and Niacin Supplementation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes the NAD-deficiency/VCRL2 disease mechanism and in-vitro activity of mutant KYNU. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Intracellular localization and characterization of 3-hydroxykynureninase in human liver.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; early biochemical localization/characterization of the human liver enzyme. Basis for both cytosol and mitochondrion IDA annotations. Abstract-only.

title: Isolation and expression of a cDNA clone encoding human kynureninase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary cloning and functional expression of human kynureninase establishing the catalytic activity and PLP dependence. Abstract-only.

title: Cloning and recombinant expression of rat and human kynureninase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; independent cloning/kinetic characterization of human kynureninase. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Different kynurenine pathway enzymes limit quinolinic acid formation by various human cell types.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports the quinolinate-biosynthesis and IFN-gamma-response annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Structural basis for altered activity of M- and H-isozyme forms of human lactate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; crystal structures of human M (LDHA) and H (LDHB) isoforms as NADH/oxamate ternary complexes; establishes catalytic activity and homotetramerization. Abstract-only in cache but directly on-target.

title: Molecular characterization of genetic mutation in human lactate dehydrogenase-A (M) deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; characterizes a frameshift mutation causing human LDH-A(M) deficiency (GSD11). Directly relevant to LDHA function and disease.

title: Structural characterization of the apo form and NADH binary complex of human lactate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; apo and NADH-bound crystal structures of human LDH-A; describes A vs B subunit kinetics and the five A/B tetramer isoenzymes.

title: E-cadherin interactome complexity and robustness resolved by quantitative proteomics.
review_notes: BioID proximity-proteomics study; LDHA is a proximity hit near the E-cadherin tail, not a demonstrated functional cadherin interactor.

title: An Upstream Open Reading Frame in Phosphatase and Tensin Homolog Encodes a Circuit Breaker of Lactate Metabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; identifies MP31 micropeptide that competes with LDH for NAD+; supports the LDHA-MP31 IPI. Regulatory context, not core enzyme function.

title: The tumor suppressor folliculin inhibits lactate dehydrogenase A and regulates the Warburg effect.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; FLCN is a direct uncompetitive inhibitor of LDHA; functional activity assays and dimer/tetramer state analysis support the MF (IMP) and interaction (IPI) annotations.

title: Structural basis for altered activity of M- and H-isozyme forms of human lactate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; establishes the core L-lactate dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity and the H (heart) subunit identity of LDHB.

title: Identification and activity of a series of azole-based compounds with lactate dehydrogenase-directed anti-malarial activity.
review_notes: Primarily about Plasmodium LDH inhibitors; used by ComplexPortal as the reference for the human LDH complex annotations. Supports LDH's central role in NAD+ regeneration.

title: Proteomics of human umbilical vein endothelial cells applied to etoposide-induced apoptosis.
review_notes: HUVEC proteomics; source of a TAS cytoplasm localization. Contextual only.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Exosome proteomics; abundant-cytosolic-protein detection, not a functional localization.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Membrane-fraction proteomics; generic membrane detection for a soluble enzyme.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: Exosome proteomics; abundant-cytosolic-protein detection.

title: Genome-wide YFP fluorescence complementation screen identifies new regulators for telomere signaling in human cells.
review_notes: High-throughput interaction screen (TERF1); source of a generic protein binding datum.

title: Toward an understanding of the protein interaction network of the human liver.
review_notes: Interactome study (LDHA); generic protein binding datum consistent with LDH tetramer assembly.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Exosome proteomics; abundant-cytosolic-protein detection.

title: Ribosomal protein s15 phosphorylation mediates LRRK2 neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease.
review_notes: LRRK2 interactome context; generic protein binding datum.

title: Flotillin-1 facilitates toll-like receptor 3 signaling in human endothelial cells.
review_notes: Membrane-raft proteomics; the raft localization of a soluble glycolytic enzyme is most likely a co-isolation artifact.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Interactome map; source of protein binding (LDHA) and identical protein binding (self) data.

title: A massively parallel pipeline to clone DNA variants and examine molecular phenotypes of human disease mutations.
review_notes: Variant-cloning interaction pipeline; source of an identical protein binding (self) datum consistent with homotetramerization.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Interaction-perturbation study (LDHA); generic protein binding datum.

title: Lactate metabolism is associated with mammalian mitochondria.
review_notes: Full text available; direct experimental support for LDHB catalytic activity, tetramer composition, H-subunit identity, and a non-canonical mitochondrial localization.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Interactome community study (LDHA/LDHC); generic protein binding data.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Variant interaction study (LDHA); source of protein binding and identical protein binding data.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Binary interactome map; source of protein binding (SDCBP/LDHA) and identical protein binding (self) data.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegeneration interactome (HTT); generic protein binding datum.

title: An Upstream Open Reading Frame in Phosphatase and Tensin Homolog Encodes a Circuit Breaker of Lactate Metabolism.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; UniProt curates this as the LDHB-MP31 (C0HLV8) interaction abolished by LDHB D53A/R100A. Functionally meaningful regulatory interaction, though annotated only as generic protein binding.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Cell-specific interactome remodeling (LDHA/LDHC); generic protein binding data.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell interactome (LDHA/LDHC); generic protein binding data.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map interactome (LDHC); generic protein binding datum.

title: Analysis of a genetic mutation in an electrophoretic variant of the human lactate dehydrogenase-B(H) subunit.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; source of the TAS L-lactate dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity annotation and confirms LDHB = H subunit.

title: Human galectin-3 is a novel chemoattractant for monocytes and macrophages.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary paper; underpins the BHF-UCL chemotaxis/migration IDA annotations. Shows galectin-3 chemoattracts monocytes/macrophages, blocked by lactose, via a PTX-sensitive pathway - i.e. a downstream consequence of its lectin/lattice activity.

title: Galectin-9 induces maturation of human monocyte-derived dendritic cells.
review_notes: This paper is about galectin-9, not galectin-3; it grounds a NOT annotation indicating galectin-3 does not promote dendritic cell differentiation.

title: Galectin-3 negatively regulates TCR-mediated CD4+ T-cell activation at the immunological synapse.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports immunological synapse localization and negative regulation of TCR signaling / endocytosis. The ISS T-cell terms are transferred from mouse ortholog (P16110) using this paper.

title: Analysis of proteomic changes induced upon cellular differentiation of the human intestinal cell line Caco-2.
review_notes: Proteomic differentiation study of Caco-2 cells; correlative IEP evidence for an association with epithelial cell differentiation, not a direct functional assay.

title: Human IgE-binding protein: a soluble lectin exhibiting a highly conserved interspecies sequence and differential recognition of IgE glycoforms.
review_notes: Original cloning/characterization establishing galectin-3 as a soluble lectin that binds IgE glycoforms.

title: Downregulation of galectin-3 by EGF mediates the apoptosis of HepG2 cells.
review_notes: Supports an anti-apoptotic role of cytoplasmic galectin-3 in tumor cells and its nuclear/cytoplasmic localization.

title: Molecular cloning of a human macrophage lectin specific for galactose.
review_notes: Original cloning of galectin-3 as a galactose-specific macrophage lectin; supports laminin binding and the core galactoside-binding identity.

title: β1,6 GlcNAc branches-modified PTPRT attenuates its activity and promotes cell migration by STAT3 pathway.
review_notes: Shows galectin-3 binds branched N-glycans on PTPRT and promotes its dimerization, indirectly reducing phosphatase activity - a glycan-lattice effect, not a direct enzyme-inhibitor molecular function.

title: Tumor-released Galectin-3, a soluble inhibitory ligand of human NKp30, plays an important role in tumor escape from NK cell attack.
review_notes: Establishes galectin-3 as a soluble inhibitory ligand of NKp30 (NCR3), supporting receptor ligand inhibitor activity and negative regulation of NK/NKT activation.

title: Group 2 Innate Lymphoid Cells Express Functional NKp30 Receptor Inducing Type 2 Cytokine Production.
review_notes: Galectin-3 acts as an inhibitory ligand blocking NKp30-B7-H6 activation of ILC2; supports receptor ligand inhibitor activity and the negative-regulation immune terms.

title: TRIMs and Galectins Globally Cooperate and TRIM16 and Galectin-3 Co-direct Autophagy in Endomembrane Damage Homeostasis.
review_notes: Full text available. Establishes galectin-3 + TRIM16 cooperation in sensing damaged endomembranes and directing autophagy - a key intracellular glycan-sensing function.

title: The intrinsically disordered N-terminal domain of galectin-3 dynamically mediates multisite self-association of the protein through fuzzy interactions.
review_notes: Full text available. Mechanistic basis for galectin-3 multivalency - the disordered N-terminal tail self-associates and drives liquid-liquid phase separation.

title: Novel polysaccharide binding to the N-terminal tail of galectin-3 is likely modulated by proline isomerization.
review_notes: Full text available. NMR mapping of carbohydrate binding sites including a novel site in the N-terminal tail; supports carbohydrate binding (EXP, DisProt).

title: Liquid-liquid phase separation and extracellular multivalent interactions in the tale of galectin-3.
review_notes: Full text available. Shows the N-terminal domain drives LLPS and that this explains galectin-3's extracellular agglutination/bridging of glycosylated molecules.

title: A Translocation Pathway for Vesicle-Mediated Unconventional Protein Secretion.
review_notes: Establishes the TMED10-facilitated non-classical secretion route for galectin-3 (cytoplasm to ERGIC to extracellular); supports cytoplasm and extracellular region localization.

title: MERIT, a cellular system coordinating lysosomal repair, removal and replacement.
review_notes: Full text available (PMC). Landmark study establishing that cytosolic LGALS3/galectin-3 detects lysosomal membrane damage by binding exposed luminal glycans, then recruits/organizes ESCRT components (PDCD6IP/ALIX, CHMP4A, CHMPB) for membrane repair and, at later stages, cooperates with TRIM16 to drive autophagic removal (lysophagy) of damaged lysosomes. Directly supports the damaged-endomembrane glycan-sensing role and the new lysophagy annotation.

title: LGALS3 (galectin 3) mediates an unconventional secretion of SNCA/α-synuclein in response to lysosomal membrane damage by the autophagic-lysosomal pathway in human midbrain dopamine neurons.
review_notes: Full text available (PMC). Shows LGALS3 senses lysosomal membrane damage and mediates TRIM16/ATG16L1-dependent autophagic (unconventional) secretion of SNCA/alpha-synuclein in human midbrain dopamine neurons, linking the galectin-3 damaged-endomembrane sensing role to secretory autophagy and cell-to-cell propagation of pathological alpha-synuclein. Context-specific neuronal disease mechanism downstream of the core glycan-sensing function.

title: Galectin-3 directs mitophagy in response to Parkin-/proteasome-dependent rupture of mitochondrial outer membrane.
review_notes: Full text available (PMC). Proteomic study showing galectin-3 is enriched on the ruptured outer membrane of damaged mitochondria, relocalizes from the cytosol to enclose them, interacts with PHB2 and recruits ULK1 to drive PINK1/Parkin mitophagy. Critically, residue mutations that abolish galectin-3 liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) abrogate its mitochondrial relocalization and mitophagy function, directly tying the LLPS/condensate-scaffold molecular function to intracellular organelle quality control. Emerging, context-specific extension of the damaged-endomembrane glycan-sensing role.

title: Decreased expression of Mac-2 (carbohydrate binding protein 35) and loss of its nuclear localization are associated with the neoplastic progression of colon carcinoma.
review_notes: Supports nuclear localization of galectin-3 (Mac-2/CBP35) in colonic epithelium.

title: Expression of galectin-3 modulates T-cell growth and apoptosis.
review_notes: Shows galectin-3 overexpression promotes T-cell growth and resistance to apoptosis; notes Bcl-2-like NWGR motif and lactose-inhibitable Bcl-2 interaction.

title: X-ray crystal structure of the human galectin-3 carbohydrate recognition domain at 2.1-A resolution.
review_notes: High-resolution structure of the galectin-3 CRD; structural basis of beta-galactoside recognition (PDB 1A3K).

title: Bleeding due to disruption of a cargo-specific ER-to-Golgi transport complex.
review_notes: Establishes the LMAN1-MCFD2 complex as a cargo receptor for ER-to-Golgi transport of FV/FVIII; MCFD2 localized to ERGIC via Ca2+-dependent LMAN1 interaction. Source of the cargo receptor complex and ERGIC membrane annotations.

title: Proteomics of endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC) membranes from brefeldin A-treated HepG2 cells identifies ERGIC-32, a new cycling protein that interacts with human Erv46.
review_notes: ERGIC proteomics enriched ERGIC-53 ~110-fold; supports ERGIC localization. Primary focus is ERGIC-32, but ERGIC-53 is the enrichment marker.

title: Combined deficiency of factor V and factor VIII is due to mutations in either LMAN1 or MCFD2.
review_notes: F5F8D is due to LMAN1 or MCFD2 mutations; the complex is a cargo receptor ferrying FV/FVIII from ER to Golgi. Source of an LMAN1-MCFD2 IPI annotation.

title: Sequential steps and checkpoints in the early exocytic compartment during secretory IgM biogenesis.
review_notes: ERp44 interacts with the hexameric ERGIC-53 lectin; source of the ERGIC-53/ERp44 IPI annotation.

title: Deletion of 3 residues from the C-terminus of MCFD2 affects binding to ERGIC-53 and causes combined factor V and factor VIII deficiency.
review_notes: ERGIC-53/MCFD2 complex functions as transport receptor of FV/FVIII; MCFD2 C-terminal deletion impairs binding and causes F5F8D.

title: The cargo receptors Surf4, endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC)-53, and p25 are required to maintain the architecture of ERGIC and Golgi.
review_notes: Surf4+ERGIC-53 silencing fragments Golgi and reduces ERGIC clusters via impaired COPI recruitment; supports Golgi organization (IMP) and the NOT early-endosome-to-Golgi negation (ERGIC-53 acts in ER/ERGIC/Golgi, not endosomal traffic). Source of the Surf4 IPI.

title: Proteomic analysis of human parotid gland exosomes by multidimensional protein identification technology (MudPIT).
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; basis for the extracellular exosome over-annotation, not a true site of ERGIC-53 action.

title: Role of syntaxin 18 in the organization of endoplasmic reticulum subdomains.
review_notes: Direct evidence supporting ER localization of ERGIC-53.

title: A novel missense mutation causing abnormal LMAN1 in a Japanese patient with combined deficiency of factor V and factor VIII.
review_notes: F5F8D1 W67S variant in the CRD abolishes MCFD2 interaction and D-mannose binding; recombinant WT LMAN1 binds D-mannose but the mutant does not. Key support for the D-mannose binding molecular function.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane proteomics; basis for the uninformative bare "membrane" annotation.

title: Crystal structure of the LMAN1-CRD/MCFD2 transport receptor complex provides insight into combined deficiency of factor V and factor VIII.
review_notes: Crystal structure of the LMAN1-CRD/MCFD2 complex; LMAN1 is a glycoprotein receptor mediating ER-to-ERGIC transfer with co-receptor MCFD2.

title: Structural basis for the cooperative interplay between the two causative gene products of combined factor V and factor VIII deficiency.
review_notes: ERGIC-53-CRD binds MCFD2 at a surface remote from the sugar-binding site, independent of sugar binding; forms a 1:1 complex. Defines the cargo receptor interface.

title: C4orf41 and TTC-15 are mammalian TRAPP components with a role at an early stage in ER-to-Golgi trafficking.
review_notes: TRAPP study; provides direct ERGIC localization evidence for ERGIC-53 in early ER-to-Golgi trafficking.

title: Protein interaction profiling of the p97 adaptor UBXD1 points to a role for the complex in modulating ERGIC-53 trafficking.
review_notes: p97-UBXD1 modulates ERGIC-53 trafficking; ERGIC-53 C-terminal tail interacts with RAB3GAP1/2 and UBXN6. Source of these IPI partners.

title: High-content genome-wide RNAi screens identify regulators of parkin upstream of mitophagy.
review_notes: Genome-wide parkin-translocation RNAi screen; LMAN1 is a high-throughput hit underlying the negative-regulation-of-protein-localization-to-mitochondrion annotation. Peripheral, not mechanistically connected to ERGIC-53's core function.

title: Structural basis for disparate sugar-binding specificities in the homologous cargo receptors ERGIC-53 and VIP36.
review_notes: ERGIC-53 and VIP36 are L-type lectin cargo receptors; ERGIC-53 has broad, lower-affinity high-mannose specificity. Ca2+ in the CRD underpins the metal ion binding annotation.

title: TMEM115 is an integral membrane protein of the Golgi complex involved in retrograde transport.
review_notes: TMEM115 (Golgi, COG-interacting) interacts with ERGIC-53; source of the TMEM115 IPI annotation.

title: Extracellular matrix signatures of human primary metastatic colon cancers and their metastases to liver.
review_notes: High-throughput ECM proteomics; basis for the extracellular matrix over-annotation, not a true ECM localization.

title: Characterization of the Extracellular Matrix of Normal and Diseased Tissues Using Proteomics.
review_notes: High-throughput ECM proteomics; basis for the extracellular matrix over-annotation.

title: The E3 ubiquitin ligase MARCH2 regulates ERGIC3-dependent trafficking of secretory proteins.
review_notes: Primarily about ERGIC3, but documents SERPINA1/alpha-1-antitrypsin as a secretory glycoprotein cargo; source of the ERGIC-53/SERPINA1 IPI annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex high-throughput interactome; source of an LMAN1-MCFD2 IPI capture.

title: BET1 variants establish impaired vesicular transport as a cause for muscular dystrophy with epilepsy.
review_notes: Identifies ERGIC-53 as a novel interaction partner of the ER-to-Golgi SNARE BET1; source of the BET1 IPI annotation.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous-tagging interactome; source of an LMAN1-MCFD2 IPI capture.

title: Separate roles of LMAN1 and MCFD2 in ER-to-Golgi trafficking of FV and FVIII.
review_notes: Dissects separable roles; cargo binding/transport are carried out by MCFD2 with LMAN1 acting as a shuttling carrier; N-glycan binding by LMAN1 is not essential for FV/FVIII transport. Supports the ER-to-Golgi transport process annotation.

title: Cargo selection in endoplasmic reticulum-to-Golgi transport and relevant diseases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:36594468, Tang & Ginsburg, J Clin Invest 2023, DOI 10.1172/jci163838). Authoritative review of ER-to-Golgi cargo receptors framing LMAN1/ERGIC-53 as a prototypical L-type lectin cargo receptor with a luminal CRD, coiled-coil stalk, TM helix, and a cytosolic KKFF motif (FF = ER-exit/COPII determinant; KK = COPI retrieval), and noting the cargo repertoire and recognition rules remain incompletely defined. Not cached; no supporting_text added. Identified via Falcon deep research.

title: Structure of full-length ERGIC-53 in complex with MCFD2 for cargo transport.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:38493152, Watanabe et al., Nat Commun 2024, DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-46747-1). Cryo-EM structure of full-length human ERGIC-53/LMAN1 in complex with MCFD2, resolving a homotetrameric assembly (a "four-leaf clover" head with a long four-helix-bundle coiled-coil stalk and the TM anchor), revising older hexamer models, and proposing regulation of cargo capture/release via stalk bending and metal (Zn2+/Ca2+) binding, including an N-terminal Zn2+ site in MCFD2. The top-level description has been updated to reflect this homotetramer (revising the older hexamer model). Not cached; no supporting_text added. Identified via Falcon deep research.

title: LMAN1 serves as a cargo receptor for thrombopoietin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:39499573, Everett et al., JCI Insight 2024, DOI 10.1172/jci.insight.175704). Identifies thrombopoietin (TPO) as a new LMAN1-dependent cargo: Lman1-/- and hepatocyte-specific Lman1-deletion mice show reduced plasma TPO and thrombocytopenia despite unchanged hepatic Tpo mRNA, TPO co-IPs with LMAN1, and this cargo relationship is MCFD2-independent (MCFD2 did not co-IP with TPO). Expands the LMAN1 cargo repertoire and links LMAN1 to platelet homeostasis. Not cached; no supporting_text added. Identified via Falcon deep research.

title: ERGIC-53, a membrane protein of the endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi intermediate compartment, is identical to MR60, an intracellular mannose-specific lectin of myelomonocytic cells.
review_notes: Not cached in publications/; foundational identification of ERGIC-53 as the mannose-specific lectin MR60. Supporting text drawn from the UniProt record, which documents this identity and the ER/Golgi membrane localization.

title: Mutations in the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment protein ERGIC-53 cause combined deficiency of coagulation factors V and VIII.
review_notes: Foundational F5F8D paper; proposes ERGIC-53 as a chaperone/receptor for ER-to-Golgi transport of a subset of secreted proteins including FV and FVIII.

title: Molecular cloning of the oncofetal isoform of the human pancreatic bile salt-dependent lipase.
review_notes: Cloning study; source of an IPI interaction (bile salt-dependent lipase, O75612). Peripheral to ERGIC-53's established function.

title: Characterization of the Extracellular Matrix of Normal and Diseased Tissues Using Proteomics.
review_notes: PMC-verified ECM proteomics methods paper; sole source of the extracellular matrix HDA annotation. The text explicitly flags LMAN1L as a transmembrane protein detected only in the insoluble pellet, so this is a peripheral/contaminant detection, not evidence of an extracellular function.

title: UniProt entry Q9HAT1 (LMA1L_HUMAN), Protein ERGIC-53-like (LMAN1L/ERGL)
review_notes: Primary source for LMAN1L domain architecture, membrane topology, family/lectin assignment, similarity-based ERGIC localization, and tissue specificity. Underscores that functional roles are homology-inferred (PE 2, ECO:0000250) rather than experimentally demonstrated.

title: Proteomics of endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC) membranes from brefeldin A-treated HepG2 cells identifies ERGIC-32, a new cycling protein that interacts with human Erv46.
review_notes: ERGIC proteomics study; supports VIP36 ERGIC localization (IDA). Title foregrounds ERGIC-32 but VIP36 is among the cargo receptors in the ERGIC-enriched fraction.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics catalog; supports only an over-annotated extracellular exosome localization.

title: Role of the lectin VIP36 in post-ER quality control of human alpha1-antitrypsin.
review_notes: Key functional paper establishing VIP36's high-mannose binding (D-mannose binding IMP), ERGIC/Golgi localization, retrograde Golgi-to-ER recycling, and the alpha1-AT (protein binding IPI) / BiP (heat shock protein binding IPI) interactions. Cached entry is abstract-only.

title: VIP36 protein is a target of ectodomain shedding and regulates phagocytosis in macrophage Raw 264.7 cells.
review_notes: Source of the cell-surface / plasma membrane / extracellular region IDA and the positive regulation of phagocytosis IMP. Establishes the secondary shedding/macrophage role; confirms ER-Golgi as the main localization.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics catalog; supports only an over-annotated extracellular exosome localization.

title: Parallel quantification of lectin-glycan interaction using ultrafiltration.
review_notes: Quantitative biophysical support for VIP36 carbohydrate (high-mannose) binding (carbohydrate binding IDA).

title: Exploring the landscape of ectodomain shedding by quantitative protein terminomics.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:33796845, Tsumagari et al., iScience 2021, DOI 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102476). Quantitative protein terminomics identifies VIP36/LMAN2 as a metalloprotease-regulated ectodomain-shedding substrate with a reproducible cleavage site at F298 down-arrow L299 (SVNF/LKSP) detected across multiple cell lines and reduced by the broad-spectrum metalloprotease inhibitor BB-94. Provides the specific cleavage-site mechanism underlying the previously curated cell-surface shedding role (PMID:22016386). Not cached; no supporting_text added. Identified via Falcon deep research.

title: Profile-based data base scanning for animal L-type lectins and characterization of VIPL, a novel VIP36-like endoplasmic reticulum protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary characterization of VIPL. Establishes ER-resident localization, L-type lectin domain/high-mannose glycoprotein status, and the regulator-of-ERGIC-53 model. Mannose binding is inferred from the conserved CRD/homology rather than a direct binding assay in the abstract.

title: VIPL, a VIP36-like membrane protein with a putative function in the export of glycoproteins from the endoplasmic reticulum.
review_notes: PubMed-verified functional study; provides the IMP knockdown evidence and the ER/Golgi localization underpinning the ER export receptor model.

title: Intracellular lectins involved in folding and transport in the endoplasmic reticulum.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:19420740; DOI:10.1248/bpb.32.767). Authoritative review of intracellular L-type lectins (ERGIC-53/LMAN1, VIP36/LMAN2, VIPL/LMAN2L) in ER glycoprotein quality control and transport. Background/contextual support for the family-level lectin and ER-export framing; not LMAN2L-primary. Not in publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Homozygous missense mutation in the LMAN2L gene segregates with intellectual disability in a large consanguineous Pakistani family.
review_notes: Establishes LMAN2L involvement in autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder MRT52 (R53Q variant). Disease relevance; not a direct source of an MF/CC/BP term.

title: Dominant LMAN2L mutation causes intellectual disability with remitting epilepsy.
review_notes: Establishes LMAN2L involvement in autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder MRD69. Disease relevance; not a direct source of an MF/CC/BP term.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput HuRI binary interactome; source of the IPI protein binding annotation with MAL (P21145). Not informative for VIPL's specific function.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegenerative-disease Y2H interactome; source of the IPI protein binding annotation with huntingtin HTT (P42858). Not informative for VIPL's core function.

title: Novel compound heterozygous variants in lectin mannose-binding 2-like gene identified in a Chinese autosomal recessive mental retardation-52 (MRT52) patient with phenotype expansion.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:37667433; DOI:10.1097/CM9.0000000000002285). Extends MRT52 beyond consanguineous homozygous pedigrees by reporting compound heterozygous LMAN2L variants (c.256C>T p.R86C; c.902del p.F301Sfs*8) in a Chinese proband with phenotype expansion (developmental delay, severe ID, early seizures, hearing loss, dystonia). Disease relevance; not a direct source of an MF/CC/BP term. Not in publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: HCMV US2 co-opts TRC8 to degrade the endoplasmic reticulum-resident protein LMAN2L.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:38687323; DOI:10.1099/jgv.0.001980). First gene-specific cell-biology study to directly assay LMAN2L as an endogenous protein - identifies LMAN2L as a novel target of HCMV pUS2, degraded via the host E3 ligase TRC8 (ERAD). Plasma-membrane profiling of LMAN2L-deficient cells shows reduced surface integrin alpha-6 (ITGA6), supporting LMAN2L's hypothesized role in glycoprotein trafficking. Corroborates the ER-resident localization and ER-export receptor model; provides the first candidate physiological client (ITGA6). Not in publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Identification of a putative lysosomal cobalamin exporter altered in the cblF defect of vitamin B12 metabolism.
review_notes: Founding cblF study; identified LMBRD1/LMBD1 as the lysosomal membrane protein whose loss causes lysosomal cobalamin accumulation. Establishes the core disease/localization link.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput NK-cell membrane proteome; source of the generic GO:0016020 membrane HDA. Background-only for LMBRD1 function.

title: Purification and interaction analyses of two human lysosomal vitamin B12 transporters: LMBD1 and ABCD4.
review_notes: SPR/biophysical study showing LMBD1 and ABCD4 (and MMACHC) interact with low-nanomolar affinity and proposing vectorial hand-off of lysosomal B12 to cytosolic MMACHC. Source of the LMBD1-ABCD4 and LMBD1-MMACHC IPIs.

title: Translocation of the ABC transporter ABCD4 from the endoplasmic reticulum to lysosomes requires the escort protein LMBD1.
review_notes: Key mechanistic paper: LMBD1 escorts ABCD4 from the ER to the lysosome; LMBRD1 knockout mislocalizes ABCD4. Establishes the protein-localization-to-lysosome core function.

title: Clinical or ATPase domain mutations in ABCD4 disrupt the interaction between the vitamin B(12)-trafficking proteins ABCD4 and LMBD1.
review_notes: Live-cell FRET confirmation of the selective ABCD4-LMBD1 interaction and that ABCD4 lysosomal targeting depends on LMBD1.

title: The lysosomal protein ABCD4 can transport vitamin B(12) across liposomal membranes in vitro.
review_notes: In vitro reconstitution showing ABCD4 alone transports cobalamin (ATP-dependent) and LMBD1 has no cobalamin transport or ATPase activity. Directly informs the over-annotation of transporter MF terms to LMBD1.

title: A novel kinase, AATYK induces and promotes neuronal differentiation in a human neuroblastoma (SH-SY5Y) cell line.
review_notes: Direct human cellular environment; construct species/isoform unresolved in the abstract, so do not describe it as unambiguous human-Q6ZMQ8 IDA.

title: Characterization of the apoptosis-associated tyrosine kinase (AATYK) expressed in the CNS.
review_notes: Direct mouse evidence underlying human IBA propagation, not human IDA. The reported neuronal phenotype and tyrosine-activity result are explicit in the cached abstract. Newer direct human evidence establishes Ser/Thr kinase activity but does not exclude weak or dual Tyr activity; with the older full text unavailable, the human IBA transfer remains unresolved.

title: Apoptosis-associated tyrosine kinase is a Cdk5 activator p35 binding protein.
review_notes: Human-sequence evidence with mixed rat-brain-extract and HEK293 assays. The native short hAATYKs-p35BP fragment lacks the kinase domain; the kinase-containing hAATYKs construct was engineered.

title: Apoptosis-associated tyrosine kinase scaffolding of protein phosphatase 1 and SPAK reveals a novel pathway for Na-K-2C1 cotransporter regulation.
review_notes: Mechanistic precedent for repeated human PP1 interactions, with the functional assay performed in Xenopus oocytes. The abstract does not identify the AATYK1 construct species, so this is not direct human pathway evidence and should not be described as a mouse construct from the cached record alone.

title: Palmitoylation-dependent endosomal localization of AATYK1A and its interaction with Src.
review_notes: Isoform-specific neuronal/heterologous localization evidence. The abstract does not establish direct topology or localization for human Q6ZMQ8, and the transmembrane-domain-free AATYK1A result must not be generalized to all human isoforms.

title: Phosphorylation of AATYK1 by Cdk5 suppresses its tyrosine phosphorylation.
review_notes: Strong rodent neuronal regulatory evidence. LMTK1 is the CDK5/p35 substrate; p35/CDK5R1 is the direct binding subunit, not CDK5 itself.

title: AATYK1A phosphorylation by Cdk5 regulates the recycling endosome pathway.
review_notes: Heterologous Chinese-hamster cell evidence; supports pathway order/localization, not a direct Rab11A interaction or human-neuron annotation.

title: Protein phosphatase 1α interacting proteins in the human brain.
review_notes: Supports human PP1α binding, but the abstract does not name AATK and does not establish a stable complex or downstream mechanism.

title: LMTK1/AATYK1 is a novel regulator of axonal outgrowth that acts via Rab11 in a Cdk5-dependent manner.
review_notes: Strong direct mouse ortholog evidence; any human annotation is orthology-supported, not IDA.

title: Apoptosis-associated tyrosine kinase 1 inhibits growth and migration and promotes apoptosis in melanoma.
review_notes: Direct human-cell evidence and independent corroboration of growth suppression. Historical AATKA/AATKB names must not be mapped naively to current UniProt isoform numbers.

title: LMTK1 regulates dendritic formation by regulating movement of Rab11A-positive endosomes.
review_notes: Strong direct mouse ortholog evidence; not human IDA.

title: Integrative analysis of kinase networks in TRAIL-induced apoptosis provides a source of potential targets for combination therapy.
review_notes: Pair-level provenance is in the data/GOA rather than the abstract; this is not direct evidence for an LMTK1 catalytic or TRAIL-pathway mechanism.

title: A Global Analysis of the Receptor Tyrosine Kinase-Protein Phosphatase Interactome.
review_notes: Independent human phosphatase-interaction evidence; no stable-complex or substrate inference.

title: The LMTK1-TBC1D9B-Rab11A Cascade Regulates Dendritic Spine Formation via Endosome Trafficking.
review_notes: Direct mouse ortholog evidence. The study does not identify TBC1D9B as a direct human LMTK1 phosphorylation substrate or establish a stable human complex.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Supports a binary screen contact only; no evidence for TEPSIN regulation, substrate status, or a stable complex.

title: Physical and functional interactome atlas of human receptor tyrosine kinases.
review_notes: The paper-level text does not identify which assay produced this specific pair; avoid stable- complex or enzyme-substrate claims.

title: Epigenetically silenced apoptosis-associated tyrosine kinase (AATK) facilitates a decreased expression of Cyclin D1 and WEE1, phosphorylates TP53 and reduces cell proliferation in a kinase-dependent manner.
review_notes: Strongest direct human catalytic evidence. Human coding sequence and human cell systems were used, but the construct is not mapped unambiguously to a current Q6ZMQ8 isoform number. The site-specific assay used separately immunoprecipitated kinase and substrate rather than purified recombinant components, so it supports direct TP53 Ser366 phosphorylation without defining full intrinsic substrate specificity.

title: UniProtKB record for human LMTK1 (Q6ZMQ8)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProt record for human Q6ZMQ8. It is authoritative for the displayed sequence, isoform definitions, curated provenance, and the predicted canonical transmembrane segment; its membrane topology is inference-based and must not be treated as direct human experimental evidence or generalized to every isoform.

title: PANTHER PTHR24417 serine/threonine-protein kinase LMTK family metadata
review_notes: The curated family name corroborates the LMTK serine/threonine classification. The generated family description is marked llm:true and checked:false and is not used as evidence.

title: A novel transmembrane Ser/Thr kinase complexes with protein phosphatase-1 and inhibitor-2.
review_notes: Foundational direct human biochemical evidence. The abstract does not identify the PP1C catalytic isoform, so the GOA/IntAct and UniProt records are needed to resolve P36873 specifically. Abstract only.

title: Identification of a novel, membrane-associated neuronal kinase, cyclin-dependent kinase 5/p35-regulated kinase.
review_notes: Direct support for the p35 interaction, Golgi localization, and CDK5/p35 regulation. Its dual-specificity description was predictive, not a substrate specificity result, and is superseded by direct serine/threonine assays.

title: Peptide microarray analysis of substrate specificity of the transmembrane Ser/Thr kinase KPI-2 reveals reactivity with cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator and phosphorylase.
review_notes: Strong recombinant biochemical specificity evidence. CFTR was an in-vitro substrate here; PMID:24727471 supplies human-airway cellular validation. Abstract only.

title: Azoospermia in mice with targeted disruption of the Brek/Lmtk2 (brain-enriched kinase/lemur tyrosine kinase 2) gene.
review_notes: Strong mouse physiological evidence but not direct human evidence. Suitable for conservative orthology transfer or a non-core contextual function.

title: Myosin VI and its interacting protein LMTK2 regulate tubule formation and transport to the endocytic recycling compartment.
review_notes: Direct human-cell trafficking and interaction evidence. The paper supports unconventional MYO6/myosin VI, Q9UM54. GOA's P13533 WITH/FROM is MYH6 and is a source-entity miscitation, not evidence against the GO term.

title: BREK/LMTK2 is a myosin VI-binding protein involved in endosomal membrane trafficking.
review_notes: Independent direct support for MYO6 binding and early-to-recycling-endosome traffic. It does not support early-endosome-to-late-endosome transport. GOA's P13533 entity is MYH6 rather than MYO6. Abstract only.

title: Lemur tyrosine kinase-2 signalling regulates kinesin-1 light chain-2 phosphorylation and binding of Smad2 cargo.
review_notes: Mechanistically important PP1/KLC2 pathway. Mutant/overexpression experiments use mouse LMTK2 in HeLa cells, while the siRNAs target endogenous human LMTK2; this species boundary is retained.

title: Cdk5/p35 phosphorylates lemur tyrosine kinase-2 to regulate protein phosphatase-1C phosphorylation and activity.
review_notes: Direct mechanistic bridge between p35/CDK5 regulation and PP1 inhibition. Abstract only.

title: Determination of the membrane topology of lemur tyrosine kinase 2 (LMTK2) by fluorescence protease protection.
review_notes: Direct fluorescence-protease-protection topology evidence. Strong support for integral endosome membrane localization and cytosolic orientation; older sequence predictions are not treated as the direct experiment.

title: Interaction proteome of human Hippo signaling: modular control of the co-activator YAP1.
review_notes: GOA/IntAct records LMTK2-PPP1CC, but neither partner is named in cached narrative. Resource-level support only.

title: LMTK2-mediated phosphorylation regulates CFTR endocytosis in human airway epithelial cells.
review_notes: Strong direct human cellular evidence for a specific cargo and tissue context. Appropriate for CFTR phosphorylation/endocytosis annotations, but not evidence that every LMTK2 trafficking role uses CFTR.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: GOA/IntAct records LMTK2-PPP1CC, but the specific pair is absent from cached narrative. Abstract only; do not infer mechanism or a stoichiometric complex.

title: Signal dependent ER export of lemur tyrosine kinase 2.
review_notes: Direct human-LMTK2 construct and endogenous-knockdown work in CHO/HeLa systems. Supports membrane trafficking and the requirement for correct ER export.

title: A Global Analysis of the Receptor Tyrosine Kinase-Protein Phosphatase Interactome.
review_notes: GOA/IntAct records LMTK2-PPP1CC. Use as interaction evidence only; PMID:12393858 and PMID:22220831 establish directionality and PP1 inhibition.

title: Systematic Analysis of Human Protein Phosphatase Interactions and Dynamics.
review_notes: GOA/IntAct records LMTK2-PPP1CC, but the pair is absent from cached narrative. Use direct LMTK2-PP1 work for mechanism. Abstract only.

title: LMTK2 binds to kinesin light chains to mediate anterograde axonal transport of cdk5/p35 and LMTK2 levels are reduced in Alzheimer's disease brains.
review_notes: Strong transport mechanism, but functional transport assays used mouse LMTK2 constructs and rat cortical neurons. Treat human transfer as orthology-supported; the human brain samples measured abundance, not transport.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: GOA/IntAct records LMTK2-PPP1CC, but the cached prose does not expose the pair. Resource-level interaction evidence only.

title: Physical and functional interactome atlas of human receptor tyrosine kinases.
review_notes: The study includes the LMR family and GOA/IntAct records LMTK2-PPP1CC, but cached paper prose does not identify which modality generated that pair. Do not infer a stable complex or enzyme-substrate relationship from this citation alone.

title: A revised nomenclature for the lemur family of protein kinases.
review_notes: Current expert nomenclature review and useful alias reconciliation. Use primary experiments for catalytic and mechanistic assertions.

title: LMTK2 switches on canonical TGF-β1 signaling in human bronchial epithelial cells.
review_notes: Direct human-cell evidence for positive regulation of canonical TGF-β signaling. Keep it as a bronchial-epithelial signaling context rather than the universal definition of LMTK2.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: GOA/IntAct records LMTK2-PPP1CC, but neither partner is named in cached narrative. Treat as resource provenance, not a mechanistic LMTK2 study.

title: Unconventional myosin-VI (Homo sapiens)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProtKB entry Q9UM54 is the correct human MYO6/unconventional myosin-VI partner established by PMID:18029400 and PMID:18429820. The GOA WITH/FROM identifier P13533 instead resolves to MYH6 (cardiac myosin heavy chain 6, whose UniProt recommended name is Myosin-6) and is a source-entity miscitation; neither cited paper supports LMTK2-MYH6 binding.

title: UniProtKB record for human LMTK2 (Q8IWU2)
review_notes: Reviewed human Q8IWU2 record, authoritative for displayed sequence and curated cross-references. Its sequence-similarity Tyr-kinase-family classification must not override direct serine/threonine biochemical evidence.

title: Kinome screening for regulators of the estrogen receptor identifies LMTK3 as a new therapeutic target in breast cancer.
review_notes: Foundational experimental study of human LMTK3 in ERalpha-positive breast-cancer systems. Only the abstract is cached. It supports direct in-vitro ESR1 phosphorylation, but neither the abstract nor the curated record identifies the LMTK3-dependent ESR1 phosphosite; do not present ESR1 Ser167 as a mapped direct LMTK3 site.

title: LMTK3 deficiency causes pronounced locomotor hyperactivity and impairs endocytic trafficking.
review_notes: Direct mouse knockout and primary-neuron evidence for a neuronal trafficking role. The PMC full text is cached; the findings remain ortholog evidence rather than a direct assay of human Q96Q04.

title: LMTK3 Represses Tumor Suppressor-like Genes through Chromatin Remodeling in Breast Cancer.
review_notes: Direct human breast-cancer-cell evidence for a context-specific LMTK3-KAP1-PP1alpha chromatin scaffold. Only the abstract is cached, but independent inspection of the primary full PDF verified that endogenous LMTK3 immunoprecipitation recovers PP1alpha in MCF7 cells, GST pull-down supports direct binding, and RVxF-motif substitutions weaken the interaction. The paper's old LMTK3 motif coordinates 1376-1382 map to residues 1347-1353 in current Q96Q04. KAP1 is the PP1-regulated partner, not an established direct phosphorylation substrate of LMTK3.

title: Phosphorylation of Rab-coupling protein by LMTK3 controls Rab14-dependent EphA2 trafficking to promote cell:cell repulsion.
review_notes: Strong human cancer-cell evidence using LMTK3-versus-LMTK1 siRNA, phosphosite detection, an RCP S435A mutant, trafficking assays, and functional rescue logic. The study does not show purified recombinant LMTK3 phosphorylating RCP, so Ser435 is a strong cellular LMTK3-dependent site but should not be described as biochemically purified-direct.

title: The lncRNA MIR2052HG regulates ERα levels and aromatase inhibitor resistance through LMTK3 by recruiting EGR1.
review_notes: Direct human ER-positive breast-cancer-cell evidence for upstream control of LMTK3 expression and downstream ERalpha regulation. The ERalpha Ser167 signal discussed in this paper is mediated through the downstream MEK-ERK-RSK1 axis and is not a mapped direct LMTK3 phosphorylation site.

title: Lmtk3-KO Mice Display a Range of Behavioral Abnormalities and Have an Impairment in GluA1 Trafficking.
review_notes: Direct mouse knockout evidence for neuronal AMPA-receptor trafficking and synaptic plasticity. Only the abstract is cached; it is ortholog evidence and does not establish the same role for human Q96Q04.

title: The structure-function relationship of oncogenic LMTK3.
review_notes: Strong direct structural and biochemical evidence for human LMTK3. The paper used the older 1489-aa NP_001073903.1 sequence with a 29-aa N-terminal extension absent from current Q96Q04/NP_001073903.2; its LMTK3 residue numbers therefore require a 29-residue offset before use with the current 1460-aa record. Substrate-site numbering is unaffected. CDC37 is directly phosphorylated in vitro but its site is unknown. Because C28 both inhibits the kinase and disrupts HSP90-CDC37-dependent LMTK3 stability, C28 phenotypes alone do not isolate catalytic inhibition.

title: The brain-specific kinase LMTK3 regulates neuronal excitability by decreasing KCC2-dependent neuronal Cl(-) extrusion.
review_notes: Strong mouse-brain and neuronal evidence for a context-specific LMTK3-PP1-KCC2 scaffold. The mechanistic physiology is based on mouse tissue, knockout mice, and neuronal preparations; conservation of this scaffold function in human neurons is unresolved and should not be presented as direct human evidence.

title: LMTK3 regulation of EV biogenesis and cargo sorting promotes tumour growth by reducing monocyte infiltration and driving pro-tumourigenic macrophage polarisation in breast cancer.
review_notes: Direct recombinant kinase evidence plus human T47D and MDA-MB-231 cellular evidence for RAB7A Ser72 phosphorylation, late-endosome localization, and MVB/EV remodeling. The paper distinguishes EV size, subpopulation, and cargo effects from particle concentration; it does not support a blanket claim that LMTK3 increases EV number.

title: UniProtKB record for human LMTK3 (Q96Q04)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProt record for current human Q96Q04. It is authoritative for the displayed 1460-aa sequence, predicted topology, and curated provenance. The record has no ALTERNATIVE PRODUCTS section and therefore no curated protein isoforms. Q5XJV6 is the mouse ortholog, and localization statements carrying that evidence tag are not direct human localization assays.

title: UniProtKB entry Q496Y0 (LONF3_HUMAN)

Isoform 3 changes residues 605-610 and lacks residues 611-759, truncating most of the Lon N-terminal domain while retaining both RING fingers. UniProt provides no direct LONRF3 activity, substrate, complex, or experimental localization evidence.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Correct mapping source for UniProt cell-surface/endosome vocabulary. Direct human trafficking papers provide stronger evidence for those locations.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Correct Ensembl-Compara transfer route, but most detailed nervous-system, developmental, synaptic, and cytoskeletal rows derive from mouse or rat Lpar1. Those phenotypes cannot be treated as direct human LPAR1 evidence.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: Correct ARBA provenance for broad lipid-binding and calcium-response predictions; direct ligand-binding and signaling studies are more informative.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Correct combined-IEA provenance. The resulting receptor, membrane, and signaling terms should be evaluated against the direct human papers, while neuronal-process transfers remain species-bounded.

title: Large-scale identification and characterization of human genes that activate NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways.
review_notes: The PMID and title are correct and GOA cites it for an LPAR1 NF-kappaB expression phenotype, but the abstract-only cache does not name LPAR1 or expose the gene-specific experiment. It cannot independently establish core LPAR1 signaling.

title: Complete sequencing and characterization of 21,243 full-length human cDNAs.
review_notes: Correct primary sequencing source cited by UniProt for the Q92633-2 N-terminal sequence change. The paper supplies transcript sequence, not evidence that the two LPAR1 isoforms differ in ligand binding, trafficking, coupling, or expression.

title: Dual regulation of lysophosphatidic acid (LPA1) receptor signalling by Ral and GRK.
review_notes: Direct human-cell mechanistic study supporting agonist-dependent RalA/PLC signaling, GRK2 desensitization, receptor trafficking, and RalA/GRK2 interactions. Cache is abstract-only, so claims are limited to the accessible text and UniProt summary.

title: Lysophosphatidic acid mediates migration of human mesenchymal stem cells stimulated by synovial fluid of patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
review_notes: Human endogenous loss-of-function/pharmacology evidence for LPA1-dependent calcium signaling and chemotaxis. Ki16425 also inhibits LPA3, but LPAR1 RNA silencing supplies receptor-specific support.

title: Molecular regulation of lysophosphatidic acid receptor 1 trafficking to the cell surface.
review_notes: Cached full text directly supports LPA1 biosynthetic maturation, N-glycosylation, COPII/Sar1-dependent export, ER retention of folding mutants, cell-surface location, and functional consequences of failed trafficking.

title: Crystal Structure of Antagonist Bound Human Lysophosphatidic Acid Receptor 1.
review_notes: Decisive human structural and antagonist-pharmacology source. The full text also contains functional calcium, cAMP, neurite-retraction, and stress-fiber assays, but speculative phosphorylated-endocannabinoid promiscuity is not treated as core.

title: Akt Regulates a Rab11-Effector Switch Required for Ciliogenesis.
review_notes: Mechanistic cellular evidence for an LPAR1-PI3K-Akt branch controlling ciliogenesis. The cache is abstract-only, so the exact experimental species/cell-context details should be checked before broad developmental generalization.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: Valid source for the quantitative PDZ-domain/PBM screen. LPAR1-specific partner identities were verified from the GOA/IntAct WITH/FROM records because the cached narrative does not enumerate the individual LPAR1 contacts. The screen does not make those contacts core receptor activities or establish their physiological co-occurrence.

title: LPA receptor 1 (LPAR1) is a novel interaction partner of Filamin A that promotes Filamin A phosphorylation, MRTF-A transcriptional activity and oncogene-induced senescence.
review_notes: Direct human HCC-cell and organoid evidence for a contextual LPAR1-FLNA-MRTF-A signaling branch. It supports the FLNA interaction and actin/SRF consequences, not a universal developmental function.

title: Multiplexed mapping of the interactome of GPCRs with receptor activity-modifying proteins.
review_notes: Valid systematic source for the multiplexed GPCR-RAMP screen. LPAR1-RAMP1/2/3 partner identities were verified from GOA/IntAct WITH/FROM records because the cached narrative does not name LPAR1. The paper does not establish an LPAR1-specific trafficking or pharmacological consequence, so these interactions remain non-core candidates.

title: Ventricular zone gene-1 (vzg-1) encodes a lysophosphatidic acid receptor expressed in neurogenic regions of the developing cerebral cortex.
review_notes: Founding functional Lpar1/Vzg-1 study, but the experiments and embryonic brain expression are mouse. It supports conserved receptor biochemistry and an orthologous developmental context, not direct human cortical-development claims.

title: Molecular cloning of the human Edg2 protein and its identification as a functional cellular receptor for lysophosphatidic acid.
review_notes: Decisive primary human receptor-identification paper: direct LPA binding, selective LPA-responsive signaling, sequence identity, and tissue-expression evidence.

title: Recombinant human G protein-coupled lysophosphatidic acid receptors mediate intracellular calcium mobilization.
review_notes: Direct recombinant-human comparison supporting LPAR1 coupling to Gi-sensitive PLC/IP3/calcium signaling. It also shows that compounds described as Xenopus LPA receptor antagonists acted as EDG2 agonists/partial agonists, a species/receptor pharmacology warning.

title: Liganded Gq/11-activating GPCRs act as GEFs for Gq/11
review_notes: Curated human pathway reaction containing LPAR1, but it is generic Gq/11 mechanism; primary LPAR1 papers should carry the mechanistic weight.

review_notes: Curated human Gi reaction containing LPAR1; useful pathway context but not independent evidence for receptor specificity.

title: LPA-binding receptors bind LPA

title: Liganded Gq-activating GPCRs bind inactive heterotrimeric Gq
review_notes: Generic curated Gq-binding event; direct human LPAR1 evidence is stronger for Gi-sensitive PLC/calcium signaling, while broader Gq coupling is supported at pathway/family level.

title: The Ligand:GPCR:Gq complex dissociates

title: The Ligand:GPCR:Gi complex dissociates

review_notes: Current reviewed Q92633 record inspected directly. It integrates the human ligand, signaling, trafficking, tissue, and structural studies and records Q92633-1 and Q92633-2. No isoform-specific functional comparison is supplied, so the isoform field should not be interpreted as evidence of distinct receptor biology.

title: Lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) receptors of the EDG family are differentially activated by LPA species. Structure-activity relationship of cloned LPA receptors.

title: TRIP6 enhances lysophosphatidic acid-induced cell migration by interacting with the lysophosphatidic acid 2 receptor.
review_notes: Direct LPAR2 interaction and perturbation study; the migration consequence is demonstrated in SKOV3 ovarian cancer cells and should remain context-bounded.

title: NHERF2 specifically interacts with LPA2 receptor and defines the specificity and efficiency of receptor-mediated phospholipase C-beta3 activation.
review_notes: Decisive direct mechanistic source for the LPAR2 PDZ motif, NHERF2 specificity, and PLCB3 signaling complex; cached accessible content is abstract-level.

title: Lysophosphatidic acid inhibits cholera toxin-induced secretory diarrhea through CFTR-dependent protein interactions.
review_notes: Direct human epithelial localization, complex-assembly, and Gi-functional evidence, complemented by mouse knockout physiology; species and epithelial-context boundaries remain explicit.

title: MAGI-3 regulates LPA-induced activation of Erk and RhoA.
review_notes: Direct interaction, motif-mutagenesis, and signaling-perturbation evidence; downstream results are bounded to the SW480 colon cancer model.

title: Dual regulation of lysophosphatidic acid (LPA1) receptor signalling by Ral and GRK.
review_notes: Despite the LPA1-focused title, the abstract directly assays LPAR2 association and desensitization. RalA activation and Ral-dependent PLC activity are LPAR1-specific and must not be transferred to LPAR2.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: The LPAR2-LGALS3 candidate association is carried by the GOA/IntAct record; the cached narrative establishes the BioPlex screening context but does not enumerate LPAR2 or establish a receptor-signaling consequence.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: The LPAR2-LGALS3 candidate association is carried by the GOA/IntAct record. The paper is useful for cell-context caution, but its cached narrative does not establish this pair as a functional LPAR2 complex.

title: Multiplexed mapping of the interactome of GPCRs with receptor activity-modifying proteins.
review_notes: Direct systematic evidence for LPAR2-RAMP1/2/3 complex formation under ectopic coexpression; no LPAR2-specific trafficking, pharmacology, or native-tissue consequence was established.

title: Characterization of a novel subtype of human G protein-coupled receptor for lysophosphatidic acid.
review_notes: Founding direct human receptor characterization. The two transcript sizes are expression observations, not evidence for functionally distinct protein isoforms.

title: Identification of an EDG7 variant, HOFNH30, a G-protein-coupled receptor for lysophosphatidic acid.

title: Activity of 2-substituted lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) analogs at LPA receptors: discovery of a LPA1/LPA3 receptor antagonist.
