title: LPA3-mediated lysophosphatidic acid signalling in embryo implantation and spacing.
review_notes: Decisive in vivo mouse knockout evidence for Lpar3-dependent implantation timing and embryo spacing, with a COX2-prostaglandin link. It supports ortholog physiology and pathway context, not direct proof of the same role in humans.

title: Phosphorylation and Internalization of Lysophosphatidic Acid Receptors LPA1, LPA2, and LPA3.
review_notes: Direct comparative signaling, phosphorylation, desensitization, and internalization study in transfected C9 rat hepatocyte cells; it establishes receptor regulation but not native human-tissue behavior.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Valid high-throughput binary-interaction map underlying many IntAct partner rows. The paper does not narratively validate LPAR3 partners or receptor-signaling consequences, so curator provenance should be preserved while mechanistic interpretation remains cautious.

title: The LPA(3) Receptor: Regulation and Activation of Signaling Pathways.
review_notes: Useful receptor-focused synthesis and gap source, but mechanistic claims are secondary and newer primary phosphorylation/internalization studies supersede its 2021 trafficking uncertainty.

title: LPA(3) Receptor Phosphorylation Sites: Roles in Signaling and Internalization.
review_notes: Direct mutational evidence linking mapped phosphorylation regions to β-arrestin recruitment and internalization in T-REx HEK293 cells; phenotypic effects remain heterologous-cell-context evidence.

title: Lysophosphatidic Acid Receptor 3 (LPA3): Signaling and Phosphorylation Sites.
review_notes: Direct signaling, phosphorylation-site, β-arrestin, and trafficking study using T-REx HEK293 expression; strong mechanism evidence with an explicit heterologous-system boundary.

review_notes: Curated human pathway event supporting the generic Gq/11 nucleotide-exchange step; it is pathway-model provenance rather than an LPAR3-specific experiment.

title: Identification of p2y9/GPR23 as a novel G protein-coupled receptor for lysophosphatidic acid, structurally distant from the Edg family.
review_notes: Decisive primary human receptor study with direct ligand binding, ligand rank order, calcium and adenylyl-cyclase outputs, and tissue-expression context; signaling was measured in heterologous rodent cells.

title: LPA(4)/GPR23 is a lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) receptor utilizing G(s)-, G(q)/G(i)-mediated calcium signaling and G(12/13)-mediated Rho activation.
review_notes: Primary mechanistic LPAR4 study using tagged receptor, pharmacological perturbation, and G-protein mini-genes. It directly informs Gs, Gq/pertussis-toxin-sensitive calcium, G12/13-Rho, and internalization capability, but the abstract does not establish endogenous native-human coupling weights.

title: LPA4/p2y9/GPR23 mediates rho-dependent morphological changes in a rat neuronal cell line.
review_notes: Direct mechanistic LPAR4 signaling study in a rat neuroblastoma transfection system; valuable for coupling and Rho biology but not proof of native human neuronal function.

title: Role of LPA4/p2y9/GPR23 in negative regulation of cell motility.
review_notes: Primary genetic and cell-biological evidence for negative regulation of motility; combines mouse knockout/MEF data with ectopic human cancer-cell assays, so neither context should be generalized to all native human tissues.

title: Strategy for the identification of GPR23/LPA4 receptor agonists and inverse agonists.
review_notes: Primary human-receptor pharmacology in engineered CHO cells; supports constitutive activity and ligand-tool development, not endogenous physiological responses.

title: Autotaxin promotes cancer invasion via the lysophosphatidic acid receptor 4: participation of the cyclic AMP/EPAC/Rac1 signaling pathway in invadopodia formation.
review_notes: Primary disease-model evidence for an LPAR4-cAMP-EPAC-Rac1 invasion pathway. The abstract does not establish a normal-tissue role or identify the fibrosarcoma cells as a native human LPAR4 context, so the finding is kept explicitly model-bounded.

title: Development of a GPR23 cell-based β-lactamase reporter assay.
review_notes: Methods-focused primary pharmacology paper establishing assay-detectable constitutive activity and inverse agonists in an engineered system.

title: Lysophosphatidic Acid Receptor 4 Is Transiently Expressed during Cardiac Differentiation and Critical for Repair of the Damaged Heart.
review_notes: Mixed human/mouse PSC differentiation and mouse injury study; informs developmental context and an LPAR4-responsive progenitor state but not the receptor's universal core function or native adult-human cardiac mechanism.

title: Multiplexed mapping of the interactome of GPCRs with receptor activity-modifying proteins.
review_notes: IntAct/GOA reports LPAR4 partner rows for RAMP1, RAMP2, and RAMP3 from this multiplexed screen. The paper supports screen-level complex detection in engineered cells, not an endogenous LPAR4 complex or a demonstrated RAMP effect on LPAR4 trafficking or pharmacology.

title: Cloning and chromosomal mapping of four putative novel human G-protein-coupled receptor genes.
review_notes: Primary human cloning and mapping paper for GPR23 identity; it predates LPA deorphanization and does not establish receptor function.

review_notes: Primary human cloning and negative ligand-screen evidence; important for the historical P2Y9 nomenclature boundary but superseded functionally by LPA deorphanization.

review_notes: Curated human Gq/11 pathway context consistent with LPAR4 calcium signaling; the cached summary is generic rather than direct LPAR4 experimental evidence.

title: Lysophosphatidic acid binds to and activates GPR92, a G protein-coupled receptor highly expressed in gastrointestinal lymphocytes.

title: GPR92 as a new G12/13- and Gq-coupled lysophosphatidic acid receptor that increases cAMP, LPA5.
review_notes: Independent primary LPAR5 identification and coupling study using heterologous tagged-receptor systems; establishes receptor capability, not fixed native-human coupling weights.

title: Identification of farnesyl pyrophosphate and N-arachidonylglycine as endogenous ligands for GPR92.
review_notes: Primary alternative-ligand and mutagenesis study. It supports receptor activation by FPP and NAG in assay systems, but does not establish their dominant endogenous ligand status across human tissues.

title: Unique ligand selectivity of the GPR92/LPA5 lysophosphatidate receptor indicates role in human platelet activation.
review_notes: Primary ligand-recognition, pharmacology, and human platelet study; antagonist effects support an LPAR5 contribution but are less definitive than receptor-selective genetic perturbation.

title: GPR92/LPA₅ lysophosphatidate receptor mediates megakaryocytic cell shape change induced by human atherosclerotic plaques.
review_notes: Full-text primary human megakaryocytic-cell and plaque study with receptor-selective knockdown; supports a platelet-lineage context but does not directly manipulate LPAR5 in anucleate platelets.

title: Targeted deletion of LPA5 identifies novel roles for lysophosphatidic acid signaling in development of neuropathic pain.
review_notes: Primary mouse knockout evidence for neuropathic-pain development and the key source underlying pain-related transfer; it is not direct evidence for a constitutive human pain role.

title: Down-regulation of LPA receptor 5 contributes to aberrant LPA signalling in EBV-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
review_notes: Primary human disease-tissue and cell-line evidence for context-dependent suppression of migration by LPAR5; it should not be generalized as a universal normal-tissue motility function.

title: Structural basis for lysophosphatidic acid recognition and atypical Gα(q) coupling by LPAR5.
review_notes: Decisive primary structural and mutational evidence for human LPAR5 recognition of 1-oleoyl-LPA and direct Gq coupling; the deposited full text was not yet accessible through project tooling, so findings are abstract-bounded.

title: Liganded Gq/11-activating GPCRs act as GEFs for Gq/11
review_notes: Generic curated human Gq/11 pathway context consistent with direct LPAR5 coupling studies; it is not receptor-specific experimental evidence.

review_notes: Generic Gi-cycle provenance attached to an LPAR5 pathway model. The audited direct LPAR5 studies establish Gq, G12/13, and Gs outputs but do not provide equally decisive Gi coupling evidence, so this entry should not be treated as direct support for LPAR5-Gi coupling.

review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. This independently establishes the human woolly-hair genetics and follicular expression context; it does not itself identify the ligand or signaling pathway.

title: Identification and characterization of a novel lysophosphatidic acid receptor, p2y5/LPA6.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. This is a decisive primary receptor-deorphanization and signaling study; most mechanistic assays used human LPAR6 expressed in rat receptor-null cell lines, while the contraction/knockdown experiment used human endothelial cells.

title: P2Y5 is a G(alpha)i, G(alpha)12/13 G protein-coupled receptor activated by lysophosphatidic acid that reduces intestinal cell adhesion.

title: Cell-trafficking impairment in disease-associated LPA6 missense mutants and a potential pharmacoperone therapy for autosomal recessive woolly hair/hypotrichosis.

title: Molecular mechanism of ligand recognition and activation of lysophosphatidic acid receptor LPAR6.
review_notes: PubMed identity and full text were verified. This is the strongest current structural evidence for human LPAR6 ligand recognition and G-protein coupling; engineered receptor constructs, mini-G proteins, insect-cell expression, and 1-acyl-LPA used for purification define the experimental context.

title: Liganded Gq/11-activating GPCRs act as GEFs for Gq/11

title: P2Y5 receptor can bind to LPA
review_notes: The cached human Reactome reaction was verified as database participant provenance. title: MAGT1 transports Mg2+ from extracellular region to cytosol
review_notes: Reactome reaction encoding the historical direct Mg2+-transporter model; the direct transporter activity is contested. Title left exactly as fetched.

title: Identification, expression, and characterization of a cDNA encoding human endoplasmic reticulum mannosidase I, the enzyme that catalyzes the first mannose trimming step in mammalian Asn-linked oligosaccharide biosynthesis.
review_notes: Foundational characterization of human ERManI; supports the mannosidase activity, ER localization, and calcium dependence.

title: Cloning and expression of a specific human alpha 1,2-mannosidase that trims Man9GlcNAc2 to Man8GlcNAc2 isomer B during N-glycan biosynthesis.
review_notes: Defines the specific product (Man8B) and the calcium/inhibitor profile of MAN1B1.

title: The specificity of the yeast and human class I ER alpha 1,2-mannosidases involved in ER quality control is not as strict previously reported.
review_notes: Establishes the broader (concentration-dependent) trimming specificity underlying the mannose timer.

title: Mechanism of class 1 (glycosylhydrolase family 47) alpha-mannosidases involved in N-glycan processing and endoplasmic reticulum quality control.
review_notes: Mechanistic/structural basis of the GH47 mannosidase catalysis.

title: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) mannosidase I is compartmentalized and required for N-glycan trimming to Man5-6GlcNAc2 in glycoprotein ER-associated degradation.
review_notes: Key in vivo evidence for ERQC localization and the ERAD/mannose-trimming requirement.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane proteome; source of the generic membrane HDA annotation, peripheral to function.

title: Mannose trimming is required for delivery of a glycoprotein from EDEM1 to XTP3-B and to late endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation steps.
review_notes: Links ERManI trimming to specific downstream ERAD machinery.

title: In vitro mannose trimming property of human ER alpha-1,2 mannosidase I.
review_notes: Demonstrates extended trimming and misfolding selectivity in vitro.

title: Proteomic analysis of cerebrospinal fluid extracellular vesicles: a comprehensive dataset.
review_notes: High-throughput CSF extracellular vesicle proteomics; source of the extracellular vesicle HDA annotation, peripheral to function.

title: Mammalian ER mannosidase I resides in quality control vesicles, where it encounters its glycoprotein substrates.
review_notes: Supports cytoplasmic vesicle (QCV) localization and argues the Golgi localization is artifactual.

title: The cytoplasmic tail of human mannosidase Man1b1 contributes to catalysis-independent quality control of misfolded alpha1-antitrypsin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:32958677, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1919013117). Establishes a second, catalysis-independent quality-control function of MAN1B1 mediated by its N-terminal cytoplasmic tail, distinct from the luminal mannose-trimming activity. Not cached; supporting_text not added to supported_by. Identified via Falcon deep research.

title: Microtubule-associated protein 1S, a short and ubiquitously expressed member of the microtubule-associated protein 1 family.
review_notes: Original MAP1S characterization (also indexed under the C19ORF5/MAP8 names). Source of the core microtubule/tubulin binding and bundle-formation annotations.

title: Depletion of the Ras association domain family 1, isoform A-associated novel microtubule-associated protein, C19ORF5/MAP1S, causes mitotic abnormalities.
review_notes: Source of the centrosome/MTOC localization and mitotic-role annotations (spindle organization, MTOC anchoring, metaphase chromosome alignment).

title: Microtubule-associated protein 1S (MAP1S) bridges autophagic components with microtubules and mitochondria to affect autophagosomal biogenesis and degradation.
review_notes: Full text available in cache. Defines MAP1S's distinctive core function bridging the autophagy machinery (LC3/Atg8, LRPPRC) to microtubules and mitochondria; basis of the autophagy (GO:0006914) annotation.

title: Effect of C-terminal truncations on MLK7 catalytic activity and JNK activation.
review_notes: Anchored to GOA: this PMID supports IDA annotations to GO:0004706 (JUN kinase kinase kinase activity) and GO:0004709 (MAP kinase kinase kinase activity), establishing MAP3K20/ZAK as a MAP3K driving the JNK cascade. Not cached; verification via GOA evidence codes for the core MF.

title: ZAKα Recognizes Stalled Ribosomes through Partially Redundant Sensor Domains.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title exactly; establishes ZAKalpha as the proximal sensor of stalled/colliding ribosomes. GOA IDA from this PMID supports GO:0004709 (MAP3K activity) and GO:0043022 (ribosome binding), the core sensor function.

title: Ribosome Collisions Trigger General Stress Responses to Regulate Cell Fate.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title exactly; shows ZAKalpha senses ribosome collisions and bifurcates the stress response (p38/JNK death vs GCN2 survival). Supports the ribotoxic-stress core function.

title: Crystal structures of ASK1-inhibtor complexes provide a platform for structure-based drug design.
review_notes: Crystal structures of the human ASK1 (MAP3K5) kinase domain (PDB 4BF2, 4BHN, 4BIB-4BIE) with ATP-competitive inhibitors bound in the ATP pocket, resolving the serine/threonine kinase active site.

title: Specificity of linear motifs that bind to a common mitogen-activated protein kinase docking groove.
review_notes: Comparative crystallographic study (ERK2 structures PDB 2Y9Q/3TEI/4FMQ with bound D-motif peptides) defining the structural basis of MAPK docking-groove specificity for short linear D-motifs.

title: Interaction of tau with the neural membrane cortex is regulated by phosphorylation at sites that are modified in paired helical filaments.
review_notes: Primary study supporting axonal tau association with the neural membrane cortex and phosphorylation-sensitive membrane association.

title: Surface-decoration of microtubules by human tau.
review_notes: Primary structural/microtubule study supporting tau microtubule surface binding and microtubule stabilization.

title: Dendritic function of tau mediates amyloid-beta toxicity in Alzheimer's disease mouse models.
review_notes: Primary AD mouse-model paper supporting tau-dependent dendritic/Fyn/synaptic and memory phenotypes, kept as non-core downstream disease context.

title: Tau promotes neurodegeneration via DRP1 mislocalization in vivo.
review_notes: Full-text primary tauopathy model paper supporting actin-mediated mitochondrial dynamics phenotypes, kept as non-core downstream toxicity context.

title: Multiple isoforms of human microtubule-associated protein tau: sequences and localization in neurofibrillary tangles of Alzheimer's disease.
review_notes: Primary human tau isoform paper supporting incorporation of multiple tau isoforms into Alzheimer neurofibrillary tangles.

title: The Role of MAPT in Neurodegenerative Diseases: Genetics, Mechanisms and Therapy.
review_notes: Review supporting MAPT roles in neurodegenerative disease, microtubules, axonal transport, and neurofibrillary tangles.

title: Roles of tau protein in health and disease.
review_notes: Full-text review supporting broad tau health/disease biology; useful for secondary pathway context but not sufficient to make all broad review-derived terms core.

title: A Translocation Pathway for Vesicle-Mediated Unconventional Protein Secretion.
review_notes: Primary unconventional secretion paper supporting extracellular/secreted tau context through leaderless cargo secretion, not the core tau function.

title: Microtubule-associated protein/microtubule affinity-regulating kinase (p110mark). A novel protein kinase that regulates tau-microtubule interactions and dynamic instability by phosphorylation at the Alzheimer-specific site serine 262.
review_notes: Primary study supporting phosphorylation-dependent reduction of tau microtubule binding and microtubule dynamic instability.

title: Manual MAPT review notes
review_notes: Manual notes document the deep-research timeout and summarize the cached UniProt, PANTHER, GOA, and publication evidence used for this review.

title: UniProt text export for MAPT (P10636)
review_notes: Local UniProt record directly summarizes tau microtubule assembly/stability, neuronal polarity, axonal microtubule binding, membrane-component binding, subcellular localization, and tubulin-repeat domain biology.

title: Methionine adenosyltransferase I/III deficiency: novel mutations and clinical variations.
review_notes: Primary paper for MAT1A catalytic activity (IDA), SAM biosynthesis / methionine catabolism (IMP), and the MATD disease phenotype; full text available.

title: Insight into S-adenosylmethionine biosynthesis from the crystal structures of the human methionine adenosyltransferase catalytic and regulatory subunits.
review_notes: Crystal structure of human MAT1A bound to SAM (PDB 2OBV); establishes homotetramer/ dimer architecture and the two-step catalytic mechanism.

title: Structure and function study of the complex that synthesizes S-adenosylmethionine.
review_notes: Focuses on the MATalpha2beta complex but characterizes MAT catalytic function and shows a MAT1A (alpha1)-containing complex is stable in vitro; ComplexPortal used it for the MAT complex / SAM-biosynthesis annotations.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome screen; source of a MAT1A self (identical protein binding) interaction consistent with homo-oligomerization.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 AP-MS screen; source of a generic protein-binding IPI (MAT1A-MAT2A); uninformative for MAT1A molecular function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary (Y2H) interactome; source of both a generic protein-binding IPI and a self (identical protein binding) IPI.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegeneration interactome screen; source of generic protein-binding IPIs (MAT1A-APP, MAT1A-HTT); abstract-only cache; uninformative for MAT1A function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 AP-MS screen; source of a generic protein-binding IPI (MAT1A-MAT2A).

title: Formaldehyde regulates S-adenosylmethionine biosynthesis and one-carbon metabolism.
review_notes: Identifies MAT1A as the terminal enzyme in SAM biosynthesis and its isoform-specific Cys120 as a formaldehyde-reactive regulatory site; used by ComplexPortal for MAT complex membership.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Systems-scale multimodal cell-map study; source of a generic protein-binding IPI (MAT1A-MAT2A).

title: UniProtKB Q00266 (METK1_HUMAN) S-adenosylmethionine synthase isoform type-1
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; catalytic activity, cofactors, subunit structure, tissue specificity, disease, and PTMs used to ground the review.

title: Interaction properties of human mannan-binding lectin (MBL)-associated serine proteases-1 and -2, MBL-associated protein 19, and MBL.
review_notes: Characterizes the MBL-MASP1/MASP2/MAp19 interactions that constitute the lectin-protease initiating complex. Supports MBL as a scaffold for the MASP proteases (basis of the GO:0005515 IPI), but protein binding is uninformative as an MF.

title: MASP-3 and its association with distinct complexes of the mannan-binding lectin complement activation pathway.
review_notes: Documents MASP-3 association with MBL complexes; supports MBL-MASP complex membership rather than an informative independent MF.

title: Endothelial oxidative stress activates the lectin complement pathway: role of cytokeratin 1.
review_notes: Shows oxidative-stress-induced cytokeratin-1 on endothelium binds MBL and activates the lectin pathway (altered-self recognition). The response-to-oxidative-stress link is indirect and context-specific; not a core MBL function.

title: Characterization of the interaction between L-ficolin/p35 and mannan-binding lectin-associated serine proteases-1 and -2.
review_notes: Primarily about L-ficolin-MASP interactions; informs the shared MASP system and grounds a calcium-dependent protein binding IPI for the MBL/ficolin-MASP complex.

title: High frequencies in African and non-African populations of independent mutations in the mannose binding protein gene.
review_notes: Population genetics of MBL2 structural variants (codon 54/57) causing MBL deficiency. Background for the secreted-protein/disease context; used here only for an extracellular-region location annotation.

title: The X-ray structure of human mannan-binding lectin-associated protein 19 (MAp19) and its interaction site with mannan-binding lectin and L-ficolin.
review_notes: Structure of MAp19 and its MBL/ficolin interaction site; supports the MBL-MASP/MAp complex assembly (basis of an IPI protein-binding annotation).

title: Mannose-binding lectin-deficient mice are susceptible to infection with Staphylococcus aureus.
review_notes: In vivo MBL-null mouse (Mbl1/Mbl2 double KO) shows 100% mortality after i.v. S. aureus vs 45% in WT; full text frames MBL as a prototypic pattern-recognition molecule and opsonin. Strong functional support for innate defense / lectin pathway via the rodent orthologs (cross-species transfer to human MBL2).

title: The chaperone and potential mannan-binding lectin (MBL) co-receptor calreticulin interacts with MBL through the binding site for MBL-associated serine proteases.
review_notes: Calreticulin interacts with MBL via the MASP-binding site (possible co-receptor). A specific partner interaction; protein binding remains uninformative as MF.

title: Crystal structure of the CUB1-EGF-CUB2 domain of human MASP-1/3 and identification of its interaction sites with mannan-binding lectin and ficolins.
review_notes: Structural mapping of the MASP-1/3 sites that bind MBL/ficolins; supports the calcium-dependent MBL-MASP interaction underlying complex assembly.

title: MBL-associated serine protease-3 circulates in high serum concentrations predominantly in complex with Ficolin-3 and regulates Ficolin-3 mediated complement activation.
review_notes: Mainly about MASP-3/Ficolin-3; touches the shared MASP system. Weak direct support for MBL function.

title: Collectin 11 (CL-11, CL-K1) is a MASP-1/3-associated plasma collectin with microbial-binding activity.
review_notes: About collectin-11; a comparator collectin in the MASP system. Background only.

title: Serum concentration and interaction properties of MBL/ficolin associated protein-1.
review_notes: MAP-1/MAp44 interaction properties within MBL/ficolin complexes; supports complex membership, uninformative as MF.

title: CD91 interacts with mannan-binding lectin (MBL) through the MBL-associated serine protease-binding site.
review_notes: CD91/LRP1 binds MBL via the MASP-binding site (possible clearance receptor). Specific interaction; not a core MF.

title: Heterocomplexes of mannose-binding lectin and the pentraxins PTX3 or serum amyloid P component trigger cross-activation of the complement system.
review_notes: MBL-pentraxin heterocomplexes cross-activate complement; supports MBL self/identical-protein and pentraxin interactions modulating the lectin pathway.

title: Specific interaction of hepatitis C virus glycoproteins with mannan binding lectin inhibits virus entry.
review_notes: MBL binds HCV glycoproteins and inhibits entry; an example of antiviral carbohydrate recognition. Supports the lectin/antiviral role rather than generic binding.

title: Serglycin inhibits the classical and lectin pathways of complement via its glycosaminoglycan chains: implications for multiple myeloma.
review_notes: Serglycin GAGs inhibit the lectin pathway; MBL is a target. Regulatory context.

title: Mannan-binding lectin directly interacts with Toll-like receptor 4 and suppresses lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammatory cytokine secretion from THP-1 cells.
review_notes: MBL binds the TLR4 ectodomain and dampens LPS-induced TNF-alpha/IL-12 and NF-kB in THP-1 cells - an immunomodulatory interaction. Supports a regulatory partner interaction; protein binding still uninformative as MF.

title: MASP interactions with plasma-derived MBL.
review_notes: Quantitative MASP-MBL interaction study; supports MBL-MASP complex assembly.

title: Revised mechanism of complement lectin-pathway activation revealing the role of serine protease MASP-1 as the exclusive activator of MASP-2.
review_notes: Establishes that in normal human serum MASP-1 is the exclusive activator of MASP-2 within the MBL/ficolin-MASP complex, and MASP-1 generates ~60% of C2a. Strong mechanistic support for the lectin-pathway-initiation core process and the proteolysis that MBL nucleates (MBL itself is not the protease).

title: The salivary scavenger and agglutinin binds MBL and regulates the lectin pathway of complement in solution and on surfaces.
review_notes: DMBT1/SALSA binds MBL and regulates the lectin pathway; a specific regulatory interaction.

title: Crystal structure and functional characterization of the complement regulator mannose-binding lectin (MBL)/ficolin-associated protein-1 (MAP-1).
review_notes: Structure of MAP-1, a competitive regulator of the MBL/ficolin-MASP complex; supports complex membership/regulation.

title: Mannan-binding lectin-associated serine protease (MASP)-1 is crucial for lectin pathway activation in human serum, whereas neither MASP-1 nor MASP-3 is required for alternative pathway function.
review_notes: Patient-based functional study; MASP-1 is crucial for lectin-pathway activation and co-complexes with MASP-2 on MBL. Strong support for the MBL-MASP initiating complex and lectin-pathway / PRR-signaling annotations.

title: Deciphering complement receptor type 1 interactions with recognition proteins of the lectin complement pathway.
review_notes: Maps MBL (and C1q/ficolin) interactions with CR1; supports a specific receptor interaction, not an informative independent MF.

title: Serum amyloid P is a sialylated glycoprotein inhibitor of influenza A viruses.
review_notes: Paper primary subject is serum amyloid P (SAP), but the full text genuinely discusses MBL as a beta-type C-type-lectin inhibitor of influenza A and uses purified human MBL as a comparator/reagent. The paper therefore does support the MBL annotations grounded on it (mannose binding, antiviral/negative regulation of viral process, extracellular location, innate immune response), albeit weakly/comparatively - so it is correctly cited (not MISCITED), with LOW relevance. The antiviral role itself is real and better supported elsewhere (PMID:21203938, PMID:35102342).

title: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) binding protein opsonizes LPS-bearing particles for recognition by a novel receptor on macrophages.
review_notes: This paper is about lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LBP), an acute-phase opsonin - NOT MBL2, and it does not assay MBL. The functions it is used to ground for MBL2 (opsonization, acute-phase response, defense response to bacterium, cell surface) are independently true of MBL but are correctly supported by other references; the D-mannose binding TAS attributed to this paper is not supported by it at all. Treat as a likely wrong-paper / over-broad TAS citation.

title: Structural insights into the initiating complex of the lectin pathway of complement activation.
review_notes: Architecture of the ~450 kDa MBL/MASP-1 initiating complex by SAXS/EM; strong support for MBL membership in the serine-type endopeptidase (MBL-MASP) complex and for the intercomplex activation model.

title: Association of low levels of mannan-binding protein with a common defect of opsonisation.
review_notes: Classic study linking low serum MBP (a Ca2+-dependent serum lectin) to a common opsonic defect that purified MBP corrects dose-dependently. Supports MBL as a Ca2+-dependent lectin acting at the pathogen surface and in opsonization/innate defense.

title: Oligomerization of Mannan-binding Lectin Dictates Binding Properties and Complement Activation.
review_notes: Higher oligomers (tetramers) of the MBL homotrimer bind microbes and MASPs more strongly and activate complement better than trimers/dimers - establishing oligomerization as central to MBL function. Supports identical-protein (self) association and the complement-activation role.

title: C1q and Mannose-Binding Lectin Interact with CR1 in the Same Region on CCP24-25 Modules.
review_notes: Localizes the MBL (and C1q) binding site on CR1 to CCP24-25; supports a specific receptor interaction.

title: C1q/TNF-Related Protein 6 Is a Pattern Recognition Molecule That Recruits Collectin-11 from the Complement System to Ligands.
review_notes: Primarily about CTRP6/collectin-11; MBL appears as part of the broader collectin system. Background relevance.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome (HuRI). Generic, low-specificity source of the GO:0005515 protein-binding IPI; not informative about MBL molecular function.

title: Complement Activation and Thrombin Generation by MBL Bound to β2-Glycoprotein I.
review_notes: MBL binds beta2-glycoprotein I and can trigger complement/thrombin generation; a specific ligand interaction linking MBL to coagulation crosstalk.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput AP-MS interactome (BioPlex). Generic source of the protein-binding IPI; not informative about MBL molecular function.

title: Recognition and inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 by humoral innate immunity pattern recognition molecules.
review_notes: MBL binds SARS-CoV-2 trimeric spike (including VoC) in a glycan- and calcium-dependent manner, activates the lectin pathway after binding, and inhibits the virus in vitro; MBL2 polymorphisms associate with COVID-19 severity. Strong support for calcium-dependent carbohydrate/glycoprotein recognition, PRR activity, antiviral innate immunity and lectin-pathway activation.

title: Isolation and characterization of a mannan-binding protein from human serum.
review_notes: Original isolation of human serum MBP; defines it as a Ca2+-dependent serum lectin specific for mannose and N-acetylglucosamine with high-affinity, saturable, reversible mannan binding (Kd ~2.3e-9 M). Foundational support for the core D-mannose/carbohydrate binding MF.

title: Structure and function of mannan-binding proteins isolated from human liver and serum.
review_notes: Purifies liver and serum MBP; shows both are liver-synthesized, secreted, differ in oligomer number (L-MBP ~9, S-MBP ~18 subunits), and that complement activation requires higher oligomerization and the collagen-like-domain N-terminus. Supports secreted location and oligomer-dependent complement activation.

title: Binding of mannan-binding protein to various bacterial pathogens of meningitis.
review_notes: MBP (a Ca2+-dependent plasma lectin) binds bacterial surfaces; binding inhibited by mannose and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine. Supports Ca2+-dependent carbohydrate recognition at the microbial cell surface and defense against bacteria.

title: A second serine protease associated with mannan-binding lectin that activates complement.
review_notes: Identifies MASP-2 and establishes that MBL binds microbial carbohydrates and activates complement through associated serine proteases (analogous to C1r/C1s), with MBL structurally related to C1q. Foundational support for PRR activity and lectin-pathway initiation.

title: MBL binds to repetitive carbohydrate structures on the surfaces of viruses, bacteria, fungi, and protozoa
review_notes: Reactome reaction capturing the core MBL recognition event - binding repetitive microbial surface carbohydrate. Supports the carbohydrate-binding MF and extracellular location.

title: MBL2 binds SARS-CoV-2 S
review_notes: Reactome reaction for MBL2 binding SARS-CoV-2 spike; consistent with PMID:35102342.

title: FutureHouse Falcon deep-research report for MBL2 (P11226)
review_notes: AI deep-research synthesis used as a starting point. Its core conclusions (Ca2+-dependent carbohydrate binding, lectin-pathway complement activation, innate defense/opsonization as core; cytoplasm/cytosol/nucleus/synapse/apoptosis-execution/pyroptosis/neuronal roles as high-risk and unsupported) agree with the primary literature reviewed here, and all its cited sources resolve to real published papers (no preprint-only/unresolvable PMIDs). Used to corroborate, not as primary evidence.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for MBL2 GO:0043129
review_notes: Focused OpenScientist report supports removing GO:0043129 as collectin-family surfactant-homeostasis over-propagation from pulmonary surfactant collectins to serum MBL2.

title: The molecular basis of 3-methylcrotonylglycinuria, a disorder of leucine catabolism.
review_notes: Primary molecular characterization of the human MCCA (MCCC1) gene; PubMed-verified. Establishes the alpha subunit as biotin-containing and the leucine-catabolic role of MCC.

title: The molecular basis of human 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency.
review_notes: Independent primary characterization of MCCA/MCCB and disease-causing mutations; PubMed-verified.

title: Human biotin-containing subunit of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase gene (MCCA): cDNA sequence, genomic organization, localization to chromosomal band 3q27, and expression.
review_notes: Defines the domain architecture (biotin carboxylase + biotin-carrier) and mitochondrial localization of MCCC1; PubMed-verified.

title: Mitochondrial targeting signals and mature peptides of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase.
review_notes: Direct experimental evidence for mitochondrial matrix localization and transit peptide cleavage; PubMed-verified.

title: Expression, purification, characterization of human 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase (MCCC).
review_notes: Biochemical characterization of the assembled MCC holoenzyme; basis for the IDA carboxylase-activity, complex, and matrix-localization annotations. PubMed-verified.

title: Structure and function of biotin-dependent carboxylases.
review_notes: Family-level structure/function review; supports the modular BC/CT/BCCP architecture but is not gene-specific experimental evidence for MCCC1.

title: Mitochondrial Protein Interaction Mapping Identifies Regulators of Respiratory Chain Function.
review_notes: Large-scale mitochondrial protein-interaction mapping; source of an IntAct protein-binding IPI. MCCC1 is one node in a high-throughput dataset; not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex high-throughput AP-MS interactome; source of an IntAct protein-binding IPI (partner OXCT2). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Leucine regulates autophagy via acetylation of the mTORC1 component raptor.
review_notes: Knockdown/autophagy study confirming MCCC1's role as the leucine-metabolizing enzyme; it does not itself assay carboxylase catalytic activity (UniProt attaches the ECO:0000269 catalytic-activity claim to this paper alongside PMID:17360195).

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 dual proteome-scale interactome; source of IntAct protein-binding IPIs (partners OXCT2, MCCC2). High-throughput, not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteomics; supports mitochondrial localization at proteome scale (HTP evidence code).

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-mapping resource; source of an IntAct protein-binding IPI (partner MCCC2). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: The molecular basis of 3-methylcrotonylglycinuria, a disorder of leucine catabolism.
review_notes: Full text cached and verified. Establishes MCC as a heteromeric alpha/beta biotin-dependent carboxylase of leucine catabolism, that the beta subunit binds the acyl-CoA substrate, characterizes the human MCCB gene (563-residue polypeptide), and demonstrates in vivo involvement of MCC in leucine catabolism via a fungal MCCA-null model.

title: The molecular basis of human 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified title matches; parallel molecular characterization of human MCC deficiency and MCCC2 disease variants. Cache is abstract-only; claims (carboxylase activity, complex membership) are consistent with the well-established enzymology and corroborated by the IDA evidence.

title: Mitochondrial targeting signals and mature peptides of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase.
review_notes: Abstract-cached; directly supports mitochondrial matrix import of MCCbeta via a cleavable N-terminal presequence (cleavage Ala22/Tyr23), grounding the matrix localization annotations.

title: Expression, purification, characterization of human 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase (MCCC).
review_notes: Abstract-cached. Direct enzymatic characterization of purified recombinant human MCC (alpha/beta complex, ~500-800 kDa, 1:1 stoichiometry, kcat ~4.0 s-1, KM values), grounding the carboxylase-activity and complex-membership annotations.

title: Structure and function of biotin-dependent carboxylases.
review_notes: Review of biotin-dependent carboxylase structure/function; supports the multi-subunit (BC/CT/BCCP) architecture of MCC and the carboxyltransferase role of the beta subunit.

title: Mitochondrial Protein Interaction Mapping Identifies Regulators of Respiratory Chain Function.
review_notes: Large-scale mitochondrial interaction mapping; the MCCC2-MCCC1 interaction it captures is real but only supports a generic protein-binding annotation better represented by the carboxylase complex term.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome study; source of a generic protein-binding IPI (MCCC1). Contextual, not function-establishing for MCCC2.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome (MitoCoP); corroborates mitochondrial localization of MCCC2 by high-throughput proteomics.

title: CFTR interactome mapping using the mammalian membrane two-hybrid high-throughput screening system.
review_notes: High-throughput CFTR-interactome screen; the CFTR-MCCC2 IPI has no established biological relationship to this matrix enzyme and is likely non-specific.

title: Differential CFTR-Interactome Proximity Labeling Procedures Identify Enrichment in Multiple SLC Transporters.
review_notes: CFTR proximity-labeling screen; source of a generic CFTR-MCCC2 protein-binding IPI, not indicative of MCCC2 function.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map genomics study; source of a generic protein-binding IPI (MCCC1). Contextual.

title: 3-Methylcrotonyl-coenzyme A carboxylase deficiency in Amish/Mennonite adults identified by detection of increased acylcarnitines in blood spots of their children.
review_notes: Abstract-cached. Documents isolated MCC deficiency in humans, underpinning the IMP link between loss of MCC and disrupted leucine catabolism.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/GO_Central phylogenetic (IBA) inference for the MCEE ortholog group; consistent with the well-established epimerase function and mitochondrial localisation.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SubCell mapping (SL-0173 Mitochondrion) to GO:0005739; consistent with the UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION and experimental mitochondrial-proteome data.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: EC 5.1.99.1 / RHEA:20553 to GO:0004493 mapping; the EC and Rhea assignments are experimentally supported (PMID:11481338) so this electronic mapping is correct.

title: Identification of the human methylmalonyl-CoA racemase gene based on the analysis of prokaryotic gene arrangements. Implications for decoding the human genome.
review_notes: Primary paper establishing MCEE function and catalytic activity; PubMed-verified. Basis for the experimental (IDA) GO:0004493, GO:0046491 and GO:1901290 annotations.

title: A homozygous nonsense mutation in the methylmalonyl-CoA epimerase gene (MCEE) results in mild methylmalonic aciduria.

title: Falcon deep research report for MCTS1
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/Falcon) summary, marked UNVERIFIED pending source-by-source checking. The core MCTS1-specific claims it makes (cytoplasmic, 40S-/ribosome-associated non-canonical reinitiation+recycling factor obligately partnered with DENR; JAK2 5'UTR uORF dependence; impaired recycling on MCTS1 loss) are independently corroborated by the cached full text of Bohlen 2023 (PMID:37875108) and by the existing experimental annotations, so they are reliable. CAVEATS: (1) much of the mechanistic and target-class detail (uORF re-initiation, ATF4, mitotic translation, ~200-240 targets) derives from DENR-centric or MCTS1-DENR-complex work (Castelo-Szekely 2019, Meurs 2024/2025, von Hohenberg 2022, Vasudevan 2020) and should be read as properties of the heterodimer, not of MCTS1 in isolation. (2) The oncogene/cancer claims (PA2G4-P48 stabilization in HNSCC, IL-6/IL-6R/STAT3, EMT/stemness; Sun 2023, Weng 2019) are phenotypic/association-level and do not by themselves establish a distinct MCTS1 molecular function beyond translational control; not used to add or strengthen molecular-function annotations here. None of these cited papers (except PMID:37875108) are in the local publications cache, so their supporting_text was not independently verified.

title: Genome-wide YFP fluorescence complementation screen identifies new regulators for telomere signaling in human cells.

review_notes: Prostatic-secretion exosome proteomics; MDH1 among ~900 detected proteins. Supports only the over-annotated exosome localization.

review_notes: Establishes that human cytosolic malate dehydrogenase and the historically described aromatic alpha-keto acid reductase are the same protein; cited by UniProt for EC 1.1.1.37. Supports both the core MDH activity and the promiscuous KAR side activity. Abstract-only cache.

title: MDH1 deficiency is a metabolic disorder of the malate-aspartate shuttle associated with early onset severe encephalopathy.

review_notes: UniProt reference for MDH1's reduction of 2-oxoglutarate to 2-hydroxyglutarate (basis of the (S)-2-hydroxyglutarate dehydrogenase side activity). Not cached locally; not manually verified.

review_notes: Reports a cytosolic MDH1/ME1/pyruvate-carboxylase hydride transfer complex that transfers reducing equivalents from NADH to NADP+ in cancer/hypoxic cells. Basis for the NAD+/NADP+ metabolic-process and cytoplasm IDA annotations. Abstract-only cache.

title: The malate-aspartate shuttle is important for de novo serine biosynthesis.
review_notes: Genetic disruption of MAS components in HEK293 cells; MDH1-deficient cells show the most severe metabolic disruption, providing IMP support for MDH1's role in the malate-aspartate shuttle. Abstract-only cache.

title: Molecular cloning and mapping of a human cDNA for cytosolic malate dehydrogenase (MDH1).
review_notes: cDNA cloning and chromosomal mapping (2p15) of cytosolic MDH1; supports the cytosol localization. Does NOT support the "malic enzyme activity" molecular function it is cited for (that MF is EC 1.1.1.40, a different enzyme).

title: An NADH-tetrazolium-coupled sensitive assay for malate dehydrogenase in mitochondria and crude tissue homogenates.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false); a sensitive spectrophotometric assay for mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase activity. Used by Reactome as evidence that the MDH2 dimer dehydrogenates malate; supports the NAD-dependent malate dehydrogenase activity annotation.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: High-throughput B-cell exosome proteomics; MDH2 detected as background. Supports only a likely-contaminant extracellular-exosome location.

review_notes: Full text available; primary disease/functional paper. Directly establishes MDH2's NAD-dependent malate dehydrogenase activity, its TCA and malate-aspartate-shuttle roles, and support for aerobic respiration.

review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Old (1983) case study; provides IMP/dosage support linking the chromosome-7 MDH2 locus to mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase activity and malate metabolism.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Yeast two-hybrid interactome map; correctly cited as the source of an IPI row whose partner (UniProtKB:P63010, AP2B1) is now known to be a real, if secondary, MEA1 client. Useful corroboration rather than a functional study.

title: Male-enhanced antigen gene is phylogenetically conserved and expressed at late stages of spermatogenesis.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed as Lau YF, Chan KM, Sparkes R, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 1989 Nov;86(21):8462-6, doi 10.1073/pnas.86.21.8462; abstract only in the cache. The identifier and title are correct, but the paper does not support the two biological-process annotations drawn from it. It reports cloning, conservation and an expression pattern, and states its functional claim explicitly as a hypothesis; it contains no functional assay of MEA1 in spermatogenesis or gonad development. Flagged MISCITED on that basis rather than for any defect in the paper itself.

review_notes: HuRI binary interactome. Records MEA1 with UniProtKB:Q9BXS5 (AP1M1, the mu1 subunit), which the 2026 mechanistic work confirms as a direct client - an early and correct observation buried under a bare protein binding term.

title: Regulation of AP1 adaptor assembly by the bi-handed chaperone MEA1.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed as Wan C, Wu J, Ouyang Y, Puscher H, Tian Y, Li S, Yin Q, Shen J, Nat Commun 2026 Jan 20;17(1), doi 10.1038/s41467-026-68662-3, PMC12923701; full text cached. The sole primary source for MEA1's molecular function, and a well-controlled one: heterologous reconstitution in E. coli, domain mapping with interface point mutants, endogenous co-IP, knockout-and-rescue in two human cell lines, and cargo-trafficking readouts. The AlphaFold-derived interface details are predictions, but each was tested by mutagenesis. Still a single study and a single laboratory; independent replication of the dual-chaperone collision model is not yet available.

Correctly cited and methodologically substantial, but it is a single-laboratory study with no independent replication - a PubMed search for 'MICU metabolon' returns only this paper and its own Research Square preprint (PMID:40678212) - and no published rebuttal. Its headline assertion of primacy over matrix-Ca2+-dependent dehydrogenase activation is framed as a proposal, and the paper itself continues to describe MICU1 as the primary regulator of uniporter-mediated uptake, so no existing annotation is retracted on its basis.

title: Falcon deep research report for MKKS
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report (Falcon/Edison) over recent reviews (Alvarez-Satta 2017, Tian 2023, Gupta 2022, etc.). Correctness left UNVERIFIED because the underlying review papers are not in the local cache and the synthesis was machine-generated. MKKS-CHAPERONIN-SPECIFIC claims that are well anchored and consistent with the curated literature: (1) MKKS is a chaperonin-LIKE assembly factor, NOT a stable/core BBSome subunit; (2) MKKS does not perform canonical ATP-dependent protein folding - its ATP-hydrolysis motif is divergent and the actual folding is executed by the associated canonical CCT/TRiC chaperonins; (3) MKKS/BBS12 act as substrate-binding units mediating association of CCT with the client BBS7, stabilizing BBS7 for the BBS2-BBS7-BBS9 core; (4) basal-body/ centrosome-centered localization, and chaperonin-like BBS proteins are generally NOT detected along the cilium itself. These are used to STRENGTHEN existing annotations only, not to add new ones. CLAIMS to treat with caution as BBSome/CCT GENERALIZATION rather than direct MKKS evidence: BBSome cargo-adaptor trafficking, Hedgehog/GPCR/ARL6 trafficking detail, and SMARCC1/nuclear moonlighting (the report itself flags these as less established); these were not used to alter MKKS molecular-function calls.
