title: NANP dephosphorylates Neu5Ac-9-P to Neu5Ac
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the NANP-catalyzed step; supports the cytosolic localization (TAS) and the biosynthetic role.

title: Cloning and expression of the human N-acetylneuraminic acid phosphate synthase gene with 2-keto-3-deoxy-D-glycero- D-galacto-nononic acid biosynthetic ability.
review_notes: Primary biochemical characterization of human NANS; PubMed title/authors match the cited record. Establishes EC 2.5.1.57 (and the minor EC 2.5.1.132 KDN-9-P) activity.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Large-scale exosome proteomics; supports only mass-spec detection in an exosome preparation (source of the HDA extracellular-exosome annotation), not a curated functional location for a cytosolic biosynthetic enzyme.

title: NANS-mediated synthesis of sialic acid is required for brain and skeletal development.
review_notes: Disease/function paper (van Karnebeek et al. 2016) establishing NANS deficiency (SEMDG). Not in GOA and not cached locally; included via the UniProt Q9NR45 entry, which attributes its FUNCTION and DISEASE statements to this PMID. No verbatim supporting_text quoted because the publication is not cached.

title: Activity of N-acylneuraminate-9-phosphatase (NANP) is not essential for de novo sialic acid biosynthesis.
review_notes: Human cell-line loss-of-function study; NANS KO abolishes cell-surface sialylation and CMP-sialic acid. Supports the IMP annotations for sialic acid / CMP-sialic acid biosynthetic process.

title: NANS converts ManNAc-6-P to Neu5Ac-9-P
review_notes: Reactome human reaction for the NANS catalytic step; consistent with the primary literature (Lawrence et al. 2000).

title: Elevation of cellular NAD levels by nicotinic acid and involvement of nicotinic acid phosphoribosyltransferase in human cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified original identification of human NAPRT; abstract-only cache but directly supports the IDA/IMP catalytic, salvage-biosynthesis, and oxidative-stress annotations.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary-exosome proteomics; supports the extracellular exosome location only as MS detection of an abundant cytosolic protein, not a functional localization.

title: Characterization of human nicotinate phosphoribosyltransferase: Kinetic studies, structure prediction and functional analysis by site-directed mutagenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified enzymology of human NAPRT; abstract cites EC 2.4.2.11 (transferase), the same enzyme now assigned EC 6.3.4.21 (ATP-coupled ligase). Supports the EXP MF.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Prostatic-secretion exosome shotgun proteomics; supports the extracellular exosome location only as MS detection, not a functional site.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Systematic Y2H interactome (Rolland et al. 2014); source of the bare "protein binding" IPI annotations, which are uninformative for NAPRT's molecular function.

title: Crystal structure of human nicotinic acid phosphoribosyltransferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Supports the catalytic MF, homodimer subunit, and Preiss-Handler pathway role.

title: NAPRT1 dimer transfers PRIB to NCA to form NAMN
review_notes: Reactome reaction modeling cytosolic NAPRT catalysis (nicotinate + PRPP -> NaMN); supports the cytosol location and catalytic function.

title: Exocytosis of azurophil granule lumen proteins
review_notes: Reactome neutrophil-degranulation pathway; source of the extracellular region and azurophil granule lumen locations, which are secondary to the cytosolic NAD-synthesis function.

title: Prediction of the coding sequences of unidentified human genes. XIX. The complete sequences of 100 new cDNA clones from brain which code for large proteins in vitro.
review_notes: Gene-discovery cDNA paper; supports only the generic nuclear localization statement.

title: Purification of human telomerase complexes identifies factors involved in telomerase biogenesis and telomere length regulation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Fu & Collins, Mol Cell 2007). Correctly cited, but the paper describes NAT10 as an associated NTPase rather than a holoenzyme component, and the telomere-shortening phenotype is from overexpression - both of which temper the GO:0005697 and GO:0032211 annotations drawn from it.

title: Purification of proteins associated with specific genomic Loci.
review_notes: PICh methodology paper; source of a high-throughput telomeric-chromatin association only.

title: NAT10, a nucleolar protein, localizes to the midbody and regulates cytokinesis and acetylation of microtubules.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Exp Cell Res 2009). Solid for the nucleolus/midbody localization. Its microtubule-acetylation claim is one of the in vitro protein-KAT results that UniProt flags as of unsure in vivo relevance.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Membrane-fraction proteomics; the resulting GO:0016020 annotation for a soluble nucleolar protein is best read as co-fractionation.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: mRNA-interactome capture; recovering NAT10 as a poly(A)-binding protein is part of what originally motivated the search for mRNA ac4C.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: Independent mRNA-bound proteome study recovering NAT10.

title: Human NAT10 is an ATP-dependent RNA acetyltransferase responsible for N4-acetylcytidine formation in 18 S ribosomal RNA (rRNA).
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Ito et al., J Biol Chem 2014). The defining biochemical paper for the core activity; also the source of the explicit statement that the protein-lysine activity of full-length NAT10 remains undetermined.

title: Yeast Kre33 and human NAT10 are conserved 18S rRNA cytosine acetyltransferases that modify tRNAs assisted by the adaptor Tan1/THUMPD1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sharma et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2015). Establishes both the two 18S rRNA sites and the THUMPD1-dependent tRNA activity.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome; source of a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: Histone Interaction Landscapes Visualized by Crosslinking Mass Spectrometry in Intact Cell Nuclei.
review_notes: Crosslinking MS; source of a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: Acetylation of Cytidine in mRNA Promotes Translation Efficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Arango et al., Cell 2018). Correctly cited for the annotations that rest on it, but its central mRNA-ac4C claim is contested by PMID:32555463 and PMID:38640895 and was defended in PMID:38640896. The acRIP-seq method is antibody-based and not base-resolution.

title: CCDC84 Acetylation Oscillation Regulates Centrosome Duplication by Modulating HsSAS-6 Degradation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Wang et al., Cell Rep 2019). NAT10 is the acetyltransferase arm of a SIRT1/NAT10 pair acting on CCDC84 K31; this is the sole basis for the protein-acetylation and centrosome-duplication annotations.

title: Dynamic RNA acetylation revealed by quantitative cross-evolutionary mapping.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sas-Chen et al., Nature 2020). The primary negative result for human mRNA ac4C by chemical base-resolution mapping, and simultaneously the primary positive result for archaeal mRNA ac4C. Not currently represented in GOA for NAT10.

title: Quantitative nucleotide resolution profiling of RNA cytidine acetylation by ac4C-seq.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Thalalla Gamage et al., Nat Protoc 2021). The published protocol for the method behind the negative human-mRNA result; itself frames human mRNA ac4C as an open question.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interaction network; source of bare protein-binding annotations.

title: Nucleolar maturation of the human small subunit processome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Singh et al., Science 2021). Cryo-EM structures placing NAT10 within the human SSU processome; the strongest evidence for the complex-membership and 40S-biogenesis annotations.

title: Direct epitranscriptomic regulation of mammalian translation initiation through N4-acetylcytidine.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Arango et al., Mol Cell 2022; note a published erratum, Mol Cell 82:2912). The base-resolution positive result for human mRNA ac4C. Directly challenged by PMID:38640895 on reproducibility and duplicate-read grounds and defended in PMID:38640896. The cryo-EM component, showing how ac4C at position -1 perturbs the initiator tRNA t6A37 interaction, is independent of the mapping dispute.

title: No evidence for ac4C within human mRNA upon data reassessment.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Georgeson & Schwartz, Mol Cell 2024). The formal challenge to the mRNA ac4C claim; argues the RedaC:T-seq mismatch signature is driven by low library complexity and disappears after duplicate removal. Not currently represented in GOA for NAT10.

title: Detection of ac4C in human mRNA is preserved upon data reassessment.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Beiki et al., Mol Cell 2024). The back-to-back rebuttal defending RedaC:T-seq and raising depth and reduction-efficiency problems in the ac4C-seq data. Marked DISPUTED because it is one half of an unresolved exchange, not because the citation is faulty.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Cell-mapping resource; source of a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: NAT10 promotes cisplatin resistance and immune escape by increasing the expression of DUSP1 and PD-L1 in gastric cancer.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Death Discov 2026). Representative of the 2025-2026 disease literature that asserts NAT10-dependent mRNA ac4C on named transcripts using antibody-based ac4C-RIP plus knockdown, without citing or addressing PMID:38640895. Does not provide independent methodological support for the contested substrate claim.

title: Gasdermin C reprograms metabolism through the CAMKK2-AMPK axis to promote lung adenocarcinoma progression and radioresistance.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as a citation (Ren et al., Cell Rep 2026); abstract-only in the local cache. Reports GSDMC scaffolding NAT10 to drive histone H3 acetylation, a protein-acetyltransferase claim distinct from the RNA activity. Marked UNVERIFIED because the mechanistic claim rests on chromatin and knockdown experiments that I could not inspect, and an indirect route via impaired ribosome biogenesis is not excluded.

title: NAT10 deficiency in aging drives impaired liver regeneration by disrupting PARP10 in an ac4C-dependent manner.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Clin Mol Hepatol 2026); abstract-only in the local cache. Another ac4C-RIP-based single-transcript mRNA acetylation claim that does not engage the mapping dispute.

title: Targeting NAT10 with Remodelin reshapes the pro-fibrotic microenvironment in renal fibrogenesis via inhibiting exosome oversecretion from tubular cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Acta Pharm Sin B 2026). Invokes both contested activities at once - nuclear mRNA ac4C and cytoplasmic lysine acetylation - and relies on remodelin, which impairs ribosome biogenesis, so the phenotype does not discriminate between the proposed mechanisms.

title: A role for NBR1 in autophagosomal degradation of ubiquitinated substrates.
review_notes: Foundational study establishing NBR1 as an autophagy receptor. Abstract-only in cache; domain/mutagenesis detail corroborated by UniProt features.

title: Interactions with LC3 and polyubiquitin chains link nbr1 to autophagic protein turnover.
review_notes: Establishes the core ubiquitin-binding and LC3-binding activities. Abstract available in cache.

title: Spred2 interaction with the late endosomal protein NBR1 down-regulates fibroblast growth factor receptor signaling.
review_notes: Supports the late-endosome localization and a receptor-trafficking role.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane proteome; source of the generic membrane (HDA) annotation.

title: Nix is a selective autophagy receptor for mitochondrial clearance.
review_notes: Establishes the LC3/GABARAP selective-autophagy receptor paradigm; NBR1 cited in the receptor network; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Interactome mapping of the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-mammalian target of rapamycin pathway identifies deformed epidermal autoregulatory factor-1 as a new glycogen synthase kinase-3 interactor.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: The selective macroautophagic degradation of aggregated proteins requires the PI3P-binding protein Alfy.
review_notes: Supports the aggrephagy context; NBR1 acts as a cargo partner in p62/NBR1-positive inclusions.

title: Network organization of the human autophagy system.
review_notes: Autophagy interactome network; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: NBR1 is a new PB1 signalling adapter in Th2 differentiation and allergic airway inflammation in vivo.
review_notes: Establishes a pleiotropic PB1-domain immune signaling-adapter role (mouse in vivo).

title: Broad activation of the ubiquitin-proteasome system by Parkin is critical for mitophagy.
review_notes: Source of the mitochondrion colocalizes_with annotation; reflects recruitment to damaged mitochondria during mitophagy.

title: Solution structure of the ubiquitin-associated (UBA) domain of human autophagy receptor NBR1 and its interaction with ubiquitin and polyubiquitin.
review_notes: Structural basis of the core ubiquitin-binding function. Not in publications cache; verified via PubMed and UniProt mutagenesis features.

title: Phosphorylation of NBR1 by GSK3 modulates protein aggregation.
review_notes: Establishes the aggregation-promoting (aggrephagy) function and its GSK3 regulation. Abstract in cache.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome (HuRI); source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: An AP-MS- and BioID-compatible MAC-tag enables comprehensive mapping of protein interactions and subcellular localizations.
review_notes: High-throughput interaction/localization mapping; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Isoform-specific GSK3A activity is negatively correlated with human sperm motility.
review_notes: GSK3A context; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Receptor-mediated clustering of FIP200 bypasses the role of LC3 lipidation in autophagy.
review_notes: Supports the cargo-receptor/autophagy-initiation role and TAX1BP1 interaction. Full text available.

title: The PB1 protein of influenza A virus inhibits the innate immune response by targeting MAVS for NBR1-mediated selective autophagic degradation.
review_notes: Establishes NBR1-mediated selective autophagy of MAVS and an antiviral-restricting role. Not in cache; verified via PubMed.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome (BioPlex); source of a bare protein binding annotation.

review_notes: Mechanistic in vitro evidence for the cargo-receptor / condensate-formation function. Full text available.

review_notes: Macroautophagy proximity interactome; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: NBR1 mediates autophagic degradation of IRF3 to negatively regulate type I interferon production.
review_notes: Establishes selective autophagy of IRF3 and negative regulation of type I IFN. Abstract in cache.

title: Selective Autophagy Receptor NBR1 Retards Nucleus Pulposus Cell Senescence by Directing the Clearance of SRBD1.
review_notes: Adds a specific selective-autophagy substrate (SRBD1). Full text available.

title: Nicastrin modulates presenilin-mediated notch/glp-1 signal transduction and betaAPP processing.
review_notes: Cached abstract directly supports nicastrin as a presenilin-associated component needed for Notch/GLP-1 and betaAPP intramembrane proteolysis.

title: Mammalian APH-1 interacts with presenilin and nicastrin and is required for intramembrane proteolysis of amyloid-beta precursor protein and Notch.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports nicastrin participation with APH-1 and presenilin in gamma-secretase-dependent APP and Notch proteolysis.

title: APH1, PEN2, and Nicastrin increase Abeta levels and gamma-secretase activity.

title: Purification and characterization of the human gamma-secretase complex.
review_notes: Cached abstract reports purification of active human gamma-secretase and identifies mature nicastrin with presenilin, APH-1, and Pen-2 as core components.

title: Three-dimensional structure of human γ-secretase.

title: An atomic structure of human γ-secretase.

title: The subunit composition of the human NADH dehydrogenase obtained by rapid one-step immunopurification.

title: Novel localization of OCTN1, an organic cation/carnitine transporter, to mammalian mitochondria.

title: Identification of mitochondrial complex I assembly intermediates by tracing tagged NDUFS3 demonstrates the entry point of mitochondrial subunits.
review_notes: Supports Complex I membrane-arm assembly and NDUFA1 membrane localization.

title: Architecture of Human Mitochondrial Respiratory Megacomplex I(2)III(2)IV(2).

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteomics; source of the HTP mitochondrion localization annotation.

title: cDNA of eight nuclear encoded subunits of NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase: human complex I cDNA characterization completed.
review_notes: cDNA characterization of nuclear-encoded Complex I subunits; source of the NAS complex-membership and NADH-to-ubiquinone electron transport annotations.

title: The subunit composition of the human NADH dehydrogenase obtained by rapid one-step immunopurification.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; supports NDUFA10 as a stable Complex I subunit (source of an IDA complex-membership annotation).

title: Accessory subunits are integral for assembly and function of human mitochondrial complex I.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt FUNCTION line; underpins the structural/assembly (non-catalytic) role of NDUFA10.

title: Architecture of Human Mitochondrial Respiratory Megacomplex I(2)III(2)IV(2).
review_notes: Source of ComplexPortal IDA/IPI complex-membership and inner-membrane localization annotations.

title: Assembly of mammalian oxidative phosphorylation complexes I-V and supercomplexes.
review_notes: Review supporting ComplexPortal NAS process annotations; general OXPHOS/supercomplex context.

title: cDNA of eight nuclear encoded subunits of NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase: human complex I cDNA characterization completed.
review_notes: Source of NAS complex-membership, process, and (over-reaching) MF annotations; supports structural/process roles, not a subunit-level catalytic MF.

review_notes: Complex I biogenesis pathway reaction; source of a TAS inner-membrane localization.

review_notes: Complex I biogenesis pathway reaction; source of a TAS inner-membrane localization.

review_notes: Complex I biogenesis pathway reaction; source of a TAS inner-membrane localization.

review_notes: Complex I biogenesis pathway reaction; source of a TAS inner-membrane localization.

title: The subunit composition of the human NADH dehydrogenase obtained by rapid one-step immunopurification.
review_notes: Primary MS evidence for NDUFA11 complex membership; cited by the UniProt SUBUNIT/localization statements. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Accessory subunits are integral for assembly and function of human mitochondrial complex I.
review_notes: Systematic knockout/proteomics study; primary evidence that accessory subunits including NDUFA11 are required for Complex I assembly and function. Cited by the UniProt FUNCTION statement. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Architecture of Human Mitochondrial Respiratory Megacomplex I(2)III(2)IV(2).
review_notes: Structural basis (ComplexPortal IDA/IPI) for NDUFA11 as an inner-membrane Complex I subunit and for supercomplex context. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Assembly of mammalian oxidative phosphorylation complexes I-V and supercomplexes.
review_notes: Review used by ComplexPortal for the pathway-level aerobic respiration and ATP-synthesis (NAS) annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Genome-wide binary Y2H interactome (HuRI); source of the bare "protein binding" IPI. NDUFA11 is not discussed individually (one PPI among >50,000); the reported partner MEOX2 is not a plausible functional partner for a Complex I membrane subunit. Uninformative for molecular function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteomics; source of the HTP mitochondrion localization annotation. NDUFA11 not named individually in body text.

title: Characterization of the human complex I NDUFB7 and 17.2-kDa cDNAs and mutational analysis of 19 genes of the HP fraction in complex I-deficient-patients.
review_notes: Original characterization of the human 17.2-kDa (B17.2) Complex I subunit cDNA (= NDUFA12). Establishes identity; the derived NAS 'NADH dehydrogenase (ubiquinone) activity' MF reflects the enzyme name, not a catalytic activity of this non-catalytic subunit.

title: The subunit composition of the human NADH dehydrogenase obtained by rapid one-step immunopurification.
review_notes: Mass-spec identification of NDUFA12 (the differentiation-linked 13 kDa protein) as a subunit of immunopurified human Complex I. Direct support for Complex I membership. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Cyclin B1/Cdk1 coordinates mitochondrial respiration for cell-cycle G2/M progression.
review_notes: Study of cyclin B1/Cdk1 phosphorylation of Complex I subunits to enhance CI activity for G2/M. Abstract addresses CI subunits generically (does not name NDUFA12); underpins complex-level BP annotations treated here as non-core. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Accessory subunits are integral for assembly and function of human mitochondrial complex I.
review_notes: CRISPR knockout of each accessory subunit + quantitative proteomics defining NDUFA12 as an integral accessory (non-catalytic) subunit of human Complex I. Primary support for the accessory-subunit function. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Architecture of Human Mitochondrial Respiratory Megacomplex I(2)III(2)IV(2).
review_notes: Cryo-EM of the human respiratory megacomplex assigning individual CI subunits, including NDUFA12, in the inner membrane. Supports inner-membrane localization and Complex I membership (ComplexPortal curation). Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Assembly of mammalian oxidative phosphorylation complexes I-V and supercomplexes.
review_notes: Review of OXPHOS/supercomplex assembly; supernumerary subunits play roles in assembly, regulation and stability. Basis for ComplexPortal NAS complex-level BP annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI high-throughput binary (Y2H) interactome. Source of the three IntAct IPI 'protein binding' annotations (TMED8, MYO15B, SYT4). Full text available but the NDUFA12 interactions appear only in supplementary data, not the main text; these binary hits are not the physiologically relevant Complex I contacts, hence the uninformative MF is treated as over-annotation.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial-proteome study; supports mitochondrial localization of NDUFA12 (coarse relative to inner-membrane/Complex I). Cached record is very large; localization use is consistent with UniProt.

title: Identification of GRIM-19, a novel cell death-regulatory gene induced by the interferon-beta and retinoic acid combination, using a genetic approach.
review_notes: Discovery paper: isolated GRIM-19 in an antisense-knockout screen for mediators of IFN-beta/RA-induced tumor-cell death; found it primarily nuclear and IFN/RA-inducible. Underpins the moonlighting cell-death role and the nuclear/cytoplasmic localization annotations. The NAS 'ATP binding' asserted here is not experimentally demonstrated. Abstract-only in cache.

title: The subunit composition of the human NADH dehydrogenase obtained by rapid one-step immunopurification.
review_notes: Mass-spec identification of GRIM-19 as a subunit of immunopurified human Complex I; primary support for Complex I membership and mitochondrial localization. Abstract-only in cache.

title: GRIM-19, a death-regulatory gene product, suppresses Stat3 activity via functional interaction.
review_notes: Independent Y2H identification of GRIM-19 as a specific Stat3-interacting negative regulator; also documents mitochondrial co-localization and a nuclear pool. Supports the STAT3 moonlighting function and localization annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: The cell death regulator GRIM-19 is an inhibitor of signal transducer and activator of transcription 3.
review_notes: Primary demonstration that GRIM-19 specifically binds STAT3 (via the TAD/Ser727) and represses STAT3-dependent transcription without blocking STAT3 phosphorylation or DNA binding. Basis for the negative-regulation-of-transcription (STAT3) annotation. Full text available and verified.

title: GW112, a novel antiapoptotic protein that promotes tumor growth.
review_notes: OLFM4/GW112 study that also examined GRIM-19 subcellular localization (mitochondrial). Supports inner-membrane localization. Abstract-only in cache.

title: GRIM-19, a cell death regulatory protein, is essential for assembly and function of mitochondrial complex I.
review_notes: Gene-targeting study: GRIM-19 knockout is embryonic-lethal; GRIM-19 is in native Complex I and its loss destroys CI assembly and electron-transfer activity. Strong support for the core structural/assembly role and mitochondrial localization. Abstract-only in cache.

title: GRIM-19 interacts with nucleotide oligomerization domain 2 and serves as downstream effector of anti-bacterial function in intestinal epithelial cells.
review_notes: Y2H + functional study: GRIM-19 interacts with NOD2/CARD15 and is required for NOD2-mediated NF-kB activation and antibacterial responses in intestinal epithelium. Source of the NOD2 protein-binding IPI; a non-core innate-immunity function. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Coupling mitochondrial respiratory chain to cell death: an essential role of mitochondrial complex I in the interferon-beta and retinoic acid-induced cancer cell death.
review_notes: Links Complex I (GRIM-19/NDUFS3) to IFN-beta/RA-induced apoptosis via ROS; source of a mitochondrial-localization IDA and support for the moonlighting cell-death role. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Identification of mitochondrial complex I assembly intermediates by tracing tagged NDUFS3 demonstrates the entry point of mitochondrial subunits.

title: [Profanities and the profane person].

It is cited in GOA as the IDA support for GO:0060090 and GO:0030674 and is a digit-dropped form of PMID:31189953 (Sharif et al., Nature 2019, NEK7-licensed activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome), which supports the neighbouring annotations made on the same dates. title: A novel PAAD-containing protein that modulates NF-kappa B induction by cytokines tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interleukin-1beta.
review_notes: Describes 'PAN2', a PAAD-containing protein that suppresses cytokine-induced NF-kappaB. The PAN/PYPAF nomenclature of 2002 is ambiguous across NLRP family members and the abstract does not use the NLRP3 or cryopyrin names, so the gene identity could not be confirmed from the cached text. The annotation it supports (GO:0006954) is uncontroversial for NLRP3 and is not challenged.

title: De novo CIAS1 mutations, cytokine activation, and evidence for genetic heterogeneity in patients with neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease (NOMID): a new member of the expanding family of pyrin-associated autoinflammatory diseases.

Correctly cited and scientifically sound, but the annotations derived from it (GO:0032691, GO:0050728) invert the direction of the biology: the mutations are gain-of-function and the patients are hyper-inflammatory. Correctly identified, and reasonable as TAS support for the general cytoplasm and defense-response annotations, but it is cited in GOA as the support for GO:0042834 peptidoglycan binding, a ligand-binding molecular function for which neither this review nor any primary study provides direct evidence. That is the basis for the REMOVE on that annotation.

title: Silica crystals and aluminum salts activate the NALP3 inflammasome through phagosomal destabilization.
review_notes: Hornung et al. 2008. Cited in GOA as IDA support for molecular sensor activity, but the paper's own conclusion is that what NLRP3 senses is lysosomal damage downstream of phagocytosis, not the crystal itself - which is why that annotation is marked over-annotated. Note PubMed records a 2026 erratum for this article (Nat Immunol 27(4):881).

title: The receptor NLRP3 is a transcriptional regulator of TH2 differentiation.
review_notes: Bruchard et al., Nat Immunol 2015, doi 10.1038/ni.3202 - PubMed-verified. The sole primary source behind every DNA-binding, IRF4-binding, nuclear and T helper 2 annotation on human NLRP3, all of which reach the human gene by IBA or ISS from mouse Nlrp3. Single laboratory, mouse only, carries a published corrigendum (PMID:26580508), and no NLRP3 DNA-binding domain or NLRP3-DNA structure has been reported since despite extensive structural work. Flagged DISPUTED rather than MISCITED: the citation is correct, the claim is uncorroborated.

title: Corrigendum: The receptor NLRP3 is a transcriptional regulator of TH2 differentiation.
review_notes: Corrigendum to PMID:26098997 (Nat Immunol 2015). Cited so that the correction is visible alongside the primary claim; the corrigendum text itself was not available.

title: Falcon deep research report for NLRX1
review_notes: LLM synthesis (Edison/Falcon) built almost entirely from recent secondary reviews (Bi 2024, Pickering 2021, Chou 2023/2022, Jewell 2024) and very recent primary papers (Xiao 2025 mPTP; Zhang 2026 acetyl-CoA; Song 2024 SLC39A7) that are NOT in the local publications cache, so the cited claims could not be verified against primary text and are marked UNVERIFIED. Several claims are debated or go beyond what the cached primary literature shows: (1) Localization - falcon asserts NLRX1 is in the matrix and inner mitochondrial membrane in addition to the outer membrane, whereas the foundational cached papers (PMID:18200010, PMID:22749352) place its MAVS-regulatory activity at the mitochondrial outer membrane; the matrix/inner-membrane and mPTP claims rest on uncached 2024-2025 work. (2) Mitophagy - falcon frames direct NLRX1-LC3 binding and mitophagy as the overarching function, but the cached full-text PMID:22749352 states mitophagy "was not occurring under these test conditions" and that NLRX1 promotes (non-selective) autophagy indirectly via TUFM/ATG5-ATG12, not by direct LC3 binding; the LC3-receptor/acetyl-CoA model is newer and not independently verified here. (3) NF-kappaB - falcon (citing reviews) reports NLRX1 NEGATIVELY regulates NF-kappaB, which contradicts the human-specific cached primary report (PMID:18219313) that NLRX1 AMPLIFIES NF-kappaB/JNK via ROS; this confirms the field is genuinely mixed. Useful as a pointer to recent literature and to flag controversy, but not used as sole support for any annotation action change.

The underlying complex membership is correct, but this citation is a wrong identifier and should be replaced.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The IBA propagated GO:0003955 (NAD(P)H dehydrogenase (quinone) activity, EC 1.6.5.2) to NQO2, but NQO2 uses NRH rather than NAD(P)H; the phylogenetic inference over-generalizes the family cofactor. The IBA cytosol annotation is correct.

title: Bioactivation of 5-(aziridin-1-yl)-2,4-dinitrobenzamide (CB 1954) by human NAD(P)H quinone oxidoreductase 2: a novel co-substrate-mediated antitumor prodrug therapy.
review_notes: Establishes the NRH co-substrate requirement (the key distinction from NQO1) and the quinone/nitroaromatic (CB1954) reductase activity. Abstract-level cache; the NRH-dependence claim is anchored to the GOA IDA evidence.

title: Crystal structure of quinone reductase 2 in complex with resveratrol.
review_notes: Primary structural + binding paper for the QR2-resveratrol interaction (crystal structure PDB 1SG0; Kd ~35 nM by tryptophan-fluorescence titration). This is the definitive experimental basis for resveratrol binding (GO:1905594) and is evidence-grade for a GO IDA - arguably the better primary reference than PMID:18254726 (which used resveratrol as an ITC control) - but it is not currently cited by GOA as the annotation's evidence. Added here for provenance/completeness, not to assert a new annotation.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome screen; source of a generic protein binding annotation, non-core.

title: Kinetic, thermodynamic and X-ray structural insights into the interaction of melatonin and analogues with quinone reductase 2.
review_notes: Primary structural/kinetic paper; source of the FAD/Zn/chloride/melatonin/resveratrol binding, homodimerization, and quinone-reduction IDA annotations. PMC full text verified.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; source of an extracellular-exosome HDA annotation, non-core.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; source of an extracellular-exosome HDA annotation, non-core.

title: Cochaperone binding to LYR motifs confers specificity of iron sulfur cluster delivery.
review_notes: Source of a generic protein binding annotation (HSC20/HSCB context); non-core for NQO2.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI interactome map; source of a generic protein binding annotation, non-core.

title: OpenScientist blinded function-assignment report for NQO2 (NAD(P)H dehydrogenase (quinone) activity, GO:0003955)
review_notes: Blinded computational hypothesis assessment (3-iteration run) used as independent corroboration of the manual MODIFY (GO:0003955 -> GO:0001512), not as primary evidence. Its key claim rests on cached/curated primary data (NRH dependence); it additionally cites Wu et al. 1997 (PMID:9367528) as the definitive enzymology - a valid lead not currently in this review's reference set.

title: The gene mutated in bare patches and striated mice encodes a novel 3beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Identifies the gene and establishes its role in cholesterol biosynthesis via mouse Bpa/Str alleles; abstract-only cache.

title: Mutations in the NSDHL gene, encoding a 3beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, cause CHILD syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes NSDHL-CHILD syndrome link and cholesterol-pathway role; abstract-only cache.

title: Identification of major proteins in the lipid droplet-enriched fraction isolated from the human hepatocyte cell line HuH7.
review_notes: Lipid-droplet proteomics; the abstract does not name NSDHL specifically (curator full-text-based IDA), so treated as supporting the LD localization only.

title: Hypomorphic temperature-sensitive alleles of NSDHL cause CK syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Basis for the EXP ER-membrane localization and CK syndrome association; abstract-only cache.

title: Human lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferases 1 and 2 are located in lipid droplets where they catalyze the formation of phosphatidylcholine.
review_notes: About LPCAT1/2; the abstract does not mention NSDHL (curator full-text IDA). Supports the LD localization context.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome screen; correctly cited but yields only uninformative 'protein binding'.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome screen; correctly cited but uninformative for MF.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO mapping. Correctly applied, but produces only generic parents where the exact reaction is known from experiment.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Orthology transfers from mouse Nsun2. Appropriate for the tRNA stabilisation and for the skin and stem-cell phenotypes, which are genuine mouse knockout results.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The tRNA-related IBAs on this gene are sound. Three others (rRNA C5 methyltransferase activity, rRNA processing, mitochondrial large ribosomal subunit assembly) name mouse Nsun4 as the donor in the GOA WITH/FROM column and appear to carry a paralogue-specific function onto NSUN2.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Subcellular-location mapping. Nucleolus, cytoplasm and mitochondrion are right; extracellular region is an over-reach from the exosome observation.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learning annotations. tRNA methylation is right; mRNA processing is the wrong branch for what NSUN2 does to mRNA.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automatic methods; consistent with the manual annotations on this gene.

title: Identification of human tRNA:m5C methyltransferase catalysing intron-dependent m5C formation in the first position of the anticodon of the pre-tRNA Leu (CAA).
review_notes: Full text available and read. Founding identification of the human Trm4 orthologue, with single-nucleotide substrate specificity and yeast complementation. Basis of the core molecular function.

title: The tRNA methyltransferase NSun2 stabilizes p16INK⁴ mRNA by methylating the 3'-untranslated region of p16.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Reports in vitro methylation of the p16 3'UTR and an mRNA half-life effect, but the site is given as "A988", and the paper carries an erratum (Nat Commun 2013;4:2703). Supports the mRNA activity in principle while illustrating why site-level claims in this literature need orthogonal confirmation.

title: Whole exome sequencing identifies a splicing mutation in NSUN2 as a cause of a Dubowitz-like syndrome.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Human loss-of-function genetics: patient cells lack NSUN2 and lose m5C at C47/C48 of tRNA-Asp, confirming the substrate in vivo.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. High-throughput mRNA interactome capture; supports RNA binding but no NSUN2-specific conclusion.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. Second, independent mRNA-bound proteome survey.

title: Cytosolic YB-1 and NSUN2 are the only proteins recognizing specific motifs present in mRNAs enriched in exosomes.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. NSUN2 recognises one of three exosome-enrichment motifs and is present in HEK293 exosomes. Peripheral to the enzymatic function.

title: 5-methylcytosine promotes mRNA export - NSUN2 as the methyltransferase and ALYREF as an m(5)C reader.
review_notes: Full text available and read. The best-controlled of the mRNA m5C studies, because the export phenotype is rescued by wild-type but not methyltransferase-dead NSUN2.

title: Loss of 5-methylcytosine alters the biogenesis of vault-derived small RNAs to coordinate epidermal differentiation.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Establishes vault RNA VTRNA1.1 C69 as an NSUN2-exclusive substrate, a third non-mRNA substrate class.

title: NSUN2 introduces 5-methylcytosines in mammalian mitochondrial tRNAs.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Mitochondrial import by proximity labelling, plus mt-tRNA m5C in three genetic models. Also the source of the useful negative result that NSUN2 loss does not much perturb mitochondrial translation.

title: Mammalian NSUN2 introduces 5-methylcytidines into mitochondrial tRNAs.
review_notes: Full text available and read. In vitro reconstitution with purified NSUN2 and SAM, with product positions mapped by mass spectrometry - the strongest evidence for the core activity.

title: 5-methylcytosine promotes pathogenesis of bladder cancer through stabilizing mRNAs.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. Influential single-nucleotide mRNA m5C map in bladder cancer and the source of the YBX1 reader model. The site-level conclusions depend on bisulfite mapping whose specificity is questioned in PMID:42587746.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Full text available and read. BioPlex-style proteome-scale interactome; the resulting annotation is bare protein binding and carries no functional content.

title: Activity-based RNA-modifying enzyme probing reveals DUS3L-mediated dihydrouridylation.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Mechanism-based covalent capture plus oligo-dT selection, a rare piece of orthogonal evidence for mRNA methylation, and notable for stating its own polyA-purity caveat explicitly.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Full text available and read. High-throughput mitochondrial proteome; corroborative only.

title: The RNA methyltransferase NSUN2 catalyzes 5-methylcytosine (m(5)C) on IL1B mRNA to promote transcript stability.
review_notes: Full text available. Representative of the recent single-transcript m5C literature (IL1B, read by YBX1). Cited here as an example of the pattern, not as support for any annotation; no orthogonal, site-resolved validation is presented.

title: m5C Methylation of mRNA: Still More Questions Than Answers.
review_notes: Full text available and read. The main source for the methodological dispute recorded in this review. Note that it does not deny that NSUN2 methylates mRNA - it accepts NSUN2 and NSUN6 as the mRNA m5C writers - but it argues that the site maps, the stoichiometry and the reader mechanisms are unresolved.

title: NSUN2 methylates cytidine-40, cytidine-48, cytidine-49, cytidine-50 of tRNA(GLY)(GCC)
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing NSUN2 methylation of tRNA-Gly(GCC); consistent with the experimental literature.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The InterPro2GO mapping is correctly applied as a procedure, but IPR001678 fires on the NOL1/NOP2/Sun fold and cannot see that NSUN7's motif IV has lost the SAM-binding aspartate. The resulting methyltransferase-activity assertion is refuted by direct assay.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Transfer from mouse Nsun7 (UniProtKB:Q14AW5) is appropriate; the mouse phenotype and localisation data are strong and the human gene is a clear one-to-one orthologue.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Cytoplasm and motile cilium follow correctly from the UniProt subcellular location lines for this entry.

title: Sperm motility defects and infertility in male mice with a mutation in Nsun7, a member of the Sun domain-containing family of putative RNA methyltransferases.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. The founding ENU forward-genetic identification of Nsun7; note the authors already hedged with "putative RNA methyltransferases".

title: T26248G-transversion mutation in exon7 of the putative methyltransferase Nsun7 gene causes a change in protein folding associated with reduced sperm motility in asthenospermic men.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. Small candidate-gene association study in one Iranian cohort with in silico folding predictions rather than functional work; supports human relevance but should not be treated as establishing a mechanism.

title: Positioning of sperm tail longitudinal columns depends on NSUN7, an RNA-binding protein destabilizing elongated spermatid transcripts.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Source of the direct RNA-binding evidence (UV CLIP-seq from testis). Its own bisulfite sequencing found no NSUN7-dependent methylation that correlated with binding, which the authors state explicitly.

title: Testis-specific RNA methyltransferase NSUN7 contains a re-arranged catalytic site.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. Independent laboratory, and a stronger genetic design than a null - a knock-in of the putative catalytic cysteine to alanine, which produced no phenotype. Title still calls NSUN7 a methyltransferase while the content argues the opposite.

title: NSUN7-mediated m5C methylation of NLRP3 promotes pyroptosis in ovarian granulosa cells in polycystic ovary syndrome.
review_notes: Knockdown plus MeRIP and actinomycin D chase in a granulosa cell line. Catalysis is assumed rather than tested.

title: NSUN7-mediated m(5)C modification of circNTRK2 regulates stemness properties of glioblastoma cells by activating STK31.
review_notes: Uses the word "catalyzes" of a knockdown-plus-m5C-mapping result in glioblastoma lines. No direct test of catalysis, and NSUN7 is not appreciably expressed outside testis.

title: NSUN7 is a catalytically inactive RNA m(5)C methyltransferase essential for sperm flagellum assembly.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Decisive for catalytic inactivity - ITC on purified mouse and human NSUN domains plus transcriptome-wide m5C mass spectrometry and bisulfite sequencing in the knockout. The authors are also candid that they could not perform RIP or IP because no usable antibody was available, so the mechanism downstream of NSUN7 remains open.

title: NSUN7 Regulates Sperm Flagella Formation at All Stages of Spermiogenesis.
review_notes: Proteomics of sorted spermatid populations from Nsun7 knockout mice; supports a flagellar-assembly role and a protein-complex-stabilising model rather than an RNA-turnover model.

title: The m5C orchestrator NSUN7 drives SPARC/HMGB1 axis-mediated inflammation to exacerbate kidney injury.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache (PMC full text is publisher-restricted). Asserts that NSUN7 is the main driver of kidney m5C, which conflicts with the direct biochemistry and with the testis-restricted expression of NSUN7. A fall in bulk m5C after deleting a protein does not establish that the protein is the methyltransferase; the abstract reports no SAM binding, no in vitro methylation and no catalytically dead rescue.

title: Human cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase I: characterization and role in nucleoside analog resistance.
review_notes: Primary characterization of the human enzyme; PubMed-verified. Underlies the UniProt FUNCTION, catalytic activity, ADP activation and tissue-specificity calls.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome (Rolland 2014). Source of a bare protein-binding (NTAQ1) IPI; no NT5C1A-specific functional data.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Systematic SNV interaction-perturbation study (Fragoza 2019). Source of a bare protein-binding (NTAQ1) IPI; no NT5C1A-specific functional characterization.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome (Luck 2020). Source of bare protein-binding IPIs (CDC37, NTAQ1); systematic mapping only.

title: The decreased serum activity of cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase IA as a potential marker of breast cancer-associated muscle inflammation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; measures serum cN-IA activity and states the AMP->adenosine function and autoantigen role. Supports GO:0008253 and GO:0046085.

title: Regulation of the fatty acid composition of alkyl ether phospholipid in Ehrlich ascites tumor cells. The substrate specificities of 1-O-alkylglycerol 3-phosphate and 1-O-alkylglycero-3-phosphocholine acyltransferases.
review_notes: PMID:599155 (Waku & Nakazawa 1977, J Biochem) is an Ehrlich-ascites acyltransferase paper unrelated to NT5C1A. It is a transcription error in GOA for PMID:7599155 (Tavenier 1995, "Kinetics of adenylate metabolism in human and rat myocardium"), the paper UniProt actually cites (ECO:0000305|PubMed:7599155) for 5'-nucleotidase activity and cytoplasmic location. Annotations citing PMID:599155 are marked UNDECIDED pending correction of the identifier.

title: Kinetics of adenylate metabolism in human and rat myocardium.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the paper UniProt cites for cN-I 5'-nucleotidase activity and cytoplasmic location. This is the correct target of the mis-entered PMID:599155.

title: Soluble forms of 5'-nucleotidase in rat and human heart.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports GO:0008253 (IDA), GO:0000287 (Mg2+, IDA) and the adenosine-generation biological role in ischemic heart.

title: ATP and phosphate reciprocally affect subunit association of human recombinant High Km 5'-nucleotidase. Role for the C-terminal polyglutamic acid tract in subunit association and catalytic activity.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; establishes catalytic activity, ATP/phosphate regulation and the role of the C-terminal acidic tail in tetramer assembly. Consistent with the IDA annotations attributed to it.

title: Cytosolic and mitochondrial deoxyribonucleotidases: activity with substrate analogs, inhibitors and implications for therapy.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Supports 5'-nucleotidase activity on (deoxy)purine analog substrates and the drug-inactivation role.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Large-scale Y2H interactome screen; source of bare protein-binding IPI annotations only. Uninformative about molecular function.

title: Nucleoside phosphotransferase activity of human colon carcinoma cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Foundational characterization of both the 5'-nucleotidase and phosphotransferase activities and their allosteric activation.

title: Crystal structure of human cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase II: insights into allosteric regulation and substrate recognition.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; structural basis of catalysis and allosteric regulation.

title: An empirical framework for binary interactome mapping.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI annotation.

title: Structural basis for the allosteric regulation and substrate recognition of human cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase II.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; supports ATP binding (allosteric activator site), the homotetramer (identical protein binding), and Mg2+ dependence.

title: Suppression of 5'-nucleotidase enzymes promotes AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) phosphorylation and metabolism in human and mouse skeletal muscle.
review_notes: Full text available. Direct genetic (IMP) evidence for cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase activity and IMP catabolism; source of the MGI-curated BP/CC annotations.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome map; source of bare protein-binding IPI annotations.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Interactome community study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Binary interactome reference map; source of a bare protein-binding IPI annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Cell-specific interactome study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI annotation.

title: TRIM22 orchestrates the proliferation of GBMs and the benefits of TMZ by coordinating the modification and degradation of RIG-I.
review_notes: Full text available. Sole source of the ubiquitin-ligase (GO:0061630), K48-linked ubiquitination (GO:0070936) and antiviral (GO:0050689) annotations. This is a moonlighting claim well outside the enzyme's HAD-fold metabolic role (no recognizable E3 domain; interaction with RIG-I is indirect via TRIM22) and is not independently corroborated; treated as a likely over-annotation.

title: Molecular cloning of human cytosolic purine 5'-nucleotidase.
review_notes: Original cloning of human NT5C2; basis of the TAS 5'-nucleotidase activity annotation.

title: Bovine cytosolic IMP/GMP-specific 5'-nucleotidase: cloning and expression of active enzyme in Escherichia coli.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Bovine ortholog 99.5% identical to human; curator source for several IDA annotations on the human enzyme (5'-nucleotidase, phosphotransferase, cytosol, IMP/GMP metabolic).

title: carbovir + IMP => carbovir monophosphate + inosine
review_notes: Reactome reaction (abacavir/carbovir metabolism) placing NT5C2 in the cytosol; illustrates the phosphotransferase activity on a nucleoside-analog prodrug.

title: (d)GMP or (d)IMP + H2O => (2'-deoxy)guanosine or (2'-deoxy)inosine + orthophosphate (NT5C2)
review_notes: Reactome reaction capturing the core (d)GMP/(d)IMP dephosphorylation by NT5C2 in the cytosol.

title: NT5C2 tetramer phosphorylates RBV
review_notes: Reactome reaction (ribavirin metabolism); NT5C2 tetramer, cytosol.

title: NT5C2 tetramer dephosphorylates RBV-MP
review_notes: Reactome reaction (ribavirin metabolism); NT5C2 tetramer dephosphorylating ribavirin monophosphate in the cytosol.

title: Human erythrocyte pyrimidine 5-nucleotidase, PN-I, is identical to p36, a protein associated to lupus inclusion formation in response to alpha-interferon.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes PN-I (= NT5C3A) as an active pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase and its identity with p36. Supports the 5'-nucleotidase MF calls.

title: Human erythrocyte pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase, PN-I.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (abstract only). Primary biochemical characterization; underpins the 5'-nucleotidase MF, Mg2+ dependence, and UMP/CMP/dTMP/dUMP catabolic-process annotations (all curated by MGI from this paper).

title: Molecular characterization of six unrelated Italian patients affected by pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; disease/genetics context confirming the physiological importance of the enzyme's pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase activity.

title: Evidence for essential catalytic determinants for human erythrocyte pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the EXP source for the 5'-nucleotidase activity annotation. Defines the HAD catalytic mechanism and separates nucleotidase from phosphotransferase activity.

title: A diverse range of gene products are effectors of the type I interferon antiviral response.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. NT5C3A ("NT5C3") appears only as a weak/non-hit in the screen; the "defense response to virus" IDA is at best a peripheral role, not core.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; high-throughput binary interactome. Supports only uninformative "protein binding"; interactors match the UniProt INTERACTION block.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. HTP spatial-proteome hit; inconsistent with the well-established cytosolic localization, so treated as non-core.

title: Purification, microsequencing, and immunolocalization of p36, a new interferon-alpha-induced protein that is associated with human lupus inclusions.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of the ER/cytoplasm IDA localization. ER localization is isoform-2-specific.

title: Pyrimidine nucleotidases from human erythrocyte possess phosphotransferase activities specific for pyrimidine nucleotides.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cited as support for GO:0000215 (tRNA 2'-phosphotransferase activity), but the paper describes a pyrimidine-nucleotide phosphotransferase, not a tRNA 2'-phosphotransferase; the GO:0000215 annotation is a mis-mapping.

title: (d)CMP, TMP, or (d)UMP + H2O => (deoxy)cytidine, thymidine, or (deoxy)uridine + orthophosphate (NT5C3)
review_notes: Reactome pathway step consistent with the enzyme's core catalytic reaction and cytosolic location.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; supports only a secondary exosomal localization of CD73.

title: Quantitative proteomics identifies a Dab2/integrin module regulating cell migration.
review_notes: Cell-surface proteomics dataset; supports cell-surface localization only.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: Exosome proteomics; supports only secondary exosomal localization.

title: Primary structure of human placental 5'-nucleotidase and identification of the glycolipid anchor in the mature form.
review_notes: Primary structure paper; establishes the 574-aa sequence, signal peptide, and C-terminal GPI (glycophospholipid) membrane anchor. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Protein profile of exosomes from trabecular meshwork cells.
review_notes: Exosome proteomics; secondary localization only.

title: The high-resolution crystal structure of periplasmic Haemophilus influenzae NAD nucleotidase reveals a novel enzymatic function of human CD73 related to NAD metabolism.
review_notes: Title foregrounds H. influenzae NadN but the study also demonstrates human CD73 processes NAD and NMN, extending its substrate scope. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Crystal structure of a soluble form of human CD73 with ecto-5'-nucleotidase activity.
review_notes: Human soluble CD73 crystal structure retaining ecto-5'-nucleotidase activity; dimerization, Zn2+ site, glycosylation. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Crystal structure of the human ecto-5'-nucleotidase (CD73): insights into the regulation of purinergic signaling.
review_notes: Human e5NT crystal structures; establishes AMP-to-adenosine hydrolysis as the major control point for extracellular adenosine and the open/closed conformational switch. Abstract-only in cache.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Exosome proteomics; secondary localization only.

title: NT5E mutations that cause human disease are associated with intracellular mistrafficking of NT5E protein.
review_notes: Full text in cache. CALJA disease mutants mistraffic and lack surface AMPase activity; wild-type NT5E traffics to and is active at the plasma membrane.

title: Adenosine derived from ecto-nucleotidases in calcific aortic valve disease promotes mineralization through A2a adenosine receptor.
review_notes: CD73-derived adenosine promotes VIC mineralization via A2aR; supports biomineral tissue development and response-to-ATP annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Ectopic calcification in pseudoxanthoma elasticum responds to inhibition of tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase.
review_notes: Full text in cache; study is about ABCC6/PXE and TNAP inhibition. Cited for a CD73 5'-nucleotidase activity IDA (via MGI) but the abstract does not detail the CD73 assay; the annotated function is nonetheless correct and redundant.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Systematic yeast two-hybrid interactome (Luck et al. 2020); source of the CD73 protein-binding IPI to ZNRF4/RNF24, also listed in UniProt. Generic protein binding is uninformative about function.

title: Substrate binding modes of purine and pyrimidine nucleotides to human ecto-5'-nucleotidase (CD73) and inhibition by their bisphosphonic acid derivatives.
review_notes: Structural/kinetic characterization of AMP and other mono-/deoxyribonucleotide substrates; AMP is the best substrate, ribonucleotides favoured over deoxyribonucleotides. Abstract-only in cache.

title: CD73 is involved in lymphocyte binding to the endothelium: characterization of lymphocyte-vascular adhesion protein 2 identifies it as CD73.
review_notes: Identifies L-VAP-2 as CD73 and demonstrates its adhesion function (lymphocyte binding to endothelium) plus ecto-5'-nucleotidase activity. Abstract + short full text in cache.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline. Correctly recovers family-level MF/BP terms (ATP binding, Fe-S binding, ATP-dependent FeS chaperone activity, Fe-S cluster assembly). The generic parent GO:0051536 is redundant with the specific GO:0051539.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/IBA pipeline; correctly recovers the core functions (4Fe-4S binding, Complex I assembly, Fe-S cluster assembly, mitochondrial localization).

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SubCell keyword mapping to mitochondrion; correct but generic relative to the matrix-specific localization.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: HPA immunofluorescence supporting mitochondrial localization (IDA).

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learning annotations for mitochondrial matrix localization and Complex I assembly; consistent with experimental and Reactome evidence.

title: Nogo-B receptor stabilizes Niemann-Pick type C2 protein and regulates intracellular cholesterol trafficking.

title: Endothelial miR-26a regulates VEGF-Nogo-B receptor-mediated angiogenesis.
