title: PETA and CTP are condensed to CDP-ETA by PCY2
review_notes: Correctly captures the catalyzed reaction, but localizes ET to the ER membrane as a membrane-bound dimer, which conflicts with its established soluble cytosolic nature; basis for marking the ER-membrane CC annotation as over-annotated.

title: Structural basis for flip-flop action of thiamin pyrophosphate-dependent enzymes revealed by human pyruvate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Crystal structure of holo human E1 (alpha2beta2) with Mg2+ and TPP; establishes the TPP/Mg2+ cofactor site and the alpha-beta heterotetramer. Interaction PMID for the PDHA1-PDHB IntAct entry.

title: Phosphorylation of serine 264 impedes active site accessibility in the E1 component of the human pyruvate dehydrogenase multienzyme complex.
review_notes: Kinetic + structural study of human E1 and the S264 phospho-variant; supports the EXP pyruvate dehydrogenase activity annotation and phospho-regulation.

title: Structural basis for inactivation of the human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex by phosphorylation: role of disordered phosphorylation loops.
review_notes: Full text available; defines the E1p reactions, PDC overall reaction, matrix context, phosphorylation sites, and Km for pyruvate. Primary support for MF/BP/CC core annotations.

title: Subunit and catalytic component stoichiometries of an in vitro reconstituted human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Reconstituted human PDC stoichiometry; supports PDHA1 (E1p heterotetramer) as part of the assembled complex.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
review_notes: Mitochondrial phosphoproteome of human muscle; supports mitochondrial localization (HDA) but is high-throughput.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Sperm-nucleus proteome; the PDHA1 nucleus HDA is a single high-throughput detection in a specialized cell type and does not establish a physiological nuclear function for the mitochondrial matrix enzyme.

title: Component co-expression and purification of recombinant human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex from baculovirus infected SF9 cells.
review_notes: Functional recombinant human PDC; supports the pyruvate-to-acetyl-CoA process and mitochondrial-enzyme identity.

title: A Map of Human Mitochondrial Protein Interactions Linked to Neurodegeneration Reveals New Mechanisms of Redox Homeostasis and NF-κB Signaling.
review_notes: Large-scale mitochondrial interactome; PDHA1 interactions (PDHB, IMMT) are high-throughput and captured better as complex membership than as protein binding.

title: An AP-MS- and BioID-compatible MAC-tag enables comprehensive mapping of protein interactions and subcellular localizations.
review_notes: AP-MS/BioID methods paper; PDHA1-PDK1 IntAct entry; high-throughput evidence for a known regulatory contact.

title: The human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. Isolation of cDNA clones for the E1 alpha subunit, sequence analysis, and characterization of the mRNA.
review_notes: Original human E1alpha cDNA/protein characterization; establishes EC 1.2.4.1 identity and mitochondrial import leader / matrix maturation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome (BioPlex); PDHA1-PDHB IntAct entry; high-throughput.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP high-confidence mitochondrial proteome; supports mitochondrial localization (HTP).

title: CFTR interactome mapping using the mammalian membrane two-hybrid high-throughput screening system.
review_notes: Membrane two-hybrid CFTR screen; PDHA1-CFTR contact of uncertain physiological relevance; uninformative protein-binding annotation.

title: Differential CFTR-Interactome Proximity Labeling Procedures Identify Enrichment in Multiple SLC Transporters.
review_notes: CFTR proximity-labeling study; PDHA1-CFTR contact; high-throughput, uninformative MF term.

title: Mutagenesis studies of the phosphorylation sites of recombinant human pyruvate dehydrogenase. Site-specific regulation.
review_notes: Mutagenesis of E1alpha phosphorylation sites; supports EXP pyruvate dehydrogenase activity and phospho-regulation; also the PDHA1-PDK1 IntAct entry.

title: Structural basis for flip-flop action of thiamin pyrophosphate-dependent enzymes revealed by human pyruvate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Crystal structure of the alpha2beta2 human E1 (PDB 1NI4); establishes the TPP-dependent, heterotetrameric E1 that PDHB forms with PDHA1. Verbatim quote confirmed in cached abstract.

title: Mutations of the E1beta subunit gene (PDHB) in four families with pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency.
review_notes: Directly ties PDHB loss-of-function variants to reduced PDC activity in PDC-deficiency patients; supports the E1 activity and disease link. Abstract-only cache but the assayed gene is PDHB.

title: Binding of pyruvate dehydrogenase to the core of the human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Maps the E1beta C-terminal surface residues that dock E1 onto the E2 (DLAT) core; supports the E1beta-E2 interaction underlying the protein-binding IPI.

title: Structural basis for inactivation of the human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex by phosphorylation: role of disordered phosphorylation loops.
review_notes: Full-text source establishing E1-catalysed TPP-dependent decarboxylation of pyruvate and reductive acetylation of the E2 lipoyl group; PDC as the gateway linking glycolysis to the TCA cycle. Anchors core_functions.

title: Subunit and catalytic component stoichiometries of an in vitro reconstituted human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Defines PDC subunit and catalytic stoichiometry (40 E2p, 20 E3BP, 40 E1p, 20 E3); demonstrates E1 (PDHB-containing) incorporation into the assembled complex.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Large-scale sperm-nucleus proteomics; the single PDHB hit underlies the nucleus annotation, best interpreted as dataset over-annotation for this mitochondrial matrix enzyme.

title: Isolation of tryptic fragment of antigen from mitochondrial inner membrane proteins reacting with antimitochondrial antibody in sera of patients with primary biliary cirrhosis.
review_notes: UniProt cites this paper for direct protein sequencing of mature PDHB (residues 31-55) and the mitochondrion is_active_in IDA; the cached abstract foregrounds an E2 subunit-binding domain, but the curated PDHB protein sequence is the load-bearing evidence.

title: Characterization of two cDNA clones for pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 beta subunit and its regulation in tricarboxylic acid cycle-deficient fibroblast.
review_notes: Early characterization of human PDH E1beta cDNA; source of the E1 activity TAS and (over-broad) TCA-cycle TAS annotations.

title: Component co-expression and purification of recombinant human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex from baculovirus infected SF9 cells.
review_notes: Recombinant functional human PDC (all components co-expressed); supports PDHB's role in the pyruvate-to-acetyl-CoA reaction within the assembled complex.

title: A Map of Human Mitochondrial Protein Interactions Linked to Neurodegeneration Reveals New Mechanisms of Redox Homeostasis and NF-κB Signaling.
review_notes: Large-scale mitochondrial interactome; recovers the PDHB-PDHA1 interaction underlying one protein-binding IPI. Not specific to PDHB function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex proteome-scale interactome; recovers PDHB interactions with PDHA1 and DLAT underlying two protein-binding IPIs. Background/contextual for gene function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteome; corroborates mitochondrial localization of PDHB but at low specificity.

title: How dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase-binding protein binds dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase in the human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Crystal structure of the E3BP E3-binding domain with DLD (E3); directly establishes the E3-anchoring/structural-core function. PubMed-verified.

title: Structural insight into interactions between dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase (E3) and E3 binding protein of human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Second crystal structure + hot-spot mutagenesis of the E3BP/E3 interface; supports the tethering function. PubMed-verified.

title: Subunit and catalytic component stoichiometries of an in vitro reconstituted human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Explicitly describes E3BP as a "noncatalytic component" that tethers E3 dimers to the PDC; key evidence for the non-catalytic structural role.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.
review_notes: Methods paper for a high-throughput Y2H interactome; source of an uninformative AGTRAP protein-binding hit.

title: Component co-expression and purification of recombinant human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex from baculovirus infected SF9 cells.
review_notes: Recombinant reconstitution of functional human PDC (including E3BP); supports involvement in pyruvate decarboxylation as a complex subunit.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale binary interactome; source of an uninformative AGTRAP hit.

title: Sirtuin 4 is a lipoamidase regulating pyruvate dehydrogenase complex activity.
review_notes: Establishes PDHX as a lipoylated structural subunit and SIRT4 lipoamidase substrate (Lys97); relevant to regulation, not to a catalytic MF.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex AP-MS interactome; captures the DLD interaction as a generic hit.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Variant/interaction-disruption screen; source of an uninformative AGTRAP hit.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference interactome; DLD hit consistent with biology, CIDEB uncharacterized.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 interactome; captures the DLD interaction as a generic hit.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; corroborates mitochondrial localization.

title: Dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase-binding protein of the human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. DNA-derived amino acid sequence, expression, and reconstitution of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Primary characterization: E3BP anchors E3 to the E2 core; catalytic His replaced by Ser so acetyltransferase catalysis is unlikely. Foundational.

title: Characterization of solanesyl and decaprenyl diphosphate synthases in mice and humans.
review_notes: Abstract-only in local cache (full_text_available: false). PubMed-verified as the primary characterization of human PDSS1/PDSS2; directly supports the decaprenyl-diphosphate synthase activity, heterotetramer, and ubiquinone-biosynthesis annotations.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Full text cached. Large-scale mitochondrial proteome; PDSS1 is part of the proteome dataset rather than named in prose, consistent with the HTP localization annotation.

title: PDSS1,2 ligates FPP to IPPP
review_notes: Reactome curation consistent with UniProt and Saiki et al. 2005; supports the matrix localization and the reaction catalyzed by the heterotetramer.

title: Characterization of solanesyl and decaprenyl diphosphate synthases in mice and humans.
review_notes: Primary characterization of human PDSS1 (hDPS1) and PDSS2 (hDLP1); establishes the heterotetramer, in vitro decaprenyl diphosphate synthase activity, Q10 production, and joint chain-length determination. Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available false); all supporting quotes taken verbatim from the abstract.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome; supports the mitochondrial localization (HTP) of PDSS2. Full text available in cache; PDSS2 is a dataset entry rather than a highlighted finding.

title: PDSS1,2 ligates FPP to IPPP
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the PDSS1/PDSS2 heterotetramer condensing FPP with IPP to all-trans-decaprenyl diphosphate in the mitochondrial matrix; supports the complex, activity, and matrix-localization annotations.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline; correctly assigns the core PLP salvage process from the pyridoxal kinase InterPro signature.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/IBA pipeline; correctly recovers the core kinase activity, cytosolic location, and PLP salvage process.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SubCell mapping; correctly transfers the curated cytosolic location.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: HPA immunofluorescence pipeline; yields a nucleoplasm localization that is not the core (cytosolic) location for this enzyme.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA model; assigns the broader vitamin B6 metabolic process, a correct but general parent of PLP salvage.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined IEA (InterPro/EC/RHEA); correctly assigns the core kinase activity.

title: Human pyridoxal kinase: overexpression and properties of the recombinant enzyme.
review_notes: Primary characterization of the recombinant human enzyme; establishes kinase activity, Zn2+ preference, and kinetic parameters. Note the MBP-fusion form is an active monomer.

title: Crystal structure of human pyridoxal kinase.
review_notes: Crystal structure supporting ATP binding and homodimeric assembly.

title: Cell array-based intracellular localization screening reveals novel functional features of human chromosome 21 proteins.
review_notes: High-throughput chromosome-21 localization screen supporting a cytosolic (HDA) localization; a bulk screen, not a PDXK-focused study.

title: Crystal Structure of human pyridoxal kinase: structural basis of M(+) and M(2+) activation.
review_notes: Key structural/kinetic study establishing substrate scope, ATP/Mg2+ binding, the monovalent-cation site, and the homodimer.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Bulk urinary-exosome proteome (1132 proteins); source of the extracellular exosome HDA annotation, a bystander capture of an abundant cytosolic enzyme.

title: Kinetic and structural studies of the role of the active site residue Asp235 of human pyridoxal kinase.
review_notes: Mutagenesis/structural study identifying the catalytic proton-acceptor Asp235; EXP support for the core kinase activity.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Bulk sperm-nucleus MS catalogue (403 proteins); source of the nucleus HDA annotation, not evidence of a nuclear function.

title: PDXK mutations cause polyneuropathy responsive to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate supplementation.
review_notes: Disease-gene discovery with functional validation; IMP support for the kinase activity and PLP salvage process, and clinical proof of physiological role.

title: Human pyridoxal kinase. cDNA cloning, expression, and modulation by ligands of the benzodiazepine receptor.
review_notes: Original cloning/characterization of human PDXK; establishes identity, kinetics, tissue distribution, and cytosolic location.

title: Kinetic studies of the effects of K+, Na+ and Li+ on the catalytic activity of human erythrocyte pyridoxal kinase.
review_notes: Kinetic study of the monovalent-cation activation (K+/Na+/Li+); supports the regulatory cation-binding annotations (Li+ only a poor activator).

title: Exocytosis of secretory granule lumen proteins
review_notes: Neutrophil-degranulation secretome pathway; source of extracellular/granule annotations that are bystander localizations for a cytosolic enzyme.

title: Exocytosis of specific granule lumen proteins
review_notes: Neutrophil-degranulation secretome pathway (specific granule); bystander extracellular/granule localizations.

title: 2xPDXK:2xZn2+ phosphorylates PXA
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the B6 activation pathway (pyridoxamine phosphorylation); captures the core cytosolic kinase reaction.

title: 2xPDKX:2xZn2+ phosphorylates PDX
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the B6 activation pathway (pyridoxine phosphorylation); core cytosolic kinase reaction.

title: 2xPDXK:2xZn2+ phosphorylates PXL
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the B6 activation pathway (pyridoxal phosphorylation); core cytosolic kinase reaction.

title: Human pyridoxal phosphatase. Molecular cloning, functional expression, and tissue distribution.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary molecular cloning/characterization of human PDXP; direct source of the pyridoxal phosphatase (GO:0033883) and PLP catabolic (GO:0032361) annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Chronophin, a novel HAD-type serine protein phosphatase, regulates cofilin-dependent actin dynamics.
review_notes: PubMed-verified discovery paper for the cofilin (protein-serine) phosphatase moonlighting activity; source of the GO:0004721/GO:0004722 protein-phosphatase and actin-regulation annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Beta-arrestin-dependent regulation of the cofilin pathway downstream of protease-activated receptor-2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports the cofilin-pathway scaffolding context and a beta-arrestin interaction (source of the IntAct GO:0005515 IPI). The bare protein-binding term is uninformative. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Chronophin mediates an ATP-sensing mechanism for cofilin dephosphorylation and neuronal cofilin-actin rod formation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Source of the Hsp90 (heat shock protein) binding, actin rod assembly and cellular response to ATP annotations; establishes the ATP-sensing regulatory switch over the cofilin phosphatase activity.

title: Identification of an essential cysteine residue in pyridoxal phosphatase from human erythrocytes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the classical human erythrocyte pyridoxal-phosphatase biochemistry underpinning the GO:0033883 / GO:0032361 annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Fusion of the human gene for the polyubiquitination coeffector UEV1 with Kua, a newly identified gene.
review_notes: Original description of the Kua gene (= PEDS1/TMEM189) and the Kua-UEV (PEDS1-UBE2V1) fusion. Abstract reports cytoplasmic localization of Kua; the ER-membrane EXP annotation and UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION citation rest on the full text (not in cache). Predates identification of the desaturase function.

title: A bacterial light response reveals an orphan desaturase for human plasmalogen synthesis.
review_notes: Identified the orphan human plasmanylethanolamine desaturase via the bacterial CarF homolog; TMEM189 knockout eliminated cellular plasmalogens and human TMEM189 rescued CarF function. Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available: false), but the abstract directly supports the MF and BP claims.

title: The TMEM189 gene encodes plasmanylethanolamine desaturase which introduces the characteristic vinyl ether double bond into plasmalogens.
review_notes: Independent identification of TMEM189 as PEDS; knockout/knockdown, mouse KO, substrate accumulation, and essentiality of the eight conserved histidines. Full text available. Cites historic EC 1.14.99.19; current UniProt/Rhea EC is 1.14.19.77.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Source of the IntAct protein-binding IPI (LAMP2, SH3GLB1) from a large-scale yeast two-hybrid neurodegeneration interactome. Binary high-throughput interactions only; no functional interpretation for PEDS1.

title: Dissociation by Pelota, Hbs1 and ABCE1 of mammalian vacant 80S ribosomes and stalled elongation complexes.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches; establishes the PELO-HBS1L-ABCE1 ribosome dissociation/recycling activity (anchors GO:0043022 ribosome binding IDA in GOA).

title: The Hbs1-Dom34 protein complex functions in non-stop mRNA decay in mammalian cells.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches; establishes PELO-HBS1L role in non-stop mRNA decay (GO:0070966).

title: Conserved functions of human Pelota in mRNA quality control of nonstop mRNA.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches; mutational analysis establishes human PELO's stalled-ribosome rescue function in nonstop mRNA QC.

title: Decoding Mammalian Ribosome-mRNA States by Translational GTPase Complexes.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches; cryo-EM structural evidence supports the stalled-ribosome sensor activity (GO:0170011 IDA in GOA).

title: Insufficient glucose supply is linked to hypothermia upon cold exposure in high-fat diet-fed mice lacking PEMT.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Mouse Pemt-null study; basis for the ISS transfer to human of GO:0120162 (positive regulation of cold-induced thermogenesis). Supports an indirect, whole-organism physiological phenotype rather than a direct molecular function of PEMT. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Identification of three novel cDNAs for human phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase and localization of the human gene on chromosome 17p11.2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cloned/expressed human PEMT cDNAs showing 27-115-fold elevation of PEMT activity and mapped the gene to 17p11.2; directly supports the core molecular function (GO:0004608). Abstract-only in cache.

title: Iterative orthology prediction uncovers new mitochondrial proteins and identifies C12orf62 as the human ortholog of COX14, a protein involved in the assembly of cytochrome c oxidase.
review_notes: Ortho-Profile study predicting PET100 (LOC100131801) as the human ortholog of yeast Pet100p (COX assembly factor) and experimentally co-purifying COX subunit VIIa (COX7A2) specifically with PET100, corroborating the conserved Pet100p-VIIa interaction in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Full text available and verified.

title: A founder mutation in PET100 causes isolated complex IV deficiency in Lebanese individuals with Leigh syndrome.
review_notes: Establishes PET100 (C19orf79) as the causal gene for isolated complex IV deficiency / Leigh syndrome via a founder c.3G>C (p.Met1?) mutation, confirmed by lentiviral phenotypic correction. Shows PET100 is located in the mitochondrial inner membrane and forms a ~300 kDa subcomplex with complex IV subunits. Cached abstract is abstract-only (full_text_available: false) but PMID/title verified and the quoted localization statement is verbatim in the cached record.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome (MitoCoP); source of independent HTP support for PET100's mitochondrial localization.

title: UniProtKB entry P0DJ07 (PT100_HUMAN)
review_notes: UniProt record for PET100; FUNCTION ("essential role in mitochondrial complex IV maturation and assembly"), SUBUNIT (interacts with COX7A2), inner-membrane SUBCELLULAR LOCATION, single-pass membrane topology, and MC4DN12 disease association used as supporting evidence.

title: Iterative orthology prediction uncovers new mitochondrial proteins and identifies C12orf62 as the human ortholog of COX14, a protein involved in the assembly of cytochrome c oxidase.
review_notes: Identifies human PET117 as the ortholog of yeast PET117 (COX assembly), shows GFP-PET117 mitochondrial co-localization, and co-purifies COX17 with PET117-TAP. Directly establishes PET117's mitochondrial localization and link to COX assembly.

title: MR-1S Interacts with PET100 and PET117 in Module-Based Assembly of Human Cytochrome c Oxidase.
review_notes: Places PET117 with the conserved PET100 chaperone (and MR-1S) in module-based human COX assembly. Cache is abstract-only, but the abstract supports the complex IV assembly role; underlies the experimental IDA to GO:0033617.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome; PET117 membership corroborates mitochondrial localization (HTP).

title: PET117 assembly factor stabilizes translation activator TACO1 thereby upregulates mitochondria-encoded cytochrome C oxidase 1 synthesis.
review_notes: Shows PET117 is a complex IV assembly chaperone that stabilizes TACO1 to promote COX1 synthesis; PET117 depletion impairs mitochondrial respiration. Cache is abstract-only but the abstract supports both the assembly role and the phenotype.

title: UniProtKB entry Q6UWS5 (PET117, Protein PET117 homolog, mitochondrial)
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; source for the Mitochondrion subcellular location, the PET117 family membership, the transit peptide, and the MC4DN19 disease association.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Large-scale binary interactome resource. Correctly cited as the source of five IPI protein binding rows, but the partners have no established peroxisomal connection and the paper says nothing about PEX39 function.

title: An interactome perturbation framework prioritizes damaging missense mutations for developmental disorders.
review_notes: High-throughput interaction source only; no functional information about PEX39.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: High-throughput interaction source only; no functional information about PEX39.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome; high-throughput interaction source only.

title: PEX39 facilitates the peroxisomal import of PTS2-containing proteins.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed as Chen WW et al., Nat Cell Biol 2025 Aug;27(8):1256-1271, doi 10.1038/s41556-025-01711-z, PMC12339391; full text cached. This is the sole primary source for every functional claim about PEX39 and it is a strong one - in vitro reconstitution with recombinant proteins, yeast genetics and human knockout cells, from three independent peroxisome laboratories. It is nevertheless a single paper, and the co-receptor role of PEX39 has not yet been independently replicated.

title: Human phosphoribosylformylglycineamide amidotransferase (FGARAT): regional mapping, complete coding sequence, isolation of a functional genomic clone, and DNA sequence analysis.
review_notes: Cloning/complementation paper for human FGARAT/PFAS; establishes the enzyme as step four of de novo purine synthesis and demonstrates catalytic function by AdeB CHO complementation. Source of the IDA MF and NAS BP annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: B-cell exosome proteomics (539 proteins). PFAS is a bulk-catalog hit; supports only the over-annotated extracellular-exosome CC, not a functional role.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 induced mutations along de novo purine synthesis in HeLa cells result in accumulation of individual enzyme substrates and affect purinosome formation.
review_notes: CRISPR knockouts of individual DNPS enzymes in HeLa; substrate accumulation and impaired purinosome assembly. Source of the MGI IMP/IDA annotations. Abstract frames DNPS at the pathway level without naming PFAS; full text (uncached) assays the FGAR-AT step, so deferring to the MGI curator.

title: The a-subunit of the V-type H+-ATPase interacts with phosphofructokinase-1 in humans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports a kidney alpha-intercalated-cell apical plasma membrane localization and PFK1-V-ATPase a-subunit interaction; peripheral to the core muscle enzyme function.

title: Toward an understanding of the protein interaction network of the human liver.
review_notes: High-throughput liver interactome map; source of an uninformative bare protein binding IPI.

title: Crystallization and preliminary crystallographic analysis of human muscle phosphofructokinase, the main regulator of glycolysis.
review_notes: Full text available. Directly characterizes human muscle PFK as an M4 tetramer and describes the reaction and allosteric regulation; strongly supports complex, catalytic and glycolysis annotations.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: HuRI systematic binary interactome; source of uninformative protein binding / identical protein binding IPIs.

title: Aerobic glycolysis tunes YAP/TAZ transcriptional activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes a moonlighting PFK1-TEAD/YAP-TAZ transcriptional role and nuclear localization in proliferating cells; supports the enzymatic activity but the transcriptional/nuclear annotations are context-specific and non-core.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 AP-MS interactome; source of an uninformative bare protein binding IPI.

title: Characterization of the enzymatic defect in late-onset muscle phosphofructokinase deficiency. New subtype of glycogen storage disease type VII.
review_notes: Characterizes muscle PFK deficiency (GSD VII); supports the muscle 6-phosphofructokinase activity annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 AP-MS interactome; source of an uninformative bare protein binding IPI.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: High-throughput PDZ/affinity interactome mapping; source of uninformative bare protein binding IPIs (many PDZ-domain partners).

title: The molecular mechanism of the inherited phosphofructokinase deficiency associated with hemolysis and myopathy.
review_notes: Establishes that the M subunit is absent in Tarui disease and that muscle PFK activity is lost; supports the IMP/IDA activity, complex, and muscle homeostasis annotations.

title: Isozymes of human phosphofructokinase: identification and subunit structural characterization of a new system.
review_notes: Defines the M/L subunit tetramer system (M4, M3L, M2L2, ML3, L4); supports complex assembly, identical/kinase binding, and 6-phosphofructokinase activity annotations.

title: Isozymes of human phosphofructokinase in blood cells and cultured cell lines: molecular and genetic evidence for a trigenic system.
review_notes: Abstract-only cached record supporting the trigenic (M/L/P) PFK system; Reactome-sourced EXP support for muscle 6-phosphofructokinase activity.

title: Functional expression of human mutant phosphofructokinase in yeast: genetic defects in French Canadian and Swiss patients with phosphofructokinase deficiency.
review_notes: Reconstitutes human PFK-M activity in a PFK-null yeast system; the Gly209Asp GSD VII variant is completely inactive, directly supporting the 6-phosphofructokinase activity annotation.

title: Isozyme analysis of human polymorphonuclear leukocyte phosphofructokinase from insulin resistant individuals.
review_notes: Measures M-type isozyme activity, F-6-P affinity and ATP inhibition; supports the IDA activity, ATP binding and fructose binding annotations.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Sperm-nucleus proteome; PGAM detected as one of 403 proteins. Supports the nucleus HDA localization but is a high-throughput co-detection with no functional nuclear role; over-annotation for a cytosolic enzyme.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Exosome proteome from prostatic secretions; PGAM detected as a high-throughput co-purifying protein. Supports the exosome HDA localization only; over-annotation.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 AP-MS interactome; source of a PGAM2-BPGM protein-binding IPI. Supports only generic protein binding, not a specific molecular function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary (Y2H) interactome; source of protein-binding IPIs and the PGAM2 self-interaction (identical protein binding), consistent with the homodimer.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 AP-MS interactome; source of a PGAM2-BPGM protein-binding IPI. Generic protein binding only.

title: Phosphoglycerate mutase isozyme marker for tissue differentiation in man.
review_notes: Foundational characterization of human PGAM isozymes (M vs B subunits) as tissue-differentiation markers; underpins the EXP phosphoglycerate mutase activity annotation.

title: Human muscle phosphoglycerate mutase deficiency: newly discovered metabolic myopathy.
review_notes: First description of human muscle PGAM deficiency (GSD X): muscle PGAM activity 5.7% of control, residual activity is BB isozyme, implicating the M subunit. Directly supports the core catalytic and glycolytic roles of PGAM2; the muscle-contraction annotation from this paper is a downstream phenotype.

title: Exome sequencing links corticospinal motor neuron disease to common neurodegenerative disorders.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt as a second reference implicating PGAP1 in the inherited disorder; corroborates disease relevance rather than molecular function.

title: Null mutation in PGAP1 impairing Gpi-anchor maturation in patients with intellectual disability and encephalopathy.
review_notes: Full text available and PubMed-verified; directly establishes PGAP1 function, its ER localization, the post-attachment inositol-deacylation, and the human disease phenotype. Supporting quotes verified as verbatim substrings.

title: Molecular basis of the inositol deacylase PGAP1 involved in quality control of GPI-AP biogenesis.
review_notes: Full text available and PubMed-verified; structural/biochemical study of the inositol-deacylase and its role in GPI-AP quality control and ER export. Supporting quotes verified as verbatim substrings.

title: uPAR-acyl-GPI + H2O -> uPAR + long-chain fatty acid
review_notes: Reactome reaction directly representing PGAP1 deacylase activity; title left exactly as fetched.

title: Attachment of GPI anchor to uPAR
review_notes: Reactome pathway grouping the deacylation reaction under GPI attachment; title left exactly as fetched.

title: Human FRAG1 encodes a novel membrane-spanning protein that localizes to chromosome 11p15.5, a region of frequent loss of heterozygosity in cancer.
review_notes: Original cloning of FRAG1 (=PGAP2); establishes multi-pass membrane topology and ubiquitous expression. Golgi assignment is from the full text / curated record (abstract does not state Golgi). Basis for the EXP Golgi and TAS membrane annotations.

title: Hypomorphic mutations in PGAP2, encoding a GPI-anchor-remodeling protein, cause autosomal-recessive intellectual disability.
review_notes: Direct functional evidence - CHO rescue with WT vs mutant PGAP2 alters surface DAF/CD59; establishes HPMRS3. Basis for the IDA GPI-anchor annotation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome map; source of a single uninformative protein-binding IPI. Does not inform PGAP2's molecular function.

title: Widespread Expansion of Protein Interaction Capabilities by Alternative Splicing.
review_notes: Alternative-splicing interactome screen; source of an uninformative protein-binding IPI. Does not inform PGAP2's molecular function.

title: Identification of a Golgi GPI-N-acetylgalactosamine transferase with tandem transmembrane regions in the catalytic domain.
review_notes: Primarily a PGAP4 paper, but the full text gives the clearest verbatim description of PGAP2's role (Golgi reacylation with stearic acid after PGAP3); cited for the IMP GPI-anchor annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference Y2H interactome; source of multiple uninformative protein-binding IPIs on isoform 5. Does not inform PGAP2's molecular function.

title: UniProtKB entry Q9UHJ9 (PGAP2_HUMAN)
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; source of the fatty-acid remodeling function, Golgi apparatus membrane localization, multi-pass topology, and HPMRS3 disease association. Quotes verified as verbatim substrings.

title: Identification of the CAB2/hCOS16 gene required for the repair of DNA double-strand breaks on a core amplified region of the 17q12 locus in breast and gastric cancers.
review_notes: First cloning of CAB2/hCOS16 (=PGAP3) as a 17q12 amplicon gene; reports GFP-fusion translocation into vesicles. Predates the enzymatic characterization; DNA-repair/Mn2+ framing is not related to PGAP3's GPI-remodeling function.

title: PER1 is required for GPI-phospholipase A2 activity and involved in lipid remodeling of GPI-anchored proteins.
review_notes: Establishes the GPI-phospholipase A2 / lyso-GPI-forming activity of the PER1 family and shows human PERLD1 (PGAP3) functionally complements yeast per1; foundational for PGAP3's molecular function.

title: Mutations in PGAP3 impair GPI-anchor maturation, causing a subtype of hyperphosphatasia with mental retardation.
review_notes: Human genetics plus CHO functional studies defining HPMRS4 and confirming PGAP3's role in GPI-anchor remodeling; source of Golgi IDA localization and disease variants.

title: Identification of a Golgi GPI-N-acetylgalactosamine transferase with tandem transmembrane regions in the catalytic domain.
review_notes: PGAP4 paper; used PGAP3-knockout cells and gives a clear verbatim description of PGAP3 removing the sn-2 unsaturated fatty acid in Golgi GPI remodeling (before PGAP2 reacylation).

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale Y2H neurodegenerative-disease interactome; source of the GTF3C3 protein-binding IPI. High-throughput; no established functional link to PGAP3's GPI-remodeling role.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex proteome-scale AP-MS interactome; source of the TBRG4 protein-binding IPI. High-throughput; no established functional link to PGAP3.

title: UniProtKB entry Q96FM1 (PGAP3_HUMAN)
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; source for FUNCTION, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY (Rhea RHEA:83847, EC 3.1.1.-), Golgi subcellular location, topology, and HPMRS4 disease association.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Large-scale urinary exosome proteome; supports an HDA extracellular-exosome detection of PGD (over-annotation for a cytosolic enzyme), not a functional role.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: B-cell exosome proteome; basis for an HDA extracellular-exosome detection of PGD (over-annotation), not a biological localization.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Sperm-nucleus proteome; basis for an HDA nuclear detection of PGD (over-annotation for a cytosolic enzyme).

title: Phosphoglycerate mutase 1 coordinates glycolysis and biosynthesis to promote tumor growth.
review_notes: Although titled for PGAM1, the study directly assays and crystallizes human 6PGD and describes its catalytic activity; supports the IDA on GO:0004616.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Prostatic-secretion exosome proteome; basis for an HDA extracellular-exosome detection of PGD (over-annotation), not a functional role.

title: γ-6-Phosphogluconolactone, a Byproduct of the Oxidative Pentose Phosphate Pathway, Contributes to AMPK Activation through Inhibition of PP2A.
review_notes: Defines 6PGD as the third oxiPPP enzyme (6PG to ribulose-5-P + NADPH); 6PGD knockdown reduces oxiPPP flux/NADPH. Supports oxidative-branch involvement and NADPH regeneration.

title: 6-Phosphogluconolactonase deficiency, a hereditary erythrocyte enzyme deficiency: possible interaction with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency.
review_notes: Cited to support the PGD oxidative-branch IDA, but the abstract concerns 6-phosphogluconolactonase (PGLS, EC 3.1.1.31), the second oxiPPP enzyme, and its interaction with G6PD deficiency, not PGD. Abstract-only; associated annotation left UNDECIDED rather than removed.

title: Human brain 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase: purification and kinetic properties.
review_notes: Purification and kinetic characterization of human 6PGD; supports the IDA on GO:0004616.

title: UniProtKB entry P52209 (6PGD_HUMAN)
review_notes: Primary source for the catalytic activity (EC 1.1.1.44, RHEA:10116), cytoplasmic localization, homodimeric structure and pathway membership of human PGD.

title: Conversion of protein farnesyltransferase to a geranylgeranyltransferase.
review_notes: Crystallographic/kinetic study of GGTase-I isoprenoid specificity; identifies beta-subunit residues (T49beta, F324beta) governing GGPP selectivity. IDA source for GGTase-I activity, complex, and geranylgeranylation on P53609.

title: Human-chromatin-related protein interactions identify a demethylase complex required for chromosome segregation.
review_notes: Large-scale chromatin AP-MS interactome; the only PGGT1B-relevant content is the IntAct-curated FNTA (P49354) interaction edge.

title: GGTase3 is a newly identified geranylgeranyltransferase targeting a ubiquitin ligase.
review_notes: Describes GGTase3 (PTAR1/RabGGTB), a distinct enzyme, not PGGT1B function; relevant only for the IntAct FNTA interaction edge and prenylation-code context.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome; source of the IntAct FNTA (P49354) interaction edge for PGGT1B.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex AP-MS interactome; source of the IntAct FNTA (P49354) interaction edge for PGGT1B.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Large-scale cell-map interactome; source of the IntAct FNTA (P49354) interaction edge for PGGT1B.

title: cDNA cloning and expression of rat and human protein geranylgeranyltransferase type-I.
review_notes: Original cloning/expression of rat and human GGTase-I beta; established subunit composition (48-kDa alpha shared with FTase, 43-kDa beta), CAAX/X=Leu specificity, and yeast ortholog CDC43. UniProt FUNCTION/SUBUNIT source.

title: FNTA:PGGT1B geranylgeranylates GBP2
review_notes: Reactome reaction; FNTA:PGGT1B geranylgeranylates GBP2 (C588, CNIL box) in host defense. Source of the cytosol localization TAS.

title: FNTA:PGGT1B geranylgeranylates GBP5
review_notes: Reactome reaction; FNTA:PGGT1B geranylgeranylates GBP5 (C583, CVLL box). Source of the cytosol localization TAS.

title: Phosphoglycerate kinase acts in tumour angiogenesis as a disulphide reductase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes the secreted disulfide-reductase moonlighting function (plasmin reduction -> angiostatin -> anti-angiogenesis). Abstract fully supports the extracellular, disulfide reductase, angiogenesis and plasminogen annotations.

title: Insulin and mTOR Pathway Regulate HDAC3-Mediated Deacetylation and Activation of PGK1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Full text shows HDAC3 directly deacetylates PGK1 at K220 to activate it; supports a regulatory interaction but the GOA annotation only captures generic protein binding.

title: Mitochondria-Translocated PGK1 Functions as a Protein Kinase to Coordinate Glycolysis and the TCA Cycle in Tumorigenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Definitive study of the PGK1 moonlighting protein kinase activity (phosphorylates PDHK1 T338), mitochondrial translocation, and the resulting suppression of pyruvate oxidation. Full text also states the core glycolytic reaction verbatim.

title: A metabolite-derived protein modification integrates glycolysis with KEAP1-NRF2 signalling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Identifies a PGK1 small-molecule inhibitor and confirms PGK1 as the glycolytic enzyme (EC 2.7.2.3); supports the core catalytic activity annotation.

title: mcPGK1-dependent mitochondrial import of PGK1 promotes metabolic reprogramming and self-renewal of liver TICs.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Shows mitochondrial circRNA mcPGK1 drives PGK1 import into mitochondria in liver tumour-initiating cells; supports the condition-dependent mitochondrial and cytosolic localization annotations.

title: A single amino acid substitution (Asp leads to Asn) in a phosphoglycerate kinase variant (PGK München) associated with enzyme deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. PGK Munchen (Asp268Asn) deficiency variant with reduced enzyme activity; genetic (IMP) support for the core phosphoglycerate kinase function and glycolytic role.

title: Identification of the cDNA encoding human 6-phosphogluconolactonase, the enzyme catalyzing the second step of the pentose phosphate pathway(1).
review_notes: Primary identification and biochemical characterization of human PGLS; establishes EC 3.1.1.31 and the second-step-of-PPP role. Source of the EXP/IDA MF and pentose-phosphate-shunt BP annotations. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: NMR spectroscopic analysis of the first two steps of the pentose-phosphate pathway elucidates the role of 6-phosphogluconolactonase.
review_notes: NMR characterization showing PGLS acts on the delta form of 6-phosphogluconolactone, accelerating its hydrolysis and preventing accumulation of the toxic/dead-end forms. Directly supports the MF and oxidative-branch role.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput MS detection of PGLS in urinary exosomes; supports only a bulk-proteomics observation, not a functional localization.

title: Genome-wide YFP fluorescence complementation screen identifies new regulators for telomere signaling in human cells.
review_notes: BiFC interactome screen; PGLS is one of >300 telomere-associated hits with no prior functional link. Supports only a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput MS detection of PGLS in prostatic-secretion/urine exosomes; supports only a bulk-proteomics observation.

title: γ-6-Phosphogluconolactone, a Byproduct of the Oxidative Pentose Phosphate Pathway, Contributes to AMPK Activation through Inhibition of PP2A.
review_notes: Full-text available. Confirms PGLS as the second oxiPPP enzyme; PGLS knockdown/knockout reduces oxiPPP flux and alters 6PGL/6PG levels. Basis for the IMP oxidative-branch annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI all-by-all binary interactome; PGLS-BLMH interaction. Supports only a bare protein-binding IPI, no PGLS-specific function.

title: PGLS hydrolyzes D-glucono-1,5-lactone 6-phosphate
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing the cytosolic PGLS-catalysed hydrolysis; supports the MF and cytosol location.

title: Pentose phosphate pathway
review_notes: Reactome pathway; step 2 is the PGLS-catalysed conversion of D-glucono-1,5-lactone 6-phosphate to 6-phospho-D-gluconate.

title: UniProtKB entry O95336 (6PGL_HUMAN)
review_notes: UniProt record for human PGLS; FUNCTION, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY (EC 3.1.1.31, RHEA:12556), PATHWAY (oxidative-stage step 2/3), and cytoplasm localization.

title: Phosphoglucomutase 1: complete human and rabbit mRNA sequences and direct mapping of this highly polymorphic marker on human chromosome 1.
review_notes: Cloning/mapping of human PGM1 cDNA; identifies it as the highly polymorphic phosphoglucomutase (EC 5.4.2.2). Supports enzyme identity and chromosomal localization; abstract-only in cache.

title: Regulation of phosphoglucomutase 1 phosphorylation and activity by a signaling kinase.
review_notes: Demonstrates PGM1 catalytic activity and its enhancement by PAK1 phosphorylation (at Thr-466/Thr-467). Directly supports the phosphoglucomutase molecular function.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Proteomic detection of PGM1 in urinary exosomes; supports a peripheral extracellular-exosome localization, not core function.

title: Genome-wide YFP fluorescence complementation screen identifies new regulators for telomere signaling in human cells.
review_notes: Large-scale split-YFP telomere-interactome screen underlying the IntAct PGM1-TINF2 interaction. Well-formed citation, but supports only a bare protein-binding annotation of unclear functional relevance to PGM1.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Shotgun proteomics of prostatic-secretion exosomes; PGM1 among ~900 detected proteins. Supports peripheral exosome localization only.

title: Compromised catalysis and potential folding defects in in vitro studies of missense mutants associated with hereditary phosphoglucomutase 1 deficiency.
review_notes: In vitro biochemical characterization of WT and disease-variant PGM1, confirming catalytic activity/kinetics and its central role in glucose metabolism.

title: Induced Structural Disorder as a Molecular Mechanism for Enzyme Dysfunction in Phosphoglucomutase 1 Deficiency.
review_notes: First WT and variant human PGM1 crystal structures; documents Mg2+ coordination, phosphoserine (Ser117) catalytic mechanism, monomeric state, and reversible G1P/G6P interconversion. Full text available and verified.

title: Impaired glycogen breakdown and synthesis in phosphoglucomutase 1 deficiency.
review_notes: Shows PGM1 deficiency blocks muscle glycogenolysis (McArdle-like second wind) and may limit glycogen synthesis; supports the glycogen catabolic-process role.

title: The Metabolic Map into the Pathomechanism and Treatment of PGM1-CDG.
review_notes: Defines PGM1 as the enzyme interconverting glucose-6-P and glucose-1-P; establishes galactose-responsive rewiring of nucleotide-sugar (UDP-glucose/UDP-galactose, Leloir) metabolism in PGM1-CDG.

title: Phosphoglucomutase 1: a gene with two promoters and a duplicated first exon.
review_notes: PGM1 gene-structure study; notes its central role in glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. Supports enzyme identity and metabolic context.

title: Functional cloning and mutational analysis of the human cDNA for phosphoacetylglucosamine mutase: identification of the amino acid residues essential for the catalysis.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false). Functionally cloned human AGM1/PGM3 and demonstrated phosphoacetylglucosamine mutase activity; identified active-site Ser64 and catalytic residues. Supports the core IDA annotation.

title: Autosomal recessive phosphoglucomutase 3 (PGM3) mutations link glycosylation defects to atopy, immune deficiency, autoimmunity, and neurocognitive impairment.
review_notes: Full text available. Established PGM3-CDG (IMD23); enzymatic assay shows reduced GlcNAc-6-P to GlcNAc-1-P conversion, reduced UDP-GlcNAc, and abnormal N-/O-glycosylation in patient cells. Supports the IMP annotations for activity, UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis, and N-/O-glycosylation.

title: Hypomorphic homozygous mutations in phosphoglucomutase 3 (PGM3) impair immunity and increase serum IgE levels.
review_notes: Full text available. Direct enzymatic assay of PGM3 mutants (20-30% residual activity, retained specificity) and glycomic profiling; cites mouse data that Pgm3-derived UDP-GlcNAc is essential for hematopoiesis. Supports the EXP activity annotation and the hemopoiesis IBA context.

title: PGM3 mutations cause a congenital disorder of glycosylation with severe immunodeficiency and skeletal dysplasia.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false). Functional studies of PGM3 variants in E. coli showed reduced activity for all mutants; defines PGM3-CDG with immunodeficiency and skeletal dysplasia. Supports the EXP activity annotation.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Urinary exosome proteomics; supports only the non-specific extracellular exosome localization of the abundant cytosolic enzyme PHGDH.

title: Proteomic analysis of human parotid gland exosomes by multidimensional protein identification technology (MudPIT).
review_notes: Parotid exosome proteomics; supports only non-specific exosome localization.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: B-cell exosome proteomics; supports only non-specific exosome localization.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Prostatic-secretion exosome proteomics; supports only non-specific exosome localization.

title: A quantitative chaperone interaction network reveals the architecture of cellular protein homeostasis pathways.
review_notes: High-throughput chaperone/co-chaperone LUMIER-AP-MS network; basis for a bare "protein binding" IPI (partner EPN1). Uninformative for PHGDH molecular function.

title: Serine biosynthesis defect due to haploinsufficiency of PHGDH causes retinal disease.
review_notes: PMC full text available; provides direct human IMP evidence for both GO:0004617 and GO:0006564 and describes PHGDH as the rate-limiting enzyme of de novo serine biosynthesis.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 proteome-scale AP-MS interactome; basis for a bare "protein binding" IPI (partner EPN1). Uninformative for molecular function.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous-tagging interaction/localization map; basis for a bare "protein binding" IPI (partner EPN1). Uninformative for molecular function.

title: Transcriptional regulation by PHGDH drives amyloid pathology in Alzheimer's disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell 2025, PMID:40273909, PMC12204802; full text cached). Not disputed by a published rebuttal; marked DISPUTED because the claim is a major, enzyme-independent reassignment of function that rests on a single laboratory, on an AlphaFold-predicted DNA-binding subdomain embedded in the NAD(H)-binding Rossmann fold, and on overexpression phenotypes. No GOA annotation currently depends on it, and none is proposed here.

title: RNA-binding activity of PHGDH drives amyloid-beta production in a human brain organoid model of sporadic Alzheimer's disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PNAS 2026, PMID:41701839, PMC12933074; full text cached). Carries a correction (PMID:41838922). Marked DISPUTED on the same grounds as PMID:40273909, plus two specific to it: it is the second mutually-independent moonlighting mechanism proposed for PHGDH by the same senior author within a year, and it is a PNAS Contributed-track submission (contributed by co-author Shu Chien), so editorial handling was not fully arms-length. No independent replication is available.

title: Correction for Chen et al., RNA-binding activity of PHGDH drives amyloid-beta production in a human brain organoid model of sporadic Alzheimer's disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PNAS 2026). Checked specifically because a correction on a single-source moonlighting claim would matter: it does not. It is a reviewer name spelling fix and carries no weight for or against the RNA-binding claim. The correction notice does, however, document the Contributed-track route ("Contributed by Shu Chien ... reviewed by Lana Garmire and Andrew Pieper").

title: 3-Phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase deficiency: an inborn error of serine biosynthesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache (full_text_available false). Supports the core phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase activity and the serine-deficiency brain phenotype; does NOT support the legacy electron transfer activity annotation.

title: PHGDH tetramer dehydrogenates 3PG
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the PHGDH-catalyzed dehydrogenation of 3-phosphoglycerate; supports the cytosolic core enzymatic step.

title: A novel PHKA1 mutation associating myopathy and cognitive impairment: Expanding the spectrum of phosphorylase kinase b (PhK) deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Abstract explicitly states PHKA1 encodes the alpha M subunit of PhK, a multimeric complex controlling muscle glycogen breakdown, and that deficiency causes X-linked GSD VIII/IXd. Directly supports PHKA1's role and the disease.

title: Architecture and activation of human muscle phosphorylase kinase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cryo-EM structure of human muscle PhK establishing that the alpha and beta subunits are non-catalytic (glucoamylase-like fold, no detectable activity) and that the alpha subunit bridges beta to the gamma-delta subcomplex and maintains gamma autoinhibition. Key evidence that PHKA1 is regulatory, not catalytic.

title: Human muscle glycogenosis due to phosphorylase kinase deficiency associated with a nonsense mutation in the muscle isoform of the alpha subunit.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. First human PHKA1 (alpha M) mutation causing X-linked muscle PhK deficiency; supports glycogen metabolic process involvement and disease association.

title: The multiphosphorylation domain of the phosphorylase kinase alpha M and alpha L subunits is a hotspot of differential mRNA processing and of molecular evolution.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cloning/sequencing of the human alpha M subunit and characterization of its multiphosphorylation (PKA) domain and splicing. Supports the regulatory phosphorylation biology; does not establish PHKA1 as catalytic, so the TAS phosphorylase kinase activity annotation it underlies is treated as over-annotated.

title: glycogen phosphorylase (PYGM) dimer b + 2 ATP => glycogen phosphorylase (PYGM) dimer a + 2 ADP
review_notes: Reactome reaction in which the cytosolic phosphorylase kinase complex (including PHKA1) phosphorylates glycogen phosphorylase (PYGM) b to a. Supports cytosolic localization and the glycogen catabolic role of the complex.

title: Interlaboratory reproducibility of large-scale human protein-complex analysis by standardized AP-MS.
review_notes: High-throughput AP-MS dataset underpinning a bare protein-binding IPI; no PHKA2-specific function established.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: Large-scale quantitative interactome dataset; source of a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome/community dataset; source of a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Binary (Y2H) reference-interactome dataset; source of bare protein-binding IPIs.

title: Kinase Interaction Network Expands Functional and Disease Roles of Human Kinases.
review_notes: Kinase-interaction-network dataset; the meaningful partner (catalytic gamma subunit PHKG2) reflects complex membership already captured elsewhere.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegenerative-disease interactome dataset; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (SPRED1), not functionally interpreted for PHKA2.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome dataset; source of a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Endogenous-tagging cellular-organization dataset; source of a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-mapping dataset; source of a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: Isolation of cDNA encoding the human liver phosphorylase kinase alpha subunit (PHKA2) and identification of a missense mutation of the PHKA2 gene in a family with liver phosphorylase kinase deficiency.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Directly establishes PHKA2 as the human liver alpha subunit of phosphorylase kinase and links it to X-linked liver PhK deficiency (GSD IXa); basis for the TAS complex/activity/process annotations.

title: Phosphorylase kinase: the complexity of its regulation is reflected in the complexity of its structure.
review_notes: Authoritative review of phosphorylase kinase structure/function; establishes the gamma subunit as the sole catalytic subunit and the Ca2+/cAMP regulation of PhK.

title: Severe phenotype of phosphorylase kinase-deficient liver glycogenosis with mutations in the PHKG2 gene.
review_notes: GSD9C PHKG2 variant characterization (E157K, D215N, W300X, H89fs); establishes PHKG2 as the cause of severe liver PhK deficiency.

title: Interlaboratory reproducibility of large-scale human protein-complex analysis by standardized AP-MS.
review_notes: High-throughput AP-MS; source of a PHKG2-PHKA2 interaction underlying a bare protein binding annotation.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome; source of a bare protein binding (PHKA2) annotation.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Interactome map; source of a bare protein binding (PHKA2) annotation.

title: Homology probing: identification of cDNA clones encoding members of the protein-serine kinase family.
review_notes: Original cloning of PSK-C3/PHKG2 cDNA; Ser/Thr kinase 72% identical to muscle phosphorylase kinase gamma subunit.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome; source of bare protein binding annotations (PHKA2, MAGEA2B).

title: Kinase Interaction Network Expands Functional and Disease Roles of Human Kinases.
review_notes: Kinase interaction network; source of a bare protein binding (PHKA2) annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex proteome-scale interactome; source of a bare protein binding (PHKA2) annotation.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous-tagging interactome; source of a bare protein binding (PHKA2) annotation.

title: A very rare case report of glycogen storage disease type IXc with novel PHKG2 variants.

title: Mutations in PIGS, Encoding a GPI Transamidase, Cause a Neurological Syndrome Ranging from Fetal Akinesia to Epileptic Encephalopathy.
review_notes: Defines GPIBD18; biallelic PIGS loss-of-function causes GPI-AP deficiency, directly linking PIGS to GPI-AP biosynthesis.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome; only the PIGT interaction is a bona fide GPI-T partner, the rest support only generic protein binding.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.

title: Functional Analysis of the GPI Transamidase Complex by Screening for Amino Acid Mutations in Each Subunit.
review_notes: Full text available; states GPI-TA has five subunits, that PIGS is indispensable for activity, and characterizes functionally important residues; supports complex membership and requirement.

title: Structure of human glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structure of human GPI-T (PDB 7W72); PIGS resolved as one of five subunits; identifies PIGK catalytic triad and substrate-binding cleft.

title: Molecular insights into biogenesis of glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor proteins.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structure showing equimolar heteropentameric GPI-T assembly including PIGS; ER membrane localization confirmed.

title: Structures of liganded glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase illuminate GPI-AP biogenesis.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map interactome; PIGT interaction consistent with GPI-T, but recorded as generic protein binding.

title: PIG-S and PIG-T, essential for GPI anchor attachment to proteins, form a complex with GAA1 and GPI8.

title: Structural requirements for the recruitment of Gaa1 into a functional glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase complex.

title: Two subunits of glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase, GPI8 and PIG-T, form a functionally important intermolecular disulfide bridge.
review_notes: Demonstrates the PIGT-PIGK/GPI8 interchain disulfide bond required for full transamidase activity; verified against cached abstract.

review_notes: Shows PIG-T is a type I ER membrane protein retained in the ER via its transmembrane span; supports ER membrane localisation.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane proteome; only supports the generic 'membrane' localisation, not specific function.

title: Analysis of exome data for 4293 trios suggests GPI-anchor biogenesis defects are a rare cause of developmental disorders.
review_notes: Identifies biallelic PIGT variants in developmental-disorder trios and demonstrates impaired GPI-AP biogenesis; supports MCAHS3 and the GPI-attachment BP.

review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 large-scale interactome; supports generic protein-binding interactions only.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 proteome-scale interactome; supports generic protein-binding interactions only.

title: Functional Analysis of the GPI Transamidase Complex by Screening for Amino Acid Mutations in Each Subunit.
review_notes: Mutational analysis of all five GPI-TA subunits including PIGT; shows loss of any subunit abolishes activity.

title: Structure of human glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase.
review_notes: First cryo-EM structure of human GPI-T; PIGK is catalytic, complex is ER-membrane; PIGT is a subunit.

title: Molecular insights into biogenesis of glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor proteins.
review_notes: 2.53-Angstrom cryo-EM structure of the equimolar heteropentameric GPI-T with bound GPI; defines the lipid-substrate cavity.

title: Case report: Functional analysis of the p.Arg507Trp variant of the PIGT gene supporting the moderate epilepsy phenotype of mutations in the C-terminal region.
review_notes: Knockout-rescue FACS assay of a PIGT MCAHS3 variant; directly ties PIGT to GPI-anchor attachment activity.

title: Structures of liganded glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase illuminate GPI-AP biogenesis.
review_notes: Substrate/product-bound GPI-T structures describing the transamidation reaction; PIGT is a subunit and binds GPI.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal interactome/cell-map study; supports generic protein-binding interactions only.

title: uPAR precursor + acyl-GPI -> uPAR-acyl-GPI + uPAR propeptide
review_notes: Reactome reaction catalysed by the ER-membrane GPI transamidase complex; supports ER membrane localisation of the complex containing PIGT.

title: PIG-S and PIG-T, essential for GPI anchor attachment to proteins, form a complex with GAA1 and GPI8.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes the GPI transamidase complex (GAA1, GPI8/PIGK, PIG-S, PIG-T) and that it mediates GPI anchoring in the ER by replacing the C-terminal GPI attachment signal peptide; PIGU was identified later as the fifth subunit. Supports the pathway/localization framing but does not itself assay PIGU.

title: Human PIG-U and yeast Cdc91p are the fifth subunit of GPI transamidase that attaches GPI-anchors to proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Primary paper identifying PIGU (PIG-U) as the fifth subunit of GPI transamidase; class-U cells lack transamidase activity and cannot cleave the GPI attachment signal; proposes PIGU recognises the GPI attachment signal or the lipid portion of GPI.

title: CDC91L1 (PIG-U) is a newly discovered oncogene in human bladder cancer.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Correctly identifies PIG-U as a GPI transamidase-complex unit and supports its role in the GPI anchoring pathway. The plasma-membrane and JAK-STAT annotations derived from this overexpression/oncogene study are downstream/indirect effects (uPAR upregulation, STAT-3 phosphorylation), not PIGU's core ER function.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. High-throughput membrane proteomics of an NK-like cell line; supports only the generic membrane localization of PIGU.

title: Mutations in PIGU Impair the Function of the GPI Transamidase Complex, Causing Severe Intellectual Disability, Epilepsy, and Brain Anomalies.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes PIGU as an essential GPI transamidase subunit and links biallelic PIGU variants to an inherited GPI-anchor deficiency (NEDBSS/GPIBD) with intellectual disability, epilepsy and brain anomalies; variant cells show reduced surface GPI-anchored proteins.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. HuRI high-throughput Y2H interactome map; source of the single PIGU-KASH5 binary interaction underlying the generic protein binding IPI. Not informative for PIGU's specific molecular function.

title: Functional Analysis of the GPI Transamidase Complex by Screening for Amino Acid Mutations in Each Subunit.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Confirms PIGU is one of five GPI-TA subunits, that loss of PIGU abolishes complex activity, that PIGU is homologous to lipid-handling GPI biosynthetic enzymes (recognises the lipid portion of GPI), and identifies functionally important PIGU residues (Leu375/Trp376).

title: Structure of human glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cryo-EM structure of the five-subunit human GPI-T (including PIGU); identifies the PIGK catalytic triad and the transmembrane GPI substrate-binding cleft.

title: Molecular insights into biogenesis of glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cryo-EM structure of the equimolar heteropentameric human GPI-T (ER membrane), including PIGU; defines a composite cavity for the lipid substrate.

title: Structures of liganded glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase illuminate GPI-AP biogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Substrate/product-bound GPI-T structures showing PIGU as one of five subunits contacting GPI; basis for the UniProt statement that PIGU binds the lipid portion of the GPI-anchor.

title: PIG-V involved in transferring the second mannose in glycosylphosphatidylinositol.
review_notes: Primary paper that cloned human PIG-V and identified it as GPI-MT-II, transferring the second mannose in GPI biosynthesis; defines catalytic activity, ER topology, and functional residues. Abstract-only in cache; full text underlies the experimental annotations.

title: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ybr004c and its human homologue are required for addition of the second mannose during glycosylphosphatidylinositol precursor assembly.
review_notes: Identifies yeast Ybr004c/GPI18 as GPI-MT-II and shows the human homologue (PIGV) complements it in vivo; supports the alpha-1,6-mannosyltransferase and GPI biosynthesis annotations.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale yeast two-hybrid neurodegenerative-disease interactome; source of bare protein binding IPIs for PIGV that are uninformative about its molecular function.

title: Glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor deficiency caused by mutations in PIGW is associated with West syndrome and hyperphosphatasia with mental retardation syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified case report; establishes the human disease association (GPIBD11) and the GPI-AP surface-transport phenotype that underlie the IMP and IC annotations. Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false).

title: glucosaminyl-PI + fatty acyl-CoA -> glucosaminyl-acyl-PI + CoA-SH
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the PIGW-catalysed inositol-acylation step; title left exactly as fetched.

title: Synthesis of glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)
review_notes: Pathway-level Reactome entry; title left exactly as fetched.
