review_notes: Curated UniProt record for the reviewed protein; source of the catalytic activity, subcellular location, topology, and disease statements.

title: Biosynthesis and biology of mammalian GPI-anchored proteins.
review_notes: Authoritative Kinoshita review; full text available and directly states PIGX's role as the stabilizing (regulatory) subunit of GPI-MTI that stabilizes catalytic PIGM. Also the ComplexPortal-cited reference for the ER-membrane and GPI-MT-I complex annotations.

title: glucosaminyl-acyl-PI + dolichol phosphate D-mannose -> mannose(al1-4)glucosaminyl-acyl-PI + dolichol phosphate
review_notes: Reactome reaction cited by GOA for PIGX ER-membrane localization; describes the PIGM/PIGX-catalyzed GPI-MT-I step and names both subunits.

title: UniProtKB Q8TBF5 PIGX record
review_notes: UniProt record for Q8TBF5; used for the subunit-stabilization function, subcellular location, and single-pass type I membrane topology statements.

title: The initial enzyme for glycosylphosphatidylinositol biosynthesis requires PIG-Y, a seventh component.
review_notes: Defining paper for PIGY; identifies PIGY as the seventh component of the GPI-GnT complex, a 71-aa two-TM ER protein that binds directly to and regulates the catalytic subunit PIGA. Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available false); all supporting quotes verified as verbatim substrings of the cached abstract.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI large-scale binary (Y2H) interactome map; source of PIGY protein-binding IPI annotations to TMEM72 and ERG28. Correctly cited but provides only bare protein-binding data with no established functional significance for PIGY; interactors are not GPI-pathway related.

title: UniProtKB entry Q3MUY2 (PIGY_HUMAN)
review_notes: UniProt/Swiss-Prot record; provides curated FUNCTION, SUBUNIT, SUBCELLULAR LOCATION, PATHWAY and DISEASE annotations used as supporting text.

title: Falcon deep research report for PIP5K1B
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/falcon) report. Cross-checkable, gene-specific claims used to strengthen this review: PIP5K1B catalyzes PI4P + ATP -> PI(4,5)P2 with PI4P as the predominant physiological substrate (PI3P phosphorylation in vitro only); plasma-membrane (cytoplasmic face) as the principal site of PI(4,5)P2 generation; and PI(4,5)P2 as the immediate class I PI3K substrate that makes PI(3,4,5)P3 (basis for the indirect, non-core PI3K/AKT annotation). These are consistent with the cached primary literature (PMID:8955136) and UniProt. The report also asserts a PIP5Kbeta-specific role at the immunological synapse (CD28/Vav1/filamin A; cites Kallikourdis et al. 2016, J Immunol) which is genuinely PIP5K1B-specific but is not currently in GOA and its source paper is not cached, so it was not used to add an annotation. Many broader functional statements (actin remodeling, adhesion, endocytosis, cell migration, cancer) are paralog-generalized from PIP5K1A/PIP5K1C or family-level reviews rather than directly evidenced for PIP5K1B, and the structural/activation-loop and dimerization mechanisms are described at the family/PIP5K1A level; these were treated as speculative and not propagated. The report cites only DOIs (no PMIDs verified against cached publications), hence UNVERIFIED.

title: Structure and function of human erythrocyte pyruvate kinase. Molecular basis of nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.
review_notes: Crystal structure and functional characterization of human erythrocyte RPK with FBP and a substrate analogue; establishes catalytic activity, cofactors, allostery, and links CNSHA2 mutations to enzyme defects.

title: Structural basis for tumor pyruvate kinase M2 allosteric regulation and catalysis.
review_notes: Structure/mechanism paper on the human M2 isozyme (PKM gene), not PKLR. Used by Reactome to support pyruvate kinase activity for PKLR by isozyme analogy; the catalytic mechanism and Mg2+/K+/FBP dependence are conserved across the L/R/M1/M2 isozymes, so it corroborates but is not a direct PKLR study.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary exosome proteomics; supports the incidental extracellular-exosome localization (HDA) but not PKLR's core catalytic function. PKLR is not individually discussed in the abstract.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI systematic yeast two-hybrid interactome; source of the single PKLR-CPNE7 (Q9UBL6-2) protein-binding IPI. High-throughput, no PKLR-specific functional characterization; underlies an uninformative bare protein-binding annotation flagged as over-annotated.

title: UniProtKB P30613 (KPYR_HUMAN) Pyruvate kinase PKLR
review_notes: Primary source record for PKLR function, catalytic activity (EC 2.7.1.40), Mg2+/Mn2+/K+ cofactors, FBP allosteric activation, homotetramer, glycolysis pathway, and CNSHA2/PKHYP disease associations.

title: Regulation of the phospholipase C-gamma2 pathway in B cells.
review_notes: Cached abstract directly supports BCR PLCG2-calcium pathway, Syk/Btk/BLNK recruitment, and PIP2-to-IP3 signaling.

title: Real time fluorescence imaging of PLC gamma translocation and its interaction with the epidermal growth factor receptor.
review_notes: Cached full text supports PLC-gamma membrane/ruffle translocation, receptor binding, substrate access, and vesicle internalization; used for PLCG2 localization by isoform-conserved mechanism.

title: Tyrosine residues in phospholipase Cgamma 2 essential for the enzyme function in B-cell signaling.
review_notes: Cached abstract directly supports Tyr753/Tyr759 function, BTK/SYK/BLNK mechanism, calcium responses, and kinase/scaffold binding decisions.

title: Activation of phospholipase Cgamma2 by tyrosine phosphorylation.
review_notes: Cached abstract directly supports recombinant PLCG2 catalytic activation by tyrosine phosphorylation and platelet Tyr753/Tyr759 phosphorylation.

title: Structural insights into formation of an active signaling complex between Rac and phospholipase C gamma 2.
review_notes: Cached PubMed abstract; supports direct Rac2/spPH-domain interaction and PLCG2 activation mechanism.

review_notes: Cached abstract supports B-cell exosome proteomics detection only; relevant to over-annotation decision for extracellular exosome.

title: Cold urticaria, immunodeficiency, and autoimmunity related to PLCG2 deletions.

title: A hypermorphic missense mutation in PLCG2, encoding phospholipase Cγ2, causes a dominantly inherited autoinflammatory disease with immunodeficiency.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports PLCG2 phospholipase activity and immune-pathway dysregulation from a hypermorphic PLCG2 variant.

title: BANK1 and BLK act through phospholipase C gamma 2 in B-cell signaling.

title: Alzheimer's-associated PLCγ2 is a signaling node required for both TREM2 function and the inflammatory response in human microglia.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports PLCG2 downstream of TREM2 and TLR signaling in human microglia-like cells, including phagocytosis, lipid metabolism, transcriptional and inflammatory phenotypes.

title: The X-ray crystal structures of human alpha-phosphomannomutase 1 reveal the structural basis of congenital disorder of glycosylation type 1a.
review_notes: PubMed-verified structural/kinetic study. Abstract foregrounds PMM1 crystal structures but explicitly compares both isozymes and underpins the EC 5.4.2.8 ECO:0000269 evidence UniProt assigns to PMM2; per guidelines not removed as 'wrong gene'.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome screen; supports only a generic, uninformative 'protein binding' annotation with no demonstrated functional relevance to PMM2.

title: Widespread Expansion of Protein Interaction Capabilities by Alternative Splicing.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome screen; supports only a generic 'protein binding' annotation, not a core function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome; generic 'protein binding' hits with no functional meaning for a cytosolic metabolic enzyme.

title: Evolutionary rescue of phosphomannomutase deficiency in yeast models of human disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:36214454, eLife 2022). Yeast SEC53/PMM2 model; corroborates that PMM2 loss-of-function impairs N-linked glycosylation and that the common p.Phe119Leu/F126L allele acts via dimer/stability defects. Added by Falcon integration to strengthen the N-glycosylation (non-core) and homodimer evidence.

title: Tracer metabolomics reveals the role of aldose reductase in glycosylation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:37257447, Cell Rep Med 2023). Confirms PMM2 deficiency depletes GDP-mannose (supports the core GDP-mannose biosynthetic process role) and explicitly states PMM2 is NOT directly involved in polyol metabolism, supporting the decision NOT to annotate polyol/metabolic-rewiring as a PMM2 function. The aldose-reductase axis is a downstream/compensatory metabolic effect, not a PMM2 molecular function. Added by Falcon integration.

title: In Silico Analysis of Phosphomannomutase-2 Dimer Interface Stability and Heterodimerization with Phosphomannomutase-1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:40572562, Molecules 2025). In silico/structural study; supports the homodimer quaternary structure asserted in core_functions and the catalytic- vs interface-defect distinction (R141H vs F119L). Predicted PMM1/PMM2 heterodimer is computational only and PMM1 does not compensate in vivo, so it does NOT justify a PMM1-containing-complex annotation. Added by Falcon integration.

title: Mutations in PMM2, a phosphomannomutase gene on chromosome 16p13, in carbohydrate-deficient glycoprotein type I syndrome (Jaeken syndrome).
review_notes: Foundational PMM2 cloning/disease paper; PubMed-verified. Anchors the gene's catalytic identity and disease association.

title: Carbohydrate-deficient glycoprotein syndrome type Ib. Phosphomannose isomerase deficiency and mannose therapy.
review_notes: Cited as the IMP source for PMM2 GDP-mannose biosynthetic process, but the paper is about phosphomannose isomerase (PMI/MPI) deficiency / CDG-Ib and mannose therapy - a different enzyme catalyzing F6P<->Man6P and a different gene (MPI). The GO term is still correct for PMM2 and is strongly supported by other references, so the annotation was kept; the citation itself appears mis-attributed. Recommendation: FlyBase should re-examine and correct this IMP annotation, since its supporting evidence derives from a different enzyme (PMI/MPI, CDG-Ib) and does not assay the PMM2 mutase step.

title: Defective PMM2 does not isomerise Man6P to Man1P
review_notes: Reactome-curated reaction; consistent with UniProt and primary literature.

title: PMM1,2 isomerise Man6P to Man1P

title: Synthesis of GDP-mannose

title: Phosphomevalonate kinase: functional investigation of the recombinant human enzyme.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary characterization of recombinant human PMVK establishing the phosphomevalonate kinase activity, ATP binding, and monomeric state.

title: Localization of the pre-squalene segment of the isoprenoid biosynthetic pathway in mammalian peroxisomes.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified HuRI interactome map. The PMVK interactors it reports are high-throughput Y2H hits with no functional follow-up; supports only a bare, and uninformative, protein-binding annotation.

title: UniProtKB Q15126 (PMVK_HUMAN) record
review_notes: Curated UniProt entry; source for the EC 2.7.4.2 catalytic activity, the isoprenoid/IPP PATHWAY statement, the cytosolic subcellular location, the ATP-binding features, and the CAUTION note reconciling the peroxisome-vs-cytosol history.

review_notes: PubMed-verified primary study on human PNMT; the IMP annotation for PNMT activity is supported by functional assay of wild-type and variant allozymes.

title: Mode of binding of methyl acceptor substrates to the adrenaline-synthesizing enzyme phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase: implications for catalysis.

title: Recombinant human phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase: overproduction in Escherichia coli, purification, and characterization.

title: Role of purine nucleoside phosphorylase in interactions between 2',3'-dideoxyinosine and allopurinol, ganciclovir, or tenofovir.

review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2010;285:6706-15). Establishes TG hydrolase activity and its loss in I148M, plus the membrane/lipid-droplet partitioning.

title: Expression and characterization of a PNPLA3 protein isoform (I148M) associated with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2011;286:37085-93), full text available. The most complete substrate survey of purified PNPLA3. It reports the glycerolipid hydrolase activities and explicit negatives for GPAT, LPAAT, DGAT, phospholipids, cholesteryl esters and retinyl esters. The citation itself is correct; what is wrong is GOA's use of it as EXP evidence for GO:0003841, a reaction this paper could not detect.

title: Adiponutrin functions as a nutritionally regulated lysophosphatidic acid acyltransferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Metab 2012;15:691-702). Correctly cited, but the central claim - that PNPLA3 is a CoA-dependent LPA acyltransferase, and that I148M increases that activity - is directly contradicted by PMID:21878620, which assayed the same reaction with CGI-58 as a positive control and detected nothing. The disagreement also runs the opposite way on the direction of the variant's effect. Retained; the annotations derived from it are marked over-annotated rather than removed.

title: PNPLA3/adiponutrin functions in lipid droplet formation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Biol Cell 2013;105:219-233). Cached record is abstract-only. Supports lipid droplet targeting and the effect of PNPLA3 dosage on droplet size; also an early report that co-expressed ABHD5/CGI-58 reverses PNPLA3-induced droplet enlargement.

title: PNPLA3 mediates hepatocyte triacylglycerol remodeling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Lipid Res 2014;55:739-46). The cellular evidence for acyl-chain remodelling, and for the shift of I148M protein towards lipid droplets.

title: PNPLA3 is a triglyceride lipase that mobilizes polyunsaturated fatty acids to facilitate hepatic secretion of large-sized very low-density lipoprotein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2024;15:4847). Not cited by any current GOA row; added here because it is the loss-of-function pole of the dispute. Its in vivo findings - hepatic Pnpla3 knockout aggravating steatosis and lowering VLDL-TG - are explicitly contradicted by PMID:39550037, which reports no hepatic phenotype in Pnpla3-null mice and increased rather than decreased phospholipid PUFA in 148M animals. Cited as one side of an open disagreement.

title: PNPLA3(148M) is a gain-of-function mutation that promotes hepatic steatosis by inhibiting ATGL-mediated triglyceride hydrolysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Hepatol 2025;82:871-881), full text available. The strongest current evidence for the ABHD5-sequestration model, and also the first demonstration that ABHD5 directly activates PNPLA3's own TG hydrolase activity. Its central claim is a gain-of-function interpretation that PMID:38844467 rejects, so it is scientifically contested even though the citation is sound.

title: Lipid droplet targeting of the lipase coactivator ABHD5 and the fatty liver disease-causing variant PNPLA3 I148M is required to promote liver steatosis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2025;301:108186), full text available. Independent support for the ABHD5 interaction and for lipid droplet targeting being required for it. Reports greater association of I148M than wild-type PNPLA3 with ABHD5, which PMID:39550037 attributes largely to higher I148M protein levels.

title: Loss or gain of function: The functional complexity of the PNPLA3 I148M variant.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Hepatol 2025;82:778-780), an editorial accompanying PMID:39550037. PubMed holds no abstract and no full text is available, so it is cited only as evidence that the loss-of-function versus gain-of-function question is recognised as unresolved by the field, with no supporting_text quoted from it.

title: PNPLA3-I148M is a neomorph that interferes with two primary hepatic triglyceride clearance pathways.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Rep 2025;44:116371). Cached record is abstract-only, so claims are anchored to the abstract. Proposes a third mechanism distinct from both loss- and gain-of-function, converging on ABHD5/CGI-58 and adding impaired ApoB/VLDL secretion.

title: Structure and properties of recombinant human pyridoxine 5'-phosphate oxidase.

title: Genomic organization, tissue distribution and deletion mutation of human pyridoxine 5'-phosphate oxidase.

title: Modification of epidermal growth factor-like repeats with O-fucose. Molecular cloning and expression of a novel GDP-fucose protein O-fucosyltransferase.
review_notes: PubMed/UniProt-verified primary cloning and enzymatic characterization of human POFUT1 (Wang et al. 2001, JBC). Abstract-only in cache; supporting_text is a verbatim quote from the abstract. Anchors the core MF and O-fucosylation process annotations. Note the abstract predicts a type-II TM anchor, but the active enzyme is later shown to be soluble ER-luminal (PMID:15653671).

title: Composition of Drosophila melanogaster proteome involved in fucosylated glycan metabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, but this is a Drosophila genome bioinformatics survey, not a study of human POFUT1 enzymatic activity. It is a weak/inappropriate basis for a TAS human peptide-O-fucosyltransferase-activity annotation; the same MF term is far better supported by human IDA (PMID:11524432, PMID:9023546, PMID:15653671).

title: O-fucosylation of notch occurs in the endoplasmic reticulum.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary localization study (Luo & Haltiwanger 2005, JBC). Abstract-only in cache; supporting_text quotes are verbatim from the abstract. Definitive evidence for soluble ER-luminal localization and KDEL-like retention; basis for treating ER as core and Golgi/membrane as incorrect/uninformative.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified high-throughput membrane-proteome MS study. POFUT1's presence in a crude membrane fraction is the basis of the HDA "membrane" annotation but is not informative of its true soluble ER-luminal localization; contributes only a generic, over-annotated location.

title: Structure of human POFUT1, its requirement in ligand-independent oncogenic Notch signaling, and functional effects of Dowling-Degos mutations.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available in cache. Provides the human POFUT1 crystal structures (GDP-fucose complex), the IMP evidence for regulation of Notch signaling, and functional analysis of Dowling-Degos mutations. Anchors the Notch-regulation annotation and the cautious (non-core) treatment of a mammalian chaperone role.

title: Identification of a GDP-L-fucose:polypeptide fucosyltransferase and enzymatic addition of O-linked fucose to EGF domains.
review_notes: PubMed-verified original enzyme-activity characterization (Wang et al. 1996, Glycobiology). Abstract-only in cache; supporting_text quotes are verbatim. Establishes the core peptide-O-fucosyltransferase activity and the folded-EGF-domain acceptor requirement.

title: FutureHouse Falcon deep-research report for POFUT1
review_notes: FutureHouse Falcon deep-research report. Conclusions are concordant with the curated review and with the primary literature. Used only to anchor the ER-localization synthesis; all substantive annotations are cited to the cached primary PMIDs rather than to Falcon's (largely review-derived, unverified) citation list. One Falcon claim (Ajima 2017 attributed to uterine/placental angiogenesis via uPA/RhoA) appears to be a citation mismatch and was rejected.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Proteome-scale AP-MS interactome (BioPlex). Source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (PPAT-NUDT5); no functional consequence established for PPAT's catalytic role.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Second proteome-scale BioPlex interactome. Source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (PPAT-NUDT5); uninformative about molecular function.

title: Two genes for de novo purine nucleotide synthesis on human chromosome 4 are closely linked and divergently transcribed.

title: Complete reconstitution of the human coenzyme A biosynthetic pathway via comparative genomics.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.

title: Complex stability and dynamic subunit interchange modulates the disparate activities of the yeast moonlighting proteins Hal3 and Vhs3.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, but this is a yeast (S. cerevisiae) study of the heterotrimeric Hal3/Vhs3/Cab3 PPCDC, not a direct assay of human PPCDC self-interaction. title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.

title: Mutations in PPCS, Encoding Phosphopantothenoylcysteine Synthetase, Cause Autosomal-Recessive Dilated Cardiomyopathy.

review_notes: Reactome curated reaction for the PPOX-catalysed step; source of the TAS intermembrane space annotation. Title left exactly as fetched.

review_notes: Direct enzymatic characterization of wild-type and mutant human PRODH (POX); establishes the core proline dehydrogenase activity (EC 1.5.5.2), FAD-cofactor dependence (T466M reduces FAD affinity), inner-membrane localization, and the link between reduced POX activity and hyperprolinemia/schizophrenia. title: Structural and biochemical studies of human 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase: implications for hydroxyproline metabolism in primary hyperoxaluria.
review_notes: Full-text paper on human HOGA (4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase). It describes the 4-hydroxyproline degradation pathway as beginning with hydroxyproline oxidase (HPOX) — the distinct paralog PRODH2/HYPDH — and does not implicate PRODH. The GO:0019470 (trans-4-hydroxy-L-proline catabolic process) annotation to PRODH from this paper is a paralog mis-attribution; marked over-annotated.

title: DJ-1 cooperates with PYCR1 in cell protection against oxidative stress.
review_notes: Cached abstract concerns DJ-1/PARK7 and PYCR1 (P5C reductase, proline biosynthesis) in oxidative-stress protection and does not mention PRODH. The IDA annotation of GO:1903376 to PRODH was made by a curator with full-text access; the abstract-only cache cannot confirm the PRODH-specific evidence, so correctness is left UNVERIFIED and the annotation retained as non-core.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome dataset; supports the HTP mitochondrial-localization annotation of PRODH.

title: A model for p53-induced apoptosis.

title: PRODH oxidises L-Pro to 1PYR-5COOH

title: Proline catabolism

title: PRSS23-eIF4E-c-Myc axis promotes gastric tumorigenesis and progression.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Oncogene 2025). Independently supports non-proteolytic PRSS23 function, since eIF4E binding and progrowth phenotypes were retained in catalytic triad mutants. title: PRSS23 promotes ovarian cancer peritoneal dissemination independent of protease activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: J Biol Chem 2026;302(6):111450, DOI 10.1016/j.jbc.2026.111450, PMC13194640; full text cached. The decisive reference for this review. title: BANK1 and BLK act through phospholipase C gamma 2 in B-cell signaling.

review_notes: Large-scale interactome (BioPlex-type) study; source of bare protein binding IPI annotations including RABGGTA (Q92696) and PTAR1 (Q7Z6K3). The RABGGTA/PTAR1 partnerships are biologically meaningful but are better captured by the complex-membership terms.

title: GGTase3 is a newly identified geranylgeranyltransferase targeting a ubiquitin ligase.
review_notes: Identifies GGTase-III as a heterodimer of the orphan alpha subunit PTAR1 and the catalytic beta subunit of GGTase2 (RABGGTB); reports that GGTase-III geranylgeranylates FBXL2. Crystal structure of the GGTase3-FBXL2-SKP1 complex. Abstract-only in cache but PMID/title verified.

title: A SNARE geranylgeranyltransferase essential for the organization of the Golgi apparatus.
review_notes: Full text available. Defines GGTase-III (PTAR1 + beta subunit of RabGGTase) and shows it geranylgeranylates mono-farnesylated YKT6 at Cys194 to produce doubly prenylated YKT6 required for Golgi SNARE assembly. Mutagenesis of RABGGTB Gly49 abolishes YKT6 modification. Also questions whether FBXL2 is a physiological GGTase-III substrate.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome map; source of bare protein binding IPI annotations (IGFBP6, WDR4, RABGGTA, B4GALT7). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 interactome; source of bare protein binding IPI annotations (PTAR1, RABGGTA). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous-tagging proximity interactome; source of bare protein binding IPI annotations (PTAR1, RABGGTA). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell map interactome; source of bare protein binding IPI annotations (PTAR1, RABGGTA). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Rab geranylgeranyl transferase catalyzes the geranylgeranylation of adjacent cysteines in the small GTPases Rab1A, Rab3A, and Rab5A.
review_notes: Direct biochemical demonstration (mass spectrometry of tryptic peptides) of di-geranylgeranylation of Rab substrates by RabGGTase; the EXP evidence underpinning the enzyme's molecular function. Abstract-only in cache but PMID/title verified and this is the reference cited by UniProt for the catalytic activity / EC 2.5.1.60.

title: Retinal degeneration in choroideremia: deficiency of rab geranylgeranyl transferase.
review_notes: This paper is about component A (REP1/CHM), the choroideremia disease gene, and explicitly finds that component B (which contains RABGGTB) is NOT deficient. It is therefore the wrong reference to attribute "visual perception" and "protein modification process" to RABGGTB; the visual phenotype maps to CHM, not to this catalytic subunit.

title: Structures of the human and Drosophila 80S ribosome.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed ("Structures of the human and Drosophila 80S ribosome"); cryo-EM structure places RACK1 as an integral 40S subunit component, establishing the core ribosome-binding/structural-subunit function (GO:0043022, GO:0022627).

title: ZNF598 and RACK1 Regulate Mammalian Ribosome-Associated Quality Control Function by Mediating Regulatory 40S Ribosomal Ubiquitylation.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; Results show RACK1 (with ZNF598) is required for regulatory 40S ubiquitylation that resolves stalled/collided ribosomes, establishing RACK1's ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) scaffold role.

title: RACK1, a receptor for activated C kinase and a homolog of the beta subunit of G proteins, inhibits activity of src tyrosine kinases and growth of NIH 3T3 cells.
review_notes: GOA-anchored (this PMID supports GO:0030292 protein tyrosine kinase inhibitor activity in RACK1-goa.tsv); seminal paper establishing RACK1's Src-family kinase inhibition / signaling-scaffold core function.

title: Ca2+ activates human homologous recombination protein Rad51 by modulating its ATPase activity.
review_notes: Bugreev & Mazin; RAD51 DNA-dependent ATPase; Ca2+ modulation of ATP hydrolysis stimulates strand exchange. Full text available; quotes confirmed.

title: RECQL5/Recql5 helicase regulates homologous recombination and suppresses tumor formation via disruption of Rad51 presynaptic filaments.
review_notes: RECQL5 disrupts RAD51 presynaptic (nucleoprotein) filaments — confirms the GO:0099182 annotation is a misnomer-driven mis-mapping, not a neuronal-synapse localization.

title: Discovery of a novel function for human Rad51: maintenance of the mitochondrial genome.
review_notes: Sage et al.; RAD51/RAD51C/XRCC3 maintain mtDNA copy number under oxidative stress; identifies mtDNA as a RAD51 substrate.

title: Purified human BRCA2 stimulates RAD51-mediated recombination.
review_notes: Jensen, Carreira & Kowalczykowski; full-length BRCA2 promotes assembly of RAD51 onto ssDNA, targets RAD51 to ssDNA over dsDNA, displaces RPA and stabilizes RAD51-ssDNA filaments by blocking ATP hydrolysis. Verified against cached full text; corroborates the Affinage narrative on BRCA2-mediated RAD51 loading. Cited here only under the over-annotated generic protein-binding rows.

title: RAD51 mutants cause replication defects and chromosomal instability.
review_notes: RAD51 mutants cause replication defects and chromosomal instability; supports fork-processing role.

title: A Dominant Mutation in Human RAD51 Reveals Its Function in DNA Interstrand Crosslink Repair Independent of Homologous Recombination.
review_notes: Dominant RAD51 variant (FANCR) with a role in interstrand crosslink repair separable from HR. Quote confirmed.

title: A novel Fanconi anaemia subtype associated with a dominant-negative mutation in RAD51.
review_notes: Dominant-negative RAD51 mutation defining a novel Fanconi anemia subtype (FANCR). Full text available.

title: TOPBP1 regulates RAD51 phosphorylation and chromatin loading and determines PARP inhibitor sensitivity.
review_notes: Moudry et al.; TOPBP1 promotes PLK1-mediated RAD51 Ser14 phosphorylation required for RAD51 chromatin loading and foci formation in HR. Verified against cached record; supports the DSB-repair and chromosome-localization rows for which it is the original reference.

title: The β-isoform of BCCIP promotes ADP release from the RAD51 presynaptic filament and enhances homologous DNA pairing.
review_notes: Describes RAD51 presynaptic filament, homology search, strand invasion and D-loop formation. Full text; quote confirmed.

title: Cryo-EM structures of RAD51 assembled on nucleosomes containing a DSB site.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of RAD51 assembled on DSB-containing nucleosomes; filament binds and peels nucleosomal DNA. Quote confirmed.

title: Purification and characterization of the human Rad51 protein, an analogue of E. coli RecA.
review_notes: Baumann et al.; establishes human RAD51 ss/dsDNA binding, DNA-dependent ATPase and helical nucleoprotein filament formation. Verbatim quote confirmed.

title: Human Rad51 protein promotes ATP-dependent homologous pairing and strand transfer reactions in vitro.
review_notes: Baumann & West; human RAD51 promotes ATP-dependent homologous pairing and strand transfer in vitro. Verbatim quote confirmed.

title: Activities of human recombination protein Rad51.
review_notes: Gupta, Bazemore, Golub & Radding (1997 PNAS); purified human RAD51 catalyzes DNA-dependent ATP hydrolysis, homologous pairing and strand exchange, and forms stable presynaptic complexes, with homologous pairing/strand exchange more tightly coupled to ATP hydrolysis than in RecA. Foundational human-RAD51 recombinase paper surfaced by the Affinage record; verified against cached full text and attached to core_functions (strand exchange, ATP hydrolysis).

title: Identification and purification of two distinct complexes containing the five RAD51 paralogs.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified. Establishes the two RAD51C-containing complexes (BCDX2 and CX3) by purification and shows BCDX2 binds ssDNA, ss gaps and nicks. Foundational for the complex and DNA-binding annotations.

title: Mediator function of the human Rad51B-Rad51C complex in Rad51/RPA-catalyzed DNA strand exchange.
review_notes: Verified (PubMed abstract). Original biochemical demonstration that the RAD51B-RAD51C complex has ssDNA-binding and ssDNA-stimulated ATPase activity and acts as a recombination mediator by partially relieving RPA competition for ssDNA, promoting RAD51-ssDNA filament assembly. Primary support for the BCDX2 HR-mediator core function (previously supported only by the later cryo-EM and epistasis papers).

title: Mammalian Rad51C contributes to DNA cross-link resistance, sister chromatid cohesion and genomic stability.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). RAD51C-mutant hamster CL-V4B cells show cross-link (MMC/cisplatin) hypersensitivity, impaired RAD51 focus formation, genomic instability, and a reduced level of sister chromatid cohesion (complemented by Rad51C cDNA). Direct experimental support for the sister-chromatid-cohesion (GO:0007062) and ICL-repair annotations.

title: Identification of functional domains in the RAD51L2 (RAD51C) protein and its requirement for gene conversion.
review_notes: Verified. Shows RAD51C ATP-binding domain (K131) is required for function, nuclear localization with a C-terminal NLS, and a requirement for gene conversion (HR).

title: RAD51C is required for Holliday junction processing in mammalian cells.
review_notes: Verified. RAD51C depletion reduces branch migration/HJ resolvase activity in extracts. Supports RAD51C's role in HJ processing, but the endonucleolytic catalysis was later attributed to GEN1; hence the crossover-junction endonuclease MF is marked over-annotated.

title: Cellular localization of human Rad51C and regulation of ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis of Rad51.
review_notes: Verified. Detects endogenous RAD51C in nucleus, cytoplasm and perinuclear region and shows RAD51C regulates ubiquitin-mediated RAD51 proteolysis.

title: Role of RAD51C and XRCC3 in genetic recombination and DNA repair.
review_notes: Verified (PubMed abstract). Shows RAD51C localizes to mouse meiotic chromosomes at pachytene/diplotene and that Holliday-junction resolvase activity co-elutes with the CX3 (RAD51C-XRCC3) complex, which associates with crossovers. Supports the non-core meiotic reciprocal-recombination annotation.

title: RAD51C deficiency in mice results in early prophase I arrest in males and sister chromatid separation at metaphase II in females.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). Hypomorphic Rad51c mice show sexually dimorphic meiotic defects: early prophase I arrest in spermatocytes (early RAD51-mediated recombination role) and precocious sister-chromatid separation/aneuploidy in oocytes. Supports the non-core meiotic recombinase-assembly annotation.

title: RAD51C facilitates checkpoint signaling by promoting CHK2 phosphorylation.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). Establishes RAD51C's early DDR role: recruitment dependent on ATM/NBS1/RPA and requirement for CHK2 activation and cell-cycle arrest.

title: Ring-shaped Rad51 paralog protein complexes bind Holliday junctions and replication forks as visualized by electron microscopy.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). Direct EM evidence that BCDX2 and CX3 bind Holliday junctions and replication forks with high specificity as ring-shaped complexes.

title: Mutation of the RAD51C gene in a Fanconi anemia-like disorder.
review_notes: Verified (PubMed abstract). Identifies a homozygous RAD51C missense mutation in a consanguineous FA-like family, establishing RAD51C as the Fanconi anemia complementation group O (FANCO) gene; patient cells lose RAD51 focus formation and are hypersensitive to MMC and camptothecin. Primary support for the NEW interstrand-cross-link-repair (GO:0036297) annotation.

title: Discovery of a novel function for human Rad51: maintenance of the mitochondrial genome.
review_notes: Verified. Demonstrates mitochondrial localization of RAD51C (with RAD51/XRCC3) and a role in maintaining mtDNA copy number under oxidative stress. Supports the non-core mitochondrial annotations.

title: The RAD51 paralogs ensure cellular protection against mitotic defects and aneuploidy.
review_notes: Verified. RAD51B/RAD51C depletion causes G2/M arrest; XRCC3 acts with GEN1 at HJ resolution. Supports the non-core G2/M annotation and the reassignment of resolvase catalysis to GEN1.

title: Rad51 paralog complexes BCDX2 and CX3 act at different stages in the BRCA1-BRCA2-dependent homologous recombination pathway.
review_notes: Verified (PMC). Epistasis places BCDX2 downstream of BRCA2/upstream of RAD51 and CX3 downstream of RAD51 within BRCA-dependent HR. Core evidence for the DSB-repair-via-HR role.

title: Breast cancer-associated missense mutants of the PALB2 WD40 domain, which directly binds RAD51C, RAD51 and BRCA2, disrupt DNA repair.
review_notes: Verified. Shows RAD51C is part of a PALB2-BRCA2-containing HR complex and characterizes FANCO/BROVCA3 variants that disrupt these interactions.

title: Mammalian RAD51 paralogs protect nascent DNA at stalled forks and mediate replication restart.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). Directly demonstrates RAD51C protects nascent DNA at stalled forks and promotes ATP-hydrolysis-dependent restart; patient mutations abolish fork protection.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; supports a protein-binding IPI only (uninformative MF).

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; supports a protein-binding IPI only (uninformative MF).

title: Sequential role of RAD51 paralog complexes in replication fork remodeling and restart.
review_notes: Supports the sequential action of RAD51 paralog complexes at replication forks and the replication-fork localization annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome; supports a protein-binding IPI only (uninformative MF).

title: A protein interaction landscape of breast cancer.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; supports a protein-binding IPI only (uninformative MF).

title: Structure and function of the RAD51B-RAD51C-RAD51D-XRCC2 tumour suppressor.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). Cryo-EM/biochemistry showing BCDX2 stimulates RAD51 filament nucleation and extension via coupled RAD51B/RAD51C ATPases. Key structural support for the RAD51-filament-mediator core function.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: High-throughput cell-map interactome; supports a protein-binding IPI only.

title: Isolation and characterization of RAD51C, a new human member of the RAD51 family of related genes.
review_notes: Verified. Original RAD51C isolation; family membership, testis-high expression, and Y2H interactions with XRCC3 and RAD51B. Supports the historical DNA-binding/repair/recombination TAS annotations.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO (IPR039731) pipeline reference. The CAAX-box protein processing mapping it produces is correct, but the metalloendopeptidase activity mapping from the same reference is the wrong catalytic class for this glutamate-type protease.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO phylogenetic (IBA) reference. The ER-membrane and CAAX-box protein processing inferences are correct, but the metalloendopeptidase-activity inference propagated in the same tree assigns the wrong catalytic class.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA electronic annotations (endopeptidase activity, CAAX-box protein maturation). Both are correct, if general; endopeptidase is refined here to the glutamic-type class.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Automated multi-method IEA producing the ER-membrane location (via UniProtKB-SubCell SL-0097), consistent with the experimental localization.

title: Cloning and characterization of a mammalian prenyl protein-specific protease.
review_notes: Foundational RCE1 characterization paper; PubMed-verified. Establishes the CAAX-processing protease function, prenyl-substrate specificity, and substrate range. Abstract-only in the cache (full_text_available: false); experimental IDA annotations derive from the full text read by the curator.

title: USP17 regulates Ras activation and cell proliferation by blocking RCE1 activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports RCE1 endopeptidase activity, ER-membrane localization, the CAAX/Ras-processing role, and ubiquitination-dependent activity regulation. Abstract-only in the cache; IDA/IMP annotations derive from the full text.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput proteomics dataset (HDA). Provides only a generic membrane-localization datapoint, uninformative relative to the specific ER-membrane annotations.

title: RAF/MAP kinase cascade
review_notes: Reactome pathway. RCE1 is connected only indirectly (via processing of its Ras substrates upstream of the cascade), so the MAPK-cascade annotation is downstream/non-core.

title: USP17 deubiquitinates RCE1, CDC25A, DDX58, IFIH1
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing USP17-mediated deubiquitination/inhibition of RCE1. Supports the regulation biology; its cytosol compartment placement is a reaction abstraction, not RCE1 residence.

title: RCE1 cleaves S-Farn proRAS proteins
review_notes: Reactome reaction directly modeling the RCE1 CAAX-cleavage step at the ER membrane. Note the associated Reactome molecular-function call (cysteine-type endopeptidase) is the wrong catalytic class.

title: USP17L2 deubiquitinates RCE1
review_notes: Reactome reaction for USP17L2-mediated deubiquitination/inactivation of RCE1 at the ER membrane; supports the ER localization and activity-regulation biology.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS pipeline reference; the WITH/FROM source is the paralog RDH12 (Q96NR8). The transferred retinol-metabolic-process BP is independently correct for RDH11, but the NAD+-cofactor MF term is mis-transferred (RDH11 prefers NADP).

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SubCell mapping to ER membrane; concordant with experimental localization.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl-Compara transfer from mouse Rdh11 (Q9QYF1). Supports visual perception (non-core) but also propagates aldehyde-detoxification / aldehyde-dehydrogenase terms that are poorly supported (species difference) or wrong-reaction for the human protein.

title: Automatic Gene Ontology annotation based on Rhea mapping
review_notes: Rhea-mapped enzymatic terms; chemically correct for the NADP-dependent retinol dehydrogenase reactions.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined IEA supporting the core NADP-dependent retinol dehydrogenase activity and retinol metabolic process.

title: Evidence that the human gene for prostate short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase (PSDR1) encodes a novel retinal reductase (RalR1).
review_notes: Primary enzymatic characterization of human RDH11; abstract-only in cache but cited by UniProt for CATALYTIC ACTIVITY, FUNCTION and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION.

title: Dual-substrate specificity short chain retinol dehydrogenases from the vertebrate retina.
review_notes: Establishes dual-substrate (all-trans + cis) specificity and RPE context; abstract-only in cache.

title: Characterization of mouse short-chain aldehyde reductase (SCALD), an enzyme regulated by sterol regulatory element-binding proteins.
review_notes: Characterizes the MOUSE ortholog (SCALD). Source of the aldehyde-detoxification and retinal-metabolism annotations; abstract-only. Human RDH11 is weaker on toxic aldehydes (UniProt CAUTION), so detox terms are non-core for the human gene.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome screen; supports only generic protein binding, not a specific RDH11 function.

title: The interaction of selenoprotein F (SELENOF) with retinol dehydrogenase 11 (RDH11) implied a role of SELENOF in vitamin A metabolism.
review_notes: Targeted interaction + activity-regulation study; full text available. Confirms RDH11 catalytic direction and SELENOF-mediated inhibition.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome screen; supports only generic protein binding.

title: Dual-substrate specificity short chain retinol dehydrogenases from the vertebrate retina.
review_notes: PubMed-verified original identification and enzymatic characterization of RDH12; abstract-only cache but the substrate-specificity claims are explicit in the abstract.

title: Biochemical properties of purified human retinol dehydrogenase 12 (RDH12): catalytic efficiency toward retinoids and C9 aldehydes and effects of cellular retinol-binding protein type I (CRBPI) and cellular retinaldehyde-binding protein (CRALBP) on the oxidation and reduction of retinoids.
review_notes: PubMed-verified biochemical characterization of purified human RDH12; basis for cofactor preference and ER-membrane localization.

title: Retinol dehydrogenase 12 detoxifies 4-hydroxynonenal in photoreceptor cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available in cache. Establishes the in-vivo aldehyde-detoxification (GO:0110095) role and inner-segment localization.

title: Disease-associated variants of microsomal retinol dehydrogenase 12 (RDH12) are degraded at mutant-specific rates.
review_notes: Basis for one IPI "protein binding" annotation (UBC/ubiquitin partner); concerns variant protein degradation rather than a specific RDH12 molecular function.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome screen; source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (partner RBPMS). No RDH12-specific functional content.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Large-scale interaction-perturbation study; source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (RBPMS isoform). Uninformative for molecular function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome; source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (partner PLEKHA7). Uninformative for molecular function.

title: Mutations in the gene encoding 11-cis retinol dehydrogenase cause delayed dark adaptation and fundus albipunctatus.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. First demonstration that RDH5 mutations cause fundus albipunctatus; supports the visual perception annotation.

title: Biochemical defects in 11-cis-retinol dehydrogenase mutants associated with fundus albipunctatus.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Source of the homodimer, ER-membrane/lumenal-side localization, and 11-cis-retinol dehydrogenase activity IDA annotations.

title: Inhibition of dihydrotestosterone synthesis in prostate cancer by combined frontdoor and backdoor pathway blockade.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text. Documents RDH5's secondary (extra-ocular) 3-alpha-oxidoreductase activity in prostate androgen metabolism; non-core relative to the visual cycle.

title: Identification and characterization of a stereospecific human enzyme that catalyzes 9-cis-retinol oxidation. A possible role in 9-cis-retinoic acid formation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes cis-retinol substrate specificity and NAD+ preference; key evidence that the all-trans-retinol dehydrogenase term is the wrong substrate for RDH5.

title: Activity of human 11-cis-retinol dehydrogenase (Rdh5) with steroids and retinoids and expression of its mRNA in extra-ocular human tissue.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Source of the retinoid and steroid (androsterone / androstanediol) dehydrogenase IDA annotations.

title: Identification and characterization of all-trans-retinol dehydrogenase from photoreceptor outer segments, the visual cycle enzyme that reduces all-trans-retinal to all-trans-retinol.
review_notes: Cached abstract-only record (full_text_available: false); title matches UniProt reference [1]. Establishes RDH8/prRDH identity, NADPH-dependent all-trans-retinal reductase activity, and exclusive photoreceptor outer segment membrane localization. The 17beta-HSD1 relationship is a homology statement, not a demonstration of steroid activity.

title: Reelin is a ligand for lipoprotein receptors.
review_notes: Cached abstract directly establishes receptor binding and links it to DAB1 phosphorylation and neuronal migration.

title: Autosomal recessive lissencephaly with cerebellar hypoplasia is associated with human RELN mutations.
review_notes: Human genetic evidence establishes an essential developmental role and supports secretion and receptor binding.

title: Reelin is a serine protease of the extracellular matrix.
review_notes: Correctly cited primary report, but its protease conclusion was directly challenged by PMID:20522975.

title: Binding of purified Reelin to ApoER2 and VLDLR mediates tyrosine phosphorylation of Disabled-1.
review_notes: Cached abstract directly supports receptor-dependent DAB1 phosphorylation.

title: Re-evaluation of protease activity of reelin.
review_notes: Primary re-evaluation directly contradicts the earlier protease assignment, leaving the GO molecular-function claim unresolved.

title: Migration, early axonogenesis, and Reelin-dependent layer-forming behavior of early/posterior-born Purkinje cells in the developing mouse lateral cerebellum.
review_notes: Full-text mouse study supports a narrowly scoped cerebellar layer-forming outcome; it does not justify generalizing the mechanism to every Purkinje cell or directly to human development.

title: Functional importance of covalent homodimer of reelin protein linked via its central region.
review_notes: Cached abstract directly supports homodimer formation, receptor binding by the C2101A mutant, and loss of signaling by that mutant.

title: The functions of Reelin in membrane trafficking and cytoskeletal dynamics: implications for neuronal migration, polarization and differentiation.
review_notes: Review abstract supports the canonical pathway and distinguishes developmental migration and polarization from adult synaptic outcomes.

title: MatrisomeDB 2.0: 2023 updates to the ECM-protein knowledge database.
review_notes: Correct database publication for the MatrisomeDB-derived extracellular-matrix classification; the narrative is not a gene-specific RELN experiment.

title: Regulation of endoplasmic reticulum turnover by selective autophagy.
review_notes: Foundational ER-phagy paper establishing the FAM134 family (including FAM134A/RETREG2) as ER-phagy receptors. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Role of FAM134 paralogues in endoplasmic reticulum remodeling, ER-phagy, and Collagen quality control.
review_notes: Full text available. Establishes RETREG2/FAM134A-specific ER-phagy function, stress-activation, ER membrane localization, and collagen quality control role.

title: Crystal structure of human riboflavin kinase reveals a beta barrel fold and a novel active site arch.
review_notes: PubMed-verified structure paper on human RFK (PDB 1NB0/1NB9/1P4M/1Q9S). Establishes the beta-barrel fold and confirms the riboflavin-kinase catalytic function; abstract supports the function and localization (cytoplasm) claims. GOA reuses it as the NAS source. The riboflavin biosynthetic process NAS is a minor mislabel (should be riboflavin metabolic process for a human salvage/utilization enzyme).

title: Riboflavin kinase couples TNF receptor 1 to NADPH oxidase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Primary experimental source for human RFK riboflavin kinase activity (IDA), the TNFRSF1A/CYBA physical interactions, and the NADPH-oxidase/ROS moonlighting role. Abstract-only in the cache (full_text_available: false); quoted claims are verbatim from the abstract.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome (Y2H) reference map; source of the RFK-CNTLN protein-binding IPI (also recorded in UniProt). Large-scale interaction screen with no RFK-specific functional characterization; contextual/background relevance only.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Large-scale human mitochondrial-proteome dataset; source of the HTP mitochondrion localization. Such datasets can include cytosolic proteins, and RFK's curated location is cytoplasm/cytosol, so this is treated as a non-core localization.

title: Translocation of lipid-linked oligosaccharides across the ER membrane requires Rft1 protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The founding genetic paper for the flippase model. Correctly cited, but its conclusion is the contested one - the authors show Rft1 is "required for" translocation in vivo, which later biochemistry (PMID:18668045, PMID:19494107) and genetics (PMID:23720757) showed does not entail that Rft1 catalyses the step. A formal Brief Communication Arising was published against it.

title: Human RFT1 deficiency leads to a disorder of N-linked glycosylation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the index RFT1-CDG paper and the source of the IMP and IGI rows in GOA. The mutant-phenotype and rescue data are solid and uncontested; only the mechanistic gloss ("translocation") inherits the family controversy.

title: Does Rft1 flip an N-glycan lipid precursor?
review_notes: PubMed-verified Nature Brief Communication Arising against PMID:11807558. This is the paper that opened the controversy and it is essential context for any RFT1 molecular function annotation; it was absent from the previous version of this review.

title: Specific transbilayer translocation of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides by an endoplasmic reticulum flippase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Characterizes a specific ER M5-DLO flippase activity biochemically; relevant as background for the claim that flipping activity exists independently of Rft1, but does not assay RFT1 itself.

title: Suppression of Rft1 expression does not impair the transbilayer movement of Man5GlcNAc2-P-P-dolichol in sealed microsomes from yeast.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Direct counter-evidence to the catalytic-flippase reading of the yeast genetics; the key observation is that the same Rft1-depleted cells that accumulate M5-DLO have undiminished flippase activity in sealed microsomes.

title: RFT1 deficiency in three novel CDG patients.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cited by UniProt for Q96AA3 but missing from the previous version of this review. Independent replication of the RFT1-CDG phenotype and rescue across three additional patients and two novel alleles.

title: Glycoprotein biosynthesis in a eukaryote lacking the membrane protein Rft1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The strongest in-vivo argument against the obligate-flippase model - an entire eukaryote lives, flips M5-DLO and N-glycosylates without Rft1. Also the origin of the chaperone hypothesis.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Correctly cited for the HuRI Y2H interactions, but it is a systematic screen with no RFT1-specific follow-up; it supports only the uninformative GO:0005515 term, which this review removes.

title: Rft1 catalyzes lipid-linked oligosaccharide translocation across the ER membrane.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text checked. Importantly for the human annotation, recombinant human RFT1 was assayed alongside the yeast and archaeal proteins, so the human IDA is not a cross-species transfer. The title states the strongest reading; the data establish the in-vitro activity, and later work (PMID:42417535) accepts the activity while contesting that it is the essential cellular role.

title: Molecular characterization of Rft1, an ER membrane protein associated with congenital disorder of glycosylation RFT1-CDG.
review_notes: PubMed-verified peer-reviewed JBC version (the bioRxiv preprint is PMID:38617304). Published after PMID:38886340 and still treating the essential role as unknown, which is the clearest evidence that the controversy was not closed by the reconstitution paper. title: OpenScientist family-constraint analysis - is the substrate cavity or the lipid portal the conserved surface of the RFT1 fold?
review_notes: Second independent computational run, framed on wild-type family constraint with disease variants excluded as both input and selection criterion. Unlike the first run this one performed real statistics - a 3,826-sequence Pfam PF04506 alignment, Henikoff-weighted Kullback-Leibler constraint per column, geometric classification against the AlphaFold model with stated criteria, and four controls (second metric, composition, 20,000-draw permutation null, membrane-axis perturbation), plus axis-independent continuous correlations. The Pfam family identity and its eukaryote-only taxonomic spread were checked against InterPro. One caveat the run does not draw itself is recorded in the gene notes - lipid-facing transmembrane residues are the fastest-evolving class in essentially every membrane protein, which the run confirms as its own frame sanity check, so low constraint at portal-lining positions has limited power to show the portal is non-functional. Its numbers live only in the report prose - unlike the first run it emitted no data artifacts, and no citations file was written.

title: OpenScientist structural analysis - do RFT1-CDG residues line the substrate cavity or the lipid portal?
review_notes: Independent computational run commissioned for this review, deliberately framed with both mechanistic models stated symmetrically rather than reusing this review's rationale. Its literature citations were spot-checked and resolve correctly, including PMID:19267216. Its central negative result - that residue mapping cannot discriminate the two models because headgroup binding is required under both - is a correction to the premise the run was given, and is recorded here rather than being quietly dropped. One secondary claim is wrong and was not imported - it flags human Q9NWF4 and mouse Q9D8F3 as divergent RFT1 paralogs at risk of annotation transfer, but those are SLC52A1/Slc52a2 riboflavin transporters that merely carry RFT1 as a legacy gene symbol; the transfer hazard is real but is nomenclature, not paralogy. No local bioinformatics holdout existed for this gene, so nothing was leaked into the prompt. Superseded in one respect - its classification of E298 as exposed and outward-facing is not reproducible and is contradicted both by the family-constraint run and by the local check in RFT1-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md. That E298 call has therefore been withdrawn from the findings list below rather than carried forward as a structured assertion; the retraction is recorded here and in RFT1-notes.md.

title: Wnt signaling in midbrain dopaminergic neuron development and regenerative medicine for Parkinson's disease.
review_notes: Review supporting the coreceptor-activity TAS annotation.

title: ROR1 is essential for proper innervation of auditory hair cells and hearing in humans and mice.
review_notes: Source of the IMP Wnt receptor activity and inner-ear/hearing annotations.

title: IGFBP5 is an ROR1 ligand promoting glioblastoma invasion via ROR1/HER2-CREB signaling axis.
review_notes: Supports signaling-receptor activity and a proliferation/invasion phenotype.

title: Human neural tissues express a truncated Ror1 receptor tyrosine kinase, lacking both extracellular and transmembrane domains.
review_notes: Basis of the legacy TAS 'transmembrane RTK activity' annotation now REMOVEd as superseded.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Large-scale Y2H interactome screen (CCSB-HI1). Source of a self-self (identical protein binding) IPI reflecting the RPE homodimer; not functionally informative beyond the known homodimer.

title: Conversion of D-ribulose 5-phosphate to D-xylulose 5-phosphate: new insights from structural and biochemical studies on human RPE.
review_notes: Definitive structural and biochemical characterisation of human RPE: EC 5.1.3.1 activity, Fe2+ cofactor, TIM-barrel fold, catalytic aspartates, and mutagenesis. Supports the core MF, metal-binding, and PPP annotations.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Shotgun proteomics of prostatic-secretion exosomes (~900 proteins). Basis of the extracellular-exosome HDA annotation; a bulk detection, not evidence of functional extracellular localisation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale binary interactome map. Source of a self-self IPI reflecting the RPE homodimer.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome. Source of both a self-self IPI (homodimer) and a heterotypic RPE-PLEKHF2 (Q9H8W4) interaction; the latter underlies the bare protein-binding annotation and is corroborated by UniProt.

title: RPE dimers isomerize XY5P to RU5P
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing cytosolic RPE homodimer interconverting XY5P and RU5P; supports cytosol localisation and homodimer.

title: RPE dimers isomerise RU5P to XY5P
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing cytosolic RPE (Fe2+ cofactor) homodimer interconverting RU5P and XY5P; supports cytosol localisation, cofactor, and homodimer.

title: UniProt entry Q96AT9 (RPE_HUMAN)
review_notes: UniProt/Swiss-Prot record: FUNCTION, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY (EC 5.1.3.1, RHEA:13677), COFACTOR (divalent metal cations), SUBUNIT (homodimer), and the RPE-PLEKHF2 interaction.

title: A homozygosity-based search for mutations in patients with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa, using microsatellite markers.
review_notes: Case report / mutation-screening study; abstract-only cache. Supports RPE65 loss-of-function causing retinal dystrophy (basis for the IMP process annotations) but does not directly assay molecular function.

title: Identification of a novel palmitylation site essential for membrane association and isomerohydrolase activity of RPE65.
review_notes: Experimental (mass spectrometry, mutagenesis, subcellular fractionation, in vitro isomerohydrolase assay) establishing lipid-anchored membrane association; abstract-only cache.

title: Identification of key residues determining isomerohydrolase activity of human RPE65.
review_notes: Experimental characterization of human RPE65 isomerohydrolase activity and key catalytic-determining residues; abstract-only cache.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Proteome-scale AP-MS; the RPE65 interaction reported is with the chaperonin subunit CCT6B (Q92526), consistent with chaperonin-assisted folding rather than a functionally specific partnership. Supports only a generic protein-binding annotation.

title: RPE65 has an additional function as the lutein to meso-zeaxanthin isomerase in the vertebrate eye.
review_notes: Experimental (cell-culture overexpression, pharmacologic inhibition, structural docking) establishing the secondary lutein-to-meso-zeaxanthin isomerase activity (EC 5.3.3.22); abstract-only cache.

title: Insights into the pathogenesis of dominant retinitis pigmentosa associated with a D477G mutation in RPE65.
review_notes: Experimental (knock-in mouse, cell lines, structural analysis, isomerase activity assay) characterizing the RP87 D477G allele and confirming RPE65 isomerase catalytic activity; abstract-only cache.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale AP-MS (BioPlex 3.0); RPE65 interaction reported with chaperonin subunit CCT6B (Q92526). Supports only a generic protein-binding annotation.

title: Mutations in RPE65 cause autosomal recessive childhood-onset severe retinal dystrophy.
review_notes: Disease-gene identification linking RPE65 mutations to visual perception and vitamin-A metabolism; basis for the TAS process annotations. Abstract-only cache.

title: RPE65 isomero-hydrolyses atREs to 11cROL
review_notes: Curated Reactome reaction capturing the core isomerohydrolase step of the visual cycle.

title: The canonical retinoid cycle in rods (twilight vision)
review_notes: Curated Reactome pathway placing RPE65's isomerohydrolase step within the rod visual cycle.

title: Ribose-5-phosphate isomerase deficiency: new inborn error in the pentose phosphate pathway associated with a slowly progressive leukoencephalopathy.
review_notes: First described patient with RPI deficiency; measured deficient RPI activity (EC 5.3.1.6) in fibroblasts, elevated ribitol/D-arabitol, and identified causative RPIA variants. Cached entry is abstract-only but the abstract itself establishes the enzyme activity and disease.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: High-throughput yeast two-hybrid interactome map (CCSB-HI1); source of a bare protein-binding IPI, uninformative for RPIA molecular function.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome-mapping methodology (Stitch-seq); source of a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: Protein interaction network of alternatively spliced isoforms from brain links genetic risk factors for autism.
review_notes: Large-scale isoform interactome screen; source of a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale binary interactome map (HI-II-14); source of bare protein-binding IPIs.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Interactome-perturbation study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome community-network study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: An interactome perturbation framework prioritizes damaging missense mutations for developmental disorders.
review_notes: Interactome-perturbation framework; source of bare protein-binding IPIs.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Variant-interaction disruption study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome; source of bare protein-binding and identical-protein-binding (self) IPIs.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex dual proteome-scale affinity-capture networks; source of a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP high-throughput mitochondrial proteome; RPIA is an HTP hit only. Given the cytosolic localisation and absence of a transit peptide, the mitochondrial signal likely reflects co-purification rather than a genuine mitochondrial pool.

title: The ribose 5-phosphate isomerase-encoding gene is located immediately downstream from that encoding murine immunoglobulin kappa.
review_notes: Cloned the mouse/human RPI gene and showed a recombinant GST-RPI fusion is enzymatically active; basis for the NAS molecular-function annotation.

title: UniProtKB entry P49247 (RPIA_HUMAN)
review_notes: Swiss-Prot record; establishes EC 5.3.1.6, the RHEA:14657 reaction, the non-oxidative PPP pathway step, cytosolic family membership, and RPIA deficiency (MIM:608611).

title: Characterization and analysis of posttranslational modifications of the human large cytoplasmic ribosomal subunit proteins by mass spectrometry and Edman sequencing.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The study characterizes post-translational modifications of human large-subunit proteins and supports composition by inference; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The mRNA interactome supports association with polyadenylated-RNA-containing complexes but not a separable RPL36A RNA-binding mechanism; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: Structures of the human and Drosophila 80S ribosome.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. Human 80S cryo-EM directly supports cytosolic ribosome and large-subunit membership; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: Host factors that interact with the pestivirus N-terminal protease, Npro, are components of the ribonucleoprotein complex.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were verified. RPL36A is one of many ribosomal proteins recovered in the viral Npro pulldown, and the authors explicitly allow indirect complex capture.

title: Structure of the human 80S ribosome.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The human 80S structure supports cytoplasmic ribosome membership and translation; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: Structural snapshots of actively translating human ribosomes.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were verified. Cryo-EM structures of actively translating human ribosomes support large-subunit membership and cytoplasmic translation.

title: Expression of Muscle-Specific Ribosomal Protein L3-Like Impairs Myotube Growth.
review_notes: PubMed identity and full text were verified. The experiments perturb RPL3L in mouse myoblasts and never assay RPL36A; the paper does not support assigning the RPL3L fusion phenotype to RPL36A.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were verified. HuRI is a systematic binary-interaction resource; its RPL36A record is retained as interaction data but not an informative molecular function.

title: Structural snapshots of human pre-60S ribosomal particles before and after nuclear export.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were verified. Human pre-60S structures support eL42 incorporation into the large ribosomal subunit.

title: Knockdown of Muscle-Specific Ribosomal Protein L3-Like Enhances Muscle Function in Healthy and Dystrophic Mice.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. This mouse study knocks down Rpl3l and does not assay RPL36A, so it cannot support an RPL36A striated-muscle-contraction annotation.

title: Characterisation of an mRNA encoding a human ribosomal protein homologous to the yeast L44 ribosomal protein.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The early cloned cDNA establishes the human L44/eL42 homolog but is weaker than current structural evidence; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: Manual deep-research synthesis for human RPL36A
review_notes: Reviewer-authored synthesis of the complete GOA set, reviewed UniProt, cached structural and interaction papers, and the RPL3L citation mismatch.

title: Manual RPL36A curation notes
review_notes: Reviewer-authored decision log with provider failures, action rationale, citation boundaries, and experimental priorities.

title: UniProtKB record for human RPL36A (P83881)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProt record fetched by the project; used for identity, family, length, cytoplasmic localization, and experimentally supported large-subunit membership.

title: Functional second genes generated by retrotransposition of the X-linked ribosomal protein genes.
review_notes: PMID and title were verified against the cached record, and the open article was manually inspected. This study distinguishes RPL36AL from X-linked RPL36A at the gene and expression levels; it does not directly demonstrate incorporation of the encoded protein into ribosomes.

title: Lys53 of ribosomal protein L36AL and the CCA end of a tRNA at the P/E hybrid site are in close proximity on the human ribosome.
review_notes: PMID, title, and abstract were verified. The paper explicitly names RPL36AL and maps a ribosome-bound tRNA contact to Lys53, providing direct support for ribosomal tRNA binding; only the abstract is cached.

title: The CCA-end of P-tRNA Contacts Both the Human RPL36AL and the A-site Bound Translation Termination Factor eRF1 at the Peptidyl Transferase Center of the Human 80S Ribosome.
review_notes: PMID, title, methods, results, and discussion were verified in the cached full text. The recombinant construct is explicitly RPL36AL, making the tRNA-binding result paralog-specific. Claims of an independent peptidyl-tRNA-hydrolase activity were not converted into GO annotations.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: PMID, title, and full text were verified. The GOA row records a high-throughput RPL36AL-KRTAP10-7 binary interaction, but the study does not define a ribosomal or partner-specific molecular activity for RPL36AL.

title: E-cadherin interactome complexity and robustness resolved by quantitative proteomics.
review_notes: PMID, title, full narrative, and localization methodology were verified. The RPL36AL-specific nuclear call is not stated in the narrative and resides in a supplementary candidate table that was not accessible, so the citation is not fully adjudicated for this gene.

title: Functional involvement of a conserved motif in the middle region of the human ribosomal protein eL42 in translation.
review_notes: PMID, title, and abstract were verified. The abstract calls the construct human eL42 but does not provide an accession or distinguish the single-residue RPL36A/RPL36AL paralogs, so this family-level result was not used to create a paralog-specific elongation annotation.

title: Manual deep research synthesis for human RPL36AL
review_notes: Reviewer-authored synthesis of the fetched records, cached publications, open primary literature, current QuickGO term record, and explicit RPL36A sequence comparison.

title: Manual RPL36AL curation notes
review_notes: Reviewer-authored decision log with inline provenance and explicit exclusion of unsupported RPL36A transfers.

title: UniProtKB record for human RPL36AL (Q969Q0)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProt record fetched by the project and used for accession, sequence, family, modification, expression, complex, and localization metadata. Its RPL36AL sequence differs from RPL36A at residue 38 only.

title: Proteomic analysis of early melanosomes: identification of novel melanosomal proteins.
review_notes: Correctly cited proteomics of melanosome fractions; supports the melanosome CC annotation but as an ER-contaminant co-purification rather than a genuine RPN1 functional site.

title: Proteomic analysis of mammalian oligosaccharyltransferase reveals multiple subcomplexes that contain Sec61, TRAP, and two potential new subunits.
review_notes: Biochemical proteomics of mammalian OST; explicitly lists ribophorin I as an OST subunit. Basis of the contributes_to GO:0004579 TAS annotation.

title: Proteomic and bioinformatic characterization of the biogenesis and function of melanosomes.
review_notes: Correctly cited melanosome proteomics; supports the melanosome CC as a co-purified ER protein, not a core localization.

title: Ribophorin I acts as a substrate-specific facilitator of N-glycosylation.
review_notes: Directly about RPN1 function; establishes the substrate-specific facilitator model. Supports the IMP for protein N-linked glycosylation and the facilitator core function.

title: Cotranslational and posttranslational N-glycosylation of polypeptides by distinct mammalian OST isoforms.
review_notes: Full text assays ribophorin I directly; supports OST membership and interaction with STT3A/ STT3B. Basis of the STT3B IPI annotation.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: Correctly cited high-throughput RBP atlas, but the RNA-binding assignment is a screen-level call without a defined molecular function for RPN1; treated as an over-annotation.

title: Malectin forms a complex with ribophorin I for enhanced association with misfolded glycoproteins.
review_notes: Directly about the RPN1-malectin complex; supports a glycoprotein quality-control adapter role. Basis of the MLEC IPI annotation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
TMEM258 Is a Component of the Oligosaccharyltransferase Complex Controlling ER Stress and Intestinal Inflammation.
Histone Interaction Landscapes Visualized by Crosslinking Mass Spectrometry in Intact Cell Nuclei.
Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
Cryo-electron microscopy structures of human oligosaccharyltransferase complexes OST-A and OST-B.
review_notes: Structural basis for RPN1 membership in both OST complexes and its cotranslational substrate-presentation role. Supports GO:0160226/GO:0160227 IDAs.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
Kinase Interaction Network Expands Functional and Disease Roles of Human Kinases.
