review_notes: Review of SLX4-nuclease complexes; cited (NAS) for a broad DNA replication annotation that over-annotates SLX4's replication-associated repair role.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map foundation dataset; generic protein-binding IPI only.

title: Identification and analysis of short open reading frames (sORFs) in the initially annotated noncoding RNA LINC00493 from human cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biochem 2021;169:421-434). Establishes that the LINC00493 ORF is translated and that the peptide is mitochondrial; does not address molecular function. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: LINC00493-encoded microprotein SMIM26 exerts anti-metastatic activity in renal cell carcinoma.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (EMBO Rep 2023;24:e56282). Source of the AGK and SLC25A11 interactions and of the outer-membrane localisation. Note that GOA's protein kinase binding annotation from this paper misclassifies AGK, which is a lipid kinase. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Microprotein SMIM26 drives oxidative metabolism via serine-responsive mitochondrial translation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Cell 2025;85:2759-2775.e12). Correctly cited, but its inner-membrane localisation and direct mitoribosome binding are topologically hard to reconcile with the outer-membrane/intermembrane-space model of PMID:41991342. The disagreement is between papers, not a citation error. Cached record is abstract-only, so the supporting experiments could not be inspected.

title: The microprotein SMIM26 connects metabolite transporters of the outer and inner mitochondrial membranes and is essential for respiratory chain function.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Genes Dev 2026;40:912-935). The most complete characterisation of SMIM26 to date, with knockout cells, knockout mice and zebrafish mutants. Single-source for the intermembrane-space-spanning topology. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: A novel protein LZTFL1 regulates ciliary trafficking of the BBSome and Smoothened.
review_notes: Full text read from PMC3207910; directly supports ciliary localization and regulated SMO trafficking in human RPE1 cells.

title: Structural basis of Smoothened regulation by its extracellular domains.
review_notes: Full text read from PMC4970916; directly establishes cholesterol binding and its functional importance for SMO signaling.

title: Cryo-EM structure of oxysterol-bound human Smoothened coupled to a heterotrimeric G(i).
review_notes: Full text read from PMC6777001; directly supports class-F GPCR activity, oxysterol responsiveness, Gi coupling, and Hedgehog transduction.

title: Bi-allelic Variations of SMO in Humans Cause a Broad Spectrum of Developmental Anomalies Due to Abnormal Hedgehog Signaling.
review_notes: PubMed identifier and abstract verified; cache is abstract-only, so only abstract-supported human genetic and cellular claims were used.

title: Sterols in an intramolecular channel of Smoothened mediate Hedgehog signaling.
review_notes: Full text read from PMC7669734; directly supports sterol binding and sterol-controlled SMO signaling.

title: A PKA inhibitor motif within SMOOTHENED controls Hedgehog signal transduction.
review_notes: Full text read from PMC9696579; establishes the direct PKA-inhibitor mechanism and supports the proposed specific MF annotation.

title: GRK2 kinases in the primary cilium initiate SMOOTHENED-PKA signaling in the Hedgehog cascade.
review_notes: Full text read from PMC11322411; validates the ciliary SMO-GRK2-PKA mechanism across cellular and in vivo models.

title: Activating Smoothened mutations in sporadic basal-cell carcinoma.
review_notes: PubMed identifier and abstract verified. The cache is abstract-only; the pathway annotation is supported, while the exact contact-inhibition assay was left undecided.

title: Characterization of two patched receptors for the vertebrate hedgehog protein family.
review_notes: PubMed identifier and abstract verified. Supports the historical patched-binding annotation, retained as non-core because modern sterol-access models do not require a stable complex.

title: UniProtKB reviewed record for human SMO (Q99835)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot record Q99835 inspected locally; its mechanistic statements are anchored to the primary publications also reviewed here.

title: Cloning and characterization of a human polyamine oxidase that is inducible by polyamine analogue exposure.
review_notes: Founding characterization of human SMOX; UniProt cites this reference for the EC 1.5.3.16 catalytic activity. Abstract-only cache; claims anchored to the verbatim abstract and the UniProt EC evidence.

title: Identification and characterization of a novel flavin-containing spermine oxidase of mammalian cell origin.
review_notes: Directly establishes SMOX substrate specificity distinguishing it from PAOX. Verbatim substrate-preference text quoted in core_functions.

title: Cloning and characterization of multiple human polyamine oxidase splice variants that code for isoenzymes with different biochemical characteristics.
review_notes: Establishes the isoform diversity of SMOX and their spermine oxidase activity. Abstract-only cache.

title: Genomic identification and biochemical characterization of the mammalian polyamine oxidase involved in polyamine back-conversion.
review_notes: Primary focus is the N1-acetylpolyamine oxidase (PAOX), but the abstract explicitly discusses SMO and its opposite substrate preference; the SMOX IDA annotations (assigned by FlyBase from full text) are defensible.

title: Nuclear localization of human spermine oxidase isoforms - possible implications in drug response and disease etiology.
review_notes: Source of the experimental nuclear-localization and isoform-specific spermine catabolism annotations; verbatim confocal/nuclear-oxidation text quoted in reviews.

title: PAOs oxidise polyamines to amines
review_notes: Family-level Reactome reaction; its mention of xenobiotic action and peroxisomal localization is a PAO-family generalization not specific to soluble SMOX.

title: SMOX-3 oxidises SPN to SPM
review_notes: SMOX-specific Reactome reaction for spermine to spermidine oxidation.

title: Interconversion of polyamines
review_notes: Mixed biosynthetic/catabolic pathway; drives an over-broad polyamine-biosynthesis TAS annotation for the catabolic SMOX.

title: Function of the cloned putative neutral sphingomyelinase as lyso-platelet activating factor-phospholipase C.
review_notes: Key functional paper. PMID/EC (3.1.4.12) match the UniProt record. Abstract only in cache; establishes lyso-PAF-PLC as the dominant cellular activity.

title: Hydrolysis of sphingosylphosphocholine by neutral sphingomyelinases.
review_notes: PMID/DOI match the UniProt catalytic-activity references. Abstract only in cache; supports SM/SPC hydrolysis and the substrate-recognition determinant.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput BioPlex interactome; supports only generic protein binding, no specific SMPD2 molecular function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome map; supports only generic protein binding.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegeneration interactome map; supports only generic protein binding.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Cell-specific BioPlex interactome; supports only generic protein binding.

title: SMPD2 and 3 hydrolyze sphingomyelin (plasma membrane)
review_notes: Models SMPD2/3 plasma-membrane sphingomyelin hydrolysis to ceramide; consistent with the enzyme's activity and membrane localization.

title: TNF-α:TNFR1:NSMAF:GNB2L1 associates with SMPD2,3
review_notes: Family-level TNFR1 ceramide-signaling model for the SMPD2/3 pair; supports membrane association, not an SMPD2-specific core function.

title: Cloning and characterization of the mammalian brain-specific, Mg2+-dependent neutral sphingomyelinase.
review_notes: Cloning/characterization of nSMase2; establishes Mg2+-dependence, neutral pH optimum, activation by phosphatidylserine/unsaturated fatty acids, and Golgi colocalization. Abstract-only in cache but PubMed-verified as the SMPD3 primary description paper.

title: Hydrolysis of sphingosylphosphocholine by neutral sphingomyelinases.
review_notes: In vitro substrate-specificity study; source of the IDA sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase / catabolic-process annotations and the additional sphingosylphosphocholine and monoradyl-glycerophosphocholine catalytic activities.

title: Role for mammalian neutral sphingomyelinase 2 in confluence-induced growth arrest of MCF7 cells.
review_notes: Establishes endogenous nSMase2 as a bona fide neutral sphingomyelinase and growth suppressor coupled to G0/G1 arrest; documents plasma-membrane relocalization in confluent cells. Source of the EC 3.1.4.12 catalytic-activity assignment.

title: The Polycomb group protein EED couples TNF receptor 1 to neutral sphingomyelinase.
review_notes: Basis of the GO:0005515 IPI (nSMase2-EED / O75530 interaction). EED N-terminus binds the nSMase2 catalytic domain and functionally couples TNF-R1 to nSMase2 activation.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro (IPR024129) is mapped to GO:0050290 sphingomyelinase D activity, which is the wrong reaction for SMPD4 (a type-C sphingomyelinase, EC 3.1.4.12). The pipeline correctly identifies an SMPD4-family function, but the target GO term is incorrect.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS transfer from mouse ortholog (UniProtKB:Q6ZPR5) for nuclear envelope and sarcolemma; both are corroborated by human experimental data.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Phylogenetic (IBA/PAN-GO) inferences; the process terms are correct, but the family MF is propagated to GO:0050290 (SMase D), the wrong term for this type-C enzyme.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Subcellular-location mappings (Golgi membrane, nuclear envelope, ER membrane, sarcolemma) all consistent with experimental localization.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Automated mapping to GO:0004767 via RHEA:19253/EC:3.1.4.12 — the correct molecular function for SMPD4.

title: Novel tumor necrosis factor-responsive mammalian neutral sphingomyelinase-3 is a C-tail-anchored protein.
review_notes: Primary biochemical and localization characterization of human nSMase3. Abstract-only cache but the enzymatic and localization findings are the basis for the core annotations.

title: Neutral sphingomyelinase-3 is a DNA damage and nongenotoxic stress-regulated gene that is deregulated in human malignancies.
review_notes: Establishes ER localization and the stress-response/proapoptotic role. Abstract-only cache.

title: Neutral sphingomyelinase-3 mediates TNF-stimulated oxidant activity in skeletal muscle.
review_notes: Full text available; confirms catalytic activity, muscle localization (including sarcolemma), and a TNF/redox signalling role. Note the study is predominantly in mouse muscle and C2C12 myotubes with corroborating human diaphragm data.

title: Loss of SMPD4 Causes a Developmental Disorder Characterized by Microcephaly and Congenital Arthrogryposis.
review_notes: Full text available. Defines the human disease (NEDMABA) and the ER/nuclear-envelope and cell-fate role; source of the ER organization IMP and nuclear-envelope/outer-nuclear-membrane annotations.

title: SMPD4 hydrolyzes sphingomyelin (ER membrane)
review_notes: Reactome reaction placing SMPD4 sphingomyelin hydrolysis at the ER membrane; consistent with the experimental data.

title: Crystal structure of human spermine synthase: implications of substrate binding and catalytic mechanism.
review_notes: PMC full text available and read; directly establishes SMS structure, spermine synthase catalytic activity (EC 2.5.1.22), homodimer requirement, and catalytic residues. Underpins the EXP molecular-function annotation.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Abstract-only (full_text_available: false). Bulk exosome proteomics; supports only the HDA extracellular-exosome co-purification, which is an over-annotation for this cytosolic enzyme.

title: Sequence analysis of 139 kb in Xp22.1 containing spermine synthase and the 5' region of PEX.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Genomic locus/characterization paper; supports the gene's chromosomal location and its general role in polyamine metabolism (TAS annotation).

title: A quantitative protein interaction network for the ErbB receptors using protein microarrays.
review_notes: Large-scale SH2/PTB protein-microarray network for ErbB receptors. Supports a generic SOCS1-ERBB2 (P04626) protein interaction (GO:0005515), not a focused SOCS1 functional study. Peripheral to SOCS1 physiology.

title: The E3 ubiquitin ligase HOIL-1 induces the polyubiquitination and degradation of SOCS6 associated proteins.
review_notes: Primarily about SOCS6/HOIL-1. The IntAct interaction underlying the SOCS1 GO:0005515 annotation is with ELOC (Q15369). The paper does state the shared SOCS-box principle that all SOCS proteins bind an Elongin BC E3 complex through the common SOCS-box, consistent with SOCS1's Elongin-BC adaptor role.

title: COMMD1 promotes the ubiquitination of NF-kappaB subunits through a cullin-containing ubiquitin ligase.
review_notes: Demonstrates an ECS(SOCS1) E3 ligase containing Elongins B/C, Cul2 and SOCS1 that ubiquitinates NF-kB RelA, with SOCS1 binding RelA as substrate. Strong support for SOCS1's SOCS-box ubiquitin-ligase substrate-recognition adaptor function, although the GOA annotation it backs is the generic GO:0005515 protein binding.

title: SOCS1 is an inducible host factor during HIV-1 infection and regulates the intracellular trafficking and stability of HIV-1 Gag.
review_notes: Full text confirms SOCS1 directly binds HIV-1 Gag via its SH2 domain and that the SOCS box is required for Gag particle production. Host-pathogen interaction; supports GO:0005515 with gag (Q77YG1) but is not part of SOCS1's core cellular physiology.

title: Downregulation of inflammatory microRNAs by Ig-like transcript 3 is essential for the differentiation of human CD8(+) T suppressor cells.
review_notes: SOCS1 appears as a direct miR-155 target in ILT3-induced CD8+ T suppressor cells. The abstract does not establish a direct SOCS1 role in regulatory T cell differentiation; the IMP annotation to GO:0045591 rests on full text not in cache.

title: DCNL1 functions as a substrate sensor and activator of cullin 2-RING ligase.
review_notes: DCNL1/CUL2 neddylation study; SOCS1 is used as an ECS(SOCS1)/CRL2 component context. Supports the generic GO:0005515 interaction (DCUN1D1) and is consistent with SOCS1's CRL2/CRL5 substrate-receptor role.

title: MiR-221 accentuates IFN's anti-HCV effect by downregulating SOCS1 and SOCS3.
review_notes: Identifies SOCS1 (and SOCS3) as miR-221 targets and explicitly describes them as well established inhibitory factors on the IFN/JAK/STAT pathway, consistent with SOCS1's core negative regulation of JAK-STAT signaling.

title: Extensive rewiring of the EGFR network in colorectal cancer cells expressing transforming levels of KRAS(G13D).
review_notes: Large-scale AP-MS EGFR-network rewiring study; underlies a generic SOCS1-ELOC (Q15369) interaction (GO:0005515). Not a focused SOCS1 functional characterization.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI all-by-all binary interactome; supports a generic SOCS1-SH3GL1 (Q99961) interaction (GO:0005515). High-throughput, context-free.

title: Downregulation of microRNA-155-5p prevents immune thrombocytopenia by promoting macrophage M2 polarization via the SOCS1-dependent PD1/PDL1 pathway.
review_notes: SOCS1 is a validated miR-155-5p target; its up-regulation promotes macrophage M2 polarization via PD1/PDL1 in an ITP model. Supports a contextual role in macrophage polarization (IMP, GO:0030225) rather than a core SOCS1 molecular function.

title: Systematic discovery of mutation-directed neo-protein-protein interactions in cancer.
review_notes: Cancer neoPPI BRET screen; underlies a generic SOCS1-SMAD4 (Q13485) interaction (GO:0005515). High-throughput screen, not a focused SOCS1 study.

title: A family of cytokine-inducible inhibitors of signalling.
review_notes: Founding SOCS1 paper (Starr et al., Nature 1997). Cloned SOCS-1 by its ability to inhibit IL6-induced macrophage differentiation; SOCS-1 inhibits IL6-induced receptor phosphorylation and STAT activation and acts in a classic negative- feedback loop. Direct support for the protein kinase inhibitor / JAK-STAT negative regulation core functions.

title: A new protein containing an SH2 domain that inhibits JAK kinases.
review_notes: Founding SOCS1/JAB paper (Endo et al., Nature 1997). Shows JAB binds the JAK2 JH1 kinase domain and that interaction with Jak1/Jak2/Jak3 markedly reduces their tyrosine-kinase activity and suppresses STAT phosphorylation/activation. Direct support for JAK binding and kinase inhibition.

title: Interaction of human suppressor of cytokine signaling (SOCS)-2 with the insulin-like growth factor-I receptor.
review_notes: Principally about SOCS-2, but the abstract explicitly states that hSOCS-1 protein also interacted strongly with IGF-IR in the two-hybrid assay, supporting the SOCS1 IGF1R-binding (GO:0005159) and protein kinase binding (GO:0019901) IPI annotations. The NAS GO:0046426 here is a by-analogy assertion.

title: SOCS3 negatively regulates IL-6 signaling in vivo.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Croker et al., Nat Immunol 2003). Abstract directly supports the in vivo IL-6-specific JAK-STAT negative-regulation role; basis for the mouse-ortholog ISS transfers.

title: VHL-box and SOCS-box domains determine binding specificity for Cul2-Rbx1 and Cul5-Rbx2 modules of ubiquitin ligases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Kamura et al. 2004). Establishes the SOCS-box -> Elongin BC -> Cul5-Rbx2 E3 ligase substrate-recognition mechanism underlying SOCS3 ubiquitin-ligase function.

title: The role of microtubule-associated protein 1S in SOCS3 regulation of IL-6 signaling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; genuinely about SOCS3. Supports a specific binding partner (MAP1S/Q66K74) but the GOA annotation is generic 'protein binding'.

title: Enhanced prediction of Src homology 2 (SH2) domain binding potentials using a fluorescence polarization-derived c-Met, c-Kit, ErbB, and androgen receptor interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified methodological/proteomics paper. Source of generic 'protein binding' IPI annotations (KIT, MET); not gene-function-defining.

title: MiR-221 accentuates IFN׳s anti-HCV effect by downregulating SOCS1 and SOCS3.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports SOCS3 as a negative regulator of JAK-STAT (loss prolongs/enhances signaling); cited as IMP for GO:0046426.

title: PKD1 phosphorylation-dependent degradation of SNAIL by SCF-FBXO11 regulates epithelial-mesenchymal transition and metastasis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The paper's focus is FBXO11/SNAIL; SOCS3 appears only as an interaction partner. Source of a generic 'protein binding' annotation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: PubMed-verified high-throughput interactome (Rolland et al. 2014). Source of generic 'protein binding' IPI annotations; not function-defining.

title: Trans-presentation of IL-6 by dendritic cells is required for the priming of pathogenic T(H)17 cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Supports the IL-6/Th17 context cited as TAS for T-helper 17 cell lineage commitment.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified high-throughput interactome (Luck et al. 2020). Source of generic 'protein binding' IPI annotations; not function-defining.

title: Cloning and functional analysis of new members of STAT induced STAT inhibitor (SSI) family: SSI-2 and SSI-3.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. SSI-3 = SOCS3; correctly cited. Abstract supports JAK-STAT inhibition and suppression of LIF-induced apoptosis (basis of TAS annotations).

title: Interaction of human suppressor of cytokine signaling (SOCS)-2 with the insulin-like growth factor-I receptor.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Abstract title foregrounds SOCS-2, but UniProt curators attribute the IDA protein-kinase-inhibitor-activity / plasma-membrane annotations for SOCS3 to this reference; per guidelines the kinase-inhibitor function is correct for SOCS3 and the experimental annotation is retained.

title: Falcon deep research report for SOD1
review_notes: LLM-generated synthesis (Edison/Falcon). It accurately recapitulates the well-established core picture of SOD1 (Cu/Zn dismutation of superoxide to H2O2 and O2 at the diffusion limit; copper redox cycling; Cu coordination by His46/His48/His63/His120 and Zn by His63/His71/His80/Asp83; CCS-mediated maturation with the Cys-Cys disulfide; cytosolic/IMS/nuclear localization). It also foregrounds a non-canonical metabolic-regulatory role in which SOD1-derived H2O2 oxidizes GAPDH and reroutes flux to the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway/NADPH (Montllor-Albalate et al. 2022 PNAS) and an emerging H2S-oxidase activity. These secondary claims are cited only to review-level/summary sources here and are not in GOA; individual primary PMIDs were not independently verified against the cache, so correctness is UNVERIFIED and these are treated as supporting context only, not grounds to add new annotations.

title: Neuronal sorting protein-related receptor sorLA/LR11 regulates processing of the amyloid precursor protein.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports SORL1 as an APP sorting receptor that reduces amyloidogenic peptide formation.

title: Interaction of the cytosolic domains of sorLA/LR11 with the amyloid precursor protein (APP) and beta-secretase beta-site APP-cleaving enzyme.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports the trafficking mechanism by which SORL1 prevents BACE-APP interactions rather than directly inhibiting BACE catalysis.

title: SorLA/LR11 regulates processing of amyloid precursor protein via interaction with adaptors GGA and PACS-1.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports SORL1 retention of APP in trans-Golgi compartments through GGA/PACS-1-dependent routing.

title: GGA1-mediated endocytic traffic of LR11/SorLA alters APP intracellular distribution and amyloid-β production.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports LR11/SORL1 endocytic trafficking as a regulator of APP intracellular distribution and amyloid-beta levels.

title: Lysosomal sorting of amyloid-β by the SORLA receptor is impaired by a familial Alzheimer's disease mutation.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports SORL1 amyloid-beta binding through the VPS10P domain and lysosomal targeting of nascent amyloid-beta peptides.

title: Signal peptidase complex subunit 1 participates in the assembly of hepatitis C virus through an interaction with E2 and NS2.
review_notes: Source of the HCV NS2/E2 interaction and virion-assembly host-factor role; secondary to SPCS1's core SPC function.

title: A CRISPR screen defines a signal peptide processing pathway required by flaviviruses.
review_notes: Genome-wide CRISPR screen establishing the flavivirus host-factor role; secondary to the core cellular function.

title: Host Factor SPCS1 Regulates the Replication of Japanese Encephalitis Virus through Interactions with Transmembrane Domains of NS2B.
review_notes: Mechanistic study of the flavivirus host-factor role via NS2B interaction; reaffirms SPCS1 is non-catalytic.

title: Signal peptidase complex subunit 1 is an essential Zika virus host factor in placental trophoblasts.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:33577859, doi:10.1016/j.virusres.2021.198338). Corroborates the flavivirus host-factor role of SPCS1 in a placental-trophoblast context; secondary to the core SPC function. Not in publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Structure of the human signal peptidase complex reveals the determinants for signal peptide cleavage.
review_notes: Definitive structural study establishing SPCS1 as an accessory SPC subunit and the membrane-thinning architecture; basis for ComplexPortal annotations.

title: SPCS1-Dependent E2-p7 processing determines HCV Assembly efficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:35130329, doi:10.1371/journal.ppat.1010310). Mechanistic study of the SPCS1 HCV host-factor role; supports the existing virion-assembly annotation. Secondary to the core SPC function. Not in publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Membrane topology of the 12- and the 25-kDa subunits of the mammalian signal peptidase complex.
review_notes: Establishes SPCS1 (SPC12) topology and SPC membership and the inference that it is not the catalytic subunit.

title: Interactomes of SARS-CoV-2 and human coronaviruses reveal host factors potentially affecting pathogenesis.
review_notes: High-throughput coronavirus interactome; the SPCS2-spike interaction is the source of the bare protein binding annotation and is not relevant to SPCS2's core function.

title: Structure of the human signal peptidase complex reveals the determinants for signal peptide cleavage.
review_notes: Definitive structural study establishing SPCS2 as an accessory SPC subunit; basis for ComplexPortal annotations.

title: Cleavage of the Jaw1 C-terminal region enhances its augmentative effect on the Ca2+ release via IP3 receptors.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:36789796, doi:10.1242/jcs.260439). Demonstrates a noncanonical SPC substrate (Jaw1) with SEC11A-paralog selectivity; SPCS2 is an accessory subunit of the executing complex but no SPCS2-specific role is assigned. Contextual for the expanded SPC substrate range. Not in publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Landscape of protein-protein interactions during hepatitis C virus assembly and release.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:38230952, doi:10.1128/spectrum.02562-22). High-throughput AP-MS interactome; SPCS2 among host factors binding HCV p7 and E2. Secondary host-pathogen context, not core function. Not in publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Spc2 modulates substrate- and cleavage site-selection in the yeast signal peptidase complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:39565596, doi:10.1083/jcb.202211035). Direct mechanistic evidence (in yeast Spc2, explicitly cross-referenced to human SPCS2) that the SPCS2 accessory subunit contributes to substrate and cleavage-site selection via membrane thinning, beyond the generic "enhances enzymatic activity" UniProt statement. Not in publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Quantitative interaction proteomics of neurodegenerative disease proteins.
review_notes: High-throughput interaction proteomics; source of a bare protein binding annotation (ATXN1), not relevant to SPCS3's core function.

title: A CRISPR screen defines a signal peptide processing pathway required by flaviviruses.
review_notes: Genome-wide CRISPR screen establishing the flavivirus host-factor role; secondary to the core cellular function.

title: Inverting the Topology of a Transmembrane Protein by Regulating the Translocation of the First Transmembrane Helix.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; full text not available. Source of the SPCS3 IDA proteolysis annotation made by a curator with full-text access; retained per guidelines.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput human interactome; source of a bare protein binding annotation (SEC11C), an intra-complex interaction.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: High-throughput neurodegenerative-disease interactome; source of bare protein binding annotations (HTT, ATXN1).

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex proteome-scale interactome; source of bare protein binding annotations (SEC11A/SEC11C), intra-complex interactions.

title: Structure of the human signal peptidase complex reveals the determinants for signal peptide cleavage.
review_notes: Definitive structural study establishing SPCS3 as an accessory SPC subunit; basis for ComplexPortal annotations.

title: Landscape of protein-protein interactions during hepatitis C virus assembly and release.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:38230952, doi:10.1128/spectrum.02562-22). High-throughput AP-MS interactome placing SPCS3 in the HCV E2 accessory interactome; secondary host-pathogen context, not core function. Not in publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Interaction of chikungunya virus glycoproteins with macrophage factors controls virion production.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:39261662, doi:10.1038/s44318-024-00193-3, EMBO J 2024). Notable new finding - SPCS3 acts as an antiviral restriction factor against CHIKV (an alphavirus, distinct from the flaviviral host-factor role) via E1 binding; Falcon reports this is peptidase-independent (overexpression did not alter CHIKV polyglycoprotein cleavage). A secondary host-pathogen/innate-immunity role, not the core SPC function. Not in publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map interactome; source of bare protein binding annotations (SEC11A/SEC11C), intra-complex interactions.

title: Cloning of ACP33 as a novel intracellular ligand of CD4.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2001;276:9123-32). Correctly cited and not contradicted; the CD4 interaction and the domain mapping are real. Its limitation is scope, not soundness - one screen, one cell context, no replication in twenty-five years - which is why the annotations derived from it are kept as non-core. Its most durable contribution is the observation that the alpha/beta hydrolase fold of this protein is non-catalytic and serves as an interaction module. Cached entry is abstract-only.

title: Maspardin is mutated in mast syndrome, a complicated form of hereditary spastic paraplegia associated with dementia.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Am J Hum Genet 2003;73:1147-56). The origin of both the gene-disease link and the catalytic-triad claim. The triad analysis is an alignment argument, explicitly hedged in the paper as 'suggests that it is unlikely to possess enzymatic function'; every later source traces back to it.

title: Interaction of the SPG21 protein ACP33/maspardin with the aldehyde dehydrogenase ALDH16A1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neurogenetics 2009;10:217-28). Cited here for its localisation data and its statement of the catalytic-triad inference. The ALDH16A1 interaction it reports has not been connected to the RAB7A effector mechanism and is not used to support any annotation in this review.

title: Targeted disruption of the Mast syndrome gene SPG21 in mice impairs hind limb function and alters axon branching in cultured cortical neurons.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neurogenetics 2010;11:369-78). Used for the explicit admission that the absence of enzymatic activity remains to be confirmed - the field's own statement of the knowledge gap. Note that its axon-branching phenotype is reported in the opposite direction to a later study (PMID:26978163), which is why no axon-branching annotation is proposed here.

title: Characterization of maspardin, responsible for human Mast syndrome, in an insect species and analysis of its evolution in metazoans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Naturwissenschaften 2012;99:537-43). Relevant chiefly for two contextual points: it restates the hedged pseudoenzyme inference, and it documents that maspardin is conserved across metazoans including insects - which is what makes a CD4-binding family-level assertion implausible. Cached entry is abstract-only.

title: Loss of Maspardin Attenuates the Growth and Maturation of Mouse Cortical Neurons.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neurodegener Dis 2016;16:260-72). Reports reduced axonal branching in SPG21-null mouse cortical neurons - the opposite direction to PMID:20661613, which reported increased branching in the same knockout. The 2026 J Cell Biol paper notes the discrepancy explicitly. Cited here only to record that the neuronal morphology phenotype is unsettled; no annotation is derived from it. Cached entry is abstract-only.

title: The hereditary spastic paraplegia type 21 (SPG21) protein is a RAB7A effector that promotes noncanonical mTORC1-catalyzed TFEB phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Biol Cell 2025;36:ar123, PMC12483374). One of the two independent 2025-2026 studies that establish the RAB7A effector function; includes the specificity control showing canonical mTORC1 substrates are unaffected. Published a few months before PMID:41400694 and reaching the same conclusion by different methods, which is why the effector call is treated as solid rather than provisional.

title: Maspardin/SPG21 controls lysosome motility and TFEB phosphorylation through RAB7 positioning.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Cell Biol 2026;225(2):e202501135, PMC12707310). Independent confirmation of the RAB7 effector function with a CRISPR knockout model, and the source of the lysosome-motility and RAB7-positioning mechanism. Its own discussion is careful about what is not established - it reports no maspardin interaction with VPS35 or TBC1D5 - which is the basis of the second knowledge gap here.

title: Functional characterization of human sphingosine kinase-1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; directly establishes the core sphingosine kinase activity and substrate specificity of human SPHK1.

title: Human sphingosine kinase: molecular cloning, functional characterization and tissue distribution.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; original cloning/characterization of human SPHK1.

title: Human sphingosine kinase: purification, molecular cloning and characterization of the native and recombinant enzymes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports calmodulin binding and Mg2+ cofactor requirement plus catalytic characterization.

title: 1-O-Hexadecyl-2-desoxy-2-amino-sn-glycerol, a substrate for human sphingosine kinase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; substrate-specificity study supporting the kinase activity.

title: Cloning and characterization of a protein kinase A anchoring protein (AKAP)-related protein that interacts with and regulates sphingosine kinase 1 activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of the SPHKAP (Q2M3C7) IPI, a regulatory interactor.

title: The nucleotide-binding site of human sphingosine kinase 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports ATP binding. Note the MGI "DNA binding" (GO:0003677) annotation citing this paper is unsupported by its content (it is a nucleotide-binding study).

title: Sphingosine kinase type 1 promotes estrogen-dependent tumorigenesis of breast cancer MCF-7 cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of the growth/migration/angiogenesis/mitotic downstream annotations.

title: Sphingosine kinase modulates microvascular tone and myogenic responses through activation of RhoA/Rho kinase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of the smooth-muscle-contraction downstream annotation.

title: Identification of functional nuclear export sequences in human sphingosine kinase 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports cytoplasm and nucleus localization/shuttling.

title: Phosphorylation-dependent translocation of sphingosine kinase to the plasma membrane drives its oncogenic signalling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Key mechanistic paper on activation/translocation and oncogenicity.

title: SphK1 and SphK2, sphingosine kinase isoenzymes with opposing functions in sphingolipid metabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports negative regulation of ceramide biosynthesis and anti-apoptotic role.

title: FHL2/SLIM3 decreases cardiomyocyte survival by inhibitory interaction with sphingosine kinase-1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of the FHL2 (Q14192) IPI.

title: Sphingosine kinase-1 is cleaved by cathepsin B in vitro: identification of the initial cleavage sites for the protease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of the cathepsin B (P07858) IPI (in vitro proteolysis).

title: Sphingosine 1-phosphate as a regulator of osteoclast differentiation and osteoclast-osteoblast coupling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of a TRAF6-related IntAct IPI in the SPHK1 record.

title: Eukaryotic elongation factor 1A interacts with sphingosine kinase and directly enhances its catalytic activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Source of the EEF1A1 (P68104) IPI and a regulatory activator of SK1.

title: Translocation of sphingosine kinase 1 to the plasma membrane is mediated by calcium- and integrin-binding protein 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports calmodulin binding, plasma membrane translocation, and the CIB1 (Q99828) IPI.

title: Sphingosine-1-phosphate is a missing cofactor for the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRAF2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Mechanistic basis for SPHK1's TNF/NF-kappaB and protein-ubiquitination annotations.

title: Guanine nucleotides regulate sphingosine kinase 1 activation by eukaryotic elongation factor 1A and provide a mechanism for eEF1A-associated oncogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of an EEF1A1 (P68104) IPI in the SPHK1 record.

title: A critical role for the protein phosphatase 2A B'α regulatory subunit in dephosphorylation of sphingosine kinase 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports the protein phosphatase 2A binding (GO:0051721) IPI and cytoplasm/plasma-membrane localization.

title: Sphingosine 1-phosphate induces filopodia formation through S1PR2 activation of ERM proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified paper, but it does NOT support assigning "sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor activity" (GO:0038036) to SPHK1: the receptor is S1PR2. The SPHK1 GO:0038036 IMP citing this paper is a mis-assignment of receptor activity to the kinase.

title: Molecular basis of sphingosine kinase 1 substrate recognition and catalysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; structural basis for the core kinase activity and ATP binding.

title: Sphingosine kinase 1 regulates tumor necrosis factor-mediated RANTES induction through p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase but independently of nuclear factor κB activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports response to TNF and positive regulation of p38MAPK cascade annotations.

title: Coupling between endocytosis and sphingosine kinase 1 recruitment.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Source of endosome/clathrin-pit/presynapse localization and lipid-binding (curvature-sensing) annotations.

title: Pathological roles of the VEGF/SphK pathway in Niemann-Pick type C neurons.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Supports the VEGF-response and kinase activity annotations.

title: Sphingosine and Sphingosine Kinase 1 Involvement in Endocytic Membrane Trafficking.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Supports the endocytosis/regulation of endocytosis annotations.

title: Neuronal SphK1 acetylates COX2 and contributes to pathogenesis in a model of Alzheimer's Disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Basis (largely By similarity in human) for acetyltransferase activity, protein acetylation, and neuroinflammation terms.

title: Molecular cloning and functional characterization of a novel mammalian sphingosine kinase type 2 isoform.
review_notes: Founding SPHK2 characterization paper; directly establishes the core sphingosine kinase activity. PubMed-verified.

title: Sphingosine kinase interacts with TRAF2 and dissects tumor necrosis factor-alpha signaling.
review_notes: Describes a SphK-TRAF2 interaction in a TNF/NF-kB context largely framed around SphK1; the specific attribution to SPHK2 is uncertain. Cited only for a bare protein-binding IPI, flagged as over-annotation.

title: Sphingosine kinase mediates vascular endothelial growth factor-induced activation of ras and mitogen-activated protein kinases.
review_notes: Basis of the NAS 'small GTPase binding' annotation to SPHK2, but the paper attributes the Ras/MAPK effect to SPHK1 (siRNA against SPK1, not SPK2, blocks it) and never assays SPHK2-GTPase binding. Does not support the SPHK2 annotation.

title: Sphingosine kinase 2 is a nuclear protein and inhibits DNA synthesis.
review_notes: Establishes nuclear localization (NLS) and the anti-proliferative/DNA-synthesis- inhibitory role of nuclear SPHK2. PubMed-verified.

title: Involvement of N-terminal-extended form of sphingosine kinase 2 in serum-dependent regulation of cell proliferation and apoptosis.

title: Alu RNA fold links splicing with signal recognition particle proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Borovska et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2023). Noncanonical Alu-exon splicing-regulation role of SRP9/14; distinct from the core SRP function.

title: Significance of signal recognition particle 9 nuclear translocation: implications for pancreatic cancer prognosis and functionality.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sato et al., Int J Oncol 2024). Biomarker/association-level finding; not core SRP9 molecular function.

title: The nucleolar phase of signal recognition particle assembly.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Issa et al., Life Sci Alliance 2024). Supports a nucleolar SRP-assembly compartment and nuclear localization of SRP9 during biogenesis.

title: The role of SRP9/SRP14 in regulating Alu RNA.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Gussakovsky et al., RNA Biol 2024). Synthesis of canonical and noncanonical SRP9/14 functions.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Cell map; captures SRP9-SRP14 interaction, bare protein binding.

title: Human signal recognition particle (SRP) Alu-associated protein also binds Alu interspersed repeat sequence RNAs. Characterization of human SRP9.
review_notes: Characterizes human SRP9 as the Alu RNA-binding protein within SRP; concerns SRP (not the SRP receptor).

title: A human protein-protein interaction network: a resource for annotating the proteome.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; source of an IPI protein-binding annotation.

title: The structure of the mammalian signal recognition particle (SRP) receptor as prototype for the interaction of small GTPases with Longin domains.
review_notes: Structural basis for the SRPRB-SRPRA heterodimer and SRPRB GTPase identity; source of SR-complex membership and targeting annotations.

title: Subcellular localization of APMCF1 and its biological significance of expression pattern in normal and malignant human tissues.
review_notes: Overexpression GFP-fusion localization study under the APMCF1 alias; diffuse cytoplasmic signal consistent with an ER-membrane protein.

title: Different effects of Sec61α, Sec62 and Sec63 depletion on transport of polypeptides into the endoplasmic reticulum of mammalian cells.
review_notes: Study of Sec61/62/63-dependent ER translocation; source of a generic membrane localization for SRPRB.

title: MTR120/KIAA1383, a novel microtubule-associated protein, promotes microtubule stability and ensures cytokinesis.
review_notes: Full text (now cached, full_text_available) is entirely about MTR120/KIAA1383 and never mentions or assays SRPRB (no occurrence of SRPRB / SR-beta / SRP receptor). The GO:0005881 cytoplasmic-microtubule IDA citing this paper is a wrong-gene mis-attribution and has been REMOVED, consistent with the sibling SERP1 review.

title: Structure of a prehandover mammalian ribosomal SRP·SRP receptor targeting complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:29567807; Science 2018). Structural basis for GTP-bound SRbeta in the targeting complex and delayed GTP hydrolysis during handover; directly informs SRPRB GTPase function and SR-complex role. Not cached; no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex affinity-MS interactome; source of an IPI protein-binding annotation.

title: Receptor compaction and GTPase rearrangement drive SRP-mediated cotranslational protein translocation into the ER.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:34020957; Sci Adv 2021). Mechanistic model of SR compaction and GTPase rearrangement during targeting; supports SRPRB GTP-binding/hydrolysis role in the receptor cycle. Not cached; no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Signal recognition particle receptor-β (SR-β) coordinates cotranslational N-glycosylation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:36921042; Sci Adv 2023). Newly described SRbeta function beyond receptor anchoring (coordinating cotranslational N-glycosylation via OST engagement, GTP-dependent). Not cached; no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Examining SRP pathway function in mRNA localization to the endoplasmic reticulum.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:37643813; RNA 2023). Direct human SRPRB knockout evidence that SRbeta stabilizes SRalpha at the ER; refines models of SR-dependent mRNA localization. Not cached; no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map interactome; source of an IPI protein-binding annotation.

title: Expression of SRPRB (SRP Receptor subunit beta)
review_notes: Reactome record; source of a TAS ER membrane localization for SRPRB.

title: Expression cloning of mouse cDNA of CMP-NeuAc:Lactosylceramide alpha2,3-sialyltransferase, an enzyme that initiates the synthesis of gangliosides.
review_notes: PubMed-verified mouse orthologue cloning paper (abstract-only in cache). Directly supports the GM3 synthase / sialyltransferase and ganglioside/ glycosphingolipid biosynthesis annotations; used by PINC as the TAS source for the human entry.

title: Expression cloning and functional characterization of human cDNA for ganglioside GM3 synthase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary human cloning/characterization paper (abstract-only in cache). Basis of the UniProtKB IDA to GO:0047291 and the IC to ganglioside biosynthesis.

title: Screening of hepatocyte proteins binding to F protein of hepatitis C virus by yeast two-hybrid system.
review_notes: Verified against the cached full text: a yeast two-hybrid screen for hepatocyte proteins binding HCV F protein, in which "1 colony was sialyltransferase" among 36 colonies, with no ST6GAL1-specific validation. This is a generic, weakly supported protein-binding (IPI) annotation that does not inform ST6GAL1 function and is recommended for removal.

title: Golgi N-glycosyltransferases form both homo- and heterodimeric enzyme complexes in live cells.
review_notes: Cached full text confirms BiFC and biochemical evidence for ST6GAL1 Golgi localization and homodimerization (GO:0000139 IDA, GO:0042803 IDA).

title: Universal phosphatase-coupled glycosyltransferase assay.
review_notes: Abstract verifies direct enzymatic measurement of ST6GAL1; supports sialyltransferase activity but the assigned parent term GO:0008373 should be refined to GO:0003835.

title: The structure of human α-2,6-sialyltransferase reveals the binding mode of complex glycans.
review_notes: Abstract verified (full text not cached). Strongest structural/mechanistic support for the core alpha-2,6-sialyltransferase activity (GO:0003835, IDA).

title: Controlled tetra-Fc sialylation of IVIg results in a drug candidate with consistent enhanced anti-inflammatory activity.
review_notes: Cached full text confirms ST6GAL1-mediated Fc sialylation; supports the core MF (EXP GO:0003835) and the IgG anti-inflammatory context.

title: Multi-level glyco-engineering techniques to generate IgG with defined Fc-glycans.
review_notes: UniProt-cited (PATHWAY) support for ST6GAL1's role in the IgG glycosylation pathway; corroborates the core sialyltransferase function.

title: Network inference from glycoproteomics data reveals new reactions in the IgG glycosylation pathway.
review_notes: UniProt-cited (SUBCELLULAR LOCATION / PATHWAY) support corroborating ST6GAL1's glycosylation-pathway role and Golgi localization.

title: The incorrect use of CD75 as a synonym for ST6GAL1 has fostered the expansion of commercial 'ST6GAL1' antibodies that do not recognize ST6GAL1.
review_notes: UniProt-cited CAUTION reference; important for interpreting historical CD75/CDw75 literature as describing the ST6GAL1 product epitope rather than the protein.

title: A universal glycoenzyme biosynthesis pipeline that enables efficient cell-free remodeling of glycans.
review_notes: UniProt-cited EXP evidence for the core catalytic activity (GO:0003835).

title: Divergent Enzymatic Assembly of a Comprehensive 64-Membered IgG N-Glycan Library for Functional Glycomics.
review_notes: UniProt-cited EXP evidence for the core catalytic activity (GO:0003835).

title: Identification and analysis of novel functional sites in human GD3-synthase.
review_notes: Human GD3 synthase IDA activity plus structure-guided mutagenesis (Asn188/Pro189/Ser190/Arg272) defining alpha-2,8-linkage specificity; directly supports the core MF.

title: Accumulation of unusual gangliosides G(Q3) and G(P3) in breast cancer cells expressing the G(D3) synthase.
review_notes: Full-text available; ST8Sia I expression in MCF-7 produces b/c-series gangliosides and unusual GQ3/GP3, demonstrating alpha-2,8-(oligo)sialyltransferase activity.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale neurodegenerative-disease interactome (Y2H) paper; source of the bare protein-binding IPI (ST8SIA1-OPTN). Correctly cited but only a passing high-throughput interaction, not informative about ST8SIA1's molecular function.

title: Isolation of GD3 synthase gene by expression cloning of GM3 alpha-2,8-sialyltransferase cDNA using anti-GD2 monoclonal antibody.
review_notes: Expression cloning of the GD3 synthase gene; supports the core catalytic activity.

title: Expression cloning of a CMP-NeuAc:NeuAc alpha 2-3Gal beta 1-4Glc beta 1-1'Cer alpha 2,8-sialyltransferase (GD3 synthase) from human melanoma cells.
review_notes: Expression cloning of GD3 synthase; identifies it as a key ganglioside-pathway enzyme.

title: Expression cloning of a GM3-specific alpha-2,8-sialyltransferase (GD3 synthase).
review_notes: Expression cloning of the GM3-specific alpha-2,8-sialyltransferase; catalytic domain reconstitutes GD3 synthase activity. Basis of several legacy ProtInc annotations.

title: Expression cloning of a human GT3 synthase. GD3 AND GT3 are synthesized by a single enzyme.
review_notes: Shows GD3 and GT3 are made by the single ST8SIA1 enzyme acting as a b/c-series alpha-2,8-polysialyltransferase; brain-restricted expression.

title: Acceptor substrate specificity of a cloned GD3 synthase that catalyzes the biosynthesis of both GD3 and GD1c/GT1a/GQ1b.
review_notes: Defines acceptor-substrate specificity (GM3, GM1b, GD1a, GT1b); supports the core MF and the enzyme's broader alpha-2,8-sialyltransferase acceptor range.

title: The steroidogenic acute regulatory protein, StAR, works only at the outer mitochondrial membrane.
review_notes: Establishes that StAR acts only at the outer mitochondrial membrane despite being targeted to the matrix; source for OMM site-of-action and matrix non-core localization.

title: Steroidogenic acute regulatory protein (StAR), a novel mitochondrial cholesterol transporter.
review_notes: Review establishing StAR's cholesterol transfer activity and exclusive action on the outer membrane; supports MF and transport annotations.

title: Intracellular cholesterol transporter StarD4 binds free cholesterol and increases cholesteryl ester formation.
review_notes: Primarily a StarD4 (paralog) paper. It names StarD1/STAR only as the reference cholesterol-binding START protein, which supports the STAR cholesterol-binding IDA. Its bile-acid biosynthesis phenotype is a StarD4 property and does not support the STAR bile-acid regulation annotation (flagged over-annotated).

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome; source of an uninformative StAR protein-binding IPI (MAGEA11). No functional relevance established.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Systematic interactome study; source of an uninformative StAR protein-binding IPI.

title: Widespread Expansion of Protein Interaction Capabilities by Alternative Splicing.
review_notes: Alternative-splicing interactome; source of an uninformative StAR protein-binding IPI.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference interactome; source of several uninformative StAR protein-binding IPIs.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegenerative-disease interactome; source of an uninformative StAR protein-binding IPI (HTT).

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome (MitoCoP); supports the HTP mitochondrion localization.

title: Human steroidogenic acute regulatory protein: functional activity in COS-1 cells, tissue-specific expression, and mapping of the structural gene to 8p11.2 and a pseudogene to chromosome 13.
review_notes: Original human StAR functional characterization: >4-fold increase in pregnenolone with P450scc/adrenodoxin; tissue expression; gene mapping.

title: Role of steroidogenic acute regulatory protein in adrenal and gonadal steroidogenesis.
review_notes: Human loss-of-function (lipoid CAH) evidence that StAR is indispensable for adrenal and gonadal steroidogenesis.

title: UniProtKB entry STAR_HUMAN (P49675)
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; FUNCTION, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY (cholesterol transport reaction), PATHWAY and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statements used as supporting text.

title: Arginine/lysine-rich structural element is involved in interferon-induced nuclear import of STATs.
review_notes: Cached full text confirms experimental cytoplasm and nucleus localization of STAT2 and IFN-induced nuclear import; supports the localization annotations.

title: Affinity of Stat2 for the subunits of the interferon alpha receptor.
review_notes: Cached abstract confirms SH2-dependent STAT2 docking to phospho-IFNAR1 (Tyr466) and constitutive IFNAR2 binding; supports receptor-interaction annotation.

title: Identification of STAT2 serine 287 as a novel regulatory phosphorylation site in type I interferon-induced cellular responses.
review_notes: Cached full text confirms STAT2 as a positive modulator of type I IFN transcription and identifies Ser287 as a negative regulatory phosphosite; supports localization and transcription annotations.

title: STAT2 deficiency and susceptibility to viral illness in humans.
review_notes: Cached full text; human STAT2 deficiency causes profound failure of type I IFN signaling and viral susceptibility, with loss of ISGF3-dependent ISG induction. Strongly supports defense response to virus and type I IFN signaling.

title: IFNβ-dependent increases in STAT1, STAT2, and IRF9 mediate resistance to viruses and DNA damage.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports STAT2 membership in ISGF3/U-ISGF3 and its role in driving antiviral ISG transcription.

title: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 2 deficiency is a novel disorder of mitochondrial fission.
review_notes: Cached full text; STAT2 deficiency reduces DRP1 (DNM1L) Ser616 phosphorylation and impairs mitochondrial fission. Supports the non-core mitochondrial fission and protein phosphorylation annotations.

title: PIPINO: A Software Package to Facilitate the Identification of Protein-Protein Interactions from Affinity Purification Mass Spectrometry Data.
review_notes: Methods/software paper; source of an uninformative high-throughput protein binding annotation.

title: Global functional profiling of human ubiquitome identifies E3 ubiquitin ligase DCST1 as a novel negative regulator of Type-I interferon signaling.
review_notes: Cached abstract confirms DCST1 as an E3 ligase that binds and ubiquitinates STAT2 to negatively regulate type I IFN signaling; supports GO:0044389 and cytoplasm annotations.

title: STAT2 is an essential adaptor in USP18-mediated suppression of type I interferon signaling.
review_notes: Cached full text; establishes STAT2 both as a positive effector and as the essential adaptor recruiting USP18 to IFNAR2 for negative feedback. Key support for core functions and GO:0060339.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome study; source of an uninformative protein binding annotation.

title: Histone deacetylase 4 promotes type I interferon signaling, restricts DNA viruses, and is degraded via vaccinia virus protein C6.
review_notes: Cached full text; ChIP shows STAT2 recruitment to ISRE-containing ISG promoters and that the STAT2 transactivation domain mediates HDAC4 interaction. Supports DNA-binding TF activity and chromatin annotations.

title: Severe type I interferonopathy and unrestrained interferon signaling due to a homozygous germline mutation in STAT2.
review_notes: Cached full text; homozygous STAT2 variant causes unrestrained IFN signaling by compromising USP18-mediated negative regulation. Supports type I IFN signaling and negative-feedback roles.

title: Homozygous STAT2 gain-of-function mutation by loss of USP18 activity in a patient with type I interferonopathy.
review_notes: Cached full text; STAT2 R148Q is a GOF that fails to traffic USP18 to IFNAR2, preventing negative regulation of IFN-I. Supports type I IFN signaling and USP18-adaptor core functions.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome study; source of an uninformative protein binding annotation.

title: Unresolvable identifier - no record in NCBI PubMed (likely a GOA data error)
review_notes: Verified via NCBI eutils esummary that PMID:34521819 returns "cannot get document summary" - the identifier does not resolve to any PubMed record and is most likely an error in the GOA source. The entry is retained only because a GOA annotation (existing_annotations[32], a generic uninformative protein binding IPI already marked MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED) references it, so it cannot be deleted without failing reference-integrity validation. Carries no supporting_text and informs no core function.

title: Human transcription factor protein interaction networks.
review_notes: Large-scale TF interaction network study; source of an uninformative protein binding annotation.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Large-scale cell-map study; source of uninformative protein binding and identical protein binding annotations.

title: Phosphorylated interferon-alpha receptor 1 subunit (IFNaR1) acts as a docking site for the latent form of the 113 kDa STAT2 protein.
review_notes: Cached abstract confirms SH2-dependent docking of latent STAT2 to phospho-IFNAR1 (Tyr466); supports receptor-interaction annotation.

title: The SH2 domains of Stat1 and Stat2 mediate multiple interactions in the transduction of IFN-alpha signals.
review_notes: Confirms SH2-mediated STAT1/STAT2 homo- and heterodimerization; supports identical protein binding (homodimerization) annotation.

title: Stat2 is a transcriptional activator that requires sequence-specific contacts provided by stat1 and p48 for stable interaction with DNA.
review_notes: Cached abstract; establishes that STAT2 is a potent transactivator that cannot stably contact DNA alone and requires STAT1/p48(IRF9) within ISGF3. Central to the DNA-binding/transactivation core function.

title: Functional subdomains of STAT2 required for preassociation with the alpha interferon receptor and for signaling.
review_notes: Maps STAT2 subdomains required for IFNAR preassociation and signaling; supports receptor-interaction annotation.

title: Identification of amino acid residues critical for the Src-homology 2 domain-dependent docking of Stat2 to the interferon alpha receptor.
review_notes: Maps SH2 residues for STAT2-IFNAR1 docking; supports receptor-interaction annotation.

title: Estrogen inhibits GH signaling by suppressing GH-induced JAK2 phosphorylation, an effect mediated by SOCS-2.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. The paper studies GH/JAK2/STAT5 signaling and its suppression by estradiol via SOCS-2; supports the GH receptor signaling, response to estradiol and cellular response to hormone IDA annotations. However the cached abstract does not mention the GO:0035259 glucocorticoid receptor binding annotation, which is BHF-UCL curator judgment from full text (not cached) - left UNDECIDED rather than removed.

title: ZFP36L1 negatively regulates erythroid differentiation of CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells by interfering with the Stat5b pathway.
review_notes: Full text cached. Supports the GO:0045648 positive regulation of erythrocyte differentiation annotation - ZFP36L1 binds the Stat5b mRNA 3'UTR and down-regulation of Stat5b drastically reduces erythroid colony formation in human hematopoietic progenitors, demonstrating STAT5B promotes erythroid differentiation.

title: The tumor suppressor hTid1 inhibits STAT5b activity via functional interaction.
review_notes: Full text cached. hTid1/DNAJA3 binds specifically to the STAT5b (not STAT5a) transactivation domain and negatively regulates STAT5b expression and transcriptional activity. Supports a GO:0005515 interaction (marked over-annotated as bare protein binding).

title: Dominant-negative STAT5B mutations cause growth hormone insensitivity with short stature and mild immune dysregulation.
review_notes: PMC full text available and read. Directly establishes STAT5B as the key GH signal transducer; provides experimental evidence for GH-induced Tyr phosphorylation, homo/heterodimerization (co-IP), nuclear translocation (IF), GHRE/GAS DNA binding (EMSA) and reporter transactivation, plus dominant-negative disease variants. Supports the GO:0001228, GO:0042803, nucleus and cytoplasm IDA annotations.

title: Structural and functional consequences of the STAT5B(N642H) driver mutation.
review_notes: Full text cached. Structural/functional study of the SH2-domain N642H oncogenic driver mutation; source of the ABL1 and self-association (GO:0042802) IntAct interactions. Informs STAT5B's role in leukemia/lymphoma but not its core physiological function.

title: Cloning of human Stat5B. Reconstitution of interleukin-2-induced Stat5A and Stat5B DNA binding activity in COS-7 cells.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. Original cloning/characterization of human STAT5B; shows IL-2 activation via JAK1/JAK3 and the IL-2R beta/gamma chains and that Tyr-699 is required for dimerization. Supports the TAS JAK-STAT and transcription-factor annotations. Cached as abstract-only.

title: Erythropoietin induces tyrosine phosphorylation of Jak2, STAT5A, and STAT5B in primary cultured human erythroid precursors.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. Directly supports the GO:0038162 erythropoietin-mediated signaling pathway IDA annotation - EPO induces JAK2, STAT5A and STAT5B tyrosine phosphorylation and nuclear translocation in primary human erythroid precursors. Cached as abstract-only.

title: Functional association of Nmi with Stat5 and Stat1 in IL-2- and IFNgamma-mediated signaling.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. NMI (Q13287) was found via yeast two-hybrid using the STAT5b coiled-coil region and augments STAT5/STAT1 transcription by enhancing CBP/p300 recruitment. Supports the GO:0005515 NMI interaction (marked over-annotated as bare protein binding). Cached as abstract-only.

title: The adaptor protein MITA links virus-sensing receptors to IRF3 transcription factor activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Zhong B et al., Immunity 2008;29(4):538-50 (the MITA paper) - the identifier and title are correct and the paper is a landmark for this gene. Flagged MISCITED because of what two of the annotations drawn from it assert, not because of the citation itself: GO:0003713 transcription coactivator activity and GO:0005741 mitochondrial outer membrane. The paper's own abstract says MITA 'was found to localize to the outer membrane of mitochondria' and that it 'interacted with IRF3', but neither supports a nuclear coactivator role for a four-pass ER membrane protein, and the mitochondrial localisation has not been sustained. Cached entry is abstract-only (full_text_available: false), so these judgements rest on the term definitions and on the subsequent literature, not on re-reading the curator's source.

title: Human STING is a proton channel.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Liu B et al., Science 2023 Aug 4;381(6657):508-514, doi 10.1126/science.adf8974. Origin of the GO:0015252 proton channel activity annotation. Liposome reconstitution of purified STING makes this a property of the protein rather than an indirect cellular readout, and C53 blockade provides specificity.

title: A TBK1-independent primordial function of STING in lysosomal biogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Lv B et al., Mol Cell 2024, doi 10.1016/j.molcel.2024.08.026. Independent requirement for the STING proton channel in TBK1-independent TFEB activation and lysosome biogenesis; supports GO:0015252, GO:1905673 and GO:1904262.

title: ArfGAP2 promotes STING proton channel activity, cytokine transit, and autoinflammation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Poddar S et al., Cell 2025, doi 10.1016/j.cell.2025.01.027. Third independent laboratory relying on and regulating STING proton channel activity (ArfGAP2); supports GO:0015252 and GO:0001819.

title: STING mediates lysosomal quality control and recovery through its proton channel function and TFEB activation in lysosomal storage disorders.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Tang Z et al., Mol Cell 2025;85(8):1624-1639.e5, doi 10.1016/j.molcel.2025.03.008. Fourth independent laboratory (Yan lab, UTSW) requiring STING proton channel function, here for lysosomal quality control in lysosomal storage disorder models. Cited in this review only as corroboration for GO:0015252; not a GOA source.

title: Beyond interferons: Non-canonical roles of MITA/STING.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Yang Y et al. (Cell Insight 2025), 'Beyond interferons: Non-canonical roles of MITA/STING', doi 10.1016/j.cellin.2025.100266. A review, and the sole support for four NAS annotations (GO:0006914, GO:0045820, GO:0055088, GO:0090398). Correctly cited, but review prose is weak evidence for process annotations; two of the four (glycolysis, lipid homeostasis) are marked as over-annotation here.

title: Regulation of STING activation by phosphoinositide and cholesterol.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Li J et al., Nature 2026 Apr;652(8109):499-507, doi 10.1038/s41586-025-10076-0, PMC13224288. Cryo-EM structures of STING1 with PtdIns(3,5)P2, PtdIns(4,5)P2 and PtdIns4P plus a cholesterol-like molecule at the dimer-dimer interface, with lipid-strip binding and mutational validation. Source of both the GO:0015485 cholesterol binding IDA and the proposed GO:0005546. Companion to PMID:41639454 with overlapping authorship: corroboration, not independent replication.

title: PtdIns(3,5)P(2) is an endogenous ligand of STING in innate immune signalling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Tan JX et al., Nature 2026 Apr;652(8109):490-498, doi 10.1038/s41586-025-10084-0, PMC13222494. Establishes PtdIns(3,5)P2 as a direct STING1 ligand (FRET, PIKFYVE interaction and knockout, lipid-binding mutants). Sound, but note it is co-submitted with PMID:41639452 and shares authors (Tan, Chen, Bai); the cryo-EM structure it cites is that companion paper, so the two are not independent. Carries a Publisher Correction, PMID:41721038, whose content I could not retrieve.

title: Publisher Correction: PtdIns(3,5)P(2) is an endogenous ligand of STING in innate immune signalling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as Publisher Correction to PMID:41639454, Nature 2026 Mar;651(8105):E11, doi 10.1038/s41586-026-10280-6. The correction's content could NOT be retrieved: PubMed carries only the erratum notice with no descriptive text, Europe PMC returns no abstract, and the Nature page is behind an authentication redirect. Springer Nature reserves 'Publisher Correction' for errors introduced in production, as opposed to 'Author Correction', so on its face it does not affect the data or conclusions - but this is a categorical inference, not something I was able to read. No annotation in this review depends on it.

title: Histone tyrosine sulfation by SULT1B1 regulates H4R3me2a and gene transcription.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Chem Biol 2023;19:855-864). The claim that SULT1B1 is a histone sulfotransferase acting on H3 Tyr99 is formally contested by PMID:40890505, which reannotated the original raw mass spectra as a phosphotyrosine peptide and found no sulfation of recombinant histone H3.2 by recombinant SULT1B1. The authors replied (PMID:40890506) and an Author Correction was published (PMID:40890508); the paper has not been retracted. Cited here only to document the dispute - no GO annotation derives from it.

title: Mass spectrometry and enzyme assays refute histone tyrosine sulfation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Chem Biol 2025;21:1667-1670), full text available via PMC12978989. A formal Matters Arising refuting PMID:36805701 on three independent grounds: sulfotyrosine is too labile to give the 100% sulfate-retaining HCD fragments reported, the reported fragment masses fit phosphotyrosine to <3 ppm versus 12.5-31.5 ppm for sulfotyrosine, and a recombinant SULT1B1 assay that efficiently sulfated T3 gave no histone H3.2 sulfation. Marked DISPUTED rather than VERIFIED because the original authors contest it in PMID:40890506, not because of any problem with the citation.

title: Reply to: Mass spectrometry and enzyme assays refute histone tyrosine sulfation.

title: THG1L transfers GMP to 5' end of tRNA(His)

review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cached entry is abstract-only (full_text_available:false). Directly establishes the ThTP-specific triphosphatase activity, cytoplasmic localization, and broad low-level tissue expression of the human enzyme.

title: THTPA:Mg2+ hydrolyzes ThTP to TDP
review_notes: Reactome reaction consistent with the enzyme's characterized activity and cytosolic localization.

title: RNA-binding proteins TIA-1 and TIAR link the phosphorylation of eIF-2 alpha to the assembly of mammalian stress granules.
