title: Identification and functional characterization of a TIA-1-related nucleolysin.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The biochemical DNA- fragmentation result and candidate granule localization are real, but neither establishes a broad physiological apoptosis or defense role.

title: Novel DNA-binding properties of the RNA-binding protein TIAR.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were checked. This direct biochemical study verifies DNA binding but does not establish it as the dominant physiological activity.

title: Translational repression by RNA-binding protein TIAR.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. Direct target-binding, translation, and silencing experiments establish negative regulation of translation in human cells.

title: Posttranscriptional derepression of GADD45alpha by genotoxic stress.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. This provides a direct transcript-specific example of human TIAR translational repression.

title: Fas-activated serine/threonine kinase (FAST K) synergizes with TIA-1/TIAR proteins to regulate Fas alternative splicing.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The joint depletion and Fas reporter experiments directly support a TIAL1 splicing-regulatory role.

title: Two isoforms of the T-cell intracellular antigen 1 (TIA-1) splicing factor display distinct splicing regulation activities. Control of TIA-1 isoform ratio by TIA-1-related protein.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. Human depletion provides direct endogenous evidence for alternative-splicing regulation by TIAL1.

title: DNA damage activates a spatially distinct late cytoplasmic cell-cycle checkpoint network controlled by MK2-mediated RNA stabilization.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were checked. This defines a stress-regulated TIAR-GADD45A post-transcriptional switch.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The GOA HDA records TIAL1 in the human mRNA-interactome dataset; the study is broad, not TIAL1-mechanistic.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The GOA HDA records TIAL1 in the source dataset and independently supports direct mRNA association.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were checked. The GOA IPI records a DZIP3-TIAL1 co-association from the screen, but generic protein binding is not an informative molecular activity.

title: Rox8 promotes microRNA-dependent yki messenger RNA decay.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The paper directly tests human TIAR, while the detailed RISC-recruitment genetics are in Drosophila.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were checked. The GOA IPI records a DZIP3-TIAL1 co-association, but it does not justify a generic protein- binding function term.

title: MOV10 Helicase Interacts with Coronavirus Nucleocapsid Protein and Has Antiviral Activity.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were checked. The endogenous co-immunoprecipitation supports association, but not a specific molecular activity for TIAL1.

title: Individual RNA recognition motifs of TIA-1 and TIAR have different RNA binding specificities.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. This is the foundational direct biochemical analysis of TIAR RNA specificity and RRM contributions.

title: An alternative form of nucleolysin binds to a T-cluster DNA in the silencer element of platelet factor 4 gene.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The reported product maps to the nucleolysin/TIAL1 locus, but it is not among the two current UniProt isoforms, so the transcription phenotype is treated as non-core.

title: Identification of TIAR as a protein binding to the translational regulatory AU-rich element of tumor necrosis factor alpha mRNA.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. This directly supports AU-rich 3-prime-UTR binding by TIAR.

title: ESRP1 and 2 bind FGFR2 pre-mRNA to promote FGFR2b maturation and expression
review_notes: The cached Reactome record was checked. It supports nucleoplasmic localization and pathway context while explicitly noting that the precise TIAL1 role remains to be elucidated.

title: Manual literature synthesis for human TIAL1 (Q01085)
review_notes: Manual research was required because both configured automated providers failed; conclusions are anchored to reviewed records and primary sources.

title: Manual literature and annotation review notes for human TIAL1
review_notes: Manual synthesis of reviewed UniProt, GOA, cached primary literature, Reactome, and verified GO term labels.

title: UniProtKB record for human TIAL1 (Q01085)
review_notes: The current reviewed UniProt record was checked directly for sequence, domains, isoforms, localization, and primary-literature provenance.

title: Assembly factors for the membrane arm of human complex I.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (DOI:10.1073/pnas.1319247110); this is the experimental source cited by UniProt for the TIMMDC1 FUNCTION and SUBUNIT statements. Not in the local publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text is quoted; provenance anchored to the UniProt FUNCTION statement it underpins.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Large-scale binary interactome (CCSB); source of an uninformative GO:0005515 IPI (WITH/FROM FATE1), not a physiological interactor.

title: Genetic diagnosis of Mendelian disorders via RNA sequencing.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (DOI:10.1038/ncomms15824); the UniProt source for INVOLVEMENT IN MC1DN31. Not in the local cache, so no verbatim supporting_text is quoted; anchored to the UniProt DISEASE statement.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: High-throughput variant-interaction study; source of an uninformative GO:0005515 IPI (WITH/FROM FATE1).

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI Y2H reference interactome; source of many uninformative GO:0005515 IPIs whose partners are mostly non-mitochondrial membrane proteins (Y2H noise).

title: TMEM70 and TMEM242 help to assemble the rotor ring of human ATP synthase and interact with assembly factors for complex I.
review_notes: Full text cached and verified; supports the TIMMDC1-TMEM70/MCIA interaction (the UniProt SUBUNIT "Interacts with TMEM70" statement).

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 AP-MS; source of a GO:0005515 IPI whose WITH/FROM partner NDUFB11 (a Complex I membrane-arm subunit) is biologically consistent with the membrane-arm assembly role, though the MF term itself is uninformative.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteome; supports mitochondrial localization.

title: Mutant mitochondrial thymidine kinase in mitochondrial DNA depletion myopathy.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary paper establishing TK2 substrate specificity, its role in the mitochondrial salvage pathway, and the MTDPS2 disease link. Abstract-only in cache but the substrate/activity statements are quoted verbatim.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome screen; correctly cited but supports only a bare protein-binding annotation (TK2-GSTK1) that is uninformative about TK2 function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput (HTP) mitochondrial-proteome study; TK2 is a MitoCoP member (in supplementary data, not named in the extracted text), supporting the mitochondrion location annotation.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: High-throughput multimodal interactome/imaging screen; correctly cited but supports only an uninformative protein-binding annotation for TK2.

title: Cloning of the cDNA and chromosome localization of the gene for human thymidine kinase 2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified original cloning/characterization paper; directly establishes TK2 substrate specificity and family membership.

title: Human thymidine kinase 2: molecular cloning and characterisation of the enzyme activity with antiviral and cytostatic nucleoside substrates.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary paper; source of the mitochondrial localization (IDA) and catalytic-activity annotations for TK2.

title: Identification of human and rat FAD-AMP lyase (cyclic FMN forming) as ATP-dependent dihydroxyacetone kinases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes that a single human protein (LOC26007 cDNA, i.e. TKFC) possesses both FMN cyclase (FAD-AMP lyase) and ATP-dependent dihydroxyacetone kinase activities, each inhibited by the substrate(s) of the other. Supports the FAD-AMP lyase and glycerone kinase MF annotations.

title: Negative regulation of MDA5- but not RIG-I-mediated innate antiviral signaling by the dihydroxyacetone kinase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Identifies DAK/TKFC as a specific MDA5 (IFIH1)-interacting protein and a physiological suppressor of MDA5- but not RIG-I-mediated antiviral signaling. Supports GO:0039534 and the moonlighting immune core function.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Bulk urinary-exosome proteomics (1132 proteins); TKFC detection is incidental for a cytosolic enzyme. Supports only the (over-annotated) extracellular exosome localization.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Sperm-nucleus proteome (403 proteins). Detection of a cytosolic enzyme likely reflects contamination/non-functional presence; supports only the over-annotated nuclear localization.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Prostatic/urinary exosome proteomics (~900 proteins). Incidental detection of a cytosolic enzyme; supports only the over-annotated extracellular exosome localization.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale binary interactome map; source of the SDCBP (O00560) protein binding IPI. No established functional interpretation for TKFC; supports only the uninformative protein binding term.

title: Bi-allelic Variants in TKFC Encoding Triokinase/FMN Cyclase Are Associated with Cataracts and Multisystem Disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Defines human TKFC deficiency (TKFCD); confirms the bifunctional enzyme (glyceraldehyde kinase in fructose metabolism plus FMN lyase generating cyclic FMN); FMN-lyase domain variants (G445S, R543I) severely reduce triokinase and glycerone kinase activities.

title: Dihydroxyacetone metabolism by human erythrocytes: demonstration of triokinase activity and its characterization.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Classic biochemical demonstration and kinetic characterization of human triokinase (dihydroxyacetone/glyceraldehyde kinase) activity in erythrocytes. Supports the triokinase and glycerone kinase MF annotations.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Large-scale urinary exosome proteomics; TKT is an incidental co-isolated cytosolic enzyme, not a functional exosomal localization.

title: Characterization of exosome-like vesicles released from human tracheobronchial ciliated epithelium: a possible role in innate defense.
review_notes: Vesicle proteomics; supports incidental presence of cytosolic metabolic enzymes in vesicle lumen, not a functional vesicular role for TKT.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: B-cell exosome proteome (539 proteins); TKT incidental, not a functional localization.

title: The crystal structure of human transketolase and new insights into its mode of action.
review_notes: Definitive human TKT crystal structure with ThDP and divalent cation; establishes catalytic activity, homodimer, cofactor binding and kinetics.

title: Genome-wide YFP fluorescence complementation screen identifies new regulators for telomere signaling in human cells.
review_notes: High-throughput telomere-interactome YFP complementation screen; source of the uninformative TKT-TERF1 protein-binding IPI, no established functional relevance.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Prostatic-secretion urinary exosome proteomics (~900 proteins); TKT incidental co-isolation.

title: Mutations in TKT Are the Cause of a Syndrome Including Short Stature, Developmental Delay, and Congenital Heart Defects.
review_notes: Establishes autosomal-recessive transketolase deficiency (SDDHD) with reduced enzyme activity in patients; in-vivo confirmation of TKT function in the non-oxidative PPP.

title: Cloning of human transketolase cDNAs and comparison of the nucleotide sequence of the coding region in Wernicke-Korsakoff and non-Wernicke-Korsakoff individuals.
review_notes: Cloning of human TKT cDNA; single-copy gene; Wernicke-Korsakoff/thiamine context.

title: Aspartate 155 of human transketolase is essential for thiamine diphosphate-magnesium binding, and cofactor binding is required for dimer formation.
review_notes: Homodimer with two active sites, non-covalent ThDP+Mg per site; D155 essential for cofactor-Mg binding and dimerization.

title: Heterologous expression of human transketolase.
review_notes: Recombinant human TKT with Km for xylulose-5-P/ribose-5-P and for ThDP/Mg2+; matches native erythrocyte enzyme.

title: Mechanotransduction in mouse inner ear hair cells requires transmembrane channel-like genes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Clin Invest 2011). Establishes that Tmc1/Tmc2 double knockout hair cells are structurally normal but lack all mechanotransduction, and localises TMC proteins to stereocilia tips.

title: TMC1 and TMC2 are components of the mechanotransduction channel in hair cells of the mammalian inner ear.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neuron 2013) and scientifically sound, but it is the source of the mouse `enables GO:0005245 voltage-gated calcium channel activity` annotation that propagates to human TMC1. The paper measures calcium permeability and single-channel conductance of a mechanically gated channel and never claims voltage gating, so it does not support the term it was used for.

title: Structural relationship between the putative hair cell mechanotransduction channel TMC1 and TMEM16 proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (eLife 2018). Provides the structural rationale that links TMC1 to the TMEM16 fold, which is the reason the channel-versus-scramblase question arises for this family at all.

title: TMC1 Forms the Pore of Mechanosensory Transduction Channels in Vertebrate Inner Ear Hair Cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neuron 2018). Cysteine-modification pore mapping in hair cells; the strongest evidence that TMC1 itself lines the permeation pathway.

title: CIB2 and CIB3 are auxiliary subunits of the mechanotransduction channel of hair cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neuron 2021). Defines CIB2/CIB3 as auxiliary subunits binding TMC1/2, supporting the contributes_to rather than enables framing.

title: The conductance and organization of the TMC1-containing mechanotransducer channel complex in auditory hair cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PNAS 2022). Six pore-region missense mutations all reduce calcium permeability, several change conductance - direct structure-function support for TMC1 as the pore.

title: Human TMC1 and TMC2 are mechanically gated ion channels.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neuron, Feb 2025 issue, e-pub Dec 2024). The paper that closes the heterologous-expression gap for human TMC1/2 and whose own abstract states that "controversy persists".

title: Mammalian TMC1 or 2 are necessary for scramblase activity in auditory hair cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Hear Res 2025). Peer-reviewed genetic evidence that TMC1 or TMC2 is necessary for hair-cell PS externalisation; explicitly does not claim that TMCs perform the scrambling.

title: TMC1 and TMC2 are cholesterol-dependent scramblases that regulate membrane homeostasis in auditory hair cells.
review_notes: PREPRINT (bioRxiv 2025.07.03.663083, PMC12236488); not peer reviewed as of this review and no journal version found in PubMed. Reports direct phospholipid translocation by reconstituted TMC1/TMC2 proteoliposomes. Treated as suggestive rather than establishing, which is why no scramblase molecular-function term is asserted.

title: TMEM120A and B: Nuclear Envelope Transmembrane Proteins Important for Adipocyte Differentiation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Batrakou et al., PLoS One 2015). Source of the nuclear envelope (NET29) assignment, the adipocyte-differentiation role, and the homo/heterooligomerization annotations. Correctly cited; its compartment assignment is contested by later work but the experiments themselves are not in dispute.

title: TACAN Is an Ion Channel Involved in Sensing Mechanical Pain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Beaulieu-Laroche et al., Cell 2020). This is the origin of the TACAN name and of every channel-related annotation on this gene, including the mouse donor annotation behind the human GO_REF:0000024 ISS rows. The channel claim was not reproduced by four independent groups in 2021, and GO now carries three human NOT|enables annotations against the same term. Correctly cited but the central claim is contested; the in vivo nociceptor knockout phenotype is a separate matter and is not itself refuted.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome map; the source of 24 bare protein-binding rows. Correctly cited but contributes no functional information about TMEM120A.

title: Involvement of TACAN, a Mechanotransducing Ion Channel, in Inflammatory But Not Neuropathic Hyperalgesia in the Rat.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Pain 2020). Antisense knockdown in rat supports a contribution to inflammatory mechanical hyperalgesia, which is relevant to the pain-process annotations. Marked DISPUTED only because the paper adopts the mechanotransducing-ion-channel framing that has since been refuted; the behavioural observation stands independently of that framing.

title: Analysis of the mechanosensor channel functionality of TACAN.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Niu et al., eLife 2021). Independent failure to detect mechanosensitive channel activity, plus native mass spectrometry confirming co-purified coenzyme A. Not currently cited in GOA but directly load-bearing for the removal of the positive ISS channel annotation.

title: TMEM120A is a coenzyme A-binding membrane protein with structural similarities to ELOVL fatty acid elongase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Xue et al., eLife 2021). Supports both the positive coenzyme A binding IDA and the negated ion channel IMP carried in GOA; verified that the paper reports both the CoA-bound structure and the failure to reproduce mechanosensitive currents.

title: TMEM120A contains a specific coenzyme A-binding site and might not mediate poking- or stretch-induced channel activities in cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Rong et al., eLife 2021). The negative electrophysiology used proper positive controls (Piezo channels, HsTMEM63a) in Piezo1-knockout HEK cells, which makes it a strong negative rather than an insensitive assay. Identifies the tryptophan required for CoASH binding.

title: Cryo-EM structures of human TMEM120A and TMEM120B.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Discov 2021). Supports the negated ion channel IDA. Notably careful - the authors observed conductance in a bilayer system yet declined to conclude channel identity because non-channel proteins also conduct in that assay.

title: Gain-of-function genetic screening identifies the antiviral function of TMEM120A via STING activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Li et al., Nat Commun 2022). Source of the antiviral innate immune response IMP and of the ER and plasma membrane IDA rows. Single-laboratory result, but includes a mouse knockout and a mechanistically coherent ER-export readout.

title: Genomic loci mispositioning in Tmem120a knockout mice yields latent lipodystrophy.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Czapiewski et al., Nat Commun 2022). Adipocyte-specific knockout gives a lipodystrophy syndrome, supporting the fat-cell and lipid-homeostasis annotations. Interprets the phenotype through nuclear envelope genome organisation, which competes with the ER lipid-flux interpretation of PMID:41423633; both are recorded rather than adjudicated here.

title: TMEM120A/TACAN inhibits mechanically activated PIEZO2 channels.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Del Rosario et al., J Gen Physiol 2022). Provides the alternative account of the mechanosensory phenotype - TMEM120A as a negative modulator of PIEZO2 rather than a channel - and explicitly states the data do not support channel identity.

title: Regulation of PKD2 channel function by TACAN.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available false), so the supporting evidence for the PKD2 interaction was not read. Cited in GOA only for a bare protein-binding row; not relied on for any action in this review beyond that row.

title: Phosphatidic acid is an endogenous negative regulator of PIEZO2 channels and mechanical sensitivity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Gabrielle et al., Nat Commun 2024). Identifies the mediator linking TMEM120A to PIEZO2 inhibition - TMEM120A expression raises phosphatidic acid and lysophosphatidic acid. This is the key reconciliation between the lipid-metabolic function and the mechanosensory phenotypes, since lysophosphatidic acid is the product of the GPAT4 reaction TMEM120A activates.

title: TMEM120A maintains adipose tissue lipid homeostasis through ER CoA channeling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cho et al., Nat Commun 2025, PMC12855804). Establishes the ER-resident CoA-binding role, the CoA-site-dependent interaction with ACSL1 and ACSL3, and the adipose phenotype of the adipocyte-specific knockout. Note that the authors hedge the transport mechanism themselves ("possibly through recycling CoA in ER"), so no CoA transporter term is proposed on its basis.

title: From nociception to therapy: The expanding role of TMEM proteins in pain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Life Sci 2026); cached record is abstract-only. A narrative review that still lists TMEM120A/TACAN among pain-relevant TMEM proteins. Its own wording is "modulating ion channels", which is compatible with the PIEZO2 model rather than with TMEM120A being a channel. Recorded to document that the channel framing persists in secondary literature; it presents no new data and is not a basis for reinstating the channel annotation.

title: A conserved ER protein prevents lipotoxicity by stimulating the key enzyme in glycerolipid synthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Li et al., Nat Commun 2026, PMC13365615). Identifies TMEM120A as a GPAT4-activating protein acting with CHP1, with an in vitro acyltransferase assay, split-GFP and co-immunoprecipitation evidence, ER localisation of endogenously tagged C. elegans TMEM-120, and a conserved high-fat-diet phenotype. Basis for the proposed enzyme-activator terms.

title: Biolayer Interferometry for Investigating Membrane Protein-Inhibitor Binding: TACAN Mutant and GsMTx4 As a Model System.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Vis Exp 2026); cached record is abstract-only. A methods paper demonstrating a biolayer-interferometry protocol, using detergent-solubilised TMEM120A M207A and the gating-modifier peptide GsMTx4 as a convenient model pair. It measures binding kinetics, not channel gating, and the authors describe TMEM120A as "multifunctional" rather than as a channel. Flagged MISCITED in the sense that its use of a mechanosensitive-channel toxin should not be read as evidence that TMEM120A is a mechanosensitive channel.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nature 2020). Correctly cited as the source of the bare protein binding row, but it is a systematic binary-interactome screen and none of the partners it reports for TMEM187 has been followed up or connected to a function. Contributes no functional information about this gene.

title: TMEM187 is a novel brakelike modulator in the regulation of erythropoiesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Blood 2026;148(3):361-375, PMC13386088), with an accompanying Blood commentary (PMID:42461672). Essentially the entire functional literature on this gene. The cellular-component and biological-process claims are well supported - loss and gain of function in human cells, zebrafish and humanised mice, in both directions. The molecular mechanism is the weaker part: the GEF-competition model is inferred from co-immunoprecipitation, colocalisation and expression changes, with no nucleotide-exchange assay, and the paper itself notes that its observed nucleotide-state preference for GRAB is opposite to earlier reports. This is a single study from one laboratory and has not yet been independently replicated.

title: The fellowship of the ring: TMEM187 guides iron to heme.
review_notes: Identifier verified against PubMed (Blood 2026;148:271-2, an Editorial/Comment by Y.Y. Yien accompanying PMID:41824385), but PubMed carries no abstract and no full text was retrievable, so its content could not be read. Listed for provenance only - that Blood commissioned a commentary indicates the finding was considered notable - and it is not used to support any annotation.

title: Integral and associated lysosomal membrane proteins.
review_notes: Lysosomal membrane proteomics; correctly cited, supports the lysosomal membrane location but carries no functional information.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Urinary exosome shotgun proteomics; correctly cited but a high-throughput co-purification dataset with no functional content for this gene.

title: The N- and C-terminal carbohydrate recognition domains of Haemonchus contortus galectin bind to distinct receptors of goat PBMC and contribute differently to its immunomodulatory functions in host-parasite interactions.
review_notes: Correctly cited, but a Haemonchus contortus galectin host-parasite interaction study; it identifies TMEM63A as a binding partner on goat PBMC and says nothing about the normal function of the human protein. Basis for marking GO:0005515 over-annotated.

title: OSCA/TMEM63 are an Evolutionarily Conserved Family of Mechanically Activated Ion Channels.
review_notes: Murthy et al. 2018 eLife; PubMed-verified. Founding demonstration that OSCA/TMEM63 proteins confer mechanosensitivity to naive cells.

title: Heterozygous Variants in the Mechanosensitive Ion Channel TMEM63A Result in Transient Hypomyelination during Infancy.
review_notes: Yan et al. 2019; PubMed-verified. Human genetics establishing TMEM63A variants as a cause of transient infantile hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.

title: TMEM63 proteins function as monomeric high-threshold mechanosensitive ion channels.
review_notes: Zheng et al. 2023 Neuron; PubMed-verified. Structures and electrophysiology of TMEM63A and TMEM63B establishing monomeric architecture and bona fide mechanosensitivity.

title: Membrane structure-responsive lipid scrambling by TMEM63B to control plasma membrane lipid distribution.
review_notes: Miyata et al. 2025 Nat Struct Mol Biol; PubMed-verified. About the paralog TMEM63B, cited here only for the paralog contrast.

title: Membrane structure-responsive lipid scramblase activity of the TMEM63/OSCA family.
review_notes: Miyata et al. 2025 FEBS Lett; PubMed-verified. Source of the NOT|enables phospholipid scramblase annotation on TMEM63A: a deliberate paralog/ortholog comparison in Tmem63b-deficient pro-B cells in which scramblase activity tracked with TMEM63B orthology. Cached abstract only.

title: Structural and functional basis of mechanosensitive TMEM63 channelopathies.
review_notes: Zheng et al. 2025 Neuron; PubMed-verified. Cryo-EM of the TMEM63A V53M lipid-open state; the V-to-M substitutions evoke constitutive scrambling without enhancing channel activity, which presupposes that wild-type TMEM63A does not scramble.

title: Oligodendrocyte mechanotransduction channel TMEM63A regulates myelin sheath geometry.
review_notes: Dereddi et al. 2026 Neuron; PubMed-verified (Neuron 114(4):699-723.e11, doi 10.1016/j.neuron.2025.11.009). Cached abstract only - full_text_available is false - so only the abstract has been used. Frames TMEM63A purely as a mechanotransduction channel in oligodendrocytes.

title: TMEM63 proteins act as mechanically activated cholesterol modulated lipid scramblases contributing to membrane mechano-resilience.
review_notes: Lin et al. 2026 Nat Commun; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Reports lipid translocation by reconstituted hTMEM63A in GUVs while explicitly stating that this does not occur in the cellular context - the key text for reconciling the NOT|enables scramblase annotation.

title: OSCA/TMEM63 are an Evolutionarily Conserved Family of Mechanically Activated Ion Channels.
review_notes: Murthy et al. 2018 eLife; PubMed-verified. Founding demonstration that OSCA/TMEM63 proteins confer mechanosensitivity; supports the mechanosensitive channel core function.

title: Overexpression of Osmosensitive Ca(2+)-Permeable Channel TMEM63B Promotes Migration in HEK293T Cells.
review_notes: Marques et al. 2019 Biochemistry; PubMed-verified. This is the mouse IDA source behind GO:0005227. Its own title and text describe TMEM63B as Ca2+-PERMEABLE and osmosensitive, not Ca2+-activated, which is the basis for the MODIFY on that term.

title: Stretch-activated ion channel TMEM63B associates with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies and progressive neurodegeneration.
review_notes: Vetro et al. 2023 Am J Hum Genet; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Defines the TMEM63B developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and characterises variant conductance; this is the source of the GO:0005227 IDA whose term choice is challenged here.

title: TMEM63 proteins function as monomeric high-threshold mechanosensitive ion channels.
review_notes: Zheng et al. 2023 Neuron; PubMed-verified. Cryo-EM structures and electrophysiology establishing TMEM63A/B as monomeric, small-conductance, high-threshold mechanosensitive channels.

title: Mechanosensitive channels TMEM63A and TMEM63B mediate lung inflation-induced surfactant secretion.
review_notes: Chen et al. 2024 J Clin Invest; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. In vivo demonstration that TMEM63A/B mechanotransduction drives lung inflation-induced surfactant secretion; source of the GO:0140135 IDA and the lamellar body membrane location.

title: Phospholipid scrambling induced by an ion channel/metabolite transporter complex.
review_notes: Niu et al. 2024 Nat Commun; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Unbiased CRISPR revival screen identifying Tmem63b as a phospholipid-scrambling factor acting with Slc19a2; independent assay system from the Segawa-lab work.

title: Membrane structure-responsive lipid scrambling by TMEM63B to control plasma membrane lipid distribution.
review_notes: Miyata et al. 2025 Nat Struct Mol Biol; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Purified-protein scramblase assays plus open and closed cryo-EM structures resolving the lipid translocation pathway. Strongest single piece of evidence for the scramblase core function.

title: Membrane structure-responsive lipid scramblase activity of the TMEM63/OSCA family.
review_notes: Miyata et al. 2025 FEBS Lett; PubMed-verified. Paralog and ortholog survey in Tmem63b-null pro-B cells; grounds both the positive scramblase annotation on TMEM63B and the NOT annotation on TMEM63A. Cached abstract only.

title: Structural and functional basis of mechanosensitive TMEM63 channelopathies.
review_notes: Zheng et al. 2025 Neuron; PubMed-verified. Cryo-EM of the TMEM63A V53M lipid-open state; establishes that the V-to-M channelopathy variants evoke constitutive scrambling without enhancing channel activity, and states that the physiological relevance of WT scramblase activity is still open.

title: TMEM63 proteins act as mechanically activated cholesterol modulated lipid scramblases contributing to membrane mechano-resilience.
review_notes: Lin et al. 2026 Nat Commun; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. GUV reconstitution plus coarse-grained MD showing mechanically activated lipid scrambling by TMEM63A/B and separable ion/lipid bottleneck residues.

title: Autoinhibition of the mechanosensitive lipid scramblase TMEM63B by its C-terminal tail.
review_notes: Nishimura et al. 2026 J Biol Chem; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Maps a C-terminal autoinhibitory motif that holds TMEM63B scrambling off at rest.

title: A TMEM63B variant with enhanced mechanosensitive channel activity and acquired lipid scramblase function.
review_notes: Lowry et al. 2026 J Gen Physiol; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Characterises I475del as a gain-of-function mechanosensitive channel variant that also acquires constitutive and osmotically potentiated scramblase activity; the clearest statement of the channel-to-scramblase switch.

title: TMEM65 is a mitochondrial inner-membrane protein.
review_notes: PeerJ 2014; verified against the cached record. Establishes mitochondrial import and inner-membrane integration, and the cleaved N-terminal targeting sequence.

title: Evolutionarily conserved intercalated disc protein Tmem65 regulates cardiac conduction and connexin 43 function.
review_notes: Nat Commun 2015; verified. Correctly cited for the intercalated-disc/connexin-43 role, but the surface localisation it reports has not been reproduced by any subsequent mitochondrial study of TMEM65 and is hard to reconcile with a cleaved mitochondrial targeting sequence. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: A mutation in the TMEM65 gene results in mitochondrial myopathy with severe neurological manifestations.
review_notes: Eur J Hum Genet 2017; verified. Confirms inner-membrane localisation and links a homozygous TMEM65 splice variant to mitochondrial encephalomyopathy.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome. Correctly cited, but yields only bare protein binding with no functional interpretation for TMEM65.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome; corroborates mitochondrial residence.

title: TMEM65 regulates and is required for NCLX-dependent mitochondrial calcium efflux.
review_notes: Nat Metab 2025; verified (title, journal and year match the cached record). Source of the NOT|enables GO:0005432 annotation. Correctly cited and methodologically sound, but its central conclusion - TMEM65 is a regulator of NCLX, not the exchanger - is directly contradicted by PMID:40691517. Recorded as DISPUTED rather than MISCITED: the paper is cited for exactly what it claims.

title: TMEM65 functions as the mitochondrial Na(+)/Ca(2+) exchanger.
review_notes: Nat Cell Biol 2025; verified (title, journal and year match the cached record). Source of the positive enables GO:0005432 annotation. Correctly cited, but the key liposome reconstitution measures 45Ca2+ accumulation rather than transmembrane flux, a limitation raised in PMID:41061666, and the conclusion is contradicted by PMID:40200126. Note also that this paper shares senior authors with PMID:40931067, which reassigns NCLX to H+/Ca2+ exchange; the two form one model rather than two independent lines of evidence.

title: Structure and mechanism of the mitochondrial calcium transporter NCLX.
review_notes: Nature 2025; verified. Cited here for context only - it does not assay TMEM65 (the word does not appear in the paper). Relevant because it reassigns NCLX to H+/Ca2+ exchange, which would remove the alternative candidate for mito-NCX and so indirectly supports Position A.

title: Mitochondrial sodium-calcium exchange-Can TMEM65 do it alone?
review_notes: Cell Metab 2025 commentary; verified. Frames the TMEM65 dispute and identifies the specific experimental gap (binding versus translocation in the proteoliposome assay). Written by the authors of PMID:40200126, so not a neutral referee, but the methodological point is concrete and checkable.

title: Enhanced CD4+ T cell proliferation and Th2 cytokine production in DR6-deficient mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Immunity 2001, Liu et al.). Founding DR6 knockout study; experimental basis, via the mouse ortholog, for the T cell proliferation and Th2 cytokine annotations.

title: Enhanced B cell expansion, survival, and humoral responses by targeting death receptor 6.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Exp Med 2003). DR6-null B cell hyperproliferation, reduced apoptosis, enhanced germinal centres and antibody titres; basis for the B cell and humoral immune response annotations.

title: APP binds DR6 to trigger axon pruning and neuron death via distinct caspases.
review_notes: RETRACTED. PubMed-verified as Nikolaev et al., Nature 2009, "APP binds DR6 to trigger axon pruning and neuron death via distinct caspases"; retracted January 2024 (see PMID:38110576) for image duplication, statistical errors and superseded mechanistic conclusions. Listed here only because it is the origin of the APP-receptor model for DR6. Critically, it is cited by no GO annotation on this gene or on the mouse ortholog, so the retraction does not invalidate anything in existing_annotations.

title: Functional analysis of the posttranslational modifications of the death receptor 6.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as Klima et al., Biochim Biophys Acta 2009, on DR6 post-translational modification. The plasma membrane IDA it supports is well matched to the abstract. The cellular response to tumor necrosis factor IDA drawn from the same paper could not be connected to any experiment described in the abstract, and the cached record is abstract-only; flagged as UNDECIDED in that annotation rather than removed.

title: Death receptor 6 negatively regulates oligodendrocyte survival, maturation and myelination.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Med 2011, Mi et al.). DR6 as negative regulator of oligodendrocyte survival, maturation and myelination, with overexpression, antagonist-antibody and knockout evidence; independent of the APP/axon-degeneration disputes.

title: Death receptor 6 induces apoptosis not through type I or type II pathways, but via a unique mitochondria-dependent pathway by interacting with Bax protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2012). Correctly cited, but the apoptosis it reports depends on ectopic overexpression of a death-domain receptor, which is weak evidence for a physiological role; hence KEEP_AS_NON_CORE for the apoptotic process annotation.

title: A DR6/p75(NTR) complex is responsible for β-amyloid-induced cortical neuron death.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Death Dis 2013, Hu et al.). DR6/p75NTR complex mediating amyloid-beta-induced cortical neuron death; the real experimental basis for the neuron apoptotic process annotation, and independent of the retracted Nature paper.

title: Genetic analysis reveals that amyloid precursor protein and death receptor 6 function in the same pathway to control axonal pruning independent of β-secretase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Neurosci 2014, Olsen et al.). The non-retracted in vivo genetic analysis that the retraction notice relies on: APP and DR6 act in the same pathway to control retinal axon pruning, while beta-secretase activity is not required. Shares authorship with the retracted paper and has not been independently replicated.

title: Death Receptor 6 and Caspase-6 Regulate Prion Peptide-Induced Axonal Degeneration in Rat Spinal Neurons.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as Wang et al., J Mol Neurosci 2015, on DR6 and caspase-6 in prion-peptide-induced axonal degeneration in rat spinal neurons. It is the sole source of the rat IMP that the human GO:0007413 axonal fasciculation IEA is propagated from, and its subject (axonal degeneration) does not match that term (collection of axons into a fascicle). Not cited directly by the human GOA row, listed here to document the provenance.

title: Death Receptor 6 Promotes Wallerian Degeneration in Peripheral Axons.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Curr Biol 2017, Gamage et al.). The claim that DR6 is required for Wallerian degeneration and Schwann cell remodelling after axotomy. Directly non-replicated by PMID:41891813 using two knockout lines including the original.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nature 2020, HuRI). High-throughput yeast two-hybrid; source of a bare protein binding annotation with SGTA. Contributes no functional information.

title: A physical wiring diagram for the human immune system.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nature 2022). Systematic extracellular-protein interactome of the human immune system; the source of the APP (P05067) and PI16 (Q6UXB8) protein binding rows. Independent redetection of the DR6-APP interaction, obtained without reference to the retracted work.

title: Retraction Note: APP binds DR6 to trigger axon pruning and neuron death via distinct caspases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified retraction notice, Nature 2024, retracting PMID:19225519. Documents both the anomalies and the authors’ position that the DR6-APP genetic interaction itself still stands via later work.

title: Death receptor 6 does not regulate axon degeneration and Schwann cell injury responses during Wallerian degeneration.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (eLife 2026, Beirowski/Huang/Babetto). Full text cached. Non-replication of PMID:28285993 across two independent DR6 knockout lines, in vivo and in culture. Covers injury-induced Wallerian degeneration in peripheral nerve only; does not test developmental CNS axon pruning, trophic-deprivation degeneration, or the immune and oligodendrocyte roles.

title: TOM20-driven E3 ligase recruitment regulates mitochondrial dynamics through PLD6.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structures (PDB 9J79, 9J7A, 9J7B, 9JCE) show the TOM20 cytosolic four-helix bundle directly binding the FEM1B ANK1 repeat, defining a TOM20-dependent recruitment of the CRL2-FEM1B E3 ubiquitin ligase to the outer mitochondrial membrane that drives PLD6 degradation and regulates mitochondrial dynamics, distinct from TOM20's canonical presequence import-receptor role.

title: Structure of human PINK1 at a mitochondrial TOM-VDAC array.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structure (PDB 9EIH/9EII/9EIJ) of dimeric human PINK1 stabilized at an endogenous TOM-VDAC array; TOMM5 appears incidentally as a TOM core subunit that, with TOM20, facilitates the symmetric two-TOM/VDAC2 arrangement and binds the PINK1 kinase C-lobes.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex AP-MS interactome screen; TPH1 appears only in high-throughput supplementary data, not in the paper text. Supports a bare "protein binding" IPI that is uninformative for TPH1 function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI Y2H binary interactome map; TPH1 appears only in high-throughput data. Supports a bare, uninformative "protein binding" annotation.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegeneration-focused Y2H interactome; full text not available in cache. Supports a bare, uninformative "protein binding" annotation for TPH1.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Second BioPlex AP-MS dataset; with-from DNAJC12 (Q9UKB3), a hydroxylase co-chaperone. Interaction itself is plausible but "protein binding" is uninformative as a molecular function.

title: The A328 V/E (rs2887147) polymorphisms in human tryptophan hydroxylase 2 compromise enzyme activity.
review_notes: PMC full text available and read. Primary biochemical characterization of recombinant full-length human TPH2: establishes wild-type tryptophan 5-monooxygenase kinetics (with BH4 and O2) and shows A328E abolishes and A328V reduces activity. Directly supports the IDA tryptophan 5-monooxygenase activity annotation and the description of TPH2 as the rate-limiting brain serotonin-synthesis enzyme.

title: Tryptophan is hydroxylated
review_notes: Reactome reaction record for the tryptophan-hydroxylation step of serotonin biosynthesis; identifies it as the first and rate-limiting step requiring iron(II), tetrahydrobiopterin and dioxygen. Supports the cytosol location (TAS) and the serotonin biosynthetic process assignment.

title: Isolation and characterization of a human thiamine pyrophosphokinase cDNA.
review_notes: Founding cloning and functional characterization of human TPK1 (hTPK1); recombinant enzyme showed thiamine pyrophosphokinase activity and the gene was mapped to 7q34. Abstract-only in the cache (full_text_available: false); supports the enzyme's core catalytic function and biosynthetic role.

title: Thiamine pyrophosphokinase deficiency in encephalopathic children with defects in the pyruvate oxidation pathway.
review_notes: Cited in UniProt as the source of the THMD5 disease variants (Pro-40, His-50, Ser-219). Establishes that biallelic TPK1 loss of function causes thiamine metabolism dysfunction syndrome 5 (episodic encephalopathy) with defects in pyruvate oxidation. Not a source for a GOA annotation but relevant disease context.

title: A massively parallel pipeline to clone DNA variants and examine molecular phenotypes of human disease mutations.
review_notes: Systematic disease-mutation cloning/interaction pipeline; TPK1 (Tpk1) is among the assayed proteins. Provides an IntAct-curated TPK1 self-interaction supporting the homodimer, but the paper is not TPK1-specific.

title: An interactome perturbation framework prioritizes damaging missense mutations for developmental disorders.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome-perturbation study; source of an IntAct TPK1 self-interaction (identical protein binding). Background/systematic, not focused on TPK1 biology.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Large-scale variant/interaction study; contributes an IntAct TPK1 self-interaction consistent with homodimerization. Not TPK1-specific.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome map; source of both the TPK1 self-interaction (identical protein binding) and the TPK1-OPLAH interaction (bare protein binding). Systematic high-throughput data, uninformative about TPK1's catalytic function.

title: Pyrimidines maintain mitochondrial pyruvate oxidation to support de novo lipogenesis.
review_notes: Full text available. Establishes that human TPK1 prefers UTP over ATP as phosphodonor (Km-UTP 0.33 mM vs Km-ATP 5 mM), links pyrimidine availability to cellular TPP synthesis, PDH activity, and de novo lipogenesis, and identifies catalytic residues (D100, F101). Primary source for the IDA/IMP annotations.

title: 2xTPK1:Mg2+ phosphorylates THMN
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing cytosolic homodimeric TPK1 (with Mg2+) phosphorylating thiamine to thiamine diphosphate. Source of the TAS cytosol annotation and consistent with the homodimer and Mg2+ requirement.

title: The SRm160/300 splicing coactivator is required for exon-enhancer function.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly supports the mechanistic link between ESE-bound TRA2 and spliceosomal snRNP machinery.

title: RBMY, a probable human spermatogenesis factor, and other hnRNP G proteins interact with Tra2beta and affect splicing.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly supports TRA2B association with hnRNP-G-family splicing regulators and a functional effect on enhancer-dependent splicing.

title: hnRNP-G promotes exon 7 inclusion of survival motor neuron (SMN) via direct interaction with Htra2-beta1.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly supports TRA2B binding to the SMN2 exon 7 enhancer and cooperation with hnRNP-G/RBM proteins.

title: Mutations in tau gene exon 10 associated with FTDP-17 alter the activity of an exonic splicing enhancer to interact with Tra2 beta.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC record directly supports TRA2B binding to and regulation through the MAPT exon 10 enhancer.

title: HnRNP G and Tra2beta: opposite effects on splicing matched by antagonism in RNA binding.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly establishes context-dependent activating and repressive effects of hTra2beta on exon incorporation.

title: Human tra2-beta1 autoregulates its protein concentration by influencing alternative splicing of its pre-mRNA.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly supports TRA2B poison-exon binding and negative autoregulation.

title: Tau exon 10, whose missplicing causes frontotemporal dementia, is regulated by an intricate interplay of cis elements and trans factors.
review_notes: The identifier and title are correct, but the cached abstract does not name TRA2B. The curator's experimental annotation is retained; independent MAPT studies provide direct corroboration.

title: Distinct sequence motifs within the 68-kDa subunit of cleavage factor Im mediate RNA binding, protein-protein interactions, and subcellular localization.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly supports a domain-localized CPSF6-TRA2B interaction; this is informative for the interaction annotation but secondary to TRA2B's core RNA-binding role.

title: Arginine/serine-rich protein interaction domain-dependent modulation of a tau exon 10 splicing enhancer: altered interactions and mechanisms for functionally antagonistic FTDP-17 mutations Delta280K AND N279K.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract independently corroborates the positive MAPT exon 10 annotation with direct TRA2B perturbation.

title: Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein G regulates splice site selection by binding to CC(A/C)-rich regions in pre-mRNA.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract verifies the splicing-factor class used to refine the P84586 interaction; the pair itself remains based on the curated IPI/WITH record.

title: Deficiency of the splicing factor Sfrs10 results in early embryonic lethality in mice and has no impact on full-length SMN/Smn splicing.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract provides a useful in-vivo caveat to biochemical SMN2 reporter evidence.

title: Structural basis for the dual RNA-recognition modes of human Tra2-β RRM.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC full text directly establishes the structural basis and dual sequence modes of TRA2B RNA recognition.

title: Molecular basis of purine-rich RNA recognition by the human SR-like protein Tra2-β1.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly supports the proposed sequence-specific mRNA-binding molecular function.

title: Human Tra2 proteins jointly control a CHEK1 splicing switch among alternative and constitutive target exons.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC full text directly supports endogenous target regulation and TRA2A/TRA2B compensation.

title: Regulation of RAGE splicing by hnRNP A1 and Tra2β-1 and its potential role in AD pathogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly supports TRA2B-dependent AGER/RAGE alternative splicing and the glucose-deprivation context.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: The source is a valid binary-interaction atlas, but its collapsed heterogeneous TRA2B partner set does not establish one coherent molecular function.

title: Molecular cloning of htra2-beta-1 and htra2-beta-2, two human homologs of tra-2 generated by alternative splicing.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly supports nuclear-speckle localization and the existence of alternatively spliced TRA2B forms.

title: Human Tra2 proteins are sequence-specific activators of pre-mRNA splicing.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly establishes sequence-specific enhancer binding and enhancer-dependent splicing activation by the human TRA2 proteins.

title: The lymphotoxin-beta receptor is necessary and sufficient for LIGHT-mediated apoptosis of tumor cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The TRAF3 claim rests on a dominant-negative construct blocking LIGHT-induced death - an indirect, overexpression-based result, which is why the GO:0006915 TAS row it anchors is marked over-annotated. Abstract-only in cache.

title: A diverse family of proteins containing tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor domains.
review_notes: PubMed-verified and correctly cited, but the interaction it supports is non-selective: isolated TRAF domains of MUL/TRIM37 and USP7 bound all six TRAF proteins in vitro. Weak basis for the GO:0031625 and GO:0031996 IPI rows, which are consequently kept only as non-core. Abstract-only in cache.

title: A novel TNF receptor family member binds TWEAK and is implicated in angiogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The paper is about Fn14/TweakR; TRAF3 appears only as one of the TRAFs bound by its cytoplasmic tail. Adequate for GO:0005164 but peripheral to TRAF3 biology. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Regulation of the NF-kappaB-inducing kinase by tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 3-induced degradation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The primary source for TRAF3-dependent NIK degradation, which is the mechanism behind TRAF3's non-canonical NF-kappaB brake. Cached record is abstract-only; the quoted conclusions are from the abstract.

title: TRAF3 forms heterotrimers with TRAF2 and modulates its ability to mediate NF-{kappa}B activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. FRET evidence for TRAF3 homotrimerisation and TRAF2/TRAF3 heterotrimerisation, and for CD40-ligation-induced dissociation. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Critical role of TRAF3 in the Toll-like receptor-dependent and -independent antiviral response.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. One of the two 2006 Nature papers establishing TRAF3 as the non-redundant link between TLR adaptors and TBK1/IKK-epsilon for IRF activation. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Specificity in Toll-like receptor signalling through distinct effector functions of TRAF3 and TRAF6.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Companion 2006 Nature paper; gives the TRAF3 vs TRAF6 division of labour and the TRIF-TBK1 recruitment mechanism. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Regulation of antiviral responses by a direct and specific interaction between TRAF3 and Cardif.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Establishes the direct TRAF3-MAVS/Cardif TRAF-domain-TIM contact underlying the mitochondrial pool and the RLR arm.

title: Promiscuous mutations activate the noncanonical NF-kappaB pathway in multiple myeloma.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Not a GOA source; cited here as orthogonal human-genetic support that TRAF3 is a constitutive negative regulator of non-canonical NF-kappaB (recurrent inactivating events in myeloma).

title: DUBA: a deubiquitinase that regulates type I interferon production.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cited for the explicit statement that TRAF3 preferentially assembles K63-linked chains, and as the source of the DUBA/thioesterase interaction. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Roles for LPS-dependent interaction and relocation of TLR4 and TRAM in TRIF-signaling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports the endosomal TRAF3 pool by colocalisation with internalised TLR4/TRAM. Colocalisation rather than functional dissection, so adequate for the CC calls but not for a mechanistic claim. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Nonredundant and complementary functions of TRAF2 and TRAF3 in a ubiquitination cascade that activates NIK-dependent alternative NF-kappaB signaling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Companion study reaching the same architecture from the TRAF2 side; corroborates PMID:18997794.

title: Noncanonical NF-kappaB activation requires coordinated assembly of a regulatory complex of the adaptors cIAP1, cIAP2, TRAF2 and TRAF3 and the kinase NIK.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Defines the division of labour in the NIK-degrading complex (TRAF3 recruits NIK, TRAF2 recruits the cIAPs) and shows TRAF3-null lethality is rescued by reducing NIK gene dosage.

title: The E3 ubiquitin ligase Triad3A negatively regulates the RIG-I/MAVS signaling pathway by targeting TRAF3 for degradation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. TRAF3 as substrate of K48-linked degradation; informs the ubiquitin switch but does not support any TRAF3 molecular function annotation.

title: Different modes of ubiquitination of the adaptor TRAF3 selectively activate the expression of type I interferons and proinflammatory cytokines.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Sound and central for the K63-vs-K48 ubiquitin switch and for GO:0061630 and GO:0032481. However, GOA also anchors a GO:0005739 (mitochondrion) IDA row to this paper, and the cached full text contains no mention of mitochondria; that specific use of the citation looks misplaced, which is recorded on the annotation rather than here.

title: Virus-triggered ubiquitination of TRAF3/6 by cIAP1/2 is essential for induction of interferon-beta (IFN-beta) and cellular antiviral response.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Identifies cIAP1/2 as the ligases that ubiquitinate TRAF3 on virus infection; supports the ubiquitin-switch model.

title: TRAF3 controls activation of the canonical and alternative NFkappaB by the lymphotoxin beta receptor.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. The GOA IMP source for GO:0030162 and GO:0033209. Note the experiments are LTBR, not TNF/TNFR1, which is why GO:0033209 is kept only as non-core.

title: Human TRAF3 adaptor molecule deficiency leads to impaired Toll-like receptor 3 response and susceptibility to herpes simplex encephalitis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Human loss-of-function genetics confirming non-redundancy of TRAF3 in TLR3-dependent interferon induction; the basis of UniProt's IMD132A disease annotation.

title: A functional C-terminal TRAF3-binding site in MAVS participates in positive and negative regulation of the IFN antiviral response.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Maps the MAVS TRAF-interacting motif required for TRAF3 binding and the downstream IFN response. GOA cites it (NAS) for GO:0000151, which is a stretch for this paper although the term itself is defensible.

title: The autoimmunity-associated gene PTPN22 potentiates toll-like receptor-driven, type 1 interferon-dependent immunity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports the TRAF3-PTPN22 interaction and TRAF3 K63 ubiquitination, but TRAF3 is the regulated partner here rather than the actor. Abstract-only in cache.

title: SARS coronavirus papain-like protease inhibits the type I interferon signaling pathway through interaction with the STING-TRAF3-TBK1 complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Supports TRAF3 as a target of viral immune evasion within the STING-TRAF3-TBK1 complex. It does not establish TRAF3 as a subunit of a serine/threonine kinase complex, so the GO:1902554 NAS row it anchors is marked over-annotated.

title: MAVS Promotes Inflammasome Activation by Targeting ASC for K63-Linked Ubiquitination via the E3 Ligase TRAF3.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the EC 2.3.2.27 evidence in UniProt and the clearest direct-substrate demonstration for TRAF3 (ASC Lys174). Abstract-only in cache. Note GOA also cites it for GO:0060337, which the paper does not support.

title: Ubiquitination of Innate Immune Regulator TRAF3 Orchestrates Expulsion of Intracellular Bacteria by Exocyst Complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Establishes a K33-linked TRAF3 mark at Lys168 that recruits RalGDS and the exocyst. Real but narrow (bladder epithelium, bacterial expulsion); treated as non-core and not proposed as a new annotation.

title: DDX3 directly regulates TRAF3 ubiquitination and acts as a scaffold to co-ordinate assembly of signalling complexes downstream from MAVS.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Two waves of K63 ubiquitination of TRAF3 downstream of RIG-I, and TRAF3-MAVS/TRAF3-IKK-epsilon complex formation. Abstract-only in cache.

title: TRIM35 mediates protection against influenza infection by activating TRAF3 and degrading viral PB2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. The EXP source for the mitochondrion CC annotation (TRAF3 co-localises with TRIM35 at mitochondria) and for TRIM35-mediated K63 ubiquitination of TRAF3.

title: A novel RING finger protein interacts with the cytoplasmic domain of CD40.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The other founding TRAF3/CD40 paper, establishing both the CD40 tail interaction and the N-terminal RING finger. Abstract-only in cache.

title: A novel member of the TRAF family of putative signal transducing proteins binds to the cytosolic domain of CD40.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. One of the two founding TRAF3/CD40 papers; the anchor for the generic GO:0007165 TAS row, which is proposed for replacement by the specific CD40 signalling term. Abstract-only in cache.

title: TRAF3 curation notes: literature synthesis and per-annotation rationale
review_notes: Local synthesis written for this review; every assertion carries an inline PMID and verbatim quote from the cached publications.

title: Falcon deep research report for TRAPPC1
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/Falcon) deep-research report compiling current understanding of TRAPPC1. Useful corroboration for established TRAPP-complex biology (core subunit membership with TRAPPC3/TRAPPC4 at the Rab-binding/GEF site; TRAPPIII activates RAB1 for ER-to-Golgi transport and autophagy; TRAPPII activates RAB11; Golgi/ER-Golgi and cis-Golgi localization). IMPORTANT caveat: the report repeatedly attributes whole-TRAPP holo-complex functions (GEF activity, Rab specificity, autophagosome formation) to the TRAPPC1 subunit specifically. Subunit-specific evidence for TRAPPC1 is limited to its structural placement in the conserved core (consistent with PMID:16828797 Bet3-Tpc6B-Mum2 sub-complex) and to patient-variant studies (Zykaj 2024; Van Bergen 2020) showing reduced TRAPPC1 destabilizes the complex and impairs trafficking/autophagy. GEF catalysis is a holo-complex property, not an independent TRAPPC1 activity. It is internally careful to distinguish TRAPPC13 subunit-specific evidence from holo-complex inference: it correctly states TRAPPC13 does NOT itself catalyze nucleotide exchange and that a recombinant "miniTRAPPIII" lacking TRAPPC12/TRAPPC13 still retains Rab1 GEF activity in vitro (subunit-specific, structural/accessory role at the TRAPPC8/TRAPPC11 arm vertex), while attributing Rab1 GEF activity, ER-to-Golgi transport, Golgi homeostasis, and autophagosome formation to the TRAPPIII complex as a whole. title: Hepatoerythropoietic porphyria due to a novel mutation in the uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase gene.

title: UniProtKB P06132 (DCUP_HUMAN) uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase record

review_notes: PubMed-verified crystal-structure paper for human UROS; full text cached; directly establishes catalytic activity, D-ring flipping, monomeric state, and CEP relevance.

review_notes: Cached PMID_10799498 title/body match; establishes USP21 as the founding dual ubiquitin/NEDD8 isopeptidase (supports GO:0004843 and GO:0019784, consistent with the GOA evidence rows for this PMID).

title: BEND3 represses rDNA transcription by stabilizing a NoRC component via USP21 deubiquitinase.
review_notes: Cached PMID_26100909 title/body match; supports USP21's nuclear deubiquitination of BAZ2A/TIP5 substrate (a basis for the protein-deubiquitination core function).

title: Distinct regulatory ribosomal ubiquitylation events are reversible and hierarchically organized.
review_notes: Cached PMID_32011234 title/body match; body explicitly names USP21 (with OTUD3) antagonizing ZNF598-mediated 40S ubiquitylation, supporting the RQC deubiquitination function.

title: Falcon deep research report for USP21
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/Falcon) literature report; useful for substrate breadth and chain-type/pathway context, but treated as UNVERIFIED. USP21-SPECIFIC substrate evidence that the report attributes to dedicated primary papers includes: RIG-I deubiquitination / negative regulation of antiviral RIG-I-IFN signaling (Fan et al. 2014, J Exp Med, doi:10.1084/jem.20122844), MEK2 stabilization driving ERK/MAPK signaling (Li et al. 2018, doi:10.1038/s41419-018-0523-z), Nanog stabilization in ESC pluripotency (Liu et al. 2016), histone H2A K119ub deubiquitination, MARK3/macropinocytosis in pancreatic cancer (Hou et al. 2021), TCF7, and microtubule/centrosome association (Urbe et al. 2012). These primary papers are NOT in the local publications cache and could not be verified here, so substrate identities and chain-type assignments are recorded but not used to change existing experimental annotations. DUB-FAMILY-LEVEL inference (broad chain-type promiscuity, ISG15 cross-reactivity, general USP catalytic mechanism) should not be over-read as USP21-specific physiological function. NOTE a conflict to flag for experts: this report (citing Ye et al. 2011 structural work) states USP21 is "inactive against NEDD8 conjugates", whereas the curated IDA annotation GO:0019784 (PMID:10799498) records deNEDDylase activity; the existing experimental deNEDDylase annotation is retained and NOT weakened on the basis of this report.

title: Ubiquitin-specific protease 25 functions in Endoplasmic Reticulum-associated degradation.
review_notes: Cached PMID_22590560 title/body match; body confirms USP25 is the DUB counteracting HRD1 in ERAD, supporting the substrate-stabilization core function.

title: Negative regulation of IL-17-mediated signaling and inflammation by the ubiquitin-specific protease USP25.
review_notes: Cached PMID_23042150 title/body match; establishes USP25 K63-DUB activity on TRAF5/TRAF6 in IL-17 signaling, supporting the substrate-deubiquitination core function.

title: USP25 regulates KEAP1-NRF2 anti-oxidation axis and its inactivation protects acetaminophen-induced liver injury in male mice.
review_notes: Cached PMID_37339955 title/body match; supports USP25 deubiquitination/stabilization of KEAP1 in the NRF2 axis (substrate-stabilization core function); cited in core_functions supported_by.

title: Falcon deep research report for VPS37D
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report. The VPS37D-specific claims it makes are appropriately hedged and consistent with the existing review: VPS37D is the least functionally characterized of the four human VPS37 paralogs, is a bona fide core ESCRT-I structural subunit, does NOT show the SH3YL1/CDIP1 selective interactions reported for VPS37B/C, and has no VPS37A-like autophagy UEVL specialization established in the cited literature; it explicitly states that direct VPS37D-specific mechanistic evidence remains limited. The one novel VPS37D-specific assertion (breast-cancer biomarker association from chen2025escrtmayfunction; negligible VPS37D expression in colorectal tissue from kolmus2021) is disease/expression context, not a molecular-function or core-process claim, and was not used to change any GO annotation. All other pathway content (autophagosome closure, cytokinetic abscission, membrane/NE repair, viral budding) is ESCRT-I holo-complex or VPS37A-C paralog inference and is NOT attributed to the VPS37D subunit. Underlying primary PMIDs were not independently re-verified here, hence UNVERIFIED.

title: Subcellular localization of xanthine oxidase in rat hepatocytes: high-resolution immunoelectron microscopic study combined with biochemical analysis.
review_notes: Rat hepatocyte immunoelectron microscopy localizing XO to the cytosol; the MGI-assigned reference for the human XDH cytosol IDA and the array of purine catabolic-process IDAs. Directly supports cytosolic localization and argues against peroxisomal/organellar XO. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Human colostrum: identification of minor proteins in the aqueous phase by proteomics.
review_notes: Proteomics identification of XDH as a minor protein in human colostrum; supports the secreted/extracellular (milk) pool. Contextual, not central to the enzyme's core catalytic function.

title: Human xanthine oxidase changes its substrate specificity to aldehyde oxidase type upon mutation of amino acid residues in the active site: roles of active site residues in binding and activation of purine substrate.
review_notes: Crystal structure of human XOR (E803V mutant) in complex with FAD, 2Fe-2S, molybdopterin and salicylate; directly establishes the cofactor complement, homodimeric subunit structure, active-site purine-binding residues and allopurinol interaction. Cited by UniProt for COFACTOR, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY, FUNCTION and SUBUNIT.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome (HuRI); source of the bare protein-binding IPI (interactor GRIP1 isoform Q9Y3R0-3). Systematic screen, not focused on XDH function; yields an uninformative molecular-function term.

title: Cloning and expression in vitro of human xanthine dehydrogenase/oxidase.
review_notes: Cloning and heterologous expression of the complete human XDH/XO coding sequence with measured XDH/XO enzyme activity; the enzyme was expressed predominantly in the dehydrogenase form. UniProt CATALYTIC ACTIVITY reference for EC 1.17.1.4. Directly supports xanthine dehydrogenase/oxidase activity in human.

title: The XRCC2 and XRCC3 repair genes are required for chromosome stability in mammalian cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes XRCC2's requirement for chromosome stability; irs1 (XRCC2-mutant) cells accumulate breaks/deletions/translocations. Supports the DNA repair IGI annotation.

title: Mammalian XRCC2 promotes the repair of DNA double-strand breaks by homologous recombination.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Johnson, Liu, Jasin, Nature 1999). Classic demonstration that XRCC2-deficient hamster cells show >100-fold decrease in DSB-induced HR between sister chromatids while NHEJ is normal. Direct experimental support for the DSBR-HR annotation.

title: XRCC2 is a nuclear RAD51-like protein required for damage-dependent RAD51 focus formation without the need for ATP binding.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (O'Regan et al., JBC 2001). XRCC2 localizes to the nucleus and is required for damage-dependent RAD51 focus formation, yet P-loop (ATP-binding) mutants still complement irs1. Supports the mediator (not ATP-dependent damage-sensor) role and the MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED call on GO:0140664.

title: Identification and purification of two distinct complexes containing the five RAD51 paralogs.
review_notes: Full text verified. Defines the BCDX2 complex (RAD51B-RAD51C-RAD51D-XRCC2) and shows it binds ssDNA and ssDNA gaps. Primary evidence for the GO:0033063 complex annotation.

title: Homologous pairing and ring and filament structure formation activities of the human Xrcc2*Rad51D complex.
review_notes: Abstract verified. Purified Xrcc2*Rad51D subcomplex catalyzes homologous pairing between ssDNA and dsDNA and forms ssDNA-dependent filaments. Supports DNA strand invasion.

title: Ring-shaped Rad51 paralog protein complexes bind Holliday junctions and replication forks as visualized by electron microscopy.
review_notes: Full text verified. Direct EM shows BCDX2 binds Holliday junctions and replication forks with high specificity. Supports four-way junction DNA binding and replication-fork localization.

title: Homologous recombination proteins are associated with centrosomes and are required for mitotic stability.
review_notes: Abstract verified. Shows XRCC2 centrosome co-localization and mitotic-stability requirement; supports the (non-core) centrosome, centrosome cycle and mitotic cell cycle annotations.

title: Rad51 paralog complexes BCDX2 and CX3 act at different stages in the BRCA1-BRCA2-dependent homologous recombination pathway.
review_notes: Verified. Places BCDX2 downstream of BRCA2 and upstream of RAD51 recruitment in HR; supports the DSBR-HR IMP annotation and the mediator model.

title: Complementation of hypersensitivity to DNA interstrand crosslinking agents demonstrates that XRCC2 is a Fanconi anaemia gene.
review_notes: Full text verified (Park et al., J Med Genet 2016; PMC5035190). Establishes XRCC2 as Fanconi anemia complementation group U (FANCU): wild-type XRCC2 corrects MMC hypersensitivity, chromosome breakage and G2-M accumulation of patient cells with biallelic XRCC2 mutation; XRCC2 acts late in the FA-BRCA pathway (FANCD2 monoubiquitination normal). Primary evidence for the new interstrand cross-link repair annotation.

title: XRCC2 mutation causes meiotic arrest, azoospermia and infertility.
review_notes: Full text verified (Yang et al., J Med Genet 2018; PMC6119352). Homozygous XRCC2 p.Leu14Pro causes meiotic arrest, azoospermia and infertility in a consanguineous family; a knockin mouse reproduces meiotic arrest, azoospermia and premature ovarian failure. Direct human/mouse evidence strengthening the (non-core) meiotic cell cycle annotation beyond the original testis-expression inference.

title: XRCC2 Regulates Replication Fork Progression during dNTP Alterations.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Saxena, Somyajit, Nagaraju, Cell Rep 2018). XRCC2 (FANCU) and RAD51D restrain active DNA synthesis during dNTP alterations independently of HDR, via ATR-mediated phosphorylation of XRCC2 Ser247. XRCC2-specific corroboration of the replication-fork localization/function annotation.

title: Sequential role of RAD51 paralog complexes in replication fork remodeling and restart.
review_notes: Verified. Shows the BCDX2 subcomplex restrains fork progression and promotes fork reversal under replication stress. Supports replication-fork localization/function.

title: Structure and function of the RAD51B-RAD51C-RAD51D-XRCC2 tumour suppressor.
review_notes: Full text verified. Definitive cryo-EM structure/function of BCDX2: RAD51C-RAD51D-XRCC2 mimic three aligned RAD51 protomers; BCDX2 stimulates RAD51 filament nucleation/extension in an ATP-hydrolysis-dependent manner (RAD51B/RAD51C ATPases); XRCC2 binds ATP via Walker A K54/T55, Walker B D149. Primary evidence for the mediator core function.

title: The XRCC2 DNA repair gene from human and mouse encodes a novel member of the recA/RAD51 family.
review_notes: Verified. Original identification of XRCC2 as a recA/RAD51-family DNA-repair gene; testis-elevated expression suggests a meiotic role. Supports DNA repair and meiotic cell cycle annotations.

title: Global landscape of HIV-human protein complexes.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Supports a physical association with HIV-1 capsid, but only as a bare protein-binding datum.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: mRNA-interactome atlas; source of an HDA RNA binding annotation.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: mRNA-bound proteome study; source of an HDA RNA binding annotation.

title: Initiation of Quality Control during Poly(A) Translation Requires Site-Specific Ribosome Ubiquitination.
review_notes: Foundational study identifying ZNF598 as the RQC-initiating ribosomal ubiquitin ligase and eS10 as its target.

title: ZNF598 and RACK1 Regulate Mammalian Ribosome-Associated Quality Control Function by Mediating Regulatory 40S Ribosomal Ubiquitylation.
review_notes: Independent confirmation of ZNF598-mediated 40S ubiquitylation in RQC.

title: The E3 ubiquitin ligase and RNA-binding protein ZNF598 orchestrates ribosome quality control of premature polyadenylated mRNAs.
review_notes: Establishes the ZNF598-UBE2D3 E2-E3 pair and dual ligase/RNA-binding nature.

title: Ubiquitination of stalled ribosome triggers ribosome-associated quality control.
review_notes: Yeast Hel2 study underpinning the ZNF598 ortholog mechanism; cited for ZNF598 cytosol localization in GOA.

title: ZNF598 Is a Quality Control Sensor of Collided Ribosomes.
review_notes: Defines ZNF598 as the collision sensor and the structural basis of recognition.

title: Identification of a novel trigger complex that facilitates ribosome-associated quality control in mammalian cells.
review_notes: Links ZNF598 ubiquitination to the downstream RQT complex.

title: The ASC-1 Complex Disassembles Collided Ribosomes.
review_notes: Downstream disassembly step following ZNF598 marking.

title: GIGYF2 and 4EHP Inhibit Translation Initiation of Defective Messenger RNAs to Assist Ribosome-Associated Quality Control.
review_notes: Establishes the ZNF598/4EHP-GYF2 adapter and translational-repression role.

title: 4EHP and GIGYF1/2 Mediate Translation-Coupled Messenger RNA Decay.
review_notes: Source of the GIGYF1 interaction and the pre-mRNA catabolic process NAS annotation.

title: Live-cell imaging reveals kinetic determinants of quality control triggered by ribosome stalling.
review_notes: Kinetic characterization of ZNF598-triggered RQC.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex interactome; uninformative protein binding annotation (GIGYF1).

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell interactome; uninformative protein binding annotation (YWHAE).

title: A distinct mammalian disome collision interface harbors K63-linked polyubiquitination of uS10 to trigger hRQT-mediated subunit dissociation.
review_notes: Characterizes ZNF598 ubiquitination chemistry (K63 uS10) and the disome interface.

title: A central chaperone-like role for 14-3-3 proteins in human cells.
review_notes: 14-3-3 interactome study; uninformative protein binding annotation (YWHAE).

title: Integrated analysis of protein composition, tissue diversity, and gene regulation in mouse mitochondria.
review_notes: High-throughput mouse mitochondrial proteomics; source of an HDA mitochondrion localization.

title: Differential induction of genes in liver and brown adipose tissue regulated by peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-alpha during fasting and cold exposure in acyl-CoA dehydrogenase-deficient mice.
review_notes: Grounds the temperature-homeostasis and lipid/cholesterol regulatory IMP annotations of mouse LCAD - the cluster mis-transferred to human ACADVL. Abstract-only in cache.

title: A mitochondrial protein compendium elucidates complex I disease biology.
review_notes: MitoCarta-type high-throughput mitochondrial proteomics; source of an HDA mitochondrion localization.
